    extendByZero X U ⋙ (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.O).flip.obj F ≅
      sliceSheafTensorRight X U (F.over U) ⋙ extendByZero X U
declarations.comment: for a site essentially u-small, objects in Type c, morphisms and modules in u

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.FreeModuleUniverse.restrictionTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8I at a free module universe.** For a sheaf of modules `F` on `X`, the extension
by zero of `G ⊗ F|_U` is the extension by zero of `G`, tensored with `F`, naturally in `G`.

The attribute records the shape at which this holds: the objects of `C` in `Type u`, its
morphisms in `v`, the structure sheaf in `w` and the modules in a free `a` with `UnivLE.{v, a}`,
and no smallness assumption on `C`. The tag is carried in full by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.ExtensionByZero.extensionByZeroTensorIso`, where objects, morphisms,
ring and modules lie in a single universe; that registration stands and this one does not
replace it, nor does it replace
`Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.OfEssentiallySmall.restrictionTensorIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictionTensorIso
    (F : SheafOfModules.{a} (ringSheaf X.O)) :
    extendByZero.{a} X U ⋙ (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.O).flip.obj F ≅
      sliceSheafTensorRight.{a} X U (F.over U) ⋙ extendByZero.{a} X U
declarations.comment: objects in Type u, morphisms in v, ring sections in w, modules in a free a with UnivLE v a, and no smallness assumption on the site

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.ExtensionByZero.extensionByZeroTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8I.** Extension by zero commutes with tensoring by a module on the original
site, naturally in the module on the slice site.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionByZeroTensorIso (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    letI := Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.sheafRestrictionIsRightAdjoint X.J (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U
    let E := _root_.SheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
      (F := Over.forget U) (𝟙 ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))
    E ⋙ ((sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} X.O).obj F) ≅
      ((sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} (X.O.over U)).obj (F.over U)) ⋙ E

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.ExtensionByZero.extensionTensorBifunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8I, bifunctorial form.** Extension by zero commutes with tensoring by a module
on the original site, naturally in the module on the slice site *and* in the module on the
original site.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionTensorBifunctorIso :
    extensionTensorBifunctor X U ≅ tensorExtensionBifunctor X U
declarations.comment: bifunctorial form

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatRestriction.OfEssentiallySmall.isFlat_over_of_essentiallySmall
declarations.doc:
Restriction to an object of a ringed site whose objects form a type in a universe of their
own, with morphisms, sections and modules in one universe `u` and the site essentially `u`-small,
preserves flatness of sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_over_of_essentiallySmall
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{c, u, u}) [EssentiallySmall.{u} X.C] (U : X.C)
    [X.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})]
    [(X.J.over U).HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}] [HasWeakSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [(X.J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasWeakSheafify (X.J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X.O))
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat F) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := X.O.over U) (F.over U)
declarations.comment: for a site essentially u-small, objects in Type c, morphisms and modules in u

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatRestriction.isFlat_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E8J.** Restriction to an object of a ringed site preserves flatness
of module sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlat_over
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf X.O))
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat F) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := X.O.over U) (F.over U)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatRestriction.FreeModuleUniverse.isFlat_over
declarations.doc:
**Restriction preserves flatness, at a free module universe.** Restriction to an object of
a ringed site preserves flatness of module sheaves, for objects of the site in `Type u`, morphisms
in `v`, the structure sheaf in `w` and the modules in `max v a`, with no smallness assumption on
the site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlat_over
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max v a} (ringSheaf X.O))
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat F) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := X.O.over U) (F.over U)
declarations.comment: objects in Type u, morphisms in v, ring sections in w, modules in max v a, and no smallness assumption on the site

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedTensor.ExtensionByZero.kFlat_restrictionComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E8K.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `U` be an object of
`C`. If `K` is a K-flat complex of `O`-modules, then `K|_U` is a K-flat complex of
`O_U`-modules.

Let `G` be an acyclic complex of `O_U`-modules. Extension by zero is exact (Stacks 03DJ), so
`j_!G` is acyclic, and the K-flatness of `K` then makes `Tot(j_!G ⊗_O K)` acyclic. That
complex is `j_!(Tot(G ⊗_{O_U} K|_U))` by `tensorComplexExtensionIso`, and extension by zero
reflects exactness (Stacks 0E8G), so `Tot(G ⊗_{O_U} K|_U)` is acyclic as well.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_restrictionComplex (Q : CochainComplex (Modules X.O) ℤ)
    (hQ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat X.O Q) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat (X.O.over U) ((restrictionComplex X U).obj Q)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedTensor.ExtensionByZero.OfEssentiallySmall.kFlat_restrictionComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E8K over a site with large objects.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site
whose objects form a type in an arbitrary universe `c` while its morphisms, the sections of `O`
and the sections of its modules lie in one universe `u`, let `C` be essentially `u`-small, and
let `U` be an object of `C`.  If `Q` is a K-flat complex of `O`-modules, then `Q|_U` is a
K-flat complex of `O|_U`-modules.

The proof is the source's.  Let `P` be an acyclic complex of `O|_U`-modules.  Extension by
zero is exact (Stacks 03DJ), so `j_{U!}P` is acyclic, and the K-flatness of `Q` then makes
`Tot(j_{U!}P ⊗_O Q)` acyclic.  That complex is `j_{U!}(Tot(P ⊗_{O|_U} Q|_U))` by
`tensorComplexExtensionIso`, and extension by zero reflects exactness (Stacks 0E8G), so
`Tot(P ⊗_{O|_U} Q|_U)` is acyclic as well.

The attribute records the universe shape.  The tag is carried in full by
`Stacks.DerivedTensor.ExtensionByZero.kFlat_restrictionComplex`, where the objects, the
morphisms and the sections lie in a single universe — the faithful reading of the tag's ringed
site, which this statement specializes to at `c := u`; that registration stands and this one
does not replace it.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_restrictionComplex (hQ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat X.O Q) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat (X.O.over U) ((restrictionComplex X U).obj Q)
declarations.comment: for a site essentially u-small, objects in Type c, morphisms and modules in u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.diagonalDottedArrowFst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8L, part (1), first arrow.** The triple `(a₁, α₁, id)` is a dotted arrow for the
square of `f` with top row `x`, bottom row `f ∘ a₁` and right edge `f`.
declarations.statement:
def diagonalDottedArrowFst :
    CategoryTheory.DottedArrow D.x D.j f.hom
      ((D.y ≫ (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS f f).fst.hom) ≫ f.hom)
      (diagonalWitness B S hS D)
declarations.comment: part (1): the dotted arrow coming from the first projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.diagonalDottedArrowSnd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8L, part (1), second arrow.** The triple `(a₂, α₂, φ)` is a dotted arrow for the
*same* square of `f`: the compatibility triangle is the statement that `γ` is a 2-morphism into
the 2-fibre product, by the exchange law and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal_whiskerLeft_twoFibreProductCell`.
declarations.statement:
def diagonalDottedArrowSnd :
    CategoryTheory.DottedArrow D.x D.j f.hom
      ((D.y ≫ (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS f f).fst.hom) ≫ f.hom)
      (diagonalWitness B S hS D)
declarations.comment: part (1): the dotted arrow coming from the second projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSetoidCategory_dottedArrow_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8L, part (2), first assertion.** The category of dotted arrows of a valuative
diagram for the relative diagonal of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks is a setoid.

The relative diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces (Stacks 04XS), hence its underlying
functor is faithful (Stacks 04Y5), and the category of dotted arrows along a faithful 1-morphism
is a thin groupoid.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetoidCategory_dottedArrow_relativeDiagonal :
    IsSetoidCategory
      (CategoryTheory.DottedArrow D.x D.j (relativeDiagonal B S hS f).hom D.y D.γ)
declarations.comment: part (2): the category of diagonal fillers is a setoid

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.diagonalDottedArrowClassesEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8L, part (2), second assertion.** The isomorphism classes of dotted arrows of a
valuative diagram for the relative diagonal of `f` correspond bijectively to the morphisms
`(a₁, α₁, id) ⟶ (a₂, α₂, φ)` of dotted arrows for `f`, by `d ↦ (β ⋆ pr₁) ∘ (β ⋆ pr₂)⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def diagonalDottedArrowClassesEquiv :
    Quotient (isIsomorphicSetoid
        (CategoryTheory.DottedArrow D.x D.j (relativeDiagonal B S hS f).hom D.y D.γ)) ≃
      (diagonalDottedArrowFst B S hS D ⟶ diagonalDottedArrowSnd B S hS D)
declarations.comment: part (2): isomorphism classes are the morphisms between the two dotted arrows

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.surjective_of_surjective_mapCotangent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8M**: a local homomorphism `A → B` with `B` finite over `A`, `m_B` finitely
generated, surjective on residue fields, and surjective on cotangent spaces, is surjective.

The cotangent hypothesis gives `m_A B = m_B`, so `B ⧸ m_A B` is the residue field of `B`, and the
residue hypothesis says `A` already surjects onto it. Nakayama (00DV (6)) promotes that to
surjectivity of `A → B`.

The tag asks for an isomorphism on residue fields; surjectivity is all that is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocalRing.surjective_of_surjective_mapCotangent [Module.Finite A B]
    (hmB : (maximalIdeal B).FG)
    (hres : Function.Surjective (ResidueField.map (algebraMap A B)))
    (hcot : Function.Surjective (Ideal.mapCotangent (maximalIdeal A) (maximalIdeal B)
      (Algebra.ofId A B) (le_of_eq (maximalIdeal_comap (algebraMap A B)).symm))) :
    Function.Surjective (algebraMap A B)

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.eventuallyConst_subobject_of_monotone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8N.** An increasing well-ordered chain of subobjects is eventually constant if
the cofinality of the index order exceeds the number of morphisms from a separator to the
ambient object.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventuallyConst_subobject_of_monotone {U X : C} (hU : IsSeparator U)
    {α : Type w} [LinearOrder α] [WellFoundedLT α]
    (hcof : Cardinal.lift.{w} (Cardinal.mk (U ⟶ X)) <
      Cardinal.lift.{v} (Order.cof α)) (f : α → Subobject X) (hf : Monotone f) :
    atTop.EventuallyConst f
declarations.comment: eventually constant

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.eventuallyConst_subobject_of_antitone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8N.** A decreasing well-ordered chain of subobjects is eventually constant if
the cofinality of the index order exceeds the number of morphisms from a separator to the

declarations.statement:
theorem eventuallyConst_subobject_of_antitone {U X : C} (hU : IsSeparator U)

    (hcof : Cardinal.lift.{w} (Cardinal.mk (U ⟶ X)) <
      Cardinal.lift.{v} (Order.cof α)) (f : α → Subobject X) (hf : Antitone f) :
    atTop.EventuallyConst f
declarations.comment: eventually constant

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.mk_subobject_le_two_pow_mk_hom
declarations.doc:
The collection of subobjects of an object has cardinality at most the cardinality of the
power set of the morphisms to it from a separator.
declarations.statement:

      (2 : Cardinal.{max u v}) ^ Cardinal.lift.{u} (Cardinal.mk (U ⟶ X))
declarations.comment: subobject cardinality

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.cardinality_le_hom_of_strictMono_subobject
declarations.doc:
A strictly increasing chain of subobjects has cardinality at most the cardinality of the
set of morphisms from a separator to the ambient object.

A strictly decreasing chain of subobjects has cardinality at most the cardinality of the

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.canonicalRestrictionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E8Q**, the canonical functor.  The functor taking a scheme of finite
presentation over `S` to the gluing datum given by its restriction to the complement of the
closed points, its restrictions to the local schemes at them, and the base-change associativity
isomorphism between the two restrictions to each punctured local scheme.

The comparison is `AlgebraicGeometry.canonicalRestrictionComparison`, which is pinned by its
compatibility equation, so this is the canonical functor and not merely a functor into the
category of gluing data.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalRestrictionFunctor :
    FinitePresentationOver S ⥤ glueingData s hs
declarations.comment: canonical functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.canonicalRestrictionFunctor_isEquivalence_of_isEmpty
declarations.doc:
For an empty family of points, the canonical restriction functor from schemes of finite
presentation over `S` to gluing data is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalRestrictionFunctor_isEquivalence_of_isEmpty [IsEmpty I] :
    (canonicalRestrictionFunctor s hs).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: equivalence, special case of an empty family of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.canonicalRestrictionFunctor_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E8Q.** Let `s : I → S` be a finite family of pairwise distinct closed
points of a scheme `S` whose open complement has quasi-compact inclusion.  Then the canonical
restriction functor from schemes of finite presentation over `S` to glueing data near the family
— a scheme of finite presentation over the open complement, a family of schemes of finite
presentation over the local schemes at the points, and an isomorphism of the two restrictions to
each punctured local scheme — is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalRestrictionFunctor_isEquivalence {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u} [Finite I]
    (s : I → S) (hs : ∀ i, s i ∈ closedPoints S) (hinj : Function.Injective s)
    (hqc : QuasiCompact (complementOfClosedPoints s hs).ι) :
    (canonicalRestrictionFunctor s hs).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: equivalence, general finite family of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.canonicalRestrictionFunctor_isEquivalence_of_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E8Q**, for a family of closed points indexed by a type with a unique
element: the canonical restriction functor from schemes of finite presentation over `S` to gluing
data near the family is an equivalence of categories.

The family is a single closed point whose open complement has quasi-compact inclusion, so this is
[Stacks, Tag 0BPA] after evaluating the one-index gluing data at its unique index.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalRestrictionFunctor_isEquivalence_of_unique [Unique I]
    (hqc : QuasiCompact (complementOfClosedPoints s hs).ι) :
    (canonicalRestrictionFunctor s hs).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: equivalence, special case of a one-element family of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.canonicalRestrictionComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E8Q**, the canonical comparison. The base-change associativity
isomorphism identifying the two ways of restricting a scheme of finite presentation over `S`
to every punctured local scheme, together with the equation saying that it commutes with the
projections down to the scheme being restricted.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalRestrictionComparison {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u} [Finite I]
    (s : I → S) (hs : ∀ i, s i ∈ closedPoints S) :
    { e : restrictToComplementOfClosedPoints s hs ⋙ restrictOpenToPuncturedLocals s hs ≅
        restrictToLocalSchemes s ⋙ restrictLocalsToPuncturedLocals s hs //
      ∀ (X : FinitePresentationOver S) (i : I),
        ((e.hom.app X) i).hom.left ≫
          pullback.fst
            (pullback.snd X.obj.hom (S.fromSpecStalk (s i)))
            (((S.fromSpecStalk (s i)) ⁻¹ᵁ (complementOfClosedPoints s hs)).ι) ≫
          pullback.fst X.obj.hom (S.fromSpecStalk (s i)) =
        pullback.fst
            (pullback.snd X.obj.hom (complementOfClosedPoints s hs).ι)
            ((S.fromSpecStalk (s i)) ∣_ (complementOfClosedPoints s hs)) ≫
          pullback.fst X.obj.hom (complementOfClosedPoints s hs).ι }
declarations.comment: canonical comparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativelyVeryAmple_and_isClosedImmersion_toProjectiveSpaceOfModule_of_separates
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E8S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E8S).** Let `k` be an
algebraically closed field, let `X` be a proper `k`-scheme, let `ℒ` be an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module and let `V ⊂ H⁰(X, ℒ)` be a `k`-subvector space. If

1. for every pair of distinct closed points `x, y ∈ X` there is a section `s ∈ V` which vanishes
   at `x` but not at `y`, and
2. for every closed point `x ∈ X` and nonzero tangent vector `θ ∈ T_{X/k, x}` there exists a
   section `s ∈ V` which vanishes at `x` but whose pullback by `θ` is nonzero,

then `ℒ` is very ample and the canonical morphism `φ_{ℒ, V} : X ⟶ 𝐏(V)` is a closed immersion.

The conclusion is the conjunction of four assertions: `V` is finite-dimensional over `k`; `ℒ` is
very ample relative to the structure morphism; `V` generates `ℒ`, provided no closed point of `X`
is its only one; and for every basis of `V` whose family of images generates `ℒ` the canonical
morphism `φ_{ℒ, V} : X ⟶ 𝐏(V)` of [Stacks, Tag 0FCY] read in that basis is a closed immersion.

Finite-dimensionality of `V` is not assumed but derived, from [Stacks, Tag 02O6] for the
invertible module `ℒ` on the proper scheme `X`; so is generation, and so is the canonical
morphism itself, together with the identification of the pulled-back hyperplane sheaf with `ℒ`.
The side condition on the third assertion is the gap in the source's proof, discussed in the
module documentation: on a scheme with exactly one closed point condition (1) is vacuous and
`V` can generate nothing.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_and_isClosedImmersion_toProjectiveSpaceOfModule_of_separates
    (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper p] (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] :
    letI : Module k Γ(L, ⊤) := Module.compHom _ (baseRingMap p)
    ∀ V : Submodule k Γ(L, ⊤),
      SeparatesClosedPoints (fun v : V => (v : Γ(L, ⊤))) →
      SeparatesTangentVectors p (fun v : V => (v : Γ(L, ⊤))) →
      Module.Finite k V ∧
      Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple p L ∧
      ((∀ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) → ∃ y : X, IsClosed ({y} : Set X) ∧ y ≠ x) →
        GeneratesStalks (fun v : V => (v : Γ(L, ⊤)))) ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin (n + 1)) k V)
        (hb : GeneratesStalks fun i => ((b i : V) : Γ(L, ⊤))),
        IsClosedImmersion (toProjectiveSpaceOfModule b (fun i => ((b i : V) : Γ(L, ⊤))) hb p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativelyVeryAmple_of_surjectsOnDegreeTwo
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E8T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E8T).** Let `k` be an
algebraically closed field, let `X` be proper over `k` through `p`, let `E` be a quasi-coherent
`k`-module and let `i : X ⟶ 𝐏(E)` be a morphism over `k` with `i^* 𝒪_{𝐏(E)}(1) ≅ ℒ` realizing the
complete linear system of an invertible `ℒ`. If `H⁰(X, ℒ) ⟶ H⁰(Z, ℒ|_Z)` is surjective for every
closed subscheme `Z ⊆ X` which is zero-dimensional of degree two over `k`, then `ℒ` is very ample
relative to `p`.

The two kinds of degree-two subscheme give the two separation conditions of
[Stacks, Tag 0E8S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E8S), whose very-ampleness clause then
applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_of_surjectsOnDegreeTwo [IsAlgClosed k]
    {E : (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).Modules} [E.IsQuasicoherent]
    (p : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [IsProper p]
    (i : X ⟶ (relativeProj (symAlgebra E)).scheme)
    (h : i ≫ (relativeProj (symAlgebra E)).toBase = p)
    {L : X.Modules} [IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj (twistOne E) ≅ L)
    {V : Type v} {t : V → (twistOne E).val.obj (op ⊤)} {ψ : V → L.val.obj (op ⊤)}
    (htψ : ∀ v, e.hom.val.app (op ⊤) (pullbackSectionTop i (twistOne E) (t v)) = ψ v)
    (hfull : Function.Surjective ψ) (hsurj : SurjectsOnDegreeTwo p L)
    (hpair : HasDegreeTwoPointPairs p L) (htan : HasDegreeTwoFatPoints p L) :
    IsRelativelyVeryAmple p L
declarations.comment: the degree-two hypothesis is stated with the degree of a zero-dimensional subscheme as finrank over k; the classification of degree-two subschemes into point pairs and fat points is a hypothesis, as is the Tag 0FCY morphism to 𝐏(E) inherited from Tag 0E8S, and the linear system is required to be complete

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativelyVeryAmple_of_surjectsOnDegreeTwo_of_complete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E8T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E8T), with the classification of
the degree-two subschemes proved.** Let `k` be algebraically closed, let `X` be proper over `k`
through `p`, let `E` be a quasi-coherent `k`-module and let `i : X ⟶ 𝐏(E)` be a morphism over
`k` with `i^* 𝒪_{𝐏(E)}(1) ≅ ℒ` realizing the complete linear system of an invertible `ℒ`. If
`H⁰(X, ℒ) ⟶ H⁰(Z, ℒ|_Z)` is surjective for every closed subscheme `Z ⊆ X` which is
zero-dimensional of degree two over `k`, then `ℒ` is very ample relative to `p`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativelyVeryAmple_of_surjectsOnDegreeTwo` with its two
classification hypotheses supplied: `AlgebraicGeometry.hasDegreeTwoPointPairs` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasDegreeTwoFatPoints`. What is still a hypothesis is the morphism to `𝐏(E)`
with its identification of the pulled-back twist, which is the morphism of
[Stacks, Tag 0FCY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FCY) inherited from the criterion of
[Stacks, Tag 0E8S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E8S), together with completeness of the
linear system it realizes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_of_surjectsOnDegreeTwo_of_complete
    {E : (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).Modules} [E.IsQuasicoherent]
    (p : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [IsProper p]
    (i : X ⟶ (relativeProj (symAlgebra E)).scheme)
    (h : i ≫ (relativeProj (symAlgebra E)).toBase = p)
    {L : X.Modules} [IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj (twistOne E) ≅ L)
    {V : Type v} {t : V → (twistOne E).val.obj (op ⊤)} {ψ : V → L.val.obj (op ⊤)}
    (htψ : ∀ v, e.hom.val.app (op ⊤) (pullbackSectionTop i (twistOne E) (t v)) = ψ v)
    (hfull : Function.Surjective ψ) (hsurj : SurjectsOnDegreeTwo p L) :
    IsRelativelyVeryAmple p L
declarations.comment: the degree-two criterion with the classification of the degree-two zero-dimensional subschemes into point pairs and fat points PROVED; what is still assumed is the Tag 0FCY morphism to 𝐏(E) with its twist identification, inherited from Tag 0E8S, and completeness of the linear system it realizes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativelyVeryAmple_of_surjectsOnDegreeTwo'
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E8T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E8T).** Let `k` be an
algebraically closed field, let `X` be a proper `k`-scheme and let `ℒ` be an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module. If `H⁰(X, ℒ) ⟶ H⁰(Z, ℒ|_Z)` is surjective for every closed subscheme `Z ⊆ X` of
dimension zero and degree two over `k`, then `ℒ` is very ample on `X` over `k`.

The pairs of distinct closed points and the fat points among those subschemes give the two
separation conditions of [Stacks, Tag 0E8S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E8S); the same
hypothesis makes the global sections generate `ℒ`, so a basis of the finite-dimensional space
`H⁰(X, ℒ)` defines a morphism to `ℙⁿ_k` realizing the complete linear system, and that morphism
is a closed immersion. Projective space over the affine base is the projective bundle of a free
module, which turns the immersion into the datum relative very ampleness asks for.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_of_surjectsOnDegreeTwo' {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper p] (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hsurj : SurjectsOnDegreeTwo p L) :
    Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple p L
declarations.comment: the full statement, with no assumed data: the dimension of a zero-dimensional closed subscheme is the topological Krull dimension of its space and its degree is the dimension over k of its ring of global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.VeryAmpleSixthPower.isRelativelyVeryAmple_tensorPowModule_six_of_regularSection
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E8V].** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper scheme over `k` of dimension
`1` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, and let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. Assume that `ℒ` has a
regular global section, that `H¹(X, ℒ) = 0` and that `ℒ` is ample. Then `ℒ^{⊗ 6}` is very ample
on `X` over `k`.

The regular global section is a monomorphism `s : 𝒪_X ⟶ ℒ`; `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` is the hypothesis
that the map `k ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` is an isomorphism; very ampleness is relative very ampleness for
`f : X ⟶ Spec k` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 01VM].

The proof is the source's. The section ring `S = Γ_*(X, ℒ)` is generated over `S₀` in degrees
`1`, `2`, `3` (`exists_generators_le_three`, the first two paragraphs of the source), so its sixth
Veronese subring is generated in degree one (`veroneseGeneratedInDegOne_six`), and that makes
`ℒ^{⊗ 6}` very ample
(`Stacks.VeroneseVeryAmple.isRelativelyVeryAmple_tensorPowModule_of_generators`,
the source's closing sentence, which runs through `X = Proj S` of [Stacks, Tag 0C6J]).
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_tensorPowModule_six_of_regularSection (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)]
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] (s : 𝟙_ X.Modules ⟶ L)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (hs : Mono s)
    (hH1 : IsZero (AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyOverField k f L 1)) (hample : IsAmple X L) :
    Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f (tensorPowModule X L (6 : ℤ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.VeryAmpleSquare.isRelativelyVeryAmple_tensorPowModule_two
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and `f : X ⟶ Spec k` proper with `X` of dimension `1` and
`H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`. Let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module which is globally generated, has
`H¹(X, ℒ) = 0`, and is ample. Then `ℒ^{⊗ 2}` is very ample relative to `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_tensorPowModule_two (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1)
    (hgg : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsGeneratedByGlobalSections L)
    (hH1 : IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f L 1)) (hample : IsAmple X L) :
    Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f (tensorPowModule X L 2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativelyVeryAmple_tensorPower_three_dualizingSheafOverField_and_isZero_cohomology_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E8X.** Let `X` be a proper scheme of dimension one over a field `k`
with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, of genus `g ≥ 2`, with at-worst-nodal singularities, and assume the
dualizing sheaf `ω_X` is ample. Then `ω_X^{⊗ 3}` is very ample and `H¹(X, ω_X^{⊗ 3}) = 0`.

`ω_X` is invertible since `X` is Gorenstein ([Stacks, Tag 0E37]). `X` has no rational tail, so
`ω_X^{⊗ 3}` is globally generated ([Stacks, Tag 0E3K]); its sections define a morphism to
projective space, which is a closed immersion once it is one after base change to `k̄`
([Stacks, Tag 02L6]). Over `k̄` the base change is again nodal of genus `g` with ample dualizing
sheaf the pullback of `ω_X` ([Stacks, Tag 0E32]), and `H¹(ℐ_Z ω^{⊗ 3}) = 0` for every degree-two
`Z` gives the criterion of [Stacks, Tag 0E8T].
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_tensorPower_three_dualizingSheafOverField_and_isZero_cohomology_one
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (hg : 2 ≤ genus (X ↘ Spec (.of k)))
    (hnodal : Stacks.Curves.HasAtWorstNodalSingularities k X)
    (hω : haveI := connectedSpace_of_isIso_globalSections k (X ↘ Spec (.of k))
      letI := isInvertible_dualizingSheafOverField_of_hasAtWorstNodalSingularities k X hdim hnodal
      Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField (X ↘ Spec (.of k)))) :
    haveI := connectedSpace_of_isIso_globalSections k (X ↘ Spec (.of k))
    letI := isInvertible_dualizingSheafOverField_of_hasAtWorstNodalSingularities k X hdim hnodal
    Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple (X ↘ Spec (.of k))
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2
          (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField (X ↘ Spec (.of k))) 3) ∧
      IsZero (cohomologyOverField k (X ↘ Spec (.of k))
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2
          (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField (X ↘ Spec (.of k))) 3) 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_iff_forall_isAlgebraicSpace_relocalizeRestrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E8Z, the algebraicity criterion.** Let `{jᵢ : Tᵢ ⟶ S}` be a finite family of open
immersions of a big fppf site whose images cover `S`. An fppf sheaf on the big fppf site of `S`
is an algebraic space over `S` exactly when its restriction along each `jᵢ` is an algebraic
space over `Tᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_iff_forall_isAlgebraicSpace_relocalizeRestrict [Finite I]
    (hj : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (B.inclusion.map (j i)))
    (hcov : ∀ x : S, ∃ i, x ∈ Set.range (B.inclusion.map (j i)))
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) F) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F ↔
      ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B (T i) (hT i) ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (j i)).obj F)
declarations.comment: algebraicity is detected on an open covering of the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentationSpacesOver.isEquivalence_glueingFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The algebraic spaces of finite presentation over a base covered by two opens `U` and `W`
with intersection `V` are the `2`-fibre product `FP_U ×_{FP_V} FP_W`.** The comparison functor
taking a space to its two restrictions together with their canonical identification over `V` is
an equivalence: it is faithful and full by the sheaf condition at the Mayer--Vietoris squares of
the covering, and essentially surjective because the space glued from a datum restricts back to
it.
declarations.statement: theorem isEquivalence_glueingFunctor : (glueingFunctor B S hS hV.w).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence clause: for an open covering of the base, base change is an equivalence onto the 2-fibre product of the categories of finite-presentation algebraic spaces over the two members. The criterion clause, that algebraicity is detected on such a covering, is `AlgebraicGeometry.isAlgebraicSpace_iff_forall_isAlgebraicSpace_relocalizeRestrict` in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.AlgebraicityOnBaseCover`, which this module imports, so the two clauses cannot live in one file

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentationSpacesOver.isEquivalence_glueingFunctor_of_colimit
declarations.doc:
**The algebraic spaces of finite presentation over the base are the `2`-fibre product
`FP_U ×_{FP_N} FP_M`, when `M` is a cofiltered limit of open neighbourhoods of the point
complementary to `U` and `N` is the corresponding limit of their intersections with `U`.**

This is Stacks 0E90 for `M = Spec O_{S,s}` and `N = Spec O_{S,s} ∖ {s}`, granted the two
colimit identifications carried as the hypotheses `hloc` and `hoverlap`: what the theorem proves
is the formal combination, namely that the comparison functor is faithful, full and essentially
surjective. Faithfulness and fullness come from the equivalence of Stacks 0E8Z at a single
neighbourhood, which applies because the complement of the point and any neighbourhood of it
cover the base; essential surjectivity needs in addition that a glueing datum descends to a
neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_glueingFunctor_of_colimit :
    (glueingFunctor B S hS hsq.w).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence, granted the two colimit identifications. The theorem is stated for an arbitrary object `M` of the site equipped with a cofiltered system of open neighbourhoods `W i` of the point complementary to `U`, and an object `N` over their intersections with `U`, such that base change exhibits `FP_M` as the cofiltered 2-colimit of the `FP_{W i}` and `FP_N` as that of the `FP_{W i ∩ U}`; these two statements are the hypotheses `hloc` and `hoverlap`. For `M = Spec O_{S,s}` they are what Stacks 07SK gives once the affine open neighbourhoods of `s` are known to have `Spec O_{S,s}` as their limit and the `W i ∩ U` to have its puncture as theirs — neither limit identification is available in this library, which is why the two colimit statements are carried as hypotheses rather than proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentationSpacesOver.isEquivalence_glueingFunctor_specStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E90.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `s` be a point of `S` and let `U` be an open of `S`
whose underlying set is the complement of `s` — so `s` is a closed point of `S` — with
quasi-compact inclusion morphism.  Then for every affine open neighbourhood `W₀` of `s` the
comparison functor
`FP_S ⥤ FP_U ×_{FP_V} FP_{Spec 𝒪_{S, s}}`
is an equivalence, where `FP_T` is the category of algebraic spaces of finite presentation over
`T` and `V` is the vertex of the system of overlaps, whose underlying scheme is the complement of
the closed point of `Spec 𝒪_{S, s}` — the tag's `V` —
by `AlgebraicGeometry.toScheme_obj_opensSpecStalkSiteObj_eq_compl_closedPoint`.

Every input is unconditional.  The two cartesian squares are
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_opensSpecStalkApex` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_opensSpecStalkStage`; the four compatibilities hold by terminality;
the colimit identification over the neighbourhoods is
`FinitePresentationSpacesOver.isFinitePresentationColimit_restrictedSpecStalkSiteCone`,
which has no hypothesis, and the one over the overlaps is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentationSpacesOver.isFinitePresentationColimit_opensSpecStalkSiteCone`,
whose single hypothesis is retrocompactness of `U` — the form the tag's quasi-compactness of
`U → S` takes, by `AlgebraicGeometry.isRetrocompact_of_quasiCompact_ι`.  Quasi-compactness of
`U → S` is used in that one place, exactly as in the tag's proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_glueingFunctor_specStalk (hUc : (U : Set S) = {s}ᶜ)
    (hqc : QuasiCompact U.ι) :
    (glueingFunctor B S hS (isPullback_opensSpecStalkApex B S hS s W₀ U).w).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence, unconditionally: for a point `s` of `S` whose complement is an open `U` with quasi-compact inclusion — the tag's closed point and quasi-compact `U → S` — the comparison functor `FP_S ⥤ FP_U ×_{FP_V} FP_{Spec O_{S,s}}` is an equivalence, with `V = Spec O_{S,s} ∖ {s}` the complement of the closed point, which the vertex of the system of overlaps is by `toScheme_obj_opensSpecStalkSiteObj_eq_compl_closedPoint`. The two colimit identifications that the general theorem `isEquivalence_glueingFunctor_of_colimit` carries as hypotheses are discharged here from Stacks 07SK and the identification of `Spec O_{S,s}` and of its puncture as the limits of the affine open neighbourhoods of `s` and of their intersections with `U`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentationSpacesOver.isGlueingColimitEquivalence_of_colimit
declarations.doc:
**The algebraic spaces of finite presentation over the opens between `U` and `S` containing
the point `s` have the `2`-fibre product `FP_U ×_{FP_V} FP_{Spec 𝒪_{S,s}}` as their filtered
`2`-colimit**, when `M` is a cofiltered limit of the stages `W i` and `N` the corresponding
limit of the `Wn i = U ∩ W i`, and the stages `Z i = U ∪ W i` are covered by `U` and `W i`.

This is Stacks 0E91. What the theorem proves is the formal combination: the comparison functors
`FP_{Z i} ⥤ FP_U ×_{FP_N} FP_M` are jointly essentially surjective, full and faithful in the
sense of an equivalence out of a filtered `2`-colimit, which is the content of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentationSpacesOver.IsGlueingColimitEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGlueingColimitEquivalence_of_colimit :
    IsGlueingColimitEquivalence B S hS Z jU jM
      (glueingSquare B S hS hsqW hjMW hpNU hpNW) hjUZ
      (glueingCone B S hS hjWZ hjMW hpM)
declarations.comment: the equivalence out of the filtered 2-colimit, in the concrete form: the comparison functors out of the stages are jointly essentially surjective, full and faithful. The 2-colimit category itself is not constructed. The theorem is stated for an arbitrary object `M` of the site equipped with a cofiltered system of opens `W i` under it, an object `N` over the system of the `Wn i`, and a system of stages `Z i` covered by `U` and `W i`, such that base change exhibits `FP_M` as the cofiltered 2-colimit of the `FP_{W i}` and `FP_N` as that of the `FP_{Wn i}` — the hypotheses `hloc` and `hoverlap`. For `M = Spec O_{S,s}`, `W i` the affine open neighbourhoods of `s`, `Wn i = W i ∩ U` and `Z i = U ∪ W i` these two are what Stacks 07SK gives once the `W i` are known to have `Spec O_{S,s}` as their limit and the `Wn i` to have `V = Spec O_{S,s} ∩ U` as theirs — the `Wn i` being quasi-compact because `U` is retrocompact in `S`. Neither limit identification is available in this library, which is why the two colimit statements are carried as hypotheses rather than proved; `hstage` is Stacks 0E8Z at the stage `Z i`, which this library proves only for a base that is terminal in the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentationSpacesOver.isEquivalence_specStalkStageColimitFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, `U` a retrocompact open of `S` and `s` a point of `S`, and put
`V = Spec 𝒪_{S, s} ∩ U`. Then the comparison functor
`colim_{s ∈ U' ⊇ U open} FP_{U'} ⟶ FP_U ×_{FP_V} FP_{Spec 𝒪_{S, s}}`
is an equivalence of categories.

The colimit is the category `StageColimit` over the stages `U ∪ W`, `W` running over the affine
open neighbourhoods of `s` contained in `W₀`. The first two clauses say that the stages are
cofinal among the opens `U'` of `S` with `U ⊆ U'` and `s ∈ U'`; the third and fourth identify
the remaining vertices of the `2`-fibre product as `Spec 𝒪_{S, s}` and as `V`, the preimage of
`U` in `Spec 𝒪_{S, s}`; the fifth is the equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_specStalkStageColimitFunctor (hU : IsRetrocompact (U : Set S)) :
    (∀ j : Over W₀, U ≤ U ⊔ j.left.obj.1 ∧ s ∈ U ⊔ j.left.obj.1) ∧
      (∀ U' : S.Opens, U ≤ U' → s ∈ U' → ∃ j : Over W₀, U ⊔ j.left.obj.1 ≤ U') ∧
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (restrictedSpecStalkSiteCone B S hS s W₀).pt =
            Spec (S.presheaf.stalk s) ∧
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (opensSpecStalkSiteObj B S hS s W₀ U) =
              (S.fromSpecStalk s ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme ∧
            (specStalkStageColimitFunctor B S hS s W₀ U).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence of categories out of the filtered 2-colimit. The colimit of the categories `FP_{U ∪ W}` is the category `StageColimit` — objects the spaces over a stage, morphisms the germs — and the comparison functor `specStalkStageColimitFunctor` out of it to `FP_U ×_{FP_V} FP_{Spec O_{S,s}}` is full, faithful and essentially surjective, which is the fifth clause. The colimit runs over the stages `U ∪ W`, `W` an affine open neighbourhood of `s` inside a fixed one; the first two clauses say these are a cofinal family among the tag's opens `U'` with `U ⊆ U'` and `s ∈ U'`, so the colimit is the tag's. The third and fourth clauses pin the other two vertices: `Spec O_{S,s}`, and `V` as the preimage of `U` in it. The sole hypothesis is the tag's, that `U` is retrocompact in `S`; the tag's `s ∉ U` is unused, so the statement covers it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentationSpacesOver.ClosedPointsGlueingData.essSurj_comparisonFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E92, essential surjectivity of the comparison functor, granted the case `n = 1`.**
Every object of the `n`-fold `2`-fibre product — an algebraic space of finite presentation over
the open part, a family of such over the local parts, and a family of identifications over the
overlaps — is, up to isomorphism, the image of an algebraic space of finite presentation over
the base, as soon as the glueing data admits a tower of splittings whose binary comparison
functors are essentially surjective. The induction splits off the last point by one such
comparison functor and applies the induction hypothesis to the remaining points.
declarations.statement:
theorem essSurj_comparisonFunctor :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (D : ClosedPointsGlueingData B S hS n), Solvable n D →
      D.comparisonFunctor.EssSurj
declarations.comment: the comparison functor, and its essential surjectivity granted the case n = 1 of the lemma — that is, Stacks 0E90 — at each step of a tower of intermediate bases, carried as the hypothesis `Solvable`. The target is the iso-comma category of the two functors into `∀ i, FP_{Uᵢ}` assembled from the base changes, which is the 2-fibre product the lemma names. Full faithfulness, and hence that the functor is an equivalence, is NOT proved: the proof of Stacks 0E92 omits it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentationSpacesOver.isEquivalence_comparisonFunctor_closedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E92.** Let `S` be a scheme of a big fppf site and let `s₁, …, sₙ` be pairwise
distinct closed points of `S` such that `U = S ∖ {s₁, …, sₙ} ⟶ S` is quasi-compact. With
`Sᵢ = Spec 𝒪_{S,sᵢ}` and `Uᵢ = Sᵢ ∖ {sᵢ}`, the comparison functor
`FP_S ⥤ FP_U ×_{(FP_{U₁} × ⋯ × FP_{Uₙ})} (FP_{S₁} × ⋯ × FP_{Sₙ})`,
taking an algebraic space of finite presentation over `S` to its base change to `U`, the family
of its base changes to the `Sᵢ` and the family of the canonical identifications of their base
changes to the `Uᵢ`, is an equivalence of categories. Here `FP_T` is the category of algebraic
spaces of finite presentation over `T`, and the `2`-fibre product is the iso-comma category of
the two functors into `∀ i, FP_{Uᵢ}` assembled from the base changes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_comparisonFunctor_closedPoints {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → S)
    (hinj : Function.Injective s) (hs : ∀ i, IsClosed ({s i} : Set S)) (U : S.Opens)
    (hU : (U : Set S) = (Set.range s)ᶜ) (hqc : QuasiCompact U.ι) :
    (closedPointsGlueingData B S hS s hs U hU).comparisonFunctor.IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SpacesOverSpace.finiteTypeBaseChange_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E93**, the first equivalence: finite type morphisms of algebraic spaces `X ⟶ T`,
with isomorphisms over `T`, are equivalent through base change to the functors over the site from
the algebraic stack `𝒮_T` of `T` to the stack `Spaces'_ft` of finite type families of algebraic
spaces.
declarations.statement: theorem finiteTypeBaseChange_isEquivalence : (finiteTypeBaseChange B S hS T).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the first equivalence: finite type morphisms X ⟶ T and functors 𝒮_T ⟶ Spaces'_ft

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SpacesOverSpace.properFlatBaseChange_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E93**, the second equivalence: finitely presented, flat and proper morphisms of
algebraic spaces `X ⟶ T`, with isomorphisms over `T`, are equivalent through base change to the
functors over the site from the algebraic stack `𝒮_T` of `T` to the stack
`Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}` of finitely presented, flat and proper families.
declarations.statement: theorem properFlatBaseChange_isEquivalence : (properFlatBaseChange B S hS T).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the second equivalence: finitely presented, flat and proper morphisms X ⟶ T and functors 𝒮_T ⟶ Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SpacesOverSpace.spacesOverSpace_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E93.** Base change along the points of an algebraic space `T` gives an equivalence
of finite type morphisms `X ⟶ T` with the functors over the site from `𝒮_T` to `Spaces'_ft`, and an
equivalence of finitely presented, flat and proper morphisms `X ⟶ T` with the functors over the
site from `𝒮_T` to `Spaces'_{fp, flat, proper}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem spacesOverSpace_isEquivalence :
    (finiteTypeBaseChange B S hS T).IsEquivalence ∧
      (properFlatBaseChange B S hS T).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: both equivalences

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.PolarizedOverSpace.polarizedBaseChange_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Let `T` be an algebraic space over `Spec(ℤ)` and `𝒮_T` its algebraic stack. Base change is an
equivalence from the category of pairs `(X ⟶ T, L)`, where `X ⟶ T` is a proper, flat and finitely
presented morphism of algebraic spaces and `L` is an invertible module ample on `X/T`, to the
category of functors over the site from `𝒮_T` to `Polarized`
(`Mor_{Cat/Sch_fppf}(𝒮_T, Polarized)`).
declarations.statement: theorem polarizedBaseChange_isEquivalence : (polarizedBaseChange B T).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: base change is an equivalence of the polarized proper flat finitely presented spaces over T with Mor_{Cat/Sch_fppf}(S_T, Polarized)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_denseTestUniqueness
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E95.** Let
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `h : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`, with `𝒴` locally
Noetherian, `f` locally of finite type and quasi-separated, `h` of finite type and the image of
`|h|` dense in `|𝒳|`. If every discrete valuative square for `f` through `h` has a category of
dotted arrows which is either empty or a setoid with exactly one isomorphism class, then `f` is
separated.

`Δ_f` is separated by the first case applied to `Δ_f` and `h`: the relative diagonal of `Δ_f` is
separated because `Δ_f` is representable by algebraic spaces (Stacks 04YQ part (4), read in the
sense of Stacks 04YW by Stacks 04YS), `Δ_{Δ_f}` is quasi-compact because `Δ_f` is
quasi-separated (Stacks 04YZ part (2) and Stacks 050T), and the hypothesis passes from `f` to
`Δ_f` by Stacks 0E8L. Then the first case applies to `f` and `h`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_denseTestUniqueness
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (h : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hY : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒴)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hh : IsFiniteType B S hS h)
    (hdense : letI := Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val;
      Dense (Set.range (Stack.pointsMap B S hS 𝒰.val.val 𝒰.val.property 𝒳.val.property
        h.hom.hom)))
    (hu : ValuativeCriterion.DenseTestUniqueness B S hS h f) :
    IsSeparated B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_discreteUniquenessAlong_of_dense
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0E95.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `h : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S`. Assume that `𝒴` is locally Noetherian, that `f` is locally of finite type and
quasi-separated, that `h` is of finite type, and that the image of `|h| : |𝒰| ⟶ |𝒳|` is dense in
`|𝒳|`. If for every 2-commutative diagram for `f` over a discrete valuation ring `A` with fraction
field `K` whose generic point is `h ∘ u` for some `u : Spec K ⟶ 𝒰`, the category of dotted arrows
is either empty or a setoid with exactly one isomorphism class, then `f` is separated.

The hypothesis on dotted arrows is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteUniquenessAlong`. The proof is the source's:
the first case (`isSeparated_of_isSeparated_relativeDiagonal_of_discreteUniquenessAlong`) applied
to `Δ_f` in place of `f` shows that `Δ_f` is separated, and the first case applied to `f`
concludes. For the first application, `Δ_f` is representable by algebraic spaces, so every
category of dotted arrows of a diagram for `Δ_f` is a setoid (Stacks 0E8L, Stacks 0CLC), whence
`Δ_{Δ_f}` is separated; uniqueness along `h` passes from `f` to `Δ_f` by Stacks 0E8L; `Δ_f` is
quasi-separated because `f` is; and `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` is locally Noetherian (Stacks 06R6).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_discreteUniquenessAlong_of_dense
    {𝒰 𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (h : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒴 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒴)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hh : IsFiniteType B S hS h)
    (hdense : @Dense _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val) (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS h)))
    (huniq : ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteUniquenessAlong B S hS h f) :
    IsSeparated B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.noetherianSpace_of_isHilbertPolarizedPoint
declarations.doc:
Let `n ∈ ℕ`, let `P ∈ ℚ[t]` and let `T ⊆ |𝒫olarized|` be a set of points each represented
over a field by a polarized proper scheme `(X, ℒ)` satisfying conditions (1) and (2)
(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsHilbertPolarizedOver`): the Hilbert polynomial of `ℒ` on `X` is `P`, and
there is a closed immersion `i : X ⟶ ℙⁿ` over the base with `i^*𝒪(1) ≅ ℒ`. Then `T` is a
Noetherian topological space, in particular quasi-compact. The source's hypotheses `n ≥ 1` and
that `P` is numerical are not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherianSpace_of_isHilbertPolarizedPoint (hT : IsTerminal (B.obj hS)) (n : ℕ)
    (P : Polynomial ℚ)
    (T : Set (Stack.points B S hS (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT).val
      (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT).property))
    (hTP : ∀ ξ ∈ T, ∃ p, Stack.pointClass B S hS _ _ p = ξ ∧
      IsHilbertPolarizedPoint B hS hT n P p) :
    letI := Stack.pointTopology B S hS (polarizedStackUnconditional B hS hT)
    NoetherianSpace T

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.existsUnique_isModelHom_iso_of_isStableFamilyOfSchemesOfGenus
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field `K` and `C` a smooth proper curve over
`K` with `K = H⁰(C, 𝒪_C)` and genus `g`. If `X` and `X'` are models of `C` (Section 0C2R) which are
stable families of genus `g` curves over `R`, then there exists a unique isomorphism of models
`X ≅ X'`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.stableReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E98** (stable reduction, [DM, Corollary 2.7]). Let `R` be a discrete
valuation ring with fraction field `K` and let `C` be a smooth projective curve over `K` with
`H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K` and genus `g ≥ 2`. Let `B` be a big fppf site containing `Spec R`. Then

1. there exist an extension of discrete valuation rings `R ⊆ R'` inducing a finite separable
   extension of fraction fields `K'/K` and a stable family of curves `Y ⟶ Spec R'` of genus `g`
   with `Y_{K'} ≅ C_{K'}` over `K'`, and
2. there exist a finite separable extension `L/K` and a stable family of curves `Y ⟶ Spec A` of
   genus `g`, where `A ⊆ L` is the integral closure of `R` in `L`, such that `Y_L ≅ C_L` over
   `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stableReduction (R K : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K] {C : Scheme.{u}} (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c] (hproj : IsProjective c)
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ c.appTop)] (hg : 2 ≤ genus c) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hZ : B.Contains integerBase) (hR : B.Contains (Spec (.of R))) :
    (∃ (K' : Type u) (_ : Field K') (_ : Algebra K K') (_ : Algebra R K')
      (_ : IsScalarTower R K K'), FiniteDimensional K K' ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K K' ∧
      ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : IsDomain R') (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R')
        (_ : Algebra R' K') (_ : IsFractionRing R' K') (_ : Algebra R R')
        (_ : IsScalarTower R R' K'), IsLocalHom (algebraMap R R') ∧
        ∃ (hR' : B.Contains (Spec (.of R'))) (Y : Scheme.{u}) (p : Y ⟶ Spec (.of R')),
          IsStableFamilyOfSchemesOfGenus B hZ (genus c) p hR' ∧
          Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R' K')))) ≅
            Over.mk (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K')))))) ∧
    (∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra K L) (_ : Algebra R L)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R K L), FiniteDimensional K L ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K L ∧
      ∃ (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of (integralClosure R L)))) (Y : Scheme.{u})
        (p : Y ⟶ Spec (.of (integralClosure R L))),
        IsStableFamilyOfSchemesOfGenus B hZ (genus c) p hA ∧
        Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd p
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (integralClosure R L) L)))) ≅
          Over.mk (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_moduliStableCurvesOfGenus_unconditional
declarations.doc:
Let `g ≥ 2`. The stack `𝓜̄_g` is separated: the morphism `𝓜̄_g → Spec(ℤ)` (the inclusion of
the open substack of stable families of genus `g` into the small model of the algebraic stack
`Curves`, followed by its structure morphism) is separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_moduliStableCurvesOfGenus_unconditional (g : ℕ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) :
    Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B integerBase hZ
      ((curvesSmallOpenSubstack B hZ
          (curvesFiberedCategory_isAlgebraicStack.{u, u + 1} B hZ)
          (isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamilyOfGenus_unconditional B hZ g)).inclusion ≫
        Stack.structureMorphism B integerBase hZ (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
          (curvesFiberedCategory_isAlgebraicStack.{u, u + 1} B hZ)))
declarations.comment: g ≥ 2 (hg); 𝓜̄_g → Spec(ℤ) is separated, which is what the source says the statement means; nothing is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_points_moduliStableCurvesOfGenusSmall
declarations.doc:
Let `g ≥ 2`. The moduli stack `𝓜̄_g` of stable curves of genus `g` is
quasi-compact: the space of points of its small model
`AlgebraicGeometry.moduliStableCurvesOfGenusSmall` (Stacks 04XG), with the topology of
Stacks 04XL, is compact. This is quasi-compactness of an algebraic stack in the sense of
Stacks 04YB (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsQuasiCompactStack`, which is this `CompactSpace`).
declarations.statement:
theorem compactSpace_points_moduliStableCurvesOfGenusSmall (g : ℕ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) :
    @CompactSpace (Stack.points B integerBase hZ (moduliStableCurvesOfGenusSmall B hZ g).val
      (moduliStableCurvesOfGenusSmall B hZ g).property)
      (Stack.pointTopology B integerBase hZ (moduliStableCurvesOfGenusSmall B hZ g))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.moduliStableCurves_isDeligneMumford_proper_smooth
declarations.doc:
Let `g ≥ 2`. The algebraic stack `𝓜̄_g` is a Deligne–Mumford stack, proper and smooth over
`Spec(ℤ)`. Moreover, the locus `𝓜_g` parametrizing smooth curves is a dense open substack.

Here `𝓜̄_g` is the open substack of the algebraic stack of curves (Stacks 0D5A) cut out by the
stable families of genus `g` (Stacks 0E78), and `𝓜_g` the one cut out by the families smooth of
relative dimension one with `f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_S` universally and of genus `g` (Stacks 0E83); the
conjuncts are: `𝓜̄_g` is Deligne–Mumford, `𝓜̄_g → Spec(ℤ)` is proper, it is smooth, and `𝓜_g`
is contained in `𝓜̄_g` (so it is an open substack of `𝓜̄_g`) with points dense in `|𝓜̄_g|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduliStableCurves_isDeligneMumford_proper_smooth (g : ℕ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) :
    Stack.IsDeligneMumfordStack.{u, u + 1} B integerBase hZ
        (curvesSmallOpenSubstack B hZ
          (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, u + 1} B hZ)
          (isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamilyOfGenus_of_isStable B hZ
            (C1590Private.isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamily B hZ)
            g)).toAlgebraicStack.val.val ∧
      Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsProper B integerBase hZ
        ((curvesSmallOpenSubstack B hZ
            (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, u + 1} B hZ)
            (isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamilyOfGenus_of_isStable B hZ
              (C1590Private.isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamily B hZ) g)).inclusion ≫
          Stack.structureMorphism B integerBase hZ (curvesAlgebraicStack B hZ
            (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, u + 1} B hZ))) ∧
      IsSmoothOverIntegers B hZ
        (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, u + 1} B hZ)
        (isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamilyOfGenus_of_isStable B hZ
          (C1590Private.isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamily B hZ) g) ∧
      ∃ hle : (curvesSmallOpenSubstack B hZ
            (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, u + 1} B hZ)
            (isOpenCurvesLocus_isSmoothH0FamilyOfGenus_of_isStable B hZ
              (C1590Private.isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamily B hZ) hg)).property ≤
          (curvesSmallOpenSubstack B hZ
            (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, u + 1} B hZ)
            (isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamilyOfGenus_of_isStable B hZ
              (C1590Private.isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamily B hZ) g)).property,
        @Dense _ (Stack.pointTopology B integerBase hZ
            (curvesSmallOpenSubstack B hZ
              (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, u + 1} B hZ)
              (isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamilyOfGenus_of_isStable B hZ
                (C1590Private.isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamily B hZ)
                g)).toAlgebraicStack.val)
          (Set.range (Stack.AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B integerBase hZ
            (Stack.OpenSubstack.homOfLE B integerBase hZ
              (curvesSmallOpenSubstack B hZ
                (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, u + 1} B hZ)
                (isOpenCurvesLocus_isSmoothH0FamilyOfGenus_of_isStable B hZ
                  (C1590Private.isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamily B hZ) hg))
              (curvesSmallOpenSubstack B hZ
                (C1590Private.isAlgebraicStack_curvesFiberedCategory.{u, u + 1} B hZ)
                (isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamilyOfGenus_of_isStable B hZ
                  (C1590Private.isOpenCurvesLocus_isStableCurveFamily B hZ) g))
                hle)))
declarations.comment: g ≥ 2 (hg); 𝓜̄_g is Deligne–Mumford, proper and smooth over Spec(ℤ), and 𝓜_g is an open substack of 𝓜̄_g whose points are dense in |𝓜̄_g|; nothing is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_unit_restrict_pushforward_of_depth_ge_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E9I.** A coherent sheaf with depth at least two along the
complement of an open subscheme is canonically the pushforward of its restriction.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_unit_restrict_pushforward_of_depth_ge_two
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (U : X.Opens)
    (hdepth : ∀ x : X, x ∉ (U : Set X) →
      let M := TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x
      letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x) M :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          F.val x
      (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) M) :
    IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction U.ι).unit.app F)
declarations.comment: canonical sheaf isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.restriction_bijective_of_depth_ge_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E9I.** Under the same depth hypothesis, every section on
the open subscheme extends uniquely to a global section.
declarations.statement:
theorem restriction_bijective_of_depth_ge_two
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (U : X.Opens)
    (hdepth : ∀ x : X, x ∉ (U : Set X) →
      let M := TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x
      letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x) M :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          F.val x
      (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) M) :
    Function.Bijective
      (F.presheaf.map (homOfLE (show U ≤ (⊤ : X.Opens) from le_top)).op)
declarations.comment: global sections

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_natIso_dualizingDerivedHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E9L] for an arbitrary finite-type `φ`, as an isomorphism of functors on
`D_Coh(A)`.**  Let `φ : A →+* B` be a homomorphism of finite type with `A` Noetherian, let `p` be
any polynomial presentation of `φ` and let `ω` be a dualizing complex for `A`.  Write `φ^!` for
the algebraic upper shriek functor of `p`, put `ω_B = φ^!(ω)`, `D_A(-) = RHom_A(-, ω)` and
`D_B(-) = RHom_B(-, ω_B)`.  Then

`φ^!(K) ≅ D_B(D_A(K) ⊗_A^L B)`

as an isomorphism of functors on `D_Coh(A)`.

**No surjectivity, and no projection-formula keystone.**  The surjective case is
`Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_natIso_dualizingDerivedHom_of_surjective`; the passage to a general
finite-type `φ` is made here by reading that statement's engine — the tag for derived coextension
of scalars along an arbitrary ring homomorphism — at the object `K ⊗_A^L P` over the polynomial
algebra of the presentation, and feeding it the flat base change of derived Hom along `A → P`.
That base change is the unconditional [Stacks, Tag 0A6A], not the Tor-independent square of
[Stacks, Tag 0BZM]; so unlike [Stacks, Tag 0BZT] in general
(`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.exists_upperShriekComp_of_finiteType`) this carries no
`Dualizing.KFlatAlgebraActionEq`.  See the module documentation for the chain.

The derived base change `- ⊗_A^L B` is the chosen model; for an arbitrary model see
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_natIso_dualizingDerivedHom_model`.
The statement is a `Nonempty` because the adjunction of [Stacks, Tag 0A70] that the engine
consumes is itself only known to exist.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_natIso_dualizingDerivedHom [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (p : PolynomialPresentation φ) (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω) :
    Nonempty ((hasFiniteCohomology.{u, u} A).ι ⋙ p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, u} ≅
      (hasFiniteCohomology.{u, u} A).ι ⋙ dualizingBaseChangeFunctor.{u, u} φ
        (totalDerivedExtension φ) ω (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, u}.obj ω))
declarations.comment: in general: an arbitrary finite-type φ of Noetherian rings at an arbitrary polynomial presentation, as an isomorphism of functors on D_Coh(A), with no surjectivity and no projection-formula keystone

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_natIso_dualizingDerivedHom_model
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E9L] in general, at an arbitrary model of derived base change.**  This is
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_natIso_dualizingDerivedHom` with the
chosen model of `- ⊗_A^L B` replaced by an arbitrary one.  Two models of derived extension of
scalars along `φ` are isomorphic by uniqueness of the total left derived functor,
`CategoryTheory.Functor.leftDerivedNatIso`, and
`Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.dualizingBaseChangeFunctorIsoOfModelIso` carries that
isomorphism into the right-hand side of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_natIso_dualizingDerivedHom_model [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (p : PolynomialPresentation φ)
    (E : CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.TotalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, u,
      u + 1, u + 1} φ)
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω) :
    Nonempty ((hasFiniteCohomology.{u, u} A).ι ⋙ p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, u} ≅
      (hasFiniteCohomology.{u, u} A).ι ⋙ dualizingBaseChangeFunctor.{u, u} φ E ω
        (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, u}.obj ω))
declarations.comment: in general, at an arbitrary model of derived base change as well as an arbitrary polynomial presentation

declarations.name: Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_localization_isNormalizedDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
Let `φ : R → A` be a finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings with `R` local, and let
`m ⊆ A` be a maximal ideal lying over the maximal ideal of `R`.  If `ω_R` is a normalized
dualizing complex for `R`, then `φ^!(ω_R)_m` is a normalized dualizing complex for `A_m`, for
every polynomial presentation of `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PolynomialPresentation.upperShriekFunctor_localization_isNormalizedDualizingComplex
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsLocalRing R] {f : R →+* A} (p : PolynomialPresentation f)
    (m : Ideal A) [m.IsMaximal] (hlies : m.comap f = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} K) :
    IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u}
      ((StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.derivedExtensionScalars
        (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime m))).obj (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, u}.obj K))

declarations.name: Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_neg_relativeDimensionAt_le_of_nontrivial_localizedHomology
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E9P].** Let `R → A` be a finite type homomorphism of Noetherian rings, let
`𝔮 ⊂ A` be a prime and let `d` be the dimension at `𝔮` of the fibre of `Spec(A) → Spec(R)` over
the prime below `𝔮`.  If the localization at `𝔮` of `H^i(ω^•_{A/R})` is nonzero then `-d ≤ i`.
Here `ω^•_{A/R} = f^!(R)` is computed from an arbitrary polynomial presentation of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_neg_relativeDimensionAt_le_of_nontrivial_localizedHomology
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Algebra R A] (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A))
    (q : PrimeSpectrum A) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R q.asIdeal = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (i : ℤ) :
    Nontrivial
        (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj
            (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
                (ModuleCat.of R R))))) →
      -(d : ℤ) ≤ i
declarations.comment: for the upper shriek functor of an arbitrary polynomial presentation of the homomorphism, the relative dualizing complex being well defined only up to isomorphism, and with the fibre dimension named by a hypothesis identifying it with a natural number

declarations.name: Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_relativeDimensionAt_bounds_of_nontrivial_localizedHomology
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E9Q], the local bounds.** Let `R → A` be a flat finite type homomorphism of
Noetherian rings, let `𝔮 ⊂ A` be a prime and let `d` be the dimension at `𝔮` of the fibre of
`Spec(A) → Spec(R)` over the prime below `𝔮`.  If the localization at `𝔮` of `H^i(ω^•_{A/R})` is
nonzero then `-d ≤ i ≤ 0`.  Here `ω^•_{A/R} = f^!(R)` is computed from an arbitrary polynomial
presentation of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_relativeDimensionAt_bounds_of_nontrivial_localizedHomology
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Algebra R A] [Module.Flat R A] (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A))
    (q : PrimeSpectrum A) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : Algebra.relativeDimensionAt R q.asIdeal = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (i : ℤ) :
    Nontrivial
        (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj
            (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
                (ModuleCat.of R R))))) →
      -(d : ℤ) ≤ i ∧ i ≤ 0
declarations.comment: the local bounds: H^i(omega)_q nonzero implies -d <= i <= 0, d the dimension at q of the fibre through q, for the upper shriek functor of an arbitrary polynomial presentation of the homomorphism, the relative dualizing complex being well defined only up to isomorphism; the Tor amplitude clause is Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_hasTorAmplitude_of_fiber_dimension_le

declarations.name: Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_hasTorAmplitude_of_fiber_dimension_le
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E9Q], the Tor amplitude clause.**  Let `R → A` be a flat finite type
homomorphism of Noetherian rings.  If all fibres of `Spec(A) → Spec(R)` have dimension at most
`d`, then `ω^•_{A/R}` has Tor amplitude in `[-d, 0]` as a complex of `R`-modules.

Here `ω^•_{A/R} = f^!(R)` is read at an arbitrary polynomial presentation of `R → A`, being
defined only up to isomorphism, and Tor amplitude is read at the canonical certified derived
tensor product of `R`.  Nothing is carried.  Following the source, the Tor test at a finitely
presented module `M` is the cohomology of `ω^•_{A/R} ⊗_R^L (R ⊕ M)`, a base change to a Noetherian
ring whose fibres have dimension at most `d`: that is
`Dualizing.isZero_homology_totalDerivedExtensionScalars_upperShriekFunctor_of_lt`, proved by
computing the base change on a finite projective resolution of `A` over the polynomial algebra,
which needs no comparison of `A`-linear structures; arbitrary modules are filtered colimits of
finitely presented ones.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_hasTorAmplitude_of_fiber_dimension_le
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Algebra R A] [Module.Flat R A] (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A)) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : ∀ 𝔭 : AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of R),
      topologicalKrullDim ((AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A))).fiber 𝔭) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude
      (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.canonicalCertifiedDerivedTensoring R).tensor
      (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.canonicalCertifiedDerivedTensoring R).comparison
      (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.canonicalCertifiedDerivedTensoring R).isLeftDerived
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R A)).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R))))
      (-(d : ℤ)) 0
declarations.comment: the Tor amplitude clause: if all fibres of Spec(A) -> Spec(R) have dimension at most d then the relative dualizing complex has Tor amplitude in [-d, 0] over R; the relative dualizing complex is read at the upper shriek functor of an arbitrary polynomial presentation of the homomorphism, being well defined only up to isomorphism

declarations.name: Dualizing.le_of_nontrivial_localizedModule_homology_relativeDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E9R], the vanishing.**  Let `R → A` be a finite type homomorphism of
Noetherian rings and let `𝔭 ⊂ R` be a prime.  Assume that `R_𝔭` is Cohen--Macaulay and that
`trdeg_{κ(R ∩ 𝔮)} κ(𝔮) ≤ r` for every minimal prime `𝔮 ⊂ A`.  Then

`H^i(ω^•_{A/R})_𝔭 ≠ 0 ⟹ -r ≤ i` .

Here `ω^•_{A/R} = φ^!(R)` is the relative dualizing complex, computed from an arbitrary polynomial
presentation `p` of `R → A` (it is well defined only up to isomorphism, so the statement is made
for every presentation), and the localization at `𝔭` is the localization of the `A`-module at the
image of `R ∖ 𝔭`.

The proof does not go through a dualizing complex of `R_𝔭`.  At a prime `𝔮 ⊂ A` over a prime
contained in `𝔭`, the localization of `H^i(ω^•_{A/R})` is `Ext^{i+n}_{P_𝔯}(A_𝔯, P_𝔯)`, where
`P_𝔯` is Cohen--Macaulay and `depth_{I}(P_𝔯) ≥ n - r` by the dimension formula; see
`Dualizing.subsingleton_and_min_two_le_moduleDepth_localizedModule_homology_upperShriek`.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_of_nontrivial_localizedModule_homology_relativeDualizingComplex
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Algebra R A] (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A)) (𝔭 : Ideal R) [𝔭.IsPrime]
    (hCM : IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭)) (r : ℕ)
    (htrdeg : ∀ (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime], q ∈ minimalPrimes A →
      letI := Ideal.ResidueField.algebraOfLiesOver (q.under R) q
      Algebra.trdeg (q.under R).ResidueField q.ResidueField ≤ r)
    (i : ℤ) :
    Nontrivial (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.map (algebraMap R A) 𝔭.primeCompl)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj
        (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R))))) →
      -(r : ℤ) ≤ i
declarations.comment: the vanishing H^i(ω_{A/R})_𝔭 = 0 for i < -r, in full

declarations.name: Dualizing.propertySkModule_localizedModule_homology_relativeDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E9R], the `(S₂)` clause.**  Let `R → A` be a finite type homomorphism of
Noetherian rings and let `𝔭 ⊂ R` be a prime.  Assume that `R_𝔭` is Cohen--Macaulay and that
`trdeg_{κ(R ∩ 𝔮)} κ(𝔮) ≤ r` for every minimal prime `𝔮 ⊂ A`.  Then `H^{-r}(ω^•_{A/R})_𝔭`
satisfies Serre's condition `(S₂)` as an `A_𝔭`-module, where `A_𝔭` is the localization of `A` at
the image of `R ∖ 𝔭`.

As in `Dualizing.le_of_nontrivial_localizedModule_homology_relativeDualizingComplex`,
`ω^•_{A/R} = φ^!(R)` is computed from an arbitrary polynomial presentation `p`. At a prime `𝔮`
of `A_𝔭`, the module is `Ext^{n-r}_{P_𝔯}(A_𝔯, P_𝔯)` with `P_𝔯` Cohen--Macaulay and
`n - r ≤ depth_I(P_𝔯)`, and such an `Ext` satisfies `(S₂)`
(`Dualizing.min_two_le_moduleDepth_ext_of_le_depth`).
declarations.statement:
theorem propertySkModule_localizedModule_homology_relativeDualizingComplex
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Algebra R A] (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R A)) (𝔭 : Ideal R) [𝔭.IsPrime]
    (hCM : IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭)) (r : ℕ)
    (htrdeg : ∀ (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime], q ∈ minimalPrimes A →
      letI := Ideal.ResidueField.algebraOfLiesOver (q.under R) q
      Algebra.trdeg (q.under R).ResidueField q.ResidueField ≤ r) :
    letI : Module.Finite A ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (-(r : ℤ))).obj
        (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)))) :=
      finite_homology_upperShriekFunctor p _
    PropertySkModule (Localization (Submonoid.map (algebraMap R A) 𝔭.primeCompl))
      (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.map (algebraMap R A) 𝔭.primeCompl)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (-(r : ℤ))).obj
          (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, 0}.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of R R))))) 2
declarations.comment: the (S_2) clause, H^{-r}(ω_{A/R})_𝔭 is (S_2) as an A_𝔭-module, in full

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange_restrict_comm
declarations.doc:
**The restriction of the base change map to `U'`, as a commutative square.** For a Tor
independent cartesian square of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes and quasi-compact opens
`V ⊆ Y`, `V' ⊆ Y'` with `g(V') ⊆ V`, write `γ` for the base change map of [Stacks, Tag 0AA6],
`γ_V` for that of the square of opens `U' ⟶ U` over `V' ⟶ V`, and `ρ`, `ρ'` for the maps of
[Stacks, Tag 0A9L] for `U ⊆ X` over `V ⊆ Y` and `U' ⊆ X'` over `V' ⊆ Y'`. Then
```
γ(K)|_{U'} ≫ ρ'(Lg^* K) ≫ a_{U'}((Lg^*K)|_{V'} ≅ L(g|)^*(K|_V))
  = ((L(g')^* a(K))|_{U'} ≅ L(g'|)^*(a(K)|_U)) ≫ L(g'|)^* ρ(K) ≫ γ_V(K|_V).
```
declarations.statement:
theorem torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange_restrict_comm
    (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y) :
    Rs[(f' ⁻¹ᵁ V').ι].map ((torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange sq hTor).app K) ≫
        (qcqsTwistedInverseImageRestrictionMap f' V').app (Lq[g].obj K) ≫
        a[f' ∣_ V'].map ((quasiCoherentDerivedRestrictPullbackIso V.ι V'.ι (g.resLE V V' hVV') g
          (Scheme.Hom.resLE_comp_ι g hVV').symm).hom.app K) =
      (quasiCoherentDerivedRestrictPullbackIso (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι (f' ⁻¹ᵁ V').ι
          (g'.resLE (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (f' ⁻¹ᵁ V')
            (preimage_le_of_comm sq.w hVV')) g'
          (Scheme.Hom.resLE_comp_ι g'
            (preimage_le_of_comm sq.w hVV')).symm).hom.app
          (a[f].obj K) ≫
        Lq[g'.resLE (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (f' ⁻¹ᵁ V')
            (preimage_le_of_comm sq.w hVV')].map
          ((qcqsTwistedInverseImageRestrictionMap f V).app K) ≫
        (torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange (isPullback_restrictBasesSquare sq V hVV')
          (torIndependent_morphismRestrict_resLE f g hTor hVV')).app (Rs[V.ι].obj K)
declarations.comment: the commutative square of maps exhibiting the isomorphism: the two maps of 0A9L and the identifications of restriction with derived pullback carry the restriction to U' of the base change map 0AA6 to that of the square of opens

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChangeRestrictArrowIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E9S].** Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact and quasi-separated
schemes
```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```
with `f` and `g` Tor independent, and quasi-compact (for instance affine) opens `V ⊆ Y`,
`V' ⊆ Y'` with `g(V') ⊆ V`; set `U = f⁻¹(V)`, `U' = (f')⁻¹(V')`. Assume that the map of
[Stacks, Tag 0A9L] for `U ⊆ X` over `V ⊆ Y` is an isomorphism at `K`, and that for `U' ⊆ X'` over
`V' ⊆ Y'` it is an isomorphism at `Lg^* K`. Then the restriction to `U'` of the base change map
`L(g')^* a(K) ⟶ a'(Lg^* K)` of [Stacks, Tag 0AA6] is isomorphic, as an arrow, to the base change
map of Tag 0AA6 for `K|_V` and the cartesian square `U' ⟶ U` over `V' ⟶ V`
(`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FlatBaseChangeCohomology.isPullback_restrictBasesSquare`, Tor
independent by `AlgebraicGeometry.torIndependent_morphismRestrict_resLE`). The two components are
the two maps of Tag 0A9L composed with the identifications of restriction and derived pullback;
the square commutes by
`Stacks.Duality.torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange_restrict_comm`.
declarations.statement:
def torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChangeRestrictArrowIso
    (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y)
    [IsIso ((qcqsTwistedInverseImageRestrictionMap f V).app K)]
    [IsIso ((qcqsTwistedInverseImageRestrictionMap f' V').app (Lq[g].obj K))] :
    Arrow.mk (Rs[(f' ⁻¹ᵁ V').ι].map ((torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange sq hTor).app K)) ≅
      Arrow.mk ((torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange
        (isPullback_restrictBasesSquare sq V hVV')
          (torIndependent_morphismRestrict_resLE f g hTor hVV')).app
          (Rs[V.ι].obj K))
