declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.upperShriek_structureSheaf_isPerfectRelativeTo_and_isIso_homothety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E9T (Lemma 48.17.10).** In Situation 48.16.1 (`S` Noetherian), let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of `FTS S`, with `f^!` computed at any compactification `j`. Then
`f^!𝒪_Y` is a `Y`-perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` and `𝒪_X ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(f^!𝒪_Y, f^!𝒪_Y)` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriek_structureSheaf_isPerfectRelativeTo_and_isIso_homothety :
    (letI := locallyOfFinitePresentation_left f;
      Scheme.Hom.IsPerfectRelativeTo.{u + 1, u + 1} f.left
        (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily _)
        (relativeDualizingComplexObj f j)) ∧
      IsIso (Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomothety X.left.sheaf
        (relativeDualizingComplexObj f j))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isPseudoCoherent_of_isShriekOfStructureSheafOnCharts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E9T, the pseudo-coherence half of the first assertion.** In
Situation 48.16.1, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of finite presentation of `FTS S`. Then the
relative dualizing complex `ω^•_{X/Y} = f^!𝒪_Y` is a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)`.

Over each chart the model of `f^!𝒪_Y` lies in `D^b_Coh` of the chart ring by
Tag 0BZK (2); the chart bounds glue, and on a Noetherian scheme a bounded object with coherent
cohomology is pseudo-coherent by Tag 08E8.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_isShriekOfStructureSheafOnCharts
    [Flat f.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f.left]
    (ω : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory.{u + 1, u} X.left)
    (hw : IsShriekOfStructureSheafOnCharts f ω.obj) :
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.left.toRingedSpace) ω.obj
declarations.comment: the pseudo-coherence half of the first assertion: f^! O_Y is a pseudo-coherent object of D(O_X), which is the first of the two conjuncts of Y-perfectness (Tag 0DI0). NOT claimed: the Tor-dimension conjunct of the first assertion, and the whole of the second assertion that O_X -> R SheafHom(f^! O_Y, f^! O_Y) is an isomorphism. Both rest on Stacks 0BZW, whose parts (1)(a), (1)(b) and (1)(c) are all proved in this repository at the level of rings -- (1)(b) as Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.relativeDualizingComplex_hasFiniteTorDimension_of_isPerfectRingMap and (1)(c) as Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_unit_isIso_derivedHomothety_of_isPerfectModule -- but what is absent is the affine-locality assembly for Tor dimension that Stacks 0DI2 would need, and there is no map O_X -> R SheafHom(K, K) on a scheme in this repository at all, so the sheaf-level second assertion cannot even be stated. Neither is carried as a hypothesis, since either would be the assertion itself. One hypothesis IS carried, hw: the affine-chart description of f^! O_Y, which is Stacks 0AA1 together with clause (b) of Stacks 0BV2; it asserts only an isomorphism, and it is the same hypothesis carried by Tag 0B6U part (a) and Tag 0AA3. Everything asserted about pseudo-coherence is proved, from Tag 0BZK (2) chart by chart -- whose perfect-ring-map hypothesis is discharged, not carried, from Flat and LocallyOfFinitePresentation through Tag 068A -- and Tag 08E8. f^! O_Y enters as an object of D+_QCoh(O_X) at CategoryTheory.HasDerivedCategory.standard characterised by hw, the idiom of Tag 0AA3, rather than as a value of Stacks.Duality.upperShriek, which is defined at the locally small model that Tag 08E8 is not available at

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.upperShriekFlatBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Flat base change for `f^!`.** Let `S` be Noetherian and let `X' ⟶ X` over `Y' ⟶ Y` be a
cartesian square of `FTS S` with `g` flat. Then `L(g')^* ∘ f^! ≅ (f')^! ∘ Lg^*` on
`D^+_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, with `f^!` computed at any compactification `j` of `f` and `(f')^!` at any
compactification `c'` of `f'`. It is the base change map `L(g')^* j^* ā ≅ (j')^* L(ḡ')^* ā ⟶
(j')^* ā' Lg^*` of the base change `j'` of `j`, followed by the comparison
`(f')^!_{j'} ≅ (f')^!_{c'}` of [Stacks, Tag 0AA0] at `Lg^*K ∈ D^+_QCoh(𝒪_{Y'})`.
declarations.statement:
def upperShriekFlatBaseChangeIso (c' : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f'.left)) :
    (ObjectProperty.ι _ : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel Y.left ⥤ _) ⋙
        upperShriek f c ⋙ quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' g'.left ≅
      (ObjectProperty.ι _ : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel Y.left ⥤ _) ⋙
        quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' g.left ⋙ upperShriek f' c'

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.propertySkModule_modulesStalk_homology_upperShriek_of_residueTrdeg_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E9V (Lemma 48.21.5), the `(S₂)` clause.** Under the hypotheses of the
tag, the stalk `H^{-r}(f^!𝒪_Y)_x` satisfies `(S₂)` as an `𝒪_{X,x}`-module, for every
compactification `j` defining `f^!`. On a chart the stalk is the localization of
`H^{-r}(ω^•_{A/R})` at the prime of `x`, which is `(S₂)` by the ring-level [Stacks, Tag 0E9R].
declarations.statement:
theorem propertySkModule_modulesStalk_homology_upperShriek_of_residueTrdeg_le
    (x : X.left) (r : ℕ)
    (hCM : IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Y.left.presheaf.stalk (f.left.base x)))
    (htrdeg : ∀ ξ : X.left, closure {ξ} ∈ irreducibleComponents X.left → x ∈ closure {ξ} →
      Stacks.Chow.residueTrdeg f.left ξ ≤ (r : Cardinal)) :
    letI := module_finite_modulesStalk_homology_upperShriek f j x (-(r : ℤ))
    PropertySkModule (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) ((modulesStalkFunctor x).obj
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules (-(r : ℤ))).obj
        (((upperShriek f j).obj (derivedStructureSheaf Y.left)).obj))) 2
declarations.comment: the (S_2) property of the stalk H^{-r}(f^! O_Y)_x as an O_{X,x}-module

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.neg_le_of_nontrivial_stalk_homology_upperShriek_of_residueTrdeg_le_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E9V (Lemma 48.21.4), the vanishing.** If `𝒪_{Y, f x}` is
Cohen–Macaulay and the residue transcendence degree of `f` is at most `r` at every generic point
of a component of `X` through `x`, then `H^i(f^!𝒪_Y)_x ≠ 0` implies `-r ≤ i`, for every `j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem neg_le_of_nontrivial_stalk_homology_upperShriek_of_residueTrdeg_le_unconditional
    (x : X.left) (r : ℕ)
    (hCM : IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Y.left.presheaf.stalk (f.left.base x)))
    (htrdeg : ∀ ξ : X.left, closure {ξ} ∈ irreducibleComponents X.left → x ∈ closure {ξ} →
      Stacks.Chow.residueTrdeg f.left ξ ≤ (r : Cardinal))
    (i : ℤ)
    (hi : Nontrivial (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules i).obj
      (((upperShriek f j).obj
        (derivedStructureSheaf Y.left)).obj)).presheaf.stalk x)) :
    -(r : ℤ) ≤ i
declarations.comment: the vanishing: H^i(f^! O_Y)_x nonzero implies -r <= i

registrations.name: Stacks.Duality.neg_le_of_nontrivial_stalk_homology_upperShriek_of_residueTrdeg_le
registrations.comment:
THE VANISHING BOUND ONLY; the tag is NOT proved. Proved: in the stated
situation, if the stalk at x of H^i(f^! O_Y) is nontrivial then -r <= i. NOT PROVED: the second
conclusion, that the stalk H^{-r}(f^! O_Y)_x is (S_2) as an O_{X,x}-module -- nothing about (S_2)
is stated in this file, and the module-level stalk dictionary it needs does not exist in the
library (only the abelian-group version does). TWO HYPOTHESES ARE CARRIED, neither dischargeable
here. h0BV2 is clause (b) of Stacks 0BV2, the affine formula for f^! O_Y, which needs Stacks 0AA1
(f^! = Lf^*[1] for A^1_V -> V), absent from this repository; the library's Stacks 0BV2 explicitly
declines clause (b). NOTE IT IS CARRIED IN A STRENGTHENED FORM relative to the library's Stacks 0BV5
and 0B6U, which take one chart: here it must be COFINAL in neighbourhoods of x, which is what
permits the chart shrinking. h0E9R is clause (1) of Stacks 0E9R at the SHARP bound r, whereas the
library's subsingleton_localizedModule_homology_relativeDualizingComplex gives only the crude
bound (the number of variables); the sharp bound needs the dimension formula of Stacks 0BAE via
the duality formula of Stacks 0E9L localized at a maximal ideal. Stacks 0E9L itself is proved in
general as Dualizing.PolynomialPresentation.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_natIso_dualizingDerivedHom;
the passage to the localization is the base change of Stacks 0BZV, conditional in this library.

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_isRelativeDualizingComplex_upperShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0E9W.** In Situation 48.16.1 (`S` Noetherian), let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of `FTS S`, with `f^!` computed at any compactification `j`. Then
`f^!𝒪_Y` is the first component of a relative dualizing complex for `X` over `Y`
(Definition 0E2T): for every open `W ⊆ X ×_Y X` through which the diagonal factors as a closed
immersion `Δ : X ⟶ W` there is `ξ : Δ_*𝒪_X ⟶ L pr₁^* f^!𝒪_Y|_W` making `(f^!𝒪_Y, ξ)` a relative
dualizing complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativeDualizingComplex_upperShriek (D : f.left.DiagonalOpen) :
    letI := locallyOfFinitePresentation_left f
    ∃ ξ : D.diagonalObject ⟶ D.derivedPullbackProj (relativeDualizingComplexObj f j),
      Scheme.Hom.IsRelativeDualizingComplex.{u + 1, u} f.left
        (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily _) D
        (relativeDualizingComplexObj f j) ξ

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_stalkMap_locallyRingedSpaceDeterminantMap_iff
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0E9Y].** Let `X` be a locally ringed space and `E₁ --α--> E₀ --π--> F ⟶ 0` an
exact sequence of `O_X`-modules with `E₁` and `E₀` finite locally free of ranks `r₁` and `r₀`.
The canonical map `⋀^{r₀ - r₁} F ⟶ ⋀^{r₁}(E₁^∨) ⊗ ⋀^{r₀} E₀` is an isomorphism on the stalk at
`x` if and only if `F` is locally free of rank `r₀ - r₁` on an open neighbourhood of `x`: that
is, `r₀ - r₁` is a natural number and `F` is free of that rank on some open `U ∋ x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_stalkMap_locallyRingedSpaceDeterminantMap_iff [Epi π]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E₁ r₁]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E₀ r₀]
    (x : ↥Y.toRingedSpace.carrier) :
    IsIso (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.stalkMap
        (toRingCat (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥Y.toRingedSpace.carrier) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf) x
        (locallyRingedSpaceDeterminantMap Y α π hαπ hS r₁ r₀)) ↔
      r₁ ≤ r₀ ∧ ∃ U : Opens ↥Y.toRingedSpace.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
        ∃ t : LocallyFreeRank.Trivialization Y.toRingedSpace.carrier
          (LocallyFreeRank.toRingSheaf Y.toRingedSpace.carrier Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf) F U,
          Nonempty (t.ι ≃ Fin (r₀ - r₁))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.ClosedOpenProperFactorization.exists_fundamentalClass_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be Noetherian and `f : X ⟶ Y` a local complete intersection morphism of `FTS S`
which factors as an immersion `ι : X ⟶ P` followed by a proper smooth morphism `g : P ⟶ Y`; let
`f^!` be computed at any compactification `j` of `f`. Then there is a locally constant function
`r` on `X` such that `ω_{X/Y} = H^{-r}(f^!𝒪_Y)` is the only nonzero cohomology sheaf of `f^!𝒪_Y`
(the stalk of `H^k(f^!𝒪_Y)` at `x` is nonzero exactly for `k = -r(x)`), and a map
`∧^r Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ ω_{X/Y}` whose stalk at `x` is an isomorphism exactly when `f` is smooth at `x`.

As `r` is only locally constant, the map is given on each piece of a decomposition of `X` into
pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes covering `X` on which `r` is constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fundamentalClass_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
    (hlci : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f.left) (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) :
    ∃ r : X.left → ℤ, IsLocallyConstant r ∧
      (∀ (x : X.left) (k : ℤ),
        Nontrivial ↑((upperShriekHomology f j k).presheaf.stalk x) ↔ k = -r x) ∧
      ∃ (A : Type) (V : A → X.left.Opens) (n : A → ℤ),
        (∀ a, IsClosed (V a : Set X.left)) ∧ Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint V) ∧ (⨆ a, V a) = ⊤ ∧
        (∀ a, ∀ x ∈ V a, r x = n a) ∧
        ∀ a, ∃ φ : (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (V a).ι).obj
            (Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f.left) (n a)) ⟶
          (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (V a).ι).obj (upperShriekHomology f j (-n a)),
          ∀ x : (V a).toScheme, IsIso (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.stalkMap
              (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.toRingCat (Opens.grothendieckTopology
                ↥(V a).toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace.carrier)
                (V a).toScheme.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace.sheaf) x φ) ↔
            InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f.left ((V a).ι x)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.SmoothLocus.exists_map_exteriorPower_isIso_of_smoothAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EA0.** Let `S` be Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ Y` a morphism of `FTS S` and
`r ≥ 0`. Assume
1. `Y` is Cohen–Macaulay,
2. `f` factors as an immersion `ι : X ⟶ P` followed by a smooth proper `g : P ⟶ Y`,
3. `f` is Koszul at every `x ∈ X` with `dim 𝒪_{X,x} ≤ 1`, and
4. `trdeg_{κ(f(ξ))} κ(ξ) = r` at every generic point `ξ` of an irreducible component of `X`.

Then, with `ω_{X/Y} = H^{-r}(f^!𝒪_Y)` (`f^!` at any compactification `j`), there is a map
`∧^r Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ ω_{X/Y}` which is an isomorphism at every point where `f` is smooth.

Two steps of the source's proof are corrected. The locally constant function of
[Stacks, Tag 0E9Z] on the local complete intersection locus `U` is `r` only on the pieces where it
equals `r` (in general it is `r - dim 𝒪_{Y,f(ξ)}` at generic points `ξ`); every smooth point lies
on such a piece, and on the others `ω_{X/Y}` vanishes and the map is taken to be zero. The
extension across `X ∖ U` by [Stacks, Tag 0E9I] needs `depth(ω_{X/Y,x}) ≥ 2` there; the `(S₂)`
property of [Stacks, Tag 0E9V] does not give this alone, and it is proved as
`min(2, dim 𝒪_{X,x}) ≤ depth(ω_{X/Y,x})`
(`Stacks.Duality.min_two_ringKrullDim_le_moduleDepth_modulesStalk_homology_upperShriek`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_map_exteriorPower_isIso_of_smoothAt {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S]
    {X Y : FTS S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (r : ℕ) (hY : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay Y.left)
    {P : Scheme.{u}} (ι : X.left ⟶ P) [IsImmersion ι] (g : P ⟶ Y.left) [Smooth g] [IsProper g]
    (hfac : ι ≫ g = f.left)
    (hK : ∀ x : X.left, ringKrullDim (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) ≤ 1 → KoszulAt f.left x)
    (htr : ∀ ξ : X.left, closure {ξ} ∈ irreducibleComponents X.left →
      Stacks.Chow.residueTrdeg f.left ξ = (r : Cardinal))
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) :
    ∃ φ : Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f.left) (r : ℤ) ⟶
        upperShriekHomology f j (-(r : ℤ)),
      ∀ x : X.left, InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f.left x →
        IsIso (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.stalkMap
          (Sheaf.toRingCat (Opens.grothendieckTopology
            ↥X.left.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace.carrier)
            X.left.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace.sheaf) x φ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DualizingDivisor.eq_top_of_isMinimalResolution_of_relativeDualizingModule_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EA2], second sentence.** Let `A` be a Noetherian normal local domain of
dimension two which is Nagata and has a dualizing module `ω_A`, and let `f : X ⟶ Spec(A)` be a
minimal resolution of singularities. Let `ω_X = H^{-2}(f^×(ω_A[2]))` be as in
[Stacks, Remark 0B4R] (`Stacks.Duality.relativeDualizingModule` at `ω_A[2]^~`, as in the first
sentence, `definesRationalSingularity_of_relativeDualizingModule_iso`). If `ω_X ≅ 𝒪_X(E)` for an
effective Cartier divisor `E ⊆ X` supported on the exceptional fibre, then `E = 0`, i.e. the ideal
sheaf of `E` is the unit ideal `⊤`. The hypotheses are those of the first sentence with
`IsMinimalResolution f` in place of `IsResolution f`; properness of `f` and quasi-compactness and
quasi-separatedness of `X`, needed to form `f^×`, are derived from it inside the statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_top_of_isMinimalResolution_of_relativeDualizingModule_iso (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNormalDomain A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2)
    (hNagata : IsNagataRing A) (ωA : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (hω : Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingRingModule A ωA)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) (hf : IsMinimalResolution f)
    (E : X.IdealSheafData) [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor E]
    (hE : ∀ x : X, x ∈ E.support → f x = closedPoint A)
    (e : haveI : IsProper f := hf.1.1.isProper
      haveI : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
      haveI : QuasiSeparatedSpace X := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f
      Nonempty (relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        ((derivedTilde (CommRingCat.of A)).obj ((singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (-2)).obj ωA)) ≅
          (Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' E : X.Modules))) :
    E = ⊤
declarations.comment: second sentence: if f is a minimal resolution, then E = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DualizingDivisor.definesRationalSingularity_of_relativeDualizingModule_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EA2], first sentence.** Let `A` be a Noetherian normal local domain of
dimension two which is Nagata, has a dualizing module `ω_A`, and has a resolution of
singularities `f : X ⟶ Spec(A)`. Let `ω_X` be as in [Stacks, Tag 0B4R]: the dualizing module of
`X` normalized with respect to `ω_A`, that is `ω_X = H^{-2}(f^×(ω_A[2]))` with `f^×` the twisted
inverse image (`Stacks.Duality.relativeDualizingModule` at `ω_A[2]^~`, whose degree `-dim X` is
`-2`). If `ω_X ≅ 𝒪_X(E)` for an effective Cartier divisor `E ⊆ X` supported on the exceptional
fibre (every point of `E` lies over the closed point), then `A` defines a rational singularity.

Following the source, duality turns the map `𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_X(E) = ω_X` into a generator of
`Hom(RΓ(X, 𝒪_X[2]), ω_A[2])` (`hom_derivedSectionsUnitShift_free`); the criterion
`Stacks.PurityRamification.subsingleton_homology_succ_of_forall_eq_smul` (depth of `ω_A`,
[Stacks, Tag 0AXC], torsion of `H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`) gives `H¹(X, 𝒪_X) = 0`, and a resolution with
`H¹(X, 𝒪_X) = 0` makes `A` a rational singularity
(`definesRationalSingularity_of_isResolution_of_isZero_structureSheafH1`). Forming `f^×`, hence
`ω_X`, uses that `f` is proper and `X` quasi-compact and quasi-separated; inside the statement
these are derived from `IsResolution f` (a resolution is proper over the affine scheme
`Spec(A)`) by `haveI`, not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem definesRationalSingularity_of_relativeDualizingModule_iso (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNormalDomain A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2)
    (hNagata : IsNagataRing A) (ωA : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (hω : Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingRingModule A ωA)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) (hf : IsResolution f)
    (E : X.IdealSheafData) [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor E]
    (hE : ∀ x : X, x ∈ E.support → f x = closedPoint A)
    (e : haveI : IsProper f := hf.1.isProper
      haveI : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
      haveI : QuasiSeparatedSpace X := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f
      Nonempty (relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        ((derivedTilde (CommRingCat.of A)).obj ((singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (-2)).obj ωA)) ≅
          (Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' E : X.Modules))) :
    DefinesRationalSingularity A
declarations.comment: first sentence: if ω_X ≅ O_X(E) for an effective Cartier divisor E supported on the exceptional fibre of a resolution, then A defines a rational singularity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_of_etaleAt_outside_closure_of_ringKrullDim_eq_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EA3.** Let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be a morphism (locally) of finite type and
`x ∈ X`. Assume `A` is an excellent regular local ring, `𝒪_{X, x}` is normal of dimension `2`,
and `f` is étale at every point outside `closure {x}`. Then `f` is étale at `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleAt_of_etaleAt_outside_closure_of_ringKrullDim_eq_two {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hA : IsExcellent A) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) (hX : IsNormalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 2)
    (het : ∀ z : X, z ∉ closure ({x} : Set X) → EtaleAt f z) : EtaleAt f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_of_etaleAt_codimensionOne
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EA4], purity of the ramification locus.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
locally Noetherian schemes, let `x : X` and `y = f x`, and assume that (1) `𝒪_{X,x}` is normal of
dimension at least one, (2) `𝒪_{Y,y}` is regular, (3) `f` is locally of finite type, and (4) `f`
is étale at every specialization `x' ⤳ x` with `dim 𝒪_{X,x'} = 1`. Then `f` is étale at `x`.

The hypotheses are exactly the tag's own. "Normal" is `IsNormalRing` of the stalk (for a local
ring: a normal domain), "dimension" is `ringKrullDim`, and a specialization `x' ⤳ x` of the
source is Mathlib's `x' ⤳ x`, that is `x ∈ closure {x'}`.

The proof is the source's: the proper generizations of `x` are handled by induction on
`dim 𝒪_{X,x}`, base change to `Spec 𝒪_{Y,f x}` ([Stacks, Tag 0476]) and then to the spectrum of
its completion changes neither étaleness at the relevant point (both being flat) nor normality of
the local ring there (Serre's criterion), and over the complete — hence excellent — regular local
base the induction of `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_of_etaleAt_codimensionOne_over_excellent`
applies, with [Stacks, Tag 0EA3] in dimension two and [Stacks, Tag 0BMB] above it.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleAt_of_etaleAt_codimensionOne
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X)
    (hX : IsNormalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hY : IsRegularLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (hpositive : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hetale : ∀ x' : X, x' ⤳ x → ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x') = 1 → EtaleAt f x') :
    EtaleAt f x
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: hypotheses (1) `𝒪_{X,x}` normal of dimension `≥ 1`, (2) `𝒪_{Y,f x}` regular, (3) `f` locally of finite type, (4) `f` étale at every `x' ⤳ x` with `dim 𝒪_{X,x'} = 1`; the conclusion is `EtaleAt f x`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.localizationTorsionModuleProperty_isSerreClass
declarations.doc: The modules whose elements are annihilated locally by `S` form a Serre subcategory.
declarations.statement:
public instance localizationTorsionModuleProperty_isSerreClass {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (S : Submonoid R) :
    (localizationTorsionModuleProperty (R := R) S :
      ObjectProperty (ModuleCat.{v} R)).IsSerreClass
declarations.comment: the Serre subcategory

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.localizedModuleFunctor_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
Localizing modules at `S` presents the category of modules over `Localization S` as the Serre
quotient by the modules whose elements are annihilated by members of `S`.

In particular, `CategoryTheory.Localization.equivalenceFromModel` applied to this instance is the
canonical equivalence from the Serre quotient to `ModuleCat (Localization S)`, and
`CategoryTheory.Localization.qCompEquivalenceFromModelFunctorIso` identifies its composite with
the quotient functor with `ModuleCat.localizedModuleFunctor S`.
declarations.statement:
public instance localizedModuleFunctor_isLocalization {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (S : Submonoid R) [Small.{v, u} R] :
    (ModuleCat.localizedModuleFunctor.{v} S).IsLocalization
      (localizationTorsionModuleProperty (R := R) S :
        ObjectProperty (ModuleCat.{v} R)).isoModSerre
declarations.comment: the canonical equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.periodicLength_zero_eq_length_quotient_sub_length_ker
declarations.doc:
The additive Herbrand quotient of a `(2, 1)`-periodic complex whose first map is zero is the
length of the cokernel of its second map minus the length of the kernel of that map.
declarations.statement:
public lemma periodicLength_zero_eq_length_quotient_sub_length_ker {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (ψ : Module.End R M) :
    periodicLength (twoPeriodicComplex (0 : Module.End R M) ψ (zero_mul ψ) (mul_zero ψ)) =
      ((Module.length R (M ⧸ LinearMap.range ψ)).toNat : ℤ) -
        ((Module.length R (LinearMap.ker ψ)).toNat : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteLengthHomology_X3_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
In a short exact sequence of two-periodic complexes, finite-length cohomology of the first
two terms implies finite-length cohomology of the third.
declarations.statement:
public lemma finiteLengthHomology_X3_of_shortExact {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (S : ShortComplex (HomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up (ZMod 2))))
    (hS : S.ShortExact) (h₁ : HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₁)
    (h₂ : HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₂) : HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₃
declarations.comment: two-out-of-three, third term

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteLengthHomology_X2_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
In a short exact sequence of two-periodic complexes, finite-length cohomology of the outer
terms implies finite-length cohomology of the middle term.
declarations.statement:
public lemma finiteLengthHomology_X2_of_shortExact {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (S : ShortComplex (HomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up (ZMod 2))))
    (hS : S.ShortExact) (h₁ : HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₁)
    (h₃ : HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₃) : HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₂
declarations.comment: two-out-of-three, middle term

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteLengthHomology_X1_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
In a short exact sequence of two-periodic complexes, finite-length cohomology of the last
two terms implies finite-length cohomology of the first.
declarations.statement:
public lemma finiteLengthHomology_X1_of_shortExact {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (S : ShortComplex (HomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up (ZMod 2))))
    (hS : S.ShortExact) (h₂ : HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₂)
    (h₃ : HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₃) : HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₁
declarations.comment: two-out-of-three, first term

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.periodicLength_additive_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
Periodic length is additive on a short exact sequence of two-periodic complexes as soon as
the cohomology of any two of its terms has finite length.
declarations.statement:
public lemma periodicLength_additive_of_shortExact {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (S : ShortComplex (HomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up (ZMod 2))))
    (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hfin : (HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₁ ∧ HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₂) ∨
      (HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₁ ∧ HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₃) ∨
      (HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₂ ∧ HasFiniteLengthHomology S.X₃)) :
    periodicLength S.X₂ = periodicLength S.X₁ + periodicLength S.X₃
declarations.comment: additivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.periodicLength_eq_length_sub_length
declarations.doc:
The multiplicity of a two-periodic complex of finite-length modules is the difference of
the lengths of its two terms.
declarations.statement:
public lemma periodicLength_eq_length_sub_length {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (C : HomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up (ZMod 2)))
    (h₀ : IsFiniteLength R (C.X (0 : ZMod 2)))
    (h₁ : IsFiniteLength R (C.X (1 : ZMod 2))) :
    periodicLength C =
      ((Module.length R (C.X (0 : ZMod 2))).toNat : ℤ) -
        ((Module.length R (C.X (1 : ZMod 2))).toNat : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the length formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.periodicLength_eq_zero_of_iso
declarations.doc: The multiplicity of a finite-length two-periodic complex with isomorphic terms vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public lemma periodicLength_eq_zero_of_iso {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (C : HomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up (ZMod 2)))
    (hfin : IsFiniteLength R (C.X (0 : ZMod 2)))
    (e : C.X (0 : ZMod 2) ≅ C.X (1 : ZMod 2)) :
    periodicLength C = 0
declarations.comment: the (2, 1)-periodic case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.periodicLength_eq_of_finite_length_kernel_cokernel
declarations.doc:
A morphism between `(2, 1)`-periodic complexes with finite-length kernel and cokernel
preserves their periodic length when the cohomology modules of both complexes have finite
length.
declarations.statement:
public theorem periodicLength_eq_of_finite_length_kernel_cokernel
    {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    {C D : HomologicalComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up (ZMod 2))}
    (f : C ⟶ D)
    (hC : ∀ i, IsFiniteLength R (C.homology i))
    (hD : ∀ i, IsFiniteLength R (D.homology i))
    (hker : IsFiniteLength R ((kernel f).X (0 : ZMod 2)))
    (hcoker : IsFiniteLength R ((cokernel f).X (0 : ZMod 2)))
    (eker : (kernel f).X (0 : ZMod 2) ≅ (kernel f).X (1 : ZMod 2))
    (ecoker : (cokernel f).X (0 : ZMod 2) ≅ (cokernel f).X (1 : ZMod 2)) :
    periodicLength C = periodicLength D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.periodicLength_powers_eq_zero_of_nilpotent
declarations.doc:
If `φ` is nilpotent of order at most `n` and
`ker φ / range (φ ^ (n - 1))` has finite length, then the periodic length associated to
`φ ^ i` and `φ ^ (n - i)` vanishes for every `0 ≤ i ≤ n`.

Since `periodicLength` reads infinite lengths as zero, this alone does not say that the
multiplicity is defined; the full statement of Stacks 0EAB, including the finiteness of both
cohomology modules, is
`isFiniteLength_homology_and_periodicLength_powers_eq_zero_of_nilpotent`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma periodicLength_powers_eq_zero_of_nilpotent {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (φ : Module.End R M) (n : ℕ) (hnpos : 0 < n) (hnil : φ ^ n = 0)
    (hfinite : IsFiniteLength R ((LinearMap.ker φ) ⧸
      (LinearMap.range (φ ^ (n - 1))).comap (LinearMap.ker φ).subtype)) :
    ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ n),
      periodicLength
        (twoPeriodicComplex (φ ^ i) (φ ^ (n - i))
          (by rw [← pow_add, Nat.add_sub_of_le hi, hnil])
          (by rw [← pow_add, Nat.sub_add_cancel hi, hnil])) = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLength_homology_and_periodicLength_powers_eq_zero_of_nilpotent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAB.** Let `φ` be an endomorphism of an `R`-module `M` and `n > 0` with
`φ ^ n = 0` such that `ker φ / range (φ ^ (n - 1))` has finite length. Then for every
`0 ≤ i ≤ n` the multiplicity `e_R(M, φ ^ i, φ ^ (n - i))` is defined, that is, both
cohomology modules `ker (φ ^ i) / range (φ ^ (n - i))` and `ker (φ ^ (n - i)) / range (φ ^ i)`
of the two-periodic complex `(M, φ ^ i, φ ^ (n - i))` have finite length, and it vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteLength_homology_and_periodicLength_powers_eq_zero_of_nilpotent
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (φ : Module.End R M) (n : ℕ) (hnpos : 0 < n) (hnil : φ ^ n = 0)
    (hfinite : IsFiniteLength R ((LinearMap.ker φ) ⧸
      (LinearMap.range (φ ^ (n - 1))).comap (LinearMap.ker φ).subtype)) :
    ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ n),
      IsFiniteLength R
        ((twoPeriodicComplex (φ ^ i) (φ ^ (n - i))
          (by rw [← pow_add, Nat.add_sub_of_le hi, hnil])
          (by rw [← pow_add, Nat.sub_add_cancel hi, hnil])).homology (0 : ZMod 2)) ∧
      IsFiniteLength R
        ((twoPeriodicComplex (φ ^ i) (φ ^ (n - i))
          (by rw [← pow_add, Nat.add_sub_of_le hi, hnil])
          (by rw [← pow_add, Nat.sub_add_cancel hi, hnil])).homology (1 : ZMod 2)) ∧
      periodicLength
        (twoPeriodicComplex (φ ^ i) (φ ^ (n - i))
          (by rw [← pow_add, Nat.add_sub_of_le hi, hnil])
          (by rw [← pow_add, Nat.sub_add_cancel hi, hnil])) = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.periodicLength_smul_fst
declarations.doc:
Multiplying the first differential of a two-periodic complex by `x` subtracts the periodic
length of its image with differentials zero and multiplication by `x`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma periodicLength_smul_fst {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (φ ψ : M →ₗ[R] M) (hφψ : φ.comp ψ = 0) (hψφ : ψ.comp φ = 0) (x : R)
    (hH₀ : IsFiniteLength R
      ((twoPeriodicComplex φ ψ hφψ hψφ).homology (0 : ZMod 2)))
    (hH₁ : IsFiniteLength R
      ((twoPeriodicComplex φ ψ hφψ hψφ).homology (1 : ZMod 2)))
    (hsupp : Module.supportDim R (QuotSMulTop x M) ≤ 0) :
    periodicLength
        (twoPeriodicComplex (x • φ) ψ
          (by change (x • φ).comp ψ = 0; rw [LinearMap.smul_comp, hφψ, smul_zero])
          (by change ψ.comp (x • φ) = 0; rw [LinearMap.comp_smul, hψφ, smul_zero])) =
      periodicLength (twoPeriodicComplex φ ψ hφψ hψφ) -
        periodicLength
          (twoPeriodicComplex (0 : Module.End R (LinearMap.range φ))
            (LinearMap.lsmul R (LinearMap.range φ) x) (zero_mul _) (mul_zero _))
declarations.comment: multiplying the first differential

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.periodicLength_smul_snd
declarations.doc:
Multiplying the second differential of a two-periodic complex by `x` adds the periodic
length of its image with differentials zero and multiplication by `x`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma periodicLength_smul_snd {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (φ ψ : M →ₗ[R] M) (hφψ : φ.comp ψ = 0) (hψφ : ψ.comp φ = 0) (x : R)
    (hH₀ : IsFiniteLength R
      ((twoPeriodicComplex φ ψ hφψ hψφ).homology (0 : ZMod 2)))
    (hH₁ : IsFiniteLength R
      ((twoPeriodicComplex φ ψ hφψ hψφ).homology (1 : ZMod 2)))
    (hsupp : Module.supportDim R (QuotSMulTop x M) ≤ 0) :
    periodicLength
        (twoPeriodicComplex φ (x • ψ)
          (by
            change φ.comp (x • ψ) = 0
            rw [LinearMap.comp_smul, hφψ, smul_zero])
          (by
            change (x • ψ).comp φ = 0
            rw [LinearMap.smul_comp, hψφ, smul_zero])) =
      periodicLength (twoPeriodicComplex φ ψ hφψ hψφ) +
        periodicLength
          (twoPeriodicComplex (0 : Module.End R (LinearMap.range ψ))
            (LinearMap.lsmul R (LinearMap.range ψ) x) (zero_mul _) (mul_zero _))
declarations.comment: multiplying the second differential

declarations.name: Stacks.RingHomGluing.exists_ringHom_inducing_at_maximal_ideal
declarations.doc:
Ring maps over the localizations at finitely many pairwise distinct maximal ideals glue to
one global ring map. The map has kernel and cokernel killed by powers of the
intersection, and it inherits finiteness, injectivity, or surjectivity when all the local maps
have the corresponding property.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ringHom_inducing_at_maximal_ideal
    (hm : Pairwise fun i j ↦ m i ≠ m j)
    (f : ∀ i, Localization.AtPrime (m i) →+* B i)
    (hker : ∀ i, KernelIsKilledByIdealPower (f i)
      ((m i).map (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime (m i)))))
    (hcoker : ∀ i, CokernelIsKilledByIdealPower (f i)
      ((m i).map (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime (m i))))) :
    ∃ (B' : Type (max u v w)) (_ : CommRing B') (g : A →+* B'),
      (∀ i, ∃ gᵢ : B' →+* B i,
        gᵢ.comp g = (f i).comp (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime (m i))) ∧
        (Submonoid.map g (m i).primeCompl).IsLocalizationMap gᵢ) ∧
      KernelIsKilledByIdealPower g (⨅ i, m i) ∧
      CokernelIsKilledByIdealPower g (⨅ i, m i) ∧
      ((∀ i, (f i).Finite) → g.Finite) ∧
      ((∀ i, Function.Injective (f i)) → Function.Injective g) ∧
      ((∀ i, Function.Surjective (f i)) → Function.Surjective g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_factorization_exponent_of_finite_extension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EAF.** Let `R` be a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring and let
`a` and `b` be nonzerodivisors, with `a` in the maximal ideal. There is a uniform bound on an
exponent `m` for which the image of `b` in a finite ring extension is a multiple of `a ^ m`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_bound_factorization_exponent_of_finite_extension
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (_hdim : ringKrullDim R = 1) {a b : R} (ha : IsSMulRegular R a)
    (hb : IsSMulRegular R b) (ha_mem : a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S],
      (algebraMap R S).Finite → Function.Injective (algebraMap R S) → ∀ m : ℕ,
        (∃ c : S, algebraMap R S b = (algebraMap R S a) ^ m * c) → m ≤ n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_tameSymbolPreparation_of_ringKrullDim_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EAG.** Nonzerodivisors in a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring, not
all of which are units, admit a simultaneous tame-symbol preparation after a finite extension
whose quotient is supported at the maximal ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_tameSymbolPreparation_of_ringKrullDim_eq_one {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] {r : ℕ} (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (a : Fin r → A) (ha : ∀ i, IsRegular (a i))
    (hunit : ¬ ∀ i, IsUnit (a i)) (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B),
      Nonempty (TameSymbolPreparation a B)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.regularTameSymbolOfKrullDimOne
declarations.doc:
The tame symbol of a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring `A` on pairs of nonzerodivisors:
the symbol of Stacks 02PZ on the module `A` itself, which satisfies Stacks 0EAL, 0EAM, 0EAN and
0EAP.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def regularTameSymbolOfKrullDimOne : RegularTameSymbol A
declarations.comment: on nonzerodivisors, for every one-dimensional Noetherian local ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolOfKrullDimOne
declarations.doc:
The tame symbol `∂_A : Q(A)^* × Q(A)^* → κ(𝔪)^*` of a one-dimensional Noetherian local
ring `A`, satisfying Stacks 0EAI, 0EAJ and 0EAK: the extension
(`Stacks.Chow.RegularTameSymbol.extend`) of the symbol of Stacks 02PZ on pairs of
nonzerodivisors.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tameSymbolOfKrullDimOne (Q : Type v) [CommRing Q] [Algebra A Q]
    [IsFractionRing A Q] : TameSymbol A Q
declarations.comment: on Q(A)^*, for every one-dimensional Noetherian local ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.normPushforwardOfIsIntegrallyClosed
declarations.doc:
The tame symbol on nonzerodivisors of a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain `A` with a
normal finite modification: for `A ⊆ B` module-finite with `B` an integrally closed domain and
`B/A` annihilated by a power of `𝔪`,

`∂_A(a, b) = ∏_𝔮 Norm_{κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔪)}(∂_{B_𝔮}(a, b))`,

the product over the maximal ideals `𝔮` of `B`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normPushforwardOfIsIntegrallyClosed (hA : ¬ IsField A)
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B))
    (hquot : ∃ n : ℕ, maximalIdeal A ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A B) ≤
      LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap A B)) :
    RegularTameSymbol A
declarations.comment: on nonzerodivisors, for a local domain with a normal finite modification

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure
declarations.doc:
The tame symbol `∂_A : Q(A)^* × Q(A)^* → κ(𝔪)^*` of a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain
`A` whose integral closure in its fraction field is module finite: the extension
`Stacks.Chow.RegularTameSymbol.extend` of `Stacks.Chow.normPushforwardOfFiniteIntegralClosure`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure (hA : ¬ IsField A)
    (Q : Type*) [CommRing Q] [Algebra A Q] [IsFractionRing A Q] : TameSymbol A Q
declarations.comment: on Q(A)^*, for a local domain with a module-finite integral closure

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbol_apply_eq_of_tameSymbolPreparation
declarations.doc:
**The tame symbol on a localization of a tame-symbol preparation.** At a maximal ideal `q` of
the finite extension produced by Stacks 0EAG, two members of the prepared family are unit multiples
of powers of the common parameter, with unit parts units of `B_q`; so the symbol of the two is

`∂_{B_q}(a i, a j) = ((-1) ^ (e_i e_j) ū_i ^ (e_j) v̄_j ^ (-e_i)) ^ m`,
`m = length_{B_q}(B_q / π_q B_q)`,

by Stacks 0EAL, 0EAM and 0EAN. The unit parts of a preparation are units of the very ring carrying
the symbol, so this is `Stacks.Chow.RegularTameSymbol.apply_eq_of_factorization` applied directly;
no passage between units of the base and units of a localization is involved.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbol_apply_eq_of_tameSymbolPreparation
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    {r : ℕ} {a : Fin r → A} (P : TameSymbolPreparation a B)
    (q : Ideal B) [q.IsMaximal]
    [IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime q)] [Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    (symb : RegularTameSymbol (Localization.AtPrime q))
    (i j : Fin r) (x y : nonZeroDivisors (Localization.AtPrime q))
    (hx : (x : Localization.AtPrime q) = algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q) (a i))
    (hy : (y : Localization.AtPrime q) = algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q) (a j)) :
    symb x y =
      ((-1) ^ (P.exponent q i * P.exponent q j) *
          Units.map (residue (Localization.AtPrime q)).toMonoidHom (P.factorUnit q i) ^
            P.exponent q j *
          (Units.map (residue (Localization.AtPrime q)).toMonoidHom
            (P.factorUnit q j))⁻¹ ^ P.exponent q i) ^
        (Ring.ord (Localization.AtPrime q) (P.parameter q)).toNat
declarations.comment: the factor at a single maximal ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.normPushforward_apply_eq_of_tameSymbolPreparation
declarations.doc:
**The tame symbol pushed back from a tame-symbol preparation to its base, evaluated on the
preparation's data.** The norm pushforward of Stacks 0EAT assembles the symbols on the
localizations of a finite extension into a symbol on the base; on the output of Stacks 0EAG each of
those symbols is the formula of
`Stacks.Chow.tameSymbol_apply_eq_of_tameSymbolPreparation`, so the symbol on the base is the
product of the norms of those formulas.

This is the passage the proof of Stacks 0EAW makes from the prepared finite extension back to the
ring it began with. The order-of-vanishing form of it, which is what that proof actually uses,
needs Algebra 02MJ at the residue fields and is not proved here.
declarations.statement:
theorem normPushforward_apply_eq_of_tameSymbolPreparation
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [Ring.KrullDimLE 1 A]
    {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B]
    [Fintype (MaximalSpectrum B)]
    [∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B, IsLocalHom (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))]
    [∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B, IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)]
    [∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B, Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)]
    (hass : ¬ IsAssociatedPrime (maximalIdeal A) B)
    (symb : ∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B, RegularTameSymbol (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B))
    (hquot : ∃ n : ℕ, maximalIdeal A ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A B) ≤
      LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap A B))
    {r : ℕ} {a : Fin r → A} (P : TameSymbolPreparation a B) (i j : Fin r)
    (x y : nonZeroDivisors A) (hx : (x : A) = a i) (hy : (y : A) = a j) :
    normPushforward hass symb hinj hquot x y =
      ∏ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
        Units.map (Algebra.norm (ResidueField A) :
            ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) →* ResidueField A)
          (((-1) ^ (P.exponent q.asIdeal i * P.exponent q.asIdeal j) *
              Units.map (residue (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)).toMonoidHom
                (P.factorUnit q.asIdeal i) ^ P.exponent q.asIdeal j *
              (Units.map (residue (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)).toMonoidHom
                (P.factorUnit q.asIdeal j))⁻¹ ^ P.exponent q.asIdeal i) ^
            (Ring.ord (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) (P.parameter q.asIdeal)).toNat)
declarations.comment: the product over the maximal ideals

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.normPushforwardOfIsIntegrallyClosed_apply_eq_symbolValue
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAQ for the tame symbol of a normal finite modification.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a
one-dimensional Noetherian local domain that is not a field and let `A ⊆ B` be module finite with
`B` an integrally closed domain and `B/A` annihilated by a power of `𝔪`. Let `P` be a
tame-symbol preparation of a family `a` over `B`, as produced by Stacks 0EAG: a local parameter
`π_𝔮` at each maximal ideal of `B` together with factorizations `a_i = u_{i, 𝔮} π_𝔮^{e_{i, 𝔮}}`
in `B_𝔮`. Then for two members `a i`, `a j` of the family, both nonzerodivisors of `A`,

`∂_A(a i, a j) = ∏_𝔮 Norm_{κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔪)}((-1)^{e_i e_j} ū_i^{e_j} ū_j^{-e_i})^{m_𝔮}`,

`m_𝔮 = length_{B_𝔮}(B_𝔮 / π_𝔮 B_𝔮)`, which is the displayed equation of the source.

`∂_A` on the left is this development's tame symbol
`Stacks.Chow.normPushforwardOfIsIntegrallyClosed`, not a symbol carried as a hypothesis: the
family of symbols on the localizations is the canonical one of a discrete valuation ring, and the
three remaining hypotheses of `Stacks.Chow.normPushforward_apply_eq_symbolValue` are consequences
of the finiteness of `A → B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem normPushforwardOfIsIntegrallyClosed_apply_eq_symbolValue
    [Fintype (MaximalSpectrum B)]
    [∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B, IsLocalHom (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))]
    (hA : ¬ IsField A) (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B))
    (hquot : ∃ n : ℕ, maximalIdeal A ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A B) ≤
      LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap A B))
    {r : ℕ} {a : Fin r → A} (P : TameSymbolPreparation a B) (i j : Fin r)
    (x y : nonZeroDivisors A) (hx : (x : A) = a i) (hy : (y : A) = a j) :
    normPushforwardOfIsIntegrallyClosed A B hA hinj hquot x y = P.symbolValue i j
declarations.comment:
for the tame symbol of a normal finite modification, on a preparation over that
modification

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.normPushforwardOfFiniteIntegralClosure_apply_eq_symbolValue
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAQ for the tame symbol on nonzerodivisors of `A`.** With `B` the integral closure
of `A` in its fraction field, the symbol of
`Stacks.Chow.normPushforwardOfIsIntegrallyClosed` is
`Stacks.Chow.normPushforwardOfFiniteIntegralClosure`, which depends on nothing but `A` and `K`;
so the displayed equation of the source holds for it, on a preparation over that integral
closure — for instance `Stacks.Chow.integralClosurePreparation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem normPushforwardOfFiniteIntegralClosure_apply_eq_symbolValue (hA : ¬ IsField A)
    {r : ℕ} {a : Fin r → A} (P : TameSymbolPreparation a (integralClosure A K)) (i j : Fin r)
    (x y : nonZeroDivisors A) (hx : (x : A) = a i) (hy : (y : A) = a j) :
    normPushforwardOfFiniteIntegralClosure A K hA x y = P.symbolValue i j
declarations.comment:
for the tame symbol on nonzerodivisors of A, on a preparation over the integral
closure of A in its fraction field

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure_apply_eq_symbolValue
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAQ, at the spelling of the source.** For a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain
`A` that is not a field and whose integral closure in its fraction field is module finite, the
tame symbol

`∂_A : Q(A)^* × Q(A)^* → κ(𝔪)^*`

of Stacks 0EAH — `Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure` — is given on a pair of
nonzerodivisors of `A` by the product of the source:

`∂_A(a₁, a₂) = ∏_j Norm_{κ(𝔪_j)/κ(𝔪)}((-1)^{e_{1,j} e_{2,j}} u_{1,j}^{e_{2,j}} u_{2,j}^{-e_{1,j}}
  mod 𝔪_j)^{m_j}`,

computed from any tame-symbol preparation of the pair over the integral closure. The extension of
a symbol on nonzerodivisors to `Q(A)^*` restricts back to it
(`Stacks.Chow.RegularTameSymbol.extend_regularFractionUnit`), so this is the previous statement
transported along `Stacks.Chow.regularFractionUnit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure_apply_eq_symbolValue (hA : ¬ IsField A)
    (Q : Type*) [CommRing Q] [Algebra A Q] [IsFractionRing A Q]
    {r : ℕ} {a : Fin r → A} (P : TameSymbolPreparation a (integralClosure A K)) (i j : Fin r)
    (x y : nonZeroDivisors A) (hx : (x : A) = a i) (hy : (y : A) = a j) :
    tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure A K hA Q (regularFractionUnit x) (regularFractionUnit y) =
      P.symbolValue i j
declarations.comment:
for the tame symbol on Q(A)^*, on a preparation over the integral closure of A in
its fraction field

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure_eq_symbolValue
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAQ with nothing assumed beyond the hypotheses on `A`.** For a one-dimensional
Noetherian local domain `A` that is not a field whose integral closure in its fraction field is
module finite, and for any finite family `a` of nonzerodivisors of `A`,

`∂_A(a i, a j) = ∏_j Norm_{κ(𝔪_j)/κ(𝔪)}((-1)^{e_{1,j} e_{2,j}} u_{1,j}^{e_{2,j}}
  u_{2,j}^{-e_{1,j}} mod 𝔪_j)^{m_j}`,

the preparation being the canonical one on the integral closure
(`Stacks.Chow.integralClosurePreparation`) and the symbol being
`Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure`, the map
`∂_A : Q(A)^* × Q(A)^* → κ(𝔪)^*` of Stacks 0EAH.

Nothing here is a hypothesis that the finiteness of `A → B` does not already give: the maximal
ideals of the integral closure are finite in number by
`Stacks.Length.finite_maximalSpectrum`, each localization is local over `A` by
`Stacks.Length.isLocalHom_algebraMap_localization`, and those are the two instances the product
of the source needs in order to be written down at all. They are supplied in the statement rather
than assumed, which is what distinguishes this from
`Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure_apply_eq_symbolValue`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure_eq_symbolValue (hA : ¬ IsField A)
    (Q : Type*) [CommRing Q] [Algebra A Q] [IsFractionRing A Q]
    {r : ℕ} (a : Fin r → A) (ha : ∀ i, a i ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) (i j : Fin r) :
    letI := Stacks.Length.finite_maximalSpectrum (A := A) (B := integralClosure A K)
    letI := Fintype.ofFinite (MaximalSpectrum (integralClosure A K))
    letI : ∀ q : MaximalSpectrum (integralClosure A K),
        IsLocalHom (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)) := fun q =>
      Stacks.Length.isLocalHom_algebraMap_localization q
    tameSymbolOfFiniteIntegralClosure A K hA Q
        (regularFractionUnit ⟨a i, ha i⟩) (regularFractionUnit ⟨a j, ha j⟩) =
      (integralClosurePreparation A K hA a ha).symbolValue i j
declarations.comment:
unconditionally for a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with a module-finite
integral closure: the symbol of Stacks 0EAH on Q(A)^*, the canonical preparation on the integral
closure, and no instance assumed that the finiteness of the extension does not supply

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolFormula_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAQ.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring of dimension one and `a₁, a₂ ∈ A`
nonzerodivisors. For every finite ring extension `A ⊆ B` with `B / A` annihilated by a power of
`𝔪`, every choice of nonzerodivisors `π_j ∈ B_j = B_{𝔪_j}` at the maximal ideals `𝔪_j` of `B`,
and every choice of factorizations `a_i = u_{i, j} π_j ^ {e_{i, j}}` in `B_j` with `u_{i, j}`
units and `e_{i, j} ≥ 0` — the data of Stacks 0EAG, bundled as `P` — the tame symbol is

`∂_A(a₁, a₂) = ∏_j Norm_{κ(𝔪_j)/κ(𝔪)}((-1)^{e_{1,j} e_{2,j}} u_{1,j}^{e_{2,j}} u_{2,j}^{-e_{1,j}}
  mod 𝔪_j) ^ {m_j}`,  `m_j = length_{B_j}(B_j / π_j B_j)`,

the product over the maximal ideals of `B`. The definition `Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolFormula` uses
one such choice; that every other choice gives the same element is Stacks 0EAR,
`AlgebraicGeometry.TameSymbolPreparation.symbolValue_eq_symbolValue`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbolFormula_eq (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) {a₁ a₂ : A}
    (ha₁ : IsRegular a₁) (ha₂ : IsRegular a₂) {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (P : TameSymbolPreparation ![a₁, a₂] B) :
    tameSymbolFormula hdim a₁ a₂ ha₁ ha₂ =
      ∏ᶠ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
        haveI := P.isLocalHom q
        Units.map (Algebra.norm (ResidueField A) :
            ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) →* ResidueField A)
          ((-1) ^ (P.exponent q.asIdeal 0 * P.exponent q.asIdeal 1) *
            Units.map (residue (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)).toMonoidHom
              (P.factorUnit q.asIdeal 0) ^ P.exponent q.asIdeal 1 *
            (Units.map (residue (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)).toMonoidHom
              (P.factorUnit q.asIdeal 1))⁻¹ ^ P.exponent q.asIdeal 0) ^
          (Module.length (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
            (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal ⧸ Ideal.span {P.parameter q.asIdeal})).toNat
declarations.comment: the tame symbol defined by the formula from one admissible extension, and equal to the displayed product for every admissible extension A ⊆ B and every choice of local factorizations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TameSymbolPreparation.symbolValue_eq_of_preparations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAR.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring and let `a` be a
family of elements of `A`, not all units, admitting a simultaneous power factorization after a
finite modification — that is, a `AlgebraicGeometry.TameSymbolPreparation`, which Stacks 0EAG
produces for any family of nonzerodivisors not all units. Then the right-hand side of the formula
Stacks 0EAQ,

`∏_𝔮 Norm_{κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔪)}((-1)^{e_i e_j} ū_i^{e_j} ū_j^{-e_i})^{m_𝔮}`,

depends on neither the finite modification nor the factorizations: two preparations of the same
family, over any two finite modifications, give the same element of `κ(𝔪)^*`.

This is the source's proof. The two modifications `A ⊆ B` and `A ⊆ B'` are compared through the
common refinement `C = (B ⊗_A B')/(𝔪`-power torsion`)`, built by
`Stacks.Chow.nonempty_commonRefinement`; against `C` the comparison is
`AlgebraicGeometry.TameSymbolPreparation.symbolValue_eq_of_common_refinement`, which regroups the
product over the maximal ideals of `C` into a product over those of `B` by transitivity of norms
(Stacks 0BIJ) and recognizes each fibre factor as the local factor of Stacks 0EAQ. The
nonzerodivisor the refinement is built from is a nonunit member of the family itself, which the
preparation makes regular
(`AlgebraicGeometry.TameSymbolPreparation.algebraMap_mem_nonZeroDivisors`), and every hypothesis of
Stacks 0EAT for `A ⊆ C` — at `A` and at each maximal ideal of `B` and of `B'` — is derived from
that.

Nothing is assumed. `AlgebraicGeometry.TameSymbolPreparation.symbolValue` cannot be written down
without a `Fintype` on the maximal spectrum of its extension and the locality of the structure map
at each maximal ideal, and those two are not hypotheses here either: each preparation proves them
itself, by `AlgebraicGeometry.TameSymbolPreparation.finite_maximalSpectrum` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.TameSymbolPreparation.isLocalHom`, and the statement below installs them from
the preparations rather than binding them. No generality is lost by fixing the `Fintype`: a type
has at most one of them (`Subsingleton (Fintype _)`), so the equation at the installed instance is
the equation at every instance.
declarations.statement:
theorem symbolValue_eq_of_preparations (hunit : ¬ ∀ i, IsUnit (a i))
    {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] {B' : Type w} [CommRing B'] [Algebra A B']
    (P : TameSymbolPreparation a B) (P' : TameSymbolPreparation a B') (i j : Fin r) :
    letI : Fintype (MaximalSpectrum B) := @Fintype.ofFinite _ P.finite_maximalSpectrum
    letI : ∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
      IsLocalHom (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)) := P.isLocalHom
    letI : Fintype (MaximalSpectrum B') := @Fintype.ofFinite _ P'.finite_maximalSpectrum
    letI : ∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B',
      IsLocalHom (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)) := P'.isLocalHom
    P.symbolValue i j = P'.symbolValue i j
declarations.comment: both clauses for the whole symbol: the value of the formula of Stacks 0EAQ depends neither on the choice of the local factorizations nor on the choice of B. Two arbitrary extensions B and B' of A, in unrelated universes, each carrying its own preparation of the family, give the same value; the common refinement that compares them is CONSTRUCTED here, by Stacks.Chow.nonempty_commonRefinement, not supposed. The hypotheses are the source's own: A Noetherian local of Krull dimension at most one, and the family not all units, which is the standing context of Stacks 0EAG in which the formula is written. The factorization clause alone, at a single maximal ideal, is Stacks.Chow.factorizationValue_eq_of_factorizations

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.factorizationValue_eq_of_factorizations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAR at a single maximal ideal: the formula Stacks 0EAQ does not depend on the chosen
local factorization.** If the two elements `a₁`, `a₂` of a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring
`R` admit simultaneous power factorizations against two nonzerodivisors `π` and `θ`,

`a₁ = u₁ π^{e₁} = v₁ θ^{f₁}`,  `a₂ = u₂ π^{e₂} = v₂ θ^{f₂}`,

with `u_i`, `v_i` units, then the two values of the formula agree.

This is the source's argument. Multiplicativity of the order of vanishing gives
`e_i m = f_i k` for `m = length_R(R/πR)` and `k = length_R(R/θR)`. Raising
`u₂^{e₁} a₁^{e₂} = u₁^{e₂} a₂^{e₁}` to the `m`-th power and `v₂^{f₁} a₁^{f₂} = v₁^{f₂} a₂^{f₁}`
to the `k`-th power and cancelling the nonzerodivisor `a₁^{e₂ m}` gives
`(u₁^{e₂} u₂^{-e₁})^m = (v₁^{f₂} v₂^{-f₁})^k` already in `R`. The signs agree because
`m e₁ e₂` is odd exactly when each of `m`, `e₁`, `e₂` is, and `e_i m = f_i k` turns that into
the same statement for `k`, `f₁`, `f₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorizationValue_eq_of_factorizations [IsNoetherianRing R] [Ring.KrullDimLE 1 R]
    {π θ : R} (hπ : π ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) (hθ : θ ∈ nonZeroDivisors R)
    {a₁ a₂ : R} {u₁ u₂ v₁ v₂ : Rˣ} {e₁ e₂ f₁ f₂ : ℕ}
    (hu₁ : a₁ = u₁ * π ^ e₁) (hu₂ : a₂ = u₂ * π ^ e₂)
    (hv₁ : a₁ = v₁ * θ ^ f₁) (hv₂ : a₂ = v₂ * θ ^ f₂) :
    factorizationValue π u₁ u₂ e₁ e₂ = factorizationValue θ v₁ v₂ f₁ f₂
declarations.comment: independence of the choice of the local factorizations, at a single maximal ideal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TameSymbolPreparation.symbolValue_eq_of_sameExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAR for the choice of local factorizations.** Two tame-symbol preparations of the
same family over the *same* finite extension `A ⊆ B` differ only in the local parameters, unit
parts and exponents they choose at each maximal ideal of `B`; by
`Stacks.Chow.factorizationValue_eq_of_factorizations` each factor of the formula Stacks 0EAQ is
unchanged, hence so is the product.

Independence of the choice of `B` is not proved; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem symbolValue_eq_of_sameExtension
    [∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B, IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)]
    [∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B, Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)]
    (P P' : TameSymbolPreparation a B) (i j : Fin r) :
    P.symbolValue i j = P'.symbolValue i j
declarations.comment:
independence of the choice of the local factorizations; independence of the choice
of B is not proved

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.factorizationValue_eq_of_factorizations_general
declarations.doc:
**The factorization half of Stacks 0EAR at a single maximal ideal, in an arbitrary local
ring.** The same identity as `Stacks.Chow.factorizationValue_eq_of_factorizations`, with `R`
neither Noetherian nor one-dimensional: the argument needs only that `π` and `θ` are
nonzerodivisors, so this is `Stacks.Chow.factorizationResidue_pow_ord_eq` read as a statement
about `Stacks.Chow.factorizationValue`. Since it implies the form at the Noetherian
one-dimensional local rings the source speaks of, namely
`Stacks.Chow.factorizationValue_eq_of_factorizations` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.TameSymbol.WellDefined`, it too carries Stacks 0EAR.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorizationValue_eq_of_factorizations_general
    {π θ : R} (hπ : π ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) (hθ : θ ∈ nonZeroDivisors R)
    {a₁ a₂ : R} {u₁ u₂ v₁ v₂ : Rˣ} {e₁ e₂ f₁ f₂ : ℕ}
    (hu₁ : a₁ = u₁ * π ^ e₁) (hu₂ : a₂ = u₂ * π ^ e₂)
    (hv₁ : a₁ = v₁ * θ ^ f₁) (hv₂ : a₂ = v₂ * θ ^ f₂) :
    factorizationValue π u₁ u₂ e₁ e₂ = factorizationValue θ v₁ v₂ f₁ f₂
declarations.comment: the first clause, at a single maximal ideal and in an ARBITRARY local ring: the value of the formula of Stacks 0EAQ does not depend on the choice of the local factorizations. This is strictly more general than the form the source states -- R is neither Noetherian nor one-dimensional here -- and Stacks.Chow.factorizationValue_eq_of_factorizations, the form at the rings of the source, is this statement specialised to them

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.RegularTameSymbol.extend
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAH, the tame symbol of a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring.** The symbol on
pairs of nonzerodivisors of `A` extends to the units of the total ring of fractions `Q(A)` by the
formula `∂_A(a/b, c/d) = ∂_A(a, c) ∂_A(a, d)⁻¹ ∂_A(b, c)⁻¹ ∂_A(b, d)`, and the extension
satisfies Stacks 0EAI, 0EAJ and 0EAK.

This is the "exercise" of Stacks 0EAH and the second half of Stacks 0EAS: the properties
Stacks 0EAL, 0EAM, 0EAN and 0EAP of the symbol on nonzerodivisors give the three properties of
the symbol on `Q(A)^*`. The symbol on nonzerodivisors is an argument here rather than the explicit
product of Stacks 0EAQ. The 0EAQ half — the first half of Stacks 0EAS — is supplied in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.TameSymbol.PairSymbol`, for an arbitrary one-dimensional
Noetherian local ring: `Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolValue` is the symbol of an arbitrary pair of
nonzerodivisors, `Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolValue_eq_symbolValue` identifies it with the product
formula of Stacks 0EAQ at every preparation, and `Stacks.Chow.formulaTameSymbol` feeds it through
this definition to deliver the map on `Q(A)^*`.
declarations.statement: def extend : TameSymbol A Q
declarations.comment: the passage from (4), (5), (6), (7) to (1), (2), (3), for a symbol on nonzerodivisors given as data rather than by the product formula of Stacks 0EAQ

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolValue_eq_symbolValue
declarations.doc:
**The function `Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolValue` is the formula Stacks 0EAQ, at every
preparation.** For any preparation of any family over any finite modification of `A`, in any
universe, the formula's value on two members of the family is the value of the function on those
two elements.

Nothing is assumed of the preparation. The two cases are the two clauses of the definition: where
the pair has a value, `AlgebraicGeometry.TameSymbolPreparation.symbolValue_eq_of_apply_eq`
identifies it with this one; where it has none, Stacks 0EAG forces the pair to be a pair of units,
and then both sides are `1`.

This is what makes the four identities below statements about *the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ*:
their subject `Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolValue` is here identified with the product formula
`∏_𝔮 Norm_{κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔪)}((-1)^{e_i e_j} ū_i^{e_j} ū_j^{-e_i})^{m_𝔮}` of Stacks 0EAQ at every
preparation at which that formula is written down.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbolValue_eq_symbolValue (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1)
    {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] {r : ℕ} {a : Fin r → A}
    (P : TameSymbolPreparation a B) (i j : Fin r) (x y : nonZeroDivisors A)
    (hx : (x : A) = a i) (hy : (y : A) = a j) :
    letI : Fintype (MaximalSpectrum B) := @Fintype.ofFinite _ P.finite_maximalSpectrum
    letI : ∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
      IsLocalHom (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)) := P.isLocalHom
    tameSymbolValue x y = P.symbolValue i j
declarations.comment: that the function of a pair whose properties (4), (5), (6), (7) are proved below is the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ: it is the product formula of Stacks 0EAQ at every preparation of every family, over an arbitrary one-dimensional Noetherian local ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolValue_mul_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAL in the first argument, for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ on arbitrary pairs of
nonzerodivisors.** `∂_A(a a', b) = ∂_A(a, b) ∂_A(a', b)`.

The four elements `a`, `a'`, `a a'` and `b` are prepared simultaneously
(`Stacks.Chow.exists_regularTameSymbol_apply_eq`) unless all four are units, and then the identity
is the first argument of `Stacks.Chow.RegularTameSymbol.map_mul_left` of that one symbol. If all
four are units each side is `1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbolValue_mul_left (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) (x x' y : nonZeroDivisors A) :
    tameSymbolValue (x * x') y = tameSymbolValue x y * tameSymbolValue x' y
declarations.comment: property (4) in the first argument, for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ as a function of an arbitrary pair of nonzerodivisors

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolValue_mul_right
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAL in the second argument, for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ on arbitrary pairs of
nonzerodivisors.** `∂_A(a, b b') = ∂_A(a, b) ∂_A(a, b')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbolValue_mul_right (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) (x y y' : nonZeroDivisors A) :
    tameSymbolValue x (y * y') = tameSymbolValue x y * tameSymbolValue x y'
declarations.comment: property (4) in the second argument, for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ as a function of an arbitrary pair of nonzerodivisors

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolValue_self
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAM for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ on arbitrary pairs of nonzerodivisors.**
`∂_A(b, b) = (-1)^m` with `m = length_A(A/bA)`. For `b` a unit both sides are `1`, since
`length_A(A/bA) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbolValue_self (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) (y : nonZeroDivisors A) :
    tameSymbolValue y y = (-1) ^ (Ring.ord A (y : A)).toNat
declarations.comment: property (5), for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ as a function of an arbitrary pair of nonzerodivisors

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolValue_unit_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAN for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ on arbitrary pairs of nonzerodivisors.**
`∂_A(u, b) = ū^m` with `m = length_A(A/bA)`, for `u` a unit of `A`. For `b` a unit both sides are
`1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbolValue_unit_left (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) (x y : nonZeroDivisors A) (u : Aˣ)
    (hu : (x : A) = u) :
    tameSymbolValue x y = Units.map (residue A).toMonoidHom u ^ (Ring.ord A (y : A)).toNat
declarations.comment: property (6), for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ as a function of an arbitrary pair of nonzerodivisors

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolValue_steinberg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAP for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ on arbitrary pairs of nonzerodivisors.**
`∂_A(a, b - a) ∂_A(b, b) = ∂_A(b, b - a) ∂_A(a, b)` for `a`, `b` and `b - a` nonzerodivisors. If
all three are units each of the four values is `1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbolValue_steinberg (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) (x y z : nonZeroDivisors A)
    (hz : (z : A) = (y : A) - (x : A)) :
    tameSymbolValue x z * tameSymbolValue y y = tameSymbolValue y z * tameSymbolValue x y
declarations.comment: property (7), for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ as a function of an arbitrary pair of nonzerodivisors

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.formulaTameSymbol
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAS, the map the formula Stacks 0EAQ gives on the total ring of fractions.** The
tame symbol

`∂_A : Q(A)^* × Q(A)^* → κ(𝔪)^*`

of Stacks 0EAH, satisfying Stacks 0EAI, 0EAJ and 0EAK, for an arbitrary one-dimensional Noetherian
local ring: the formula Stacks 0EAQ satisfies Stacks 0EAL, 0EAM, 0EAN and 0EAP on arbitrary pairs
of nonzerodivisors, so `Stacks.Chow.RegularTameSymbol.extend` extends it. On nonzerodivisors it is
the formula itself, by `Stacks.Chow.formulaTameSymbol_regularFractionUnit`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def formulaTameSymbol (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) (Q : Type v) [CommRing Q]
    [Algebra A Q] [IsFractionRing A Q] : TameSymbol A Q
declarations.comment: that the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ, as a function of an arbitrary pair of nonzerodivisors, hence gives a map on Q(A)^* satisfying (1), (2), (3)

registrations.name: Stacks.Chow.normPushforwardOfIsIntegrallyClosed
registrations.comment: that the product formula of Stacks 0EAQ satisfies (4), (5), (6), (7), for a local domain with a normal finite modification, where one extension serves every pair of nonzerodivisors

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolFormula_eq_finprod_norm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAT.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring of dimension one, let `A ⊆ B` be a
finite ring extension with `B / A` annihilated by a power of `𝔪` and `𝔪` not an associated prime
of `B`. For nonzerodivisors `a, b ∈ A`,

`∂_A(a, b) = ∏_j Norm_{κ(𝔪_j)/κ(𝔪)}(∂_{B_j}(a, b))`,

the product over the maximal ideals `𝔪_j` of `B`, `B_j = B_{𝔪_j}`, where `∂` is the tame symbol of
Stacks 0EAQ (`Stacks.Chow.tameSymbolFormula`) — on `A`, and on each `B_j`, which is again a
one-dimensional Noetherian local ring in which `a` and `b` are nonzerodivisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem tameSymbolFormula_eq_finprod_norm (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1)
    {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B))
    (hquot : ∃ n : ℕ, maximalIdeal A ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A B) ≤
      LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap A B))
    (hass : ¬ IsAssociatedPrime (maximalIdeal A) B) {a b : A} (ha : IsRegular a)
    (hb : IsRegular b) :
    tameSymbolFormula hdim a b ha hb =
      ∏ᶠ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
        haveI := Stacks.Length.isLocalHom_algebraMap_localization (A := A) q
        haveI : IsNoetherianRing B := IsNoetherianRing.of_finite A B
        Units.map (Algebra.norm (ResidueField A) :
            ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) →* ResidueField A)
          (tameSymbolFormula (ringKrullDim_localizationAtPrime_eq_one hdim hinj hass q)
            (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) a)
            (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) b)
            (isRegular_algebraMap_localizationAtPrime hdim hass q ha)
            (isRegular_algebraMap_localizationAtPrime hdim hass q hb))
declarations.comment: the displayed equation for the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAQ on A and on each local ring B_j

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.normProd_eq_prod_norm_normProd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAT.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring, let `A ⊆ B` be a
finite ring extension with `𝔪` not an associated prime of `B`, and let `B ⊆ C` be a further finite
extension with `𝔪` not an associated prime of `C`. Then

`∂_A(a, b) = ∏_𝔮 Norm_{κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔪)}(∂_{B_𝔮}(a, b))`,

the product being over the maximal ideals `𝔮` of `B`, where `∂_A` is the norm pushforward to `A`
of a family of tame symbols on the local rings of `C` and `∂_{B_𝔮}` is the norm pushforward of
the same family to `B_𝔮` along the semilocalization `C_𝔮`.

This is the source's proof: the maximal ideals of `C` are the maximal ideals of the
semilocalizations `C_𝔮`, whose local rings are the local rings of `C`, and transitivity of norms
for `κ(𝔪_{𝔮, v})/κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔪)` (Stacks 0BIJ) turns the product over the maximal ideals of `C` into
the iterated product.
declarations.statement:
theorem normProd_eq_prod_norm_normProd
    (hB : ¬ IsAssociatedPrime (maximalIdeal A) B)
    (hC : ¬ IsAssociatedPrime (maximalIdeal A) C)
    (hfibre : ∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
      ¬ IsAssociatedPrime (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))
        (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid C q.asIdeal.primeCompl)))
    (symb : ∀ r : MaximalSpectrum C, RegularTameSymbol (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal))
    (a b : nonZeroDivisors A) :
    normProd hC symb a b =
      ∏ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
        Units.map (Algebra.norm (ResidueField A) :
            ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) →* ResidueField A)
          (normProd (hfibre q) (fibreSymbol symb q)
            (toExtensionNonZeroDivisor hB q a) (toExtensionNonZeroDivisor hB q b))
declarations.comment:
the displayed equation, for both symbols read as the recipe of Stacks 0EAQ relative
to the common refinement C the statement quantifies over; the non-associated-prime hypothesis of
the source is imposed at each stage of the tower, and the correspondence between the maximal
ideals of C and those of B is derived here from the semilocalizations rather than assumed.
The spelling in which no refinement appears on the right-hand side is
Stacks.Chow.normProd_eq_prod_norm_tameSymbol

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.normPushforward_apply_eq_prod_norm_normPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAT between the two tame symbols the two sides define.** Both the norm pushforward
to `A` and each norm pushforward to `B_𝔮` are tame symbols in the sense of Stacks 0EAH, by
`Stacks.Chow.normPushforward`, and the displayed equation of Stacks 0EAT relates them.
declarations.statement:
theorem normPushforward_apply_eq_prod_norm_normPushforward [Module.Finite A C]
    (hB : ¬ IsAssociatedPrime (maximalIdeal A) B)
    (hC : ¬ IsAssociatedPrime (maximalIdeal A) C)
    (hfibre : ∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
      ¬ IsAssociatedPrime (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))
        (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid C q.asIdeal.primeCompl)))
    (symb : ∀ r : MaximalSpectrum C, RegularTameSymbol (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal))
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A C))
    (hquot : ∃ n : ℕ, maximalIdeal A ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A C) ≤
      LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap A C))
    (hinjFibre : ∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
      Function.Injective (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
        (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid C q.asIdeal.primeCompl))))
    (hquotFibre : ∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
      ∃ n : ℕ, maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) ^ n •
        (⊤ : Submodule (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
          (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid C q.asIdeal.primeCompl))) ≤
        LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
          (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid C q.asIdeal.primeCompl))))
    (a b : nonZeroDivisors A) :
    normPushforward hC symb hinj hquot a b =
      ∏ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
        Units.map (Algebra.norm (ResidueField A) :
            ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) →* ResidueField A)
          (normPushforward (hfibre q) (fibreSymbol symb q) (hinjFibre q) (hquotFibre q)
            (toExtensionNonZeroDivisor hB q a) (toExtensionNonZeroDivisor hB q b))
declarations.comment:
the displayed equation between the two tame symbols of Stacks 0EAH that the two
sides define, for the recipe of Stacks 0EAQ relative to the common refinement C the statement
quantifies over

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.prod_norm_factorizationValue_tower_maximalSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAT for the symbol the formula Stacks 0EAQ defines.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a
one-dimensional Noetherian local ring, let `A ⊆ B` be a finite ring extension and let `B ⊆ C` be a
further finite extension. Then

`∂_A(a, b) = ∏_j Norm_{κ(𝔪_j)/κ(𝔪)}(∂_{B_j}(a, b))`,

the product being over the maximal ideals `𝔪_j` of `B`, for both symbols read as the formula
Stacks 0EAQ attaches to the local factorization data on the local rings of `C`: the left-hand side
is the product over the maximal ideals of `C` of the residue-field norms down to `κ(𝔪)` of the
local factors, and the factor at `𝔪_j` on the right is the product over the maximal ideals of the
semilocalization `C_{𝔪_j}` of their norms down to `κ(𝔪_j)`. The two agree by transitivity of norms
for `κ(𝔪_{j,k})/κ(𝔪_j)/κ(𝔪)`, Stacks 0BIJ.

The correspondence between the maximal ideals of `C` and those of `B` — the content the source
takes from Stacks 0EAE — is *derived* here, from
`Stacks.Localization.prod_maximalSpectrum_eq_prod_prod`: the maximal ideals of `C` over `𝔪_j` are
the maximal ideals of the semilocalization `C_{𝔪_j}`, and the local ring of `C` at the one below
`v` is `Stacks.Chow.fibrePoint`. The tower `A → B_{𝔪_j} → C_{𝔪_{j,k}}` and the locality of its
structure maps are derived too, by instance resolution out of
`Localization.AtPrime.IsLiesOverAlgebra` and `Stacks.Chow.isLocalHom_fibreAlgebraMap`.

The statement quantifies over arbitrary local factorization data `(π, u₁, u₂, e₁, e₂)` on the
local rings of `C` rather than over data factoring two fixed elements of `A`, which is a
generalization and not a restriction: the elements `a` and `b` of the source enter the formula
only through that data, and the identity holds for all of it. The same equation between the two
tame symbols of Stacks 0EAH that the two sides define, rather than between the two products, is
`Stacks.Chow.normProd_eq_prod_norm_normProd` and
`Stacks.Chow.normPushforward_apply_eq_prod_norm_normPushforward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem prod_norm_factorizationValue_tower_maximalSpectrum
    (π : ∀ r : MaximalSpectrum C, Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal)
    (u₁ u₂ : ∀ r : MaximalSpectrum C, (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal)ˣ)
    (e₁ e₂ : MaximalSpectrum C → ℕ) :
    ∏ r : MaximalSpectrum C,
        Units.map (Algebra.norm (ResidueField A) :
            ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime r.asIdeal) →* ResidueField A)
          (factorizationValue (π r) (u₁ r) (u₂ r) (e₁ r) (e₂ r)) =
      ∏ q : MaximalSpectrum B,
        Units.map (Algebra.norm (ResidueField A) :
            ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) →* ResidueField A)
          (∏ s : MaximalSpectrum
              (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid C q.asIdeal.primeCompl)),
            Units.map (Algebra.norm (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)) :
                ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime (fibrePoint q s).asIdeal) →*
                  ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))
              (factorizationValue (π (fibrePoint q s)) (u₁ (fibrePoint q s))
                (u₂ (fibrePoint q s)) (e₁ (fibrePoint q s)) (e₂ (fibrePoint q s))))
declarations.comment: the displayed equation for the symbol as the formula of Stacks 0EAQ defines it, over the maximal ideals of the refinement C the statement quantifies over, and generalized to arbitrary local factorization data on the local rings of C. The correspondence between the maximal ideals of C and those of B (Stacks 0EAE) is derived here from the semilocalizations rather than assumed, as is the tower of local rings along a fibre

declarations.name: exists_finite_local_extension_with_prescribed_localizations
declarations.doc:
Finite modifications at the finitely many primes above a nonzerodivisor in a Noetherian local
ring come from one finite local modification.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_local_extension_with_prescribed_localizations
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {t : A} (_htm : t ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (ht : IsSMulRegular A t)
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (q : ι → Ideal A) (hq : ∀ i, (q i).IsPrime)
    (hq_ne : ∀ i, q i ≠ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (hq_inj : Function.Injective q)
    (hV : ∀ p : Ideal A, p.IsPrime →
      (t ∈ p ↔ p = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ∨ ∃ i, p = q i))
    (Bᵢ : ι → Type w) [∀ i, CommRing (Bᵢ i)]
    [∀ i, Algebra (Localization.AtPrime (q i)) (Bᵢ i)]
    [∀ i, Algebra A (Bᵢ i)]
    [∀ i, IsScalarTower A (Localization.AtPrime (q i)) (Bᵢ i)]
    (hinj : ∀ i, Function.Injective
      (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime (q i)) (Bᵢ i)))
    (hfinite : ∀ i, Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime (q i)) (Bᵢ i))
    (htorsion : ∀ i, ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ b : Bᵢ i, ∃ a : Localization.AtPrime (q i),
      algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime (q i)) (Bᵢ i) a =
