        algebraMap A (Bᵢ i) (t ^ n) * b) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B) (_ : IsLocalRing B)
      (_ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)),
      Function.Injective (algebraMap A B) ∧
      Module.Finite A B ∧
      Function.Bijective (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (algebraMap A B)) ∧
      (∃ n : ℕ, ∀ b : B, ∃ a : A,
        algebraMap A B a = algebraMap A B (t ^ n) * b) ∧
      ∃ ℓ : ∀ i, B →ₐ[A] Bᵢ i, ∀ i,
        letI := (ℓ i).toRingHom.toAlgebra
        IsLocalization ((q i).primeCompl.map (algebraMap A B)) (Bᵢ i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sum_ord_heightOneSymbol_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EAW.** Let `A` be a two-dimensional Noetherian local ring and let
`a, b` be nonzerodivisors of `A`. The orders of vanishing of the symbols `d_{A_𝔮}(a, b)` along
`A / 𝔮`, summed over the height-one primes `𝔮` of `A`, give zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem sum_ord_heightOneSymbol_eq_zero
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) {a b : A}
    (ha : a ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) (hb : b ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) :
    ∃ hquot : ∀ q : {q : Ideal A // q.IsPrime ∧ q.height = 1},
        Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (A ⧸ q.1),
    (∑ᶠ q : {q : Ideal A // q.IsPrime ∧ q.height = 1},
        letI : q.1.IsPrime := q.2.1
        letI := hquot q
        let d := heightOneSymbol q ha hb
        Multiplicative.toAdd (WithZero.unzero
          (x := Ring.ordFrac (A ⧸ q.1) (d : q.1.ResidueField))
          ((Units.isUnit d).map (Ring.ordFrac (A ⧸ q.1))).ne_zero)) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.finsum_fracTameSymbolOrderAt_canonical_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EAX: the Key Lemma.** Let `A` be a two-dimensional Noetherian local
domain with fraction field `K` and let `f, g ∈ K^*`. Then

`∑_{height(𝔮) = 1} ord_{A/𝔮}(∂_{A_𝔮}(f, g)) = 0`,

the sum being over the height-one primes of `A`, with `∂_{A_𝔮}` the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAH on
the one-dimensional Noetherian local ring `A_𝔮`
(`Stacks.Chow.canonicalHeightOneSymbol`). Only finitely many primes contribute, by
`Stacks.Chow.finite_fracTameSymbolOrderAt_support`, which is the first form the source gives the
statement in.

The proof is the source's:
`Stacks.Chow.fracTameSymbolOrderAt_finsum_eq_zero_of_forall_nonZeroDivisors` expands a pair of
fractions into four pairs of nonzerodivisors of `A`, and Stacks 0EAW
(`Stacks.Chow.finsum_tameSymbolOrderAt_canonical_eq_zero`) kills each of the four.
declarations.statement:
theorem finsum_fracTameSymbolOrderAt_canonical_eq_zero [IsDomain A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) (f g : (FractionRing A)ˣ) :
    ∑ᶠ p : HeightOnePrime A,
      fracTameSymbolOrderAt hdim p (canonicalHeightOneSymbol p) f g = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.finsum_heightOneOrd_tameSymbol_totalFraction_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EAX: the Key Lemma, for every two-dimensional Noetherian local
ring.** Let `A` be a two-dimensional Noetherian local ring, not necessarily a domain, with total
ring of fractions `Q(A)`, and let `f, g ∈ Q(A)^*`. Then

`∑_{height(𝔮) = 1} ord_{A/𝔮}(∂_{A_𝔮}(f, g)) = 0`,

the sum being over the height-one primes of `A`, with `∂_{A_𝔮}` the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAH on
the one-dimensional Noetherian local ring `A_𝔮`, applied to the images of `f` and `g` under
`Stacks.Chow.heightOneFractionMap`. Only finitely many terms are nonzero, by
`Stacks.Chow.finite_heightOneOrd_tameSymbol_totalFraction_support`.

The proof is the source's: writing `f = a / b`, `g = c / d` expands the sum into four reciprocity
sums of Stacks 0EAW, each of which vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem finsum_heightOneOrd_tameSymbol_totalFraction_eq_zero [IsLocalRing A]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) (f g : (FractionRing A)ˣ) :
    ∑ᶠ p : HeightOnePrime A, heightOneOrd hdim p
      (tameSymbolOfKrullDimOne (ringKrullDim_localization_heightOnePrime p)
        (FractionRing (Localization.AtPrime p.1.asIdeal))
        (Units.map (heightOneFractionMap p).toMonoidHom f)
        (Units.map (heightOneFractionMap p).toMonoidHom g)) = 0
declarations.comment: for every two-dimensional Noetherian local ring, on the total ring of fractions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sum_ord_localTameSymbol_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tags 02QJ and 0EAX.** Let `A` be a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain
with fraction field `K` and let `f, g` be units of `K`. The orders of vanishing of the tame
symbols `∂_{A_𝔮}(f, g)` along `A / 𝔮`, summed over the height-one primes `𝔮` of `A`, give zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem sum_ord_localTameSymbol_eq_zero
    {A : Type u} {K : Type v} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    [IsLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2)
    (f g : Kˣ) :
    ∃ (hquot : ∀ q : {q : Ideal A // q.IsPrime ∧ q.height = 1},
        Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (A ⧸ q.1)),
    (∑ᶠ q : {q : Ideal A // q.IsPrime ∧ q.height = 1},
        letI : q.1.IsPrime := q.2.1
        letI := hquot q
        let d := localTameSymbol q f g
        Multiplicative.toAdd (WithZero.unzero
          (x := Ring.ordFrac (A ⧸ q.1) (d : q.1.ResidueField))
          ((Units.isUnit d).map (Ring.ordFrac (A ⧸ q.1))).ne_zero)) = 0
declarations.comment: the second displayed form, the sum over all height-one primes

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dvrMilnorTameSymbol
declarations.doc:
**The tame symbol of a discrete valuation ring in every degree.** For a discrete
valuation ring `A` with fraction field `F` and residue field `κ`, and a uniformizer `ϖ`, the
homomorphism

`∂_A : K^M_{i+1}(F) ⟶ K^M_i(κ)`

of the remark. It is the coefficient of `ξ` in the image of the ring homomorphism
`Stacks.Chow.dvrMilnorShiftMap`, which sends a unit `f` of `F` to `{f ϖ ^ -v(f)} + v(f) ξ`; that
coefficient drops the degree by one. In degree two it is the tame symbol of Section 42.5
(`Stacks.Chow.dvrMilnorTameSymbol_degree_two`, the formula of Stacks 02Q6; and
`Stacks.Chow.dvrMilnorTameSymbol_milnorKTwoPureSymbol`, the comparison with
`Stacks.Chow.dvrRegularTameSymbol` itself), and it is characterized in general by
`Stacks.Chow.dvrMilnorTameSymbol_eq_zero_of_units` and
`Stacks.Chow.dvrMilnorTameSymbol_uniformizer`.

Only the discrete valuation ring case is proved here. The source's extension of `∂_A` to an
excellent local domain of dimension one is a citation to [Kato-Milnor-K], and its extension to an
arbitrary Noetherian local domain of dimension one is flagged in the source itself as a
conjecture ("presumably"); neither is formalized.
declarations.statement:
def dvrMilnorTameSymbol (hϖ : Irreducible ϖ) (i : ℕ) :
    MilnorKTheory F (i + 1) →+ MilnorKTheory (ResidueField A) i
declarations.comment: the tame symbol ∂_A : K^M_{i+1}(F) → K^M_i(κ) of a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field F and residue field κ, constructed as in Section 42.5

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dvrMilnorTameSymbol'
declarations.doc:
**The tame symbol `∂_A` of a discrete valuation ring, in every degree.** The map
of `Stacks.Chow.dvrMilnorTameSymbol` for an unspecified uniformizer, so that the statement names
no choice — as in the source, which asserts that a tame symbol exists rather than that it is
unique (Section 42.5: "We do not claim there is a unique map with these properties").
declarations.statement:
def dvrMilnorTameSymbol' (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (F : Type v) [Field F] [Algebra A F] [IsFractionRing A F] (i : ℕ) :
    MilnorKTheory F (i + 1) →+ MilnorKTheory (ResidueField A) i
declarations.comment: the existence of the tame symbol ∂_A : K^M_{i+1}(F) → K^M_i(κ) for A a discrete valuation ring, with no choice of uniformizer in the statement

declarations.name: milnorKTheoryOneAddEquiv
declarations.doc: The degree-one Milnor K-group of a field is its multiplicative group.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def milnorKTheoryOneAddEquiv (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    MilnorKTheory k 1 ≃+ Additive kˣ
declarations.comment: milnor_k_one

declarations.name: milnorKTwoEquivTensorProductQuotient
declarations.doc:
The second Milnor K-group is the tensor square of the group of units modulo the
Steinberg relations.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def milnorKTwoEquivTensorProductQuotient (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    MilnorKTheory k 2 ≃ₗ[ℤ]
      (TensorProduct ℤ (Additive kˣ) (Additive kˣ) ⧸
        milnorKTwoSteinbergSubmodule k)
declarations.comment: milnor_k_two

declarations.name: milnorKTheoryZeroAddEquiv
declarations.doc: The degree-zero Milnor K-group of a field is additively isomorphic to `ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def milnorKTheoryZeroAddEquiv (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    MilnorKTheory k 0 ≃+ ℤ
declarations.comment: milnor_k_zero

declarations.name: MilnorKTheory
declarations.doc:
The `n`th Milnor K-group of a field `k`, realized as the image of the degree-`n`
homogeneous component of the tensor algebra in its quotient by the Steinberg ideal.
declarations.statement: abbrev MilnorKTheory (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) : Type u
declarations.comment: milnor_k_theory_of_a_field

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_comp_pointwiseMilnorBoundary
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU9.** The three locally finite direct sums of Milnor K-groups of the tag form a
complex: the tame-symbol differential followed by the divisor differential of Stacks 0GU3 is the
zero homomorphism.

This is the assertion of the tag. By
`Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_comp_pointwiseMilnorBoundary_of_forall` it suffices to
check it one point of relative dimension `k + 2` and one point of relative dimension `k` at a
time, which is `Stacks.Chow.finsum_pointClosureOrdBoundaryTerm_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointwiseDivisorDifferential_comp_pointwiseMilnorBoundary (k : ℤ) :
    (pointwiseDivisorDifferential C p k).comp (pointwiseMilnorBoundary C p k) = 0
declarations.comment: the remark's closing sentence: the composition of the two displayed arrows is zero when i = 1 and j is arbitrary. The remark says this follows from Lemma 0EAX, and the proof here does run through 0EAX's content: it reduces to AlgebraicGeometry.sum_localMilnorBoundaryOrder_eq_zero at the two-dimensional local ring 𝒪_{closure {x}, y}, which reduces to AlgebraicGeometry.sum_ord_localTameSymbol_eq_zero -- the declaration registered for 0EAX, the vanishing of the sum of ord_{A/𝔮}(∂_{A_𝔮}(f, g)) over the height-one primes. The remark's preceding sentence, that it is not clear the composition is zero in general, is not a claim; for excellent X the remark cites [Kato-Milnor-K], and that citation is not formalized

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU3.** The divisor differential from pointwise Milnor K₁-chains at the points of
relative dimension `k + 1` to pointwise Milnor K₀-chains at the points of relative dimension `k`:
each Milnor K₁-class is read as a nonzero rational function on the closure of its point, and the
differential is the locally finite sum of the pushed-forward principal divisors, transported to
the pointwise description of cycles of Stacks 0GU2.
declarations.statement:
def pointwiseDivisorDifferential (k : ℤ) :
    PointwiseKOneGroup C p k →+ PointwiseCycleGroup C p k
declarations.comment: the second of the two arrows of the remark's displayed diagram, in the case i = 1: the map ⊕_{δ(x) = j} K^M_1(κ(x)) ⟶ ⊕_{δ(x) = j - 1} K^M_0(κ(x)), which on the identifications K^M_1(κ(x)) = κ(x)^* and K^M_0(κ(x)) = ℤ of the remark is the order of vanishing

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseMilnorBoundary
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU9.** The first differential of the complex of the tag: the homomorphism from the
locally finite direct sum of the degree-two Milnor K-groups at the points of relative dimension
`k + 2` to the locally finite direct sum of the degree-one Milnor K-groups at the points of
relative dimension `k + 1` whose coefficient at `x'` is the sum, over the points `x` of relative
dimension `k + 2` specializing to `x'`, of the tame-symbol boundaries
`∂_{𝒪_{closure {x}, x'}}` of the classes of the chain.
declarations.statement:
def pointwiseMilnorBoundary (k : ℤ) :
    PointwiseKTwoGroup C p k →+ PointwiseKOneGroup C p k
declarations.comment: the first of the two arrows of the remark's displayed diagram, in the case i = 1: the map ⊕_{δ(x) = j + 1} K^M_2(κ(x)) ⟶ ⊕_{δ(x) = j} K^M_1(κ(x)) which the remark builds out of the tame symbols ∂_A, taken here at the one-dimensional local rings 𝒪_{closure {x}, x'} of the Noetherian scheme X carrying the dimension function δ. For i ≥ 2 the same arrow needs the tame symbol in higher degrees at those local rings, which the remark takes from [Kato-Milnor-K]

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.milnorChainBoundary_comp_milnorChainBoundary_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAY, the case `i = 1`: the composition of the two displayed arrows is zero.** Let
`X` be locally of finite type over the base `(S, δ)` of chapter 42, with the induced dimension
function `δ_X` (the relative dimension, Stacks 02JW), and suppose the local rings of dimension
one of the closures of the points of `X` have finite normalization (as for `X` Nagata, in
particular excellent, which is the setting in which the remark constructs the tame symbols by
normalization and norm). Then for every `j` the composite

`⨁_{δ(x) = j + 2} K^M_2(κ(x)) ⟶ ⨁_{δ(x) = j + 1} K^M_1(κ(x)) ⟶ ⨁_{δ(x) = j} K^M_0(κ(x))`

of the arrows `Stacks.Chow.milnorChainBoundary` is zero. As the remark says, this follows from
Lemma 0EAX: the two arrows are the tame-symbol and divisor differentials of Stacks 0GU9
(`Stacks.Chow.milnorChainBoundary_one_apply_eq`, `Stacks.Chow.milnorChainBoundary_zero_eq`),
whose composite vanishes by the key lemma 0EAX
(`Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_comp_pointwiseMilnorBoundary`).
declarations.statement:
theorem milnorChainBoundary_comp_milnorChainBoundary_eq_zero
    (hfin : HasFiniteNormalizationPointClosureStalks X) (j : ℤ) :
    haveI := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian p
    (milnorChainBoundary (relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction p)
        (relativeDimension_lt_of_specializes C p) 0 j).comp
      (milnorChainBoundary (relativeDimension C.dimensionFunction p)
        (relativeDimension_lt_of_specializes C p) 1 (j + 1)) = 0
declarations.comment: the remark's closing sentence for the displayed arrows built from the tame symbols ∂_A by normalization and norm: when i = 1 and j is arbitrary the composition ⊕_{δ(x) = j + 2} K^M_2(κ(x)) ⟶ ⊕_{δ(x) = j + 1} K^M_1(κ(x)) ⟶ ⊕_{δ(x) = j} K^M_0(κ(x)) of the two arrows Stacks.Chow.milnorChainBoundary is zero, and it follows from Lemma 0EAX. Stated for X locally of finite type over the base of chapter 42 with the induced dimension function, and for X whose local rings of dimension one at the closures of points have finite normalization -- the case of a Nagata, in particular an excellent, X, which is the setting in which the remark constructs ∂_A by normalization and norm maps. There ∂_A is the tame symbol d_A of Section 42.5 in degree two and ord_A in degree one, so the arrows are the differentials of Stacks 0GU9, whose composite vanishes by Lemma 0EAX

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.dvrMilnorTameSymbol_one_eq_milnorKTwoTameSymbol
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAY: in degree two the tame symbol of a discrete valuation ring is the tame symbol of
Section 42.5.** For a discrete valuation ring `A` with fraction field `F` and any uniformizer `ϖ`,
the tame symbol `∂_A : K^M_2(F) → K^M_1(κ)` of the remark is the tame symbol `d_A` of Stacks 02Q1
descended to Milnor K-theory, as maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem dvrMilnorTameSymbol_one_eq_milnorKTwoTameSymbol {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra A F] [IsFractionRing A F]
    {ϖ : A} (hϖ : Irreducible ϖ) :
    dvrMilnorTameSymbol (F := F) hϖ 1 =
      milnorKTwoTameSymbol (A := A) (K := F) (IsDiscreteValuationRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one A)
declarations.comment: the tame symbol ∂_A : K^M_{i+1}(F) → K^M_i(κ) of a discrete valuation ring is defined as in Section 42.5: in degree i = 1 it is, as a map K^M_2(F) → K^M_1(κ) = κ^*, the tame symbol d_A of Section 42.5 (Stacks 02Q1) descended along the presentation of K^M_2, for every choice of uniformizer

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.sectionTameArrow
declarations.doc:
**The first displayed arrow of Stacks 0EAY at `i = 1`**, from the tame symbol of
Section 42.5.
declarations.statement:
def sectionTameArrow (j : ℤ) :
    DimMilnorChainGroup X δ (j + 1) (1 + 1) →+ DimMilnorChainGroup X δ j 1
declarations.comment: the first displayed arrow in the case i = 1: for a Noetherian (here: locally Noetherian) scheme X with a dimension function δ, the map ⊕_{δ(x) = j + 1} K^M_2(κ(x)) ⟶ ⊕_{δ(x) = j} K^M_1(κ(x)) whose coefficient at x' is the sum over the points x specializing to x' of the tame symbol ∂_A of Section 42.5 of the one-dimensional local ring A = 𝒪_{closure {x}, x'}

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.sectionOrdArrow
declarations.doc: **The second displayed arrow of Stacks 0EAY at `i = 1`**, from the order of vanishing.
declarations.statement:
def sectionOrdArrow (j : ℤ) :
    DimMilnorChainGroup X δ (j + 1) (0 + 1) →+ DimMilnorChainGroup X δ j 0
declarations.comment: the second displayed arrow in the case i = 1: for a Noetherian (here: locally Noetherian) scheme X with a dimension function δ, the map ⊕_{δ(x) = j + 1} K^M_1(κ(x)) ⟶ ⊕_{δ(x) = j} K^M_0(κ(x)) whose coefficient at x' is the sum over the points x specializing to x' of ∂_A = ord_A on κ(x)^* = K^M_1(κ(x)) for A = 𝒪_{closure {x}, x'}, with values in ℤ = K^M_0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.sectionOrdArrow_comp_sectionTameArrow_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EAY: at `i = 1` the composition of the two displayed arrows is zero.** For a
locally Noetherian scheme `X` with a dimension function `δ` and every `j`, the arrow
`⨁_{δ(x) = j + 2} K^M_2(κ(x)) → ⨁_{δ(x) = j + 1} K^M_1(κ(x))` built from the tame symbols of
Section 42.5 of the one-dimensional local rings `𝒪_{closure {x}, x'}`, followed by the arrow
`⨁_{δ(x) = j + 1} K^M_1(κ(x)) → ⨁_{δ(x) = j} K^M_0(κ(x))` built from their orders of vanishing, is
zero. As the remark says, this follows from Lemma 0EAX
(`AlgebraicGeometry.sum_localMilnorBoundaryOrder_eq_zero`).
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionOrdArrow_comp_sectionTameArrow_eq_zero (j : ℤ) :
    (sectionOrdArrow δ j).comp (sectionTameArrow δ (j + 1)) = 0
declarations.comment: the remark's closing sentence for the arrows of a Noetherian (here: locally Noetherian) scheme X with a dimension function δ: when i = 1 and j is arbitrary the composition ⊕_{δ(x) = j + 2} K^M_2(κ(x)) ⟶ ⊕_{δ(x) = j + 1} K^M_1(κ(x)) ⟶ ⊕_{δ(x) = j} K^M_0(κ(x)) of the two displayed arrows, built from the tame symbols ∂_A of Section 42.5 of the one-dimensional local rings A = 𝒪_{closure {x}, x'}, is zero; the proof runs through Lemma 0EAX at the two-dimensional local rings 𝒪_{closure {x}, y}. The remark's statement that it is not clear the composition is zero in general is not a claim, and the citation [Kato-Milnor-K] for excellent X is not formalized

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.oneDimTameSymbol
declarations.doc:
**The tame symbol `∂_A : K^M_{i+1}(F) → K^M_i(κ(A))` of a one-dimensional Noetherian local
domain `A` with fraction field `F`**, obtained from the tame symbols of the discrete valuation
rings `A'_𝔫` of its normalization by the norm maps `N_{κ(𝔫)/κ(A)}`.
declarations.statement:
def oneDimTameSymbol (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra A F] [IsFractionRing A F] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1)
    (i : ℕ) : MilnorKTheory F (i + 1) →+ MilnorKTheory (ResidueField A) i
declarations.comment: the extension of the tame symbol ∂_A : K^M_{i+1}(F) → K^M_i(κ) from discrete valuation rings to one-dimensional local domains using normalization and norm maps on K^M_i: for a Noetherian local domain A of dimension 1 with fraction field F, ∂_A is the sum over the maximal ideals 𝔫 of the normalization A' of N_{κ(𝔫)/κ} ∘ ∂_{A'_𝔫}, where A'_𝔫 is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field F and κ(𝔫)/κ is finite (Krull-Akizuki). This covers every Noetherian local domain of dimension 1, so in particular the excellent ones of the remark

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.oneDimTameSymbol_eq_dvrMilnorTameSymbol'
declarations.doc: **For a discrete valuation ring, `∂_A` is the tame symbol of Section 42.5.**
declarations.statement:
theorem oneDimTameSymbol_eq_dvrMilnorTameSymbol' (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra A F] [IsFractionRing A F]
    (i : ℕ) :
    oneDimTameSymbol A F (IsDiscreteValuationRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one A) i =
      dvrMilnorTameSymbol' A F i
declarations.comment: the general tame symbol extends the one of a discrete valuation ring: when A is a discrete valuation ring, the symbol obtained by normalization and norm is the tame symbol ∂_A : K^M_{i+1}(F) → K^M_i(κ) defined as in Section 42.5

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.milnorChainBoundary
declarations.doc:
**The arrow `⨁_{δ(x) = j + 1} K^M_{i+1}(κ(x)) → ⨁_{δ(x) = j} K^M_i(κ(x))`**, for a locally
Noetherian scheme `X` and a function `δ` strictly decreasing along proper specializations. The
coefficient at `x'` is the sum over the points `x` with `δ(x) = j + 1` specializing to `x'` of
`∂_{𝒪_{closure {x}, x'}}` applied to the class at `x`. A dimension function is strictly decreasing
along proper specializations (`DimensionFunction`, property (a)), and on a Noetherian scheme a
locally finite family is a finitely supported one
(`Stacks.Chow.mem_dimMilnorChainGroup_iff_finite`), so this is the arrow of the remark.
declarations.comment: the arrows of the remark's display, in every degree i: for a Noetherian scheme X with a dimension function δ, the map ⊕_{δ(x) = j + 1} K^M_{i+1}(κ(x)) ⟶ ⊕_{δ(x) = j} K^M_i(κ(x)) whose coefficient at x' is the sum over the points x with δ(x) = j + 1 specializing to x' of the tame symbol ∂_A, A = 𝒪_{closure {x}, x'}, applied to the class at x. Proved for X locally Noetherian and δ strictly decreasing along proper specializations, which includes the remark's setting; the second arrow of the display is the same map at (i - 1, j - 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologicalDimension_lt_of_le_of_le_jacobson
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian ring of dimension `d` and let `I ≤ I'` be ideals of `A` with `I'`
inside the Jacobson radical. If the cohomological dimension of `I'` is less than `d`, then the
cohomological dimension of `I` is less than `d` as well.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologicalDimension_lt_of_le_of_le_jacobson
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim A = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (I I' : Ideal A) (hII' : I ≤ I') (hI' : I' ≤ Ring.jacobson A)
    (hcd : cohomologicalDimension A I' (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I') < (d : ℤ)) :
    cohomologicalDimension A I (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I) < (d : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologicalDimension_lt_of_isZero_localCohomologyModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EB2 (Hartshorne–Lichtenbaum vanishing).** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring
of dimension `d` and let `I ⊆ A` be an ideal. If `H^d_{V(I)}(M) = 0` for some finite `A`-module
`M` whose support contains every irreducible component of `Spec A` of dimension `d`, then the
cohomological dimension of `I` in `A` is strictly less than `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologicalDimension_lt_of_isZero_localCohomologyModule
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim A = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (I : Ideal A)
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) [Module.Finite A M]
    (hM : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, IsMinimalPrime p.asIdeal →
      ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) → p ∈ Module.support A M)
    (hvan : IsZero
      (localCohomologyModule A I (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I) M (d : ℤ))) :
    cohomologicalDimension A I (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I) < (d : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.surjective_smul_top_localCohomologyModule_of_avoidsTopMinimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EB3.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring of Krull dimension `d`, let
`I ⊆ A` be a finitely generated ideal, let `Y = V(I)` and let `M` be a finite `A`-module. An
element `f ∈ A` lying outside every minimal prime `p` with `dim A/p = d` acts surjectively on
`H^d_Y(M)`.

The source assumes `A` local. That is not used: the dimension drop for `M/fM` and the vanishing
above the dimension of the support both hold over an arbitrary Noetherian ring, so the hypothesis
is dropped.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_smul_top_localCohomologyModule_of_avoidsTopMinimalPrimes
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim A = d) (f : A)
    (hf : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, IsMinimalPrime p.asIdeal →
      ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p.asIdeal) = d → f ∉ p.asIdeal)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) [Module.Finite A M] :
    Function.Surjective fun x : localCohomologyModule A I hI M (d : ℤ) => f • x

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologicalDimension_lt_of_isZero_homology_localCohomologyDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EB4.** Let `A` be a Noetherian local ring of dimension `d` with a
normalized dualizing complex `ω_A^•`, and let `I ⊆ A` be an ideal. If `H^0_{V(I)}(ω_A^•) = 0`,
then the cohomological dimension of `I` is strictly less than `d`.

Write `ω_A = H^{-d}(ω_A^•)`. Choose `f ∈ A` outside every minimal prime of dimension `d` which
annihilates `H^i(ω_A^•)` for `i > -d`; then `f` acts as zero on every homology object of
`U = τ_{≥ -d + 1}ω_A^•`, so `f • 𝟙_U` is nilpotent, and therefore a power of `f` annihilates
`H^{-1}_{V(I)}(U)`. The truncation triangle `ω_A[d] → ω_A^• → U` gives, after applying
`RΓ_{V(I)}`, the exact sequence `H^{-1}_{V(I)}(U) → H^0_{V(I)}(ω_A[d]) → H^0_{V(I)}(ω_A^•) = 0`,
so that same power of `f` annihilates `H^d_{V(I)}(ω_A)`. By Stacks 0EB3 multiplication by `f` is
surjective on `H^d_{V(I)}(ω_A)`, whence `H^d_{V(I)}(ω_A) = 0`, and `ω_A` is supported at every
`d`-dimensional minimal prime by Stacks 0A7V, so Stacks 0EB2 applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologicalDimension_lt_of_isZero_homology_localCohomologyDerived
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim A = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} K) (I : Ideal A)
    (hvan : IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
      ((localCohomologyDerived A I (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I)).obj K))) :
    cohomologicalDimension A I (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I) < (d : ℤ)

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_symbolicPower_le_pow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EB5.** Let `p` be a one-dimensional prime ideal in a complete
Noetherian local domain. For every `n ≥ 1`, some symbolic power `p⁽ᵐ⁾`, with `m ≥ n`, is
contained in the ordinary power `pⁿ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_symbolicPower_le_pow [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A]
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (hp : ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p) = 1)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∃ m : ℕ, n ≤ m ∧ Ideal.symbolicPower p m ≤ p ^ n

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologicalDimension_lt_of_minimalPrimes_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Hartshorne–Lichtenbaum vanishing.** Let `A` be a Noetherian
local ring with completion `A^∧` and let `I ⊆ A` be an ideal such that
`dim V(I A^∧ + 𝔭) ≥ 1` for every minimal prime `𝔭 ⊆ A^∧` of dimension `dim(A)`. Then the
cohomological dimension of `I` in `A` is strictly less than `dim(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologicalDimension_lt_of_minimalPrimes_adicCompletion
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim A = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (I : Ideal A)
    (h : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A),
      IsMinimalPrime q.asIdeal →
      ringKrullDim ((AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A) ⧸ q.asIdeal) =
        (d : WithBot ℕ∞) →
      (1 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤
        ringKrullDim ((AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A) ⧸
          (I.map (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A)) +
            q.asIdeal))) :
    cohomologicalDimension A I (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I) < (d : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologicalDimension_lt_of_isExcellent_of_isNormalRing
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0EB7].** Let `A` be an excellent normal Noetherian local ring of
dimension `d` and let `I ⊆ A` be an ideal with `dim V(I) ≥ 1`. Then the cohomological dimension
of `I` in `A` is strictly less than `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologicalDimension_lt_of_isExcellent_of_isNormalRing
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hA : IsExcellent A) (hnormal : IsNormalRing A)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim A = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : (1 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (A ⧸ I)) :
    cohomologicalDimension A I (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I) < (d : ℤ)
declarations.comment: cd(A, I) < dim(A)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.isAffineOpen_complZeroLocusOpen_of_isExcellent_of_isNormalRing
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0EB7].** For an excellent normal Noetherian local ring `A` of
dimension two and an ideal `I ⊆ A` with `dim V(I) ≥ 1`, the open `Spec A ∖ V(I)` is affine.

The cohomological dimension bound gives `cd(A, I) ≤ 1`, hence the vanishing of the cohomology of
every quasi-coherent module on the complement in degrees `≥ 1` by Stacks 0DX7; the complement is
quasi-compact, so Serre's criterion applies. This is the route of Stacks 0DXD.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineOpen_complZeroLocusOpen_of_isExcellent_of_isNormalRing
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hA : IsExcellent A) (hnormal : IsNormalRing A)
    (hd : ringKrullDim A = (2 : WithBot ℕ∞)) (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : (1 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (A ⧸ I)) :
    IsAffineOpen (complZeroLocusOpen A I)
declarations.comment: Spec(A) ∖ V(I) is affine when dim(A) = 2

declarations.name: isReflexive_of_exact_of_isReflexive_of_isTorsionFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EB8.** Let `R` be a Noetherian domain and let `0 → M → M' → M''` be an exact
sequence of finite `R`-modules. If `M'` is reflexive and `M''` is torsion-free, then `M` is
reflexive.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_of_exact_of_isReflexive_of_isTorsionFree
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type v} {M' : Type w} {M'' : Type x}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [Module.Finite R M']
    [AddCommGroup M''] [Module R M''] [Module.Finite R M'']
    (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (g : M' →ₗ[R] M'')
    (hf : Function.Injective f) (hfg : Function.Exact f g)
    (hM' : Module.IsReflexive R M') (hM'' : Module.IsTorsionFree R M'') :
    Module.IsReflexive R M

declarations.name: isReflexive_baseChange_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EB9.** A finite reflexive module over a Noetherian domain remains reflexive
after flat base change to a Noetherian domain. The base-changed module is automatically
finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_baseChange_of_flat
    {R : Type u} {R' : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    [IsDomain R] [IsDomain R'] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R']
    [Module.Flat R R'] {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] [Module.IsReflexive R M] :
    Module.IsReflexive R' (TensorProduct R R' M)

declarations.name: depth_localized_ge_two_and_propertyS2_of_isReflexive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EBA.** A finite reflexive module over a Noetherian commutative ring has depth at
least two at a prime whenever the localized ring does, and inherits Serre's condition `(S₂)`
from the ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem depth_localized_ge_two_and_propertyS2_of_isReflexive
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [Module.IsReflexive R M] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    ((2 : ℕ∞) ≤
        Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p)) (Localization.AtPrime p) →
      (2 : ℕ∞) ≤
        Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p)) (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M)) ∧
      (PropertySkRing R 2 → PropertySkModule R M 2)

declarations.name: mvPolynomial_adjoin_reflexive_propertyS2_module_not_propertyS2
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EBB.** The subalgebra `R = k[1, y, x², xy, x³]` of `k[x, y]` is a
Noetherian domain which is not `(S₂)`.  Both `R` and `k[x, y]` are reflexive as
`R`-modules, while `k[x, y]` is `(S₂)`.  Moreover, if
`m = (y, x², xy, x³)`, then the two successive `R`-duals of `k[x, y]` are `m`
and `k[x, y]`, respectively.
declarations.statement:
theorem mvPolynomial_adjoin_reflexive_propertyS2_module_not_propertyS2
    (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    let P := MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k
    let x : P := MvPolynomial.X 0
    let y : P := MvPolynomial.X 1
    let R : Subalgebra k P := Algebra.adjoin k {1, y, x ^ 2, x * y, x ^ 3}
    let m : Ideal R := Ideal.span {r | (r : P) ∈ ({y, x ^ 2, x * y, x ^ 3} : Set P)}
    ∃ (_ : IsNoetherianRing R) (_ : IsDomain R) (_ : Module.Finite R P),
      ∃ (dualPToM : Module.Dual R P ≃ₗ[R] m) (dualMToP : Module.Dual R m ≃ₗ[R] P),
        ¬ PropertySkRing R 2 ∧
          Module.IsReflexive R R ∧
          ¬ PropertySkModule R R 2 ∧
          (∀ (f : Module.Dual R P) (q : P),
            (↑(↑(dualPToM f) : R) : P) * q = (↑(f q) : P)) ∧
          (∀ (g : Module.Dual R m) (a : m),
            (↑(g a) : P) = dualMToP g * (↑(↑a : R) : P)) ∧
          Module.IsReflexive R P ∧
          PropertySkModule R P 2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.one_le_depth_stalk_internalHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EBC], part (1).** For coherent modules on a locally Noetherian scheme, the
stalk of `SheafHom(F, G)` at `x` has depth at least one as soon as `G_x` does.
declarations.statement:
public theorem one_le_depth_stalk_internalHom [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F G : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G]
    (H : SheafHom X.sheaf F G) (x : X)
    (hx : (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (G.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
      ((internalHomOf H).presheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.two_le_depth_stalk_internalHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EBC], part (2).** For coherent modules on a locally Noetherian scheme, the
stalk of `SheafHom(F, G)` at `x` has depth at least two as soon as `G_x` does.
declarations.statement:
public theorem two_le_depth_stalk_internalHom [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F G : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G]
    (H : SheafHom X.sheaf F G) (x : X)
    (hx : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (G.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
      ((internalHomOf H).presheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CohomologyColimitReduction.isAffine_of_isZero_cohomology_negative_tensorPower
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EBD].** Let `L` be an ample invertible module on a scheme `X` and let `n₀` be
an integer such that `Hᵖ(X, L^{⊗ -n}) = 0` for every `n ≥ n₀` and every `p > 0`. Then `X` is
affine.

Everything the dévissage of the tag needs beyond this hypothesis comes from ampleness itself:
quasi-compactness is part of ampleness and quasi-separatedness follows from it
([Stacks, Tag 01PV]), which makes the colimit reduction ([Stacks, Tag 01PG] with
[Stacks, Tag 01FF]) available and supplies a degree beyond which the cohomology of every
quasi-coherent module vanishes ([Stacks, Tag 071L], in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isZero_hgroup_top`); the dévissage sequence presenting a quasi-coherent
module of finite type as a quotient of a finite direct sum of negative twists of `L` is clause
(8) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3]; and the vanishing of `Hᵖ` on all quasi-coherent modules in all
positive degrees gives affineness by Serre's criterion ([Stacks, Tag 01XF]).
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_isZero_cohomology_negative_tensorPower (L : X.Modules)
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L) (n₀ : ℤ)
    (hvan : ∀ (n : ℤ) (p : ℕ), n₀ ≤ n → 0 < p →
      IsZero (Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ p (Stacks.Ample.tensorPowModule X L (-n)))) :
    IsAffine X

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CohomologyColimitReduction.isAffine_of_isZero_hgroup_unitModule
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EBE].** Let `X` be a quasi-affine scheme.  If `Hᵖ(X, 𝒪_X) = 0` for every
`p > 0`, then `X` is affine.

The source's argument verbatim: `𝒪_X` is an ample invertible module on a quasi-affine scheme
([Stacks, Tag 01QE], `Stacks.Ample.isAmple_unitModule_of_isQuasiAffine`), so affineness follows
from the vanishing of the higher cohomology of the negative twists of an ample module
([Stacks, Tag 0EBD], `isAffine_of_isZero_cohomology_negative_tensorPower`).  Tag 0EBD's family of
hypotheses collapses to this single one because the twists of `𝒪_X` are all `𝒪_X`, by
`isZero_hgroup_tensorPowModule_unitModule`; the threshold `n₀` is taken to be `0` and is
immaterial.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_isZero_hgroup_unitModule (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.IsQuasiAffine]
    (hvan : ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p →
      IsZero (Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ p (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))) :
    IsAffine X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBF.** The pullback of a coherent module along a morphism of schemes
with locally Noetherian source is coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCoherent_pullback
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (G : Y.Modules) [G.IsCoherent] :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G).IsCoherent
declarations.comment: coherence of the pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.isReflexive_pullback
declarations.doc:
**The reflexivity clause of Stacks, Tag 0EBF**: the pullback of a coherent reflexive module
along a flat morphism of integral locally Noetherian schemes is reflexive.

Reflexivity is checked on stalks by Tag 0AY3, on the target to read off reflexivity of the
stalks of `G` and on the source to put reflexivity of the stalks of `f^*G` back together;
coherence of `f^*G`, which the source half needs, is `AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback`,
and that declaration carries the coherence clause of the tag.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isReflexive_pullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f] (G : Y.Modules) [G.IsCoherent] (hG : IsReflexive G) :
    IsReflexive ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G)
declarations.comment: reflexivity of the pullback

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReflexive_of_exact_of_isReflexive_of_isTorsionFree
declarations.doc:
In an exact sequence `0 → ℱ → ℱ' → ℱ''` of coherent modules on an integral locally
Noetherian scheme, if `ℱ'` is reflexive and `ℱ''` is torsion free then `ℱ` is reflexive.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_of_exact_of_isReflexive_of_isTorsionFree {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] {F F' F'' : X.Modules} [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F'] [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F'']
    (f : F ⟶ F') (g : F' ⟶ F'') [Mono f] (hfg : f ≫ g = 0)
    (hexact : (ShortComplex.mk f g hfg).Exact) (hF' : IsReflexive F')
    (hF'' : (letI : F''.IsQuasicoherent := _root_.isQuasicoherent_of_isCoherent F'';
      IsTorsionFree F'')) :
    IsReflexive F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hullReflectionAdjunction
declarations.doc:
On an integral locally Noetherian scheme, taking reflexive hulls is a left adjoint of the
inclusion of the coherent reflexive modules into the coherent modules.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hullReflectionAdjunction : hullReflection X ⊣ inclusion X
declarations.comment: adjunction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentReflexiveModules_hasFiniteBiproducts
declarations.doc:
The coherent reflexive modules on an integral locally Noetherian scheme form an additive
category: they have finite direct sums.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance coherentReflexiveModules_hasFiniteBiproducts :
    HasFiniteBiproducts (CoherentReflexiveModules X)
declarations.comment: additive

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.internalHomObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBH.**  The sheaf Hom of two coherent reflexive modules, as a
coherent reflexive module: it is coherent by [Stacks, Tag 01Y2] and reflexive by
[Stacks, Tag 0AY4].
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def internalHomObj (G H : CoherentReflexiveModules X) :
    CoherentReflexiveModules X
declarations.comment: internal_hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.dualObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBH.**  Every coherent reflexive module has a dual object in the
category of coherent reflexive modules, namely `ℋom_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def dualObj (F : CoherentReflexiveModules X) : CoherentReflexiveModules X
declarations.comment: dual

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.isReflexive_kernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBH.**  The ordinary kernel of a morphism of coherent reflexive
modules is reflexive: it is the kernel of a map into the reflexive, hence torsion-free, module
`𝒢`.
declarations.statement: theorem isReflexive_kernel (f : F ⟶ G) : IsReflexive (kernel f.hom.hom)
declarations.comment: kernels

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.kernelIsKernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBH.**  The ordinary kernel, with its ordinary inclusion, is a
kernel in the category of coherent reflexive modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def kernelIsKernel (f : F ⟶ G) :
    IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (f := f) (kernelι f) (kernelι_comp f))
declarations.comment: kernels

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.cokernelIsCokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBH.**  The reflexive hull of the ordinary cokernel, with the
ordinary projection followed by the canonical map to the double dual, is a cokernel in the
category of coherent reflexive modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cokernelIsCokernel (f : F ⟶ G) :
    IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ (f := f) (cokernelπ f) (comp_cokernelπ f))
declarations.comment: cokernels

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.tensorObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBH.**  The tensor product of the category of coherent reflexive
modules: the reflexive hull of the ordinary tensor product.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tensorObj (F G : CoherentReflexiveModules X) : CoherentReflexiveModules X
declarations.comment: tensor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.tensorObjComm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBH.**  The tensor product of the category of coherent reflexive
modules is symmetric: the hull of the braiding of the ordinary tensor product.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorObjComm (F G : CoherentReflexiveModules X) :
    tensorObj F G ≅ tensorObj G F
declarations.comment: symmetry

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.tensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBH.**  The internal-Hom adjunction of the category of coherent
reflexive modules: morphisms out of the hull tensor product `ℱ ⊗_𝒞 𝒢` are morphisms of `ℱ` into
the internal Hom `ℋom_{𝒪_X}(𝒢, ℋ)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorHomEquiv (F G H : CoherentReflexiveModules X) :
    (tensorObj F G ⟶ H) ≃ (F ⟶ internalHomObj G H)
declarations.comment: internal_hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.tensorHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBH.**  The adjunction bijection is the currying map of
[Stacks, Tag 01CN], applied after restricting along the canonical map from the ordinary tensor
product to its double dual.  This pins the bijection down.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHomEquiv_apply (F G H : CoherentReflexiveModules X)
    (f : tensorObj F G ⟶ H) :
    (tensorHomEquiv F G H f).hom.hom =
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorHomEquiv X.toRingedSpace F.obj.obj G.obj.obj H.obj.obj
        (toDoubleDual ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u}
          ⟨((X.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((X.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (F.obj.obj)).obj
            (G.obj.obj))) ≫ f.hom.hom)
declarations.comment: internal_hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.tensorObjAssoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBH.**  The tensor product of the category of coherent reflexive
modules is associative.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorObjAssoc (F G K : CoherentReflexiveModules X) :
    tensorObj (tensorObj F G) K ≅ tensorObj F (tensorObj G K)
declarations.comment: associativity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReflexive_reflexiveHull
declarations.doc:
The reflexive hull `F^∨∨` of a coherent module on an integral locally Noetherian scheme is
reflexive: it is the dual of the coherent module `F^∨`, and duals of coherent modules are
reflexive.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_reflexiveHull (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] : IsReflexive (reflexiveHull F)
declarations.comment: hull

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.not_forall_fiberRank_one_tensorObj_dualObj_iso_unit
declarations.doc:
On an integral locally Noetherian scheme a coherent reflexive module of rank one at the
generic point need not have its dual as a tensor inverse for the hull tensor product.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_fiberRank_one_tensorObj_dualObj_iso_unit :
    ¬ ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
        (F : CoherentReflexiveModules X),
        Scheme.Modules.fiberRank (F.obj.obj : X.Modules) (genericPoint X) = 1 →
        Nonempty ((tensorObj F (dualObj F)).obj.obj ≅ unitModule X)
declarations.comment: unit_failure

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.not_forall_rank_one_sheafHom_iso_dualObj_tensorObj
declarations.doc:
On an integral locally Noetherian scheme the sheaf Hom of two coherent reflexive modules of
rank one at every point need not be the hull tensor product of the dual of the first with the
second.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_rank_one_sheafHom_iso_dualObj_tensorObj :
    ¬ ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
        (F G : CoherentReflexiveModules X),
        (∀ x : X, Module.rank (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          ((show X.Modules from F.obj.obj).presheaf.stalk x) = 1) →
        (∀ x : X, Module.rank (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          ((show X.Modules from G.obj.obj).presheaf.stalk x) = 1) →
        Nonempty (Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHomSpace X.toRingedSpace F.obj.obj G.obj.obj ≅
          (tensorObj (dualObj F) G).obj.obj)
declarations.comment: hom_failure

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveEquivalence.isCoherent_doubleDual
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01Y2] for the double dual.** The reflexive hull `F^∨∨` of a coherent module
on a locally Noetherian scheme is coherent.  This is the coherence half of the hull assertion of
[Stacks, Tag 0EBH].
declarations.comment: hull

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.InternalHomLocalKernel.reflexiveHullAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EBH.** On an integral locally Noetherian scheme the double-dual functor is
left adjoint to the inclusion of coherent reflexive modules into coherent modules, with the
canonical bidual map as its unit.

This is `reflexiveHullAdjunction_of_isLocallyStructureKernel` with its standing hypothesis
discharged by `isLocallyStructureKernel_dualSheaf_of_isCoherent`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def reflexiveHullAdjunction (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    { p : (Σ L : ReflexiveHull.CoherentModules X ⥤ ReflexiveHull.CoherentReflexiveModules X,
        L ⊣ ReflexiveHull.inclusion X) //
      ∀ F : ReflexiveHull.CoherentModules X,
        ∃ e : (p.1.obj F).obj.obj = ReflexiveModules.reflexiveHull F.obj,
          (p.2.unit.app F).hom ≫ eqToHom e =
            (ReflexiveModules.toReflexiveHull F.obj).1 }
declarations.comment: adjunction

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.depth_stalk_ge_two_of_isReflexive
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EBI], part (1).** A coherent reflexive module on a locally Noetherian
scheme has depth at least two at every point where the local ring does.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_stalk_ge_two_of_isReflexive [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    (hF : IsReflexive F) (x : X)
    (hx : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (F.presheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.sheafHasPropertySk_two_of_isReflexive
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EBI], part (2).** On a locally Noetherian scheme satisfying Serre's
condition `(S₂)`, every coherent reflexive module satisfies `(S₂)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sheafHasPropertySk_two_of_isReflexive [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    (hF : IsReflexive F) (hX : HasPropertySk X 2) :
    SheafHasPropertySk X F 2
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveStalkDepthTwo.two_le_depth_stalk_of_isCoherent_of_isReflexive
declarations.doc:
On a locally Noetherian scheme, a coherent reflexive module has depth at least two at every
point at which the structure sheaf has depth at least two.
declarations.statement:
theorem two_le_depth_stalk_of_isCoherent_of_isReflexive [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (G : X.Modules) (hc : G.IsCoherent) (hr : IsReflexive G) (x : X)
    (hx : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
      (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) G.val.presheaf x)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.reflexiveCoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBJ.** Restriction to an open subscheme whose complement
has structure-sheaf depth at least two is an equivalence on coherent reflexive modules;
its inverse is direct image. Both identifications are natural.

This is `reflexiveCoherentEquivalenceOfPushforward` with its one hypothesis discharged by
`isCoherent_and_isReflexive_pushforward`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def reflexiveCoherentEquivalence (X : Scheme.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (U : X.Opens)
    (hdepth : ∀ x : X, x ∉ (U : Set X) →
      (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    Σ e : ReflexiveCoherentModules X ≌ ReflexiveCoherentModules U.toScheme,
      (e.functor ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι
          (fun F : U.toScheme.Modules =>
            F.IsCoherent ∧ IsReflexive F) ≅
        ObjectProperty.ι
          (fun F : X.Modules => F.IsCoherent ∧ IsReflexive F) ⋙
          Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι) ×
      (e.inverse ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι
          (fun F : X.Modules => F.IsCoherent ∧ IsReflexive F) ≅
        ObjectProperty.ι
          (fun F : U.toScheme.Modules =>
            F.IsCoherent ∧ IsReflexive F) ⋙
          Scheme.Modules.pushforward U.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.isIso_dualTensorHullToSheafHom
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme and let `ℱ` and `𝒢` be coherent
reflexive `𝒪_X`-modules. Then the canonical map

`(ℋom_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒪_X) ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢)^∨∨ ⟶ ℋom_{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)`

is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_dualTensorHullToSheafHom (E F : X.Modules) [E.IsCoherent] [F.IsCoherent]
    (hE : IsReflexive E) (hF : IsReflexive F) :
    IsIso (dualTensorHullToSheafHom E F hF)
declarations.comment: the comparison (ℋom(ℱ, 𝒪_X) ⊗ 𝒢)^∨∨ → ℋom(ℱ, 𝒢) is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.rankOneSkeletonMul_toSkeleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBL.**  The product of two isomorphism classes of rank one coherent
reflexive modules is the class of `(ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢)^∨∨`.  This identifies the monoid law of
`rankOneSkeletonCommMonoid` with the rule the tag states, so the two together assert that that
rule is a commutative monoid law.
declarations.statement:
theorem rankOneSkeletonMul_toSkeleton (F G : RankOneReflexiveModules X) :
    rankOneSkeletonMul (toSkeleton F) (toSkeleton G) = toSkeleton (rankOneTensorObj F G)
declarations.comment: the monoid law is the double dual of the tensor product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.rankOneSkeletonCommMonoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBL, the monoid part of the group law.**  On an integral locally
Noetherian scheme the rule `ℱ, 𝒢 ↦ (ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢)^∨∨` is a commutative monoid law on the set of
isomorphism classes of rank one coherent reflexive `𝒪_X`-modules, with the class of the
structure sheaf as its unit.  Inverses are not provided; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rankOneSkeletonCommMonoid (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] : CommMonoid (Skeleton (RankOneReflexiveModules X))
declarations.comment: commutative monoid law on rank 1 coherent reflexive classes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.rankOneSkeletonCommGroup
declarations.doc:
On an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme the rule `ℱ, 𝒢 ↦ (ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢)^∨∨` is an
**abelian group law** on the set of isomorphism classes of rank one coherent reflexive
`𝒪_X`-modules.

Multiplication and unit are those of
`AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.rankOneSkeletonCommMonoid`, and the inverse of `[ℱ]` is the
class whose Weil divisor class is `-[ℱ]`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rankOneSkeletonCommGroup (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsNormal X] :
    CommGroup (Skeleton (RankOneReflexiveModules X))
declarations.comment: the abelian group law on isomorphism classes of rank 1 coherent reflexive modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_of_weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf_restrict_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBM, the injectivity clause.**  Let `X` be an integral locally
Noetherian normal scheme and `U ⊆ X` an open subscheme whose complement has codimension at least
two at every point.  Two coherent reflexive `𝒪_X`-modules whose restrictions to `U` are invertible
with the same Weil divisor class in `Cl(U)` are isomorphic.

This is the injectivity clause of the source's proof of Tag 0EBM, stated without the map that
clause is about: the first Chern class of `U` is injective by [Stacks, Tag 0BE8], so the two
restrictions are isomorphic, and restriction to `U` is an equivalence on coherent reflexive modules
by [Stacks, Tag 0EBJ], so the two modules are isomorphic on `X`.  The isomorphism that Tag 0EBM
itself asserts — between `Cl(X)` and the group of isomorphism classes of rank one coherent
reflexive `𝒪_X`-modules — is **not** proved here and no declaration claims it; see the
implementation notes for what is missing.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_of_weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf_restrict_eq {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsNormal X] (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ codimension (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton x))
    (M N : X.Modules) (hM : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent M) (hMr : IsReflexive M)
    (hN : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent N) (hNr : IsReflexive N)
    [hMU : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible U.toScheme.sheaf.obj U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.property
      (M.restrict U.ι)]
    [hNU : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible U.toScheme.sheaf.obj U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.property
      (N.restrict U.ι)]
    (hc : haveI : IsIntegral U.toScheme := isIntegral_of_two_le_codimension_compl U hU
      haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian U.toScheme := isLocallyNoetherian_of_isOpenImmersion U.ι
      weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf U.toScheme (M.restrict U.ι) =
        weilDivisorClassOfInvertibleSheaf U.toScheme (N.restrict U.ι)) :
    Nonempty (M ≅ N)
declarations.comment: the injectivity clause, with the two modules compared directly

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.rankOneSkeletonMulEquivWeilDivisorClass
declarations.doc:
On an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme the isomorphism classes of rank one coherent
reflexive `𝒪_X`-modules, under the monoid law `ℱ, 𝒢 ↦ (ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢)^∨∨` of [Stacks, Tag 0EBL],
are isomorphic to the Weil divisor class group `Cl(X)`, written multiplicatively.

The isomorphism is `AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.rankOneSkeletonToWeilClass`, which sends
a module to the class of its restriction to an open subscheme whose complement has codimension at
least two and on which it is invertible.
declarations.statement:
def rankOneSkeletonMulEquivWeilDivisorClass :
    Skeleton (RankOneReflexiveModules X) ≃* Multiplicative (weilDivisorClassGroup X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.isOpen_sectionIsomorphismLocus_and_nonempty_isColimit
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme, `ℱ` a rank one coherent reflexive
`𝒪_X`-module and `s ∈ Γ(X, ℱ)`.  The set `U = {x ∈ X | s : 𝒪_{X, x} → ℱ_x is an isomorphism}`
is open, so that `j : U → X` is an open subscheme, and

`j_*𝒪_U = colim (𝒪_X →ˢ ℱ →ˢ ℱ^{[2]} →ˢ ℱ^{[3]} →ˢ ⋯)`,

where `ℱ^{[1]} = ℱ` and `ℱ^{[n + 1]} = (ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℱ^{[n]})^{**}`: the cocone
`AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.sectionIsomorphismOpenCocone` on the directed system
`AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentReflexive.reflexivePowerModules` of reflexive powers under
multiplication by `s`, with vertex `j_*𝒪_U`, is a colimit cocone.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_sectionIsomorphismLocus_and_nonempty_isColimit (F : RankOneReflexiveModules X)
    (s : F.module.sections) :
    IsOpen (sectionIsomorphismLocus F.module s) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (sectionIsomorphismOpenCocone F.obj s))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexivePowers.reflexivePower
declarations.doc:
The reflexive powers of `ℱ`: `ℱ^{[1]} = ℱ` and `ℱ^{[n + 1]} = (ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℱ^{[n]})^{**}`; the
value at `0` is `𝒪_X`, the first term of the system `𝒪_X → ℱ → ℱ^{[2]} → ⋯`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def reflexivePower (F : X.Modules) : ℕ → X.Modules
declarations.comment: the reflexive powers ℱ^[1] = ℱ, ℱ^[n+1] = (ℱ ⊗ ℱ^[n])^{**}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_one_of_maximal_irreducible_compl_locus
declarations.doc:
Assumptions and notation as in [Stacks, Tag 0EBN]: `X` is an integral locally Noetherian normal
scheme, `ℱ` is a coherent reflexive `𝒪_X`-module of rank one, `s` is a global section of `ℱ`, and
`U = sectionIsomorphismLocus F s` is the open locus where `s` induces an isomorphism
`𝒪_{X, x} ⟶ ℱ_x`. If `s` is nonzero then every irreducible component `Z` of `X \ U` has codimension
one in `X`: `Z` is the closure of a point `ξ`, its generic point, and the local ring `𝒪_{X, ξ}` has
Krull dimension one, which is the codimension of `Z` in `X` by [Stacks, Tag 02IZ].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_one_of_maximal_irreducible_compl_locus [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsNormal X] (F : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] (hF : IsReflexive F)
    (hrank : Scheme.Modules.fiberRank F (genericPoint X) = 1)
    (s : F.sections) (hs : s.eval (Opposite.op (⊤ : X.Opens)) ≠ 0) {Z : Set X}
    (hZ : Maximal (fun Z : Set X =>
      IsIrreducible Z ∧ Z ⊆ (sectionIsomorphismLocus F s)ᶜ) Z) :
    ∃ ξ : X, closure {ξ} = Z ∧ ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk ξ) = 1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.codimension_eq_one_of_maximal_irreducible_compl_locus
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme, `ℱ` a coherent reflexive `𝒪_X`-module
of rank one, `s` a nonzero global section, and `U = sectionIsomorphismLocus ℱ s` the open locus of
[Stacks, Tag 0EBN] where `s` induces an isomorphism `𝒪_{X, x} ⟶ ℱ_x`. Then every irreducible
component `Z` of `X \ U` has codimension one in `X`, in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 02I3].
declarations.statement:
theorem codimension_eq_one_of_maximal_irreducible_compl_locus [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsNormal X] (F : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] (hF : IsReflexive F)
    (hrank : Scheme.Modules.fiberRank F (genericPoint X) = 1)
    (s : F.sections) (hs : s.eval (Opposite.op (⊤ : X.Opens)) ≠ 0)
    (Z : IrreducibleCloseds X)
    (hZ : Maximal (fun W : Set X =>
      IsIrreducible W ∧ W ⊆ (sectionIsomorphismLocus F s)ᶜ) (Z : Set X)) :
    codimension Z = 1
declarations.comment: every irreducible component of the complement of the isomorphism locus has codimension one in X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.objective_0EBQ
declarations.doc:
For `A` a Noetherian normal domain, `M` a finite reflexive `A`-module of rank one and `s ∈ M`
nonzero, the open `U` of [Stacks, Tag 0EBN] is the complement of `V(𝔭₁) ∪ ⋯ ∪ V(𝔭_r)` for the
height one primes `𝔭ᵢ` of `A` in the support of `M ⧸ A·s`, and `Γ(U, 𝒪_U)` is the colimit of the
reflexive powers `M^{[n]}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem objective_0EBQ (hrank : Module.rank R M = 1) {s : M} (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    ((AlgebraicGeometry.sectionIsomorphismOpen (Spec R) (tilde M)
          (tildeGlobalSection M s) : Set (Spec R)) =
        (heightOneSupportZeroLocus R s)ᶜ) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (moduleColimitCocone R M hrank hs))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveHeightOnePrimes.sectionIsomorphismPrimes_eq_compl_support
declarations.doc:
For `A` a Noetherian normal domain, `M` a finite reflexive `A`-module and `s ∈ M` nonzero, the
set of primes at which `s : A_𝔭 → M_𝔭` is an isomorphism is the complement of the support of
`M ⧸ A·s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionIsomorphismPrimes_eq_compl_support [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsIntegrallyClosed A] [Module.Finite A M] [Module.IsReflexive A M] {s : M} (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    sectionIsomorphismPrimes A s = (Module.support A (M ⧸ (A ∙ s)))ᶜ
declarations.comment:
the open U of Lemma 31.30.3, on Spec(A), identified with the complement of the
support of M/As; the identification of that support with V(p_1) ∪ … ∪ V(p_r) is Lemma 31.30.4
(Tag 0EBP)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveHeightOnePrimes.sectionIsomorphismPrimes_eq_compl_heightOneSupportZeroLocus
declarations.doc:
For `A` a Noetherian normal domain, `M` a finite reflexive `A`-module of rank one and `s ∈ M`
nonzero, `U = Spec(A) \ (V(𝔭₁) ∪ ⋯ ∪ V(𝔭_r))`, where `U` is the set of primes at which
`s : A_𝔭 → M_𝔭` is an isomorphism and `𝔭₁, …, 𝔭_r` are the height one primes of `A` in the support
of `M ⧸ A·s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionIsomorphismPrimes_eq_compl_heightOneSupportZeroLocus [IsDomain A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A] [Module.Finite A M] [Module.IsReflexive A M]
    (hrank : Module.rank A M = 1) {s : M} (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    sectionIsomorphismPrimes A s = (heightOneSupportZeroLocus A s)ᶜ
declarations.comment:
the first display, U = Spec(A) \ (V(p_1) ∪ … ∪ V(p_r)), unconditionally; the
colimit Γ(U, O_U) = colim M^[n] is AlgebraicGeometry.objective_0EBQ of
Divisors/Reflexive/ReflexiveColimitSections.lean

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.SectionLocusAffine.exists_pos_sectionPowStalk_mem_smul_maximalIdeal_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EBR], (1) ⇒ (2).** With `X`, `ℱ`, `s` and `U` as in [Stacks, Tag 0EBN]:
if the inclusion `j : U → X` is affine, then for every `x ∈ X \ U` there is an `n > 0` with
`sⁿ ∈ 𝔪_x ℱ^{[n]}_x`.

The hypotheses are the source's: `X` integral, locally Noetherian and normal, `ℱ` coherent,
reflexive (`hF`) and of rank one (`hrank`, the fibre rank at the generic point), and `s` a global
section.  The reflexive powers, the multiplication by `s` and the power `sⁿ` are the constructed
ones of `ReflexivePowers.lean`.

If `s = 0` then `s¹ = 0` lies in every submodule and there is nothing to prove.  Otherwise `U`
contains the generic point, so the colimit clause of [Stacks, Tag 0EBN] is available at `x`; the
inverse image `U_x` of `U` under `f_x : Spec 𝒪_{X, x} ⟶ X` is affine because affineness of a
morphism is stable under base change, and it misses the closed point because `f_x` carries the
closed point to `x ∉ U`; so `𝔪_x Γ(U_x, 𝒪_{U_x})` is the unit ideal, and the colimit argument
`exists_pos_powElt_mem_smul` extracts the positive power.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pos_sectionPowStalk_mem_smul_maximalIdeal_of_isAffineHom
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsNormal X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (hF : ReflexiveModules.IsReflexive F)
    (hrank : Scheme.Modules.fiberRank F (genericPoint X) = 1) (s : F.sections)
    (hj : IsAffineHom (AlgebraicGeometry.sectionIsomorphismOpen X F s).ι)
    (x : X) (hx : x ∉ AlgebraicGeometry.sectionIsomorphismOpen X F s) :
    ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ sectionPowStalk X F s x n ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ↑(X.presheaf.stalk x) •
      (⊤ : Submodule ↑(X.presheaf.stalk x) (reflexivePowerStalk F x n))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.SectionLocusAffine.isAffineHom_of_forall_exists_pos_sectionPowStalk_mem_smul_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EBR], (2) ⇒ (1).** With `X`, `ℱ`, `s` and `U` as in [Stacks, Tag 0EBN]:
if for every `x ∈ X \ U` there is an `n > 0` with `sⁿ ∈ 𝔪_x ℱ^{[n]}_x`, then the inclusion
`j : U → X` is affine.

If `s = 0` then `U` is empty (`isEmpty_sectionIsomorphismLocus_of_eval_eq_zero`) and the
inclusion of an empty open subscheme is affine.  Otherwise `U` contains the generic point, the
colimit clause of [Stacks, Tag 0EBN] identifies `(j_*𝒪_U)_x` with `colim ℱ^{[n]}_x`, and
`mem_smul_of_powElt_mem_smul` carries clause (2) over to `1 ∈ 𝔪_x (j_*𝒪_U)_x`, which is
`𝔪_x (j_*𝒪_U)_x = (j_*𝒪_U)_x`, at every point off `U`.  That is exactly the hypothesis of
`AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_of_forall_map_maximalIdeal_eq_top`, the relative-spectrum form of
the second half of the source's proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_of_forall_exists_pos_sectionPowStalk_mem_smul_maximalIdeal
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsNormal X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (hF : ReflexiveModules.IsReflexive F)
    (hrank : Scheme.Modules.fiberRank F (genericPoint X) = 1) (s : F.sections)
    (h₂ : ∀ x : X, x ∉ AlgebraicGeometry.sectionIsomorphismOpen X F s →
      ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ sectionPowStalk X F s x n ∈
        IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ↑(X.presheaf.stalk x) •
          (⊤ : Submodule ↑(X.presheaf.stalk x) (reflexivePowerStalk F x n))) :
    IsAffineHom (AlgebraicGeometry.sectionIsomorphismOpen X F s).ι

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_relativeFrobenius_of_etale
declarations.doc: The relative Frobenius of an étale scheme is an isomorphism.

declarations.name: Dualizing.LocalDuality.isZero_tor_injectiveHull_residueField_of_ne_dimension
declarations.doc:
For `(A, 𝔪, κ)` a Noetherian local Gorenstein ring of dimension `d` and `E` an injective hull
of `κ`, the group `Tor_i^A(E, κ)` vanishes for every `i ≠ d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_tor_injectiveHull_residueField_of_ne_dimension
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hA : IsGorensteinLocalRing A) (d : ℕ) (hdim : ringKrullDim A = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (E : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (j : ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) ⟶ E) [Mono j]
    (hj : Module.IsInjectiveHull j) (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≠ d) :
    IsZero (((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj E).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)))
declarations.comment: vanishing away from the dimension

declarations.name: Dualizing.LocalDuality.tor_injectiveHull_residueField_iso_of_eq_dimension
declarations.doc:
For `(A, 𝔪, κ)` a Noetherian local Gorenstein ring of dimension `d` and `E` an injective hull
of `κ`, the group `Tor_d^A(E, κ)` is isomorphic to `κ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tor_injectiveHull_residueField_iso_of_eq_dimension
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hA : IsGorensteinLocalRing A) (d : ℕ) (hdim : ringKrullDim A = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (E : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (j : ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) ⟶ E) [Mono j]
    (hj : Module.IsInjectiveHull j) :
    Nonempty ((((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} A) d).obj E).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A))) ≅
      ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A))
declarations.comment: the Tor group in the dimension

declarations.name: free_of_frobenius_baseChange_equiv
declarations.doc: A finite Frobenius-periodic module over a Noetherian local ring is free.
declarations.statement:
theorem free_of_frobenius_baseChange_equiv
    {A : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP A p]
    (h : Nonempty (frobeniusBaseChange A p M ≃ₗ[A] M)) :
    Module.Free A M

declarations.name: isIdealIndependent_snoc_left_of_mul
declarations.doc:
If an ideal-independent finite family ends in `x * y`, replacing its last member by
`x` gives another ideal-independent family.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIdealIndependent_snoc_left_of_mul {A : Type*} [CommRing A] {n : ℕ}
    (f : Fin n → A) (x y : A)
    (h : IsIdealIndependent (Fin.snoc f (x * y))) :
    IsIdealIndependent (Fin.snoc f x)

declarations.name: length_quotient_eq_add_of_isIndependent_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBX.** If appending `f * g` to a list gives an independent list,
then the length of the quotient by that list is the sum of the lengths of the quotients obtained
by appending `f` and `g` separately.
declarations.statement:
lemma length_quotient_eq_add_of_isIndependent_mul (init : List A) (f g : A)
    (h : IsIdealIndependent (fun i : Fin (init ++ [f * g]).length ↦
      (init ++ [f * g])[i])) :
    Module.length A (A ⧸ Ideal.ofList (init ++ [f * g])) =
      Module.length A (A ⧸ Ideal.ofList (init ++ [f])) +
        Module.length A (A ⧸ Ideal.ofList (init ++ [g]))

declarations.name: length_quotient_span_powers_eq_prod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EBY.** If `x` generates the maximal ideal of a local ring and
the positive powers `x i ^ e i` are independent, then the quotient by those powers has length
equal to the product of the exponents.
declarations.statement:
lemma length_quotient_span_powers_eq_prod {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {r : ℕ} (x : Fin r → A) (e : Fin r → ℕ)
    (hx : Ideal.span (Set.range x) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    (he : ∀ i, 0 < e i)
    (hind : ∀ (a : Fin r → A), (∑ i, a i * x i ^ e i) = 0 →
      ∀ i, a i ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range fun j ↦ x j ^ e j)) :
    Module.length A (A ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range fun i ↦ x i ^ e i)) =
      ((∏ i, e i : ℕ) : ℕ∞)

declarations.name: isIdealIndependent_map_of_flat
declarations.doc: The image of an ideal-independent family under a flat ring map is ideal-independent.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIdealIndependent_map_of_flat
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    {ι : Type w} (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : RingHom.Flat φ)
    {f : ι → A} (hf : IsIdealIndependent f) :
    IsIdealIndependent (fun i ↦ φ (f i))

declarations.name: isRegularRing_iff_frobeniusOfPrime_flat
declarations.doc:
**Kunz's theorem.** If a prime number vanishes in a Noetherian ring, the ring is regular if
and only if its Frobenius endomorphism is flat.
declarations.statement:
lemma isRegularRing_iff_frobeniusOfPrime_flat {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hchar : (p : A) = 0) :
    IsRegularRing A ↔ RingHom.Flat (frobeniusOfPrime p hp hchar)

declarations.name: MvPowerSeries.exists_linearEquiv_directSum_injectiveHull_of_leibniz
declarations.doc:
A maximal-ideal-power-torsion module over a characteristic-zero formal power series ring,
equipped with additive operators satisfying the partial-derivative Leibniz rules, is a direct sum
of copies of an injective hull of the residue field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_linearEquiv_directSum_injectiveHull_of_leibniz
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharZero k]
    (d : ℕ) (_hd : 0 < d)
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k) M]
    (E : Type u) [AddCommGroup E] [Module (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k) E]
    (i : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars
        (MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff : MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k →+* k)).obj
          (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ ModuleCat.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k) E)
    [Mono i]
    (_hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i)
    (_hM : IsIPowerTorsion (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k) M
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k)))
    (D : Fin d → M →+ M)
    (_hD : ∀ (j : Fin d) (f : MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k) (z : M),
      D j (f • z) = MvPowerSeries.pderiv (R := k) j f • z + f • D j z) :
    ∃ J : Type v, Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k] ⨁ _ : J, E)

declarations.name: Dualizing.isIPowerTorsion_frobeniusStable_exists_equiv_directSum_injectiveHull
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EC3.** A maximal-ideal-power-torsion module over a regular local ring
of prime characteristic which is invariant under extension of scalars by Frobenius is a direct
sum of copies of the injective hull of the residue field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIPowerTorsion_frobeniusStable_exists_equiv_directSum_injectiveHull
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hchar : (p : A) = 0)
    (M : Type (max u v)) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (hM : IsIPowerTorsion A M (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A))
    (hF : (ModuleCat.extendScalars (frobeniusOfPrime p hp hchar)).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A M) ≅ ModuleCat.of A M)
    (E : Type u) [AddCommGroup E] [Module A E]
    (i : ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) ⟶ ModuleCat.of A E) [Mono i]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) :
    ∃ J : Type (max u v), Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[A] ⨁ _ : J, E)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.derivationOperator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EC5.** A derivation `θ` of `A` induces a canonical additive operator on
each local cohomology module `H^i_{V(I)}(A)`, satisfying the Leibniz rule
`D (a x) = θ(a) x + a D(x)`. It is characterized on Čech cohomology classes by the unique
extensions of `θ` to the localizations appearing in the Čech complex, for every finite generating
family of `I`; `Stacks.LocalCohomology.DerivationOperator.ext` is the uniqueness this
characterization provides.
declarations.statement:
def derivationOperator (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (θ : Derivation ℤ A A) (i : ℕ) : DerivationOperator A I hI i θ

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyOfRing_frobeniusIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EC6.** For a commutative ring `A` in which a prime `p` vanishes and a
finitely generated ideal `I`, derived extension of scalars along the Frobenius endomorphism
fixes the local cohomology `RΓ_{V(I)}(A)` of the regular module up to isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
def localCohomologyOfRing_frobeniusIso (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hp0 : (p : A) = 0) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    (derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u} (frobeniusOfNatCastEqZero A p hp hp0)).functor.obj
        ((localCohomologyDerived A I hI).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of A A))) ≅
      (localCohomologyDerived A I hI).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of A A))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleDerivation.subsingleton_sheafDerivation
declarations.doc:
The affine-normalized, restriction-compatible extension of a base derivation to the
structure sheaf is unique.
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleDerivation.nonempty_twistedDerivation
declarations.doc:
An absolute derivation of the base ring extends to an affine-normalized derivation of the
structure sheaf of a quasi-compact, quasi-separated étale scheme. In every degree its induced
additive operator on the canonical cohomology module satisfies the twisted Leibniz rule.
declarations.comment: existence and Leibniz rule

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleFrobenius.nonempty_extendScalarsDerived_derivedGlobalSections_iso
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be a prime number, let `A` be a commutative ring in which `p` vanishes and let
`F : A → A`, `a ↦ aᵖ`, be its Frobenius endomorphism. Assuming cohomology and base change
`Stacks.EtaleFrobenius.DerivedGlobalSectionsBaseChange A`, for a quasi-compact, quasi-separated,
étale scheme `V` over `Spec A` there is an isomorphism

`RΓ(V, 𝒪_V) ⊗^L_{A, F} A ≅ RΓ(V, 𝒪_V)`

in `D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_extendScalarsDerived_derivedGlobalSections_iso
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [Etale f]
    (hbc : DerivedGlobalSectionsBaseChange A) :
    Nonempty ((StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.extendScalarsDerived
        (Stacks.LocalCohomology.frobeniusOfNatCastEqZero A p Fact.out hp0)).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj (derivedStructureSheaf V)) ≅
      (derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj (derivedStructureSheaf V))
declarations.comment: cohomology and base change is the explicit hypothesis `Stacks.EtaleFrobenius.DerivedGlobalSectionsBaseChange A`, namely Stacks 08IB for the structure sheaf over an affine base: for every ring map out of `A` and every Cartesian square over its spectrum whose left-hand morphism is flat, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, derived extension of scalars carries the derived global sections of the source to those of the base change. The library carries the base change morphism of Stacks 08HY but not its invertibility in Tor-independent generality, whose globalization step is Stacks 0DJ9. Everything else is proved: the Cartesian square supplied to that hypothesis is the absolute Frobenius square of `V`, Cartesian by Stacks 0EBS

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleFrobenius.nonempty_extendScalarsDerived_derivedGlobalSections_iso_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EC9.** Let `p` be a prime number, let `A` be a commutative ring in
which `p` vanishes and let `F : A → A`, `a ↦ aᵖ`, be its Frobenius endomorphism. If
`V ⟶ Spec A` is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and étale, then there exists an isomorphism

`RΓ(V, 𝒪_V) ⊗^L_{A, F} A ≅ RΓ(V, 𝒪_V)`

in `D(A)`.

The relative Frobenius of `V` is an isomorphism ([Stacks, Tag 0EBS]), so the absolute Frobenius
square of `V` is cartesian, and cohomology and base change for the flat morphism `V ⟶ Spec A`
(`derivedGlobalSectionsBaseChange`, [Stacks, Tag 08IB]) applies to it.
