declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.HyperplaneTwistSequence.pullbackTwistModuleIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EGK], the twist of a module restricted to the closed subscheme.**
`i^*(ℱ(d)) ≅ (i^*ℱ)(d)`, the twist on `H` being taken with respect to `i^*L`.  This is
[Stacks, Tag 01CD] for the tensor product followed by `pullbackTensorPowModuleIntIso` for the
tensor power.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackTwistModuleIso (d : ℤ) :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj (twistModule X L F d) ≅
      twistModule Hy ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj F) d
declarations.comment: the twist of a module restricted to the hyperplane: i^*(F(d)) = (i^*F)(d)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.HyperplaneTwistSequence.pushforwardTwistModuleIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EGK], the projection formula clause.**
`i_*𝒢 ⊗_{𝒪_X} L^{⊗ d} ≅ i_*(𝒢(d))`, which is what makes the third term of the twisted sequence
the direct image of a twist on `H`.

This is [Stacks, Tag 01E8] at a closed immersion — available with no quasi-coherence hypothesis
as `Stacks.AffineProjectionFormula.closedImmersionProjectionFormulaIso` — followed by
`pullbackTensorPowModuleIntIso`, which rewrites `i^*(L^{⊗ d})` as `(i^*L)^{⊗ d}` so that the
twist on `H` is taken with respect to `i^*L`.
declarations.statement:
def pushforwardTwistModuleIso (d : ℤ) :
    (tensorRightModules X (tensorPowModule X L d)).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj G) ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj
        (twistModule Hy ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L) G d)
declarations.comment: the projection formula clause: i_*(G(d)) = i_*G ⊗ O(d), by [Stacks, Tag 01E8] at a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_pullbackTwistOver_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EGK], the Serre twists on a hyperplane of `ℙ^{m+1}_k`, in every integer
degree.**

Let `v` be a global section of `𝒪(1)` on `ℙ^{m+1}_k` corresponding to a nonzero degree-one form
`f` on `Proj k[T₀, …, T_{m+1}]`. Then the zero scheme `H = Z(v)` admits an isomorphism
`φ : ℙᵐ_k ≅ H` along which, for **every** `d ∈ ℤ`, the pullback of `𝒪_{ℙ^{m+1}}(d)` is
`𝒪_{ℙᵐ}(d)`.

The degree-one case is [Stacks, Tag 089Z] on the base-change model,
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_zeroScheme_projectiveSpaceOverRing`; the passage from it to every
degree is `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.HyperplaneTwistSequence.pullbackTwistOverIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_pullbackTwistOver_zeroScheme (k : Type u) [Field k] (m : ℕ)
    (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (m + 2)) k) (hf : f ∈ polyGrading k (m + 1) 1) (hf0 : f ≠ 0)
    (v : Γ(twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1, ⊤))
    (hv : ConcreteCategory.hom (twistGammaTopIso k (m + 1)).hom v
      = degreeSection (polyGrading k (m + 1)) 1 ⟨f, hf⟩) :
    ∃ φ : projectiveSpaceOverRing m (CommRingCat.of k) ≅
        (AlgebraicGeometry.zeroScheme (projectiveSpaceOverRing (m + 1) (CommRingCat.of k))
          (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) v).subscheme,
      ∀ d : ℤ, Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (φ.hom ≫
          (AlgebraicGeometry.zeroScheme (projectiveSpaceOverRing (m + 1) (CommRingCat.of k))
            (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) v).subschemeι)).obj
        (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) d)
          ≅ twistOver m (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) d)
declarations.comment: the Serre twists on the hyperplane in every degree, the degree-one case being this chapter's own [Stacks, Tag 089Z] on the base-change model

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_hyperplane_twistedSequence_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EGK] in full.** Let `k` be an infinite field and let `ℱ` be a coherent sheaf
on `ℙ^{m+1}_k`. Then there are a nonzero global section `s` of `𝒪(1)`, an isomorphism
`φ : ℙᵐ_k ≅ H` of `ℙᵐ_k` with the hyperplane `H = Z(s)` and, writing `i : H ⟶ ℙ^{m+1}_k` for the
inclusion and `𝒢 = i^*ℱ`, a short exact sequence

`0 ⟶ ℱ(-1) ⟶ ℱ ⟶ i_*𝒢 ⟶ 0`

such that

* `𝒪_H(d) = i^*𝒪_{ℙ^{m+1}}(d)` along `φ`, for every `d ∈ ℤ`;
* for every `d ∈ ℤ` the twisted sequence `0 ⟶ ℱ(d-1) ⟶ ℱ(d) ⟶ i_*(𝒢(d)) ⟶ 0` is short exact;
* and for every `d ∈ ℤ` and every `j` the four-term sequence

  `H^j(ℙ^{m+1}_k, ℱ(d-1)) ⟶ H^j(ℙ^{m+1}_k, ℱ(d)) ⟶ H^j(H, 𝒢(d)) ⟶ H^{j+1}(ℙ^{m+1}_k, ℱ(d-1))`

  is exact at each of its three inner spots, its third term being cohomology on `H` and its
  connecting map the canonical one of the cohomological `δ`-functor of [Stacks, Tag 071H] read
  through the comparison of [Stacks, Tag 089W].

The index is written `m + 1` rather than `n` with `1 ≤ n` so that the hyperplane is `ℙᵐ_k` with
no truncated subtraction. The first clause is `exists_iso_pullbackTwistOver_zeroScheme`, the
untwisted sequence is [Stacks, Tag 08A0] and the two remaining clauses are
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.HyperplaneTwistSequence.shortExact_twistedSequence` and
`…HyperplaneTwistSequence.exact_cohomology_twistedSequence`, whose quasi-coherence input is
`isQuasicoherent_twistModule_pullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hyperplane_twistedSequence_cohomology (k : Type u) [Field k] [Infinite k]
    (m : ℕ) (F : (projectiveSpaceOverRing (m + 1) (CommRingCat.of k)).Modules)
    [F.IsCoherent] :
    ∃ (s : (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1).sections)
      (φ : projectiveSpaceOverRing m (CommRingCat.of k) ≅
        (hyperplane (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s).subscheme)
      (a : twistModule (projectiveSpaceOverRing (m + 1) (CommRingCat.of k))
          (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) F (-1) ⟶ F)
      (w : a ≫ hyperplaneUnit (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) F s = 0)
      (hS : (ShortComplex.mk a
        (hyperplaneUnit (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) F s) w).ShortExact),
      let X := projectiveSpaceOverRing (m + 1) (CommRingCat.of k)
      let G := (Scheme.Modules.pullback
        (hyperplaneι (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s)).obj F
      let g := hyperplaneUnit (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) F s
      let hG := fun d : ℤ => isQuasicoherent_twistModule_pullback
        (hyperplaneι (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s)
        (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) F (isQuasicoherent_of_isCoherent F) d
      PresheafOfModules.sections.eval s (op ⊤) ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ d : ℤ, Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
            (φ.hom ≫ hyperplaneι (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s)).obj
          (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) d)
            ≅ twistOver m (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) d)) ∧
      ∀ d : ℤ,
        (twistedSequence (hyperplaneι (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s)
          (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) F G a g w d).ShortExact ∧
        ∀ j : ℕ,
          Function.Exact (((cohomologyDeltaFunctor X).functor j).map
              (twistedSequence (hyperplaneι (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s)
                (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) F G a g w d).f)
            (cohomologyToHyperplaneMap (hyperplaneι (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s)
              (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) F G a g w d (hG d) j) ∧
          Function.Exact
              (cohomologyToHyperplaneMap (hyperplaneι (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s)
                (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) F G a g w d (hG d) j)
              (cohomologyConnectingMap (hyperplaneι (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s)
                (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) F G a g w hS d (hG d) j) ∧
          Function.Exact
              (cohomologyConnectingMap (hyperplaneι (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s)
                (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) F G a g w hS d (hG d) j)
              (((cohomologyDeltaFunctor X).functor (j + 1)).map
                (twistedSequence (hyperplaneι (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) s)
                  (twistOver (m + 1) (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1) F G a g w d).f)
declarations.comment: the whole remark in the situation of Tags 089Z and 08A0: the hyperplane is P^m_k with O_H(d) = i^*O(d) in every degree, the twisted sequence 0 → F(d-1) → F(d) → i_*(G(d)) → 0 is short exact for every d, and its long exact cohomology sequence has H^j(H, G(d)) as its third term

declarations.name: Dualizing.isArtinian_of_finite_matlisDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EGL.** A maximal-ideal-power torsion module whose Matlis dual is finite
over the completion satisfies the descending chain condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isArtinian_of_finite_matlisDual
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (E : Type u) [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E]
    (i : ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) ⟶ ModuleCat.of R E)
    [Mono i] (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i)
    (hN : IsIPowerTorsion R N (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))

declarations.name: Stacks.InverseSystem.AdicCompletionCohomology.adicCompletion_homology_iso_limit_derivedReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EGS (Kollár--Kovács).** Let `I` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring `A` and
`K ∈ D(A)`. Suppose that every cohomology module of `K` is finite and, in every degree, the
cohomology inverse system of `K ⊗ᴸ[A] A/Iⁿ` is Mittag--Leffler. Then the inverse limit of
`Hⁱ(K ⊗ᴸ[A] A/Iⁿ)` is isomorphic to the `I`-adic completion of `Hⁱ(K)` for every `i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletion_homology_iso_limit_derivedReduction
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (T : CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.DerivedTensorProduct A)
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ,
      Module.Finite A ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K))
    (hML : ∀ i : ℤ,
      (((NoetherianAdicCompletion.idealPowerQuotientSystem I ⋙ T.tensor.obj K) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i) ⋙
        forget (ModuleCat.{u} A)).IsMittagLeffler) :
    ∀ i : ℤ,
      Nonempty
        (ModuleCat.of A
            (AdicCompletion I
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K)) ≅
          limit ((NoetherianAdicCompletion.idealPowerQuotientSystem I ⋙ T.tensor.obj K) ⋙
            DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i))

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.ArtinReesHomology.exists_uniform_adic_homology_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EGU.** For a complex of finite modules over a Noetherian ring, homology after
reduction modulo `I ^ n` and the quotients by `I ^ n` of the original homology are canonically
pro-isomorphic.  A single positive shift controls the inverse-system images, the comparison on
ideal multiples, and the kernels and cokernels of all comparison maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_adic_homology_comparison
    {A K L M : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [AddCommGroup K] [Module A K] [Module.Finite A K]
    [AddCommGroup L] [Module A L] [Module.Finite A L]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (α : K →ₗ[A] L) (β : L →ₗ[A] M) (hcomplex : β.comp α = 0) :
    let H := (LinearMap.ker β) ⧸
      (LinearMap.range α).comap (LinearMap.ker β).subtype
    let cycles : ℕ → Submodule A L := fun n =>
      (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M)).comap β
    let boundaries : ℕ → Submodule A L := fun n =>
      LinearMap.range α ⊔ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A L)
    let Hn : ℕ → Type _ := fun n =>
      cycles n ⧸ (boundaries n).comap (cycles n).subtype
    ∃ (toLevel : ∀ n, H →ₗ[A] Hn n)
      (transition : ∀ n, Hn (n + 1) →ₗ[A] Hn n)
      (quotTransition : ∀ n,
        (H ⧸ I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A H)) →ₗ[A]
          (H ⧸ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A H)))
      (fromQuotient : ∀ n,
        (H ⧸ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A H)) →ₗ[A] Hn n),
      (∀ n (x : LinearMap.ker β) (y : cycles n), (y : L) = x →
        toLevel n (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = Submodule.Quotient.mk y) ∧
      (∀ n (x : cycles (n + 1)) (y : cycles n), (y : L) = x →
        transition n (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = Submodule.Quotient.mk y) ∧
      (∀ n (x : H),
        quotTransition n (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = Submodule.Quotient.mk x) ∧
      (∀ n, transition n ∘ₗ toLevel (n + 1) = toLevel n) ∧
      (∀ n, fromQuotient n ∘ₗ (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A H)).mkQ = toLevel n) ∧
      let Hsys : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat A :=
        Functor.ofOpSequence (X := fun n => ModuleCat.of A (Hn n))
          (fun n => ModuleCat.ofHom (transition n))
      let Qsys : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat A :=
        Functor.ofOpSequence
          (X := fun n => ModuleCat.of A (H ⧸ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A H)))
          (fun n => ModuleCat.ofHom (quotTransition n))
      ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧
        (∃ back : ∀ n, c ≤ n → Hn n →ₗ[A]
            (H ⧸ I ^ (n - c) • (⊤ : Submodule A H)),
          (∀ n (hn : c ≤ n),
            (back n hn).comp (fromQuotient n) =
              (tr Qsys (Nat.sub_le n c)).hom) ∧
          (∀ n (hn : c ≤ n),
            (fromQuotient (n - c)).comp (back n hn) =
              (tr Hsys (Nat.sub_le n c)).hom) ∧
          Nonempty (ProIso Hsys Qsys) ∧
          Nonempty (limit Hsys ≅ limit Qsys) ∧
          (Hsys ⋙ forget (ModuleCat A)).IsMittagLeffler ∧
          (∀ n, LinearMap.range (tr Hsys (Nat.le_add_right n c)).hom =
            LinearMap.range (toLevel n)) ∧
          (∃ toLevelQuotient : ∀ n k,
              (H ⧸ I ^ k • (⊤ : Submodule A H)) →ₗ[A]
                (Hn n ⧸ I ^ k • (⊤ : Submodule A (Hn n))),
            (∀ n k, (toLevelQuotient n k).comp
                (I ^ k • (⊤ : Submodule A H)).mkQ =
              (I ^ k • (⊤ : Submodule A (Hn n))).mkQ.comp (toLevel n)) ∧
            (∀ n (hn : c ≤ n) (x : Hn n),
              x ∈ I ^ c • (⊤ : Submodule A (Hn n)) →
              toLevelQuotient n (n - c) (back n hn x) =
                (I ^ (n - c) • (⊤ : Submodule A (Hn n))).mkQ x)) ∧
          (∀ n,
            I ^ c ≤ Module.annihilator A (LinearMap.ker (fromQuotient n)) ∧
            I ^ c ≤ Module.annihilator A
              (Hn n ⧸ LinearMap.range (fromQuotient n))))

declarations.name: Stacks.PseudoCoherent.AdicCompletion.pseudoCoherent_mittagLeffler_and_adicCompletion_iso_limit_derivedReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EGV (Kollár--Kovács).** If `K` is a pseudo-coherent object of `D(A)` for a
Noetherian ring `A`, then in every degree the cohomology of its reductions modulo the positive
powers of `I` is Mittag--Leffler, and its inverse limit is the `I`-adic completion of the
cohomology of `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherent_mittagLeffler_and_adicCompletion_iso_limit_derivedReduction
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (T : CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.DerivedTensorProduct A)
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K) :
    ∀ i : ℤ,
      (((NoetherianAdicCompletion.idealPowerQuotientSystem I ⋙ T.tensor.obj K) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i) ⋙
        forget (ModuleCat.{u} A)).IsMittagLeffler ∧
      Nonempty
        (ModuleCat.of A
            (AdicCompletion I
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K)) ≅
          limit ((NoetherianAdicCompletion.idealPowerQuotientSystem I ⋙ T.tensor.obj K) ⋙
            DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i))

declarations.name: Stacks.Modules.AdicSystem.AdicModuleSystem.delayedCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EGW.** Systems of finite `A ⧸ I ^ n`-modules, with morphisms represented by
maps `I ^ c Eₙ → Fₙ / Fₙ[I ^ c]` modulo increasing `c`, form a category. Composition is
the induced composition at delay `c + c'`.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def delayedCategory : CategoryData (A := A) (I := I)

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicModuleSystem.IsomorphismCriterion.isIso_homOfRepresentative_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EGX.** A delayed representative induces an isomorphism in the category of
systems if and only if, eventually, the kernels and cokernels of all its component maps are
annihilated by a single fixed power of the ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_homOfRepresentative_iff (r : HomRepresentative E F) :
    letI := (AdicModuleSystem.delayedCategory (A := A) (I := I)).toCategory
    IsIso (show E ⟶ F from homOfRepresentative r) ↔
      ∃ c' : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ+ in atTop, ∀ h : r.delay ≤ (n : ℕ),
        Module.IsTorsionBySet A (r.map n h).ker (↑(I ^ c') : Set A) ∧
          Module.IsTorsionBySet A
            ((underlying F n ⧸ torsionPart F n r.delay) ⧸
              LinearMap.range (r.map n h)) (↑(I ^ c') : Set A)

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.ExtDelayedIso.extAdicQuotientSystem_iso_extOfAdicQuotientsSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EGY.** For finite modules over a Noetherian ring, the system of adic
quotients of `Ext` is isomorphic, in the category of delayed morphisms, to the system of
`Ext` groups over the corresponding quotient rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem extAdicQuotientSystem_iso_extOfAdicQuotientsSystem
    (I : Ideal A) (M N : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module.Finite A N] (i : ℕ) :
    letI := (AdicModuleSystem.delayedCategory (A := A) (I := I)).toCategory
    Nonempty (extAdicQuotientSystem I M N i ≅ extOfAdicQuotientsSystem I M N i)

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.ExtComparison.exists_eventually_extOfAdicQuotients_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EGZ.** There are powers `I ^ c` and `I ^ d` such that, for `m ≫ n ≫ 0`, canonical
maps from `I ^ c Ext_{A_m}^i(M_m,N_m) / I ^ n Ext_{A_m}^i(M_m,N_m)` to
`Ext_{A_n}^i(M_n,N_n) / Ext_{A_n}^i(M_n,N_n)[I ^ c]` have kernel and cokernel annihilated
by `I ^ d`. The displayed factorization characterizes these maps in terms of mutually
inverse representatives of the isomorphism of Tag 0EGY.

The source's single exponent is split: maps are defined on I^c-multiples, and their
kernel/cokernel are annihilated by some possibly larger power I^d; with one exponent the
claim fails, e.g. for A = k[x,y,z,w]/(xy), I = (x,y,z,w), M = N = A/(x), i = 2.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_eventually_extOfAdicQuotients_comparison (I : Ideal A) (M N : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module.Finite A N] (i : ℕ) :
    letI := (AdicModuleSystem.delayedCategory (A := A) (I := I)).toCategory
    let E := extAdicQuotientSystem I M N i
    let F := extOfAdicQuotientsSystem I M N i
    ∃ (e : E ≅ F) (r : AdicModuleSystem.HomRepresentative E F)
        (s : AdicModuleSystem.HomRepresentative F E),
      AdicModuleSystem.homOfRepresentative r = e.hom ∧
      AdicModuleSystem.homOfRepresentative s = e.inv ∧
      let c := s.delay + r.delay
      ∃ d : ℕ,
      ∃ comparison : ∀ (n m : ℕ+) (_ : c ≤ (n : ℕ)) (_ : n ≤ m),
          (AdicModuleSystem.powerPart F m c ⧸
              (AdicModuleSystem.powerPart F m (n : ℕ)).comap
                (AdicModuleSystem.powerPart F m c).subtype) →ₗ[A]
            AdicModuleSystem.underlying F n ⧸ AdicModuleSystem.torsionPart F n c,
        ∀ᶠ n : ℕ+ in atTop, ∀ᶠ m : ℕ+ in atTop,
          ∀ (hn : c ≤ (n : ℕ)) (hnm : n ≤ m),
            (∀ z : AdicModuleSystem.powerPart F m c,
              ∃ (yₘ : AdicModuleSystem.powerPart E m r.delay)
                (yₙ : AdicModuleSystem.powerPart E n r.delay),
                s.map m (le_trans (Nat.le_add_right s.delay r.delay)
                    (le_trans hn (mod_cast hnm)))
                    ⟨z, AdicModuleSystem.powerPart_add_le_left F m s.delay r.delay z.2⟩ =
                  (AdicModuleSystem.torsionPart E m s.delay).mkQ yₘ.1 ∧
                extAdicQuotientTransition I M N i hnm yₘ = yₙ ∧
                comparison n m hn hnm
                    (Quotient.mk _ z) =
                  AdicModuleSystem.quotientTransitionOfLE F n
                    (Nat.le_add_left r.delay s.delay)
                    (r.map n (le_trans (Nat.le_add_left r.delay s.delay) hn) yₙ)) ∧
            Module.IsTorsionBySet A (comparison n m hn hnm).ker
              (↑(I ^ d) : Set A) ∧
            Module.IsTorsionBySet A
              ((AdicModuleSystem.underlying F n ⧸ AdicModuleSystem.torsionPart F n c) ⧸
                LinearMap.range (comparison n m hn hnm)) (↑(I ^ d) : Set A)

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.ExtFlatBaseChange.limit_ext_quotient_iso_limit_ext_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EH0.** Let `A → B` be a flat map of Noetherian rings, let `I` be an
ideal of `A`, and let `M` and `N` be finite `B`-modules. If `M` is flat over `A`, the
canonical reduction maps from the `I`-adic quotients of `Ext_B(M, N)` to the Ext groups over
`B / I ^ n B` are compatible with all transition maps and induce an isomorphism on inverse
limits.

The maps are given simultaneously in every degree. Their identity, composition, reduction,
and quotient-factorization laws record the canonical inverse-system structure. The induced
map on limits is an isomorphism of `A`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem limit_ext_quotient_iso_limit_ext_baseChange
    {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB} {M : Type uM} {N : Type uN}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Module.Flat A B]
    [Module.Finite B M] [Module.Finite B N] [Module.Flat A M]
    (I : Ideal A) :
    let J := I.map (algebraMap A B)
    let E : ℕ → Type (max uA uB uM uN) := fun i =>
      Ext (ModuleCat.of B (ULift.{max uA uB uM uN} M))
        (ModuleCat.of B (ULift.{max uA uB uM uN} N)) i
    let _ : ∀ i, Module A (E i) := fun i =>
      Module.compHom (E i) (algebraMap A B)
    let Q : ℕ → ℕ → Type (max uA uB uM uN) := fun i n =>
      E i ⧸ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (E i))
    let Bn : ℕ → Type uB := fun n => B ⧸ J ^ n
    let Mn : ℕ → Type uM := fun n =>
      M ⧸ J ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule B M)
    let Nn : ℕ → Type uN := fun n =>
      N ⧸ J ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule B N)
    let En : ℕ → ℕ → Type (max uA uB uM uN) := fun i n =>
      Ext (ModuleCat.of (Bn n) (ULift.{max uA uB uM uN} (Mn n)))
        (ModuleCat.of (Bn n) (ULift.{max uA uB uM uN} (Nn n))) i
    let _ : ∀ i n, Module A (En i n) := fun i n =>
      Module.compHom (En i n) (algebraMap A (Bn n))
    ∃ (extTransition : ∀ i m n, n ≤ m → En i m →ₗ[A] En i n)
      (reduction : ∀ i n, E i →ₗ[A] En i n)
      (comparison : ∀ i n, Q i n →ₗ[A] En i n),
      (∀ i n, extTransition i n n le_rfl = LinearMap.id) ∧
      (∀ i k m n (hkm : m ≤ k) (hmn : n ≤ m),
        (extTransition i m n hmn).comp (extTransition i k m hkm) =
          extTransition i k n (hmn.trans hkm)) ∧
      (∀ i m n (hmn : n ≤ m),
        (extTransition i m n hmn).comp (reduction i m) = reduction i n) ∧
      (∀ i n,
        (comparison i n).comp (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (E i))).mkQ = reduction i n) ∧
      (∀ i m n (hmn : n ≤ m),
        (extTransition i m n hmn).comp (comparison i m) =
          (comparison i n).comp (Submodule.factorPow I (E i) hmn)) ∧
      ∀ i,
        let Qsys : Functor ℕᵒᵖ (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uM uN} A) :=
          Functor.ofOpSequence
            (X := fun n => ModuleCat.of A (Q i n))
            (fun n => ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.factorPowSucc I (E i) n))
        let Esys : Functor ℕᵒᵖ (ModuleCat.{max uA uB uM uN} A) :=
          Functor.ofOpSequence
            (X := fun n => ModuleCat.of A (En i n))
            (fun n => ModuleCat.ofHom
              (extTransition i (n + 1) n n.le_succ))
        ∃ e : limit Qsys ≅ limit Esys,
          ∀ n, e.hom ≫ limit.π Esys (op n) =
            limit.π Qsys (op n) ≫ ModuleCat.ofHom (comparison i n)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.exists_quotientPower_extMapVanishesAbove
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EH1].** Let `I` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring `A` and let `e` be the
cohomological dimension of `I` in `A`. For every `n` there is an `m > n` for which the quotient
map `A/I^m → A/I^n` satisfies the equivalent conditions of [Stacks, Tag 0G9V] in degree `e`:
`Ext^i(A/I^n, N) → Ext^i(A/I^m, N)` is zero for every `A`-module `N` and every `i > e`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quotientPower_extMapVanishesAbove
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ m : ℕ, ∃ hnm : n < m,
      ExtMapVanishesAbove
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ A
          (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (I := I) (Nat.le_of_lt hnm))).toLinearMap)
        (cohomologicalDimension A I (IsNoetherian.noetherian I)).toNat

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.ExtCounterexample.extTwo_not_preserved_by_adicQuotients
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EH2.** For `A = k[[x, y]] / (xy)` and `M = A / (y)`, the periodic
resolution computes `Ext_A^2(M, N)` as `N[y] / xN`.  At the finite level the numerator
is the intersection of the `y`-torsion and the `x^(n - 1)`-torsion.  In particular,
for `N = M`, the original Ext group is additively isomorphic to `k`, while every
finite-level Ext group vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem extTwo_not_preserved_by_adicQuotients (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    let R := MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) k
    let X : R := MvPowerSeries.X 0
    let Y : R := MvPowerSeries.X 1
    let A := R ⧸ Ideal.span {X * Y}
    let x : A := Ideal.Quotient.mk _ X
    let y : A := Ideal.Quotient.mk _ Y
    let I : Ideal A := Ideal.span {x}
    let M := A ⧸ Ideal.span {y}
    Function.Exact (LinearMap.lsmul A A y) (LinearMap.lsmul A A x) ∧
      Function.Exact (LinearMap.lsmul A A x) (LinearMap.lsmul A A y) ∧
      Function.Exact (LinearMap.lsmul A A y) (Submodule.mkQ (Ideal.span {y})) ∧
      Function.Surjective (Submodule.mkQ (Ideal.span {y})) ∧
      (∀ (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N],
        let Ky := LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul A N y)
        Nonempty (Ext (ModuleCat.of A M) (ModuleCat.of A N) 2 ≃ₗ[A]
          (Ky ⧸ ((I • (⊤ : Submodule A N)).comap Ky.subtype)))) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ+),
        let An := A ⧸ I ^ (n : ℕ)
        let xn : An := Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x
        let yn : An := Ideal.Quotient.mk _ y
        let Mn := M ⧸ (I ^ (n : ℕ) • (⊤ : Submodule A M))
        ∃ q : An →ₗ[An] Mn,
          q 1 = Submodule.Quotient.mk (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {y}) 1) ∧
          Function.Surjective q ∧
          Function.Exact (LinearMap.lsmul An An yn) q ∧
          Function.Exact (LinearMap.lsmul An An xn) (LinearMap.lsmul An An yn) ∧
          Function.Exact
            ((LinearMap.lsmul An An yn).coprod
              (LinearMap.lsmul An An (xn ^ ((n : ℕ) - 1))))
            (LinearMap.lsmul An An xn)) ∧
      (∀ (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] (n : ℕ+),
        let An := A ⧸ I ^ (n : ℕ)
        let anCommRing : CommRing An := Ideal.Quotient.commRing (I ^ (n : ℕ))
        letI : Ring An := anCommRing.toRing
        letI : CommSemiring An := anCommRing.toCommSemiring
        letI : Semiring An := anCommRing.toSemiring
        letI : Linear An (ModuleCat An) := ModuleCat.Algebra.instLinear
        let xn : An := Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x
        let yn : An := Ideal.Quotient.mk _ y
        let Nn := N ⧸ (I ^ (n : ℕ) • (⊤ : Submodule A N))
        let K := LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul An Nn yn) ⊓
          LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul An Nn (xn ^ ((n : ℕ) - 1)))
        let xNn : Submodule An Nn := Ideal.span {xn} • ⊤
        let xK : Submodule An K := xNn.comap K.subtype
        Nonempty (Ext (ModuleCat.of An
            (M ⧸ (I ^ (n : ℕ) • (⊤ : Submodule A M))))
          (ModuleCat.of An Nn) 2 ≃ₗ[An] (K ⧸ xK))) ∧
      letI : Module k (Ext (ModuleCat.of A M) (ModuleCat.of A M) 2) :=
        Module.compHom _ (algebraMap k A)
      Nonempty (Ext (ModuleCat.of A M) (ModuleCat.of A M) 2 ≃ₗ[k] k) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ+),
        let An := A ⧸ I ^ (n : ℕ)
        let xn : An := Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x
        let Mn := M ⧸ (I ^ (n : ℕ) • (⊤ : Submodule A M))
        Nonempty (Mn ≃ₗ[k] ((Polynomial k) ⧸
          (Ideal.span {Polynomial.X ^ (n : ℕ)} : Ideal (Polynomial k)))) ∧
          Function.Exact (LinearMap.lsmul An Mn xn)
            (LinearMap.lsmul An Mn (xn ^ ((n : ℕ) - 1))) ∧
          Subsingleton (Ext (ModuleCat.of An Mn) (ModuleCat.of An Mn) 2))

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.existsUnique_gradedSplitting
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EH6.** Let `I = (f₁, …, f_r)` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring `A`
with `cd(A, I) = 1`, let `φ_j : I ^ c ⟶ A` split the inclusion against the generators, let `X`
be a Noetherian scheme over `Spec A` and let `(F_n)` be a coherent adic system along `I · 𝒪_X`
with inverse limit `F`. Then `c` may be enlarged to a `d`, with a splitting `ψ_j : I ^ d ⟶ A`
restricting `φ` and still splitting the inclusion, so that there is a *unique* graded
`𝒪_X`-module map

`Φ_F : ⨁_{n ≥ 0} I ^ (n d) F ⟶ F[T₁, …, T_r]`

with `Φ_F (g s) = Φ(g) s` for `g ∈ I ^ (n d)` and `s` a local section of `F`, and the composite
of `Φ_F` with the substitution `T_j ↦ f_j` is the inclusion `I ^ (n d) F ⟶ F` in every
degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_gradedSplitting (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (J : Ideal A) {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) (hf : J = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (hcd : Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologicalDimension A J (IsNoetherian.noetherian J) = 1)
    {c : ℕ} (hc : 1 ≤ c) (φ : Fin r → (J ^ c : Ideal A) →ₗ[A] A)
    (hφ : ∀ x : (J ^ c : Ideal A), (∑ j, f j * φ j x) = (x : A))
    (fX : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian X]
    (S : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ X.Modules) (hS : IsCoherentAdicSystem (baseIdealSheaf A J fX) S) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ∃ hcd' : c ≤ d, ∃ ψ : Fin r → (J ^ d : Ideal A) →ₗ[A] A,
      RestrictsSplitting J hcd' φ ψ ∧
      (∀ x : (J ^ d : Ideal A), (∑ j, f j * ψ j x) = (x : A)) ∧
      ∃! Ψ : GradedSplittingComponents A J fX (limit S) r d,
        IsGradedSplitting A J fX (limit S) d ψ Ψ ∧
          ∀ n : ℕ, gradedSplittingEvalHom Ψ f n =
            ιModules (idealPowerMultiple (baseIdealSheaf A J fX) (n * d) (limit S))

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.AdicInverseSystem.limitIntCohomologyTopology_eq_adicModuleTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EH7.** Let `I` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring `A`, let `X` be a
Noetherian scheme over `Spec A` and let `… ⟶ F_3 ⟶ F_2 ⟶ F_1` be an inverse system of coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules with `F_n = F_{n+1} / I ^ n F_{n+1}`. If `cd(A, I) = 1` then for every `p ∈ ℤ` the
limit topology on `lim_n H^p(X, F_n)` — the infimum of the topologies induced from the discrete
modules `H^p(X, F_n)` — is the `I`-adic topology.

Cohomology is `moduleCohomologyFunctorInt X p`, the `p`-th right derived functor of global
sections taken in `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`-modules, so that `lim_n H^p(X, F_n)` carries the module structure
the `I`-adic topology needs, and `I` acts through the ideal of `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` generated by its
image. The system is zero-indexed, so its object at `n` is the source's `F_{n+1}` and the
source's exponent `n` appears as `n + 1`; quasi-coherence of the terms is a field of
`Stacks.Algebraization.AdicInverseSystem` rather than a hypothesis here, and it follows from the
coherence `hcoh` the source assumes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem limitIntCohomologyTopology_eq_adicModuleTopology [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (S : AdicInverseSystem.{u}) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S.X]
    (fX : S.X ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    (hSI : S.I = baseIdealSheaf A I fX)
    (hcoh : ∀ n : ℕ, _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent.{u} (S.system.obj (op n)))
    (hcd : Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologicalDimension A I (IsNoetherian.noetherian I) = 1)
    (p : ℤ) :
    (⨅ n : ℕ, TopologicalSpace.induced
        (fun x : AdicInverseSystem.cohomologyLimit S (moduleCohomologyFunctorInt S.X p) =>
          (limit.π (AdicInverseSystem.cohomologySystem S
            (moduleCohomologyFunctorInt S.X p)) (op n)).hom x) ⊥) =
      (I.map (fX.appTop.hom.comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom)).adicModuleTopology
        (AdicInverseSystem.cohomologyLimit S (moduleCohomologyFunctorInt S.X p))

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.truncationEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The truncation of `A`, Stacks 0EH8.** `A ⧸ Iⁿ` is the *polynomial* chart
`k[x,y][s,t] ⧸ ((xs − yt) + (s,t)ⁿ)`: modulo `Iⁿ = (s,t)ⁿ` only the coefficients in total degree
below `n` survive, so no power series does.

This is the step whose untruncated form is false. `A[1/x]` is a *proper* subring of
`k[x^{±1}, y][[t]]`, because the pole order in `x` of the image of `a/xᵐ` grows with the degree
in `t` while `m` does not — see the docstring of
`Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.not_isUnit_mul_add_mul`. Modulo `Iⁿ` the degrees in `t` are
bounded, and what remains is a polynomial ring, which does commute with localization.
declarations.statement:
def truncationEquiv (n : ℕ) :
    (ambientPoly k ⧸
        chartIdeal (MvPolynomial.X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (MvPolynomial.X 1) n) ≃+*
      (exampleRing k ⧸ adicIdeal k ^ n)
declarations.comment: A/I^n is the polynomial chart k[x,y][s,t]/((xs - yt) + (s,t)^n): the truncation that makes the chart isomorphism true, where its untruncated form A[1/x] = k[x^{±1},y][[t]] is false

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.chartTruncationEquivX
declarations.doc:
**The truncated chart isomorphism of Stacks 0EH8, on `D(x)`.**

`A[1/x] ⧸ Iⁿ ≃+* k[x^{±1}, y][t] ⧸ (tⁿ)`, the `D(x)`-chart of `𝒪_X/Iⁿ𝒪_X` that the source's
"computation omitted" rests on. It sends `s ↦ (y/x)t`, hence `I = (s,t) ↦ (t)` and
`g = t/x ↦ x⁻¹t`.

Its *untruncated* form `A[1/x] ≅ k[x^{±1}, y][[t]]` is **false** — see the docstring of
`Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.not_isUnit_mul_add_mul`. The truncation is what makes it true, and
the proof shows why: `A ⧸ Iⁿ` is a *polynomial* ring
(`Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.truncationEquiv`), a polynomial ring does commute with
localization (`MvPolynomial.isLocalization`), and then `x` being a unit the change of variables
`s ↦ (y/x)t` eliminates `s` (`Stacks.TruncatedChart.chartEquiv`). The middle step is the one that
has no untruncated analogue.

The `D(y)` twin is `Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.chartTruncationEquivY`.
declarations.statement:
def chartTruncationEquivX (n : ℕ) :
    (Localization.Away (coordX k) ⧸
        (adicIdeal k ^ n).map
          (algebraMap (exampleRing k) (Localization.Away (coordX k)))) ≃+*
      truncPoly (coeffAwayX k) n
declarations.comment: the truncated chart isomorphism A[1/x]/I^n = k[x^{±1},y][t]/(t^n), sending s to (y/x)t; the chart the omitted computation of H^0(X, F_n) needs, and whose untruncated form is false

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.chartTruncationEquivY
declarations.doc:
**The truncated chart isomorphism of Stacks 0EH8, on `D(y)`.**

`A[1/y] ⧸ Iⁿ ≃+* k[x, y^{±1}][s] ⧸ (sⁿ)`, the twin of
`Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.chartTruncationEquivX` and the second of the two charts the
source's "computation omitted" rests on. It sends `t ↦ (x/y)s`, hence `I = (s,t) ↦ (s)` and
`g = t/x ↦ y⁻¹s`.

The proof is the `D(x)` proof with the two variables interchanged, and only the last of its three
steps is asymmetric. Steps 1 and 2 — `A ⧸ Iⁿ` is the polynomial chart
`k[x,y][s,t] ⧸ ((xs − yt) + (s,t)ⁿ)` (`Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.truncationEquiv`), and a
polynomial chart commutes with localization (`MvPolynomial.isLocalization`,
`Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.map_chartIdeal`) — do not mention which variable is inverted. Step
3 does: `Stacks.TruncatedChart.chartEquiv` eliminates the *first* variable and wants the
coefficient of `s` to be a unit, so here it is used through
`Stacks.TruncatedChart.chartEquivSwap`, which runs it after `MvPolynomial.rename (Equiv.swap 0 1)`
and eliminates `t` instead.

As for `D(x)`, the untruncated form `A[1/y] ≅ k[x, y^{±1}][[s]]` is **false**: the pole-order
argument in the docstring of `Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.not_isUnit_mul_add_mul` is symmetric
in the two variables.
declarations.statement:
def chartTruncationEquivY (n : ℕ) :
    (Localization.Away (coordY k) ⧸
        (adicIdeal k ^ n).map
          (algebraMap (exampleRing k) (Localization.Away (coordY k)))) ≃+*
      truncPoly (coeffAwayY k) n
declarations.comment: the truncated chart isomorphism A[1/y]/I^n = k[x,y^{±1}][s]/(s^n), sending t to (x/y)s; the D(y) twin of the chart the omitted computation of H^0(X, F_n) needs, and whose untruncated form is likewise false

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.notMemAdicIdealSmulFormalLimit
declarations.doc:
**`gᵉ ∉ I·M`, the last clause of Stacks 0EH8.** Each power of the rational function
`g = t/x = s/y` is a formal section tending to zero in the limit topology on
`M = lim H⁰(X, 𝒪_X/Iⁿ𝒪_X)`, and none of them lies in `I·M`. The limit topology is therefore
not the `I`-adic topology, which is what makes the example sharp against Stacks 0EH7.

The whole situation is specialized along `ρ : A ⟶ R[x,y]`, `x ↦ x`, `y ↦ y`, `s ↦ y·z`,
`t ↦ x·z` with `R = k[T]/(Tᵉ⁺¹)` and `z` the image of `T`. Since `ρ(𝔞) ⊆ (x,y)`, the punctured
plane `W = D(x) ∪ D(y) ⊆ Spec R[x,y]` maps to `X`; since `ρ(I)ᵉ⁺¹ = 0`, that map factors
through `ℱₑ₊₁`; and since `Γ(W, 𝒪) = R[x,y]` — the punctured plane acquires no new function,
which is where the codimension two of the removed locus enters — every formal section acquires
a value in `R[x,y]` (`exists_specializationFunctional`). On `gᵉ` the value is `zᵉ`, whereas a
decomposition `gᵉ = s·p + t·q` makes it `y z·(…) + x z·(…)`, which vanishes at `x = y = 0`
while `zᵉ ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement: theorem notMemAdicIdealSmulFormalLimit (e : ℕ) : NotMemAdicIdealSmulFormalLimit k e
declarations.comment: g^e is never in I*M, so the limit topology on M differs from the I-adic one and the cd = 1 hypothesis of Stacks 0EH7 is sharp

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.notMem_or_notMem_of_adicIdeal_le
declarations.doc:
**The neighbourhood `V` of Stacks 0EH8.** At every point of `X = Spec(A) ∖ V(𝔞)` at which
`I` vanishes, one of `x`, `y` is invertible: `V(I𝒪_X) ⊆ D(x) ∪ D(y)`. So `D(x) ∪ D(y)` is the
open neighbourhood of `V(I𝒪_X)` inside `X` on which the rational function `g = t/x = s/y`
below is regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem notMem_or_notMem_of_adicIdeal_le (p : PrimeSpectrum (exampleRing k))
    (hp : ¬ puncturingIdeal k ≤ p.asIdeal) (hI : adicIdeal k ≤ p.asIdeal) :
    coordX k ∉ p.asIdeal ∨ coordY k ∉ p.asIdeal
declarations.comment: the open neighbourhood V of V(I·O_X) in X on which t/x = s/y is regular is D(x) ∪ D(y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.coordX_mul_rationalFunctionAwayX
declarations.statement:
theorem coordX_mul_rationalFunctionAwayX :
    algebraMap (exampleRing k) (Localization.Away (coordX k)) (coordX k) *
        rationalFunctionAwayX k =
      algebraMap (exampleRing k) (Localization.Away (coordX k)) (coordT k)
declarations.comment: the chart t/x of the rational function g, regular on D(x)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.coordY_mul_rationalFunctionAwayY
declarations.statement:
theorem coordY_mul_rationalFunctionAwayY :
    algebraMap (exampleRing k) (Localization.Away (coordY k)) (coordY k) *
        rationalFunctionAwayY k =
      algebraMap (exampleRing k) (Localization.Away (coordY k)) (coordS k)
declarations.comment: the chart s/y of the rational function g, regular on D(y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.rationalFunctionAway_eq_of_isUnit
declarations.doc:
**The two charts are the same rational function.** In any `A`-algebra in which `x` and `y`
are both invertible, an element solving `x·gx = t` and an element solving `y·gy = s` are
equal: `t/x = s/y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalFunctionAway_eq_of_isUnit {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [Algebra (exampleRing k) R]
    (hx : IsUnit (algebraMap (exampleRing k) R (coordX k)))
    (hy : IsUnit (algebraMap (exampleRing k) R (coordY k)))
    (gx gy : R)
    (hgx : algebraMap (exampleRing k) R (coordX k) * gx =
      algebraMap (exampleRing k) R (coordT k))
    (hgy : algebraMap (exampleRing k) R (coordY k) * gy =
      algebraMap (exampleRing k) R (coordS k)) :
    gx = gy
declarations.comment: t/x = s/y: the two charts agree wherever x and y are both invertible

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.pow_rationalFunctionAwayX_mem_map_pow
declarations.doc:
**`gᵉ → 0`, on the chart `D(x)`.** The `e`-th power of `t/x` lies in `Iⁿ·A[1/x]` for every
`n ≤ e`, because `tᵉ ∈ Iⁿ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pow_rationalFunctionAwayX_mem_map_pow (e n : ℕ) (hne : n ≤ e) :
    rationalFunctionAwayX k ^ e ∈
      (adicIdeal k ^ n).map (algebraMap (exampleRing k) (Localization.Away (coordX k)))
declarations.comment: g^e dies modulo I^n for n ≤ e, on the chart D(x)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.pow_rationalFunctionAwayY_mem_map_pow
declarations.doc:
**`gᵉ → 0`, on the chart `D(y)`.** The `e`-th power of `s/y` lies in `Iⁿ·A[1/y]` for every
`n ≤ e`, because `sᵉ ∈ Iⁿ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pow_rationalFunctionAwayY_mem_map_pow (e n : ℕ) (hne : n ≤ e) :
    rationalFunctionAwayY k ^ e ∈
      (adicIdeal k ^ n).map (algebraMap (exampleRing k) (Localization.Away (coordY k)))
declarations.comment: g^e dies modulo I^n for n ≤ e, on the chart D(y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.cohomologicalDimension_adicIdeal_eq_two
declarations.doc:
**`cd(A, I) = 2`.** The ideal `I = (s,t)` of `A = k[x,y][[s,t]]/(xs - yt)` has
cohomological dimension two: at most two because `I` has two generators (Stacks 0DX9), and at
least two because specializing `x, y ↦ 0` carries `I` onto the maximal ideal of `k[[s]][[t]]`,
whose cohomological dimension is its Krull dimension (Stacks 0DXE), and that is at least two.

This is why Stacks 0EH7 — which concludes that the limit topology on `lim Hᵖ(X, ℱₙ)` is
`I`-adic — does not apply: that result needs `cd(A, I) = 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologicalDimension_adicIdeal_eq_two :
    cohomologicalDimension (exampleRing k) (adicIdeal k) (adicIdeal_fg k) = 2
declarations.comment: cd(A, I) = 2, so the cd = 1 hypothesis of Stacks 0EH7 is sharp

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.sectionG
declarations.doc:
**`g` as a genuine section of `𝒪_X` over `V = D(x) ∪ D(y)`.** The rational function
`g = t/x = s/y` of Stacks 0EH8 is regular on the neighbourhood `V` of `V(I𝒪_X)`: it is glued
from `sectionX` and `sectionY`, which agree on the overlap by `res_sectionX_eq_res_sectionY`,
via the sheaf condition for two opens.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sectionG :
    (puncturedSpectrum k).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (nearVanishingOpen k).openSet)
declarations.comment: the section g

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.formalSectionG
declarations.doc:
**`gᵉ` as a formal section, Stacks 0EH8's element of `M = lim H⁰(X, 𝒪_X/IⁿM)`.** The
image of `sectionGFormal k e` under the canonical comparison `comparisonAt` at the
neighbourhood `nearVanishingOpen k`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def formalSectionG (e : ℕ) :
    ToType (limit (formalSections (exampleRing k) (adicIdeal k) (puncturingIdeal k)
      (formalModule k)))
declarations.comment: each power g^e gives an element of M = lim H⁰(X, ℱₙ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.NonAdicLimit.tendsto_formalSectionG_atTop_nhds_zero
declarations.doc:
**`gᵉ → 0` in the limit topology, Stacks 0EH8.** For each `n`, `gᵉ` already dies in the
tower's `n`-th term as soon as `e ≥ n`, by `sectionG_pow_mem_idealPowerMultiple`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tendsto_formalSectionG_atTop_nhds_zero :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun e => formalSectionG k e) Filter.atTop
      (@nhds _ (limitTopologyFormalLimitModule k) 0)
declarations.comment: g^e → 0 as e → ∞ in the limit topology on M

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.conditions_tfae_of_quasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EH9.** Let `X` be a scheme, let `f` act by multiplication by a
global section of `𝒪_X`, and let `… → ℱ₃ → ℱ₂ → ℱ₁` be an inverse system of quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules. The following are equivalent:

1. for all `n ≥ 1` the map `f : ℱ_{n+1} → ℱ_{n+1}` factors through `ℱ_{n+1} → ℱ_n` to give a
   short exact sequence `0 → ℱ_n → ℱ_{n+1} → ℱ₁ → 0`;
2. for all `n ≥ 1` the map `f^n : ℱ_{n+1} → ℱ_{n+1}` factors through `ℱ_{n+1} → ℱ₁` to give a
   short exact sequence `0 → ℱ₁ → ℱ_{n+1} → ℱ_n → 0`;
3. there is an `f`-divisible `𝒪_X`-module `𝒢` with `ℱ_n = 𝒢[f^n]`;
4. there is an `f`-torsion-free `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` with `ℱ_n = ℱ/f^nℱ`.

The equivalence of (1), (2) and (3) holds over an arbitrary sheaf of rings and is Stacks
0H39; so does (4) ⇒ (1). The converse (1) ⇒ (4) is
`Stacks.Algebraization.condition_one_iff_four_of_quasicoherent`, which is where the scheme
structure and quasi-coherence enter.
declarations.statement:
theorem conditions_tfae_of_quasicoherent
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : End (𝟭 (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)))
    (obj : ℕ → X.Modules) (map : ∀ n, obj (n + 1) ⟶ obj n)
    (hobj : ∀ n, (obj n).IsQuasicoherent) :
    List.TFAE
      [Condition1 f obj map, Condition2 f obj map, Condition3 f obj map,
        Condition4 f obj map]

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InverseSystems.range_pow_eq_ker_limitProjection
declarations.doc:
Let `f` be a global section of `O` and let `… → 𝓕₂ → 𝓕₁` be an inverse system of `O`-modules
satisfying condition (1) of Stacks 0H39 for multiplication by `f`. For every `c = n + 1 ≥ 1` the
submodule `f^c · lim Hᵖ(C, 𝓕ₙ)` of `lim Hᵖ(C, 𝓕ₙ)` is the kernel of the projection to
`Hᵖ(C, 𝓕_c)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pow_eq_ker_limitProjection (f : ↥(GlobalSectionRing O))
    (obj : ℕ → SheafOfModules.{max u v} O) (map : ∀ n, obj (n + 1) ⟶ obj n)
    (h : Condition1 (Stacks.SheafOfModules.globalSectionToEnd O ⟨f.1, f.2⟩) obj map) (p n : ℕ) :
    LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ↥(GlobalSectionRing O)
        (limit (Functor.ofOpSequence map ⋙ globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, max u v, max u v} O p) :
          ModuleCat.{max u v} ↥(GlobalSectionRing O)) (f ^ (n + 1))) =
      LinearMap.ker (limit.π (Functor.ofOpSequence map ⋙
        globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, max u v, max u v} O p) (op n)).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InverseSystems.range_pow_eq_ker_limitProjection_and_limitTopology_eq_adic
declarations.doc:
Let `f` be a global section of `O` and let `… → 𝓕₂ → 𝓕₁` be an inverse system of `O`-modules
satisfying condition (1) of Stacks 0H39 for multiplication by `f`, and let `p ≥ 0`. Put
`Hᵖ = lim Hᵖ(C, 𝓕ₙ)`. Then for every `c = n + 1 ≥ 1` the submodule `f^c Hᵖ` is the kernel of
`Hᵖ → Hᵖ(C, 𝓕_c)`, and the limit topology on `Hᵖ` (the infimum of the topologies induced by the
projections to the discrete `Hᵖ(C, 𝓕_c)`) is the `f`-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pow_eq_ker_limitProjection_and_limitTopology_eq_adic
    (f : ↥(GlobalSectionRing O))
    (obj : ℕ → SheafOfModules.{max u v} O) (map : ∀ n, obj (n + 1) ⟶ obj n)
    (h : Condition1 (Stacks.SheafOfModules.globalSectionToEnd O ⟨f.1, f.2⟩) obj map) (p : ℕ) :
    (∀ n : ℕ, LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ↥(GlobalSectionRing O)
        (limit (Functor.ofOpSequence map ⋙ globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, max u v, max u v} O p) :
          ModuleCat.{max u v} ↥(GlobalSectionRing O)) (f ^ (n + 1))) =
      LinearMap.ker (limit.π (Functor.ofOpSequence map ⋙
        globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, max u v, max u v} O p) (op n)).hom) ∧
    (⨅ n : ℕ, TopologicalSpace.induced
        (fun y : (limit (Functor.ofOpSequence map ⋙
            globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, max u v, max u v} O p) :
          ModuleCat.{max u v} ↥(GlobalSectionRing O)) =>
          (limit.π (Functor.ofOpSequence map ⋙
            globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, max u v, max u v} O p) (op n)).hom y) ⊥) =
      (Ideal.span {f}).adicModuleTopology
        (limit (Functor.ofOpSequence map ⋙ globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, max u v, max u v} O p) :
          ModuleCat.{max u v} ↥(GlobalSectionRing O))
declarations.comment: both conclusions: `f^c Hᵖ` is the kernel of `Hᵖ → Hᵖ(X, 𝓕_c)` for all `c ≥ 1`, and the limit topology on `Hᵖ` is the `f`-adic topology

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.isEssentiallyConstantInverseSystem_localCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EHB.** If the canonical map from the local cohomology of a finite
module to the inverse limit of the local cohomology of a countable inverse
system of finite modules is an isomorphism, that local cohomology system is
essentially constant.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEssentiallyConstantInverseSystem_localCohomology
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (F : CategoryTheory.Functor ℕᵒᵖ (ModuleCat.{v} A))
    (hF : ∀ n, Module.Finite A (F.obj n))
    (M : ModuleCat.{v} A) [Module.Finite A M] (i : ℤ)
    [HasLimit F] [HasLimit (F ⋙ localCohomologyModuleFunctor A i)]
    (f : M ⟶ limit F)
    (_ : IsIso ((localCohomologyModuleFunctor A i).map f ≫
      limit.post F (localCohomologyModuleFunctor A i))) :
    CategoryTheory.IsEssentiallyConstantInverseSystem
      (F ⋙ localCohomologyModuleFunctor A i)
