    (_homega : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex (A := A) (K := omega))
    (T T' : Set (PrimeSpectrum A)) (_hTT' : T ⊆ T')
    (_hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (_hT' : StableUnderSpecialization T')
    (s : ℤ) (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (_hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K)) :
    (∃ J : Ideal A, PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ⊆ T' ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ s → J ≤ Module.annihilator A
        (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus
          A T K i)) ↔
    (∀ p q : PrimeSpectrum A, p ∉ T' → q ∈ T → (hpq : p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal) →
      letI : (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal)).IsPrime :=
        Ideal.isPrime_map_quotientMk_of_isPrime hpq
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
          (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
          (localizedComplex p K) : EInt) +
        krullDimToEInt
          (ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime
            (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal)))) > (s : EInt)))

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.annihilatorDepthCriterionPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EHZ.** The annihilator criterion for a bounded-below complex with finite
cohomology over a Noetherian ring admitting a dualizing complex, in the predicate form in
which this library states it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem annihilatorDepthCriterionPlus (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    AnnihilatorDepthCriterionPlus.{u, u, u} A
declarations.comment: the criterion, in predicate form

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.exists_annihilator_localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EI1, the implication (1) ⟹ (2).** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, let
`T ⊆ Spec(A)` be any subset, let `K` be an object of the bounded-below derived category of
`A`-modules and let `n ∈ ℤ`. If `H^i_T(K)` is finite for every `i ≤ n`, then there is an ideal
`J ⊆ A` with `V(J) ⊆ T` annihilating `H^i_T(K)` for every `i ≤ n`.

Below a degree `a` bounding `K` below the modules vanish, so their annihilator is the unit
ideal; on `[a, n]` each is annihilated by its own annihilator, whose zero locus is its support
and hence contained in `T`; the product of those finitely many ideals is the required `J`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_annihilator_localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_of_finite (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (T : Set (PrimeSpectrum A))
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (n : ℤ)
    (hfin : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n →
      Module.Finite A (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A T K i)) :
    ∃ J : Ideal A, PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ⊆ T ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n → J ≤ Module.annihilator A
        (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A T K i)
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (2); the converse (2) ⟹ (1) is not proved

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.exists_pow_annihilator_localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EI1, the implication (1) ⟹ (3) for closed support.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring,
let `I ⊆ A` be an ideal and write `Z = V(I)`, let `K` be an object of the bounded-below derived
category of `A`-modules and let `n ∈ ℤ`. If `H^i_Z(K)` is finite for every `i ≤ n`, then there is
an `e ≥ 0` such that `I ^ e` annihilates `H^i_Z(K)` for every `i ≤ n`.

The ideal produced by the implication `(1) ⟹ (2)` has zero locus inside `V(I)`, so `I` lies in
its radical and a power of `I` lies inside it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_annihilator_localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_of_finite (A : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (n : ℤ)
    (hfin : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n → Module.Finite A (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A
      (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A)) K i)) :
    ∃ e : ℕ, ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n → I ^ e ≤ Module.annihilator A
      (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A
        (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A)) K i)
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⟹ (3) for closed support T = V(I); (3) ⟹ (1) is not proved

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_finite_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EI1, the equivalence of (1) and (2).** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, let
`T ⊆ Spec(A)` be stable under specialization, let `K` be an object of `D⁺_{Coh}(A)` and let
`n ∈ ℤ`. Then `H^i_T(K)` is finite for every `i ≤ n` exactly when one ideal `J ⊆ A` with
`V(J) ⊆ T` annihilates `H^i_T(K)` for every `i ≤ n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_finite_tfae (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (T : Set (PrimeSpectrum A)) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i).obj K))
    (n : ℤ) :
    List.TFAE
      [∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n → Module.Finite A (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A T K i),
        ∃ J : Ideal A, PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ⊆ T ∧
          ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n → J ≤ Module.annihilator A
            (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A T K i)]
declarations.comment:
the equivalence of (1) and (2), for T stable under specialization and K
bounded below with finite cohomology modules

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_finite_tfae_zeroLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EI1, the equivalence of (1), (2) and (3) for closed support.** Let `A` be a
Noetherian ring, let `I ⊆ A` be an ideal and write `Z = V(I)`, let `K` be an object of
`D⁺_{Coh}(A)` and let `n ∈ ℤ`. Then the following are equivalent: `H^i_Z(K)` is finite for every
`i ≤ n`; one ideal `J ⊆ A` with `V(J) ⊆ Z` annihilates `H^i_Z(K)` for every `i ≤ n`; some power
`I ^ e` annihilates `H^i_Z(K)` for every `i ≤ n`.

A zero locus is closed, so the first equivalence is the one above, and the second is the
ideal-theoretic statement that an ideal has zero locus inside `V(I)` exactly when it contains a
power of `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_finite_tfae_zeroLocus (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i).obj K))
    (n : ℤ) :
    List.TFAE
      [∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n → Module.Finite A (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A
          (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A)) K i),
        ∃ J : Ideal A,
          PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ⊆ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) ∧
          ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n → J ≤ Module.annihilator A (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A
            (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A)) K i),
        ∃ e : ℕ, ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n → I ^ e ≤ Module.annihilator A
          (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A
            (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A)) K i)]
declarations.comment:
the equivalence of (1), (2) and (3) for closed support T = V(I), for K
bounded below with finite cohomology modules

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.depth_add_dim_gt_of_finite_localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EI2, the implication (1) ⟹ (2).** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring with a dualizing
complex, let `T ⊆ Spec(A)` be stable under specialization, let `s ∈ ℤ` and let `K` be a
bounded-below complex with finite cohomology modules. If `H^i_T(K)` is finite for every `i ≤ s`,
then `depth_{A_p}(K_p) + dim((A/p)_q) > s` for every `p ∉ T` and `q ∈ T` with `p ⊆ q`.

Finiteness gives one ideal supported in `T` annihilating all of `H^i_T(K)` for `i ≤ s`, by
`exists_annihilator_localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_of_finite`; the annihilator criterion of
Tag 0EHZ at `T' = T` turns that ideal into the depth-dimension inequality.
declarations.statement:
theorem depth_add_dim_gt_of_finite_localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hEHZ : AnnihilatorDepthCriterionPlus.{u, v, w} A)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{w} A))
    (homega : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex omega)
    (T : Set (PrimeSpectrum A)) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (s : ℤ) (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i).obj K))
    (hfin : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ s →
      Module.Finite A (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A T K i)) :
    ∀ p q : PrimeSpectrum A, p ∉ T → q ∈ T → (hpq : p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal) →
      letI : (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal)).IsPrime :=
        Ideal.isPrime_map_quotientMk_of_isPrime hpq
      (DerivedCategory.Plus.depth.{u, v} (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
          (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
          (localizedComplex.{u, v} p K) : EInt) +
        Stacks.Algebraization.krullDimToEInt
          (ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime
            (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal)))) > (s : EInt)
declarations.comment:
the implication (1) ⟹ (2), assuming only Tag 0EHZ's annihilator criterion
  (`AnnihilatorDepthCriterionPlus`), which is proved in `FaltingsAnnihilator.lean`; the step from
  finiteness to a uniform annihilator is proved

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_finite_iff_depth_add_dim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EI2, Proposition 51.14.2: finiteness of local cohomology, III.** Let `A` be a
Noetherian ring with a dualizing complex, let `T ⊆ Spec(A)` be stable under specialization, let
`s ∈ ℤ` and let `K` be a bounded-below complex with finite cohomology modules. Then `H^i_T(K)` is
finite for every `i ≤ s` if and only if `depth_{A_p}(K_p) + dim((A/p)_q) > s` for every `p ∉ T`
and `q ∈ T` with `p ⊆ q`.

This is the composition the source performs: the finiteness criterion of Tag 0EI1 replaces
finiteness through degree `s` by uniform annihilation by one ideal supported in `T`, and the
annihilator criterion of Tag 0EHZ at `T' = T` replaces that uniform annihilation by the
depth-dimension inequality.
declarations.statement:
theorem localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_finite_iff_depth_add_dim
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hEI1 : FinitenessAnnihilatorCriterionPlus.{u, v} A)
    (hEHZ : AnnihilatorDepthCriterionPlus.{u, v, w} A)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{w} A))
    (homega : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex omega)
    (T : Set (PrimeSpectrum A)) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (s : ℤ) (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i).obj K)) :
    (∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ s →
      Module.Finite A (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, v} A T K i)) ↔
      (∀ p q : PrimeSpectrum A, p ∉ T → q ∈ T → (hpq : p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal) →
        letI : (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal)).IsPrime :=
          Ideal.isPrime_map_quotientMk_of_isPrime hpq
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.depth.{u, v} (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
            (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
            (localizedComplex.{u, v} p K) : EInt) +
          Stacks.Algebraization.krullDimToEInt
            (ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime
              (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal)))) > (s : EInt))
declarations.comment:
the full equivalence (1) ⟺ (2), assuming Tag 0EI1's finiteness criterion
  (`FinitenessAnnihilatorCriterionPlus`), whose direction from an annihilator to finiteness is not
  proved in this library, and Tag 0EHZ's annihilator criterion
  (`AnnihilatorDepthCriterionPlus`), which is proved in `FaltingsAnnihilator.lean`

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_finite_iff_depth_add_dim_sameUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EI2, Proposition 51.14.2: finiteness of local cohomology, III.** Let `A` be a
Noetherian ring admitting a dualizing complex, let `T ⊆ Spec(A)` be stable under specialization,
let `s ∈ ℤ` and let `K` be an object of the bounded-below derived category of `A`-modules whose
cohomology modules are all finite. Then `H^i_T(K)` is finite for every `i ≤ s` if and only if
`depth_{A_p}(K_p) + dim((A/p)_q) > s` for every pair of primes `p ∉ T`, `q ∈ T` with `p ⊆ q`.

This is the composition the source performs: the finiteness criterion of Tag 0EI1 replaces
finiteness through degree `s` by uniform annihilation by one ideal supported in `T`, and the
annihilator criterion of Tag 0EHZ at `T' = T` replaces that uniform annihilation by the
depth-dimension inequality. Both criteria are proved in this library, so nothing is assumed here
beyond the hypotheses of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus_finite_iff_depth_add_dim_sameUniverse
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (homega : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex omega)
    (T : Set (PrimeSpectrum A)) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (s : ℤ) (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K)) :
    (∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ s →
      Module.Finite A (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus.{u, u} A T K i)) ↔
      (∀ p q : PrimeSpectrum A, p ∉ T → q ∈ T → (hpq : p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal) →
        letI : (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal)).IsPrime :=
          Ideal.isPrime_map_quotientMk_of_isPrime hpq
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.depth.{u, u} (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
            (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
            (localizedComplex.{u, u} p K) : EInt) +
          Stacks.Algebraization.krullDimToEInt
            (ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime
              (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal)))) > (s : EInt))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_isCoherent_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI3, existence for a closed subset.** A coherent module `F` on a
Noetherian scheme admits a map to a coherent module which is an isomorphism on the stalks away
from a closed subset `T` and whose stalks on `T` have depth at least two, as soon as the single
pushforward `j_{V,*}(F'|_V)` is coherent — where `V` is the complement of `T` and `F'` is the
depth-one quotient of `F` along `T`.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.isStabilizedOpenExtension_unit` this replaces the hypothesis
`hext` of `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_isStabilizedOpenExtension`, which asks
for a coherent stabilized open extension, by coherence of one explicit module: for a closed `T`
no colimit of pushforwards over the opens whose complement lies in `T` is needed, because the
complement of `T` is itself such an open and is the smallest one.

The remaining hypothesis is not removable; it is where the two hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 0EI3]
absent from `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension` — a dualizing complex and a depth
bound across the boundary of `T` — must re-enter.  See the implementation notes of this
module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_isCoherent_pushforward
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (V : X.Opens)
    (hV : (V : Set X) = Tᶜ) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hcoh : ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward V.ι).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback V.ι).obj
      (depthOneQuotient X T hT.stableUnderSpecialization F))).IsCoherent) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsDepthTwoExtension T φ
declarations.comment: existence for a closed subset, conditional only on coherence of the single pushforward of the restriction of the depth-one quotient to the complement; the hypothesis hext of exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_isStabilizedOpenExtension, namely a coherent stabilized open extension, is discharged here for a closed subset

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_locallyHasDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI3, existence along a closed subset.** Let `X` be a Noetherian
scheme which locally has a dualizing complex, let `V` be an open of `X` with complement `T` —
so `T` is closed — and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module such that `depth(F_x) ≥ 1` whenever
some point of `T` is an immediate specialization of `x ∉ T`.  Then `F` admits a depth-two
extension along `T`.

No hypothesis about extensions or colimits is left: the module is the single pushforward
`j_{V,*}(F'|_V)` of the depth-one quotient, which is a stabilized open extension by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isStabilizedOpenExtension_unit` and coherent by
`isCoherent_pushforward_restrict_depthOneQuotient`.  The two
hypotheses are the source's, and both are necessary.  See the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_locallyHasDualizingComplex
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T : Set X) (V : X.Opens) (hV : (V : Set X) = Tᶜ)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hdual : LocallyHasDualizingComplex X)
    (hdepth : ∀ x z : X, x ∉ T → z ∈ T → TopologicalSpace.IsImmediateSpecialization x z →
      (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x)) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsDepthTwoExtension T φ
declarations.comment: existence along a closed subset, with no hypothesis about extensions or colimits, and at the source's hypotheses: the dualizing hypothesis and the depth hypothesis on immediate specializations, nothing else, the coherence of the single pushforward coming from the source's Faltings criterion Tag 0EFD

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_stableUnderSpecialization
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme which locally has a dualizing complex, let `T ⊆ X` be stable
under specialization and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module such that `depth(F_x) ≥ 1` whenever
some point of `T` is an immediate specialization of `x ∉ T`.  Then `F` admits a depth-two
extension along `T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_stableUnderSpecialization
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T : Set X) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (hdual : LocallyHasDualizingComplex X)
    (hdepth : ∀ x z : X, x ∉ T → z ∈ T → TopologicalSpace.IsImmediateSpecialization x z →
      (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x)) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsDepthTwoExtension T φ
declarations.comment: existence along a specialization-stable subset, at exactly the source's two hypotheses — the dualizing hypothesis and the depth hypothesis on immediate specializations — with no hypothesis about extensions, colimits, a closed subset of T, or finiteness of an exceptional locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.depthTwoExtension_unique
declarations.doc:
Two depth-two extensions of a module along a subset are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism
compatible with the two maps.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depthTwoExtension_unique
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (T : Set X)
    (F G H : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G) (ψ : F ⟶ H)
    (hφ : IsDepthTwoExtension T φ) (hψ : IsDepthTwoExtension T ψ) :
    ∃! e : G ≅ H, φ ≫ e.hom = ψ
declarations.comment: uniqueness, unconditionally: the subset is arbitrary and no dualizing complex is needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_hasDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**Existence of the depth-two extension.**  Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme which locally has a
dualizing complex, let `T ⊆ X` be stable under specialization and let `F` be coherent.  Assume
`depth(F_x) ≥ 1` at every immediate specialization `x ⤳ x'` with `x' ∈ T` and `x ∉ T`.  Then `F`
admits a map to a coherent module which is an isomorphism on the stalks off `T` and whose stalks
on `T` have depth at least two.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_hasDualizingComplex
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (hdual : HasDualizingComplexOnAffineCover X)
    (T : Set X) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (himm : ∀ x x' : X, IsImmediateSpecialization x x' → x' ∈ T → x ∉ T →
      (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (F.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsDepthTwoExtension T φ
declarations.comment: existence, at the source's hypotheses: X Noetherian with a dualizing complex on an affine open cover, T stable under specialization, F coherent, and depth at least one at the immediate specializations into T from outside T; the witness is the single direct image j_*(F|_{X ∖ Z}) across the closure Z of the low-depth locus, not the source's colimit of pushforwards, and its coherence is proved here from Faltings through Tag 0BJY

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_isDepthTwoExtension_of_hasDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**Existence and uniqueness of the depth-two extension.**  Under the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_hasDualizingComplex` there is a map `F ⟶ F''`
of coherent modules which is an isomorphism on the stalks off `T` and whose stalks on `T` have
depth at least two, and it is unique: any other such map is carried to it by a unique
isomorphism under `F`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_isDepthTwoExtension_of_hasDualizingComplex
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (hdual : HasDualizingComplexOnAffineCover X)
    (T : Set X) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (himm : ∀ x x' : X, IsImmediateSpecialization x x' → x' ∈ T → x ∉ T →
      (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (F.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsDepthTwoExtension T φ ∧
      ∀ (H : X.Modules) (ψ : F ⟶ H), IsDepthTwoExtension T ψ →
        ∃! e : G ≅ H, φ ≫ e.hom = ψ
declarations.comment: the source's unique map, as existence together with uniqueness up to a unique isomorphism under F, at the source's hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI3, existence.** A coherent module on a Noetherian scheme admits a
map to a coherent module which is an isomorphism on the stalks away from a
specialization-stable subset and whose stalks on that subset have depth at least two.

Two inputs of the source's proof are carried as hypotheses, because this library does not have
them.

* `hext` asks for the extension of the depth-one quotient of `F` across `T` by sections over the
  opens whose complement lies in `T` — the colimit of the pushforwards `j_{V,*}(F'|_V)` — as a
  coherent module.  Its coherence is what the source derives from Faltings' finiteness criterion
  [Stacks, Tag 0EFD] applied to a dualizing complex, using the hypothesis that `X` locally has
  one and the hypothesis on the depth of `F` at the immediate specializations into `T`.  Those
  two hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 0EI3] therefore do not appear here.
* `hdepthOutside` is [Stacks, Tag 0EY0] part (3), the converse of
  `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_unit_restrict_pushforward_of_depth_ge_two`.

The map itself, the clause away from `T` and the depth clause on `T` are proved.  See the
implementation notes of this module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDepthTwoExtension
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T : Set X) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hdepthOutside : ∀ (V : X.Opens) (H : X.Modules), H.IsCoherent →
      IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction V.ι).unit.app H) →
      ∀ y : X, y ∉ (V : Set X) →
        letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk y)
            (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) H.val.presheaf y) :=
          PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
            (R := X.presheaf) H.val y
        (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk y)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk y))
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) H.val.presheaf y))
    (hext : ∃ (G : X.Modules) (ψ : depthOneQuotient X T hT F ⟶ G),
      IsStabilizedOpenExtension T ψ) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsDepthTwoExtension T φ
declarations.comment: existence, conditional on a coherent stabilized open extension of the depth-one quotient along the subset and on Tag 0EY0 part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.depthTwoExtension_pullback
declarations.doc:
The pullback of a depth-two extension along a Cohen–Macaulay morphism of Noetherian schemes
is a depth-two extension along the inverse image of the subset.

The hypothesis `hfib`, that the fibres of `f` are locally Noetherian, is the one under which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay` is stated; it follows from `[IsNoetherian Y]` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_fiber`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depthTwoExtension_pullback
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (T : Set X) (F G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hφ : IsDepthTwoExtension T φ)
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (hfib : ∀ x : X, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber x))
    (hcm : f.IsCohenMacaulay hfib) :
    IsDepthTwoExtension (f ⁻¹' T) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).map φ)
declarations.comment: the Cohen-Macaulay pullback clause, unconditionally

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_isStabilizedOpenExtension
declarations.doc:
A coherent module on a Noetherian scheme admits a map to a coherent module which is an
isomorphism on the stalks away from a specialization-stable subset and whose stalks on that
subset have depth at least two, as soon as the depth-one quotient has a stabilized open
extension across the subset.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_isStabilizedOpenExtension
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T : Set X) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hext : ∃ (G : X.Modules) (ψ : depthOneQuotient X T hT F ⟶ G),
      IsStabilizedOpenExtension T ψ) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsDepthTwoExtension T φ
declarations.comment: existence, conditional only on a coherent stabilized open extension of the depth-one quotient along the subset; the other hypothesis of exists_isDepthTwoExtension, namely Tag 0EY0 part (3), is discharged here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_isClosed_of_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI3, existence along a specialization-stable subset.** Let `X` be a
Noetherian scheme which locally has a dualizing complex, let `T ⊆ X` be stable under
specialization and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module such that `depth(F_x) ≥ 1` whenever some
point of `T` is an immediate specialization of `x ∉ T`.  Let `Z ⊆ T` be closed and such that the
depth-one quotient `F'` of `F` along `T` already has `depth(F'_x) ≥ 2` at the points of `T`
outside `Z`.  Then `F` admits a depth-two extension along `T`.

No hypothesis about extensions or colimits is left, and the depth-two extension is the single
pushforward `j_{Zᶜ,*}(F'|_{Zᶜ})`: for a closed `T` one may take `Z = T`, recovering
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_locallyHasDualizingComplex`.  See the module
documentation for the three clauses and for the status of `Z` itself.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_isClosed_of_subset
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T : Set X) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hdual : LocallyHasDualizingComplex X)
    (hdepth : ∀ x z : X, x ∉ T → z ∈ T → TopologicalSpace.IsImmediateSpecialization x z →
      (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x))
    (Z : Set X) (hZclosed : IsClosed Z) (hZT : Z ⊆ T)
    (hZ : ∀ x : X, x ∈ T → x ∉ Z →
      letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (depthOneQuotient X T hT F).val.presheaf x) :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          (R := X.presheaf) (depthOneQuotient X T hT F).val x
      (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u})
          (depthOneQuotient X T hT F).val.presheaf x)) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsDepthTwoExtension T φ
declarations.comment: existence along a specialization-stable subset, with no hypothesis about extensions or colimits, and at the source's hypotheses — the dualizing hypothesis and the depth hypothesis on immediate specializations — together with a closed subset of T outside which the depth-one quotient already has depth two on T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_finite_depthOne_locus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI3, existence along a specialization-stable subset, from finiteness
of the depth-one locus.** Same as `exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_isClosed_of_subset`, with the
closed subset replaced by the hypothesis that the set of points of `T` where the depth-one
quotient `F'` still has depth below two is **finite**.

A finite set of points has closed closure — the union of the finitely many closures of its
points — and that closure stays inside `T` because `T` is stable under specialization.  So the
finite set's closure is a legitimate `Z`, and the remaining gap in the existence half of
[Stacks, Tag 0EI3] is exactly this finiteness.  It is the shape the finiteness theorems about
depth take: [Stacks, Tag 0ECN] (`AlgebraicGeometry.finite_setOf_depth_eq_and_lt_supportDim`)
says that on a Noetherian scheme with a dualizing complex a coherent module satisfying Serre's
condition `(S₁)` has only finitely many points with `depth(F'_x) = 1` and
`dim Supp(F'_x) > 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_finite_depthOne_locus
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T : Set X) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hdual : LocallyHasDualizingComplex X)
    (hdepth : ∀ x z : X, x ∉ T → z ∈ T → TopologicalSpace.IsImmediateSpecialization x z →
      (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x))
    (hfin : {x : X | x ∈ T ∧
      letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (depthOneQuotient X T hT F).val.presheaf x) :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          (R := X.presheaf) (depthOneQuotient X T hT F).val x
      Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u})
          (depthOneQuotient X T hT F).val.presheaf x) < (2 : ℕ∞)}.Finite) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsDepthTwoExtension T φ
declarations.comment: existence along a specialization-stable subset, with no hypothesis about extensions or colimits, and at the source's hypotheses — the dualizing hypothesis and the depth hypothesis on immediate specializations — together with finiteness of the set of points of T where the depth-one quotient still has depth below two

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isNestedImprovement_of_isStabilizedOpenExtension
declarations.doc:
A coherent module on a Noetherian scheme admits an improvement along a nested pair `T' ⊆ T`
of subsets stable under specialization, as soon as the depth-one quotient along `T` has a
stabilized open extension across `T'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isNestedImprovement_of_isStabilizedOpenExtension
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T T' : Set X) (hTT' : T' ⊆ T)
    (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hext : ∃ (G : X.Modules) (ψ : depthOneQuotient X T hT F ⟶ G),
      IsStabilizedOpenExtension T' ψ) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsNestedImprovement T T' φ
declarations.comment: existence, conditional only on a coherent stabilized open extension of the depth-one quotient along T'; the other hypothesis of exists_isNestedImprovement, namely Tag 0EY0 part (3), is discharged here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nestedImprovement_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI4, uniqueness.** Two improvements of a coherent module along the
same pair of subsets are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism compatible with the two maps.

Each one factors through the depth-one quotient of its source along `T` by a depth-two extension
along `T'`, so the comparison is the one of [Stacks, Tag 0EI3], transported across the
epimorphism onto the depth-one quotient.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nestedImprovement_unique (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (T T' : Set X) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (F G H : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (φ : F ⟶ G) (ψ : F ⟶ H)
    (hφ : IsNestedImprovement T T' φ) (hψ : IsNestedImprovement T T' ψ) :
    ∃! e : G ≅ H, φ ≫ e.hom = ψ
declarations.comment: uniqueness, unconditionally: no dualizing complex is needed, no condition on immediate specializations is used, and the inclusion T' ⊆ T is not needed either

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isNestedImprovement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI4, existence.** A coherent module on a Noetherian scheme admits an
improvement along a nested pair `T' ⊆ T` of subsets stable under specialization: a map to a
coherent module which is an isomorphism on the stalks away from `T`, is surjective on the stalks
with target of depth at least one at the points of `T` outside `T'`, and has target of depth at
least two at the points of `T'`.

The map is the depth-one quotient of `F` along `T` followed by a depth-two extension of that
quotient along `T'`, which is the source's construction.  The hypotheses `hdepthOutside` and
`hext` are the two inputs of the source's existence proof which this library does not have; they
subsume what the source extracts from the dualizing complex and from the condition on immediate
specializations into `T'`, so neither of those two hypotheses of the source appears here.  See
the implementation notes of this module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isNestedImprovement (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (T T' : Set X) (hTT' : T' ⊆ T) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hdepthOutside : ∀ (V : X.Opens) (H : X.Modules), H.IsCoherent →
      IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction V.ι).unit.app H) →
      ∀ y : X, y ∉ (V : Set X) →
        letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk y)
            (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) H.val.presheaf y) :=
          PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
            (R := X.presheaf) H.val y
        (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk y)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk y))
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) H.val.presheaf y))
    (hext : ∃ (G : X.Modules) (ψ : depthOneQuotient X T hT F ⟶ G),
      IsStabilizedOpenExtension T' ψ) :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsNestedImprovement T T' φ
declarations.comment: existence, conditional on a coherent stabilized open extension of the depth-one quotient along T' and on Tag 0EY0 part (3); as for Tag 0EI3 in this library, those two hypotheses replace the dualizing complex and the condition on immediate specializations, which are therefore not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback_of_isNestedImprovement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI4, the pullback clause: coherence of the target.** The target of the
pullback of an improvement along a morphism with locally Noetherian source is again coherent.

A pullback of a coherent module needs only a locally Noetherian source, so neither flatness nor
Cohen-Macaulayness of the morphism is used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCoherent_pullback_of_isNestedImprovement {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (f : Y ⟶ X) {T T' : Set X} {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hφ : IsNestedImprovement T T' φ) :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G).IsCoherent
declarations.comment: coherence of the target of the pullback, in the assertion about the pullback along a Cohen-Macaulay morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_stalk_pullback_of_isNestedImprovement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI4, the pullback clause, condition (1).** The pullback of an
improvement along any morphism of schemes is an isomorphism on the stalks at every point outside
the inverse image of `T`.

The stalk of a pullback is the base change of the stalk, so a bijective stalk map stays
bijective; no hypothesis on the morphism is used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_stalk_pullback_of_isNestedImprovement {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    {T T' : Set X} {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G) (hφ : IsNestedImprovement T T' φ)
    (y : Y) (hy : y ∉ f.base ⁻¹' T) :
    IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab.{u} y).map
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).map φ).mapPresheaf)
declarations.comment: condition (1) for the pullback: the isomorphism away from the inverse image of T, in the assertion about the pullback along a Cohen-Macaulay morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.one_le_depth_stalk_pullback_of_isNestedImprovement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI4, the pullback clause, the depth bound of condition (2).** The
target of the pullback of an improvement along a Cohen-Macaulay morphism of Noetherian schemes
has stalks of depth at least one at every point of the inverse image of `T` lying outside the
inverse image of `T'`.

Only the flatness half of the Cohen-Macaulay hypothesis is used: the depth of the base change of
a stalk along a flat local homomorphism is the depth of the stalk plus the depth of the fibre, so
the bound downstairs is inherited.
declarations.statement:
public theorem one_le_depth_stalk_pullback_of_isNestedImprovement {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] {T T' : Set X} {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hφ : IsNestedImprovement T T' φ) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hfib : ∀ x : X, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber x)) (hcm : f.IsCohenMacaulay hfib)
    (y : Y) (hy : y ∈ f.base ⁻¹' T) (hy' : y ∉ f.base ⁻¹' T') :
    letI : Module (Y.presheaf.stalk y)
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u})
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G).val.presheaf y) :=
      PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
        (R := Y.presheaf) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G).val y
    (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (Y.presheaf.stalk y)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk y))
      (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u})
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G).val.presheaf y)
declarations.comment: the depth bound of condition (2) for the pullback, in the assertion about the pullback along a Cohen-Macaulay morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.two_le_depth_stalk_pullback_of_isNestedImprovement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI4, the pullback clause, condition (3).** The target of the pullback
of an improvement along a Cohen-Macaulay morphism of Noetherian schemes has stalks of depth at
least two at every point of the inverse image of `T'`.

Only the flatness half of the Cohen-Macaulay hypothesis is used, by the same depth formula along
a flat local homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem two_le_depth_stalk_pullback_of_isNestedImprovement {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] {T T' : Set X} {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hφ : IsNestedImprovement T T' φ) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hfib : ∀ x : X, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber x)) (hcm : f.IsCohenMacaulay hfib)
    (y : Y) (hy' : y ∈ f.base ⁻¹' T') :
    letI : Module (Y.presheaf.stalk y)
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u})
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G).val.presheaf y) :=
      PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
        (R := Y.presheaf) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G).val y
    (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (Y.presheaf.stalk y)
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk y))
      (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u})
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G).val.presheaf y)
declarations.comment: condition (3) for the pullback, in the assertion about the pullback along a Cohen-Macaulay morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNestedImprovement_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI4, the assertion about the pullback.** The pullback of an improvement
along a Cohen-Macaulay morphism of Noetherian schemes is an improvement along the inverse images
of the two subsets.

Coherence of the target and condition (1) need no hypothesis on the morphism at all.  Of the
Cohen-Macaulay hypothesis only the flatness half is used, for the two depth bounds, by the formula
for the change in depth along a flat local homomorphism [Stacks, Tag 0338]; the fibre never has to
be identified.  Surjectivity in condition (2) is epimorphy on a stalk, which is the vanishing of
the stalk of the cokernel, and the pullback preserves cokernels and kills the zero module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNestedImprovement_pullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    {T T' : Set X} {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G) (hφ : IsNestedImprovement T T' φ) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hfib : ∀ x : X, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber x)) (hcm : f.IsCohenMacaulay hfib) :
    IsNestedImprovement (f.base ⁻¹' T) (f.base ⁻¹' T')
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).map φ)
declarations.comment: the assertion about the pullback along a Cohen-Macaulay morphism: the pullback satisfies conditions (1), (2) and (3) with respect to the inverse images of the two subsets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isNestedImprovement_of_hasDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI4, existence, at the hypotheses of the source.** Let `X` be a
Noetherian scheme which locally has a dualizing complex and let `T' ⊆ T ⊆ X` be stable under
specialization and such that every immediate specialization into `T'` starts in `T`.  Then a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` admits a map to a coherent module which is an isomorphism on the
stalks away from `T`, is surjective on the stalks with target of depth at least one at the
points of `T` outside `T'`, and has target of depth at least two at the points of `T'`.

The map is the depth-one quotient of `F` along `T` followed by a depth-two extension of that
quotient along `T'`, which is the source's construction: the first step is [Stacks, Tag 0DX3],
the second is the existence half of [Stacks, Tag 0EI3] in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isDepthTwoExtension_of_hasDualizingComplex`, and the composition is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isNestedImprovement_depthOneQuotient_comp`.

The dualizing hypothesis is `AlgebraicGeometry.HasDualizingComplexOnAffineCover`, which says
every point has an affine open neighbourhood whose ring of sections admits a dualizing complex.
That is the source's phrase "locally has a dualizing complex", and it is **weaker** than
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyHasDualizingComplex`, which asks this of *every* affine open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isNestedImprovement_of_hasDualizingComplex
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (hdual : HasDualizingComplexOnAffineCover X)
    (T T' : Set X) (hTT' : T' ⊆ T)
    (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T) (hT' : StableUnderSpecialization T')
    (himm : ∀ x x' : X, IsImmediateSpecialization x x' → x' ∈ T' → x ∈ T)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsNestedImprovement T T' φ
declarations.comment: existence, at the hypotheses of the source and no others: Noetherian, locally a dualizing complex in the source's sense that every point has an affine neighbourhood carrying one, T' subset T both stable under specialization, immediate specializations into T' starting in T. Tag 0EI3 existence is composed with Tag 0DX3 here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_isNestedImprovement_of_hasDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EI4, the source's unique map.** Under the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isNestedImprovement_of_hasDualizingComplex` there is a map `F ⟶ F''`
of coherent modules which is an isomorphism on the stalks away from `T`, is surjective on the
stalks with target of depth at least one at the points of `T` outside `T'`, and has target of
depth at least two at the points of `T'`; and it is unique: any other such map is carried to it
by a unique isomorphism under `F`.

This is the source's sentence "there exists a unique map" in one statement.  Existence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isNestedImprovement_of_hasDualizingComplex` and uniqueness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.nestedImprovement_unique`, which needs neither the dualizing complex, nor the
condition on immediate specializations, nor `T' ⊆ T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_isNestedImprovement_of_hasDualizingComplex
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (hdual : HasDualizingComplexOnAffineCover X)
    (T T' : Set X) (hTT' : T' ⊆ T)
    (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T) (hT' : StableUnderSpecialization T')
    (himm : ∀ x x' : X, IsImmediateSpecialization x x' → x' ∈ T' → x ∈ T)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    ∃ (G : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ G), IsNestedImprovement T T' φ ∧
      ∀ (H : X.Modules) (ψ : F ⟶ H), IsNestedImprovement T T' ψ →
        ∃! e : G ≅ H, φ ≫ e.hom = ψ
declarations.comment: the source's unique map, as existence together with uniqueness up to a unique isomorphism under F, at the hypotheses of the source and no others

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.AdicInverseSystem.isZero_cohomology_limitModule_of_affineOpen
declarations.doc:
The positive-degree cohomology of the inverse limit of an adic inverse system vanishes on
every affine open.
declarations.comment: affine_vanishing

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.AdicInverseSystem.isDerivedLimit_single_limitModule
declarations.doc:
The inverse limit of an adic inverse system **is** its derived inverse limit: placed in
degree zero, `F = lim F_n` sits in the defining distinguished triangle
`F ⟶ ∏ F_n ⟶ ∏ F_n ⟶ F[1]` of `R lim F_n`.

The terms are quasi-coherent, hence acyclic on the affine opens, and the transitions are
surjective on affine sections, so `R¹ lim` of the sections vanishes there; those are exactly
the two hypotheses under which the ordinary limit computes the derived one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDerivedLimit_single_limitModule :
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ =>
        (S.system ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj ⟨n⟩),
      @IsDerivedLimit (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace)))
        _ _ _ _ _ _
        (S.system ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace)) 0) h
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj S.limitModule)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.AdicInverseSystem.exists_shortExact_cohomology_limitModule
declarations.doc:
**The Milnor short exact sequence of an adic inverse system.** For every degree `p` the
cohomology of `F = lim F_n` sits in a short exact sequence

`0 ⟶ R¹ lim H^(p-1)(X, F_n) ⟶ H^p(X, F) ⟶ lim H^p(X, F_n) ⟶ 0`.

Cohomology is read over a base ring `A` mapping to `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` by `ρ`, as the degree-`p`
cohomology of `RΓ(X, -)` applied to a module placed in degree zero; for `A = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and
`ρ` the identity this is sheaf cohomology with its module structure, the identification being
`Stacks.Cohomology.ModuleComparison.hfunctorIsoHomologyDerivedSectionsOver`. `R¹ lim` is the
cokernel of the difference map `1 - shift` on the product of the groups `H^(p-1)(X, F_n)`.

The sequence comes from the Milnor triangle of `RΓ(X, F)`: the ordinary limit is a derived
limit of the system by `isDerivedLimit_single_limitModule`, and derived sections commute with
derived limits. The inclusion descends the connecting morphism of that triangle and the
projection is characterized by its composites with the limit projections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_shortExact_cohomology_limitModule {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (ρ : A →+* (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj
      (op (⊤ : Opens S.X.toRingedSpace.carrier))) :
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    let K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace)) :=
      S.system ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace)) :=
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj S.limitModule
    let F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) :=
      K ⋙ derivedSectionsOver S.X.toRingedSpace ρ
    let Y : ℕ → DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) := fun n ↦ F.obj (op n)
    let d : (∏ᶜ Y) ⟶ ∏ᶜ Y := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
      Pi.π Y n - Pi.π Y (n + 1) ≫ F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
    ∃ (a : (derivedSectionsOver S.X.toRingedSpace ρ).obj L ⟶ ∏ᶜ Y)
      (b : (∏ᶜ Y) ⟶ ((derivedSectionsOver S.X.toRingedSpace ρ).obj L)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      let T := Triangle.mk a d b
      T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) ∧
        ∀ p : ℤ,
          let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) p
          let H₁ := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (p - 1)
          let homologySystem : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A := F ⋙ H
          let shiftedHomologySystem : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A := F ⋙ H₁
          let P : ModuleCat.{u} A :=
            ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (op n)
          let δ : P ⟶ P := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (op n)) n -
              Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (op n)) (n + 1) ≫
                shiftedHomologySystem.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
          ∃ (e : H₁.obj (∏ᶜ Y) ≅ P)
            (i : cokernel δ ⟶ H.obj ((derivedSectionsOver S.X.toRingedSpace ρ).obj L))
            (q : H.obj ((derivedSectionsOver S.X.toRingedSpace ρ).obj L) ⟶
              limit homologySystem)
            (w : i ≫ q = 0),
            e.hom = piComparison H₁ Y ∧
              cokernel.π δ ≫ i = e.inv ≫
                DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ T (p - 1) p ∧
              (∀ n : ℕ, q ≫ limit.π homologySystem (op n) =
                H.map a ≫ H.map (Pi.π Y n)) ∧
              (ShortComplex.mk i q w).ShortExact
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.AdicInverseSystem.idealPowerMultiple_limit
declarations.doc:
A morphism into the inverse limit factors through `I ^ n` of the limit if and only if all
its projections to the terms `F_m`, for `m ≥ n`, factor through `I ^ n F_m`. This is the
canonical limit description of the ideal-power submodule.
declarations.statement:
public theorem idealPowerMultiple_limit (hI : Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsFiniteType S.I) (n : ℕ)
    (T : S.X.Modules) (f : T ⟶ S.limitModule) :
    (∃ g : T ⟶ (idealPowerMultiple S.I n S.limitModule).toSheafOfModules,
      g ≫ (idealPowerMultiple S.I n S.limitModule).ι = f) ↔
    (∀ m : ℕ, n ≤ m + 1 →
      ∃ g : T ⟶ (idealPowerMultiple S.I n (S.system.obj (op m))).toSheafOfModules,
        g ≫ (idealPowerMultiple S.I n (S.system.obj (op m))).ι =
          f ≫ limit.π S.system (op m))
declarations.comment: ideal_powers

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.AdicInverseSystem.surjective_limitComparison_moduleCohomologyFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The Milnor surjection of an adic inverse system, in module-valued cohomology.** For an
adic inverse system `(Fₙ)` of quasi-coherent modules on a scheme `X`, with inverse limit
`F = lim Fₙ`, the canonical comparison map

`H^p(X, F) ⟶ lim_n H^p(X, Fₙ)`

is surjective. Here `H^p(X, -)` is `moduleCohomologyFunctor X p`, the `p`-th right derived
functor of global sections taken in `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`-modules, and the comparison map is
`limitComparison`.
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the comparison onto the limit, module-valued cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.AdicInverseSystem.exists_idealPowerQuotientIso
declarations.doc:
Reduction of the limit of an adic inverse system modulo `I^{n+1}` recovers its `n`-th
(zero-indexed) term, compatibly with the canonical limit projection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_idealPowerQuotientIso
    (hI : Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsFiniteType S.I) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ e : idealPowerQuotient S.I (n + 1) S.limitModule ≅ S.system.obj (op n),
      cokernel.π ((idealPowerMultiple S.I (n + 1) S.limitModule).ι) ≫ e.hom =
        limit.π S.system (op n)
declarations.comment: reduction

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.exists_pow_linearMaps_sum_eq_self
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EIA.** Let `I = (f_1, …, f_r)` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring `A`
with `cd(A, I) = 1`. Then there are `c ≥ 1` and `A`-linear maps `φ_j : I^c → A` such that
`∑ f_j φ_j : I^c → I` is the inclusion map.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_linearMaps_sum_eq_self
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A)
    (hf : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (hcd : cohomologicalDimension A I (IsNoetherian.noetherian I) = 1) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, 1 ≤ c ∧
      ∃ φ : Fin r → (I ^ c : Ideal A) →ₗ[A] A,
        ∀ x : (I ^ c : Ideal A), (∑ j, f j * φ j x) = (x : A)

declarations.name: Stacks.ReesAlgebra.extendLinearMaps
declarations.doc:
The graded `A`-algebra map `reesAlgebra J →ₐ[A] A[Xᵢ]` extending a finite family `φ` of
`A`-linear maps `J →ₗ[A] A`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def extendLinearMaps (J : Ideal A) (φ : Fin r → J →ₗ[A] A) :
    reesAlgebra J →ₐ[A] MvPolynomial (Fin r) A
declarations.comment: the extended graded algebra map

declarations.name: Stacks.ReesAlgebra.extendLinearMaps_degreeOne
declarations.doc: The extension sends an element of `J` in degree one to the linear form `∑ⱼ φ j x · Xⱼ`.
declarations.comment: the degree-one formula

declarations.name: Stacks.ReesAlgebra.extendLinearMaps_homogeneous
declarations.doc:
The extension sends an element of the Rees algebra supported in degree `n` to a homogeneous
polynomial of total degree `n`.
declarations.comment: preservation of grading

declarations.name: Stacks.ReesAlgebra.extendLinearMaps_unique
declarations.doc:
An algebra map out of the Rees algebra with the prescribed degree-one component is the
extension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem extendLinearMaps_unique (J : Ideal A) (φ : Fin r → J →ₗ[A] A)
    (Ψ : reesAlgebra J →ₐ[A] MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)
    (hΨ : ∀ x : J, Ψ (degreeOne J x) = ∑ j, MvPolynomial.C (φ j x) * MvPolynomial.X j) :
    Ψ = extendLinearMaps J φ
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: Stacks.ReesAlgebra.aeval_extendLinearMaps_eq
declarations.doc:
If the maps `φ` split the inclusion of `I ^ c` into `A` against the generators `f` of `I`,
then evaluating the extension at the `f j` in degree one is the inclusion
`reesAlgebra (I ^ c) ⊆ A[X]`.

Both sides are algebra maps out of `reesAlgebra (I ^ c)`, so by `reesAlgebra_hom_ext` it is
enough to compare them in degree one, where the comparison is exactly the splitting identity.
declarations.statement:
public theorem aeval_extendLinearMaps_eq (I : Ideal A) (c : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A)
    (hf : ∀ j, f j ∈ I) (φ : Fin r → (I ^ c : Ideal A) →ₗ[A] A)
    (hφ : ∀ x : (I ^ c : Ideal A), (∑ j, f j * φ j x) = (x : A))
    (p : reesAlgebra (I ^ c)) :
    ((MvPolynomial.aeval (fun j ↦ degreeOne I ⟨f j, hf j⟩)
        (extendLinearMaps (I ^ c) φ p) : reesAlgebra I) : Polynomial A) =
      (p : Polynomial A)
declarations.comment: the composite is the inclusion

declarations.name: Stacks.ReesAlgebra.exists_unique_extendLinearMaps_module
declarations.doc: The degreewise graded map extending the maps on a power of `I`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_unique_extendLinearMaps_module
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (N : Type w)
    [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N] [Module.Finite B N]
    (I : Ideal A) {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A)
    (hf : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (c : ℕ) (_hc : 1 ≤ c)
    (φ : Fin r → (I ^ c : Ideal A) →ₗ[A] A)
    (hφ : ∀ g : (I ^ c : Ideal A), (∑ j, f j * φ j g) = (g : A)) :
    ∃ c' : ℕ, ∃ hc' : c ≤ c',
      ∃ φ' : Fin r → (I ^ c' : Ideal A) →ₗ[A] A,
        (∀ j (g : A) (hg : g ∈ I ^ c'),
          φ' j ⟨g, hg⟩ = φ j ⟨g, Ideal.pow_le_pow_right hc' hg⟩) ∧
        (∀ g : (I ^ c' : Ideal A), (∑ j, f j * φ' j g) = (g : A)) ∧
        ∃! Ψ : ∀ n : ℕ, reesModulePiece (B := B) (N := N) I c' n →ₗ[B] moduleMvPolynomial r N,
          (∀ n (y : reesModulePiece (B := B) (N := N) I c' n) (m : Fin r →₀ ℕ),
            (m.sum fun _ e => e) ≠ n → (Ψ n y) m = 0) ∧
          (∀ n (p : reesAlgebra (I ^ c'))
              (_hp : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≠ n → (p : Polynomial A).coeff k = 0)
              (x : N)
              (hx : (algebraMap A B ((p : Polynomial A).coeff n)) • x ∈
                reesModulePiece (B := B) (N := N) I c' n)
              (m : Fin r →₀ ℕ),
            (Ψ n ⟨(algebraMap A B ((p : Polynomial A).coeff n)) • x, hx⟩) m =
              (algebraMap A B
                ((Stacks.ReesAlgebra.extendLinearMaps (I ^ c') φ' p).coeff m)) • x) ∧
          (∀ n (y : reesModulePiece (B := B) (N := N) I c' n),
            ∑ m ∈ (Ψ n y).support,
              (∏ j, (algebraMap A B (f j)) ^ m j) • (Ψ n y) m = (y : N))

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.depth_localized_gt_of_no_intermediate_prime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EID.** In the bootstrap situation the depth at `p` exceeds `s` when
no prime of `V(I) \ T` lies between `p` and a prime `q` of `T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_localized_gt_of_no_intermediate_prime
    (S : BootstrapSituation.{u, v, w})
    (p q : PrimeSpectrum S.A)
    (hpq : p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal)
    (hp : p ∉ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (S.I : Set S.A))
    (hq : q ∈ S.T)
    (h : ¬ ∃ r : PrimeSpectrum S.A,
      p.asIdeal ≤ r.asIdeal ∧ r.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal ∧
      r ∈ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (S.I : Set S.A) ∧ r ∉ S.T) :
    enatToEInt
      (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
        (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
        (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl S.M)) > (S.s : EInt)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.Bootstrap.essentiallyConstant_and_consequences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EIE.** In Situation 0EFU, for `i ≤ s` the inverse system
`{H^i_T(M/IⁿM)}_{n ≥ 0}` is essentially constant with value `H^i_T(M)` (with respect to the cone
of the maps `H^i_T(M) → H^i_T(M/IⁿM)` induced by the quotient maps). In particular it is
Mittag-Leffler, `H^i_T(M)` is annihilated by a power of `I`, and the canonical maps exhibit
`H^i_T(M)` as `lim H^i_T(M/IⁿM)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essentiallyConstant_and_consequences (S : BootstrapSituation.{u, u, w}) (i : ℤ)
    (hi : i ≤ S.s) :
    (∃ (j : ℕᵒᵖ) (σ : (tower.{u, u} S i).obj j ⟶ (cone.{u, u} S i).pt),
        EssentiallyConstantPro.IsEssentiallyConstantWith (tower.{u, u} S i) (cone.{u, u} S i)
          j σ) ∧
      IsMittagLefflerCategorical (tower.{u, u} S i) ∧
      (∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a ∈ S.I ^ n,
        ∀ x : (localCohomologyWithSupportInModuleFunctor.{u, u} S.A S.T i).obj
          (ModuleCat.of S.A S.M), a • x = 0) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit (cone.{u, u} S i))

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.isEssentiallyConstantWith_localCohomologyAdicCone_of_neg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EIE** in negative degrees, with no hypothesis.
For `i < 0` the system `{H^i_T(M/IⁿM)}` is essentially constant with value `H^i_T(M)`: local
cohomology with support in `T` of a module vanishes in negative degrees
(`Stacks.LocalCohomology.isZero_localCohomologyWithSupportIn_single_of_neg`), so every term of
the system and the value are zero and the zero morphism is a witness. The three consequences in
this range follow by composing with the implications above.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyConstantWith_localCohomologyAdicCone_of_neg (I : Ideal A) (i : ℤ)
    (hi : i < 0) (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) :
    EssentiallyConstantPro.IsEssentiallyConstantWith
      (localCohomologyAdicTower.{u, v} A T I i M) (localCohomologyAdicCone.{u, v} A T I i M)
      (op 0) 0
declarations.comment:
the negative-degree range, unconditionally: for i < 0 the system is essentially
constant with value H^i_T(M) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.exists_isEssentiallyConstantWith_localCohomologyAdicCone_of_pow_smul_top_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EIE** when `I` acts nilpotently on `M`, with no hypothesis and in
every degree. If `IᴺM = 0` then the quotient maps `M → M/IᵐM` are isomorphisms for every
`m ≥ N`, hence so are their images under `H^i_T`, and a cone whose projections are invertible
from an index on carries essential-constancy data
(`CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantPro.exists_isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_isIso_π`). The three
consequences in this range follow by composing with the implications above.

No Noetherian, finiteness or support hypothesis is used: `A` is an arbitrary commutative ring,
`T` an arbitrary subset of its spectrum and `M` an arbitrary module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEssentiallyConstantWith_localCohomologyAdicCone_of_pow_smul_top_eq_bot
    (I : Ideal A) (i : ℤ) (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) {N : ℕ}
    (hN : I ^ N • (⊤ : Submodule A M) = ⊥) :
    ∃ (j : ℕᵒᵖ) (σ : (localCohomologyAdicTower.{u, v} A T I i M).obj j ⟶
        (localCohomologyAdicCone.{u, v} A T I i M).pt),
      EssentiallyConstantPro.IsEssentiallyConstantWith
        (localCohomologyAdicTower.{u, v} A T I i M) (localCohomologyAdicCone.{u, v} A T I i M)
        j σ
declarations.comment:
the range where I acts nilpotently on M: if I^N M = 0 then in every degree the
system is essentially constant with value H^i_T(M), for an arbitrary ring, subset of the
spectrum and module

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.Bootstrap.isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_depthBound_neg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EIE** for a bootstrap situation whose depth bound is negative. Every
degree `i ≤ s < 0` is negative, so each term of `{H^i_T(M/IⁿM)}` and the value `H^i_T(M)`
vanish and the zero morphism witnesses essential constancy with value `H^i_T(M)`. The four
consequences above apply to this witness, and so hold with no hypothesis in this range.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_depthBound_neg (hs : S.s < 0) (hi : i ≤ S.s) :
    EssentiallyConstantPro.IsEssentiallyConstantWith
      (tower.{u, v} S i) (cone.{u, v} S i) (op 0) 0
declarations.comment:
the essential-constancy assertion, and with it the four consequences, for a
bootstrap situation whose depth bound s is negative

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.Bootstrap.exists_isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_pow_smul_top_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EIE** for a bootstrap situation in which `I` acts nilpotently on `M`,
with no hypothesis and in every degree. The quotient maps `M → M/IᵐM` are isomorphisms from the
nilpotency exponent on, so the canonical cone's projections are, and a cone whose projections
are invertible from an index on carries essential-constancy data.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEssentiallyConstantWith_of_pow_smul_top_eq_bot {N : ℕ}
    (hN : S.I ^ N • (⊤ : Submodule S.A S.M) = ⊥) :
    ∃ (j : ℕᵒᵖ) (σ : (tower.{u, v} S i).obj j ⟶ (cone.{u, v} S i).pt),
      EssentiallyConstantPro.IsEssentiallyConstantWith
        (tower.{u, v} S i) (cone.{u, v} S i) j σ
declarations.comment:
the essential-constancy assertion for a bootstrap situation in which I acts
nilpotently on M, with no hypothesis and in every degree

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.Bootstrap.isMittagLeffler_of_pow_smul_top_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EIE**, the Mittag-Leffler consequence for a bootstrap situation in
which `I` acts nilpotently on `M`, with no hypothesis and in every degree.
declarations.comment:
the Mittag-Leffler consequence for a bootstrap situation in which I acts
nilpotently on M, with no hypothesis and in every degree

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.Bootstrap.exists_pow_smul_eq_zero_of_pow_smul_top_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EIE**, the annihilation consequence for a bootstrap situation in which
`I` acts nilpotently on `M`, with no hypothesis and in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_smul_eq_zero_of_pow_smul_top_eq_bot {N : ℕ}
    (hN : S.I ^ N • (⊤ : Submodule S.A S.M) = ⊥) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a ∈ S.I ^ n,
      ∀ x : (localCohomologyWithSupportInModuleFunctor.{u, v} S.A S.T i).obj
        (ModuleCat.of S.A S.M), a • x = 0
declarations.comment:
the annihilation consequence for a bootstrap situation in which I acts nilpotently
on M, with no hypothesis and in every degree

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.Bootstrap.isLimit_of_pow_smul_top_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EIE**, the limit consequence for a bootstrap situation in which `I`
acts nilpotently on `M`, with no hypothesis and in every degree: the quotient maps exhibit
`H^i_T(M)` as `lim H^i_T(M/IⁿM)`.
declarations.comment:
the limit consequence H^i_T(M) = lim H^i_T(M/I^nM) for a bootstrap situation in
which I acts nilpotently on M, with no hypothesis and in every degree

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.Bootstrap.isMittagLeffler_of_eq_closedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EIE**, the Mittag-Leffler consequence for a bootstrap situation whose
ring is local and whose locus is the closed point, with no hypothesis. The terms
`H^i_T(M/IⁿM)` are then local cohomology at the maximal ideal of finite modules over a
Noetherian local ring, hence Artinian, and an inverse system of Artinian modules is
Mittag-Leffler. No degree restriction is needed either.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLeffler_of_eq_closedPoint [IsLocalRing S.A]
    (hT : S.T = {IsLocalRing.closedPoint S.A}) :
    IsMittagLefflerCategorical (tower.{u, u} S i)
declarations.comment:
the Mittag-Leffler consequence for a bootstrap situation whose ring is local and
whose locus T is the closed point, with no hypothesis and in every degree

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonMap_of_formalSectionsHypotheses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EIF.** Let `I ⊆ 𝔞` be ideals of a Noetherian ring `A` and let `F` be a coherent
module on `U = Spec(A) ∖ V(𝔞)`. Assume that `A` is `I`-adically complete and has a dualizing
complex; that every associated point `x` of `F` outside `V(I)` whose closure meets `V(I)`
outside `V(𝔞)` has `dim(𝒪_{closure {x}, z}) > cd(A, I) + 1` at every `z ∈ closure {x} ∩ V(𝔞)`;
and that either `F|_{U ∖ V(I)}` satisfies `(S₁)` or the values on `V(𝔞)` of a dimension function
on `Spec(A)` differ by at most `2` (`Stacks.Algebraization.FormalSectionsHypotheses`). Then the
map `colim_V H⁰(V, F) ⟶ lim_n H⁰(U, F/IⁿF)`, the colimit over the opens `V ⊆ U` containing
`U ∩ V(I)`, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_comparisonMap_of_formalSectionsHypotheses {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (I a : Ideal A) (hIa : I ≤ a)
    (F : (complementZeroLocus A a : Scheme).Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (h : FormalSectionsHypotheses A I a F) :
    IsIso (comparisonMap A I a F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonMap_iff_realized
declarations.doc:
The comparison map is an isomorphism exactly when every compatible family of sections of
`F / Iⁿ F` on `U` is the comparison of a section of `F` over a single open `V ⊆ U` containing
`U ∩ V(I)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_comparisonMap_iff_realized [IsNoetherianRing A] [F.IsCoherent] :
    IsIso (comparisonMap A I a F) ↔
      ∀ s : ToType (limit (formalSections A I a F)),
        ∃ (V : OpensNearVanishing A I a) (t : ToType ((sectionsNearVanishing A I a F).obj V)),
          ConcreteCategory.hom (comparisonAt A I a F V) t = s
declarations.comment: REDUCED, not proved: the conclusion holds exactly when every formal section is realized on one neighbourhood. Injectivity is proved outright here; the realization half is NOT proved and NOT assumed — it is the right-hand side of this equivalence. See the coverage note

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.FormalSectionsII.globalToFormalSections_proj
declarations.doc:
**The arrow of Stacks 0EIG is canonical**: its `n`-th component is reduction modulo `Iⁿ` of
a global section of `F` on `U`, not an arbitrary arrow into the limit.
declarations.statement:
theorem globalToFormalSections_proj (n : ℕ) :
    globalToFormalSections A I a F ≫ limit.π (formalSections A I a F) (op n) =
      (adicProj (idealSheafNearVanishing A I a) F (op n)).app ⊤
declarations.comment: canonicality of the displayed arrow: its n-th component is reduction mod I^n

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.FormalSectionsII.isIso_globalToFormalSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EIG.** Let `I ⊆ 𝔞` be ideals of a Noetherian ring `A` and let `F` be a coherent
module on `U = Spec(A) ∖ V(𝔞)`. Assume

1. `A` is `I`-adically complete and has a dualizing complex,
2. whenever `x` is an associated point of `F` outside `V(I)` whose closure meets `V(I)` outside
   `V(𝔞)`, every `z ∈ closure {x} ∩ V(𝔞)` has `dim(𝒪_{closure {x}, z}) > cd(A, I) + 1`, and
3. `depth(F_x) ≥ 2` for every `x ∈ U` whose closure meets `V(I)` only inside `V(𝔞)`.

Then `H⁰(U, F) ⟶ lim H⁰(U, F / Iⁿ F)` is an isomorphism.

What is proved here is the content of Stacks 0EIG over Stacks 0EG2: a point of `U` missed by a
neighbourhood `V` of the formal locus has its closure meeting `V(I)` only inside `V(𝔞)`, so
condition (3) bounds the depth of `F` below by `2` on all of `U ∖ V`, Hartogs extension for
coherent modules — Stacks 0E9I — makes every restriction `Γ(U, F) ⟶ Γ(V, F)` an isomorphism,
and the colimit therefore collapses onto its value at `U`.

Conditions (1) and (2) are consumed only by `Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonMap`, the
library's Stacks 0EG2, which is *applied* here: they assemble into its
`Stacks.Algebraization.BootstrapHypotheses` on the nose. The three remaining arguments are that
statement's own carried hypotheses, passed through unchanged and granting nothing about
Stacks 0EIG:

* `Stacks.Algebraization.SerreOneAlternativeComparison` grants Stacks 0EIF — the comparison map
  is an isomorphism for a coherent module that additionally satisfies the third condition of
  that lemma, the condition Stacks 0EG2 removes;
* `Stacks.Algebraization.MiddleComparisonOfShortExact` grants the middle clause of
  Stacks 0H48 — the middle comparison of a short exact sequence is an isomorphism once the
  outer two are;
* `Stacks.Algebraization.AssociatedPointSplitting` grants the short exact sequence the source
  assembles from Stacks 0BK0, 0DX3 and 0AW0, in which no comparison map occurs at all.

None of the three mentions the global sections `Γ(U, F)`, so none of them is this conclusion;
and since they are exactly the hypotheses the library's Stacks 0EG2 already carries, this
statement adds no assumption of its own beyond conditions (1), (2) and (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_globalToFormalSections [IsNoetherianRing A] [F.IsCoherent]
    (hIa : I ≤ a) (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete I A)
    (hdualizing : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hdim : AssociatedPointsClosureDimensionBound A I a F)
    (hdepth : DepthTwoOffFormalLocus A I a F)
    (hEIF : SerreOneAlternativeComparison.{u}) (h48 : MiddleComparisonOfShortExact.{u})
    (hsplit : AssociatedPointSplitting A I a) :
    IsIso (globalToFormalSections A I a F)
declarations.comment: H^0(U,F) = lim H^0(U,F/I^nF); 0EG2 applied, its 3 hypotheses passed through

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.FormalSectionsII.isIso_globalToFormalSections_of_depthTwoOffFormalLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EIG.** Let `I ⊆ 𝔞` be ideals of a Noetherian ring `A` and let `F` be a coherent
module on `U = Spec(A) ∖ V(𝔞)`. Assume

1. `A` is `I`-adically complete and has a dualizing complex,
2. whenever `x` is an associated point of `F` outside `V(I)` whose closure meets `V(I)` outside
   `V(𝔞)`, every `z ∈ closure {x} ∩ V(𝔞)` has `dim(𝒪_{closure {x}, z}) > cd(A, I) + 1`, and
3. `depth(F_x) ≥ 2` for every `x ∈ U` whose closure meets `V(I)` only inside `V(𝔞)`.

Then the arrow `H⁰(U, F) ⟶ lim H⁰(U, F / Iⁿ F)`, whose `n`-th component is reduction
modulo `Iⁿ`, is an isomorphism.

Conditions (1) and (2) make the comparison map of Stacks 0EG2 an isomorphism; condition (3) and
Stacks 0E9I identify `H⁰(V, F)` with `H⁰(U, F)` for every open `V ⊆ U` containing `U ∩ V(I)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_globalToFormalSections_of_depthTwoOffFormalLocus
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I a : Ideal A)
    (F : (complementZeroLocus A a : Scheme).Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hIa : I ≤ a) (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete I A)
    (hdualizing : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hdim : AssociatedPointsClosureDimensionBound A I a F)
    (hdepth : DepthTwoOffFormalLocus A I a F) :
    IsIso (globalToFormalSections A I a F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.mono_principalComparisonMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EIH, the injectivity half.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, let `f ∈ A`, let
`𝔞 ⊆ A` be an ideal and let `M` be a finite `A`-module. Then the map

`colim_V Γ(V, M̃) ⟶ lim Γ(U, (M/fⁿM)~)`

of the source, the colimit being over the opens `V ⊆ U = Spec(A) ∖ V(𝔞)` containing
`U ∩ V(f)`, is a monomorphism.

None of the three hypotheses of the source is needed for this half: `A` is not assumed
`f`-adically complete, `f` is not assumed a nonzerodivisor on `M`, `H¹_𝔞(M/fM)` is not assumed
finite, and `f` is not assumed to lie in `𝔞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_principalComparisonMap (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A)
    (a : Ideal A) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) [Module.Finite A M] :
    Mono (principalComparisonMap A f a M)
declarations.comment: injectivity

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.FormalSections.isIso_formalComparison
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, let `f ∈ 𝔞 ⊆ A` be an element of an ideal of `A`, and let `M`
be a finite `A`-module. Assume

1. `A` is `f`-adically complete,
2. `f` is a nonzerodivisor on `M`,
3. `H¹_𝔞(M/fM)` is a finite `A`-module.

Then, with `U = Spec(A) ∖ V(𝔞)`, the canonical map

`colim_V Γ(V, M̃) ⟶ lim_n Γ(U, (M/fⁿM)~)`

is an isomorphism, the colimit being over the opens `V ⊆ U` containing `U ∩ V(f)`.

The map is `Stacks.Algebraization.FormalSections.formalComparison`: on a neighbourhood `V` of
the formal locus it reduces a section of `M̃` modulo `fⁿ` and extends the result back to `U`,
which is legitimate because `(M/fⁿM)~` vanishes on `D(f) ⊇ U ∖ V`. The quotient `M/fM` is
written `Stacks.Algebraization.FormalSections.Quot f M 1`, which is `M` modulo the submodule
`fM`; see `Stacks.Algebraization.FormalSections.powSmul_one`.

The membership `f ∈ 𝔞` is carried but not consumed: the proof below uses only the other three
hypotheses, so the conclusion holds for every `f` and every ideal `𝔞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_formalComparison (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A)
    (a : Ideal A) (hfa : f ∈ a) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) [Module.Finite A (M : Type u)]
    [IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) A] (hf : IsSMulRegular (M : Type u) f)
    (hH1 : Module.Finite A
      (localCohomologyModule A a (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing a) (Quot f M 1) 1)) :
    IsIso (ModuleCat.ofHom (formalComparison A a f M))

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.completionFunctor
declarations.doc:
Completion of a coherent sheaf along a quasi-coherent ideal, as a coherent adic inverse
system.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def completionFunctor (X : Scheme.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf ⥤
      Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems I
declarations.comment: the same completion functor on an open subscheme, at the restricted ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isRestrictionOfCompletion_of_extendsToX
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0EIL, condition (6) implies condition (5) when `A` is `I`-adically complete.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRestrictionOfCompletion_of_extendsToX (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u})
    [IsAdicComplete S.I S.A]
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (S.Yι.ker.comap S.U.ι))
    (h : ExtendsToX S F) : IsRestrictionOfCompletion S F
declarations.comment: extendable implies restriction of a completion

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isCompletion_iff_nearClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EIL, conditions (2) and (3) are equivalent.** A coherent adic system on `U` is the
completion of a coherent module on `U` exactly when it is the completion of a coherent module on
some open neighbourhood of `U ∩ Y` in `U`.

One direction takes the neighbourhood to be `U` itself. For the other, a coherent module on the
neighbourhood `V` extends to `U`, and the two systems — the completion of the extension and the
given one — are then isomorphic over `V`; every term of either is annihilated by a power of the
ideal and so is supported inside `V`, and restriction to `V` is fully faithful on modules
supported there, so the isomorphism over `V` comes from an isomorphism over `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCompletion_iff_nearClosed (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u})
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (S.Yι.ker.comap S.U.ι)) :
    (completionFunctor S.U.toScheme (S.Yι.ker.comap S.U.ι)).essImage F ↔
      IsCompletionNearClosed S F
declarations.comment: completion iff near the closed subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isCompletion_iff_ofRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EIL, conditions (2) and (4) are equivalent.** A coherent adic system on `U` is the
completion of a coherent module on `U` exactly when it is the completion of one that extends to a
coherent module on `X`.

`X` is affine and Noetherian, so every coherent module on the open `U` is the restriction of a
coherent module on `X`; the converse direction forgets the extension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCompletion_iff_ofRestriction (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u})
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (S.Yι.ker.comap S.U.ι)) :
    (completionFunctor S.U.toScheme (S.Yι.ker.comap S.U.ι)).essImage F ↔
      IsCompletionOfRestriction S F
declarations.comment: completion iff completion of a restriction

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isCompletionOfRestriction_iff_isRestrictionOfCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EIL, conditions (4) and (5) are equivalent.** Being the completion of a module
restricted from `X` is the same as being the restriction of a completion on `X`, because
completion commutes with restriction to an open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCompletionOfRestriction_iff_isRestrictionOfCompletion
    (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u})
