declarations.comment: in particular, for I-adically complete A, (ℱₙ) is the completion of a coherent 𝒪_U-module

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.extendsToX_of_blowUp_fiber_dim_lt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJK.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0EHC] let `(ℱₙ)` be an object of
`Coh(U, I𝒪_U)`. Assume

1. `A` has a dualizing complex,
2. all fibres of the blowing up `b : X' → X` of `I` have dimension `≤ d - 1`, and
3. one of the following is true:
   (a) `(ℱₙ)` satisfies the `(d + 1, d + 2)`-inequalities ([Stacks, Tag 0EJ3]), or
   (b) for `y ∈ U ∩ Y` and a prime `𝔭 ⊆ 𝒪^∧_{X,y}` with `𝔭 ∉ V(I𝒪^∧_{X,y})` we have
   `depth((ℱ^∧_y)_𝔭) + dim(𝒪^∧_{X,y}/𝔭) + δ^Y_Z(y) > d + 2`.

Then `(ℱₙ)` extends to `X`.

Here `d` is an integer and the fibre condition `dim ≤ d - 1` is written `dim < d` for the natural
number `d.toNat`, which is the same condition (for `d ≤ 0` both say every fibre is empty). The
dualizing complex lives in the derived category `HasDerivedCategory.standard`, as in
[Stacks, Tag 0EJJ].
declarations.statement:
theorem extendsToX_of_blowUp_fiber_dim_lt (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen S))
    (d : ℤ)
    (hdual : ∃ K : @DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A) _ _
      (HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} S.A)),
      @Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex S.A _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} S.A)) K)
    (hfib : ∀ y : Spec (CommRingCat.of S.A), topologicalKrullDim ((AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase
      (Stacks.LocalCohomology.specIdealSheaf S.A S.I)).fiber y) < ((d.toNat : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (h3 : SatisfiesDepthInequalities S F (d + 1) (d + 2) ∨
      ∀ (y : S.U.toScheme) (z : S.Y), S.U.ι.base y = S.Yι.base z →
        ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (completedLocalRing (idealOnOpen S) y),
          ¬ completedLocalIdeal (idealOnOpen S) y ≤ p.asIdeal →
          depthAddDimAddDistance S F y z p > ((d + 2 : ℤ) : EInt)) :
    ExtendsToX S (toKerSystem S F)
declarations.comment: the whole statement: under (1) a dualizing complex, (2) fibres of the blowup of I of dimension ≤ d - 1, (3) the (d + 1, d + 2)-inequalities or the bound depth + dim + δ > d + 2, the object (ℱₙ) of Coh(U, I𝒪_U) extends to X

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.algebraization_of_zeroLocus_eq_range_of_depthBound
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJN (Algebraization for ideals with few generators).** In Situation
0EHC let `(ℱₙ)` be an object of `Coh(U, I𝒪_U)`. Assume (1) `A` has a dualizing complex, (2)
`V(I) = V(f₁, …, f_d)` for some `d ≥ 1`, and (3) `(ℱₙ)` satisfies the `(d + 1, d + 2)`-inequalities
or `depth((ℱ_y^∧)_𝔭) + dim(𝒪_{X,y}^∧/𝔭) + δ^Y_Z(y) > d + 2` at every `y ∈ U ∩ Y` and every prime
`𝔭 ∉ V(I𝒪_{X,y}^∧)`. Then `(ℱₙ)` extends to `X`, and if `A` is `I`-adically complete then `(ℱₙ)`
is the completion of a coherent `𝒪_U`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem algebraization_of_zeroLocus_eq_range_of_depthBound
    (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} S.A)]
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen S))
    (hdual : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (f : Fin d → S.A)
    (hV : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (S.I : Set S.A) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (Set.range f))
    (h3 : SatisfiesDepthInequalities S F (d + 1) (d + 2) ∨
      ∀ (y : S.U.toScheme) (z : S.Y), S.U.ι.base y = S.Yι.base z →
        ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (completedLocalRing (idealOnOpen S) y),
          ¬ completedLocalIdeal (idealOnOpen S) y ≤ p.asIdeal →
          depthAddDimAddDistance S F y z p > ((d + 2 : ℤ) : EInt)) :
    ExtendsToX S (toKerSystem S F) ∧
      (IsAdicComplete S.I S.A →
        (completionFunctor S.U.toScheme (S.Yι.ker.comap S.U.ι)).essImage (toKerSystem S F))
declarations.comment: the whole statement: (F_n) extends to X, and over an I-adically complete A it is the completion of a coherent O_U-module

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.extendsToX_and_essImage_of_isCohenMacaulay_of_span_eq_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJP.** In Situation 0EHC let `(ℱₙ)` be an object of `Coh(U, I𝒪_U)`.
Assume

1. `A` is a local ring which has a dualizing complex,
2. all irreducible components of `X` have the same dimension,
3. the scheme `X \ Y` is Cohen–Macaulay,
4. `I` is generated by `d` elements,
5. `dim(X) - dim(Z) > d + 2`, and
6. for `y ∈ U ∩ Y` the module `ℱ_y^∧` is finite locally free outside `V(I𝒪_{X,y}^∧)` (for
   example if `ℱₙ` is a finite locally free `𝒪_U/Iⁿ𝒪_U`-module, see
   `free_localizedModule_completedStalk_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeAdic`).

Then `(ℱₙ)` extends to `X`. In particular if `A` is `I`-adically complete, then `(ℱₙ)` is the
completion of a coherent `𝒪_U`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem extendsToX_and_essImage_of_isCohenMacaulay_of_span_eq_range
    (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} S.A)]
    [IsLocalRing S.A] (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen S))
    (hdual : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hequi : Equidimensional (PrimeSpectrum S.A))
    (hCM : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S.A, ¬ S.I ≤ q.asIdeal →
      IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))
    (d : ℕ) (f : Fin d → S.A) (hI : S.I = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (S.A ⧸ S.a) + ((d + 2 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) < ringKrullDim S.A)
    (hfree : ∀ (y : S.U.toScheme) (z : S.Y), S.U.ι.base y = S.Yι.base z →
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (completedLocalRing (idealOnOpen S) y),
        ¬ completedLocalIdeal (idealOnOpen S) y ≤ p.asIdeal →
        Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
          (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl (completedStalk (idealOnOpen S) F y))) :
    ExtendsToX S (toKerSystem S F) ∧
      (IsAdicComplete S.I S.A →
        (completionFunctor S.U.toScheme (S.Yι.ker.comap S.U.ι)).essImage (toKerSystem S F))
declarations.comment: the whole statement: under hypotheses (1)-(6) the system extends to X, and over an I-adically complete A it is the completion of a coherent O_U-module; the example in (6) is free_localizedModule_completedStalk_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeAdic

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.finite_globalSections_of_finite_idealPowerSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJS (the induction of the proof).** If `H⁰(U, F_1)` is a finite
`A`-module and every `H⁰(U, I^(n+1) F_(n+1))` is a finite `A`-module, then `H⁰(U, F_n)` is a
finite `A`-module for every `n`.

This is the step "using the assumption of finiteness of `H⁰(U, F_1)` and induction, we first
conclude that `M_n = H⁰(U, F_n)` is a finite `A`-module for all `n`" of the source. The source
gets finiteness of `H⁰(U, I^(n+1) F_(n+1))` from the stalkwise direct-sum decomposition of
`I^(n+1) F_(n+1)` into copies of `F_1`, which is not available in this library; here it is a
hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_globalSections_of_finite_idealPowerSections
    (h0 : Module.Finite S.A ((globalSectionsSystem S F).obj (op 0)))
    (hker : ∀ n, Module.Finite S.A (idealPowerSections S F n)) :
    ∀ n, Module.Finite S.A ((globalSectionsSystem S F).obj (op n))
declarations.comment: the induction giving finiteness of every H⁰(U, Fₙ), with the direct-sum decomposition of Iⁿ F₍ₙ₊₁₎ replaced by the hypothesis that its sections are finite

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_of_finite_globalSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJS (condition (c) of Tag 0EHH).** Finiteness of every `H⁰(U, F_n)`
implies the finite-image condition (c) of the Mittag-Leffler criterion Stacks 0EHH, so together
with the Mittag-Leffler condition (a) and the topology condition (b) it gives canonical
extension.

The source derives (a) and (b) from Cohomology 0GYK and 0GYM applied to the graded module
`⨁_n H^p(U, IⁿF_(n+1))`; here they are hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicallyExtends_of_finite_globalSections
    (hML : IsMittagLefflerCategorical (globalSectionsSystem S F))
    (htop : (⨅ n : ℕ, TopologicalSpace.induced
      (fun x : limitGlobalSections S F =>
        (limit.π (globalSectionsSystem S F) (op n)).hom x) ⊥) =
        S.I.adicModuleTopology (limitGlobalSections S F))
    (hfin : ∀ n, Module.Finite S.A ((globalSectionsSystem S F).obj (op n))) :
    CanonicallyExtends S F
declarations.comment: the reduction to Tag 0EHH: condition (c) from finiteness of every H⁰(U, Fₙ), with conditions (a) and (b) as hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_of_finite_idealPowerSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJS (the finiteness half).** A coherent adic system on the open
complement extends canonically to `X` as soon as its system of global sections has
Mittag-Leffler, the limit topology on the module of compatible sections is the `I`-adic topology,
`H⁰(U, F_1)` is a finite `A`-module, and every `H⁰(U, I^(n+1) F_(n+1))` is a finite
`A`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicallyExtends_of_finite_idealPowerSections
    (hML : IsMittagLefflerCategorical (globalSectionsSystem S F))
    (htop : (⨅ n : ℕ, TopologicalSpace.induced
      (fun x : limitGlobalSections S F =>
        (limit.π (globalSectionsSystem S F) (op n)).hom x) ⊥) =
        S.I.adicModuleTopology (limitGlobalSections S F))
    (h0 : Module.Finite S.A ((globalSectionsSystem S F).obj (op 0)))
    (hker : ∀ n, Module.Finite S.A (idealPowerSections S F n)) :
    CanonicallyExtends S F
declarations.comment: the finiteness half: conditions (a), (b) of Tag 0EHH and finiteness of the sections of Iⁿ F₍ₙ₊₁₎ are hypotheses instead of consequences of the regular sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.HasRegularSequenceOnCompletedStalks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJS, hypothesis (1).** There are `f₁, …, f_d ∈ I` such that at every
point `y` of `U ∩ Y` the ideal `I 𝒪_{X,y}` is generated by the germs of `f₁, …, f_d` and those
germs form an `F_y^∧`-regular sequence.

The locus `U ∩ Y` is the support of the ideal sheaf `I 𝒪_U`, and `F_y^∧` is
`Stacks.Algebraization.completedStalk`. The sequence is taken as a sequence of elements of the
local ring `𝒪_{X,y}` acting on `F_y^∧`, which is how the source's `f_i ∈ I ⊆ A` act.
declarations.statement: def HasRegularSequenceOnCompletedStalks : Prop
declarations.comment: hypothesis (1), as a predicate; not used by any result in this file

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.HasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJS, hypothesis (2).** `H⁰(U, F_1)` and `H¹(U, F_1)` are finite
`A`-modules.

Degree zero is the global-sections module of the system, and degree one is the first right
derived functor of sections over the base, `Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologyOverBase`.
declarations.statement: def HasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology : Prop
declarations.comment: hypothesis (2), as a predicate; not used by any result in this file

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_of_regularSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJS.** In Situation 0EHC let `(F_n)` be an object of
`Coh(U, I 𝒪_U)`. Assume that

1. there exist `f₁, …, f_d ∈ I` such that for `y ∈ U ∩ Y` the ideal `I 𝒪_{X,y}` is generated by
   `f₁, …, f_d` and `f₁, …, f_d` form an `F_y^∧`-regular sequence
   (`Stacks.Algebraization.HasRegularSequenceOnCompletedStalks`),
2. `H⁰(U, F_1)` and `H¹(U, F_1)` are finite `A`-modules
   (`Stacks.Algebraization.HasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology`).

Then `(F_n)` extends canonically to `X`.

The proof is the source's: the decomposition
`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_isIso_idealPowerDesc_of_regularSequence` of `Iⁿ F_(n+1)` into copies
of `F_1` indexed by the monomials in the `fᵢ`, fed to
`Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_of_idealPowerDesc`, which verifies conditions (a), (b),
(c) of Stacks 0EHH.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicallyExtends_of_regularSequence (hreg : HasRegularSequenceOnCompletedStalks S F)
    (h2 : HasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology S F) : CanonicallyExtends S F
declarations.comment: the system extends canonically to X

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.essImage_completionFunctor_of_regularSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJS, the second sentence.** Under the hypotheses of Stacks 0EJS, if
`A` is moreover `I`-adically complete, then `(F_n)` is the completion of a coherent
`𝒪_U`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_completionFunctor_of_regularSequence [IsAdicComplete S.I S.A]
    (hreg : HasRegularSequenceOnCompletedStalks S F) (h2 : HasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology S F) :
    (completionFunctor S.U.toScheme (idealOnOpen S)).essImage F
declarations.comment: in particular, if A is complete, the system is the completion of a coherent 𝒪_U-module

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.hasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology_iff_hasDepthDimensionAt_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJT (the equivalence).** Assume `A` has a dualizing complex. Then
hypothesis (2) of Stacks 0EJS, that `H⁰(U, F_1)` and `H¹(U, F_1)` are finite `A`-modules, holds
if and only if `depth(F_{1,y}) + dim(𝒪_{closure{y}, z}) > 2` for every `y ∈ U ∩ Y` and every
`z ∈ Z ∩ closure{y}`.

The right-hand side is `Stacks.Algebraization.HasDepthDimensionAt` at `2` for a finite
`A`-module `M` whose associated sheaf restricts to `F_1` on `U`. The equivalence is the
criterion of Stacks 0BJY at `n = 2`, which is proved here as
`Stacks.Algebraization.affineDepthDimensionCriterion`; the dualizing complex discharges its
catenarity assumption by Stacks 0A80 and enters the proof only through that and through
`hformalOfDual`. The two comparison hypotheses are a bridge between two spellings of the same
`A`-module `H^p(U, F_1)` and assume nothing about the situation, and the passage from
`complementCohomologyBase` to coherence of the higher direct images is clause (3) of
Stacks 0BK0 and is proved.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology_iff_hasDepthDimensionAt_two
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen S))
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} (CommRingCat.of S.A)) (hM : Module.Finite S.A M)
    (hdual : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hformalOfDual :
      (∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K) →
        ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S.A,
          Stacks.LocalCohomology.FormalFibersHavePropertySk
            (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) 2)
    (hcompare₀ : Module.Finite S.A ((globalSectionsSystem S F).obj (op 0)) ↔
      Module.Finite S.A (complementCohomologyBase (A := CommRingCat.of S.A) S.a M 0))
    (hcompare₁ : Module.Finite S.A
        (Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologyOverBase.{u, u} S.A S.U.ι (F.obj.obj (op 0)) 1) ↔
      Module.Finite S.A (complementCohomologyBase (A := CommRingCat.of S.A) S.a M 1)) :
    HasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology S F ↔ HasDepthDimensionAt S M 2
declarations.comment: the equivalence; only the formal-fibre step and an H^p(U, F₁) bridge are assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.hasDepthDimensionAt_two_of_pointwiseBounds
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJT (the sufficient condition).** The depth–dimension inequality at
`2` holds when `F_1` is finite locally free on `𝒪_{U ∩ Y}`, `Y` is `(S₂)`, and
`codim(Z', Y') ≥ 3` for every pair of irreducible components `Y'` of `Y` and `Z'` of `Z` with
`Z' ⊆ Y'`.

The two pointwise bounds that the condition yields are hypotheses, for one reason each.
`PointwiseSerreTwoBound` would follow from `(S₂)` for `Y` by way of the depth of a finite
locally free module over a local ring being the depth of that ring, and that statement has no
public form in this library; the other two steps it needs do, namely
`moduleDepth_eq_depth` and `Module.depth_eq_depth_map_algebraMap`.
`PointwiseCodimensionThreeBound` would follow from the codimension clause by additivity of
codimension along a chain, which is available as `catenary_height_add`, but in the direction
required that needs `A` to be catenary, and catenarity is not part of the condition stated by
the source. What is proved here is that those two bounds, together with the positivity of
`dim(𝒪_{closure{y},z})` for `z` strictly above `y`, give the inequality.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasDepthDimensionAt_two_of_pointwiseBounds
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} (CommRingCat.of S.A))
    (N : ModuleCat.{u} (CommRingCat.of (S.A ⧸ S.I)))
    (hcond : HasLocallyFreeCodimensionThreeCondition S N)
    (hserre : PointwiseSerreTwoBound S M N)
    (hcodim : PointwiseCodimensionThreeBound S M N) :
    HasDepthDimensionAt S M 2
declarations.comment: the trailing sufficient condition, via the two pointwise bounds it yields

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.finite_lowDegreeCohomology_iff_depthDimension_of_isDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJT.** In Situation 0EHC, let `(F_n)` be a coherent `I`-adic system on
`U = Spec A ∖ V(𝔞)`, as in Stacks 0EJS, and assume `A` has a dualizing complex.

* `H⁰(U, F₁)` and `H¹(U, F₁)` are finite `A`-modules if and only if
  `depth(F_{1,y}) + dim(𝒪_{closure{y}, z}) > 2` for all `y ∈ U ∩ Y` and `z ∈ Z ∩ closure{y}`.
  The depth is that of the stalk of `F₁` at `y` over `𝒪_{U,y}`; the point `z` is a prime `𝔮` of
  `A` containing `𝔞` and the prime `𝔭` of `y`, and `dim(𝒪_{closure{y}, z})` is the height of the
  image of `𝔮` in `A ⧸ 𝔭`.
* This holds if `F₁` is a finite locally free `𝒪_{U ∩ Y}`-module, that is its pullback along the
  closed immersion `U ∩ Y ⟶ U` is finite locally free, `Y = Spec(A ⧸ I)` is `(S₂)`, and
  `codim(Z', Y') ≥ 3` for every pair of irreducible components `Y'` of `Y` and `Z'` of `Z` with
  `Z' ⊆ Y'`. The components of `Y` and `Z` are the minimal primes of `I` and of `𝔞`, `Z' ⊆ Y'`
  is the inclusion of those primes, and `codim(Z', Y')` is the height of the image of the prime
  of `Z'` in the quotient by the prime of `Y'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_lowDegreeCohomology_iff_depthDimension_of_isDualizingComplex
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen S))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A)) (hK : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K) :
    (HasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology S F ↔
      ∀ y : S.U.toScheme, S.I ≤ (underlyingPrime S y).asIdeal →
        ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S.A, S.a ≤ q.asIdeal → (underlyingPrime S y).asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal →
          (2 : ℕ∞) < Module.depth (S.U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk y)
              (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (S.U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk y))
              ((F.obj.obj (op 0)).presheaf.stalk y) +
            (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (underlyingPrime S y).asIdeal)).height) ∧
      (Scheme.Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (intersectionUYι S)).obj (F.obj.obj (op 0))) →
        PropertySkRing (S.A ⧸ S.I) 2 →
        (∀ p ∈ S.I.minimalPrimes, ∀ q ∈ S.a.minimalPrimes, p ≤ q →
          3 ≤ (q.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p)).height) →
        HasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology S F ∧
          ∀ y : S.U.toScheme, S.I ≤ (underlyingPrime S y).asIdeal →
            ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S.A, S.a ≤ q.asIdeal → (underlyingPrime S y).asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal →
              (2 : ℕ∞) < Module.depth (S.U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk y)
                  (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (S.U.toScheme.presheaf.stalk y))
                  ((F.obj.obj (op 0)).presheaf.stalk y) +
                (q.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (underlyingPrime S y).asIdeal)).height)
declarations.comment: the equivalence and the sufficient condition

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.canonicallyExtends_of_flatLocalBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJU.** In Situation 0EHC let `(F_n)` be a coherent `I`-adic system on
`U`, and let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring with a ring map `R → A` such that `I = 𝔪 A` and
the formal stalks `F_y^∧`, `y ∈ U ∩ Y`, are `R`-flat (both recorded by `B`), and suppose that
`H⁰(U, F_1)` and `H¹(U, F_1)` are finite `A`-modules. Then `(F_n)` extends canonically to `X`.

The proof verifies the three conditions of Stacks 0EHH: (a) is
`Stacks.Algebraization.isMittagLeffler_globalSectionsSystem_of_flatLocalBase`, (b) is
`Stacks.Algebraization.limitTopology_eq_adicModuleTopology_of_flatLocalBase`, and (c) comes from
the finiteness of every `H⁰(U, Iⁿ F_(n+1))`, which the direct-sum decomposition
`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_isoDirectSum_idealPowerSub` gives.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicallyExtends_of_flatLocalBase (B : FlatLocalBase S F)
    (h3 : HasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology S F) : CanonicallyExtends S F

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.essImage_completionFunctor_of_flatLocalBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EJU, the concluding sentence.** Under the hypotheses of Stacks 0EJU, if
`A` is moreover `I`-adically complete, then `(F_n)` is the completion of a coherent
`𝒪_U`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_completionFunctor_of_flatLocalBase [IsAdicComplete S.I S.A]
    (B : FlatLocalBase S F) (h3 : HasFiniteLowDegreeCohomology S F) :
    (completionFunctor S.U.toScheme (idealOnOpen S)).essImage F
declarations.comment: in particular, over an I-adically complete A the system is the completion of a coherent 𝒪_U-module

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isCompletionOfCoherent_of_flat_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EJV, algebraization over a complete local base.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a complete
Noetherian local ring, let `p : X ⟶ Spec R` be proper, let `Z` be a closed subset of the special
fibre `X_1`, let `U = X ∖ Z` with inclusion `j = U.ι`, and let `(F_n)` be an object of
`Coh(U, 𝔪𝒪_U)`. Assume that `F_n` is flat over `R/𝔪ⁿ` for all `n`, and that `j_*F_1` and
`R¹j_*F_1` are coherent. Then `(F_n)` is the completion of a coherent `𝒪_U`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompletionOfCoherent_of_flat_of_isCoherent
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IsProper p]
    (Z : Closeds X) (hZ : Z ≤ (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).support)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : (U : Set X) = (Z : Set X)ᶜ)
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems
      ((baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).comap U.ι))
    (hflat : ∀ n : ℕ, StalksFlatOverQuotient R (baseToStalk R (U.ι ≫ p))
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R ^ (n + 1)) (F.obj.obj (op n)))
    (h0 : ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward U.ι).obj (F.obj.obj (op 0))).IsCoherent)
    (h1 : (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward U.ι).rightDerived 1).obj (F.obj.obj (op 0))).IsCoherent) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian p
    IsCompletionOfCoherent ((baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).comap U.ι) F
declarations.comment: algebraization: a flat object of Coh(U, 𝔪𝒪_U) with j_*F₁ and R¹j_*F₁ coherent is the completion of a coherent 𝒪_U-module

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_specialFibre_directImage_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EJV, the closing paragraph: `j_*F_1` and `R¹j_*F_1` are conditions on the special
fibre.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring, `p : X ⟶ Spec R` proper, `U ⊆ X` open with
inclusion `j`, and `(F_n)` an object of `Coh(U, 𝔪𝒪_U)`. Write `i : X_1 ⟶ X` and `i_U : U_1 ⟶ U`
for the special fibres and `j₁ : U_1 ⟶ X_1` for the special fibre of `j`. Then `F_1` is a coherent
sheaf on `U_1`: there is a coherent `𝒪_{U_1}`-module `G` with `i_{U,*} G ≅ F_1`; and
`j_*F_1 ≅ i_* j₁_* G` and `R¹j_*F_1 ≅ i_* R¹j₁_* G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_specialFibre_directImage_iso
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IsProper p] (U : X.Opens)
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems
      ((baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).comap U.ι)) :
    ∃ G : ((baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).comap U.ι).subscheme.Modules,
      G.IsCoherent ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
        ((baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).comap U.ι).subschemeι).obj G ≅
          F.obj.obj (op 0)) ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward U.ι).obj (F.obj.obj (op 0)) ≅
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
          (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).subschemeι).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
            (specialFibreMap (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p) U)).obj G)) ∧
      Nonempty (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward U.ι).rightDerived 1).obj (F.obj.obj (op 0)) ≅
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
          (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).subschemeι).obj
          (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
            (specialFibreMap (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p) U)).rightDerived
              1).obj G))
declarations.comment: the closing paragraph: F₁ is a coherent sheaf on the special fibre U₁, and j_*F₁ = j₁,*F₁ and R¹j_*F₁ = R¹j₁,*F₁ for the special fibre j₁ : U₁ → X₁ of j

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isCoherent_specialFibre_directImages_of_hasPropertySk_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EJV, the closing paragraph: the `(S₂)` criterion on the special fibre.** Let
`(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring, `p : X ⟶ Spec R` locally of finite type, `Z ⊆ X` closed and
`U = X ∖ Z`. Write `X₁` and `U₁` for the special fibres and `j₁ : U₁ ⟶ X₁` for the special fibre
of the inclusion `U ⊆ X`. If `X₁` is `(S₂)` and irreducible, `dim(X₁) - dim(Z) ≥ 3`, and `G` is a
finite locally free `𝒪_{U₁}`-module, then `j₁,*G` and `R¹j₁,*G` are coherent.

The special fibre is locally of finite type over the residue field `R/𝔪`, being the base change
`X ×_{Spec R} Spec(R/𝔪)`
(`Stacks.PuncturedSpectrumPicard.baseIdealSubschemeIsoPullback`); `j₁` is an open immersion
whose image is `X₁ ∖ Z`; and the closed subset `X₁ ∩ Z` of `X₁` has dimension at most `dim(Z)`.
So `Stacks.Algebraization.isCoherent_pushforward_and_rightDerived_one_of_hasPropertySk_two`
applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_specialFibre_directImages_of_hasPropertySk_two
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [LocallyOfFiniteType p]
    (Z : Closeds X) (U : X.Opens) (hU : (U : Set X) = (Z : Set X)ᶜ)
    [IrreducibleSpace (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).subscheme]
    (hS₂ : letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian p
      letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).subscheme :=
        isLocallyNoetherian_of_isClosedImmersion
          (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).subschemeι
      HasPropertySk (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).subscheme 2)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (Z : Set X) + 3 ≤
      topologicalKrullDim (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).subscheme)
    (G : ((baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p).comap U.ι).subscheme.Modules)
    (hG : Scheme.Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree G) :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
        (specialFibreMap (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p) U)).obj G).IsCoherent ∧
      (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
        (specialFibreMap (baseIdealSheaf R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) p) U)).rightDerived
          1).obj G).IsCoherent
declarations.comment: the closing paragraph: if X₁ is (S₂) and irreducible, dim(X₁) - dim(Z) ≥ 3 and F₁ is a locally free O_{U₁}-module, then j₁,*F₁ and R¹j₁,*F₁ are coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.faithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_components_meet

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_sectionsComplete_of_or
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EJZ].** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and `Y ⊆ X` a closed subscheme, with
infinitesimal neighbourhoods `Y_n ⊆ X`. Assume one of the following holds:

1. `X` is quasi-affine and `Γ(X, 𝒪_X) → lim Γ(Y_n, 𝒪_{Y_n})` is an isomorphism, or
2. `X` has an ample invertible module `L` and `Γ(X, L^{⊗ m}) → lim Γ(Y_n, L^{⊗ m}|_{Y_n})` is an
   isomorphism for all `m ≫ 0`, or
3. for every finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module `ℰ` the map `Γ(X, ℰ) → lim Γ(Y_n, ℰ|_{Y_n})` is an
   isomorphism.

Then the restriction functor `FÉt_X ⟶ FÉt_Y` is fully faithful.

As in the source, cases (1) and (2) are reduced to case (3) by the implications `(1) ⇒ (2) ⇒ (3)`
of [Stacks, Tag 0EKP], case (3) gives full faithfulness of completion on finite locally free
modules by `(3) ⇒ (4)` of the same tag, and [Stacks, Tag 0EL8] concludes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_sectionsComplete_of_or
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsNoetherian X] [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (h : SectionsCompleteQuasiAffine i ∨ SectionsCompleteAmplePowers i ∨
      SectionsCompleteFiniteLocallyFree i) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange i).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.bijective_map_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_sectionsComplete_of_or
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EJZ], restated as bijectivity on hom sets.** Under any one of the three
conditions of
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_sectionsComplete_of_or`,
restriction of finite étale covers of `X` to the closed subscheme `Y` is bijective on every hom
set.

`CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful` carries the inverse map on hom sets as data, so full
faithfulness is recorded as `Nonempty _.FullyFaithful`;
`CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful.nonempty_iff_map_bijective` turns it into bijectivity on hom
sets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_map_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_sectionsComplete_of_or
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsNoetherian X] [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (h : SectionsCompleteQuasiAffine i ∨ SectionsCompleteAmplePowers i ∨
      SectionsCompleteFiniteLocallyFree i)
    (A B : FiniteEtaleOver X) :
    Function.Bijective (fun φ : A ⟶ B => (finiteEtaleBaseChange i).map φ)
declarations.comment: restated as bijectivity on hom sets

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_restrictionFunctor_of_neighbourhoodSectionsComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EK0].** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `Y ⊆ X` a closed subscheme with
infinitesimal neighbourhoods `Y_n ⊆ X`, and `𝒱` the open subschemes of `X` containing `Y`,
ordered by reverse inclusion. If one of

1. `X` is quasi-affine and `colim_𝒱 Γ(V, 𝒪_V) → lim Γ(Y_n, 𝒪_{Y_n})` is an isomorphism,
2. `X` has an ample invertible module `L` and
   `colim_𝒱 Γ(V, L^{⊗ m}) → lim Γ(Y_n, L^{⊗ m}|_{Y_n})` is an isomorphism for all `m ≫ 0`,
3. `colim_{V' ≥ V} Γ(V', ℰ|_{V'}) → lim Γ(Y_n, ℰ|_{Y_n})` is an isomorphism for every `V ∈ 𝒱` and
   every finite locally free `𝒪_V`-module `ℰ`,

holds, then the restriction functor `colim_𝒱 FÉt_V ⟶ FÉt_Y` is fully faithful.

The source's proof is to combine [Stacks, Tag 0ELA] with [Stacks, Tag 0EK2]. Of that chain this
library carries the implication `(1) ⇒ (2)` of Tag 0EK2 and no more, so condition (1) is
converted to condition (2) here by the library's proof of that implication and the remaining steps are the two
hypotheses `h0EK2` and `h0ELA`; see
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.AmplePowersImpliesFiniteLocallyFree` and
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.FullyFaithfulRestrictionOfSectionsComplete`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_restrictionFunctor_of_neighbourhoodSectionsComplete
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    (P : FiniteEtaleColimitPresentation X Y) [HasColimit P.diagram]
    (h : NeighbourhoodSectionsCompleteQuasiAffine Y ∨
      NeighbourhoodSectionsCompleteAmplePowers Y ∨
      NeighbourhoodSectionsCompleteFiniteLocallyFree Y)
    (h0EK2 : AmplePowersImpliesFiniteLocallyFree.{u})
    (h0ELA : FullyFaithfulRestrictionOfSectionsComplete.{u}) :
    Nonempty P.restrictionFunctor.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: granted Stacks 0EK2 (2)⇒(3), and Stacks 0EK2 (3)⇒(4) together with Stacks 0ELA

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.finiteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful_of_neighbourhoodSectionsComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EK0].** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `Y ⊆ X` a closed subscheme with
infinitesimal neighbourhoods `Y_n ⊆ X`, and `𝒱` the open subschemes of `X` containing `Y`,
ordered by reverse inclusion. Assume one of the following holds:

1. `X` is quasi-affine and `colim_𝒱 Γ(V, 𝒪_V) → lim Γ(Y_n, 𝒪_{Y_n})` is an isomorphism;
2. `X` has an ample invertible module `L` and
   `colim_𝒱 Γ(V, L^{⊗ m}) → lim Γ(Y_n, L^{⊗ m}|_{Y_n})` is an isomorphism for all `m ≫ 0`;
3. for every `V ∈ 𝒱` and every finite locally free `𝒪_V`-module `ℰ` the map
   `colim_{V' ≥ V} Γ(V', ℰ|_{V'}) → lim Γ(Y_n, ℰ|_{Y_n})` is an isomorphism.

Then the restriction functor `colim_𝒱 FÉt_V ⟶ FÉt_Y` is fully faithful. The conclusion is in the
form `FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful`, which describes the hom sets of the directed colimit.

The proof follows the source. By [Stacks, Tag 0EK2], condition (1) gives (2), (2) gives (3), and
(3) gives full faithfulness of completion on the finite locally free objects. [Stacks, Tag 0ELA]
then gives full faithfulness of restriction.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful_of_neighbourhoodSectionsComplete
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    (h : NeighbourhoodSectionsCompleteQuasiAffine Y ∨
      NeighbourhoodSectionsCompleteAmplePowers Y ∨
      FiniteLocallyFreeComplete Y.subschemeι) :
    FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful X Y
declarations.comment: all three cases, under the tag's own hypotheses; full faithfulness spelled through the directed-colimit description of the hom sets of colim_V FEt_V

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.isEquivalence_restrictionFunctor_of_fullyFaithful_of_essentialImage
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EK1].** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `Y ⊆ X` a closed subscheme with ideal
sheaf `I`, and `𝒱` the open subschemes of `X` containing `Y`, ordered by reverse inclusion. If the
completion functor `colim_𝒱 Coh(𝒪_V) ⟶ Coh(X, I)`, `ℱ ↦ ℱ^∧`, is an equivalence of the full
subcategories of finite locally free objects, then the restriction functor
`colim_𝒱 FÉt_V ⟶ FÉt_Y` is an equivalence.

The hypothesis is carried through the two consequences the source draws from it, because it
cannot be stated here: the finite locally free objects of `Coh(X, I)` and the comparison of
`Coh(X, I)` with `Coh(V, I|_V)` for a neighbourhood `V` are both absent from this library. The
first consequence, `h0ELA`, is full faithfulness of the restriction functor, which the source
obtains from the fully faithful half of the hypothesis by [Stacks, Tag 0ELA]. The second,
`hessImage`, is that every finite étale cover of `Y` is the restriction of a finite étale cover of
some neighbourhood; the source obtains it by algebraizing the tower `π_{n, *}𝒪_{U_n}` of pushed
forward structure sheaves of the covers of the infinitesimal neighbourhoods, which is a finite
locally free object of `Coh(X, I)`, transporting the algebra structure along the equivalence, and
taking the relative spectrum, which is étale near `Y` by More on Morphisms, Tag 0A43. What is
proved here is that the second consequence gives essential surjectivity of the functor out of the
colimit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_restrictionFunctor_of_fullyFaithful_of_essentialImage
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    (P : FiniteEtaleColimitPresentation X Y) [HasColimit P.diagram]
    (h0ELA : Nonempty P.restrictionFunctor.FullyFaithful)
    (hessImage : ∀ A : FiniteEtaleOver Y.subscheme, ∃ (W : Neighborhood X Y)
      (U : FiniteEtaleOver (Neighborhood.open X Y W).toScheme),
      Nonempty ((finiteEtaleBaseChange (Neighborhood.toSchemeHom X Y W)).obj U ≅ A)) :
    P.restrictionFunctor.IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: granted Stacks 0ELA for full faithfulness and the essential image of restriction

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.restriction_isEquivalence_of_completionEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EK1].** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `Y ⊆ X` a closed subscheme with ideal
sheaf `I`, and `𝒱` the open subschemes of `X` containing `Y`, ordered by reverse inclusion. If the
completion functor `colim_𝒱 Coh(𝒪_V) ⟶ Coh(X, I)` defines an equivalence of the full
subcategories of finite locally free objects, then the restriction functor
`colim_𝒱 FÉt_V ⟶ FÉt_Y` is an equivalence: it is fully faithful in the directed-colimit sense of
`FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful`, and every finite étale cover of `Y` is the restriction of a
finite étale cover of some `V ∈ 𝒱`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem restriction_isEquivalence_of_completionEquivalence [IsNoetherian X]
    (h : CompletionEquivalenceFiniteLocallyFree X Y) :
    FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful X Y ∧
      ∀ A : FiniteEtaleOver Y.subscheme, ∃ (W : Neighborhood X Y)
        (U : FiniteEtaleOver (Neighborhood.open X Y W).toScheme),
        Nonempty ((finiteEtaleBaseChange (Neighborhood.toSchemeHom X Y W)).obj U ≅ A)
declarations.comment: the colimit functor is an equivalence: fully faithful, and every finite étale cover of Y extends to a neighbourhood

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.NeighbourhoodCompletion.implications_among_conditions
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EK2].** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and let `Y ⊂ X` be a closed subscheme
with ideal sheaf `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪_X`. Let `Y_n ⊂ X` be the `n`-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of `Y` in `X`,
and let `𝒱` be the set of open subschemes `V ⊂ X` containing `Y`, ordered by reverse inclusion.
Consider the conditions

1. `X` is quasi-affine and `colim_𝒱 Γ(V, 𝒪_V) ⟶ lim Γ(Y_n, 𝒪_{Y_n})` is an isomorphism;
2. `X` has an ample invertible module `ℒ` and
   `colim_𝒱 Γ(V, ℒ^{⊗ m}) ⟶ lim Γ(Y_n, ℒ^{⊗ m}|_{Y_n})` is an isomorphism for all `m ≫ 0`;
3. for every `V ∈ 𝒱` and every finite locally free `𝒪_V`-module `ℰ` the map
   `colim_{V' ≥ V} Γ(V', ℰ|_{V'}) ⟶ lim Γ(Y_n, ℰ|_{Y_n})` is an isomorphism;
4. the completion functor `colim_𝒱 Coh(𝒪_V) ⟶ Coh(X, ℐ)`, `ℱ ↦ ℱ^∧`, is fully faithful on the
   full subcategory of finite locally free objects.

Then `(1) ⇒ (2) ⇒ (3) ⇒ (4)` and `(4) ⇒ (3)`.

The source proves `(1) ⇒ (2)` from the ampleness of `𝒪_X` on a quasi-affine scheme, `(2) ⇒ (3)`
from a universally exact sequence `0 → ℰ → (ℒ^{⊗ p})^{⊕ r}|_V → (ℒ^{⊗ q})^{⊕ s}|_V`, and
`(3) ⇒ (4)` by applying `(3)` to the internal hom; it omits the proof of `(4) ⇒ (3)`, which is
`(4)` applied to the pair `(𝒪_V, ℰ)`, read through the identification of a section of `ℰ` with a
morphism `𝒪 ⟶ ℰ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem implications_among_conditions [IsNoetherian X] :
    (IsQuasiAffineComplete i → HasAmpleComplete i) ∧
      (HasAmpleComplete i → FiniteLocallyFreeComplete i) ∧
      (FiniteLocallyFreeComplete i → CompletionFullyFaithfulComplete i) ∧
      (CompletionFullyFaithfulComplete i → FiniteLocallyFreeComplete i)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.quasiAffine_neighbourhoodSectionsComplete_implies_amplePower
declarations.doc:
**Condition (1) implies condition (2).** Let `i : Y ⟶ X` be a closed immersion into a
Noetherian quasi-affine scheme such that the colimit of the sections of `𝒪_X` over the open
neighbourhoods of `Y` is the limit of its sections on the infinitesimal neighbourhoods. Then `X`
carries an ample invertible module `L` for which the same holds for every tensor power `L^{⊗ m}`
with `m` large enough.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiAffine_neighbourhoodSectionsComplete_implies_amplePower
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsNoetherian X]
    (hX : Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X)
    (h : IsNeighbourhoodSectionsComplete i (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)) :
    ∃ (L : X.Modules)
      (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L),
      letI := hL
      AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L ∧
        ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m →
          IsNeighbourhoodSectionsComplete i
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
              (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (m : ℤ))
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtalePushoutRestriction_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EK4.**  The restriction functor
`FÉt_{Y ⨿_Z X} ⟶ FÉt_Y ×_{FÉt_Z} FÉt_X` is an equivalence of categories.  Composed with the
pushout of finite étale cartesian triples, which is an equivalence by
[Stacks Project, Tag 0ECL], it is reading a triple in the 2-fibre product, which is an
equivalence; so it is one itself.
declarations.statement:
instance finiteEtalePushoutRestriction_isEquivalence
    (s : PushoutAlongClosedImmersionAndIntegralSituation.{u}) :
    (finiteEtalePushoutRestriction s).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the restriction functor is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtalePushoutEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EK4.**  In the pushout situation of [Stacks Project, Tag 0ECI] — for
example when `Z ⟶ Y` and `Z ⟶ X` are closed immersions of schemes — there is an equivalence of
categories
`FÉt_{Y ⨿_Z X} ⟶ FÉt_Y ×_{FÉt_Z} FÉt_X`.
Its functor is `AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtalePushoutRestriction`, which sends a finite étale
cover of the pushout to its base changes to `Y` and to `X` together with the canonical
identification of their restrictions to `Z`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finiteEtalePushoutEquivalence
    (s : PushoutAlongClosedImmersionAndIntegralSituation.{u}) :
    FiniteEtaleOver (pushoutScheme s) ≌
      CategoricalPullback (finiteEtaleBaseChange s.j) (finiteEtaleBaseChange s.i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtalePushoutEquivalence_functor
declarations.doc: The equivalence of [Stacks Project, Tag 0EK4] is the restriction functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteEtalePushoutEquivalence_functor
    (s : PushoutAlongClosedImmersionAndIntegralSituation.{u}) :
    (finiteEtalePushoutEquivalence s).functor = finiteEtalePushoutRestriction s
declarations.comment: the comparison functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocalLefschetzSituation.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_depth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EK5]** under hypothesis (c)(ii), in the case where `A` is in addition
`f`-adically complete. In the local Lefschetz situation assume that `A` has a dualizing complex,
that the pair `(A, (f))` is henselian, and that `depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > 2` for every prime
`𝔭 ⊂ A` with `f ∉ 𝔭`. If moreover `A` is `f`-adically complete, then `FÉt_U ⟶ FÉt_{U₀}` is
fully faithful.

Two restrictions of the tag are recorded in the attribute.

* Hypothesis (c) of the tag is a disjunction, and only branch (ii) — the depth-plus-dimension
  inequality — is treated. Branch (c)(i) is not: deducing (ii) from it is the
  `(S₂)`-plus-dimension argument of the source, which goes through Stacks 0339, 0A80, 0AW6 and
  0AWY and is not carried out here.
* The `f`-adic completeness of `A` is the one hypothesis beyond the tag's own. The source
  obtains it by replacing `A` by its `𝔪`-adic completion, which is Stacks 0BLI, available here
  as `…fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_completion`, together with Stacks 0EHW for the
  inheritance of (c)(ii); that reduction is not carried out here. The henselian hypothesis `hS`
  is the tag's hypothesis (b) and is exactly what the omitted reduction consumes, so it is
  stated but not used below.

The carried hypotheses `hEKP`, `h0GN2` and `halgebra` are the ones discussed on
`fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_annihilated`; here `hEKP` arrives through
`Stacks.Algebraization.completionFullyFaithful_of_isAdicComplete_of_depth` (Stacks 0EKT) rather
than through Stacks 0EKS. None of the three mentions `A`, `f`, `U` or `U₀`, and none is about
finite étale covers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_depth
    (S : LocalLefschetzSituation.{u})
    (hS : HenselianPair S.A S.principalIdeal)
    (omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A))
    (homega : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex (A := S.A) (K := omega))
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {S.f}) S.A)
    (hdepth : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S.A, S.f ∉ p.asIdeal →
      enatToEInt
          (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
            (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
            (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl S.A)) +
        krullDimToEInt (ringKrullDim (S.A ⧸ p.asIdeal)) > ((2 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (hEKP : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] (b : Ideal B) (g : B),
      Scheme.IsQuasiAffine (complementZeroLocus B b : Scheme) →
      Function.Bijective
        (Stacks.Algebraization.ComplementTower.sectionsToLimit B b g (ModuleCat.of B B)) →
      CompletionFullyFaithfulOnFiniteLocallyFree (complementZeroLocus B b : Scheme)
        (complementPrincipalIdealSheaf B b g))
    (h0GN2 : ∀ {Z Z' : Scheme.{u}} (κ : Z' ⟶ Z) [IsClosedImmersion κ] (N : Z.Modules),
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} N →
      Stacks.Algebraization.IsInfinitesimalSectionsComplete κ
        (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.dualSheaf N) →
      (∀ φ ψ : N ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf,
          (∀ n : ℕ, φ ≫ nthOrderUnitMap κ n = ψ ≫ nthOrderUnitMap κ n) → φ = ψ) ∧
        ∀ α : ∀ n : ℕ, N ⟶ AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModule (nthOrderAlgebra κ n),
          (∀ n : ℕ, α (n + 1) ≫ nthOrderTransitionMap κ n = α n) →
          ∃ φ : N ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf,
            ∀ n : ℕ, φ ≫ nthOrderUnitMap κ n = α n)
    (halgebra : ∀ {Z : Scheme.{u}} (B C : AlgebraSheaf Z) (D : ℕ → AlgebraSheaf Z)
      (r : ∀ n : ℕ, C ⟶ D n)
      (φ : AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModule B ⟶ AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModule C),
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
        (AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModule B) →
      _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent (AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModule B) →
      (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ ψ : B ⟶ D n,
        AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModuleMap ψ = φ ≫ AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModuleMap (r n)) →
      (∀ P : Z.Modules, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} P →
        _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent P →
        ∀ a b : P ⟶ AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModule C,
          (∀ n : ℕ, a ≫ AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModuleMap (r n) =
            b ≫ AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModuleMap (r n)) → a = b) →
      ∃ ψ : B ⟶ C, AlgebraSheaf.underlyingModuleMap ψ = φ) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange S.U₀ToU).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: under hypothesis (c)(ii), the depth-plus-dimension form, and in the case where `A` is in addition `f`-adically complete; branch (c)(i) and the reduction to the complete case are not carried out, and hEKP (the chain (1) ⇒ (4) of Stacks 0EKP), h0GN2 (Stacks 0GN2) and halgebra are granted as general hypotheses about other rings and other schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocalLefschetzSituation.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_dualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EK5].** In the local Lefschetz situation assume

* (a) `A` has a dualizing complex,
* (b) the pair `(A, (f))` is henselian,
* (c) one of the following is true:
  * (i) `A_f` is `(S₂)` and every irreducible component of `X` not contained in `X₀` has
    dimension `≥ 3`, or
  * (ii) for every prime `𝔭 ⊂ A` with `f ∉ 𝔭` we have `depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > 2`.

Then the restriction functor `FÉt_U ⟶ FÉt_{U₀}` is fully faithful.

Hypothesis (a) is `hdual`, (b) is `hS` and (c) is the disjunction `hc`. In branch (c)(i), `(S₂)`
for `A_f` is `PropertySkRing (Localization.Away S.f) 2`, and an irreducible component of `X` not
contained in `X₀` is `V(𝔮)` for a minimal prime `𝔮` of `A` with `f ∉ 𝔮`, of dimension
`dim(A/𝔮)`. In branch (c)(ii) the depth of `A_𝔭` is that of `A_𝔭` as a module over itself along
its maximal ideal, and the inequality is read in the extended integers.

The proof is the source's: branch (c)(i) implies branch (c)(ii), by
`two_lt_depth_add_ringKrullDim_of_propertySkRing_away` — `A` is universally catenary by
Stacks 0A80 because it has a dualizing complex — and under (c)(ii) the statement is
`fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_depth_add_dim`: reduction to the `𝔪`-adic completion by
Stacks 0BLI, then Stacks 0EKT and Stacks 0EL8.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleRestriction_of_dualizingComplex
    (S : LocalLefschetzSituation.{u})
    (hdual : ∃ omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex omega)
    (hS : HenselianPair S.A S.principalIdeal)
    (hc : (PropertySkRing (Localization.Away S.f) 2 ∧
        ∀ q : Ideal S.A, q ∈ minimalPrimes S.A → S.f ∉ q →
          (3 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (S.A ⧸ q)) ∨
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S.A, S.f ∉ p.asIdeal →
        enatToEInt
            (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
              (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
              (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl S.A)) +
          krullDimToEInt (ringKrullDim (S.A ⧸ p.asIdeal)) > ((2 : ℤ) : EInt)) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange S.U₀ToU).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocalLefschetzSituation.exists_finiteEtale_extension_of_dualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EK6].** In the local Lefschetz situation (Tag 0BLF) let `V` be finite étale
over `U`. Assume

* (a) `A` has a dualizing complex,
* (b) the pair `(A, (f))` is henselian,
* (c) one of the following is true:
  (i) `A_f` is `(S₂)` and every irreducible component of `X` not contained in `X₀` has dimension
  `≥ 3`, or (ii) `depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > 2` for every prime `𝔭 ⊂ A` with `f ∉ 𝔭`,
* (d) `V₀ = V ×_U U₀` is equal to `Y₀ ×_{X₀} U₀` for some `Y₀ → X₀` finite étale.

Then `V = Y ×_X U` for some `Y → X` finite étale.

Spelling. Hypothesis (a) is `hdual`, (b) is `hS` and (c) is the disjunction `hc`. "`A` has a
dualizing complex" is `∃ ω, Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex ω`, the predicate of [Stacks, Tag 0A7B]
on the derived category of `A`-modules. `(S₂)` for `A_f` is
`PropertySkRing (Localization.Away S.f) 2`, Serre's condition of [Stacks, Tag 031P]. The
irreducible components of `X = Spec A` are the `V(𝔮)` for `𝔮` a minimal prime of `A`; `V(𝔮)` is
contained in `X₀ = V(f)` exactly when `f ∈ 𝔮`, and its dimension is `dim(A/𝔮)`; so the second
half of (c)(i) is the quantification over minimal primes `𝔮` with `f ∉ 𝔮`. In (c)(ii)
`depth(A_𝔭)` is the depth of the `A_𝔭`-module `A_𝔭` along its maximal ideal and the sum is formed
in `ℤ ∪ {±∞}`. Hypothesis (d) and the conclusion record "`V₀ = Y₀ ×_{X₀} U₀`" and
"`V = Y ×_X U`" as cartesian squares (`CategoryTheory.IsPullback`), `V ×_U U₀` being the chosen
pullback.

The proof is the source's. Branch (c)(i) implies branch (c)(ii) for a ring with a dualizing
complex (`two_lt_depth_add_ringKrullDim_of_propertySkRing_away`, through the universal
catenarity of Stacks 0A80), and under (c)(ii) the statement is
`exists_finiteEtale_extension_of_depth_add_dim`: Stacks 0BLL reduces to the complete case,
where Stacks 09ZL/09ZS lifts `Y₀` (the pair being henselian by Stacks 0ALJ) and Stacks 0EK5
descends the isomorphism over `U₀` to one over `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteEtale_extension_of_dualizingComplex
    (S : LocalLefschetzSituation.{u})
    (hdual : ∃ omega : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex omega)
    (hS : HenselianPair S.A S.principalIdeal)
    (hc : (PropertySkRing (Localization.Away S.f) 2 ∧
        ∀ q : Ideal S.A, q ∈ minimalPrimes S.A → S.f ∉ q →
          (3 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (S.A ⧸ q)) ∨
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S.A, S.f ∉ p.asIdeal →
        enatToEInt
            (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
              (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
              (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl S.A)) +
          krullDimToEInt (ringKrullDim (S.A ⧸ p.asIdeal)) > ((2 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (V : Scheme.{u}) (pi : V ⟶ S.U) [IsFinite pi] [Etale pi]
    (Y₀ : Scheme.{u}) (f₀ : Y₀ ⟶ S.X₀) [IsFinite f₀] [Etale f₀]
    (g₀ : pullback pi S.U₀ToU ⟶ Y₀)
    (h₀ : IsPullback (pullback.snd pi S.U₀ToU) g₀ S.U₀Open.ι f₀) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (p : Y ⟶ S.X) (g : V ⟶ Y),
      IsFinite p ∧ Etale p ∧ IsPullback pi g S.UOpen.ι p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocalLefschetzSituation.essSurj_finiteEtaleBaseChange_U₀ToU_of_dualizing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EK9.**  Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and let `f ∈ 𝔪`.
Write `X = Spec A`, let `U = X ∖ {𝔪}` and `U₀ = Spec (A / fA) ∖ {𝔪}` be the two punctured
spectra.  Assume

1. `A` has a dualizing complex and is `f`-adically complete,
2. one of
   * (a) `A_f` satisfies Serre's condition `(S₂)` and every irreducible component of `X` not
     contained in `V(f)` has dimension at least `4`, or
   * (b) `depth(A_𝔭) + dim(A/𝔭) > 3` whenever `𝔭 ∉ V(f)` and `V(𝔭) ∩ V(f) ≠ {𝔪}`,
3. purity holds for `(A_f)_𝔭` for every maximal ideal `𝔭 ⊂ A_f`.

Then the restriction functor `FÉt_U ⥤ FÉt_{U₀}` is essentially surjective.

The source's argument is followed.  Hypotheses (1) and (2) make the restriction functor
`colim_{U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U} FÉt_{U'} ⥤ FÉt_{U₀}` an equivalence, so a given finite étale cover of `U₀`
is already the restriction of a cover of some open `U'` of `X` with `U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U`.  The points of
`U` that `U'` omits correspond to maximal ideals of `A_f`, so hypothesis (3) makes purity
available at each of them and the cover extends from `U'` across them to a cover of `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essSurj_finiteEtaleBaseChange_U₀ToU_of_dualizing
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} S.A)]
    (hdual : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S.A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {S.f}) S.A)
    (hcond :
      (PropertySkRing (Localization.Away S.f) 2 ∧
          ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S.A, IsMinimalPrime p.asIdeal → S.f ∉ p.asIdeal →
            (4 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (S.A ⧸ p.asIdeal)) ∨
        (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S.A, S.f ∉ p.asIdeal →
          ({q : PrimeSpectrum S.A | p.asIdeal ≤ q.asIdeal} ∩
            {q : PrimeSpectrum S.A | S.f ∈ q.asIdeal}) ≠
            {⟨maximalIdeal S.A, (maximalIdeal.isMaximal S.A).isPrime⟩} →
          (3 : WithBot ℕ∞) <
            (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
              (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
              (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) : WithBot ℕ∞) +
              ringKrullDim (S.A ⧸ p.asIdeal)))
    (haway : ∀ (p : Ideal (Localization.Away S.f)) [p.IsMaximal],
      HasPurity (Localization.AtPrime p)) :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange S.U₀ToU).EssSurj
declarations.comment: the restriction functor FÉt_U ⥤ FÉt_{U₀} is essentially surjective, under the tag's three hypotheses; nothing beyond them is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocalLefschetzSituation.essSurj_finiteEtaleBaseChange_U₀ToU_of_isAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EKA.**  Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and let `f ∈ 𝔪`.
Assume

1. `A` is `f`-adically complete,
2. `f` is a nonzerodivisor,
3. `H¹_𝔪(A/fA)` and `H²_𝔪(A/fA)` are finite `A`-modules, and
4. purity holds for `(A_f)_𝔭` for every maximal ideal `𝔭 ⊂ A_f`.

Then the restriction functor `FÉt_U ⥤ FÉt_{U₀}` is essentially surjective.

The source proves this by the proof of Stacks 0EK9 with Stacks 0BLV in place of Stacks 0DXY, and
that is what happens here.  Hypotheses (1)–(3) are the hypotheses of Stacks 0BLV, and give an
open `U'` of `X` with `U₀ ⊆ U' ⊆ U` over which a given finite étale cover of `U₀` is already
defined.  The points of `U` outside `U'` are maximal ideals of `A_f`, so hypothesis (4) makes
purity available at each of them and the cover extends from `U'` to `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essSurj_finiteEtaleBaseChange_U₀ToU_of_isAdicComplete
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete S.principalIdeal S.A) (hnzd : S.f ∈ nonZeroDivisors S.A)
    (hH1 : Module.Finite S.A (localCohomologyModule S.A (maximalIdeal S.A)
      (maximalIdeal S.A).fg_of_isNoetherianRing (ModuleCat.of S.A S.quotientRing) 1))
    (hH2 : Module.Finite S.A (localCohomologyModule S.A (maximalIdeal S.A)
      (maximalIdeal S.A).fg_of_isNoetherianRing (ModuleCat.of S.A S.quotientRing) 2))
    (haway : ∀ (p : Ideal (Localization.Away S.f)) [p.IsMaximal],
      HasPurity (Localization.AtPrime p)) :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange S.U₀ToU).EssSurj
declarations.comment: the restriction functor FÉt_U ⥤ FÉt_{U₀} is essentially surjective, under the tag's four hypotheses; nothing beyond them is assumed

declarations.name: Submodule.IsHomogeneous.le_of_le_smul_of_le_irrelevant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EKB** (graded Nakayama). Let `A = ⨁ᵢ 𝒜ᵢ` be a graded ring and `M = ⨁_d ℳ_d` a
graded `A`-module. Let `N, N' ⊆ M` be graded submodules with `N'` finitely generated, and let
`I ⊆ 𝒜₊ = ⨁_{i > 0} 𝒜ᵢ` be an ideal. If `N' ⊆ N + I N'`, then `N' ⊆ N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Submodule.IsHomogeneous.le_of_le_smul_of_le_irrelevant
    {ιA ιM σA σM A M : Type*} [CommSemiring A] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module A M]
    [DecidableEq ιA] [AddCommMonoid ιA] [PartialOrder ιA] [CanonicallyOrderedAdd ιA]
    [SetLike σA A] [AddSubmonoidClass σA A] {𝒜 : ιA → σA} [GradedRing 𝒜]
    [DecidableEq ιM] [PartialOrder ιM] [SetLike σM M] [AddSubmonoidClass σM M]
    {ℳ : ιM → σM} [DirectSum.Decomposition ℳ]
    [AddAction ιA ιM] [IsOrderedCancelVAdd ιA ιM] [SetLike.GradedSMul 𝒜 ℳ]
    {I : Ideal A} {N N' : Submodule A M}
    (hN : N.IsHomogeneous ℳ) (hN' : N'.IsHomogeneous ℳ) (hfg : N'.FG)
    (hI : I ≤ 𝒜₊.toIdeal) (hle : N' ≤ N ⊔ I • N') :
    N' ≤ N

declarations.name: Ideal.IsHomogeneous.exists_finite_graded_forall_ker_eq_pow_smul_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EKC**. Let `A = ⨁_{i ≥ 0} 𝒜 i` be a graded ring, let `I ⊆ 𝒜₊ = ⨁_{i > 0} 𝒜 i` be a
homogeneous ideal, and let `(Nₙ)` be an inverse system of finite graded `A`-modules whose
transition maps `t n : N_{n+1} → Nₙ` are graded and exhibit `Nₙ = N_{n+1}/Iⁿ N_{n+1}`. Then there
is a finite graded `A`-module `M` and a compatible system of graded surjections `f n : M → Nₙ`
with `ker (f n) = Iⁿ M`, i.e. `Nₙ = M/Iⁿ M` as graded modules for all `n`.

The source assumes `A` Noetherian; the argument uses only that each `Nₙ` is a finite `A`-module,
so that hypothesis is omitted.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_graded_forall_ker_eq_pow_smul_top
    {A : Type u} {σ : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [SetLike σ A] [AddSubmonoidClass σ A] {𝒜 : ℕ → σ} [GradedRing 𝒜]
    {I : Ideal A} (hIhom : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
    (hI : I ≤ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal)
    {N : ℕ → Type v} [∀ n, AddCommGroup (N n)] [∀ n, Module A (N n)]
    [∀ n, Module.Finite A (N n)]
    (𝒩 : ∀ n, ℤ → AddSubgroup (N n)) [∀ n, DirectSum.Decomposition (𝒩 n)]
    (h𝒩 : ∀ (n i : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (a : A) (x : N n), a ∈ 𝒜 i → x ∈ 𝒩 n d → a • x ∈ 𝒩 n (i + d))
    (t : ∀ n, N (n + 1) →ₗ[A] N n)
    (ht : ∀ (n : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (x : N (n + 1)), x ∈ 𝒩 (n + 1) d → t n x ∈ 𝒩 n d)
    (htsurj : ∀ n, Function.Surjective (t n))
    (htker : ∀ n, LinearMap.ker (t n) = I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (N (n + 1)))) :
    ∃ (M : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module A M) (ℳ : ℤ → AddSubgroup M)
        (_ : DirectSum.Decomposition ℳ) (f : ∀ n, M →ₗ[A] N n),
      Module.Finite A M ∧
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (a : A) (x : M), a ∈ 𝒜 i → x ∈ ℳ d → a • x ∈ ℳ (i + d)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (x : M), x ∈ ℳ d → f n x ∈ 𝒩 n d) ∧
      (∀ n, Function.Surjective (f n)) ∧
      (∀ n, LinearMap.ker (f n) = I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M)) ∧
      (∀ n, (t n).comp (f (n + 1)) = f n)

declarations.name: GradedCompletionData.main_theorem
declarations.doc:
Stacks tag 0EKD (Lemma 10.98.4): if the induced map `φ : M ⊗_A A' → lim_n Gₙ` is an
isomorphism, then for every `d ∈ ℤ` the induced map `φ^(d) : M_d → lim_n G_{n,d}` is an
isomorphism.

Bijectivity of `φ^(d)` splits into injectivity and surjectivity, each reduced through
`limGdIncl` to `baseChange_degree_injective` and `baseChange_degree_surjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem (D : GradedCompletionData)
    (hφ : Function.Bijective D.φ) (d : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective (D.phiD d)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleNonvanishingUniversallyClosed.isAffineHom_nonvanishingOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EKE.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a universally closed morphism, `L` an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module ample relative to `f`, and `s` a global section of `L`. Then the nonvanishing open
`X_s` of Stacks Tag 01CY is affine over `S`.

Affineness of a morphism is checked over an affine open `V` of `S`. There the restriction of `L`
to `f⁻¹V` is ample, by the very definition of relative ampleness, the restriction of `f` is still
universally closed, and the nonvanishing open of the restricted section is the preimage of `X_s`
by Stacks Tag 0H78; so the affine base case applies and gives `X_s ∩ f⁻¹V` affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_nonvanishingOpen {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f]
    (L : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) :
    IsAffineHom ((nonvanishingOpen X L s).ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Truncation.span_degreeOne_pow_eq_truncationIdeal
declarations.doc:
If `A` is generated over `A_0` by its degree-one part, in the form `A_{d+1} ⊆ A_1 · A_d`
for every `d`, then `(A_+)^m = A_{≥ m}` for every `m ≥ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem span_degreeOne_pow_eq_truncationIdeal
    (hgen : ∀ d : ℕ, ∀ a ∈ 𝒜 (d + 1),
      a ∈ Ideal.span (𝒜 1 : Set A) * Ideal.span (𝒜 d : Set A))
    (m : ℕ) : Ideal.span (𝒜 1 : Set A) ^ m = truncationIdeal 𝒜 m
declarations.comment: the clause that makes the section's cone a blowup: if A is generated over A₀ by elements of degree one then (A₊)^m = A_{≥ m} for every m ≥ 0, so that B = ⨁_{d ≥ 0} A_{≥ d} is the Rees algebra of A₊ and L = Proj(B) ⟶ X = Spec(A) is the blowing up of Z = V(A₊). Nothing else of Section 37.51 is claimed here: the graded ring B with its maps σ, ψ, τ is Tag 0EKG, already in this file; the five localization facts about σ(f), σ(A_d) and ker(τ) on D₊(ψ(f)), the identification B_{σ(f)} ≅ A_f[T] that makes L ⟶ X an isomorphism over U = X ∖ Z, and the description of L over the largest open of P on which 𝒪_P(1) is invertible, are not proved

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.zToX
declarations.doc: The closed immersion `Z = Spec A₀ ⟶ X = Spec A` induced by the projection `A → A₀`.
declarations.statement: def zToX : Spec (CommRingCat.of (𝒜 0)) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)
declarations.comment: the morphism Z → X

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.xToZ
declarations.doc: The morphism `X = Spec A ⟶ Z = Spec A₀` induced by the inclusion `A₀ → A`.
declarations.statement: def xToZ : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of (𝒜 0))
declarations.comment: the morphism X → Z

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.openU
declarations.doc:
The open `U = X ∖ V(A₊)` of `X = Spec A`: the union of the standard opens `D(f)` of the
homogeneous elements `f` of positive degree.
declarations.statement: def openU : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens
declarations.comment: the open U ⊆ X

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.projMapDomain_tau_eq_top
declarations.doc: `τ` induces a morphism on all of `P = Proj 𝒜`.
declarations.statement: theorem projMapDomain_tau_eq_top : mapDomain ℬ 𝒜 c.tau = ⊤
declarations.comment: τ defines a morphism on all of Proj(A)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.projMapDomain_psi_eq_top
declarations.doc:
`ψ` induces a morphism on all of `L = Proj ℬ`: the power condition is exactly the radical
inclusion of irrelevant ideals that makes the standard opens `D₊(ψ f)` cover `Proj ℬ`.
declarations.statement: theorem projMapDomain_psi_eq_top : mapDomain 𝒜 ℬ c.psi = ⊤
declarations.comment: ψ defines a morphism on all of Proj(B)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.pi
declarations.doc: The cone projection `π : L = Proj ℬ ⟶ P = Proj 𝒜`, induced by `ψ`.
declarations.statement: def pi : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj ℬ ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒜
declarations.comment: the cone projection π : L → P

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.zeroSection
declarations.doc: The zero section `0 : P = Proj 𝒜 ⟶ L = Proj ℬ`, induced by `τ`.
declarations.statement: def zeroSection : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒜 ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Proj ℬ
declarations.comment: the zero section 0 : P → L

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.toSpecA
declarations.doc:
The structure morphism `L = Proj ℬ ⟶ X = Spec A`, using the identification `σ` of `A` with
the degree-zero part of `B`.
declarations.statement: def toSpecA : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj ℬ ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)
declarations.comment: the structure morphism L → X

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.openUInL
declarations.doc: The inverse image in `L` of the open `U = X ∖ V(A₊)`.
declarations.statement: def openUInL : (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj ℬ).Opens
declarations.comment: the open U ⊆ L

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.pi_preimage_basicOpen
declarations.doc:
**The inverse image under `π` of a standard open** of `P` is the standard open of the image
element: `π⁻¹(D₊(f)) = D₊(ψ f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pi_preimage_basicOpen (f : A) (d : ℕ) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) (hd : 0 < d) :
    pi c ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f = Proj.basicOpen ℬ (c.psi f)
declarations.comment: π⁻¹ of a standard open

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.isAffineHom_pi
declarations.doc:
**The cone projection is affine.** The standard opens of positive-degree homogeneous elements
cover `P` and are affine, and their inverse images are again standard opens of positive-degree
homogeneous elements.
declarations.statement: theorem isAffineHom_pi : IsAffineHom (pi c)
declarations.comment: π is affine

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.zeroSection_comp_pi
declarations.doc: **`π ∘ 0 = id_P`**: the zero section is a section of the cone projection.
declarations.statement: theorem zeroSection_comp_pi : zeroSection c ≫ pi c = 𝟙 (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒜)
declarations.comment: π ∘ 0 = id_P

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.isClosedImmersion_zeroSection
declarations.doc: **The zero section is a closed immersion**, `τ` being surjective in every degree.
declarations.statement: theorem isClosedImmersion_zeroSection : IsClosedImmersion (zeroSection c)
declarations.comment: 0 : P → L is a closed immersion

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.range_zeroSection
declarations.doc:
**The zero section maps onto the inverse image of `Z`.** Set theoretically the image of
`0 : P → L` is the complement of the part of `L` lying over `U = X ∖ V(A₊)`. A point of the image
contains `σ (A₊)` because `τ ∘ σ` kills the positive degrees; conversely a homogeneous prime of
`B` containing `σ (A₊)` is the image of its own contraction along `ψ`, which is relevant because
`ψ` is everywhere defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_zeroSection :
    Set.range (zeroSection c) = ((openUInL c : Set (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj ℬ)))ᶜ
declarations.comment: the image of the zero section is the inverse image of Z

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.isAffineHom_pi_restrict
declarations.doc:
**The punctured cone is affine over `P`.** Over the standard open `D₊(f)` the part of `L`
lying over `U` is the standard open `D₊(σ f · ψ f)` of a positive-degree homogeneous element,
hence affine.
declarations.statement: theorem isAffineHom_pi_restrict : IsAffineHom ((openUInL c).ι ≫ pi c)
declarations.comment: U → P is affine

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.pi_comp_toSpecZero
declarations.doc: **The right square commutes**: `L → P → Z` equals `L → X → Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pi_comp_toSpecZero :
    pi c ≫ Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜 = toSpecA c ≫ xToZ 𝒜
declarations.comment: the square L → P, X → Z commutes

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.zeroSection_comp_toSpecA
declarations.doc: **The left square commutes**: `P → L → X` equals `P → Z → X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroSection_comp_toSpecA :
    zeroSection c ≫ toSpecA c = Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜 ≫ zToX 𝒜
declarations.comment: the square P → L, Z → X commutes

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjConeTwist.truncationCone
declarations.doc:
**`π : L ⟶ P` is a cone over `P`** in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 062R], graded by the algebra
`⨁_{m ≥ 0} 𝒪_P(m)` of nonnegative twists: `π` is affine, the homogeneous pieces include in
`π_* 𝒪_L` by the degreewise inclusions `𝒪_P(m) ⟶ π_* 𝒪_L`, every function on the cone is locally
a unique finite sum of homogeneous ones, the inclusions are multiplicative, the negative pieces
vanish and the degree-zero piece is `𝒪_P`, included by the structure map.
declarations.statement: def truncationCone : AbstractCone (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒜)
declarations.comment: π : L → P is a cone over P, whose direct-image algebra is graded by the twists O_P(m), m ≥ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjConeTwist.range_zeroSection_eq_preimage_range_zToX
declarations.doc:
**The zero section `0 : P ⟶ L` maps set theoretically onto the inverse image of `Z` in `L`**:
its image is the inverse image under `σ : L ⟶ X` of the image of `Z = Spec A₀ ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_zeroSection_eq_preimage_range_zToX :
    Set.range (zeroSection 𝒜) = toSpecA 𝒜 ⁻¹' Set.range (ProjAndSpec.zToX 𝒜)
declarations.comment: the zero section maps set theoretically onto the inverse image of Z in L

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjConeTwist.zeroSection_appLE_coneIota_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The zero section `0 : P ⟶ L` is the vertex of the cone `π : L ⟶ P`**: it is a section of
`π`, and pulling functions back along it kills every homogeneous piece `𝒪_P(m)`, `m > 0`, of
`π_* 𝒪_L = ⨁_{m ≥ 0} 𝒪_P(m)`, over every open of `P`. So `0` is the closed immersion cut out by the
positive part of the grading, `Spec_P(𝒪_P) ⟶ Spec_P(⨁_{m ≥ 0} 𝒪_P(m))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroSection_appLE_coneIota_eq_zero (m : ℤ) (hm : 0 < m)
    (U : Opens (ProjectiveSpectrum.top 𝒜)) (s : (nonnegTwistingSheaf 𝒜 m).val.obj (op U)) :
    (zeroSection 𝒜).appLE (pi 𝒜 ⁻¹ᵁ U) U (le_zeroSection_preimage_pi_preimage 𝒜 U)
      ((coneIota 𝒜 m).val.app (op U) s) = 0
declarations.comment: the zero section 0 : P → L is the vertex of the cone π

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjConeTwist.projAndSpec_diagram
declarations.doc:
**The diagram of [Stacks, Tag 0EKG].** Let `A` be a graded ring, `X = Spec A`,
`Z = V(A₊) = Spec A₀`, `U = X ∖ Z`, `P = Proj A`, and let `L = Proj B` for
`B = ⨁_{d ≥ 0} A_{≥ d}`, with cone projection `π : L ⟶ P`, structure morphism `σ : L ⟶ X` and zero
section `0 : P ⟶ L`. Then, writing `j : Spec_P(⨁_{m ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_P(m)) ⟶ L` for the top-left arrow and
`e : Spec_P(⨁_{m ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_P(m)) ≅ U` for the left identification:

* `π` is a cone over `P` (`truncationCone`, graded by `⨁_{m ≥ 0} 𝒪_P(m)`, whose pieces are the
  twisting sheaves `𝒪_P(m)`, `m ≥ 0`), and `L = Spec_P(⨁_{m ≥ 0} 𝒪_P(m))` over `P`;
* `j` lies over `P`, it is an open immersion, and its image is the part of `L` over `U`;
* `e` is an identification over `P`;
* the left square `j ≫ σ = e ≫ (U ⟶ X)` and the right square `π ≫ (P ⟶ Z) = σ ≫ (X ⟶ Z)`
  commute;
* the zero section is a section of `π`, it is the vertex of the cone (pulling back along it kills
  the pieces `𝒪_P(m)`, `m > 0`, of `π_* 𝒪_L`), and it maps set theoretically onto the inverse image
  of `Z` in `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projAndSpec_diagram :
    -- `π` is a cone over `P`, graded by the nonnegative twists
    (truncationCone 𝒜).π = pi 𝒜 ∧
    (truncationCone 𝒜).grading = nonnegTwistAlgebra 𝒜 ∧
    (truncationCone 𝒜).ι = coneIota 𝒜 ∧
    (∀ m : ℕ, (truncationCone 𝒜).grading.piece m = twistingSheaf 𝒜 m) ∧
    (∀ m : ℤ, (integerTwistAlgebra 𝒜).piece m = twistingSheaf 𝒜 m) ∧
    -- `L = Spec_P(⨁_{m ≥ 0} 𝒪_P(m))` over `P`
    (coneProjIsoRelativeSpecTwistAlgebra 𝒜).hom ≫
        relativeSpecToBase (nonnegTwistAlgebraSheaf 𝒜) = pi 𝒜 ∧
    -- the top-left arrow lies over `P`, is an open immersion, with image the part of `L` over `U`
    puncturedToConeProj 𝒜 ≫ pi 𝒜 = relativeSpecToBase (integerTwistAlgebraSheaf 𝒜) ∧
    IsOpenImmersion (puncturedToConeProj 𝒜) ∧
    (puncturedToConeProj 𝒜).opensRange = openUInL 𝒜 ∧
    -- the left identification `Spec_P(⨁_{m ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_P(m)) = U` lies over `P`
    (puncturedConeRelativeSpecTwistAlgebraIsoOpenU 𝒜).hom ≫ openUToProj 𝒜 =
      relativeSpecToBase (integerTwistAlgebraSheaf 𝒜) ∧
    -- the left square
    puncturedToConeProj 𝒜 ≫ toSpecA 𝒜 =
      (puncturedConeRelativeSpecTwistAlgebraIsoOpenU 𝒜).hom ≫ (ProjAndSpec.openU 𝒜).ι ∧
    -- the right square
    pi 𝒜 ≫ Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜 = toSpecA 𝒜 ≫ ProjAndSpec.xToZ 𝒜 ∧
    -- the zero section
    zeroSection 𝒜 ≫ pi 𝒜 = 𝟙 (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒜) ∧
    (∀ (m : ℤ), 0 < m → ∀ (U : Opens (ProjectiveSpectrum.top 𝒜))
        (s : (nonnegTwistingSheaf 𝒜 m).val.obj (op U)),
      (zeroSection 𝒜).appLE (pi 𝒜 ⁻¹ᵁ U) U (le_zeroSection_preimage_pi_preimage 𝒜 U)
        ((coneIota 𝒜 m).val.app (op U) s) = 0) ∧
    Set.range (zeroSection 𝒜) = toSpecA 𝒜 ⁻¹' Set.range (ProjAndSpec.zToX 𝒜)
declarations.comment: the commutative diagram Spec_P(⨁_{m ∈ ℤ} O_P(m)) → L = Spec_P(⨁_{m ≥ 0} O_P(m)) → P over U → X → Z, with π a cone whose zero section maps set theoretically onto the inverse image of Z in L

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpecTruncation.isIso_toSpecA_restrict
declarations.doc:
**The structure morphism `L ⟶ X` is an isomorphism over `U = X ∖ V(A₊)`.** This is the
equality on the left of the diagram of [Stacks, Tag 0EKG]: being an isomorphism over an open is
local on that open, and over each standard open of a positive-degree homogeneous element the
morphism is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_toSpecA_restrict : IsIso (toSpecA 𝒜 ∣_ ProjAndSpec.openU 𝒜)
declarations.comment: L → X is an isomorphism over U

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpecTruncation.openUInL_ι_comp_toSpecA
declarations.doc:
**The punctured cone is the open `U`, over `X`**: the part of `L` lying over `U` maps to `X`
through the isomorphism of `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpecTruncation.isIso_toSpecA_restrict`
followed by the inclusion of `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem openUInL_ι_comp_toSpecA :
    (openUInL 𝒜).ι ≫ toSpecA 𝒜 =
      (toSpecA 𝒜 ∣_ ProjAndSpec.openU 𝒜) ≫ (ProjAndSpec.openU 𝒜).ι
declarations.comment: the part of L over U is U, over X

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpecTruncation.truncationConeData
declarations.doc:
The truncation algebra `B = ⨁_{d ≥ 0} A_{≥ d}` is cone data over `A`: the maps `ψ`,
`τ` and `σ` satisfy `τ ∘ ψ = id`, the two formulas tying `σ` to `ψ` and `τ`, and the three
divisibility conditions.
declarations.statement: def truncationConeData : ProjAndSpec.ConeData 𝒜 (grading 𝒜)
declarations.comment: the truncation algebra B = ⨁_{d ≥ 0} A_{≥ d} is cone data over A

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpecTruncation.openUInL_eq_iSup
declarations.doc:
The part of `L` lying over `U` is the union of the standard opens of the
`σ`-images of the positive-degree homogeneous elements of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem openUInL_eq_iSup :
    openUInL 𝒜 = ⨆ (d : ℕ) (_ : 0 < d) (f : 𝒜 d),
      Proj.basicOpen (grading 𝒜) ((sigma 𝒜 (f : A) : grading 𝒜 0) : TruncationRing 𝒜)
declarations.comment: U ⊆ L is a union of standard opens, for the truncation algebra

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpecTruncation.openUInL_inf_basicOpen
declarations.doc:
Over a standard open `D₊(f)` of `P` the part of `L` lying over `U` is the standard open
of `σ f · ψ f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem openUInL_inf_basicOpen (f : A) (d : ℕ) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) (hd : 0 < d) :
    openUInL 𝒜 ⊓ Proj.basicOpen (grading 𝒜) (psi 𝒜 f) =
      Proj.basicOpen (grading 𝒜)
        (((sigma 𝒜 f : grading 𝒜 0) : TruncationRing 𝒜) * psi 𝒜 f)
declarations.comment: U ⊆ L over a standard open, for the truncation algebra

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpecTruncation.toSpecA_preimage_specBasicOpen
declarations.doc:
The inverse image in `L` of a standard open of `X` is the standard open of
`σ f · ψ f`, a homogeneous element of positive degree, for `f` homogeneous of positive
degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem toSpecA_preimage_specBasicOpen (f : A) (d : ℕ) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) :
    toSpecA 𝒜 ⁻¹ᵁ ProjAndSpec.specBasicOpen f =
      Proj.basicOpen (grading 𝒜)
        (((sigma 𝒜 f : grading 𝒜 0) : TruncationRing 𝒜) * psi 𝒜 f)
declarations.comment: the inverse image in L of a standard open of X

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpecTruncation.isAffineOpen_toSpecA_preimage_specBasicOpen
declarations.doc:
The part of `L` lying over a standard open of `X` is affine, for `f` homogeneous of
positive degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineOpen_toSpecA_preimage_specBasicOpen (f : A) (d : ℕ) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d)
    (hd : 0 < d) : IsAffineOpen (toSpecA 𝒜 ⁻¹ᵁ ProjAndSpec.specBasicOpen f)
declarations.comment: the part of L over a standard open of X is affine

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.awayι_comp_pi
declarations.doc:
**On the affine chart `Spec B_{(ψ f)}` of `L` the cone projection is `Spec` of the map
`A_{(f)} ⟶ B_{(ψ f)}` of degree-zero localizations.** The chart of `L` is carried by the
inclusion of `D₊(ψ f)`, on which the cone projection is the local morphism attached to `f`, and
that local morphism is by construction the one of the degree-zero localizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem awayι_comp_pi :
    Proj.awayι ℬ (c.psi f) (c.psi.map_mem hf) hd ≫ pi c =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Away.map c.psi f)) ≫ Proj.awayι 𝒜 f hf hd
declarations.comment: the cone projection on an affine chart is Spec of the map of degree-zero localizations

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.awayToSection_comp_pi_appLE
declarations.doc:
**The cone projection acts on functions over a standard open by the map of degree-zero
localizations.** Through the identifications `A_{(f)} = Γ(P, D₊(f))` and
`B_{(ψ f)} = Γ(L, D₊(ψ f))` of [Stacks, Tag 01M6], the pullback of functions along `π` is
`HomogeneousLocalization.Away.map ψ f`. This is the module-theoretic content of the chart
description `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.awayι_comp_pi`: it says which
`A_{(f)}`-algebra the functions on the part of `L` over `D₊(f)` form.
declarations.statement:
theorem awayToSection_comp_pi_appLE :
    Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 f ≫ (pi c).appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f)
        (Proj.basicOpen ℬ (c.psi f)) (pi_preimage_basicOpen c f d hf hd).ge =
      CommRingCat.ofHom (Away.map c.psi f) ≫ Proj.awayToSection ℬ (c.psi f)
declarations.comment: the cone projection on functions over a standard open is the map of degree-zero localizations

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.awayToSection_comp_pi_appLE_sigmaMulPsi
declarations.doc:
**On the chart `D₊(σ f · ψ f)` of the punctured cone the projection acts on functions by the
map `A_{(f)} ⟶ B_{(σ f · ψ f)}` of degree-zero localizations.** Through the identifications
`A_{(f)} = Γ(P, D₊(f))` and `B_{(σ f · ψ f)} = Γ(L, D₊(σ f · ψ f))` of [Stacks, Tag 01M6], the
pullback of functions along `π` to the part of `U` over `D₊(f)` is `puncturedAwayMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem awayToSection_comp_pi_appLE_sigmaMulPsi (hd : 0 < d) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) :
    Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 f ≫ (pi c).appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f)
        (Proj.basicOpen ℬ ((c.sigma f : B) * c.psi f))
        (basicOpen_sigmaMulPsi_le_pi_preimage c hd hf) =
      CommRingCat.ofHom (puncturedAwayMap c hd hf) ≫
        Proj.awayToSection ℬ ((c.sigma f : B) * c.psi f)
declarations.comment: the punctured cone projection on functions over a standard open is the map of degree-zero localizations A_(f) to B_(sigma f * psi f)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAndSpec.awayToSection_comp_puncturedPi_appLE
declarations.doc:
