    [E.IsQuasicoherent] [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E]
    (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = ((2 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞))
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A]
    {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    {I : Ideal A} {r : ℕ} {fam : Fin r → A} {f : A} [IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) A]
    {proj : PrimeSpectrum A → X}
    (hin : ZeroSchemeAlgebraizationInput k X L s E 1 A M I fam f proj) :
    IsIso (zeroSchemeComparison X L s E 0)
declarations.comment: clause (2): on a Cohen-Macaulay (for example normal) surface, H^0(X,E) -> lim H^0(Y_n,E_n) is an isomorphism; the depth-dimension bound is proved from the Cohen-Macaulay condition and the dimension formula, hin bundles the three inputs of 0EL1

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_zeroSchemeComparison_of_cohenMacaulayThreefold
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EL3 (Example 52.28.3), clause (3).** In the situation of clause (2),
if `X` is a Cohen–Macaulay threefold then both

`H⁰(X, 𝓔) ⟶ lim H⁰(Yₙ, 𝓔ₙ)` and `H¹(X, 𝓔) ⟶ lim H¹(Yₙ, 𝓔ₙ)`

are isomorphisms.

This is the general pattern at `d = 3`, hence `σ = 2` and the two degrees `i = 0, 1`. The
source's closing remark that a *normal* threefold still gives `H⁰` is the general pattern at
`d = 2` applied to it: a normal local ring has depth at least `min(2, dim)`, so the bound `2`
holds although the dimension is three.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_zeroSchemeComparison_of_cohenMacaulayThreefold
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (fX : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [IsProperVariety k fX]
    {L : X.Modules} [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] {s : Γ(L, ⊤)} {E : X.Modules}
    [E.IsQuasicoherent] [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E]
    (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = ((3 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞))
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A]
    {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    {I : Ideal A} {r : ℕ} {fam : Fin r → A} {f : A} [IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) A]
    {proj : PrimeSpectrum A → X}
    (hin : ZeroSchemeAlgebraizationInput k X L s E 2 A M I fam f proj)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : i < 2) :
    IsIso (zeroSchemeComparison X L s E i)
declarations.comment: clause (3): on a Cohen-Macaulay threefold, H^i(X,E) -> lim H^i(Y_n,E_n) is an isomorphism for i = 0 and i = 1; the depth-dimension bound is proved from the Cohen-Macaulay condition and the dimension formula, hin bundles the three inputs of 0EL1

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_finite_graded_proIso_completion_of_canonicallyExtends
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EL4.** In the algebraization situation (Situation 0EHC) let `A` be
graded with irrelevant ideal `𝔞 = A₊` and `I` homogeneous, let `(ℱₙ)` be an object of
`Coh(U, I𝒪_U)` presented as `(M̃ₙ|_U)` by an inverse system `(Mₙ)` of graded `A`-modules, and
suppose `(ℱₙ)` extends canonically to `X = Spec(A)`. Then there is a finite graded `A`-module `N`
such that

* (a) the inverse systems `(N/IⁿN)` and `(Mₙ)` are pro-isomorphic in the category of graded
  `A`-modules modulo `A₊`-power torsion modules, and
* (b) `(ℱₙ)` is the completion of the coherent module associated to `N`.

The category of graded `A`-modules modulo `A₊`-power torsion modules is the localization of
`GradedModuleCat` at the maps with `A₊`-power torsion kernel and cokernel
(`GradedModuleCat.isoModTorsion`), and the pro-objects of the two inverse systems composed with
the localization functor are presented as colimits of representables, as in
`Stacks.ProObject.hasProLadder`. The systems are indexed from `0`: the term `n` of `(Mₙ)` and of
`(ℱₙ)` is the source's term `n + 1`, and the term `n` of the adic quotients is `N/Iⁿ⁺¹N`
(`GradedModuleCat.adicQuotients`). The coherent module associated to `N` is restricted to `U`
before completing, `(ℱₙ)` living on `U`.

The restriction maps `Mₙ → Γ(U, ℱₙ)` become isomorphisms in the quotient category, and
`(Γ(U, ℱₙ))` is linked to `(N/Iⁿ⁺¹N)` by a ladder of degree-preserving maps
(`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_finite_graded_ladder_of_canonicallyExtends`), which is a
pro-isomorphism of graded modules (`Stacks.ProObject.nonempty_colimitYonedaIso_of_hasProLadder`)
and stays one after localizing.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_graded_proIso_completion_of_canonicallyExtends
    (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u})
    {σ : Type v} [SetLike σ S.A] [AddSubgroupClass σ S.A] {𝒜 : ℕ → σ} [GradedRing 𝒜]
    (hirr : S.a = (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal) (hIhom : S.I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
    (M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ GradedModuleCat.{u, u, v} 𝒜)
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen S))
    (hpres : Nonempty (F.obj ≅ M ⋙ GradedModuleCat.toModuleCat 𝒜 ⋙ tilde.functor (.of S.A) ⋙
      Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor S.U.ι))
    (hext : CanonicallyExtends S F) :
    ∃ (N : GradedModuleCat.{u, u, v} 𝒜) (hN : Module.Finite S.A N.carrier),
      Nonempty (colimit ((GradedModuleCat.adicQuotients 𝒜 N S.I hIhom ⋙
          (GradedModuleCat.isoModTorsion 𝒜 (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal).Q).op ⋙
            yoneda) ≅
        colimit ((M ⋙
          (GradedModuleCat.isoModTorsion 𝒜 (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal).Q).op ⋙
            yoneda)) ∧
      Nonempty ((completionFunctor S.U.toScheme (idealOnOpen S)).obj
          (restrictCoherentModules S.U.ι
            (tildeCoherentModule S (ModuleCat.of S.A N.carrier) hN)) ≅ F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_finite_graded_algebraization
declarations.doc:
In the algebraization situation of a graded ring `A` whose irrelevant ideal is `𝔞` and whose
ideal `I` is homogeneous, let `(Mₙ)` be the inverse system of graded modules presenting a coherent
formal module on `U`, let `(Nₙ)` be the graded inverse system attached to its canonical extension,
and let `(Mₙ) → (Nₙ)` be a degree-preserving comparison with `𝔞`-power torsion kernel and cokernel.
Then there is a finite graded `A`-module `N` with `N/IⁿN ≃ Nₙ` compatibly with the transition maps,
and `(Mₙ)` maps to the inverse system `(N/IⁿN)` by degree-preserving maps with `𝔞`-power torsion
kernel and cokernel.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_graded_algebraization (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u})
    {σ : Type v} [SetLike σ S.A] [AddSubmonoidClass σ S.A] {𝒜 : ℕ → σ} [GradedRing 𝒜]
    (hirr : S.a = (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal) (hIhom : S.I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
    {M : ℕ → Type w} [∀ n, AddCommGroup (M n)] [∀ n, Module S.A (M n)]
    (ℳ : ∀ n, ℤ → AddSubgroup (M n)) [∀ n, DirectSum.Decomposition (ℳ n)]
    (s : ∀ n, M (n + 1) →ₗ[S.A] M n)
    {N : ℕ → Type w} [∀ n, AddCommGroup (N n)] [∀ n, Module S.A (N n)]
    [∀ n, Module.Finite S.A (N n)]
    (𝒩 : ∀ n, ℤ → AddSubgroup (N n)) [∀ n, DirectSum.Decomposition (𝒩 n)]
    (h𝒩 : ∀ (n i : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (a : S.A) (x : N n), a ∈ 𝒜 i → x ∈ 𝒩 n d → a • x ∈ 𝒩 n (i + d))
    (t : ∀ n, N (n + 1) →ₗ[S.A] N n)
    (ht : ∀ (n : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (x : N (n + 1)), x ∈ 𝒩 (n + 1) d → t n x ∈ 𝒩 n d)
    (htsurj : ∀ n, Function.Surjective (t n))
    (htker : ∀ n, LinearMap.ker (t n) = S.I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule S.A (N (n + 1))))
    (c : ∀ n, M n →ₗ[S.A] N n)
    (hc : ∀ (n : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (x : M n), x ∈ ℳ n d → c n x ∈ 𝒩 n d)
    (hcs : ∀ n, (t n).comp (c (n + 1)) = (c n).comp (s n))
    (hcker : ∀ n, IsIPowerTorsion S.A (LinearMap.ker (c n)) S.a)
    (hccoker : ∀ n, IsIPowerTorsion S.A (N n ⧸ LinearMap.range (c n)) S.a) :
    ∃ (P : Type w) (_ : AddCommGroup P) (_ : Module S.A P) (𝒬 : ℤ → AddSubgroup P)
        (_ : DirectSum.Decomposition 𝒬)
        (e : ∀ n, (P ⧸ S.I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule S.A P)) ≃ₗ[S.A] N n)
        (g : ∀ n, M n →ₗ[S.A] P ⧸ S.I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule S.A P)),
      Module.Finite S.A P ∧
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (a : S.A) (x : P), a ∈ 𝒜 i → x ∈ 𝒬 d → a • x ∈ 𝒬 (i + d)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (x : P), x ∈ 𝒬 d → e n (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) ∈ 𝒩 n d) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : P),
        t n (e (n + 1) (Submodule.Quotient.mk x)) = e n (Submodule.Quotient.mk x)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : M n), e n (g n x) = c n x) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (d : ℤ) (x : M n), x ∈ ℳ n d →
        ∃ p ∈ 𝒬 d, g n x = Submodule.Quotient.mk p) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : M (n + 1)) (p : P), g (n + 1) x = Submodule.Quotient.mk p →
        g n (s n x) = Submodule.Quotient.mk p) ∧
      (∀ n, IsIPowerTorsion S.A (LinearMap.ker (g n)) S.a) ∧
      (∀ n, IsIPowerTorsion S.A
        ((P ⧸ S.I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule S.A P)) ⧸ LinearMap.range (g n)) S.a)
declarations.comment: (a) and (b); graded Gm-descent (0EKL) and the 0BK0 comparison hypothesised

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.satisfiesDepthInequalities_one_two_iff
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0EHC let `(ℱ_n)` be an object of `Coh(U, I𝒪_U)` and assume `cd(A, I) = 1`.
Then `(ℱ_n)` satisfies the `(1, 2)`-inequalities if and only if

`depth((ℱ_y^∧)_𝔭) + dim(𝒪_{X,y}^∧/𝔭) + δ^Y_Z(y) > 2`

for every `y ∈ U ∩ Y` and every prime `𝔭 ⊆ 𝒪_{X,y}^∧` with `𝔭 ∉ V(I𝒪_{X,y}^∧)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem satisfiesDepthInequalities_one_two_iff (S : AlgebraizationSituation.{u})
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (idealOnOpen S))
    (hcd : Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologicalDimension S.A S.I
      (IsNoetherian.noetherian S.I) = 1) :
    SatisfiesDepthInequalities S F 1 2 ↔
      ∀ (y : S.U.toScheme) (z : S.Y), S.U.ι.base y = S.Yι.base z →
        ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (completedLocalRing (idealOnOpen S) y),
          ¬ completedLocalIdeal (idealOnOpen S) y ≤ p.asIdeal →
          depthAddDimAddDistance S F y z p > ((2 : ℤ) : EInt)
declarations.comment: only the opening step, as an equivalence: the depth hypothesis is the (1, 2)-inequalities, this library's encoding of conditions (b), (c), (d) of 0EJF at d = 1; in the affine Situation 0EHC, with the distance function for dim(closure q) and with cd(A, I) = 1 hypothesised; the conclusion that the system is a completion is not proved

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isCompletionOfCoherent_of_two_lt_depth_add_dim
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, `P` a proper scheme over `k`, `𝓛` an ample invertible `𝒪_P`-module,
`s ∈ Γ(P, 𝓛)` and `𝓘` the ideal of the zero scheme `Q = Z(s)`. Let `(𝓕ₙ)` be an object of
`Coh(P, 𝓘)` such that for all `q ∈ Q` and all primes `𝔭` of `𝒪_{P,q}^∧` not containing `𝓘_q^∧`,
`depth((𝓕_q^∧)_𝔭) + dim(𝒪_{P,q}^∧/𝔭) + dim({q}‾) > 2`.
Then `(𝓕ₙ)` is the completion of a coherent `𝒪_P`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompletionOfCoherent_of_two_lt_depth_add_dim
    (F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (zeroScheme P L s))
    (hdepth : ∀ q ∈ (zeroScheme P L s).support,
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum (completedLocalRing (zeroScheme P L s) q),
        ¬ completedLocalIdeal (zeroScheme P L s) q ≤ p.asIdeal →
        (2 : EInt) < enatToEInt (completedStalkDepth (zeroScheme P L s) F q p) +
          krullDimToEInt (ringKrullDim (completedLocalRing (zeroScheme P L s) q ⧸ p.asIdeal)) +
          krullDimToEInt (dimClosureAt P q)) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian P := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian fP
    IsCompletionOfCoherent (zeroScheme P L s) F

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.not_two_lt_completedStalkDepth_of_dim_le_two
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a proper variety over a field with an effective Cartier divisor `Y` whose sheaf
`𝒪_X(Y)` is ample, and let `(𝓔ₙ)` be an object of `Coh(X, 𝓘)` whose terms are finite locally free
over the infinitesimal neighbourhoods. If `X` is a curve or a surface, the hypothesis

`depth((𝓔_q^∧)_𝔭) + dim(𝒪_{X,q}^∧/𝔭) + dim({q}‾) > 2`

of Stacks 0EL5 fails at every point `q` of `Y` where the completed stalk is nonzero and every
prime `𝔭` of `𝒪_{X,q}^∧`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_two_lt_completedStalkDepth_of_dim_le_two (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProperVariety k f] (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor Y]
    (_hample : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf Y))
    (E : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems Y) (hfree : IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic Y E)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ ((2 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞))
    {q : X} (hq : q ∈ Y.support) [Nontrivial (completedStalk Y E q)]
    (p : PrimeSpectrum (completedLocalRing Y q)) :
    ¬ (2 : EInt) < enatToEInt (completedStalkDepth Y E q p) +
      krullDimToEInt (ringKrullDim (completedLocalRing Y q ⧸ p.asIdeal)) +
      krullDimToEInt (dimClosureAt X q)
declarations.comment: clause (1): for a curve or a surface the inequality of 0EL5 fails at every point of Y with nonzero completed stalk and every prime off the completed ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_completion_iso_of_hasPropertySk_three
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a proper variety over a field `k`, `Y ⊂ X` an effective Cartier divisor such that
`𝒪_X(Y)` is ample, with ideal sheaf `𝓘`, and `(𝓔ₙ)` an object of `Coh(X, 𝓘)` whose terms are
finite locally free over the infinitesimal neighbourhoods. If `dim(X) ≥ 3` and `X` is `(S₃)`, then
`(𝓔ₙ)` is the completion of a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓔`, and `𝓔` is finite locally free on an
open neighbourhood of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_completion_iso_of_hasPropertySk_three (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProperVariety k f] (Y : X.IdealSheafData) [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor Y]
    (hample : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf Y))
    (E : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems Y) (hfree : IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic Y E)
    (hdim : ((3 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim X) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    HasPropertySk X 3 →
      ∃ G : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
        Nonempty (((completionFunctor X Y).obj G).obj ≅ E.obj) ∧
          ∃ V : X.Opens, (Y.support : Set X) ⊆ (V : Set X) ∧
            AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree
              (Scheme.Modules.restrict (show X.Modules from G.obj) V.ι)
declarations.comment: clause (3) with the closing remark: dim X >= 3 and X is (S_3); the freeness of E_n is read over the infinitesimal neighbourhoods Y_n

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_completion_iso_of_isCohenMacaulay_of_dim_eq_three
declarations.doc:
In the situation of `exists_completion_iso_of_hasPropertySk_three`, if `X` is a Cohen–Macaulay
threefold then `(𝓔ₙ)` is the completion of a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓔`, finite locally free on an
open neighbourhood of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_completion_iso_of_isCohenMacaulay_of_dim_eq_three (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProperVariety k f] (Y : X.IdealSheafData) [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor Y]
    (hample : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf Y))
    (E : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems Y) (hfree : IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic Y E)
    (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = ((3 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    ∃ G : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
      Nonempty (((completionFunctor X Y).obj G).obj ≅ E.obj) ∧
        ∃ V : X.Opens, (Y.support : Set X) ⊆ (V : Set X) ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree
            (Scheme.Modules.restrict (show X.Modules from G.obj) V.ι)
declarations.comment: clause (2) with the closing remark: X a Cohen-Macaulay threefold; the freeness of E_n is read over the infinitesimal neighbourhoods Y_n

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isCompletionOfCoherent_of_hasPropertySk_three
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EL6, clause (3).** Let `X` be a proper variety over a field with an
effective Cartier divisor `Y` whose sheaf `𝒪_X(Y)` is ample, and let `(𝓔ₙ)` be an object of
`Coh(X, 𝓘)` whose terms are finite locally free over the infinitesimal neighbourhoods. If
`dim(X) ≥ 3` and `X` satisfies `(S₃)`, then `(𝓔ₙ)` is the completion of a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCompletionOfCoherent_of_hasPropertySk_three (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProperVariety k f] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor Y]
    (_hample : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf Y))
    (E : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems Y)
    (_hfree : IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic Y E)
    (hdim : ((3 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim X) (hS₃ : HasPropertySk X 3)
    (hform : ∀ x : X,
      ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) + dimClosureAt X x = topologicalKrullDim X)
    (halgebraize : (∀ x : X, x ∉ Y.support →
        ((2 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) < localDepthAddDimClosure X x) → IsCompletionOfCoherent Y E) :
    IsCompletionOfCoherent Y E
declarations.comment: clause (3): dim X >= 3 and (S_3); the freeness of E_n is corrected to be read over Y_n, since over O_X it would force E_n = 0; 0EL5's conclusion and 0A21 hypothesised

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isCompletionOfCoherent_of_isCohenMacaulay_threefold
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EL6, clause (2).** In the situation of clause (3), a Cohen–Macaulay
threefold satisfies `(S₃)` and has dimension `3`, so `(𝓔ₙ)` is again the completion of a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCompletionOfCoherent_of_isCohenMacaulay_threefold (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProperVariety k f] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor Y]
    (_hample : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf Y))
    (E : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems Y)
    (_hfree : IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic Y E)
    (hCM : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = ((3 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hform : ∀ x : X,
      ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) + dimClosureAt X x = topologicalKrullDim X)
    (halgebraize : (∀ x : X, x ∉ Y.support →
        ((2 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) < localDepthAddDimClosure X x) → IsCompletionOfCoherent Y E) :
    IsCompletionOfCoherent Y E
declarations.comment: clause (2): a Cohen-Macaulay threefold; the freeness of E_n is corrected to be read over Y_n, since over O_X it would force E_n = 0; 0EL5 and 0A21 hypothesised

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_neighbourhood_of_isCompletionOfCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EL6, the closing remark.** If the object `(𝓔ₙ)` is the completion of a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓔`, then `𝓔` is finite locally free on an open neighbourhood of `Y`.

At a point `y` of `Y` the terms of the system identify the adic quotients
`𝓔_y / 𝓘_y ^ (n + 1) 𝓔_y` with the stalks of finite locally free modules on the infinitesimal
neighbourhoods, hence make them free over `𝒪_{X,y} / 𝓘_y ^ (n + 1)`
(`Stacks.Algebraization.free_quotient_stalk_of_pushforward_iso`); a module with a free tower of
adic quotients over a Noetherian local ring is free
(`Stacks.FreeOfAdicQuotients.free_of_forall_free_quotient_pow_smul_top`), so `𝓔_y` is a finite
free `𝒪_{X,y}`-module. Stacks 0B8J spreads a free stalk to a free neighbourhood, and those
neighbourhoods cover a neighbourhood of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_neighbourhood_of_isCompletionOfCoherent
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProperVariety k f] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor Y]
    (_hample : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X (Stacks.Divisors.divisorSheaf Y))
    (E : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems Y)
    (hfree : IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic Y E)
    (G : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    (hcompletion : Nonempty (((completionFunctor X Y).obj G).obj ≅ E.obj)) :
    ∃ V : X.Opens, (Y.support : Set X) ⊆ (V : Set X) ∧ ∀ x : X, x ∈ V →
      ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : x ∈ U) (_ : U ≤ V) (ρ : Type u) (_ : Finite ρ),
        Nonempty (Scheme.Modules.restrict G.obj U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.free.{u} ρ)
declarations.comment: closing remark: such an E is finite locally free near Y

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isCompletionEquivalence_of_two_lt_depth_add_dimClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EL7.** Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field, `𝓛` an ample invertible
`𝒪_X`-module, `s ∈ Γ(X, 𝓛)` and `Y = Z(s)` with sheaf of ideals `𝓘`. If
`depth(𝒪_{X,x}) + dim({x}‾) > 2` at every point off `Y`, then completion along `𝓘` is fully
faithful on finite locally free coherent modules, and every finite locally free object of
`Coh(X, 𝓘)` is the completion of a coherent module finite locally free near `Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCompletionEquivalence_of_two_lt_depth_add_dimClosure (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (L : X.Modules)
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] (_hample : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L) (s : Γ(L, ⊤))
    (hdepth : ∀ x : X, x ∉ ((zeroScheme X L s).support : Set X) →
      ((2 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) < localDepthAddDimClosure X x)
    (hff : CompletionFullyFaithfulOnFiniteLocallyFree X (zeroScheme X L s))
    (halgebraize : ∀ F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (zeroScheme X L s),
      (∀ n : ℕ, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (F.obj.obj (op n))) →
      (∀ x : X, x ∉ ((zeroScheme X L s).support : Set X) →
        ((2 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) < localDepthAddDimClosure X x) →
      ∃ G : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf,
        Nonempty (((completionFunctor X (zeroScheme X L s)).obj G).obj ≅ F.obj) ∧
          ∀ y ∈ ((zeroScheme X L s).support : Set X),
            ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : y ∈ U) (ρ : Type u) (_ : Finite ρ),
              Nonempty (Scheme.Modules.restrict G.obj U.ι ≅ SheafOfModules.free.{u} ρ)) :
    IsCompletionEquivalenceOnFiniteLocallyFree X (zeroScheme X L s)
declarations.comment: essential surjectivity up to V; full faithfulness over X; 0EL5, 0EL2 assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.completionEquivalence_finiteLocallyFree_of_two_lt_depth_add_dimClosure
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper scheme over `k`, `𝓛` an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module,
`s ∈ Γ(X, 𝓛)`, `Y = Z(s)` its zero scheme with sheaf of ideals `𝓘`, and `𝒱` the open subschemes
of `X` containing `Y`. Assume `depth(𝒪_{X,x}) + dim({x}‾) > 2` for all `x ∈ X ∖ Y`. Then the
completion functor `colim_𝒱 Coh(𝒪_V) ⟶ Coh(X, 𝓘)` is an equivalence on the full subcategories of
finite locally free objects: it lands in the finite locally free objects, it is fully faithful on
finite locally free objects, and every finite locally free object of `Coh(X, 𝓘)` is the
completion of a finite locally free coherent module on some `V ∈ 𝒱`. See the module documentation
for how each half is written.
declarations.statement:
public theorem completionEquivalence_finiteLocallyFree_of_two_lt_depth_add_dimClosure
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (L : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : Stacks.Ample.IsAmple X L)
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤))
    (hdepth : ∀ x : X, x ∉ ((zeroScheme X L s).support : Set X) →
      ((2 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) < localDepthAddDimClosure X x) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    (∀ (V : X.Opens), ((zeroScheme X L s).support : Set X) ⊆ (V : Set X) →
        ∀ G : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf,
          AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree G.obj →
          IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic ((zeroScheme X L s).comap V.ι)
            ((completionFunctor V.toScheme ((zeroScheme X L s).comap V.ι)).obj G)) ∧
      NeighbourhoodCompletion.CompletionFullyFaithfulComplete (zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι ∧
      (∀ F : Stacks.Coherent.CoherentAdicSystems (zeroScheme X L s),
        IsFiniteLocallyFreeAdic (zeroScheme X L s) F →
        ∃ (V : X.Opens) (_ : ((zeroScheme X L s).support : Set X) ⊆ (V : Set X))
          (G : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf),
          AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree
              (restrictCoherentModules V.ι G).obj ∧
            Nonempty (((completionFunctor X (zeroScheme X L s)).obj G).obj ≅ F.obj) ∧
            Nonempty (((completionFunctor V.toScheme ((zeroScheme X L s).comap V.ι)).obj
                (restrictCoherentModules V.ι G)).obj ≅
              F.obj ⋙ Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι))

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_completionFullyFaithfulOnFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and `Y ⊆ X` a closed subscheme with ideal sheaf `I`. If the
completion functor `Coh(𝒪_X) ⟶ Coh(X, I)` is fully faithful on the full subcategory of finite
locally free objects, then the restriction functor `FÉt_X ⟶ FÉt_Y` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_completionFullyFaithfulOnFiniteLocallyFree
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsNoetherian X] [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hcompletion : Stacks.Algebraization.CompletionFullyFaithfulOnFiniteLocallyFree X i.ker) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange i).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: proved from full faithfulness of completion on the finite locally free coherent modules alone

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_of_completionEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EL9].** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and `Y ⊆ X` a closed subscheme with
ideal sheaf `I`. If the completion functor `Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ Coh(X, I)`, `ℱ ↦ ℱ^∧`, is an equivalence
on the full subcategories of finite locally free objects, then the restriction functor
`FÉt_X ⥤ FÉt_Y`, `U ↦ U ×_X Y`, is an equivalence.

The closed subscheme is given by a closed immersion `i : Y ⟶ X` with ideal sheaf `I = ker i`.
Restriction factors as restriction to the closed subscheme cut out by `I` followed by base change
along the isomorphism from `Y` onto it, and the second is an equivalence because an isomorphism is
a thickening ([Stacks, Tag 0BQB]); the first is
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_of_completion`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteEtaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_of_completionEquivalence
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsNoetherian X] [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [(finiteLocallyFreeCompletion X i.ker).IsEquivalence] :
    (AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleBaseChange i).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: completion an equivalence on finite locally free objects implies restriction FEt_X to FEt_Y an equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.finiteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful_of_sectionsExtendNearSubscheme
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ELA], granted the section-extension input.** Let `X` be a scheme, let
`Y ⊆ X` be the closed subscheme cut out by the ideal sheaf `Y`, and let `𝒱` be the open
subschemes of `X` containing it, ordered by reverse inclusion. If sections of a finite étale
cover of a neighbourhood extend to a smaller neighbourhood and are determined there after
further shrinking, then the restriction functor `colim_𝒱 FÉt_V ⟶ FÉt_Y` is fully faithful.

This is the first paragraph of the source's proof, which is the only part of it that is about
finite étale covers: the category of finite étale coverings has an internal hom
([Stacks, Tag 0BL7]), and a section of the internal hom `Hom_V(A, B)` over a base is exactly a
morphism `A ⟶ B` after that base change, so a morphism between the restrictions to the closed
subscheme is a section of the internal hom over the closed subscheme and full faithfulness over
the colimit is the extension property for sections of one finite étale cover.

**What is granted and what is not.** The hypothesis of the tag — full faithfulness of the
completion functor `colim_𝒱 Coh(𝒪_V) ⟶ Coh(X, I)` on the finite locally free objects — is
**not** used here at all: the section-extension property
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.SectionsExtendNearSubscheme` is assumed in its place. That property is
the shrinking form of the conclusion of [Stacks, Tag 0EL8], and deducing it from the completion
hypothesis is the rest of the source's proof: lift the section over the closed subscheme to the
infinitesimal neighbourhoods ([Stacks, Tag 0BQB]), algebraize the resulting compatible system of
module maps out of the finite locally free module `f _* 𝒪_U` over some smaller neighbourhood by
fullness of completion, and shrink once more to make the algebraized map multiplicative by
faithfulness of completion. That half is carried in this library only in its non-shrinking form,
on the nose at a single scheme, as
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_completionFullyFaithful`; the
shrinking form would need the restriction of a direct image algebra to an open subscheme and the
comparison of the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the closed subscheme taken inside `X` and
inside a neighbourhood, neither of which has a carrier here.

It is **not** enough to assume the pointwise analogue of the hypothesis at each individual
neighbourhood, which would make the statement a formal consequence of Tag 0EL8 applied one
neighbourhood at a time. The quantifiers over smaller neighbourhoods in both
`SectionsExtendNearSubscheme` and `FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful` are the content.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful_of_sectionsExtendNearSubscheme
    (h : SectionsExtendNearSubscheme X Y) : FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful X Y
declarations.comment: granted SectionsExtendNearSubscheme: the shrinking form of Tag 0EL8

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.finiteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful_of_completionFullyFaithfulComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ELA].** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and let `Y ⊆ X` be a closed subscheme
with ideal sheaf `I`. Let `𝒱` be the set of open subschemes `V ⊆ X` containing `Y`, ordered by
reverse inclusion. Assume the completion functor `colim_𝒱 Coh(𝒪_V) ⟶ Coh(X, I)`, `ℱ ↦ ℱ^∧`, is
fully faithful on the full subcategory of finite locally free objects. Then the restriction
functor `colim_𝒱 FÉt_V ⟶ FÉt_Y` is fully faithful.

The hypothesis is condition (4) of [Stacks, Tag 0EK2],
`Stacks.Algebraization.NeighbourhoodCompletion.CompletionFullyFaithfulComplete`, at the closed
immersion of `Y`; the conclusion is `Stacks.FundamentalGroup.FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful`,
full faithfulness spelled through the directed-colimit description of the hom sets of
`colim_𝒱 FÉt_V`. The proof is the source's: the internal hom reduces the statement to the
extension of sections of one finite étale cover
(`finiteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful_of_sectionsExtendNearSubscheme`), and that extension is
`sectionsExtendNearSubscheme_of_completionFullyFaithfulComplete`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful_of_completionFullyFaithfulComplete [IsNoetherian X]
    (h : NeighbourhoodCompletion.CompletionFullyFaithfulComplete Y.subschemeι) :
    FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful X Y
declarations.comment: proved from full faithfulness of completion on the finite locally free objects of the neighbourhood colimit, the tag's own hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_depthAddDim
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ELC], first statement.** Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper scheme over `k`,
`L` an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module, `s ∈ Γ(X, L)` and `Y = Z(s)` the zero scheme of `s`. If
`depth(𝒪_{X, x}) + dim({x}‾) > 1` at every point `x` of `X` outside `Y`, then the restriction
functor `FÉt_X ⟶ FÉt_Y` is fully faithful.

The statement is that of
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_isProper`, and
**nothing is carried here**: the source's appeal to
Algebraic and Formal Geometry, Proposition [Stacks, Tag 0EL1] is
`Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_zeroSchemeComparison_of_isProper`, and the route from there to full
faithfulness runs through conditions (2) and (4) of [Stacks, Tag 0EKP] rather than through
[Stacks, Tag 0EJZ]; see the module documentation for the chain. This is the full faithfulness that
the source uses in [Stacks, Tag 0ELE].

`CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful` carries the inverse map on hom sets as data, so full
faithfulness is recorded as `Nonempty _.FullyFaithful`. `X` is
Noetherian by `Stacks.FundamentalGroup.isNoetherian_of_isProper_of_isAmple`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_depthAddDim
    (hdepth : DepthAddDimGtOneOutsideSupport X (zeroScheme X L s)) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange (zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: first statement: restriction FÉt_X → FÉt_Y to the zero scheme of a section of an ample invertible module is fully faithful. Nothing is carried: Stacks 0EL1 is isIso_zeroSchemeComparison_of_isProper, and the passage from it to full faithfulness is the formalized Stacks 0EKP chain followed by Stacks 0EL8

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ELC], first statement.** Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper scheme over `k`,
`L` an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module, `s ∈ Γ(X, L)` and `Y = Z(s)` the zero scheme of `s`. If
`depth(𝒪_{X, x}) + dim({x}‾) > 1` at every point `x` of `X ∖ Y`, then the restriction functor
`FÉt_X ⟶ FÉt_Y` is fully faithful.

`CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful` carries the inverse map on hom sets as data, so full
faithfulness is stated as `Nonempty _.FullyFaithful`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_isProper
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper g]
    (L : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L) (s : Γ(L, ⊤))
    (hdepth : DepthAddDimGtOneOutsideSupport X (zeroScheme X L s)) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange (zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: first statement: restriction FÉt_X → FÉt_Y to the zero scheme of a section of an ample invertible module on a proper scheme over a field is fully faithful when depth + dim > 1 off the zero scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_neighborhood_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ELC], second statement.** In the situation of
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_isProper`, the
restriction functor `FÉt_V ⟶ FÉt_Y` is fully faithful for every open subscheme `V ⊆ X`
containing `Y`.

The open subschemes containing `Y` are `Stacks.FundamentalGroup.Neighborhood X Y`, and the
closed immersion `Y ⟶ V` is `Stacks.FundamentalGroup.Neighborhood.toSchemeHom`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_neighborhood_of_isProper
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper g]
    (L : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L) (s : Γ(L, ⊤))
    (hdepth : DepthAddDimGtOneOutsideSupport X (zeroScheme X L s))
    (W : Neighborhood X (zeroScheme X L s)) :
    Nonempty (finiteEtaleBaseChange
      (Neighborhood.toSchemeHom X (zeroScheme X L s) W)).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: second statement: restriction FÉt_V → FÉt_Y is fully faithful for every open V of X containing the zero scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.finiteEtaleColimitEquivalence_zeroScheme_of_depth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ELD.** Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper scheme over `k`, `L` an ample
invertible `𝒪_X`-module, `s ∈ Γ(X, L)`, `Y = Z(s)` the zero scheme of `s`, and `𝒱` the open
subschemes of `X` containing `Y`, ordered by reverse inclusion. If
`depth(𝒪_{X, x}) + dim({x}‾) > 2` for every `x ∈ X ∖ Y`, then the restriction functor
`colim_𝒱 FÉt_V ⟶ FÉt_Y` is an equivalence.

The equivalence `colim_𝒱 FÉt_V ≃ FÉt_Y` is stated as its two halves: the restriction functor is
fully faithful (`FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful X Y`: morphisms of restrictions to `Y` come from
morphisms over a smaller neighbourhood, and morphisms with equal restrictions to `Y` agree over a
smaller neighbourhood), and essentially surjective (every finite étale cover of `Y` is the
restriction of a finite étale cover of some open neighbourhood of `Y`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteEtaleColimitEquivalence_zeroScheme_of_depth
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper g]
    (L : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L) (s : Γ(L, ⊤))
    (hdepth : DepthAddDimGtTwoOutsideSupport X (zeroScheme X L s)) :
    FiniteEtaleColimitFullyFaithful X (zeroScheme X L s) ∧
      ∀ A : FiniteEtaleOver (zeroScheme X L s).subscheme,
        ∃ (W : Neighborhood X (zeroScheme X L s))
          (U : FiniteEtaleOver (Neighborhood.open X (zeroScheme X L s) W).toScheme),
          Nonempty ((finiteEtaleBaseChange
            (Neighborhood.toSchemeHom X (zeroScheme X L s) W)).obj U ≅ A)
declarations.comment: the restriction functor colim_V FÉt_V → FÉt_Y is an equivalence, stated as its fully faithful half and its essentially surjective half, at exactly the source's hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_hasPurity_of_depth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ELE], the first conclusion.** Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper scheme over
`k`, `L` an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module, `s ∈ Γ(X, L)` and `Y = Z(s)` the zero scheme of `s`.
Assume that `depth(𝒪_{X, x}) + dim({x}‾) > 2` for every `x ∈ X ∖ Y`, and that purity holds for
`𝒪_{X, x}` at every closed `x ∈ X ∖ Y`. Then the restriction functor `FÉt_X ⟶ FÉt_Y` is an
equivalence.

The proof is the source's. Full faithfulness is
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fullyFaithful_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_depthAddDim`
([Stacks, Tag 0ELC]), whose bound `> 1` follows from the bound `> 2` assumed here. For essential
surjectivity, [Stacks, Tag 0ELD] writes a given finite étale cover of `Y` as the restriction of a
finite étale cover of an open neighbourhood `V` of `Y`; every point of `X ∖ V` is a closed point
off `Y`, because its closure misses `Y` and so lies in the affine open where `s` does not vanish,
and purity therefore holds there, so [Stacks, Tag 0EY7] extends the cover from `V` to all of `X`.

The depth hypothesis is `Stacks.FundamentalGroup.DepthAddDimGtTwoOutsideSupport`, which unfolds
to the displayed inequality in the extended integers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_hasPurity_of_depth
    (hdepth : DepthAddDimGtTwoOutsideSupport X (zeroScheme X L s))
    (hpurity : ∀ x : X, x ∉ ((zeroScheme X L s).support : Set X) → IsClosed ({x} : Set X) →
      AlgebraicGeometry.HasPurity (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange (zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: first conclusion: restriction FÉt_X → FÉt_Y to the zero scheme of a section of an ample invertible module is an equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.connectedSpace_zeroScheme_iff_of_hasPurity_of_depth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ELE], the "or equivalently".** In the situation of
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_hasPurity_of_depth` the
zero scheme `Y = Z(s)` is connected exactly when `X` is. This is [Stacks, Tag 0BQA] part (2)
applied to the equivalence `FÉt_X ⟶ FÉt_Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem connectedSpace_zeroScheme_iff_of_hasPurity_of_depth
    (hdepth : DepthAddDimGtTwoOutsideSupport X (zeroScheme X L s))
    (hpurity : ∀ x : X, x ∉ ((zeroScheme X L s).support : Set X) → IsClosed ({x} : Set X) →
      AlgebraicGeometry.HasPurity (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ConnectedSpace (zeroScheme X L s).subscheme ↔ ConnectedSpace X
declarations.comment: the "or equivalently": X is connected if and only if its zero scheme Y = Z(s) is

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupEquiv_zeroScheme_of_hasPurity_of_depth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ELE], the second conclusion.** In the situation of
`Stacks.FundamentalGroup.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_zeroScheme_of_hasPurity_of_depth`,
with `X` and `Y = Z(s)` connected, the map `π₁(Y, y‾) ⟶ π₁(X, y‾)` induced by the closed immersion
is an isomorphism of topological groups for every geometric point `y‾` of `Y`. The isomorphism
produced is the canonical induced map `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap`. This is
[Stacks, Tag 0BQA] part (2), the lemma the source's proof quotes for the `π₁` statement.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fundamentalGroupEquiv_zeroScheme_of_hasPurity_of_depth
    (hdepth : DepthAddDimGtTwoOutsideSupport X (zeroScheme X L s))
    (hpurity : ∀ x : X, x ∉ ((zeroScheme X L s).support : Set X) → IsClosed ({x} : Set X) →
      AlgebraicGeometry.HasPurity (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    [ConnectedSpace (zeroScheme X L s).subscheme] [ConnectedSpace X]
    (y : AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricPoint (zeroScheme X L s).subscheme) :
    ∃ e : AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFundamentalGroup (zeroScheme X L s).subscheme y ≃ₜ*
        AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFundamentalGroup X (y.map (zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι),
      ∀ σ : AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFundamentalGroup (zeroScheme X L s).subscheme y,
        e σ = AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap
          (zeroScheme X L s).subschemeι y σ
declarations.comment: second conclusion: for X, equivalently Y, connected, the induced map π₁(Y, y‾) → π₁(X, y‾) is an isomorphism of topological groups at every geometric point of Y

registrations.name: IsContainedInJacobson
registrations.comment:
A Zariski pair is a pair `(A, I)` with `I` contained in the Jacobson radical
of `A`; the ambient ring is determined by the type of the ideal.

declarations.name: bijective_algebraMap_of_bijective_quotientMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ELZ.** Let `(A, I)` be a Zariski pair and let `B` be a flat, integral,
finitely presented `A`-algebra. If the canonical map `A ⧸ I → B ⧸ IB` is an isomorphism,
then `A → B` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_algebraMap_of_bijective_quotientMap
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.IsIntegral A B] [Algebra.FinitePresentation A B]
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : IsContainedInJacobson I)
    (hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap A B)) (algebraMap A B) Ideal.le_comap_map)) :
    Function.Bijective (algebraMap A B)

declarations.name: exists_monic_isRoot_map_eq_X_sub_one_mul_X_pow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EM0.** Let `(A, I)` be a Zariski pair and `B` a finite `A`-algebra. If
`B / IB` decomposes as a product of `A / I`-algebras, the first factor is generated by the
image of `A / I`, and `b` maps to `(1, 0)`, then `b` is annihilated by a monic polynomial
whose reduction is `(X - 1) X ^ d` for some `d ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_monic_isRoot_map_eq_X_sub_one_mul_X_pow
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Module.Finite A B]
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : IsContainedInJacobson I)
    (B₁ : Type w) (B₂ : Type x) [CommRing B₁] [CommRing B₂]
    [Algebra (A ⧸ I) B₁] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) B₂]
    (e : (B ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A B)) ≃ₐ[A ⧸ I] (B₁ × B₂))
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap (A ⧸ I) B₁))
    (b : B)
    (hb : e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A B)) b) = (1, 0)) :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (f : A[X]), 1 ≤ d ∧ f.Monic ∧
      (f.map (algebraMap A B)).IsRoot b ∧
      f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) =
        ((Polynomial.X : (A ⧸ I)[X]) - 1) * Polynomial.X ^ d

declarations.name: exists_quotient_algEquiv_prod_of_etale_section
declarations.doc:
Let `A'` be an étale `A`-algebra and let `A' → A/I` be an `A`-algebra map. Then `A'/IA'` is
isomorphic, as an `A/I`-algebra, to a product `A/I × C`. Under this isomorphism, the map to the
first factor is the map induced by the given section.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quotient_algEquiv_prod_of_etale_section
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (A' : Type v) [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A']
    [Algebra.Etale A A'] (I : Ideal A) (retraction : A' →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I) :
    ∃ (C : Type v) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra (A ⧸ I) C)
      (e : (A' ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A A')) ≃ₐ[A ⧸ I] ((A ⧸ I) × C)),
      ∀ x : A', (e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A A')) x)).1 = retraction x

declarations.name: exists_integral_factor_decomposition_of_gabber_root_condition
declarations.doc:
Under Gabber's Jacobson-radical and root-lifting conditions, a section modulo `I` of an
étale `A`-algebra comes from a product decomposition whose first factor is integral over `A`
and has reduction `A ⧸ I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_integral_factor_decomposition_of_gabber_root_condition
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal A))
    (hroot : ∀ (f : A[X]), f.Monic →
      ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n →
        ∀ a : Fin (n + 1) → I,
          f = X ^ n * (X - 1) + ∑ i : Fin (n + 1), C (a i : A) * X ^ (i : ℕ) →
            ∃ α : A, α - 1 ∈ I ∧ f.IsRoot α)
    (A' : Type (max u v)) [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A'] [Algebra.Etale A A']
    (σ : A' →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I) :
    ∃ (A₁ A₂ : Type (max u v))
      (_ : CommRing A₁) (_ : CommRing A₂)
      (_ : Algebra A A₁) (_ : Algebra A A₂)
      (e : A' ≃ₐ[A] A₁ × A₂) (q : A₁ →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I),
      Algebra.IsIntegral A A₁ ∧
        Function.Surjective q ∧
        RingHom.ker q = I.map (algebraMap A A₁) ∧
        q.comp ((AlgHom.fst A A₁ A₂).comp e.toAlgHom) = σ

declarations.name: exists_integralClosure_quotient_algEquiv_prod
declarations.doc:
If the reduction of a finite type `A`-algebra `B` modulo `I` decomposes as `(A ⧸ I) × C`, then
the reduction of the integral closure of `A` in `B` has a compatible decomposition `(A ⧸ I) × C'`.
Compatibility is expressed using the canonical map induced by the inclusion
`integralClosure A B → B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_integralClosure_quotient_algEquiv_prod
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (I : Ideal A) [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (C : Type w) [CommRing C] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) C]
    (e : (B ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A B)) ≃ₐ[A ⧸ I] ((A ⧸ I) × C)) :
    let B' := integralClosure A B
    let IB' := I.map (algebraMap A B')
    let IB := I.map (algebraMap A B)
    let toReduction : (B' ⧸ IB') →+* (B ⧸ IB) :=
      Ideal.quotientMap IB (B'.val : B' →+* B) (by
        rw [Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap]
        intro a ha
        change ((B'.val : B' →+* B) (algebraMap A B' a)) ∈ IB
        change algebraMap A B a ∈ IB
        exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem (algebraMap A B) ha)
    ∃ (C' : Type (max u v)) (hC' : CommRing C'),
      let _ := hC'
      ∃ hAlg : Algebra (A ⧸ I) C',
        let _ := hAlg
        ∃ (e' : (B' ⧸ IB') ≃ₐ[A ⧸ I] ((A ⧸ I) × C'))
          (k : C' →ₐ[A ⧸ I] C),
          ∀ x, e (toReduction x) = ((e' x).1, k (e' x).2)

registrations.name: AlgEquiv.prodQuotientOfIsIdempotentElem
registrations.comment: product decomposition by complementary idempotents

declarations.name: prodQuotientOfIsIdempotentElem_apply_idempotent_mod
declarations.doc:
The canonical `A / I`-algebra product decomposition of `B / IB` associated to an idempotent is
induced by the two quotient maps and sends that idempotent to `(1, 0)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem prodQuotientOfIsIdempotentElem_apply_idempotent_mod
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (I : Ideal A) (b : B)
    (hb : IsIdempotentElem (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A B)) b)) :
    let Q := B ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A B)
    let bbar : Q := Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A B)) b
    let e : Q ≃ₐ[A ⧸ I]
        (Q ⧸ Ideal.span {1 - bbar}) × (Q ⧸ Ideal.span {bbar}) :=
      AlgEquiv.prodQuotientOfIsIdempotentElem (A ⧸ I)
        (e := 1 - bbar) (f := bbar) hb.one_sub hb (by simp) hb.one_sub_mul_self
    e bbar = (1, 0)

declarations.name: henselianPair_limit
declarations.doc: A limit of henselian pairs is a henselian pair.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselianPair_limit
    {J : Type v} [SmallCategory J]
    (F : J ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (I : ∀ j, Ideal (F.obj j))
    (hI : ∀ ⦃j k⦄ (f : j ⟶ k), Ideal.map (F.map f).hom (I j) ≤ I k)
    (c : Cone F) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (h : ∀ j, HenselianPair (F.obj j) (I j)) :
    HenselianPair c.pt
      (⨅ j, Ideal.comap (c.π.app j).hom (I j))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.tfae_isQuasicoherentClause
declarations.doc:
**The three-way equivalence of Stacks 0EM8**, over its two inputs at the Zariski and the
étale topology: for a presheaf of modules on a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf
category of schemes over `S`, being a quasi-coherent Zariski module, being a quasi-coherent
étale module, and being a quasi-coherent module on `𝒳` in the sense of Stacks 06WG are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tfae_isQuasicoherentClause
    (h₁z : IsSheafFppfOfQuasicoherentOnSite B S hS p hp .zariski)
    (h₁e : IsSheafFppfOfQuasicoherentOnSite B S hS p hp .etale)
    (h₂z : QuasicoherentOnSiteOfLeFppf B S hS p hp .zariski)
    (h₂e : QuasicoherentOnSiteOfLeFppf B S hS p hp .etale)
    (𝓕 : PresheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingPresheaf B S hS p hp)) :
    [IsQuasicoherentClause B S hS p hp .zariski 𝓕,
      IsQuasicoherentClause B S hS p hp .etale 𝓕,
      IsQuasicoherentClause B S hS p hp .fppf 𝓕].TFAE
declarations.comment: the three-way equivalence, with the two inputs at each of the Zariski and the étale topology carried as explicit hypotheses: `h₁z`/`h₁e`, a `τ`-sheaf of modules that is quasi-coherent on `(𝒳_τ, 𝒪_𝒳)` is a sheaf for the inherited fppf topology, and `h₂z`/`h₂e`, quasi-coherence passes from the inherited fppf topology to a coarser one. At `τ = .fppf` both are discharged here. Neither is discharged at `τ = .zariski` or `τ = .etale`: both funnel into the essential-surjectivity half of Descent, Proposition 03DX, which this repository does not prove and carries as the hypothesis `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.QuasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule`, its only open reduction being `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.AssociatedModuleGlueDescentDatum`; the two existing 03DX declarations state the different criterion that quasi-coherence on the small étale site of an algebraic space is equivalent to being cartesian on affine charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.tfae_isQuasicoherentClause'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EM8.**  For a category `𝒳` fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of
schemes over `S` and a presheaf of modules `𝓕` on `𝒳`, the three conditions

1. `𝓕` is an object of `Mod(𝒳_Zar, 𝒪_𝒳)` and is quasi-coherent on `(𝒳_Zar, 𝒪_𝒳)`,
2. `𝓕` is an object of `Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)` and is quasi-coherent on `(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)`,
3. `𝓕` is a quasi-coherent module on `𝒳` in the sense of Stacks 06WG, that is on
   `(𝒳_fppf, 𝒪_𝒳)`,

are equivalent.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.tfae_isQuasicoherentClause` with its four hypotheses
discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isSheafFppfOfQuasicoherentOnSite_zariski`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isSheafFppfOfQuasicoherentOnSite_etale`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.quasicoherentOnSiteOfLeFppf_zariski` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.quasicoherentOnSiteOfLeFppf_etale`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tfae_isQuasicoherentClause'
    (𝓕 : PresheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingPresheaf B S hS p hp)) :
    [IsQuasicoherentClause B S hS p hp .zariski 𝓕,
      IsQuasicoherentClause B S hS p hp .etale 𝓕,
      IsQuasicoherentClause B S hS p hp .fppf 𝓕].TFAE
declarations.comment: the three-way equivalence, for a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of schemes over S and a presheaf of modules on it

declarations.name: Finset.Nonempty.exists_sum_pow_ne_zero
declarations.statement:
theorem Finset.Nonempty.exists_sum_pow_ne_zero {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    {s : Finset R} (hs : s.Nonempty) : ∃ n, ∑ x ∈ s, x ^ n ≠ 0

declarations.name: weakAss_eq_minimalPrimes0EMA
declarations.doc:
For a reduced commutative ring `R`, the weakly associated primes of `R` are exactly the minimal
primes of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weakAss_eq_minimalPrimes0EMA [IsReduced R] :
    weaklyAssociatedPrimes R R = minimalPrimes R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.MultiplicativeSubpresheaf.toLocalizationSheaf
declarations.doc: The canonical map from the ring sheaf to the sheafified localization.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toLocalizationSheaf (S : MultiplicativeSubpresheaf X)
    [HasWeakSheafify X.J CommRingCat.{w}] :
    X.O ⟶ (presheafToSheaf X.J CommRingCat.{w}).obj S.localizationPresheaf
declarations.comment: canonical homomorphism of sheaves of rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.MultiplicativeSubpresheaf.isUnit_toLocalizationSheaf
declarations.doc: The canonical map sends each prescribed section to a unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnit_toLocalizationSheaf (S : MultiplicativeSubpresheaf X)
    [HasWeakSheafify X.J CommRingCat.{w}]
    (U : X.Cᵒᵖ) (s : S.obj U) :
    IsUnit (((S.toLocalizationSheaf).hom.app U).hom (s : X.O.obj.obj U))
declarations.comment: inversion of the prescribed sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.MultiplicativeSubpresheaf.existsUnique_lift_toLocalizationSheaf
declarations.doc:
A morphism inverting every prescribed section factors uniquely through the
sheafified sectionwise localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_lift_toLocalizationSheaf (S : MultiplicativeSubpresheaf X)
    [HasWeakSheafify X.J CommRingCat.{w}]
    (A : Sheaf X.J CommRingCat.{w}) (f : X.O ⟶ A)
    (hf : ∀ (U : X.Cᵒᵖ) (s : S.obj U),
      IsUnit ((f.hom.app U).hom (s : X.O.obj.obj U))) :
    ∃! g : (presheafToSheaf X.J CommRingCat.{w}).obj S.localizationPresheaf ⟶ A,
      S.toLocalizationSheaf ≫ g = f
declarations.comment: universal property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.MultiplicativeSubpresheaf.existsUnique_lift_localizationModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of `(S⁻¹F)^#`.**  A map of sheaves of `O_X`-modules `φ : F ⟶ G`
such that each prescribed local section of `S` acts invertibly on `G` factors uniquely through
the canonical map `F ⟶ (S⁻¹F)^#`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_lift_localizationModuleSheaf
    {F G : SheafOfModules.{max w z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hG : ∀ (U : X.Cᵒᵖ) (s : S.obj U),
      letI : Module (X.O.obj.obj U) (G.val.obj U) := (G.val.obj U).isModule
      Function.Bijective fun t : G.val.obj U ↦ (s : X.O.obj.obj U) • t) :
    ∃! ψ : S.localizationModuleSheaf F ⟶ G, S.toLocalizationModuleSheaf F ≫ ψ = φ
declarations.comment: localization_universal_property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.MultiplicativeSubpresheaf.localizationModuleSheafIsoTensor
declarations.doc:
**`(S⁻¹F)^# = (S⁻¹O_X)^# ⊗_{O_X} F` as sheaves of `(S⁻¹O_X)^#`-modules.**  The
sheafification of the sectionwise localization of `F` is the extension of scalars of `F` along
`O_X ⟶ (S⁻¹O_X)^#`.
declarations.statement:
def localizationModuleSheafIsoTensor
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max w z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    (PresheafOfModules.sheafification σ).obj (S.localizationModulePresheaf F.val) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.pullback (S.localizationRingSheafHom σ)).obj F
declarations.comment: localization_tensor_iso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.MultiplicativeSubpresheaf.unit_comp_localizationModuleSheafIsoTensor
declarations.doc:
The identification `(S⁻¹F)^# = (S⁻¹O_X)^# ⊗_{O_X} F` is compatible with the canonical maps
out of `F`: the unit of the pullback--pushforward adjunction corresponds to the sectionwise
localization map followed by the sheafification unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem unit_comp_localizationModuleSheafIsoTensor
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max w z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    (SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
        (S.localizationRingSheafHom σ)).unit.app F ≫
      (SheafOfModules.pushforward (S.localizationRingSheafHom σ)).map
        (S.localizationModuleSheafIsoTensor σ F).inv =
      toPushforwardSheafification _ σ (changeOfRingsAdjunction S.toLocalizationPresheaf) F
declarations.comment: localization_tensor_iso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weaklyAssociatedPointsOfScheme_eq_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EME.** The weakly associated points of a reduced scheme are exactly
the generic points of its irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyAssociatedPointsOfScheme_eq_genericPoints (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X] :
    Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X = genericPoints X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.regularSectionGerms_eq_nonZeroDivisors_of_weaklyAssociatedPoints_subset_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
If weakly associated points are generic points of irreducible components and
quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components, then the germs of regular
sections at every point are exactly the nonzerodivisors in its local ring.
declarations.statement:
lemma regularSectionGerms_eq_nonZeroDivisors_of_weaklyAssociatedPoints_subset_genericPoints
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (x : X) :
    (⨆ (U : Opens X) (hx : x ∈ U),
      ((X.presheaf.submonoidPresheafOfStalk
        (fun y ↦ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y))).obj (Opposite.op U)).map
          (X.presheaf.germ U x hx).hom) =
      nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment: regular_elements_in_stalks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalk_totalQuotientPresheaf_isFractionRing_of_weaklyAssociatedPoints_subset_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
If every weakly associated point of a scheme is a generic point of an irreducible component
and every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components, then the stalk of the
presheaf of meromorphic functions at any point is the total quotient ring of the local ring.
declarations.statement:
lemma stalk_totalQuotientPresheaf_isFractionRing_of_weaklyAssociatedPoints_subset_genericPoints
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.presheaf.totalQuotientPresheaf.stalk x) :=
      ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map
        X.presheaf.toTotalQuotientPresheaf).hom.toAlgebra
    IsFractionRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.presheaf.totalQuotientPresheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment: stalk_total_quotient_ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalk_totalQuotientSheaf_isFractionRing_of_weaklyAssociated
declarations.doc:
If every weakly associated point of a scheme is a generic point of an irreducible component
and every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components, then the stalk `K_{X, x}`
of the sheaf of meromorphic functions at any point is the total quotient ring of the local ring
`𝒪_{X, x}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma stalk_totalQuotientSheaf_isFractionRing_of_weaklyAssociated
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.stalk x) :=
      ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map
        X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom).hom.toAlgebra
    IsFractionRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment: stalk_total_quotient_ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_toGenericPointStalkProduct
declarations.doc:
The comparison map of sheaves of rings is an isomorphism: it is so on stalks, because the
presheaf-level comparison is bijective on the affine opens and the sheafification unit is an
isomorphism on stalks.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_toGenericPointStalkProduct
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) :
    IsIso (toGenericPointStalkProduct X)
declarations.comment: generic_point_decomposition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.meromorphicFunctions_iso_product_genericPointStalks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMF.** The `𝒪_X`-module of meromorphic functions is the product of the
pushed-forward structure sheaves of the local schemes at the generic points of the irreducible
components, for a scheme whose weakly associated points are generic points of irreducible
components and whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicFunctions_iso_product_genericPointStalks
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hassoc : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) →
      (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    Nonempty (meromorphicFunctions X ≅
      ∏ᶜ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModule X η)
declarations.comment: generic_point_decomposition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.meromorphicFunctions_iso_coproduct_genericPointStalks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMF, displayed direct-sum decomposition.** For a scheme whose weakly associated
points are generic points of irreducible components and whose quasi-compact opens have finitely
many irreducible components, the `𝒪_X`-module of meromorphic functions is the direct sum over
the generic points of the irreducible components of the pushed-forward structure sheaves of the
spectra of the local rings there.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicFunctions_iso_coproduct_genericPointStalks (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hassoc : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    Nonempty (meromorphicFunctions X ≅
      ∐ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModule X η)
declarations.comment: generic_point_decomposition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalization_totalQuotientSheaf_obj
declarations.doc:
**Part (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0EMF].** On an affine open `U` of a scheme whose weakly associated
points are generic points of irreducible components and whose quasi-compact opens have finitely
many irreducible components, the sections `K_X(U)` of the *sheaf* of meromorphic functions — not
only those of the presheaf — are the total quotient ring of `Γ(X, U)`, that is, its localization
at its nonzerodivisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalization_totalQuotientSheaf_obj
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite)
    {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(X, U) (X.totalQuotientSheaf.obj.obj (op U)) :=
      (X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom.app (op U)).hom.toAlgebra
    IsLocalization (nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, U)) (X.totalQuotientSheaf.obj.obj (op U))
declarations.comment: part (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_pi_genericPointStalkModuleOf
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0EMF], the product decomposition.** For a quasi-coherent module `F`
on a scheme whose weakly associated points are generic points of irreducible components and whose
quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components, the sheaf `K_X(F)` of meromorphic
sections of `F` is the product over the generic points of the irreducible components of the
generic-point contributions.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_pi_genericPointStalkModuleOf
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Nonempty (meromorphicSections X F ≅
      ∏ᶜ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModuleOf X F η)
declarations.comment: part (2), product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_sigma_genericPointStalkModuleOf
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0EMF], the direct-sum decomposition.** The family of generic-point
contributions is locally finite, so the product of the previous theorem is also their direct
sum.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_sigma_genericPointStalkModuleOf
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Nonempty (meromorphicSections X F ≅
      ∐ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModuleOf X F η)
declarations.comment: part (2), direct sum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.meromorphicSections_isQuasicoherent_of_genericHypotheses
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0EMF], quasi-coherence.** The sheaf `K_X(F)` of meromorphic
sections of a quasi-coherent module `F` is quasi-coherent, being the product of the generic-point
contributions.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicSections_isQuasicoherent_of_genericHypotheses
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (meromorphicSections X F).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: part (2), quasi-coherence

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicQuasicoherent.meromorphicFunctions_isQuasicoherent_of_genericHypotheses
declarations.doc:
**Part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0EMF].** On a scheme whose weakly associated points are generic
points of irreducible components and whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible
components, the sheaf of meromorphic functions is quasi-coherent: it is then the product of the
generic-point contributions, and that product is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicFunctions_isQuasicoherent_of_genericHypotheses {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfin : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents (U : Set X)).Finite) :
    (meromorphicFunctions X).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_commRing_rationalFunctions_ringEquiv_totalQuotientSheaf_top
declarations.doc:
**Part (6) of [Stacks, Tag 0EMF]**, with the commutative ring structure on the rational
functions constructed rather than assumed: it is transported from the global sections of the sheaf
of total quotient rings along the bijection, and every section on a dense open set is a ring
homomorphism to it, which is the characterization of [Stacks, Tag 01RU].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_commRing_rationalFunctions_ringEquiv_totalQuotientSheaf_top (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.schemeWeaklyAssociatedPoints X ⊆ genericPoints X)
    (hfinite : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) :
    ∃ _ : CommRing X.rationalFunctions,
      (∀ (U : X.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set X)),
          ∃ ψ : Γ(X, U) →+* X.rationalFunctions,
            ∀ s, ψ s = X.rationalFunctionOfSection U hU s) ∧
        Nonempty (X.rationalFunctions ≃+* X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
declarations.comment: part (6)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GenericPointCoproduct.meromorphicFunctions_iso_coproduct_of_noEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EMH.** On a locally Noetherian scheme without embedded points, the
`𝒪_X`-module of meromorphic functions is the direct sum, over the generic points of the
irreducible components, of the structure sheaves of the local schemes there, pushed forward to
`X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicFunctions_iso_coproduct_of_noEmbeddedPoints (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.HasNoEmbeddedPoints X) :
    Nonempty (meromorphicFunctions X ≅
      ∐ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModule X η)
declarations.comment: meromorphic functions as a direct sum

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GenericPointProduct.meromorphicFunctions_iso_product_of_noEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EMH.** On a locally Noetherian scheme without embedded points, the
`𝒪_X`-module of meromorphic functions is the product, over the generic points of the irreducible
components, of the structure sheaves of the local schemes there, pushed forward to `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicFunctions_iso_product_of_noEmbeddedPoints (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.HasNoEmbeddedPoints X) :
    Nonempty (meromorphicFunctions X ≅
      ∏ᶜ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModule X η)
declarations.comment: meromorphic functions as a product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_product_genericPointStalks_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0EMH**, the product decomposition of the sheaf of meromorphic sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_product_genericPointStalks_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : HasNoEmbeddedPoints X)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Nonempty (meromorphicSections X F ≅
      ∏ᶜ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModuleOf X F η)
declarations.comment: meromorphic sections as a product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_coproduct_genericPointStalks_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0EMH**, the direct-sum decomposition of the sheaf of meromorphic sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_meromorphicSections_iso_coproduct_genericPointStalks_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : HasNoEmbeddedPoints X)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Nonempty (meromorphicSections X F ≅
      ∐ fun η : genericPoints X ↦ genericPointStalkModuleOf X F η)
declarations.comment: meromorphic sections as a direct sum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.meromorphicSections_isQuasicoherent_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0EMH**, quasi-coherence of the sheaf of meromorphic sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicSections_isQuasicoherent_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : HasNoEmbeddedPoints X)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (meromorphicSections X F).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence of meromorphic sections

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicQuasicoherent.meromorphicFunctions_isQuasicoherent_of_noEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EMH.** On a locally Noetherian scheme without embedded points, the
sheaf of meromorphic functions is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicFunctions_isQuasicoherent_of_noEmbeddedPoints (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.HasNoEmbeddedPoints X) :
    (meromorphicFunctions X).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence of meromorphic functions

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicSectionsTensor.meromorphicSections_isQuasicoherent_of_noEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EMH, quasi-coherence of meromorphic sections.** On a locally Noetherian
scheme without embedded points, the sheaf of meromorphic sections of a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem meromorphicSections_isQuasicoherent_of_noEmbeddedPoints (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.HasNoEmbeddedPoints X) (F : X.Modules)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) :
    (meromorphicSections X F).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence of meromorphic sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_commRing_rationalFunctions_ringEquiv_totalQuotientSheaf_top_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EMH]**: on a locally Noetherian scheme without embedded points, the ring of
rational functions is the ring of global meromorphic functions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_commRing_rationalFunctions_ringEquiv_totalQuotientSheaf_top_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : HasNoEmbeddedPoints X) :
    ∃ _ : CommRing X.rationalFunctions,
      (∀ (U : X.Opens) (hU : Dense (U : Set X)),
          ∃ ψ : Γ(X, U) →+* X.rationalFunctions,
            ∀ s, ψ s = X.rationalFunctionOfSection U hU s) ∧
        Nonempty (X.rationalFunctions ≃+* X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
declarations.comment: rational functions are meromorphic functions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EMI]**, which is case (3) of [Stacks, Tag 02OZ]. An invertible sheaf of
modules on a locally Noetherian scheme without embedded points has a regular meromorphic
section.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_hasNoEmbeddedPoints (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : HasNoEmbeddedPoints X) (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L] :
    ∃ s : MeromorphicSection X.sheaf L, IsRegularMeromorphicSection X.sheaf L s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompactMap_pointsMap
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S`
induces a quasi-compact map `|X| → |Y|` of point spaces: the preimage of a quasi-compact
open subset of `|Y|` is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactMap_pointsMap {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) :
    ∀ ⦃U : Set (points B S hS Y)⦄, IsOpen U → IsCompact U →
      IsCompact (pointsMap B S hS X f ⁻¹' U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PartialMap.Equivalent
declarations.doc: Two partial maps agree after restriction to a common dense open subspace.
declarations.statement: def Equivalent (f g : PartialMap B S hS hX Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1): equivalence of representatives

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PartialMap.equivalence_equivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMM, part (1).** Agreement on a common dense open subspace is an equivalence
relation.

Transitivity restricts to the dense open subspace common to the two witnesses, which exists
by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isDenseOpenSubspace_le`.
declarations.statement:
theorem equivalence_equivalent :
    Equivalence (Equivalent B S hS (X := X) (Y := Y) (hX := hX))
declarations.comment: part (1): equivalence relation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RationalMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMM, part (2).** A rational map of algebraic spaces is a class of dense-open
representatives.
declarations.statement:
def RationalMap (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Type _
declarations.comment: part (2): rational maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RationalMap.IsOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMM, part (3).** A rational map is over another algebraic space if one
representative is.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsOver {T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (xToT : X ⟶ T) (yToT : Y ⟶ T)
    (φ : RationalMap B S hS hX Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3): relative rational maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctions
declarations.doc: A rational function is a rational map to the relative affine line.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev rationalFunctions (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: rational functions as rational maps to the relative affine line

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionsRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMP.** Pointwise ring operations on common dense-open representatives
determine the commutative ring structure on rational functions.

The ring is the direct limit of the rings of sections over the dense open subspaces, which
is a directed system because two dense open subspaces contain a common one.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalFunctionsRing (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    ∃ R : CommRing (rationalFunctions B S hS hX),
      letI := R
      (∀ (U : Subfunctor X) (hU : IsDenseOpenSubspace B S hS hX U)
          (f g : U.toFunctor ⟶ affineLineFunctor B S hS),
        ∃ a m : U.toFunctor ⟶ affineLineFunctor B S hS,
          (∀ T x, affineLineCoordinate B S hS T (a.app T x) =
            affineLineCoordinate B S hS T (f.app T x) +
              affineLineCoordinate B S hS T (g.app T x)) ∧
          (∀ T x, affineLineCoordinate B S hS T (m.app T x) =
            affineLineCoordinate B S hS T (f.app T x) *
              affineLineCoordinate B S hS T (g.app T x)) ∧
          (PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS
            (⟨U, hU, a⟩ : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS)) =
            PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS
              (⟨U, hU, f⟩ : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS)) +
            PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS
              (⟨U, hU, g⟩ : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS))) ∧
          (PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS
            (⟨U, hU, m⟩ : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS)) =
            PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS
              (⟨U, hU, f⟩ : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS)) *
            PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS
              (⟨U, hU, g⟩ : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS)))) ∧
      (∀ (U : Subfunctor X) (hU : IsDenseOpenSubspace B S hS hX U),
        ∃ z o : U.toFunctor ⟶ affineLineFunctor B S hS,
          (∀ T x, affineLineCoordinate B S hS T (z.app T x) = 0) ∧
          (∀ T x, affineLineCoordinate B S hS T (o.app T x) = 1) ∧
          (PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS
            (⟨U, hU, z⟩ : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS)) = 0) ∧
          (PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS
            (⟨U, hU, o⟩ : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS)) = 1)) ∧
      (∀ (U : Subfunctor X) (hU : IsDenseOpenSubspace B S hS hX U)
          (f : U.toFunctor ⟶ affineLineFunctor B S hS),
        ∃ n : U.toFunctor ⟶ affineLineFunctor B S hS,
          (∀ T x, affineLineCoordinate B S hS T (n.app T x) =
            -affineLineCoordinate B S hS T (f.app T x)) ∧
          (PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS
            (⟨U, hU, n⟩ : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS)) =
            -PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS
              (⟨U, hU, f⟩ : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RationalMap.IsDefinedAt
declarations.doc:
A rational map is *defined at a point* of its source when it has a representative whose
domain contains that point.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsDefinedAt (φ : RationalMap B S hS hX Y) (x : points B S hS X) : Prop
declarations.comment: defined at a point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RationalMap.domainOfDefinition
declarations.doc: The *domain of definition* of a rational map is the set of points at which it is defined.
declarations.statement: abbrev domainOfDefinition (φ : RationalMap B S hS hX Y) : Set (points B S hS X)
