declarations.comment: domain of definition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_hom_of_eq_domainOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMR.** Let `X` be a reduced algebraic space over `S` and let `Y` be an algebraic
space separated over `S`. A rational map from `X` to `Y` is represented by exactly one morphism
on the open subspace of `X` whose point set is its domain of definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_hom_of_eq_domainOfDefinition
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T))
    (hYsep : IsSeparatedOver B S hS Y)
    (φ : RationalMap B S hS hX Y)
    (U : Subfunctor X) (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U)
    (hUdom : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι) =
      RationalMap.domainOfDefinition B S hS φ) :
    ∃! f : U.toFunctor ⟶ Y, ∃ hUd : IsDenseOpenSubspace B S hS hX U,
      PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS ⟨U, hUd, f⟩ = φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RationalMap.IsDominant
declarations.doc:
A rational map is *dominant* when every one of its dense-open representatives is a dominant
morphism.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsDominant (φ : RationalMap B S hS hX Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Birational
declarations.doc:
Two algebraic spaces over `S` with irreducible point spaces are *birational* when they have
mutually inverse dominant rational maps: two dominant rational maps whose composites agree with
the respective identities on dense open subspaces.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Birational (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (_hXirr : IrreducibleSpace (points B S hS X))
    (_hYirr : IrreducibleSpace (points B S hS Y)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.birational_iff_exists_isOpenSubspace_iso
declarations.doc:
Two algebraic spaces over `S` with irreducible point spaces are birational if and only if
they contain nonempty open subspaces which are isomorphic as algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem birational_iff_exists_isOpenSubspace_iso (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hXirr : IrreducibleSpace (points B S hS X))
    (hYirr : IrreducibleSpace (points B S hS Y)) :
    Birational B S hS hX hY hXirr hYirr ↔
      ∃ (U : Subfunctor X) (V : Subfunctor Y), IsOpenSubspace B S hS U ∧
        IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧ Nonempty (points B S hS U.toFunctor) ∧
        Nonempty (points B S hS V.toFunctor) ∧ Nonempty (U.toFunctor ≅ V.toFunctor)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.residueFieldRepresentative
declarations.doc:
The chosen field-valued representative of a point of a decent algebraic space whose morphism
to the space is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def residueFieldRepresentative (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    {p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X //
      p.class B S hS X = x ∧ Mono (fieldMorphism B S hS X p)}
declarations.comment: field-valued monomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.residueField
declarations.doc:
The residue field of a decent algebraic space at a point: the field of the monomorphism from
a field spectrum representing that point.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev residueField (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (x : points B S hS X) : Type u
declarations.comment: residue field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.residueFieldRepresentative_unique
declarations.doc:
A monomorphic field-valued representative of a point of a decent algebraic space is uniquely
isomorphic, over the space, to the chosen one: the residue field is unique up to unique
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem residueFieldRepresentative_unique (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (x : points B S hS X)
    (q : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X) (hq : q.class B S hS X = x)
    (hmq : Mono (fieldMorphism B S hS X q)) :
    ∃! e : yoneda.obj ((residueFieldRepresentative B S hS X hDecent x).1.siteObject B S hS X) ≅
        yoneda.obj (q.siteObject B S hS X),
      e.hom ≫ fieldMorphism B S hS X q = residueFieldMorphism B S hS X hDecent x
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_residueFieldHom_iff_mono
declarations.doc:
A morphism of decent algebraic spaces induces an isomorphism of residue fields at a point
exactly when the morphism from the spectrum of the residue field at that point to the target
space is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_residueFieldHom_iff_mono (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hDecentX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hDecentY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : points B S hS X) :
    IsIso (CommRingCat.ofHom (residueFieldHom B S hS X Y hY hDecentX hDecentY f x)) ↔
      Mono (residueFieldMorphism B S hS X hDecentX x ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkToHenselianLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMY.** The canonical homomorphism from the local ring of an elementary étale
neighborhood at its distinguished point into the henselian local ring of the algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
def stalkToHenselianLocalRing (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x) :
    U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point →+*
      (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: the canonical map from the stalk of an elementary étale neighbourhood

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkToHenselianLocalRing_openGerm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMY.** The canonical homomorphism sends the germ of a section over a pointed open
subscheme to the canonical image of that section in the henselian local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkToHenselianLocalRing_openGerm (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x)
    (W : U.scheme.left.1.Opens) (hW : U.point ∈ W)
    (s : U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.obj (op W)) :
    stalkToHenselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent U
        (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.germ W U.point hW s) =
      openRestrictionSectionHom B S hS X hX x hDecent U W hW s
declarations.comment: the canonical map on germs over a pointed open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.stalkToHenselianLocalRing_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMY.** The canonical homomorphisms out of the local rings of the elementary étale
neighborhoods are compatible with every morphism of neighborhoods.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkToHenselianLocalRing_naturality (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    {V U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x} (f : V ⟶ U) :
    (stalkToHenselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent V).comp
        (neighborhoodStalkMap B S hS X hX x f).hom =
      stalkToHenselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent U
declarations.comment: naturality of the canonical map in the neighbourhood

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMY.** The henselian local ring of a decent algebraic space at a point is a local
ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    IsLocalRing (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: O^h is a local ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.henselianLocalRing_isHenselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMY.** The henselian local ring of a decent algebraic space at a point is a
henselization of the local ring of any elementary étale neighborhood at its distinguished
point.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselianLocalRing_isHenselization (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x) :
    letI := henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent
    letI := stalkAlgebra B S hS X hX x hDecent U
    IsLocalRing.IsHenselization (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point))
      (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: O^h is a henselization of the stalk

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.map_maximalIdeal_stalkToHenselianLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMY.** The maximal ideal of the henselian local ring is generated by the image of
the maximal ideal of the local ring of any elementary étale neighborhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_maximalIdeal_stalkToHenselianLocalRing (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x) :
    letI := henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent
    (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point)).map
        (stalkToHenselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent U) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: the maximal ideal of O^h

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_residueFieldEquiv_henselianLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMY.** The residue field of the henselian local ring is the residue field of the
local ring of any elementary étale neighborhood at its distinguished point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_residueFieldEquiv_henselianLocalRing (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x) :
    letI := henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent
    ∃ e : IsLocalRing.ResidueField (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point) ≃+*
        IsLocalRing.ResidueField
          (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1)),
      ∀ r : U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point,
        e (IsLocalRing.residue _ r) =
          IsLocalRing.residue _ (stalkToHenselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent U r)
declarations.comment: the residue field of O^h

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.neighborhoodSectionsToGenericHenselianLocalRing_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMY.** The map from the global sections of an elementary étale neighbourhood of
the generic point of a prime divisor into the henselian local ring there is compatible with
every morphism of neighbourhoods.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.neighborhoodSectionsToGenericHenselianLocalRing_naturality
    {V U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX (Z.genericPoint B S hS X)} (f : V ⟶ U)
    (a : Γ(U.scheme.left.1, ⊤)) :
    Z.neighborhoodSectionsToGenericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec V (f.hom.left.1.appTop a) =
      Z.neighborhoodSectionsToGenericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec U a
declarations.comment: naturality in the neighbourhood of the map from global sections into the henselian local ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalRing_henselianLocalRing
declarations.doc: The henselian local ring of a decent algebraic space at a point is a local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalRing_henselianLocalRing :
    IsLocalRing (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hXdec : Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: O^h is a local ring for a decent space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isHenselization_etaleLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EMZ.** The étale local ring of a decent algebraic space at a geometric point is a
strict henselization of the henselian local ring of the space at the point it lies over.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isHenselization_etaleLocalRing (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X) (hxbar : xbar.LiesOver x)
    (κsep : Type u) [Field κsep]
    [Algebra (ResidueField (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point : Type u)) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point : Type u)) κsep] :
    letI := henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent
    letI := isLocalRing_etaleLocalRing B S hS X hX xbar
    ∃ (algU : Algebra (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point : Type u)
        (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)))
      (alg : Algebra (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1))
        (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)))
      (algRes : Algebra (ResidueField
        (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1))) κsep),
      (@algebraMap (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1))
            (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)) _ _ alg).comp
          (stalkToHenselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent U) =
        @algebraMap (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point : Type u)
          (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)) _ _ algU ∧
      @IsHenselization (U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point : Type u) _ _ κsep _ _
        (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)) _ _ algU ∧
      @IsHenselization (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1)) _ _
        κsep _ algRes (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)) _ _ alg
declarations.comment:
the étale local ring at a geometric point is a strict henselization of the
henselian local ring at the point below it, for a chosen separable closure κsep of the residue
field. The algebra structures are produced, not assumed; the structure map is pinned by lying
over the neighborhood stalk, of which the étale local ring is also a strict henselization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.genericResidueFieldEquivHenselian
declarations.doc:
**The canonical isomorphism `κ(u) ≃+* κ(𝒪^h_{X, ξ})`** induced by the henselization map
`𝒪_{U, u} → 𝒪^h_{X, ξ}`.
declarations.statement:
def PrimeDivisor.genericResidueFieldEquivHenselian :
    letI := henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing B S hS X hX (Z.genericPoint B S hS X) hdec
    Z.genericResidueField B S hS hX hdec ≃+*
      IsLocalRing.ResidueField ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)
declarations.comment: the residue field of the henselian local ring at the generic point of a prime divisor is the residue field of the chosen chart, canonically through the henselization map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_residueFieldEquiv_residueField
declarations.doc:
The residue field of the henselian local ring of a decent algebraic space at a point is the
residue field of the space at that point, through an isomorphism compatible with the canonical
homomorphism out of the stalk of a given elementary étale neighborhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_residueFieldEquiv_residueField (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x) :
    letI := henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent
    ∃ (eκ : (neighborhoodFieldPoint B S hS X hX x U).carrier ≃+*
        residueField B S hS X hDecent x)
      (g : (residueFieldRepresentative B S hS X hDecent x).1.siteObject B S hS X ⟶
        (neighborhoodFieldPoint B S hS X hX x U).siteObject B S hS X)
      (e : residueField B S hS X hDecent x ≃+*
        IsLocalRing.ResidueField (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1))),
      fieldValuedPointHom B S hS X _ _ g = eκ.toRingHom ∧
        yoneda.map g ≫ fieldMorphism B S hS X (neighborhoodFieldPoint B S hS X hX x U) =
          residueFieldMorphism B S hS X hDecent x ∧
        ∀ r : U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point,
          e (eκ (IsLocalRing.residue _ r)) =
            IsLocalRing.residue _ (stalkToHenselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent U r)
declarations.comment:
the residue field of the henselian local ring is the residue field of the space.
Both fields are determined only up to canonical isomorphism, so the identification is
existential, pinned by the isomorphism `eκ` of the neighborhood residue field with the residue
field of the space lying over the space (the morphism `g`) and by compatibility with the
canonical homomorphism out of the neighborhood stalk. No hypothesis is carried: cofilteredness of
the elementary étale neighborhoods comes from Stacks 0BGV, nonemptiness from the given
neighborhood

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_residueFieldEquiv_residueField
declarations.doc:
The residue field of the henselian local ring of a decent algebraic space at a point is the
residue field of the space at that point: there is exactly one isomorphism
between them compatible with every elementary étale neighborhood of the point, namely the one
carrying the class of the image of a germ `r` of the neighborhood to the value at `r` of the
homomorphism of residue fields lying over the space.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_residueFieldEquiv_residueField (hDecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    letI := henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent
    ∃! e : IsLocalRing.ResidueField
        (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent : Type (u + 1)) ≃+*
          residueField B S hS X hDecent x,
      ∀ (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX x)
        (g : (residueFieldRepresentative B S hS X hDecent x).1.siteObject B S hS X ⟶
          (neighborhoodFieldPoint B S hS X hX x U).siteObject B S hS X),
        yoneda.map g ≫ fieldMorphism B S hS X (neighborhoodFieldPoint B S hS X hX x U) =
            residueFieldMorphism B S hS X hDecent x →
        ∀ r : U.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk U.point,
          e (IsLocalRing.residue _ (stalkToHenselianLocalRing B S hS X hX x hDecent U r)) =
            fieldValuedPointHom B S hS X (residueFieldRepresentative B S hS X hDecent x).1
              (neighborhoodFieldPoint B S hS X hX x U) g (IsLocalRing.residue _ r)
declarations.comment:
the residue field of the henselian local ring is the residue field of the space,
by the canonical isomorphism: the unique one compatible, for every elementary étale neighborhood,
with the canonical homomorphism out of its stalk and the homomorphism of residue fields over the
space. No neighborhood is assumed; one exists by Stacks 0BBP

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace_eq_setOf_localRingDimension_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EN1.** The weakly associated points of a reduced algebraic space are exactly its
points of codimension zero, that is the points whose local ring has Krull dimension zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace_eq_setOf_localRingDimension_eq_zero
    (hred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)) :
    weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X =
      {x : points B S hS X.1 | localRingDimension B S hS x = 0}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.meromorphicFunctionSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EN3.** The *sheaf of meromorphic functions* `𝒦_F` on the algebraic space `F`: the
sheaf on the small étale site of `F` associated to the presheaf of sectionwise localizations
`U ↦ 𝒮_F(U)⁻¹ 𝒪_F(U)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def meromorphicFunctionSheaf (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS F) CommRingCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the sheaf of meromorphic functions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MeromorphicFunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EN3.** A *meromorphic function* on the algebraic space `F` is a global section of
its sheaf of meromorphic functions `𝒦_F`.
declarations.statement: abbrev MeromorphicFunction (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
declarations.comment: meromorphic functions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularSection_iff_mem_nonZeroDivisors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EN4.** Over an affine étale chart `U` of the algebraic space `F` the regular
sections of `𝒪_F` are exactly the nonzerodivisors of the ring of sections `𝒪_F(U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularSection_iff_mem_nonZeroDivisors (U : SmallEtale B S hS F)
    (hU : IsAffine (smallEtaleScheme B S hS F U))
    (s : (structurePresheaf B S hS F).obj (op U)) :
    IsRegularSection B S hS F U s ↔ s ∈ ((structurePresheaf B S hS F).obj (op U))⁰

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.meromorphicSectionSheaf
declarations.doc:
The sheaf `𝒦_F(M)` of *meromorphic sections* of a sheaf of `𝒪_F`-modules `M`: the extension
of scalars of `M` along `𝒪_F ⟶ 𝒦_F`, sheafified.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev meromorphicSectionSheaf (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (M : Modules.{u, max u z} B S hS F hF) :
    SheafOfModules.{max (u + 1) z}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (meromorphicRingedSite B S hS F hF).O)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
A *meromorphic section* of a sheaf of `𝒪_F`-modules `M` is a global section of the sheaf
`𝒦_F(M)` of meromorphic sections of `M`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev MeromorphicSection (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (M : Modules.{u, max u z} B S hS F hF) : Type _
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFractionRing_meromorphicFunctionSheaf_obj
declarations.doc:
For an affine object `U` of the small étale site of an algebraic
space `X` satisfying hypotheses (a) and (b), the ring `𝒦_X(U)` of meromorphic functions over `U`
is the total ring of fractions of `𝒪_X(U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFractionRing_meromorphicFunctionSheaf_obj
    (hwa : ∀ z ∈ weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS z = 0)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X.1)
    (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (hU : IsAffine (smallEtaleScheme B S hS X.1 U)) :
    letI : Algebra ((structurePresheaf B S hS X.1).obj (op U))
        ((meromorphicFunctionSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2).obj.obj (op U)) :=
      ((toMeromorphicFunctionSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2).hom.app (op U)).hom.toAlgebra
    IsFractionRing ((structurePresheaf B S hS X.1).obj (op U))
      ((meromorphicFunctionSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2).obj.obj (op U))
declarations.comment:
part (2): over an affine object of the small étale site the ring of meromorphic
functions is the total ring of fractions of the ring of sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherent_meromorphicAlgebraSheaf
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic space `X` satisfying hypotheses (a) and (b), the
sheaf of meromorphic functions `𝒦_X` is a quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_X`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_meromorphicAlgebraSheaf
    (hwa : ∀ z ∈ weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS z = 0)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X.1) :
    (meromorphicAlgebraSheaf B S hS X).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment:
part (1): the sheaf of meromorphic functions is a quasi-coherent sheaf of
algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.regularSectionsStalk_eq_nonZeroDivisors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EN6, part (3).** Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` such that every
weakly associated point of `X` is a point of codimension `0` and every quasi-compact open of
every étale scheme chart of `X` has finitely many irreducible components (the condition of
Stacks 0BB1).  Then for every geometric point `x̄` of `X` the set `𝒮_x̄` of germs of regular
sections is exactly the set of nonzerodivisors of the étale local ring `𝒪_{X, x̄}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem regularSectionsStalk_eq_nonZeroDivisors (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hwa : ∀ z ∈ weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS z = 0)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X.1)
    (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) :
    regularSectionsStalk x = (etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 x)⁰
declarations.comment:
part (3): for a geometric point the germs of regular sections are exactly the
nonzerodivisors of the étale local ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFractionRing_meromorphicStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EN6, part (4).** Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` such that every
weakly associated point of `X` is a point of codimension `0` and every quasi-compact open of
every étale scheme chart of `X` has finitely many irreducible components (the condition of
Stacks 0BB1).  Then for every geometric point `x̄` of `X` the stalk `𝒦_{X, x̄}` of the sheaf of
meromorphic functions is the total ring of fractions of the étale local ring `𝒪_{X, x̄}`.

The stalk of `𝒦_X` is the stalk of the presheaf of sectionwise localizations, which is the
localization of `𝒪_{X, x̄}` at `𝒮_x̄`; by part (3) that multiplicative subset is exactly the
set of nonzerodivisors of `𝒪_{X, x̄}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFractionRing_meromorphicStalk
    (hwa : ∀ z ∈ weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS z = 0)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X.1) :
    letI : Algebra (etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 x) (meromorphicStalk B S hS X x) :=
      (toMeromorphicStalk B S hS X x).toAlgebra
    IsFractionRing (etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 x) (meromorphicStalk B S hS X x)
declarations.comment:
part (4): for a geometric point the stalk of the sheaf of meromorphic functions
is the total ring of fractions of the étale local ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_meromorphicFunctionSheaf_iso_representedMeromorphicAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EN7.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` all of whose weakly associated
points are points of codimension `0` and which satisfies the condition of Stacks 0BB1, and let
`X` be representable by a scheme `X₀`.  Then the sheaf of meromorphic functions `𝒦_X` is, as a
sheaf of `𝒪_X`-algebras, the algebra on the small étale site of `X` associated to the
quasi-coherent algebra `𝒦_{X₀}` of meromorphic functions on `X₀`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_meromorphicFunctionSheaf_iso_representedMeromorphicAlgebra
    (codimZero : ∀ z ∈ weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS z = 0)
    (finiteComponents : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X.1)
    (i : X.1 ≅ yoneda.obj T) :
    Nonempty (Under.mk (toMeromorphicFunctionSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2).hom ≅
      representedMeromorphicAlgebra B S hS X T codimZero finiteComponents i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PullbacksMeromorphicSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EN8.** *Pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined for `f : X ⟶ Y`* when, for
every commuting square of an étale chart `U` of `X` over an étale chart `V` of `Y`, the pullback
`f^♯` along the underlying morphism of schemes carries every regular section of `𝒪_Y` over `V`
to a regular section of `𝒪_X` over `U`.
declarations.statement: abbrev PullbacksMeromorphicSections {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EN9, part (2).** Pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined along a flat
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`: the morphism of schemes underlying a commuting square of étale charts of
`f` is flat, and pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined along a flat morphism of
schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_flat {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f) : PullbacksMeromorphicSections B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (2): flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_mapsTo_codimensionZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EN9, part (1).** Pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined along a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces carrying every weakly associated point of `X` to a point of
codimension `0` of `Y`.

Over a commuting square of étale scheme charts the claim is the scheme-level criterion of
Stacks 02OU: a weakly associated point of the chart of `X` lies over a weakly associated point
of `X`, which is carried to a point of codimension `0` of `Y`, and such a point is a generic
point of an irreducible component on the chart of `Y` above it.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_mapsTo_codimensionZero
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X.1 ⟶ Y.1)
    (hf : ∀ x ∈ weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X,
      localRingDimension B S hS (pointsMap B S hS X.1 f x) = 0) :
    PullbacksMeromorphicSections B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (1): weakly associated points of X mapped to codimension-zero points of Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_codimensionZeroPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENA, the assertion that the construction makes sense.** Let `X` be an algebraic
space over a scheme `S` satisfying hypotheses (b) and (c) of Stacks 0ENA — the equivalent
conditions of Stacks 0BB1, and representability of every codimension-zero point by a
monomorphism from the spectrum of a field.  Then `X` has a dense open subspace which is a
scheme and whose point set contains the whole of `X⁰`.

Consequently the local rings `𝒪_{X, η}` and the canonical morphisms
`j_η : Spec(𝒪_{X, η}) ⟶ X` for `η ∈ X⁰` are defined; they are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CodimensionZeroPresentation.stalk` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CodimensionZeroPresentation.fromSpecStalk`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_codimensionZeroPresentation
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X)
    (hmono : HasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X) :
    Nonempty (CodimensionZeroPresentation B S hS X)
declarations.comment:
the assertion of the statement that the construction makes sense: the set of
codimension-zero points is contained in the schematic locus, so that the local rings and the
morphisms j_η are defined

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.codimensionZero_mem_schematicLocus_of_hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENA, the assertion that the construction makes sense**, stated with the
schematic locus of Stacks 03JH: under hypotheses (b) and (c) of Stacks 0ENA every point of
codimension `0` of `X` lies in the schematic locus.

The dense open subspace of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_codimensionZeroPresentation` is a
representable open subspace, hence contained in the schematic locus.
declarations.statement:
theorem codimensionZero_mem_schematicLocus_of_hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X)
    (hmono : HasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X)
    (x : points B S hS X) (hx : localRingDimension B S hS x = 0) :
    x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (schematicLocus B S hS X).toFunctor
      (schematicLocus B S hS X).ι)
declarations.comment:
the assertion of the statement that the construction makes sense, read on the
schematic locus of Tag 03JH

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CodimensionZeroPresentation.exists_codimensionZeroPresentation_isIso_genericPointComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENA, the first conclusion.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` such
that

* (a) every weakly associated point of `X` is a point of codimension `0`,
* (b) every quasi-compact open of every étale scheme chart of `X` has finitely many irreducible
  components, the condition of Stacks 0BB1, and
* (c) every point of codimension `0` of `X` is represented by a monomorphism from the spectrum
  of a field.

Then the local rings `𝒪_{X, η}` at the points `η ∈ X⁰` of codimension `0` and the canonical
morphisms `j_η : Spec(𝒪_{X, η}) ⟶ X` are defined — this is the presentation `P` of the
schematic locus whose existence is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_codimensionZeroPresentation`
— and the sheaf of meromorphic functions `𝒦_X` is both the direct sum and the product over `X⁰`
of the direct images `j_{η, *}𝒪_{X, η}`:

`𝒦_X = ⨁_{η ∈ X⁰} j_{η, *}𝒪_{X, η} = ∏_{η ∈ X⁰} j_{η, *}𝒪_{X, η}`.

The two identifications are the canonical comparisons: the one into the product has components
the canonical maps `𝒦_X ⟶ j_{η, *}𝒪_{X, η}` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CodimensionZeroPresentation.genericPointComparison`, and the one out of
the direct sum is `CategoryTheory.Limits.sigmaPiComparison`, the identity on the diagonal and
zero off it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_codimensionZeroPresentation_isIso_genericPointComparison
    (hwa : ∀ z ∈ weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS z = 0)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X.1)
    (hmono : HasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X.1) :
    ∃ P : CodimensionZeroPresentation B S hS X.1,
      IsIso P.genericPointModuleComparisonPi ∧
        letI : DecidableEq (CodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X.1) := Classical.decEq _
        letI := P.hasCoproduct_genericPointModule
        IsIso (sigmaPiComparison fun η : CodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X.1 =>
          P.genericPointModule η.2)
declarations.comment:
the first conclusion: the sheaf of meromorphic functions is the direct sum, and
equally the product, over the codimension-zero points of the direct images of the local rings
there, through the canonical comparisons

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CodimensionZeroPresentation.exists_codimensionZeroPresentation_isIso_meromorphicSectionComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENA, the second conclusion.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` such
that

* (a) every weakly associated point of `X` is a point of codimension `0`,
* (b) every quasi-compact open of every étale scheme chart of `X` has finitely many irreducible
  components, the condition of Stacks 0BB1, and
* (c) every point of codimension `0` of `X` is represented by a monomorphism from the spectrum
  of a field.

Then the local rings `𝒪_{X, η}` at the points `η ∈ X⁰` of codimension `0` and the canonical
morphisms `j_η : Spec(𝒪_{X, η}) ⟶ X` are defined — this is the presentation `P` of the
schematic locus whose existence is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_codimensionZeroPresentation`
— and for every quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` the sheaf `𝒦_X(F)` of meromorphic sections of
`F` is both the direct sum and the product over `X⁰` of the direct images `j_{η, *}j_η^*F` of the
inverse images of `F`:

`𝒦_X(F) = ⨁_{η ∈ X⁰} j_{η, *}j_η^*F = ∏_{η ∈ X⁰} j_{η, *}j_η^*F`.

The two identifications are the canonical comparisons: the one into the product is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CodimensionZeroPresentation.meromorphicSectionGenericPointComparisonPi`,
the transpose across sheafification of the family `a ⊗ s ↦ a · s|_{U ×_X Spec(𝒪_{X, η})}`, and
the one out of the direct sum is `CategoryTheory.Limits.sigmaPiComparison`, the identity on the
diagonal and zero off it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_codimensionZeroPresentation_isIso_meromorphicSectionComparison
    (hwa : ∀ z ∈ weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS z = 0)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X.1)
    (hmono : HasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X.1) :
    ∃ P : CodimensionZeroPresentation B S hS X.1,
      ∀ F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2, F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite →
        IsIso (P.meromorphicSectionGenericPointComparisonPi F) ∧
          letI : DecidableEq (CodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X.1) := Classical.decEq _
          letI := P.hasCoproduct_genericPointMeromorphicModule F
          IsIso (sigmaPiComparison fun η : CodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X.1 =>
            SheafOfModules.uliftObj.{_, _, _, _, u + 1}
              (P.genericPointMeromorphicModule η.2 F))
declarations.comment:
the second conclusion: for every quasi-coherent module the sheaf of its
meromorphic sections is the direct sum, and equally the product, over the codimension-zero points
of the direct images of its inverse images there, through the canonical comparisons

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_ringEquiv_rationalFunctions_meromorphicFunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENA, the third conclusion.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S`
such that (a) every weakly associated point of `X` has codimension `0`, (b) the irreducible
components of `X` are locally finite, and (c) every codimension-zero point of `X` is
representable by a monomorphism from the spectrum of a field.  Then the ring `R(X)` of rational
functions of `X` — the classes, modulo agreement on a dense open subspace, of morphisms to the
relative affine line defined on a dense open subspace, of Stacks 0EMP — is the ring
`Γ(X, 𝒦_X)` of meromorphic functions on `X`, the global sections of the sheaf of meromorphic
functions of Stacks 0EN3.

The comparison is the canonical one: a rational function represented by a morphism `ν` regular
on a dense open subspace `W` is sent to the meromorphic function whose value at an étale chart
`U` lying in `W` is the image in `𝒦_X(U)` of the coordinate of `ν` at `U`, and the displayed
equation says exactly that.  It is a ring homomorphism by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalToMeromorphicRingHom`, injective by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.injective_rationalToMeromorphic` and surjective by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjective_rationalToMeromorphic`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ringEquiv_rationalFunctions_meromorphicFunction
    (hwa : ∀ z ∈ weaklyAssociatedPointsOfSpace B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS z = 0)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X.1)
    (hmono : HasMonomorphicCodimensionZeroPoints B S hS X.1) :
    ∃ e : rationalFunctions B S hS X.2 ≃+* MeromorphicFunction B S hS X.1 X.2,
      ∀ (f : PartialMap B S hS X.2 (affineLineFunctor B S hS))
        (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (τ : yoneda.obj U.obj.left ⟶ f.domain.toFunctor),
        τ ≫ f.domain.ι = U.1.hom →
        (e (PartialMap.toRationalMap B S hS f)).val (op U) =
          ((toMeromorphicFunctionSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2).hom.app (op U)).hom
            (affineLineCoordinate B S hS (op U.obj.left)
              (f.hom.app (op U.obj.left) (yonedaEquiv τ)))
declarations.comment:
the third conclusion: the ring of rational functions of the space is its ring of
meromorphic functions, R(X) = Γ(X, 𝒦_X), through the comparison that reads a rational function
regular on a dense open subspace as a meromorphic function on every étale chart lying in that
subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRegularMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
A meromorphic section `s` of a sheaf of `𝒪_F`-modules `L` is *regular* when the induced map
`𝒦_F ⟶ 𝒦_F(L)`, multiplication by `s`, is injective; this is tested on every étale chart of `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsRegularMeromorphicSection (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (L : Modules.{u, max u z} B S hS F hF)
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} B S hS F hF L) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSectionOfGood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENC, part (2), in this chapter's vocabulary.** The pullback `f^*s` of a nonzero —
that is, regular — meromorphic section of an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module `ℒ` is again a nonzero
meromorphic section, now of `f^*ℒ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSectionOfGood
    (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sY hY L)
    (hσ : IsRegularMeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem Y hY.1 L σ) :
    IsRegularMeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1
      (pullbackSheaf D sY hY sX hX (spaceMorphismOfGood D sX hX sY hY (f := f)) L)
      (pullbackMeromorphicSectionOfGood D sX hX sY hY L σ hPull)
declarations.comment:
part (2) in the vocabulary of this chapter: the pullback f^*s of a regular
meromorphic section of an invertible sheaf on a good algebraic space is regular

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartMeromorphicFunctionPullback
declarations.doc:
**The chartwise pullback of meromorphic functions on the sheaves.**  Over a commuting square
of étale charts `U` of `X` above `V` of `Y` the comparison `𝒦_Y ⟶ f_*𝒦_X` projects to a
homomorphism of commutative rings `𝒦_Y(V) ⟶ 𝒦_X(U)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartMeromorphicFunctionPullback (d : ChartDiagram B S hS X.1 Y.1 f.hom) :
    (meromorphicFunctionSheaf B S hS Y.1 Y.2).obj.obj (op d.V) →+*
      (meromorphicFunctionSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2).obj.obj (op d.U)
declarations.comment: part (1), chartwise on the SHEAVES of meromorphic functions: the fraction rule a/b ↦ f♯a/f♯b over an étale chart diagram as a homomorphism 𝒦_Y(V) ⟶ 𝒦_X(U), where AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartPullbackMeromorphicFunctions is the same rule on the presheaves of sectionwise localizations. This is the coefficient rule for part (1) read through the second of the two descriptions of 𝒦(F) in Stacks 0EN5, the sheafification of F ⊗_𝒪 𝒦, which is the one AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MeromorphicSection and hence part (2) use. The global map Γ(Y, 𝒦_Y(F)) ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒦_X(f^*F)) of part (1) is asserted for the first description by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackSheafifiedRegularSections, and for the second by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection, which is built over this rule. Part (2) is proved for an invertible module by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSection, over that same description, and is not asserted here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartPullbackMeromorphicFunctions
declarations.doc:
**The local fraction rule `a/b ↦ f^♯a/f^♯b`.**  When pullbacks of meromorphic functions
are defined for `f`, the pullback along a chart diagram carries the sectionwise localization
`𝒮_Y(V)⁻¹𝒪_Y(V)` into `𝒮_X(U)⁻¹𝒪_X(U)`: a denominator regular over `V` pulls back to one
regular over `U`, so the universal property of the localization applies.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartPullbackMeromorphicFunctions
    (hf : PullbacksMeromorphicSections B S hS f) (d : ChartDiagram B S hS X Y f) :
    (regularSectionsSubpresheaf B S hS Y hY).localizationPresheaf.obj (op d.V) →+*
      (regularSectionsSubpresheaf B S hS X hX).localizationPresheaf.obj (op d.U)
declarations.comment: part (1), chartwise: the local fraction rule a/b ↦ f♯a/f♯b over an étale chart diagram, on the presheaf of sectionwise localizations. The global map Γ(Y, 𝒦_Y(F)) ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒦_X(f^*F)) of part (1) is asserted for ONE of the two spellings of 𝒦(F): AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackSheafifiedRegularSections gives it with 𝒦(F) read as the first description in Stacks 0EN5, the sheafification of the presheaf of sectionwise localizations. It is asserted for AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MeromorphicSection, which realizes Stacks 0EN5 through the other description there, the sheafification of F ⊗_𝒪 𝒦, by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection. Stacks 0EMD, which identifies the two descriptions, is not proved and neither map uses it. Part (2), stated through AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRegularMeromorphicSection, is not asserted here; it is proved for an invertible module by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSection. Erratum: part (2) as printed reads 'invertible 𝒪_X-module', but pulling back along f : X ⟶ Y needs an 𝒪_Y-module, which is what the scheme-level form of the lemma, 02OY, says

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fmapMeromorphicFunctions
declarations.doc:
The chartwise fraction rules assemble into an `f`-map of presheaves of sets from the
sectionwise localization `𝒮_Y⁻¹𝒪_Y` to `𝒮_X⁻¹𝒪_X`, in the sense of Stacks 03G3: pullback of
meromorphic functions is compatible with étale restriction of both charts of a diagram.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fmapMeromorphicFunctions (hf : PullbacksMeromorphicSections B S hS f) :
    FMap B S hS X Y f
      ((regularSectionsSubpresheaf B S hS X hX).localizationPresheaf ⋙
        CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{u})
      ((regularSectionsSubpresheaf B S hS Y hY).localizationPresheaf ⋙
        CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{u})
declarations.comment: part (1), chartwise: the fraction rule is canonical, being an f-map of Stacks 03G3 on the presheaves of sectionwise localizations. The global pullback map of part (1) is asserted for the sheafification of those presheaves, the first of the two descriptions of 𝒦 in Stacks 0EN5, by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackSheafifiedRegularSections, and for the second, AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MeromorphicSection, by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection. Part (2) is not asserted here; it is proved for an invertible module by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackSheafifiedRegularSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENC, part (1), for the sheafification of the sectionwise localizations.**  When
pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined for `f`, there is a canonical map on global
sections

`Γ(Y, 𝒦_Y(M)) ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒦_X(f^*M))`

with the sheaf of meromorphic sections taken as Stacks 0EN5 describes it, the sheafification of
the presheaf of sectionwise localizations `U ↦ 𝒮(U)⁻¹M(U)`.

It is the chartwise fraction rule `m/b ↦ (f^*m)/(f^♯b)` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartPullbackMeromorphicSections`, carried along three identifications:
the descent of Stacks 03G4 for a presheaf of sections on the target
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.meromorphicSectionsDescendedHom`), the extension of a morphism into a
sheaf over the sheafification of its source
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafifyForgetHomEquiv`), and the identification of the global
sections of a direct image with those of the sheaf
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.equivSectionsSpacesDirectImage`).

Only the additive structure of the sectionwise localizations is used, so the map is produced on
the underlying sets; it is a map of sets of global sections and is not here asserted to be
additive.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackSheafifiedRegularSections
    (hf : PullbacksMeromorphicSections B S hS f.hom) :
    (regularSectionsLocalizationModuleSheafSet B S hS Y.1 Y.2 M).obj.sections →
      (regularSectionsLocalizationModuleSheafSet B S hS X.1 X.2
        ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj M)).obj.sections
declarations.comment: part (1), for the first of the two descriptions of the sheaf of meromorphic sections in Stacks 0EN5: the global map Γ(Y, 𝒦_Y(F)) ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒦_X(f^*F)) with 𝒦(F) taken to be the sheafification of the presheaf of sectionwise localizations U ↦ 𝒮(U)⁻¹F(U). The same map for AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MeromorphicSection, which realizes Stacks 0EN5 through the other description there, the sheafification of the extension of scalars F ⊗_𝒪 𝒦, is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection. Stacks 0EMD, which identifies the two descriptions, is not proved and neither map uses it. Additivity of the map is not asserted, and neither is part (2), which is stated through AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRegularMeromorphicSection and proved for an invertible module by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartPullbackMeromorphicSections
declarations.doc:
**The local fraction rule `m/b ↦ (f^*m)/(f^♯b)`.**  When pullbacks of meromorphic functions
are defined for `f`, the pullback along a chart diagram carries the sectionwise localization
`𝒮_Y(V)⁻¹M(V)` of a sheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules `M` into `𝒮_X(U)⁻¹(f^*M)(U)`: the numerator is
pulled back by the chart component of the unit of the Stacks 03D7 adjunction and the
denominator by the fraction rule on the structure sheaf, which inverts it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartPullbackMeromorphicSections
    (hf : PullbacksMeromorphicSections B S hS f.hom)
    (d : ChartDiagram B S hS X.1 Y.1 f.hom) :
    (regularSectionsLocalizationModule B S hS Y.1 Y.2 M).obj (op d.V) →+
      (regularSectionsLocalizationModule B S hS X.1 X.2
        ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj M)).obj (op d.U)
declarations.comment: part (1), chartwise for an arbitrary sheaf of 𝒪_Y-modules F: the local fraction rule m/b ↦ (f^*m)/(f♯b) on the sectionwise localizations over an étale chart diagram. This generalizes the structure-sheaf case AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartPullbackMeromorphicFunctions from F = 𝒪_Y to an arbitrary F. The global map Γ(Y, 𝒦_Y(F)) ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒦_X(f^*F)) of part (1) is asserted for ONE of the two spellings of 𝒦(F): AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackSheafifiedRegularSections gives it with 𝒦(F) read as the first description in Stacks 0EN5, the sheafification of this presheaf of sectionwise localizations, and AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection gives it for the other description there, the sheafification of F ⊗_𝒪 𝒦, which is the one AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MeromorphicSection uses. Stacks 0EMD, which identifies the two descriptions, is not proved and neither map uses it. Part (2), stated through AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRegularMeromorphicSection, is not asserted here; it is proved for an invertible module by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fmapMeromorphicSections
declarations.doc:
The chartwise fraction rules for a sheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules `M` assemble into an `f`-map of
presheaves of sets from the sectionwise localization `𝒮_Y⁻¹M` to `𝒮_X⁻¹(f^*M)`, in the sense of
Stacks 03G3: the rule `m/b ↦ (f^*m)/(f^♯b)` is compatible with étale restriction of both charts
of a diagram.  This is the module-level form of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fmapMeromorphicFunctions`, which is the case `M = 𝒪_Y`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fmapMeromorphicSections
    (hf : PullbacksMeromorphicSections B S hS f.hom) :
    FMap B S hS X.1 Y.1 f.hom
      ((regularSectionsLocalizationModule B S hS X.1 X.2
          ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj M)).presheaf ⋙
        CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})
      ((regularSectionsLocalizationModule B S hS Y.1 Y.2 M).presheaf ⋙
        CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})
declarations.comment: part (1), chartwise for an arbitrary sheaf of 𝒪_Y-modules F: the fraction rule m/b ↦ (f^*m)/(f♯b) is canonical, being an f-map of Stacks 03G3 from the presheaf of sectionwise localizations of F to that of f^*F. This generalizes the structure-sheaf case AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fmapMeromorphicFunctions from F = 𝒪_Y to an arbitrary F. It is a statement about the presheaves of sectionwise localizations, not about their sheafifications; the global map Γ(Y, 𝒦_Y(F)) ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒦_X(f^*F)) of part (1) that this f-map descends to is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackSheafifiedRegularSections, which is part (1) with 𝒦(F) read as the first description in Stacks 0EN5, the sheafification of these sectionwise localizations. Part (1) for AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MeromorphicSection, which realizes Stacks 0EN5 through the other description there, the sheafification of F ⊗_𝒪 𝒦, is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection, built over the same rule taken over the sheaf 𝒦 instead of the presheaf 𝒮⁻¹𝒪. Part (2), stated through AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRegularMeromorphicSection, is not asserted here; it is proved for an invertible module by AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENC, part (1).**  When pullbacks of meromorphic functions are defined for `f`,
there is a canonical map on global meromorphic sections

`Γ(Y, 𝒦_Y(M)) ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒦_X(f^*M))`

with `𝒦(M)` the sheaf of meromorphic sections of Stacks 0EN5,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.meromorphicSectionSheaf`, and a meromorphic section a global section of
it, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MeromorphicSection`.

It is the chartwise rule `m ⊗ a ↦ (f^*m) ⊗ (f^♯a)` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartPullbackMeromorphicSectionsSheaf`, carried along three
identifications: the descent of Stacks 03G4 for a presheaf of sections on the target
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.meromorphicSectionSheafDescendedHom`), the extension of a morphism
into a sheaf over the sheafification of its source
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafifyForgetHomEquiv`), and the identification of the global
sections of a direct image with those of the sheaf
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.equivSectionsSpacesDirectImage`).

Only the additive structure of `M ⊗_{𝒪} 𝒦` is used, so the map is produced on the underlying
sets and nothing in the construction is a map of abelian groups.  That it is nonetheless
additive and `𝒦`-semilinear is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_eval_add` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_eval_smul_chartDiagram`, proved from its
values; `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_add` is global additivity against
the group structure on global sections.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackMeromorphicSection :
    MeromorphicSection.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2 M →
      MeromorphicSection.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj M)
declarations.comment: part (1): the global map Γ(Y, 𝒦_Y(F)) ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒦_X(f^*F)) on AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MeromorphicSection, the meromorphic sections of Stacks 0EN5 as the library spells them -- global sections of the sheafification of F ⊗_𝒪 𝒦. AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackSheafifiedRegularSections is the same map for the other description in Stacks 0EN5, the sheafification of the presheaf of sectionwise localizations. Additivity and semilinearity of this map are AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_eval_add and AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_eval_smul_chartDiagram, and global additivity is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_add; part (2) for an invertible module is AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_eval_add
declarations.doc:
**The global pullback map of Stacks 0ENC, part (1) is additive.**  Let `w` be a meromorphic
section of `M` whose value over every étale scheme chart of `Y` is the sum of the values of `s`
and `s'` there.  Then the value of the pullback of `w` over every étale scheme chart of `X` is
the sum of the values of the pullbacks of `s` and `s'`.

A meromorphic section is a section of a sheaf of modules, a type carrying no module structure, so
this is the assertion that the global map of part (1) is additive.

Every chart of `X` is covered by the charts of `X` of affine commuting squares
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_chartDiagram_ofArrows`), over which the identity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_eval_add_chartDiagram`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackMeromorphicSection_eval_add
    (s s' w : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2 M)
    (hw : ∀ V : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1, w.eval (op V) = s.eval (op V) + s'.eval (op V))
    (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) :
    (pullbackMeromorphicSection B S hS f M hf w).eval (op U) =
      (pullbackMeromorphicSection B S hS f M hf s).eval (op U) +
        (pullbackMeromorphicSection B S hS f M hf s').eval (op U)
declarations.comment: the algebra of the part (1) map, which its construction leaves unasserted: the global map on meromorphic sections is additive

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_eval_smul_chartDiagram
declarations.doc:
**The global pullback map of Stacks 0ENC, part (1) is semilinear over the chartwise pullback
of meromorphic functions.**  Let `d` be a commuting square of affine étale scheme charts, `d.U`
of `X` above `d.V` of `Y`, let `c` be a meromorphic function on `d.V` and let the meromorphic
sections `s` and `s'` of `M` satisfy `s|_{d.V} = c · s'|_{d.V}`.  Then over `d.U`

`(f^*s)|_{d.U} = (f^♯c) · (f^*s')|_{d.U}`,

with `f^♯` the chartwise pullback of meromorphic functions
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartMeromorphicPullbackHom`.

Over a covering family of `d.U` refining the sieve over which `s'` is an honest element of
`M ⊗_{𝒪_Y} 𝒦_Y` both values are computed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_eval_chartDiagram`, and the identity is that
the chartwise rule carries a coefficient to its pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackMeromorphicSection_eval_smul_chartDiagram
    (s s' : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2 M)
    (d : ChartDiagram B S hS X.1 Y.1 f.hom)
    (hU : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj
      ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X.1).obj d.U)))
    (hV : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj
      ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y.1).obj d.V)))
    (c : (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (meromorphicRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).O).obj.obj
      (op d.V))
    (hc : s.eval (op d.V) = c • s'.eval (op d.V)) :
    (pullbackMeromorphicSection B S hS f M hf s).eval (op d.U) =
      chartMeromorphicRingedSitePullbackHom B S hS f hf d c •
        (pullbackMeromorphicSection B S hS f M hf s').eval (op d.U)
declarations.comment: the algebra of the part (1) map, which its construction leaves unasserted: the global map on meromorphic sections is semilinear over the chartwise pullback of meromorphic functions. The coefficient over the chart of X of a commuting square of affine etale charts is the image of the coefficient over its chart of Y under AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartMeromorphicPullbackHom; a single coefficient over all of X would need the global map on meromorphic functions, which is not available

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_sectionsMap
declarations.doc:
The global pullback of meromorphic sections is natural in the module: for a morphism
`φ : M ⟶ N` of sheaves of `𝒪_Y`-modules the pullback of the image of a meromorphic section of
`M` under `𝒦_Y(φ)` is the image of the pullback of that section under `𝒦_X(f^*φ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackMeromorphicSection_sectionsMap (φ : M ⟶ N)
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2 M) :
    pullbackMeromorphicSection B S hS f N hf
        (SheafOfModules.sectionsMap (meromorphicSectionSheafMap B S hS Y.1 Y.2 φ) s) =
      SheafOfModules.sectionsMap
        (meromorphicSectionSheafMap B S hS X.1 X.2 ((modulePullback B S hS f).map φ))
        (pullbackMeromorphicSection B S hS f M hf s)
declarations.comment: the algebra of the part (1) map, which its construction leaves unasserted: the global map on meromorphic sections is natural in the module, for the action of the sheaf of meromorphic sections on morphisms of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSection
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces for which pullbacks of meromorphic
functions are defined, let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module and let `s` be a regular meromorphic
section of `L`. Then the pullback `f^*s` is a regular meromorphic section of the invertible
`𝒪_X`-module `f^*L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSection (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : PullbacksMeromorphicSections B S hS f.hom) (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structureCommRings B S hS Y)
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS Y).property L)
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2 L)
    (hs : IsRegularMeromorphicSection.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2 L s) :
    IsRegularMeromorphicSection.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj L)
      (pullbackMeromorphicSection B S hS f L hf s)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.evalPartial_eq
declarations.doc: Evaluation is computed by any lift of the generic field-valued point.
declarations.statement:
theorem evalPartial_eq (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X)
    (hp : p.class B S hS X = genericPoint B S hS hX hInt)
    (f : PartialMap B S hS hX (affineLineFunctor B S hS))
    (j : yoneda.obj (p.siteObject B S hS X) ⟶ f.domain.toFunctor)
    (hj : j ≫ f.domain.ι = fieldMorphism B S hS X p) :
    evalPartial B S hS hX hInt p hp f =
      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of p.carrier)).hom.hom
        (affineLineCoordinate B S hS (Opposite.op (p.siteObject B S hS X))
          (yonedaEquiv (j ≫ f.hom)))
declarations.comment: the characterisation of evaluation at the generic point: the value on a representative is its coordinate along any factorisation of the residue-field morphism through the domain, independently of the factorisation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.evalRingHom
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at the generic point, as a ring homomorphism from the rational functions to
the field of a field-valued representative of that point.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def evalRingHom (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X)
    (hp : p.class B S hS X = genericPoint B S hS hX hInt) :
    rationalFunctions B S hS hX →+* p.carrier
declarations.comment: evaluation of rational functions at the generic point, as a ring homomorphism R(X) → κ(η)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isField_residueField_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0END.** The residue field at the generic point of an integral algebraic space
over `S` is a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isField_residueField_genericPoint (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) :
    IsField (residueField B S hS X hInt.2.1 (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt))
declarations.comment: the residue field at the generic point is a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.evalRingHom_injective
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at the generic point is injective: a rational function whose value there
vanishes has a representative on a representable dense open chart through the generic point,
and the coordinate of that representative, a regular function on an integral scheme, is
determined by its value at the dense point of that scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem evalRingHom_injective (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X)
    (hp : p.class B S hS X = genericPoint B S hS hX hInt) :
    Function.Injective (evalRingHom B S hS hX hInt p hp)
declarations.comment: injectivity of evaluation at the generic point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.evalRingHom_surjective
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at the generic point is surjective: the field of a monomorphic representative
of the generic point is the residue field of a representable dense open chart at the point
below the generic point, every element of that residue field is the value of a regular
function on a smaller open set, and that open set carries a representable dense open chart
again.
declarations.statement:
theorem evalRingHom_surjective (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X)
    (hp : p.class B S hS X = genericPoint B S hS hX hInt)
    (hmono : Mono (fieldMorphism B S hS X p)) :
    Function.Surjective (evalRingHom B S hS hX hInt p hp)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of evaluation at the generic point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.evalRingHom_bijective
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at the generic point is a bijection onto the field of a monomorphic
field-valued representative of that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem evalRingHom_bijective (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X)
    (hp : p.class B S hS X = genericPoint B S hS hX hInt)
    (hmono : Mono (fieldMorphism B S hS X p)) :
    Function.Bijective (evalRingHom B S hS hX hInt p hp)
declarations.comment: bijectivity of evaluation at the generic point, on a monomorphic field-valued representative

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionsRingEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0END.** The ring of rational functions of an integral algebraic space over `S` is
the residue field at its generic point: evaluation at the generic point is an isomorphism of
rings from the rational functions of Tag 0EMP onto the residue field of Tag 0EMW.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rationalFunctionsRingEquiv (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) :
    rationalFunctions B S hS hX ≃+*
      residueField B S hS X hInt.2.1 (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt)
declarations.comment: the identification R(X) = κ(η) of the rational functions with the residue field at the generic point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isField_rationalFunctions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0END.** The ring of rational functions of an integral algebraic space over `S` is
a field: it is the residue field at the generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isField_rationalFunctions (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) : IsField (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
declarations.comment: the rational functions of an integral algebraic space form a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isField_neighborhoodStalk_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
The local ring of an elementary étale neighbourhood of the generic point of an integral
algebraic space, at the marked point of that neighbourhood, is a field: the scheme of the
neighbourhood is reduced, because reducedness is an étale-local property and the neighbourhood
is étale over the space, and the local ring has Krull dimension zero, because the generic point
is a point of codimension zero by Stacks 0ABV and the dimension of the local ring of an
algebraic space at a point is measured on any étale chart above it by Stacks 0BAM.
declarations.statement:
theorem isField_neighborhoodStalk_genericPoint (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X)
    (E : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt)) :
    IsField (E.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk E.point)
declarations.comment: the local ring of an elementary étale neighbourhood at its marked point, over the generic point, is a field; the neighbourhood is a parameter because the statement is about it, and Tag 0BBP provides one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.evalNeighborhoodRingEquiv
declarations.doc:
The ring of rational functions of an integral algebraic space is the residue field of any
elementary étale neighbourhood of the generic point at its marked point: that residue field is
a *monomorphic* field-valued representative of the generic point, by the data of Stacks 0BGU,
so evaluation at the generic point is bijective onto it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def evalNeighborhoodRingEquiv (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X)
    (E : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt)) :
    rationalFunctions B S hS hX ≃+* E.scheme.left.1.residueField E.point
declarations.comment: the rational functions are the residue field of an elementary étale neighbourhood of the generic point at its marked point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isField_henselianLocalRing_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0END.** The henselian local ring of Stacks 0BGW at the generic point of an integral
algebraic space is a field: it is a henselisation of the local ring of the elementary étale
neighbourhood of Stacks 0BBP at its marked point by Stacks 0EMY, that local ring is a field, and
a henselisation of a field is a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isField_henselianLocalRing_genericPoint (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) :
    IsField (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt) hInt.2.1 :
      Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: the henselian local ring O^h_{X,η} at the generic point is a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_stalkToHenselianLocalRing_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
The canonical map of Stacks 0EMY from the local ring of an elementary étale neighbourhood of
the generic point into the henselian local ring is bijective: it is the structure map of a
henselisation of a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_stalkToHenselianLocalRing_genericPoint (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X)
    (E : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt)) :
    Function.Bijective (stalkToHenselianLocalRing B S hS X hX
      (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt) hInt.2.1 E)
declarations.comment: bijectivity at the generic point of the canonical map O_{U,u} → O^h_{X,η} of Tag 0EMY

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionsHenselianRingEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0END.** The ring of rational functions of an integral algebraic space over `S` is
the henselian local ring of Stacks 0BGW at its generic point: the comparison is built from the
elementary étale neighbourhood of Stacks 0BBP.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rationalFunctionsHenselianRingEquiv (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) :
    rationalFunctions B S hS hX ≃+*
      (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt) hInt.2.1 : Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: the identification R(X) = O^h_{X,η} of the rational functions with the henselian local ring at the generic point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionsHenselianRingEquivOfNeighborhood_eq
declarations.doc:
The identification with the henselian local ring is pinned down without inverses: it
carries a rational function to the canonical image of *any* element of the local ring of the
neighbourhood whose residue is the value of that function at the generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalFunctionsHenselianRingEquivOfNeighborhood_eq (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X)
    (E : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt))
    (x : rationalFunctions B S hS hX) (r : E.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk E.point)
    (hr : IsLocalRing.residue (E.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk E.point) r =
      evalRingHom B S hS hX hInt (genericNeighborhoodFieldPoint B S hS hX hInt E)
        (neighborhoodFieldPoint_class B S hS X hX (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt) E) x) :
    rationalFunctionsHenselianRingEquivOfNeighborhood B S hS hX hInt E x =
      stalkToHenselianLocalRing B S hS X hX (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt) hInt.2.1 E r
declarations.comment: the characterisation of that identification: a rational function goes to the canonical image of any element of the neighbourhood's local ring whose residue is its value at the generic point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.residueFieldHenselianRingEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0END.** The residue field at the generic point of an integral algebraic space over
`S` is the henselian local ring of Stacks 0BGW there: both are the ring of rational
functions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def residueFieldHenselianRingEquiv (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) :
    residueField B S hS X hInt.2.1 (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt) ≃+*
      (henselianLocalRing B S hS X hX (genericPoint B S hS hX hInt) hInt.2.1 : Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: the identification O^h_{X,η} = κ(η) of the henselian local ring at the generic point with the residue field there

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionsHenselianRingEquiv_eq_trans
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0END.** The tag asserts one chain of identifications `R(X) = O^h_{X,η} = κ(η)`, and
the three identifications are indeed the three edges of one commuting triangle: going from the
rational functions to the henselian local ring is going to the residue field and on from
there.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalFunctionsHenselianRingEquiv_eq_trans (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) :
    rationalFunctionsHenselianRingEquiv B S hS hX hInt =
      (rationalFunctionsRingEquiv B S hS hX hInt).trans
        (residueFieldHenselianRingEquiv B S hS hX hInt)
declarations.comment: the chain R(X) = O^h_{X,η} = κ(η): the three identifications commute

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.functionField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENE.** The function field, or field of rational functions, of an integral
algebraic space `X` over `S`: the ring `R(X)` of rational functions of Tag 0EMP, which
Tag 0END shows to be a field by identifying it with the residue field at the generic
point.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def functionField (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) : Field (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
declarations.comment: the function field R(X) = k(X) of an integral algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.injective_closureSingleton_points
declarations.doc:
Two points of a decent algebraic space over `S` with the same closure are equal: the map
from (1) to (2) is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_closureSingleton_points (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    Function.Injective (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton (X := points B S hS X))
declarations.comment: the map from (1) to (2) is injective, unconditionally

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_closureSingleton_points
declarations.doc:
Taking the closure of a point is a bijection from the points of a decent algebraic space
`X` over `S` onto the irreducible closed subsets of `|X|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_closureSingleton_points (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    Function.Bijective (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton (X := points B S hS X))
declarations.comment: the bijection from (1) to (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IntegralClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
An *integral closed subspace* of an algebraic space `X` over `S` is a closed subspace of
`X`, in the sense of Stacks 02YU, which is an integral algebraic space over `S`, in the sense of
Stacks 0AD4.
declarations.statement: structure IntegralClosedSubspace (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
declarations.comment: (3): the integral closed subspaces of an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.integralClosedSubspaceSupport
declarations.doc:
The set of points of an integral closed subspace of `X`, as an irreducible closed subset
of `|X|`. This is the map from (3) to (2).
declarations.statement:
def integralClosedSubspaceSupport (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace B S hS X) : IrreducibleCloseds (points B S hS X)
declarations.comment: the map from (3) to (2): the point set of an integral closed subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.injective_integralClosedSubspaceSupport
declarations.doc:
An integral closed subspace of an algebraic space over `S` is determined by its set of
points: the map from (3) to (2) is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_integralClosedSubspaceSupport (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    Function.Injective (integralClosedSubspaceSupport B S hS hX)
declarations.comment: the map from (3) to (2) is injective, unconditionally

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjective_integralClosedSubspaceSupport
declarations.doc:
Every irreducible closed subset of `|X|`, for `X` a decent algebraic space over `S`, is the
set of points of an integral closed subspace: the map from (3) to (2) is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_integralClosedSubspaceSupport (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    Function.Surjective (integralClosedSubspaceSupport B S hS hX)
declarations.comment: the map from (3) to (2) is surjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_integralClosedSubspaceSupport
declarations.doc:
Taking the set of points is a bijection from the integral closed subspaces of a decent
algebraic space `X` over `S` onto the irreducible closed subsets of `|X|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_integralClosedSubspaceSupport (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    Function.Bijective (integralClosedSubspaceSupport B S hS hX)
declarations.comment: the bijection from (3) to (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.degree_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENH.** For a dominant morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` and a morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` of
integral algebraic spaces over `S`, the degree of `X` over `Z` is the degree of `X` over `Y`
times the degree of `Y` over `Z`.

The generic point of `|X|` maps to the generic point of `|Y|` because `f` is dominant, so all
three degrees are read off the same tower of residue fields, and degrees multiply in a tower
of field extensions (Stacks 09G9).
declarations.statement:
theorem degree_comp (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hXint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X)
    (hYint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y) (hZint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hf : IsDominant B S hS f) :
    degree B S hS hX hZ hXint hZint (f ≫ g) =
      degree B S hS hX hY hXint hYint f * degree B S hS hY hZ hYint hZint g
declarations.comment: multiplicativity of the degree; local finiteness of type of the two morphisms, finiteness of the two residue field extensions and dominance of g are not needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENJ, part (1).** A *prime divisor* of `X` is an integral closed subspace of `X`
whose generic point has codimension one in `X`.
declarations.statement: structure PrimeDivisor
declarations.comment: part (1): prime divisors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.WeilDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENJ, part (2).** The group `Div(X)` of *Weil divisors* of `X`: integer
coefficient families on prime divisors of `X` whose nonzero part has locally finite support
in `|X|`.
declarations.statement: def WeilDivisor : AddSubgroup (PrimeDivisor B S hS X → ℤ)
declarations.comment: part (2): Weil divisors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.neighborhoodTotalFractionRingToGeneric_pullback_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENK, computed on an arbitrary affine chart.** The canonical map from the function
field of a decent, locally Noetherian, integral algebraic space into the total ring of fractions
of the henselian local ring at the generic point of a prime divisor is computed on *any* affine
elementary étale neighbourhood of that generic point, not only on the chart of Stacks 0BBP which
defines it.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.neighborhoodTotalFractionRingToGeneric_pullback_eq
    [IsLocalRing ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)]
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X)
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Y))
    (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX (Z.genericPoint B S hS X))
    [IsAffine U.scheme.left.1] [IsReduced U.scheme.left.1]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian U.scheme.left.1]
    (hCofiltered :
      IsCofiltered (ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX (Z.genericPoint B S hS X)))
    (r : rationalFunctions B S hS hX) :
    Z.neighborhoodTotalFractionRingToGeneric B S hS hX hdec U hCofiltered
        (rationalFunctionsToTotalFractionRing B S hS hX U.scheme U.toSpace U.etale_toSpace r) =
      Z.rationalFunctionsToGenericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec hInt hN r
declarations.comment: independence of the canonical map R(X) → Q(𝒪^h_{X, ξ}) of the affine elementary étale neighbourhood used to compute it -- a verification the source omits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.rationalFunctionsToGenericTotalFractionRing
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from the function field of a decent, locally Noetherian, integral algebraic
space into the total ring of fractions of the henselian local ring at the generic point of a
prime divisor: a rational function is pulled back to the spectrum of the total ring of fractions
of the global sections `A` of the chosen affine elementary étale neighbourhood `(U, u)` of the
generic point, and then pushed along `A → 𝒪_{U, u} → 𝒪^h_{X, ξ}`.
declarations.statement:
def PrimeDivisor.rationalFunctionsToGenericTotalFractionRing :
    rationalFunctions B S hS hX →+* Z.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec
