declarations.comment: the canonical map R(X) → Q(𝒪^h_{X, ξ}) from the function field into the total ring of fractions of the henselian local ring at the generic point of a prime divisor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.injective_rationalFunctionsToGenericTotalFractionRing
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from the function field of a decent, locally Noetherian, integral algebraic
space into the total ring of fractions of the henselian local ring at the generic point of a
prime divisor is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.injective_rationalFunctionsToGenericTotalFractionRing :
    Function.Injective
      (Z.rationalFunctionsToGenericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec hInt hN)
declarations.comment: injectivity of the canonical map R(X) → Q(𝒪^h_{X, ξ}), the function field being a field and the total ring of fractions nontrivial

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.genericFractionEmbedding
declarations.doc:
At every prime divisor of a decent, locally Noetherian, integral algebraic space: the
henselian local ring at the generic point of the prime divisor is a nontrivial Noetherian local
ring of dimension at most one, and the function field embeds in its total ring of fractions.
declarations.statement: def genericFractionEmbedding : GenericFractionEmbedding B S hS hX hdec
declarations.comment: the conclusions of the lemma assembled at every prime divisor, as the data the order of vanishing along a prime divisor is defined from

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.isReduced_and_ringKrullDim_eq_one_and_isNoetherianRing_genericHenselianLocalRing
declarations.doc:
The henselian local ring at the generic point of a prime divisor of a decent, locally
Noetherian, integral algebraic space is reduced, of Krull dimension one, and Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem
  PrimeDivisor.isReduced_and_ringKrullDim_eq_one_and_isNoetherianRing_genericHenselianLocalRing
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X)
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Y))
    (Z : PrimeDivisor B S hS X) :
    _root_.IsReduced ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec) ∧
      ringKrullDim ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec) = 1 ∧
      IsNoetherianRing ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)
declarations.comment:
the henselian local ring at the generic point of a prime divisor is a reduced
  1-dimensional Noetherian local ring; the canonical injection of the function field into its
  total ring of fractions is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.rationalFunctionsToGenericTotalFractionRing`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_mk'
declarations.doc:
The order of vanishing along a prime divisor of a fraction `a / b` of nonzerodivisors of the
henselian local ring at its generic point is the difference of the lengths of the quotients by
the ideals `(a)` and `(b)`.

This is the defining formula of the order of vanishing, computed on the total ring of fractions
of the henselian local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.ord_mk'
    (a b : nonZeroDivisors ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec))
    (hu : IsUnit (IsLocalization.mk' (Z.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec)
      (a : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)) b)) :
    Z.ord B S hS hX hdec (IsLocalization.mk' (Z.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec)
        (a : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)) b) hu =
      ((Ring.ord ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)
          (a : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec))).toNat : ℤ) -
        ((Ring.ord ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)
          (b : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec))).toNat : ℤ)
declarations.comment:
the difference-of-lengths formula, on a unit of the total ring of fractions of the
  henselian local ring at the generic point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ordRationalFunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENL.** The *order of vanishing of `f` along `Z`*, for `f` an invertible rational
function on a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space `X` and `Z` a prime divisor of `X`:
the order of vanishing, along `Z`, of the image of `f` in the total ring of fractions of the
henselian local ring at the generic point of `Z` under the canonical injection of Stacks 0ENK.

The hypotheses are those of the source and no others — the conclusions of Stacks 0ENK are
discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.genericFractionEmbedding`, and decency comes from
integrality by Stacks 0AD4 — and the defining difference of lengths is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ordRationalFunction_eq_length_sub_length`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev ordRationalFunction (f : (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)ˣ)
    (Z : PrimeDivisor B S hS X) : ℤ
declarations.comment: ord_Z(f) for an invertible rational function f on a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space, at the hypotheses of the source; the defining difference-of-lengths formula is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ordRationalFunction_eq_length_sub_length`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ordRationalFunction_eq_length_sub_length
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENL, the defining formula.** If the image of `f` in `Q(𝒪^h_{X, ξ})` is the ratio
`a / b` of nonzerodivisors `a` and `b` of `𝒪^h_{X, ξ}`, then `ord_Z(f)` is the difference of the
lengths of `𝒪^h_{X, ξ} / a 𝒪^h_{X, ξ}` and `𝒪^h_{X, ξ} / b 𝒪^h_{X, ξ}`.

The hypothesis is placed on an arbitrary such presentation, so this is simultaneously the
formula the source defines `ord_Z(f)` by and the independence of that formula from the choice
of `a` and `b`, which the source takes from Algebra, Lemma 02MC.
declarations.statement:
theorem ordRationalFunction_eq_length_sub_length (f : (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)ˣ)
    (Z : PrimeDivisor B S hS X)
    (a b : nonZeroDivisors ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace))
    (hab : Z.rationalFunctionsToGenericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace hInt hN
        (f : rationalFunctions B S hS hX) =
      IsLocalization.mk' (Z.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace)
        (a : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace)) b) :
    ordRationalFunction B S hS hX hInt hN f Z =
      ((Ring.ord ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace)
          (a : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace))).toNat : ℤ) -
        ((Ring.ord ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace)
          (b : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace))).toNat : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the difference-of-lengths formula defining ord_Z(f), on an arbitrary presentation of the image of f in Q(𝒪^h_{X, ξ}) as a ratio of nonzerodivisors; hence also the independence of the presentation, which the source cites Algebra, Lemma 02MC for

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_ordRationalFunction_eq_length_sub_length
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENL, well-definedness.** The image of an invertible rational function `f` in
`Q(𝒪^h_{X, ξ})` *is* a ratio `a / b` of nonzerodivisors of `𝒪^h_{X, ξ}`, and for one — hence,
by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ordRationalFunction_eq_length_sub_length`, for every — such
presentation `ord_Z(f)` is the difference of the lengths of `𝒪^h_{X, ξ} / a 𝒪^h_{X, ξ}` and
`𝒪^h_{X, ξ} / b 𝒪^h_{X, ξ}`.

The source defines `ord_Z(f)` *by* that difference, for `a` and `b` nonzerodivisors such that
the image of `f` is `a / b`, so the existence of such a pair is what makes the difference of
lengths an admissible description of `ord_Z(f)`. Invertibility of `f` is what produces it: the
image of `f` is a unit of the total ring of fractions, and the numerator of any presentation of
a unit is again a nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ordRationalFunction_eq_length_sub_length (f : (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)ˣ)
    (Z : PrimeDivisor B S hS X) :
    ∃ a b : nonZeroDivisors ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace),
      Z.rationalFunctionsToGenericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace hInt hN
            (f : rationalFunctions B S hS hX) =
          IsLocalization.mk' (Z.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace)
            (a : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace)) b ∧
        ordRationalFunction B S hS hX hInt hN f Z =
          ((Ring.ord ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace)
              (a : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace))).toNat : ℤ) -
            ((Ring.ord ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace)
              (b : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hInt.isDecentSpace))).toNat : ℤ)
declarations.comment: existence of the presentation a/b by nonzerodivisors of the image of f in Q(𝒪^h_{X, ξ}), which is what makes the difference of lengths an admissible description of ord_Z(f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_ordTotalFracInt_chartPointRationalFunctionMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENM at an arbitrary affine étale chart.** Let `Z` be a prime divisor of a decent,
locally Noetherian, integral algebraic space `X`, let `V` be an affine étale chart of `X` and
`v` a point of its scheme over the generic point of `Z`. Then the order of vanishing along `Z` of
an invertible rational function `f` is the order of vanishing at `v` of the reading of `f` in
the total ring of fractions of `𝒪_{V, v}`.

Unlike `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_scheme_ord_of_chart` the chart need not be
an elementary étale neighbourhood, nor integral: `𝒪_{V, v}` is a reduced one-dimensional local
ring, possibly with several minimal primes, and its order of vanishing is the one on its total
ring of fractions. The proof compares the chart with the chosen elementary étale neighbourhood
of the generic point at a common affine refinement
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ordTotalFracInt_chartPointRationalFunctionMap_eq`) and the
neighbourhood with the henselian local ring
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_ordTotalFracInt_genericEtaleChart`).

The dimension hypothesis on `𝒪_{V, v}`, needed to state the right-hand side, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.krullDimLE_chartStalk`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_ordTotalFracInt_chartPointRationalFunctionMap
    (hInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X)
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Y))
    (V : SmallEtale B S hS X) [IsAffine V.obj.left.left.1] [IsReduced V.obj.left.left.1]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian V.obj.left.left.1] (v : V.obj.left.left.1)
    (hv : chartSchemeToPoints B S hS X V v = Z.genericPoint B S hS X)
    [Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (V.obj.left.left.1.presheaf.stalk v)]
    (f : (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)ˣ) :
    (genericFractionEmbedding B S hS hX hdec hInt hN).ord f Z =
      Ring.ordTotalFracInt (V.obj.left.left.1.presheaf.stalk v)
        (chartPointRationalFunctionMap B S hS hX V v (f : rationalFunctions B S hS hX))
        (f.isUnit.map _)
declarations.comment:
at an arbitrary affine étale chart, not necessarily integral, through a point
  over the generic point of the prime divisor: the order of vanishing is the one of the total
  ring of fractions of the local ring of the chart at the point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_functionFieldToTotalFractionRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENM.** The order of vanishing along a prime divisor `Z` of the image of a nonzero
rational function `f` of an elementary étale neighbourhood `U` of the generic point of `Z` is
the order of vanishing of `f` at the marked point of `U` in the sense of Divisors, Definition
02RJ.

Both sides are a difference of lengths, and the canonical map from the stalk of `U` into the
henselian local ring is the structure map of a henselization, so it leaves those lengths
unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.ord_functionFieldToTotalFractionRing
    (hcoh : coheight U.point = 1) (f : ↥U.scheme.left.1.functionField) (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    Z.ord B S hS hX hdec (Z.functionFieldToTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec U f)
        ((isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hf).map
          (Z.functionFieldToTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec U)) =
      U.scheme.left.1.ord f U.point
declarations.comment:
with the shrinking step of the proof carried: in place of the hypothesis that `Z`
  meets the schematic locus of `X`, an elementary étale neighbourhood `U` of the generic point of
  `Z` whose scheme is integral and locally Noetherian and whose marked point has codimension one
  is given, the rational function is one of `U`, and it is compared along the induced map on
  total rings of fractions; Noetherianness and the dimension bound for the henselian local ring
  are hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_mk'_eq_ord_mk'_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENM at an arbitrary étale chart.** Let `Z` be a prime divisor of a decent algebraic
space `X` with generic point `ξ`, let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X`, and let `(U, u)` be a
small étale neighbourhood of `x̄` whose scheme is integral and locally Noetherian and whose point
has codimension one. Let `a / b` be a fraction of nonzerodivisors of `𝒪^h_{X, ξ}` and `c / d` one
of nonzerodivisors of `𝒪_{U, u}` whose numerators and denominators agree in `𝒪_{X, x̄}`, along a
map `ψ : 𝒪^h_{X, ξ} → 𝒪_{X, x̄}` leaving `Ring.ord` unchanged and the canonical map of Stacks
05VP. Then the order of vanishing of `a / b` along `Z` is the order of vanishing of `c / d` at
`u` in the sense of Divisors, Definition 02RJ.

Both sides are a difference of two `Ring.ord`s, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_mk'` and `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ord_mk'`, and the
four `Ring.ord`s are pairwise equal: the canonical map of Stacks 05VP is the structure map of a
strict henselization, so it leaves `Ring.ord` unchanged
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ord_chartLocalRingToEtaleLocalRing`), and `hψ` says the same of `ψ`.

The hypothesis `hψ` is supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_ringHom_ord_henselianLocalRing` at any geometric point above `ξ`;
unlike the elementary-neighbourhood comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_functionFieldToTotalFractionRing`, nothing here asks
that `(U, u)` be an elementary étale neighbourhood of `ξ`, which is what makes the statement
usable on a chart chosen for a different reason — in the proof of Stacks 0EPX, one trivializing
an invertible module.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.ord_mk'_eq_ord_mk'_chart
    [Nontrivial ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)]
    [IsNoetherianRing ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)]
    [Ring.KrullDimLE 1 ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)]
    {xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X}
    (V : SmallEtaleNeighborhood xbar)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral (chartScheme V.chart)]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian (chartScheme V.chart)]
    (ψ : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec) →+*
      (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)))
    (hψ : ∀ r, Ring.ord (etaleLocalRing B S hS X xbar : Type (u + 1)) (ψ r) =
      Ring.ord ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec) r)
    (hcoh : coheight (chartPoint B S hS X V) = 1)
    (a b : (↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec))⁰)
    (c d : (↥(chartLocalRing B S hS X V))⁰)
    (hac : ψ (a : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)) =
      chartLocalRingToEtaleLocalRing B S hS X hX V (c : ↥(chartLocalRing B S hS X V)))
    (hbd : ψ (b : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)) =
      chartLocalRingToEtaleLocalRing B S hS X hX V (d : ↥(chartLocalRing B S hS X V)))
    (hu : IsUnit (IsLocalization.mk' (Z.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec)
      (a : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)) b)) :
    Z.ord B S hS hX hdec (IsLocalization.mk' (Z.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec)
        (a : ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec)) b) hu =
      (chartScheme V.chart).ord
        (IsLocalization.mk' (chartScheme V.chart).functionField
          (c : ↥(chartLocalRing B S hS X V)) d) (chartPoint B S hS X V)
declarations.comment:
at an arbitrary étale chart, routed through the étale local ring at a geometric
  point rather than through the canonical map into the henselian local ring: in place of the
  hypothesis that `Z` meets the schematic locus of `X`, a small étale neighbourhood `(U, u)` of a
  geometric point whose scheme is integral and locally Noetherian and whose point has
  codimension one is given, and the two fractions are compared through their images in
  `𝒪_{X, x̄}`. Noetherianness and the dimension bound for the henselian local ring are
  hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.exists_affine_schematic_neighborhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENM**, the shrinking step of the proof in affine form. If a prime divisor `Z` of a
locally Noetherian integral algebraic space `X` meets the schematic locus of `X`, then the
generic point of `Z` has an *affine* elementary étale neighbourhood whose scheme is integral,
locally Noetherian and of codimension one at the marked point.

The schematic locus itself is such a neighbourhood except for affineness, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.exists_schematic_neighborhood`; restricting it to an
affine open around the marked point preserves integrality and local Noetherianness, as
properties of an open subscheme, and preserves the codimension of the marked point because
codimension is computed in any open neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.exists_affine_schematic_neighborhood
    (hmeet : (Z.support B S hS X ∩
      subspacePointSet B S hS X (schematicLocus B S hS X)).Nonempty) :
    ∃ U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX (Z.genericPoint B S hS X),
      IsAffine U.scheme.left.1 ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral U.scheme.left.1 ∧
      IsLocallyNoetherian U.scheme.left.1 ∧
      coheight U.point = 1
declarations.comment:
the shrinking step of the proof, with the neighbourhood affine: from the
  hypothesis that the prime divisor meets the schematic locus, an affine elementary étale
  neighbourhood of its generic point whose scheme is integral, locally Noetherian and of
  codimension one at the marked point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_scheme_ord
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENM.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic
space over `S` and let `f ∈ R(X)^*`. If the prime divisor `Z ⊂ X` meets the schematic locus of
`X`, then the order of vanishing `ord_Z(f)` of Definition 0ENL agrees with the order of
vanishing of Divisors, Definition 02RJ.

After shrinking `X` to the schematic locus and then to an affine open around the generic point
`ξ` of `Z` we are on an integral Noetherian affine scheme `U` with a point of codimension one;
there `𝒪^h_{X, ξ}` is a henselization of `𝒪_{U, u}`, so the two orders of vanishing, each a
difference of lengths, agree.

The hypotheses are exactly those of the source: decency, which the henselian local ring and
hence the order of vanishing of Definition 0ENL are defined from, is part of integrality of an
algebraic space — Stacks 0AD4, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsIntegralSpace` — and is taken from
`hInt` rather than assumed separately.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_scheme_ord
    (hmeet : (Z.support B S hS X ∩
      subspacePointSet B S hS X (schematicLocus B S hS X)).Nonempty)
    (f : (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)ˣ) :
    ∃ (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX (Z.genericPoint B S hS X))
      (_ : IsAffine U.scheme.left.1) (_ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral U.scheme.left.1)
      (_ : IsLocallyNoetherian U.scheme.left.1),
      coheight U.point = 1 ∧
        (genericFractionEmbedding B S hS hX (hInt.isDecentSpace B S hS X) hInt hN).ord f Z =
          U.scheme.left.1.ord
            (rationalFunctionsToFunctionField B S hS hX U.scheme U.point U.toSpace
              U.etale_toSpace (f : rationalFunctions B S hS hX)) U.point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.exists_schematic_neighborhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENM**, the shrinking step of the proof. If a prime divisor `Z` of a locally
Noetherian integral algebraic space `X` meets the schematic locus of `X`, then the generic point
of `Z` has an elementary étale neighbourhood whose structure morphism is an open immersion and
whose scheme is integral, locally Noetherian and of codimension one at the marked point.

The neighbourhood is the schematic locus itself: it is an open subspace represented by a scheme
`V` by Stacks 03JH, its point set is open in `|X|` and meets `|Z|`, hence contains the generic
point `ξ` of `Z`, and the point `v ∈ V` over `ξ` has codimension one because `|V| → |X|` is an
open embedding.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.exists_schematic_neighborhood
    (hmeet : (Z.support B S hS X ∩
      subspacePointSet B S hS X (schematicLocus B S hS X)).Nonempty) :
    ∃ U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood B S hS X hX (Z.genericPoint B S hS X),
      IsOpenImmersion B S hS U.toSpace ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral U.scheme.left.1 ∧
      IsLocallyNoetherian U.scheme.left.1 ∧
      coheight U.point = 1
declarations.comment:
the shrinking step of the proof: from the hypothesis that the prime divisor meets
  the schematic locus, an elementary étale neighbourhood of its generic point which is an open
  immersion and whose scheme is integral, locally Noetherian and of codimension one at the
  marked point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyFinite_principalDivisorCoefficients_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENN, the second set.** The prime divisors of `X` along which a rational function
`f` has nonzero order of vanishing are locally finite in `|X|`, given a nonempty open subset of
`|X|` over which `f` is invertible.

This is the source's argument. Such a prime divisor has its generic point outside the open set,
by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.genericPoint_notMem_of_principalDivisorCoefficients_ne_zero`, so its
point set is an irreducible component of the closed complement — codimension one leaves no room
for a larger irreducible closed subset of that complement — and the irreducible components of a
closed set are locally finite by Stacks 0EE5. Both steps are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyFinite_primeDivisor_of_genericPoint_notMem`, already in the
library in exactly this generality; it is also the Stacks 0EE5 step in the proof of Stacks
0EPS.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFinite_principalDivisorCoefficients_ne_zero
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Y))
    (hirr : IrreducibleSpace (points B S hS X))
    (emb : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, rationalFunctions B S hS hX →+*
      W.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec)
    (f : rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
    (hf : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, IsUnit (emb W f))
    (U : Set (points B S hS X)) (hUopen : IsOpen U) (hUne : U.Nonempty)
    (hreg : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, W.genericPoint B S hS X ∈ U →
      ∃ r : ↥(W.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec), IsUnit r ∧
        emb W f = algebraMap _ (W.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec) r) :
    LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X =>
      if principalDivisorCoefficients B S hS hX hdec emb f hf W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support B S hS X
declarations.comment:
the second set: the prime divisors with ord_Z(f) ≠ 0 are locally finite. The
  first set, the prime divisors at whose generic point f is not regular, is
  locallyFinite_primeDivisor_not_isDefinedAt

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyFinite_primeDivisor_not_isDefinedAt_and_ordRationalFunction_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENN.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space over `S` and let
`f ∈ R(X)^*`. Then the prime divisors `Z` of `X` whose generic point `ξ` has `f ∉ 𝒪_{X, ξ}` —
`f` not defined at `ξ` in the sense of Stacks 0EMQ — and the prime divisors `Z` with
`ord_Z(f) ≠ 0`, for the order of vanishing of Stacks 0ENL, are both locally finite collections
in `|X|`.

As in the source, both follow from Stacks 0EE5 once the generic points of the prime divisors in
question avoid a nonempty open. For the first collection that open is the domain of a
representative of `f`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyFinite_primeDivisor_not_isDefinedAt`; for the second it is the
open on which `f` is a unit section, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ordRationalFunction_mem_weilDivisor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFinite_primeDivisor_not_isDefinedAt_and_ordRationalFunction_ne_zero
    (f : (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)ˣ) :
    LocallyFinite (fun Z : {Z : PrimeDivisor B S hS X //
        ¬ RationalMap.IsDefinedAt B S hS (f : rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
          (Z.genericPoint B S hS X)} ↦ Z.1.support B S hS X) ∧
    LocallyFinite (fun Z : {Z : PrimeDivisor B S hS X //
        ordRationalFunction B S hS hX hInt hN f Z ≠ 0} ↦ Z.1.support B S hS X)
declarations.comment: both collections, with the source's hypotheses only: the prime divisors at whose generic point f is not defined (f ∉ 𝒪_{X,ξ}) and those with ord_Z(f) ≠ 0 are locally finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.principalDivisorCoefficients
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENP, the coefficients.** The coefficients `ord_Z(f)` of the principal divisor
`div(f) = ∑_Z ord_Z(f) [Z]` of a rational function `f` on `X`, indexed by the prime divisors of
`X`: the coefficient at `Z` is the order of vanishing along `Z` of the image of `f` in the total
ring of fractions of `𝒪^h_{X,ξ}`.

The embeddings `R(X) → Q(𝒪^h_{X,ξ})` of Stacks 0ENK are the parameter `emb`, as in Stacks 0EPT;
regularity of `f` is the hypothesis `hf` that each image is a unit.
declarations.statement:
def principalDivisorCoefficients
    (emb : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, rationalFunctions B S hS hX →+*
      W.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec)
    (f : rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
    (hf : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, IsUnit (emb W f)) :
    PrimeDivisor B S hS X → ℤ
declarations.comment:
the coefficients ord_Z(f) of div(f); the embeddings R(X) → Q(O^h_{X,ξ}) of
  Stacks 0ENK are the parameter emb, as they are for Stacks 0EPT

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.principalWeilDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENP.** The *principal divisor associated to `f ∈ R(X)^*`*, that is
`div(f) = ∑_Z ord_Z(f) [Z]`, as an element of `Div(X)`.

That the sum makes sense is Stacks 0ENN, the argument `hfin`, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyFinite_principalDivisorCoefficients_ne_zero` proves and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.principalWeilDivisorOfRegularLocus` discharges from a nonempty open
subset of `|X|` over which `f` is invertible.
declarations.statement:
def principalWeilDivisor
    (emb : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, rationalFunctions B S hS hX →+*
      W.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec)
    (f : rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
    (hf : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, IsUnit (emb W f))
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X =>
      if principalDivisorCoefficients B S hS hX hdec emb f hf W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support B S hS X) :
    WeilDivisor B S hS X
declarations.comment:
div(f) = ∑ ord_Z(f) [Z] as an element of Div(X); local finiteness is Stacks 0ENN,
  the argument hfin, discharged by locallyFinite_principalDivisorCoefficients_ne_zero in
  principalWeilDivisorOfRegularLocus; the embeddings of Stacks 0ENK are the parameter emb

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.principalWeilDivisorOfRegularLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENP.** The principal divisor `div(f) = ∑_Z ord_Z(f) [Z]` of a rational function
`f ∈ R(X)^*` as an element of `Div(X)`, with the local finiteness of Stacks 0ENN supplied from a
nonempty open subset of `|X|` over which `f` is invertible.
declarations.statement:
def principalWeilDivisorOfRegularLocus
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Y))
    (hirr : IrreducibleSpace (points B S hS X))
    (emb : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, rationalFunctions B S hS hX →+*
      W.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec)
    (f : rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
    (hf : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, IsUnit (emb W f))
    (U : Set (points B S hS X)) (hUopen : IsOpen U) (hUne : U.Nonempty)
    (hreg : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, W.genericPoint B S hS X ∈ U →
      ∃ r : ↥(W.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec), IsUnit r ∧
        emb W f = algebraMap _ (W.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec) r) :
    WeilDivisor B S hS X
declarations.comment:
div(f) in Div(X), with local finiteness (Stacks 0ENN) discharged here: it is
  proved from a nonempty open U over which f is invertible, the datum (U, hUopen, hUne, hreg)
  that is the first sentence of the source's own proof of Stacks 0ENN

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.principalWeilDivisorOfUnit
declarations.doc:
The *principal Weil divisor associated to `f ∈ R(X)^*`*,
`div(f) = div_X(f) = ∑_Z ord_Z(f) [Z]`, as an element of `Div(X)`, for `X` a locally Noetherian
integral algebraic space over `S`.

The sum is over the prime divisors of `X`, and `ord_Z(f)` is the order of vanishing of Stacks
0ENL, taken along the canonical embedding `R(X) → Q(𝒪^h_{X, ξ})` of Stacks 0ENK
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.genericFractionEmbedding`).
declarations.statement:
def principalWeilDivisorOfUnit (f : (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)ˣ) :
    ↥(WeilDivisor B S hS X)
declarations.comment: div(f) = ∑ ord_Z(f) [Z] as an element of Div(X), for X a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space over S and f ∈ R(X)^*: the order of vanishing of Stacks 0ENL along the canonical embedding R(X) → Q(O^h_{X,ξ}) of Stacks 0ENK, whose ring-theoretic properties are proved; the local finiteness of Stacks 0ENN is proved, nothing is carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.divRationalFunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENP.** The *principal Weil divisor* `div_X(f) = ∑ ord_Z(f) [Z]` of an invertible
rational function `f` on a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space `X`, the sum running over
the prime divisors `Z` of `X` and `ord_Z(f)` being the order of vanishing of Stacks 0ENL. It is
a Weil divisor by Stacks 0ENN, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ordRationalFunction_mem_weilDivisor`.
declarations.statement: abbrev divRationalFunction (f : (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)ˣ) : ↥(WeilDivisor B S hS X)
declarations.comment: div_X(f) = ∑ ord_Z(f) [Z] as a Weil divisor, at the hypotheses of the source: the order of vanishing is the canonical one of Stacks 0ENL and the local finiteness is Stacks 0ENN, both proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.principalWeilDivisor_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENQ.** The principal divisor of a product of rational functions is the sum of
their principal divisors, `div(fg) = div(f) + div(g)` in `Div(X)`.

Local finiteness for `fg` is not assumed: it is deduced from local finiteness for `f` and for
`g`, which is what makes `div(f)` and `div(g)` elements of `Div(X)` in the first place.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalWeilDivisor_mul
    (emb : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, rationalFunctions B S hS hX →+*
      W.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec)
    (f g : rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
    (hf : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, IsUnit (emb W f))
    (hg : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, IsUnit (emb W g))
    (hfg : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, IsUnit (emb W (f * g)))
    (hfinf : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X =>
      if principalDivisorCoefficients B S hS hX hdec emb f hf W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support B S hS X)
    (hfing : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X =>
      if principalDivisorCoefficients B S hS hX hdec emb g hg W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support B S hS X) :
    principalWeilDivisor B S hS hX hdec emb (f * g) hfg
        (locallyFinite_principalDivisorCoefficients_mul B S hS hX hdec emb f g hf hg hfg hfinf
          hfing) =
      principalWeilDivisor B S hS hX hdec emb f hf hfinf +
        principalWeilDivisor B S hS hX hdec emb g hg hfing
declarations.comment: div(fg) = div(f) + div(g) in Div(X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.principalWeilDivisorOfRegularLocus_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENQ.** The principal divisor of a product of rational functions is the sum of
their principal divisors, `div(fg) = div(f) + div(g)` in `Div(X)`, with the local finiteness of
Stacks 0ENN proved for all three divisors from a nonempty open subset of `|X|` over which both
`f` and `g` are invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalWeilDivisorOfRegularLocus_mul
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Y))
    (hirr : IrreducibleSpace (points B S hS X))
    (emb : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, rationalFunctions B S hS hX →+*
      W.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec)
    (f g : rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
    (hf : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, IsUnit (emb W f))
    (hg : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, IsUnit (emb W g))
    (hfg : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, IsUnit (emb W (f * g)))
    (U : Set (points B S hS X)) (hUopen : IsOpen U) (hUne : U.Nonempty)
    (hregf : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, W.genericPoint B S hS X ∈ U →
      ∃ r : ↥(W.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec), IsUnit r ∧
        emb W f = algebraMap _ (W.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec) r)
    (hregg : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor B S hS X, W.genericPoint B S hS X ∈ U →
      ∃ r : ↥(W.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec), IsUnit r ∧
        emb W g = algebraMap _ (W.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdec) r) :
    principalWeilDivisorOfRegularLocus B S hS hX hdec hN hirr emb (f * g) hfg U hUopen hUne
        (exists_isUnit_emb_mul_eq_algebraMap B S hS hX hdec emb f g U hregf hregg) =
      principalWeilDivisorOfRegularLocus B S hS hX hdec hN hirr emb f hf U hUopen hUne hregf +
        principalWeilDivisorOfRegularLocus B S hS hX hdec hN hirr emb g hg U hUopen hUne hregg
declarations.comment: div(fg) = div(f) + div(g) in Div(X), local finiteness proved throughout

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.divRationalFunction_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENQ.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space over `S` and let
`f, g ∈ R(X)^*`. Then `div_X(fg) = div_X(f) + div_X(g)` as Weil divisors on `X`.

As in the source this is the additivity of the order of vanishing,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GenericFractionEmbedding.ord_mul_apply`, at every prime divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem divRationalFunction_mul (f g : (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)ˣ) :
    divRationalFunction B S hS hX hInt hN (f * g) =
      divRationalFunction B S hS hX hInt hN f + divRationalFunction B S hS hX hInt hN g
declarations.comment: div_X(fg) = div_X(f) + div_X(g) as Weil divisors on X, at the hypotheses of the source only

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GenericFractionEmbedding.ord_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENQ.** The order of vanishing of a product of invertible rational functions is
the sum of the orders of vanishing, as coefficient families on the prime divisors of `X`.

This is the equation `div(fg) = div(f) + div(g)` of the source, read on the coefficient families
of which the two sides of that equation are the Weil divisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem ord_mul (f g : (rationalFunctions B S hS hX)ˣ) :
    E.ord (f * g) = E.ord f + E.ord g
declarations.comment:
additivity of the principal Weil divisor, read on the coefficient families over
  the prime divisors; this form needs no hypothesis beyond the embedding of Stacks 0ENK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GenericFractionEmbedding.principalWeilDivisors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENR.** The subgroup of `Div(X)` of principal Weil divisors: they contain zero and
are closed under addition and negation by the additivity of the order of vanishing, which is
Stacks 0ENQ.
declarations.statement: def principalWeilDivisors : AddSubgroup ↥(WeilDivisor B S hS X)
declarations.comment: the subgroup of principal Weil divisors, by which the class group is formed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GenericFractionEmbedding.weilDivisorClassGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENR.** The *Weil divisor class group* `Cl(X)` of `X`: the group of Weil divisors
on `X` modulo the subgroup of principal Weil divisors.
declarations.statement: abbrev weilDivisorClassGroup : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment:
the Weil divisor class group as the quotient of the Weil divisors by the
  principal Weil divisors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.weilDivisorClassGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENR.** The *Weil divisor class group* `Cl(X)` of a locally Noetherian integral
algebraic space `X` over `S`: the quotient of the group `Div(X)` of Weil divisors by the
subgroup of principal Weil divisors `div(f)`, `f ∈ R(X)^*`.
declarations.statement: abbrev weilDivisorClassGroup : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: Cl(X) = Div(X) / {div(f) : f ∈ R(X)^*}, at the source's hypotheses only: the principal divisors are the range of the homomorphism div of Stacks 0ENP and 0ENQ, built from the canonical order of vanishing

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.involutionQuotient_classGroup
declarations.statement:
theorem involutionQuotient_classGroup (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj ∧
      Space.IsSmooth B (Spec (.of k)) hk (terminal.from (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj) ∧
      Space.UniversalHomeomorphism B (Spec (.of k)) hk (squaringMap k B hk) ∧
      IsIso (pullback.snd (squaringMap k B hk) (Space.puncturedLineInclusion k B hk)) ∧
      Space.IsNoetherian B (Spec (.of k)) hk hZ (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj ∧
      Space.IsIntegralSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj ∧
      topologicalKrullDim (Space.points B (Spec (.of k)) hk (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj) = 1 ∧
      (∃ e : Space.PrimeDivisor B (Spec (.of k)) hk (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj ≃
          {ξ : Space.points B (Spec (.of k)) hk (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj //
            IsClosed ({ξ} : Set _)},
        ∀ Z, (e Z : Space.points B (Spec (.of k)) hk _) = Z.genericPoint B (Spec (.of k)) hk _) ∧
      IsClosed ({(originDivisor k B hk hchar hZ).genericPoint B (Spec (.of k)) hk _} :
        Set (Space.points B (Spec (.of k)) hk (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj)) ∧
      (∀ ξ : Space.points B (Spec (.of k)) hk (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj,
        Space.pointsHomeomorphAffineLine (squaringMap k B hk)
            (universalHomeomorphism_squaringMap k B hk hchar) ξ = origin k ↔
          ξ = (originDivisor k B hk hchar hZ).genericPoint B (Spec (.of k)) hk _) ∧
      (∀ Z : Space.PrimeDivisor B (Spec (.of k)) hk (involutionQuotient k B hk).obj,
        Z ≠ originDivisor k B hk hchar hZ →
          (Space.primeDivisorClass Z : Space.weilDivisorClassGroup B (Spec (.of k)) hk
            (isAlgebraicSpace_involutionQuotient k hchar B hk)
            (isIntegralSpace_involutionQuotient k B hk hchar hZ)
            (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian k B hk hchar)) = 0) ∧
      Space.divRationalFunction B (Spec (.of k)) hk
          (isAlgebraicSpace_involutionQuotient k hchar B hk)
          (isIntegralSpace_involutionQuotient k B hk hchar hZ)
          (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian k B hk hchar)
          (Space.coordinatePullbackUnit (squaringMap k B hk)
            (isAlgebraicSpace_involutionQuotient k hchar B hk)
            (isIntegralSpace_involutionQuotient k B hk hchar hZ)
            (isIso_squaringMap_pullback_puncturedAffineLine k hchar B hk)) =
        2 • Space.primeDivisorClass (originDivisor k B hk hchar hZ) ∧
      ∃ e : Space.weilDivisorClassGroup B (Spec (.of k)) hk
          (isAlgebraicSpace_involutionQuotient k hchar B hk)
          (isIntegralSpace_involutionQuotient k B hk hchar hZ)
          (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian k B hk hchar) ≃+ ZMod 2,
        e (Space.primeDivisorClass (originDivisor k B hk hchar hZ)) = 1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.isNoetherian_involutionQuotient
declarations.doc:
Away from characteristic two, the quotient of the affine line by the punctured graph of
negation is a Noetherian algebraic space over the ground field: it is quasi-compact,
quasi-separated and locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherian_involutionQuotient (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    Space.IsNoetherian B (Spec (.of k)) hS hZ (involutionQuotient k B hS).obj
declarations.comment: the Noetherian property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineLineInvolution.isSmooth_involutionQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENT.** Away from characteristic two, the quotient of the affine line by the
punctured graph of negation is smooth over the ground field.

Smoothness is tested on the quotient chart, which is a surjective étale chart of the
quotient by Stacks 0265, and on the affine line itself, which is smooth over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_involutionQuotient (hchar : (2 : k) ≠ 0) (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    Space.IsSmooth B (Spec (.of k)) hS
      (terminal.from (involutionQuotient k B hS).obj)
declarations.comment: smoothness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoordinateAxesQuotient.coordinateAxesQuotient_properties
declarations.statement:
theorem coordinateAxesQuotient_properties (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) :
    Stacks.Groupoids.IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (relationPreRelation S) ∧
      IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (quotientSpace S B hS).obj ∧
      quotientMap S B hS ≫ sumMap S B hS =
        (Over.post (X := B.obj hS) B.inclusion).op.whiskerLeft
          (yoneda.map (coordinateSumMap S)) ∧
      Space.UniversalHomeomorphism B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (sumMap S B hS) ∧
      IsIso (pullback.snd (sumMap S B hS) (Space.puncturedLineInclusion S.k B hS)) ∧
      Space.IsIntegralSpace B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (quotientSpace S B hS).obj ∧
      Space.IsNoetherian B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS hZ (quotientSpace S B hS).obj ∧
      (∀ ξ : Space.points B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (quotientSpace S B hS).obj,
        (∃ Z : Space.PrimeDivisor B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (quotientSpace S B hS).obj,
          Z.genericPoint B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS _ = ξ) ↔ IsClosed {ξ}) ∧
      (originDivisor S B hS hZ).genericPoint B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS _ = originPoint S B hS ∧
      IsClosed {originPoint S B hS} ∧
      (∀ ξ : Space.points B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (quotientSpace S B hS).obj,
        Space.pointsHomeomorphAffineLine (sumMap S B hS) (universalHomeomorphism_sumMap B S hS) ξ =
            AffineLineInvolution.origin S.k ↔ ξ = originPoint S B hS) ∧
      Space.divRationalFunction B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSpace S B hS)
          (isIntegralSpace_quotientSpace S B hS hZ)
          (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian S B hS)
          (Space.coordinatePullbackUnit (sumMap S B hS) (isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSpace S B hS)
            (isIntegralSpace_quotientSpace S B hS hZ)
            (isIso_sumMap_pullback_puncturedAffineLine B S hS)) =
        2 • Space.primeDivisorClass (originDivisor S B hS hZ) ∧
      (∀ Z : Space.PrimeDivisor B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (quotientSpace S B hS).obj,
        Z ≠ originDivisor S B hS hZ →
        (Space.primeDivisorClass Z : Space.weilDivisorClassGroup B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS
            (isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSpace S B hS)
            (isIntegralSpace_quotientSpace S B hS hZ)
            (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian S B hS)) = 0) ∧
      (∃ e : Space.weilDivisorClassGroup B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS
            (isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSpace S B hS)
            (isIntegralSpace_quotientSpace S B hS hZ)
            (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian S B hS) ≃+ ZMod 2,
        e (Space.primeDivisorClass (originDivisor S B hS hZ)) = 1) ∧
      (letI := Space.henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (quotientSpace S B hS).obj
          (isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSpace S B hS) (originPoint S B hS)
            (isIntegralSpace_quotientSpace S B hS hZ).isDecentSpace;
        letI := Space.stalkAlgebra B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (quotientSpace S B hS).obj
          (isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSpace S B hS) (originPoint S B hS)
            (isIntegralSpace_quotientSpace S B hS hZ).isDecentSpace
          (originNeighborhood S B hS _ rfl);
        IsLocalRing.IsHenselization
          ((originNeighborhood S B hS _ rfl).scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk
            (originNeighborhood S B hS _ rfl).point)
          (ResidueField ((originNeighborhood S B hS _ rfl).scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalk
            (originNeighborhood S B hS _ rfl).point))
          (Space.henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (quotientSpace S B hS).obj
            (isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSpace S B hS) (originPoint S B hS)
              (isIntegralSpace_quotientSpace S B hS hZ).isDecentSpace : Type (u + 1))) ∧
      ¬ IsDomain (Space.henselianLocalRing B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS (quotientSpace S B hS).obj
        (isAlgebraicSpace_quotientSpace S B hS) (originPoint S B hS)
          (isIntegralSpace_quotientSpace S B hS hZ).isDecentSpace)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.EtaleRelation.isEtaleEquivalenceRelation
declarations.doc: The specified relation is an étale equivalence relation on the coordinate axes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleEquivalenceRelation (S : CoordinateAxesQuotientSetup.{u}) :
    Stacks.Groupoids.IsEtaleEquivalenceRelation (relationPreRelation S)
declarations.comment: etale_relation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoordinateAxesQuotient.coordinateSumMap_invariant
declarations.doc:
The coordinate-sum map is invariant under the relation: it has the same composite with the
source and the target of `relationPreRelation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coordinateSumMap_invariant (S : Setup.{u}) :
    (relationPreRelation S).target ≫ coordinateSumMap S =
      (relationPreRelation S).source ≫ coordinateSumMap S
declarations.comment: quotient_map_exists

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoordinateAxesQuotient.quotientSumMap
declarations.doc:
The morphism from the quotient sheaf to the affine line through which the coordinate-sum map
factors, together with the equation expressing that factorisation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotientSumMap
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS) (Type u)] :
    { f : (Stacks.Groupoids.quotientSheaf
          (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS)
          (Over.post (X := B.obj hS) B.inclusion)
          (relationPreRelation S)).obj ⟶
        Stacks.Groupoids.points (Over.post (X := B.obj hS) B.inclusion)
          (AffineLineInvolution.affineLine S.k) //
      Stacks.Groupoids.toQuotientSheaf
          (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of S.k)) hS)
          (Over.post (X := B.obj hS) B.inclusion)
          (relationPreRelation S) ≫ f =
        (Over.post (X := B.obj hS) B.inclusion).op.whiskerLeft
          (yoneda.map (coordinateSumMap S)) }
declarations.comment: quotient_map_exists

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.residueField
declarations.doc:
The residue field `κ(x)` of a good algebraic space over the base of a
`BaseSpaceDimensionSituation` at a point `x` of `|X|`: the field of the monomorphism from a field
spectrum representing `x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.residueField (f : X ⟶ D.space)
    (hf : D.IsGood f) (x : points D.site D.base D.base_mem X) : Type u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.residueFieldMorphism_spec
declarations.doc:
A point `x` of a good algebraic space over the base of a `BaseSpaceDimensionSituation` is
represented by the morphism `Spec κ(x) ⟶ X` out of the spectrum of its residue field, and that
morphism is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.residueFieldMorphism_spec (f : X ⟶ D.space)
    (hf : D.IsGood f) (x : points D.site D.base D.base_mem X) :
    (D.residueFieldRepresentative f hf x).1.class D.site D.base D.base_mem X = x ∧
      Mono (D.residueFieldMorphism f hf x)
declarations.comment: a point is represented by a monomorphism from the spectrum of its residue field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.residueFieldRepresentative_unique
declarations.doc:
The monomorphism from a field spectrum representing a point `x` of a good algebraic space
over the base of a `BaseSpaceDimensionSituation` is unique: any monomorphic field-valued
representative of `x` is uniquely isomorphic, over the space, to `Spec κ(x) ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.residueFieldRepresentative_unique (f : X ⟶ D.space)
    (hf : D.IsGood f) (x : points D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (q : FieldValuedPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hq : q.class D.site D.base D.base_mem X = x)
    (hmq : Mono (fieldMorphism D.site D.base D.base_mem X q)) :
    ∃! e : yoneda.obj ((D.residueFieldRepresentative f hf x).1.siteObject
        D.site D.base D.base_mem X) ≅
        yoneda.obj (q.siteObject D.site D.base D.base_mem X),
      e.hom ≫ fieldMorphism D.site D.base D.base_mem X q = D.residueFieldMorphism f hf x
declarations.comment: the monomorphism from a field spectrum representing a point is unique up to unique isomorphism over the space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.exists_denseRange_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_of_isGood
declarations.doc:
A good algebraic space over the base of a `BaseSpaceDimensionSituation` has a dense open
subspace which is a scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.exists_denseRange_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_of_isGood
    (f : X ⟶ D.space) (hf : D.IsGood f) :
    ∃ G : Subfunctor X, IsOpenSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem G ∧
      G.toFunctor.IsRepresentable ∧
      DenseRange (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem G.toFunctor G.ι)
declarations.comment: a good algebraic space has a dense open subspace which is a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.exists_ringEquiv_residueField_schemeResidueField
declarations.doc:
Let `X/B` be good over the base of a `BaseSpaceDimensionSituation` and let `U ⊆ X` be an
open subspace which is a scheme, presented by an open immersion out of the presheaf
represented by an object of the site. At a point `x` of `|X|` coming from a point `u` of that
scheme, the residue field `κ(x)` agrees with the residue field of `u` on `U` as a scheme: they
are isomorphic by an isomorphism whose spectrum is the comparison morphism over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.exists_ringEquiv_residueField_schemeResidueField
    (f : X ⟶ D.space) (hf : D.IsGood f) (T : BigFppfOver D.site D.base D.base_mem)
    (j : yoneda.obj T ⟶ X) (hj : IsOpenImmersion D.site D.base D.base_mem j)
    (u : (BigFppfOver.toScheme D.site D.base D.base_mem).obj T)
    (x : points D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hu : pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem (yoneda.obj T) j
      ((schemePointRepresentative D.site D.base D.base_mem T u).class
        D.site D.base D.base_mem (yoneda.obj T)) = x) :
    ∃ (φ : D.residueField f hf x ≃+*
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme D.site D.base D.base_mem).obj T).residueField u)
      (g : (schemePointRepresentative D.site D.base D.base_mem T u).siteObject
          D.site D.base D.base_mem (yoneda.obj T) ⟶
        (D.residueFieldRepresentative f hf x).1.siteObject D.site D.base D.base_mem X),
      D.site.inclusion.map g.left = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ∧
        yoneda.map g ≫ D.residueFieldMorphism f hf x =
          yoneda.map (schemePointRepresentative D.site D.base D.base_mem T u).siteHom ≫ j
declarations.comment: at a point of an open subspace which is a scheme the residue field agrees with the residue field of the corresponding point on that scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.isField_functionField
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Stacks 0EDT let `X/B` be good and let `X` be integral. Then the
function field `R(X)` of `X` is defined: the ring of rational functions of
`X` is a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.isField_functionField (f : X ⟶ D.space)
    (hf : D.IsGood f) (hInt : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) :
    IsField (rationalFunctions D.site D.base D.base_mem hf.1)
declarations.comment: the function field R(X) of a good integral algebraic space is defined: its ring of rational functions is a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.functionFieldRingEquiv
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Stacks 0EDT let `X/B` be good and let `X` be integral. Then the
function field `R(X)` of `X` is the residue field of `X` at its generic point.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.functionFieldRingEquiv (f : X ⟶ D.space)
    (hf : D.IsGood f) (hInt : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) :
    rationalFunctions D.site D.base D.base_mem hf.1 ≃+*
      residueField D.site D.base D.base_mem X hInt.2.1
        (genericPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem hf.1 hInt)
declarations.comment: the function field R(X) of a good integral algebraic space is the residue field at its generic point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.residueFieldRingEquivFunctionField
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Stacks 0EDT let `X/B` be good. For a point `ξ` of `X` the residue field
`κ(ξ)` is the function field of the unique integral closed subspace `Z ⊆ X` whose generic point
is `ξ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.residueFieldRingEquivFunctionField
    (f : X ⟶ D.space) (hf : D.IsGood f) (ξ : points D.site D.base D.base_mem X) :
    residueField D.site D.base D.base_mem X (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood f hf) ξ ≃+*
      rationalFunctions D.site D.base D.base_mem
        (integralClosedSubspaceOfPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem hf.1
          (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood f hf) ξ).isClosedSubspace.1
declarations.comment: for any point x of a good algebraic space, the residue field κ(x) is the function field of the unique integral closed subspace whose generic point is x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.factorsThrough_properIntegralClosedSubspace_or_isDominant_and_finite_functionField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENY.** In Situation 0EDT let `X` and `Y` be good integral algebraic spaces over
the fixed base with `dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y)`, and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism over the base.
Then **either** `f` factors through a proper closed subspace of `Y` — namely the integral
closed subspace of `Y` on the closure of the image of `|X|`, whose set of points is strictly
smaller than `|Y|` — **or** `f` is dominant, carries the generic point of `X` to the generic
point of `Y`, and the extension of function fields `R(X)/R(Y)` it induces is finite.

The function fields are the residue fields at the generic points, by Stacks 0END, and the
extension is the homomorphism `f` induces on them; finiteness is finiteness as a module.

If the image of `|X|` is not dense its closure is an irreducible closed proper subset of
`|Y|`, and `X` is reduced, so `f` factors through the integral closed subspace on it by
Stacks 03IQ and Stacks 03JJ. If the image is dense, then `f` is dominant and carries the
generic point to the generic point; equality of the δ-dimensions makes the relative
transcendence degree at the generic point vanish, and then Spaces over Fields, Lemma 0AD5
gives finiteness.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThrough_properIntegralClosedSubspace_or_isDominant_and_finite_functionField
    (pX : X ⟶ D.space) (pY : Y ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood pX) (hY : D.IsGood pY)
    (hXInt : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hYInt : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX)
    (hdim : deltaDimensionClosed D pX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ =
      deltaDimensionClosed D pY hY Set.univ isClosed_univ) :
    (∃ Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem Y,
        subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem Y Z.subspace ≠ Set.univ ∧
          ∃ g : X ⟶ Z.subspace.toFunctor, g ≫ Z.subspace.ι = f) ∨
      (IsDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem f ∧
        pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem X f
            (genericPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hXInt) =
          genericPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1 hYInt ∧
        letI := (residueFieldHom D.site D.base D.base_mem X Y hY.1 hXInt.2.1 hYInt.2.1 f
          (genericPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hXInt)).toAlgebra
        Module.Finite
          (residueField D.site D.base D.base_mem Y hYInt.2.1
            (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem X f
              (genericPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hXInt)))
          (residueField D.site D.base D.base_mem X hXInt.2.1
            (genericPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hXInt)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyFinite_closure_image_pointsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ENZ.** Let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good algebraic spaces over the base of the theory
of cycles and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact morphism over `B`. The closures of the images
under `|f|` of a locally finite collection of closed subsets of `|X|` form a locally finite
collection of closed subsets of `|Y|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFinite_closure_image_pointsMap
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver D.site D.base D.base_mem)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space) (hY : D.IsGood sY)
    {f : X ⟶ Y} (_hfB : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    {I : Type v} (T : I → Set (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (_hT : ∀ i, IsClosed (T i)) (hTlf : LocallyFinite T) :
    LocallyFinite (fun i ↦ closure (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem X f '' T i)) ∧
      ∀ i, IsClosed (closure (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem X f '' T i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properCycleDegree
declarations.doc:
The coefficient with which the closure `Z'` of the image of an
integral closed subspace `Z ⊆ X` occurs in `f_*[Z]`: the degree `[R(Z) : R(Z')]` when the
δ-dimension is preserved, and `0` when it drops.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def properCycleDegree (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space)
    (hY : D.IsGood sY) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) : ℤ
declarations.comment: part (1): the coefficient of the image in the pushforward of a prime cycle

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properCyclePushforward
declarations.doc:
The proper pushforward of cycles along a quasi-compact morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of good
algebraic spaces over `B`: the additive map `f_* : Z_k(X) → Z_k(Y)` sending a cycle `α` to the
cycle whose coefficient at `Z'` is `∑ α_Z · [R(Z) : R(Z')]`, the sum being over the integral
closed subspaces `Z ⊆ X` whose image closure is `Z'` and the degree being taken to be `0` where
the δ-dimension drops. The morphism `f` is assumed quasi-compact, not proper.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def properCyclePushforward (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space)
    (hY : D.IsGood sY) {f : X ⟶ Y} (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact D.site D.base D.base_mem f) (k : ℤ) :
    CycleGroup D sX k →+ CycleGroup D sY k
declarations.comment: part (2): the pushforward of a k-cycle, as a homomorphism of abelian groups

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforwardWeightInDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EP1, part (1).** The multiplicity with which proper pushforward along `f` records
an integral closed subspace `Z` of `X` in the cycle group of δ-dimension `k`: the degree
`deg(Z/Z')` of `Z` over its integral closed image `Z'` when `dim_δ(Z') = k`, and `0` when
`dim_δ(Z') < k`, which for `Z` of δ-dimension `k` is the only other case.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def properPushforwardWeightInDimension (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space)
    (hX : D.IsGood sX) (hY : D.IsGood sY) (f : X ⟶ Y) (k : ℤ)
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) : ℤ
declarations.comment: part (1): the multiplicity of an integral closed subspace in the pushforward

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforwardInDimension
declarations.doc:
Proper pushforward of cycles of δ-dimension `k` along a proper morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of good algebraic spaces over the base: the cycle whose coefficient at `Z'` is the
sum of `n_Z deg(Z/Z')` over the integral closed subspaces `Z` of `X` with integral closed image
`Z'` of δ-dimension `k`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def properPushforwardInDimension (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space)
    (hX : D.IsGood sX) (hY : D.IsGood sY) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (hf : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem f) (k : ℤ) :
    CycleGroup D sX k → CycleGroup D sY k
declarations.comment: part (2): the pushforward of a k-cycle, as a map Z_k(X) → Z_k(Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforwardInDimension_cycleOfIntegralClosedSubspace_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The pushforward of the cycle `[Z]` of
an integral closed subspace of δ-dimension `k` is zero when its integral closed image has
smaller δ-dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforwardInDimension_cycleOfIntegralClosedSubspace_eq_zero (sX : X ⟶ D.space)
    (sY : Y ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (hY : D.IsGood sY) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (hf : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem f) (k : ℤ)
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) (hZ : deltaDimension D sX Z = k)
    (hlt : deltaDimension D sY (cycleImageSubspace D sY hY f Z) < k) :
    properPushforwardInDimension D sX sY hX hY f hfB hf k
        (cycleOfIntegralClosedSubspace D sX k Z hZ) = 0
declarations.comment: part (1): f_*[Z] = 0 when dim_δ(Z') < k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforwardInDimension_cycleOfIntegralClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
The pushforward of the cycle `[Z]` of
an integral closed subspace of δ-dimension `k` whose integral closed image `Z'` again has
δ-dimension `k` is `deg(Z/Z')·[Z']`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforwardInDimension_cycleOfIntegralClosedSubspace (sX : X ⟶ D.space)
    (sY : Y ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (hY : D.IsGood sY) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (hf : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem f) (k : ℤ)
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) (hZ : deltaDimension D sX Z = k)
    (hdim : deltaDimension D sY (cycleImageSubspace D sY hY f Z) = k) :
    properPushforwardInDimension D sX sY hX hY f hfB hf k
        (cycleOfIntegralClosedSubspace D sX k Z hZ) =
      (IntegralClosedSubspace.degreeOverImage D sX sY hX hY f Z : ℤ) •
        cycleOfIntegralClosedSubspace D sY k
          (cycleImageSubspace D sY hY f Z) hdim
declarations.comment: part (1): f_*[Z] = deg(Z/Z')·[Z'] when dim_δ(Z') = k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_integralCycle_integralClosedSubspaceUniv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EP1 at the fundamental cycle.** For a dominant quasi-compact morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`
over `B` of integral good algebraic spaces with `dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y) = n`,

`f_*[X] = [R(X) : R(Y)] [Y]` in `Z_n(Y)`.

The whole of `X` is the only integral closed subspace carrying a coefficient of `[X]`, its image
closure is the whole of `Y`, and the degree there is `[R(X) : R(Y)]` because the δ-dimension does
not drop. This is the identity the source uses to read its second conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_integralCycle_integralClosedSubspaceUniv
    (hYInt : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX) (hf : IsQuasiCompact D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hdom : IsDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem f) {n : ℤ}
    (hnX : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (hnY : deltaDimensionClosed D sY hY Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt)) :
    properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hf n (integralCycle D sX n
          (integralClosedSubspaceUniv D sX hX hXInt)
          (deltaDimension_integralClosedSubspaceUniv D sX hX hXInt hnX)) =
      (functionFieldDegreeAtGenericPoint D sX hX sY hY hXInt f : ℤ) •
        integralCycle D sY n (integralClosedSubspaceUniv D sY hY hYInt)
          (deltaDimension_integralClosedSubspaceUniv D sY hY hYInt hnY)
declarations.comment:
f_*[X] = [R(X):R(Y)] [Y]: the pushforward of the fundamental cycle of an integral
good X along a dominant quasi-compact morphism to an integral good Y of the same δ-dimension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforwardInDimension_comp
declarations.doc:
Proper pushforward of `k`-cycles is functorial: pushing forward along
`f : X ⟶ Y` and then along `g : Y ⟶ W` is pushing forward along the composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforwardInDimension_comp (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space) (sW : W ⟶ D.space)
    (hX : D.IsGood sX) (hY : D.IsGood sY) (hW : D.IsGood sW) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ W)
    (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX) (hgB : g ≫ sW = sY) (hf : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hg : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem g) (k : ℤ) (α : CycleGroup D sX k) :
    properPushforwardInDimension D sY sW hY hW g hgB hg k
        (properPushforwardInDimension D sX sY hX hY f hfB hf k α) =
      properPushforwardInDimension D sX sW hX hW (f ≫ g) (by rw [Category.assoc, hgB, hfB])
        (isProper_comp D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hY.1 hW.1 f g hf hg) k α

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properCyclePushforward_associatedCycle_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EP3, part (2).** In Situation 0EDT let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of good
algebraic spaces over the base and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module with
`dim_δ(Supp(F)) ≤ k`. Then

`f_*[F]_k = [f_*F]_k`

in `Z_k(Y)`: the proper pushforward of the `k`-cycle `[F]_k` of Stacks 0EEB is the `k`-cycle
whose coefficient at an integral closed subspace `W ⊂ Y` of δ-dimension `k` is the length of
`f_*F` at the generic point of `W`. The cycles of modules are read at chosen geometric
representatives `γX`, `γY` of the points (by Stacks 0EE1 the lengths do not depend on them). That
the coefficient family of `f_*F` is a `k`-cycle is part of the statement
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleCoeffOfModule_directImageModule_mem_cyclesOfDimension`); the
coherence of `f_*F` (Stacks 08AR) is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem properCyclePushforward_associatedCycle_eq {f : X ⟶ Y} (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (hproper : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1)
    [IsCoherent D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 F] (k : ℤ)
    (hdimF : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX (moduleSupport D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 F)
      (isClosed_moduleSupport D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 F) ≤ (k : EInt))
    (γX : points D.site D.base D.base_mem X → GeometricPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hγX : ∀ x, (γX x).LiesOver x)
    (γY : points D.site D.base D.base_mem Y → GeometricPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
    (hγY : ∀ y, (γY y).LiesOver y) :
    properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hproper.2.1.2 k
        (associatedCycle D sX hX F k γX hγX hdimF) =
      ⟨cycleCoeffOfModule D sY hY (directImageModule D hX.1 hY.1 f F) k γY,
        cycleCoeffOfModule_directImageModule_mem_cyclesOfDimension D sX hX sY hY hfB hproper F k
          hdimF γX hγX γY hγY⟩
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properCyclePushforward_closedSubspaceCycle_eq
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0EDT let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of good algebraic spaces over the base
and let `Z ⊂ X` be a closed subspace with `dim_δ(Z) ≤ k`. Then

`f_*[Z]_k = [f_*𝒪_Z]_k`

in `Z_k(Y)`, where `[Z]_k` is the `k`-cycle of Stacks 0EE9 and `f_*𝒪_Z` is the direct image of
the structure sheaf of `Z` along `Z → X → Y`: the proper pushforward of `[Z]_k` is the
`k`-cycle whose coefficient at an integral closed subspace `W ⊂ Y` of δ-dimension `k` is the
length of `f_*𝒪_Z` at the generic point of `W` (read at the chosen geometric representative
`γY`; by Stacks 0EE1 it does not depend on it). That this coefficient family is a `k`-cycle is
part of the statement
(`cycleCoeffOfModule_closedSubspaceDirectImageStructureSheaf_mem_cyclesOfDimension`).
declarations.statement:
theorem properCyclePushforward_closedSubspaceCycle_eq {f : X ⟶ Y} (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (hproper : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem f) (Z : Subfunctor X)
    (hZ : IsClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem Z) (k : ℤ)
    (hdim : deltaDimensionSubspace D sX hX Z hZ ≤ (k : EInt))
    (γY : points D.site D.base D.base_mem Y → GeometricPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
    (hγY : ∀ y, (γY y).LiesOver y) :
    properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hproper.2.1.2 k
        (closedSubspaceCycle D sX hX Z hZ k hdim) =
      ⟨cycleCoeffOfModule D sY hY (closedSubspaceDirectImageStructureSheaf D sX hX sY hY f Z hZ)
          k γY,
        cycleCoeffOfModule_closedSubspaceDirectImageStructureSheaf_mem_cyclesOfDimension D sX hX
          sY hY hfB hproper Z hZ k hdim γY hγY⟩
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IntegralClosedSubspace.closure_image_subspacePointSet_preimageComponent_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of good algebraic spaces over the base and let `Z ⊆ Y` be
an integral closed subspace. An irreducible component `Z'` of `f^{-1}(Z)` dominates `Z`: the
closure of the image of `|Z'|` is `|Z|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IntegralClosedSubspace.closure_image_subspacePointSet_preimageComponent_of_isFlat
    (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space) (hY : D.IsGood sY) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hflat : IsFlat D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
    (C : irreducibleComponents (Z.preimagePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem f)) :
    closure (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem X f ''
        subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X
          (Z.preimageComponent D.site D.base D.base_mem f hX.1
            (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood sX hX) hY.1 C).subspace) =
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem Y Z.subspace
declarations.comment: a component of the inverse image of an integral closed subspace dominates it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IntegralClosedSubspace.deltaDimension_preimageComponent_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of good algebraic spaces over the base which is flat of
relative dimension `r`, and let `Z ⊆ Y` be an integral closed subspace. An irreducible component
`Z'` of `f^{-1}(Z)` satisfies `dim_δ(Z') = dim_δ(Z) + r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IntegralClosedSubspace.deltaDimension_preimageComponent_of_isFlat
    (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space) (hY : D.IsGood sY) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ) (hflat : IsFlat D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hr : HasRelativeDimension r D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
    (C : irreducibleComponents (Z.preimagePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem f)) :
    deltaDimension D sX (Z.preimageComponent D.site D.base D.base_mem f hX.1
        (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood sX hX) hY.1 C) = deltaDimension D sY Z + r
declarations.comment: the δ-dimension of a component of the inverse image of an integral closed subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.deltaDimensionClosed_preimage_eq_iSup_add
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of good algebraic spaces over the base which is flat of
relative dimension `r`, and let `T ⊆ |Y|` be a closed set of points whose inverse image is
nonempty. Then `dim_δ(f^{-1}(T))` is `r` more than the supremum of the δ-dimensions of the
irreducible components of `T` which `f` meets.

When `f` meets every component of `T`, in particular when `f` is surjective, the supremum is
`dim_δ(T)` and the formula reads `dim_δ(f^{-1}(T)) = dim_δ(T) + r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem deltaDimensionClosed_preimage_eq_iSup_add (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX)
    (sY : Y ⟶ D.space) (hY : D.IsGood sY) {f : X ⟶ Y} (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hflat : IsFlat D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hr : HasRelativeDimension r D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (T : Set (points D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (_hne : (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem X f ⁻¹' T).Nonempty) :
    deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem X f ⁻¹' T)
        (isClosed_preimage_pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hY.1 f hT) =
      (⨆ C : irreducibleComponents T,
        ⨆ _ : (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem X f ⁻¹'
            (Subtype.val '' (C : Set T))).Nonempty,
          deltaDimensionClosed D sY hY (closure (Subtype.val '' (C : Set T)))
            isClosed_closure) + ((r : ℤ) : EInt)
declarations.comment: the δ-dimension of the inverse image of a closed set of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_preimage_pointsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EP6, closedness.** The inverse image of a closed subset of the points of `Y`
under a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` is closed in the points of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_preimage_pointsMap
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (_hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    letI : TopologicalSpace (points B S hS X) := pointTopology B S hS X
    letI : TopologicalSpace (points B S hS Y) := pointTopology B S hS Y
    ∀ {T : Set (points B S hS Y)}, IsClosed T →
      IsClosed ((pointsMap B S hS X f) ⁻¹' T)
declarations.comment: closedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyFinite_preimage_pointsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EP6, local finiteness.** The inverse images of a locally finite collection of
subsets of the points of `Y` under a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` form a
locally finite collection of subsets of the points of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFinite_preimage_pointsMap
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (_hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    {I : Type v} (T : I → Set (points B S hS Y)) :
    letI : TopologicalSpace (points B S hS X) := pointTopology B S hS X
    letI : TopologicalSpace (points B S hS Y) := pointTopology B S hS Y
    LocallyFinite T →
      LocallyFinite (fun i ↦ (pointsMap B S hS X f) ⁻¹' T i)
declarations.comment: local finiteness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatPullbackIntegralCycle
declarations.doc:
The flat pullback of the cycle of an integral closed subspace `W ⊆ Y` of δ-dimension `k`: the
`(k+r)`-cycle `[f^{-1}(W)]_{k+r}` of the scheme-theoretic inverse image.
declarations.statement:
def flatPullbackIntegralCycle (W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem Y) :
    CycleGroup D sX (deltaDimension D sY W + (r : ℤ))
declarations.comment: part (1): f^*[W] = [f^{-1}(W)]_{k+r} for an integral closed subspace W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatPullbackMap
declarations.doc:
The flat pullback of cycles along a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of good algebraic spaces over the base
which is flat of relative dimension `r`, as a homomorphism `f^* : Z_m(Y) →+ Z_n(X)` for
`m + r = n`.
declarations.statement:
def flatPullbackMap (m n : ℤ) (hmn : m + (r : ℤ) = n) :
    CycleGroup D sY m →+ CycleGroup D sX n
declarations.comment:
parts (2) and (3): the flat pullback of a cycle and the homomorphism
  Z_k(Y) → Z_{k+r}(X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatCyclePullback
declarations.doc:
The flat pullback of cycles along a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of good algebraic spaces over the base
which is flat of relative dimension `r`, as an inhabitant of the bundled
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatCyclePullback`: the multiplicities of the inverse images, the
homomorphisms `Z_m(Y) →+ Z_n(X)` for `m + r = n`, the defining formula relating them, and the
containment of the support of `f^*[W]` in `f^{-1}(W)`.
declarations.statement:
def flatCyclePullback (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space)
    (hY : D.IsGood sY) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hflat : IsFlat D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hr : HasRelativeDimension r D.site D.base D.base_mem f) :
    FlatCyclePullback D sX hX sY hY f r
declarations.comment: the whole definition, bundled with its defining formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleGroupRestrict_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EP9, exactness at the `k`-cycles of the ambient space.** In Situation 0EDT let
`X/B` be good, let `i : Y ⟶ X` be a closed immersion over the base and let `j : U ⟶ X` be an
open immersion over the base whose image is the complement of the image of `i`. A `k`-cycle on
`X` restricts to zero on `U` exactly when it is the pushforward of a `k`-cycle on `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleGroupRestrict_eq_zero_iff (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space)
    (hY : D.IsGood sY) (sU : U ⟶ D.space) (hU : D.IsGood sU) {i : Y ⟶ X}
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion D.site D.base D.base_mem i) (hic : i ≫ sX = sY) {j : U ⟶ X}
    (hj : IsOpenImmersion D.site D.base D.base_mem j) (hjc : j ≫ sX = sU)
    (hcomplement : Set.range (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem Y i) =
      (Set.range (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem U j))ᶜ) (k : ℤ) (α : CycleGroup D sX k) :
    cycleGroupRestrict D sX hX sU hU hj hjc k α = 0 ↔
      ∃ β : CycleGroup D sY k,
        cycleGroupClosedPushforward D hX.1 hY.1 (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood sX hX) hi sX hX.2.2
          sY hic k β = α
declarations.comment: exactness at the k-cycles of the ambient space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleGroupRestrict_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EP9, surjectivity onto the `k`-cycles of the open subspace.** In Situation 0EDT let
`X/B` and `U/B` be good and let `j : U ⟶ X` be an open immersion over the base. Every `k`-cycle
on `U` is the restriction of a `k`-cycle on `X`, namely of the coefficient family extending it by
zero along the map which takes the closure of the image of an integral closed subspace.

That extension is a `k`-cycle: it has the right δ-dimension because taking the closure of the
image preserves it, and its support family is locally finite because `|X|` is locally Noetherian,
the structure morphism being locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian base.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleGroupRestrict_surjective (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (sU : U ⟶ D.space)
    (hU : D.IsGood sU) {j : U ⟶ X} (hj : IsOpenImmersion D.site D.base D.base_mem j)
    (hjc : j ≫ sX = sU) (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Surjective (cycleGroupRestrict D sX hX sU hU hj hjc k)
declarations.comment: surjectivity onto the k-cycles of the open subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_and_hasRelativeDimension_comp
declarations.doc:
Let `X/B`, `Y/B` and `Z/B` be good algebraic spaces over the base of `D` and let
`f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms over the base which are flat of relative dimensions `r`
and `s`. Then the composite `f ≫ g` is flat of relative dimension `r + s`: it is locally of
finite type, flat, and of relative dimension `r + s`.
declarations.statement:
