is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.codimension_closureSingleton_eq_one_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor`;
the passage between the two is the topological equivalence
`codimension_closureSingleton_eq_one_iff_dimensionFunction` for the dimension function `δ_{X/B}`
of Stacks 0EDN, which is where integrality of `X` and `dim_δ(X) = n` are used.
declarations.statement:
theorem deltaDimensionIrreducible_closureSingleton_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
    (D : BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.{u})
    {X : (BigFppfOver D.site D.base D.base_mem)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (sX : X ⟶ D.space)
    (hX : D.IsGood sX) (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (E : ClosedSubspaces D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hE : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hX.1⟩ E)
    {W : Set (subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X E.1)}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPrimeDivisor_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EPZ, part (1).** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good and assume `X` integral with
`dim_δ(X) = n`. For an integral closed subspace `Z ⊆ X` the following are equivalent: `Z` is a
prime divisor of `X`; the set of points of `Z` has codimension one in `|X|`; and
`dim_δ(Z) = n - 1`.

These are the hypotheses of the source and nothing else. The equivalence itself is
`isPrimeDivisor_tfae_of_isIntegralSpace`, which also takes a dimension function on `|X|` with
underlying function `δ_{X/B}`; that is not an input of Stacks 0EPZ but the conclusion of Stacks
0EDN, `exists_dimensionFunction_inducedDimensionValue`, applied to the standing data of
Situation 0EDT: the base is a quasi-separated, locally Noetherian, universally catenary
algebraic space with a dimension function, a quasi-separated algebraic space is decent, and a
good `X/B` is decent and locally of finite type over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPrimeDivisor_tfae (D : BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.{u})
    {X : (BigFppfOver D.site D.base D.base_mem)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (sX : X ⟶ D.space)
    (hX : D.IsGood sX) (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) :
    List.TFAE
      [∃ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X, W.subspace = Z.subspace,
        codimension (integralClosedSubspaceSupport D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 Z) = 1,
        deltaDimension D sX Z = n - 1]
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPrimeDivisor_tfae_of_isIntegralSpace'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.principalDivisorCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ1.** The *principal divisor associated to `f ∈ R(X)^*`*, that is
`div(f) = ∑_Z ord_Z(f) [Z]`, as an element of `Z_{n-1}(X)` for `X/B` good and integral with
`dim_δ(X) = n`.

This is the principal divisor of Stacks 0ENP read as a cycle: the formal sum is the same, and it
is an `(n-1)`-cycle because a prime divisor of such an `X` has δ-dimension `n - 1` by
Stacks 0EPZ. Local finiteness is Stacks 0ENN, the argument `hfin`, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.principalDivisorCycleOfRegularLocus` discharges.
declarations.statement:
def principalDivisorCycle
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if principalDivisorCoefficients D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec emb f hf W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (d : DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (hd : ∀ x, d x = D.deltaValue sX x) {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt)) :
    CycleGroup D sX (n - 1)
declarations.comment:
div(f) = ∑ ord_Z(f) [Z] as an element of Z_{n-1}(X); the δ-dimension of a prime
  divisor is n-1 by Stacks 0EPZ, whose dimension-function hypotheses d and hd are Stacks 0EDN,
  carried; local finiteness is Stacks 0ENN, the argument hfin, discharged by
  locallyFinite_principalDivisorCoefficients_ne_zero in principalDivisorCycleOfRegularLocus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.principalDivisorCycleOfRegularLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ1.** The principal divisor `div(f) = ∑_Z ord_Z(f) [Z]` of a rational function
`f ∈ R(X)^*` as an element of `Z_{n-1}(X)`, with the local finiteness of Stacks 0ENN proved from
a nonempty open subset of `|X|` over which `f` is invertible.
declarations.statement:
def principalDivisorCycleOfRegularLocus
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty D.site D.base D.base_mem X
      (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Y))
    (U : Set (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X)) (hUopen : IsOpen U) (hUne : U.Nonempty)
    (hreg : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      W.genericPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem X ∈ U →
        ∃ r : ↥(W.genericHenselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec), IsUnit r ∧
          emb W f =
            algebraMap _ (W.genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec) r)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (d : DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (hd : ∀ x, d x = D.deltaValue sX x) {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt)) :
    CycleGroup D sX (n - 1)
declarations.comment:
div(f) in Z_{n-1}(X), with local finiteness (Stacks 0ENN) proved from a nonempty
  open U over which f is invertible, the datum (U, hUopen, hUne, hreg) of the first sentence of
  the source's own proof of that lemma; the dimension-function hypotheses d and hd are
  Stacks 0EDN, carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle
declarations.doc:
The *principal divisor associated to `f ∈ R(X)^*`*, `div(f) = div_X(f) = ∑_Z ord_Z(f) [Z]`, as
an element of `Z_{n-1}(X)`, for `X/B` good and integral with `dim_δ(X) = n`.
declarations.statement:
def rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle {n : ℤ}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etalePullback_principalDivisorCycle_eq_sum_components_iff
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0EDT let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an étale morphism of good algebraic spaces over `B`, let
`Y` be integral with `dim_δ(Y) = n` and let `g ∈ R(Y)^*`. Then the identity of cycles on `X`

`f^*(div_Y(g)) = ∑_{X'} (X' → X)_* div_{X'}(g ∘ f|_{X'})`,

the sum being over the irreducible components `X'` of `X` (Remark 0EE8), holds at every integral
closed subspace `Z ⊆ X`, coefficientwise, if and only if it holds at those of δ-dimension
`n - 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etalePullback_principalDivisorCycle_eq_sum_components_iff
    (data : EtaleComponentDivisorData D sX hX sY hY f hbase hetale hintY n hnY g) :
    (∀ Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
        (etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycle D sX hX sY hY hbase hetale hrel hintY embY g hg
            hfinY dY hdY hnY).1 Z =
          data.componentPushforwardCoeff Z) ↔
      ∀ Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
        deltaDimension D sX Z = n - 1 →
          (etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycle D sX hX sY hY hbase hetale hrel hintY embY g hg
              hfinY dY hdY hnY).1 Z =
            data.componentPushforwardCoeff Z
declarations.comment:
REDUCED, not proved: the displayed equality of cycles on X — coefficientwise at
  every integral closed subspace, with the sum over the irreducible components of X — HOLDS IF
  AND ONLY IF it holds at the integral closed subspaces of δ-dimension n-1. Proved away from
  them, where both sides vanish, both being (n-1)-cycles. The coefficient identity at those
  subspaces is NOT proved and NOT assumed: it is the source's steps three to six, namely the
  square of henselian local rings of Remark 0EPL, the multiplicity one of Lemma 0EPY, the length
  equality along a flat unramified map of Lemma 02M1 and the length decomposition of Lemma 02QG.
  Hypotheses: hrel, the relative dimension 0 of the étale morphism, flatness itself being
  supplied from Stacks 0467; and, on each irreducible component, the fields of
  EtaleComponentDivisorData — goodness over the base, the
  three hypotheses of Stacks 0ENK with the embeddings they go with, the dominance of f restricted
  to the component (the source's first step, which makes g ∘ f|_{X'} defined), that g ∘ f|_{X'}
  is in R(X')^*, local finiteness of its divisor (Stacks 0ENN) and the dimension function of
  Stacks 0EDN. That dim_δ(X') = n for every component, the source's second paragraph, is
  proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etalePullback_principalDivisorCycle_eq_sum_components_iff_eq_ord_closureImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ2, reduced to one identity of orders of vanishing, and with no data on the
components assumed.** In Situation 0EDT let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an étale morphism of good algebraic
spaces over `B`, let `Y` be integral with `dim_δ(Y) = n` and let `g ∈ R(Y)^*`. Then the identity
of cycles on `X`

`f^*(div_Y(g)) = ∑_{X'} (X' → X)_* div_{X'}(g ∘ f|_{X'})`,

read coefficientwise over the irreducible components `X'` of `X` (Remark 0EE8), holds **if and
only if** at every integral closed subspace `Z ⊆ X` of δ-dimension `n - 1`

`∑_{X'} ord_Z(g ∘ f|_{X'}) = ord_{Z'}(g)`,

`Z'` being the image of `Z` in `Y`. That one identity of integers — the last step of the source's
third to sixth paragraphs — is the whole of what is left.

Nothing about the components is assumed: the right-hand side is formed through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleComponentDivisorData`, whose only input is the local finiteness of
Stacks 0ENN on each component, which is what makes `div_{X'}(g ∘ f|_{X'})` a cycle at all and
which Stacks 0EQ1 takes in the same form on `Y`. In particular the dominance of `f|_{X'}` is
proved, not assumed
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap_genericPoint_eq_genericPoint_irreducibleComponentSubspace`).

Two reductions are combined. Away from δ-dimension `n - 1` both sides vanish, both being
`(n-1)`-cycles — on the right because every component has `dim_δ(X') = n`, the source's second
paragraph, which is proved — the reduction of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etalePullback_principalDivisorCycle_eq_sum_components_iff`, taken here
at the canonical embeddings and hence re-run rather than cited. At
δ-dimension `n - 1` the left-hand side is `ord_{Z'}(g)`, which is Lemma 0EPY in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycle_apply_eq_apply_closureImage`,
and that holds for an arbitrary `X`, not only an integral one.
declarations.statement:
theorem etalePullback_principalDivisorCycle_eq_sum_components_iff_eq_ord_closureImage
    (hfin : ComponentDivisorLocallyFinite D sX hX sY hY hetale hintY g hg) :
    (∀ Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
        (etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycleOfGood D sX hX sY hY hbase hetale hintY g hg
            hfinY hnY).1 Z =
          (etaleComponentDivisorData D sX hX sY hY f hbase hetale hintY n hnY g hg
            hfin).toEtaleComponentDivisorData.componentPushforwardCoeff Z) ↔
      ∀ Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
        deltaDimension D sX Z = n - 1 →
          (etaleComponentDivisorData D sX hX sY hY f hbase hetale hintY n hnY g hg
              hfin).toEtaleComponentDivisorData.componentPushforwardCoeff Z =
            (targetPrincipalDivisorCycle D sY hY hintY g hg hfinY hnY).1
              (Z.closureImage D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1
                (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood sY hY) f)
declarations.comment:
REDUCED to ONE identity of integers, with NOTHING about the components assumed.
  The displayed equality of cycles on X — coefficientwise, the sum over the irreducible components
  of X — HOLDS IF AND ONLY IF at every integral closed subspace Z of X of δ-dimension n-1 the sum
  over the components X' of ord_Z(g ∘ f|_{X'}), computed on X', equals ord_{Z'}(g) for Z' the
  image of Z in Y. This is that equivalence. Proved here, in both halves: away from δ-dimension
  n-1 both sides vanish, both being (n-1)-cycles, which on the right uses dim_δ(X') = n for every
  component (the source's second paragraph, PROVED in
  deltaDimensionClosed_univ_irreducibleComponentSubspace); and at δ-dimension n-1 the coefficient
  of the left side is ord_{Z'}(g) by Lemma 0EPY, for an ARBITRARY X, which is
  etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycle_apply_eq_apply_closureImage together
  with IntegralClosedSubspace.exists_eq_preimageComponent. The right side is formed through
  etaleComponentDivisorData, so the dominance of f restricted to a component — the source's first
  step, what makes g ∘ f|_{X'} defined, and formerly a field of EtaleComponentDivisorDataOfGood — is
  PROVED, in pointsMap_genericPoint_eq_genericPoint_irreducibleComponentSubspace: an étale
  morphism is flat, so generizations lift along |X| → |Y|, and a continuous generalizing map into
  a quasi-sober space carries the generic point of an irreducible component to the generic point
  of one, which for the irreducible |Y| is its generic point. The source's own route, openness of
  |f| plus local finiteness of the components, is not needed. The only input beyond the source's
  hypotheses is ComponentDivisorLocallyFinite, which is Stacks 0ENN on each component and is what
  makes div_{X'}(g ∘ f|_{X'}) a cycle at all; Stacks 0EQ1 takes it in the same shape on Y
  (TargetDivisorLocallyFinite) and this repository proves it from a nonempty open subset over
  which the function is invertible (locallyFinite_principalDivisorCoefficients_ne_zero). For X
  INTEGRAL the remaining identity of integers is PROVED and with it the whole of the source's
  displayed identity, which then reads f^* div_Y(g) = div_X(g ∘ f) in Z_{n-1}(X):
  etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycle_eq_principalDivisorCycle_of_isIntegralSpace, coefficientwise
  etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycle_apply_of_isIntegralSpace, through
  ord_rationalFunctionMap_eq_ord_of_isEtale. WHAT IS STILL MISSING, for an X with several
  components, is exactly the right-hand side of this equivalence, and it is the source's grouping
  of the branches at the generic point of Z over the components through it: ord_Z(g ∘ f|_{X'}) has
  to be identified with the sum of Ring.minimalPrimeOrd over the minimal primes 𝔭 of the local
  ring of an affine étale chart W of X at a point over the generic point of Z with
  componentOfBranch 𝔭 = X'. The partition itself is available
  (finsum_flatBranch_eq_finsum_component_finsum_flatBranch), the chart reading of g ∘ f|_{X'} is
  available with no flatness of f|_{X'}
  (rationalFunctionsToTotalFractionRing_rationalFunctionMap_componentChart,
  nonZeroDivisors_le_comap_chartGlobalSectionsRestrict), and the components of W ×_X X' are
  components of W (mem_irreducibleComponents_image_closedSubspaceBaseChangeChartProj), in the
  stalk-level form comap_stalkMap_closedSubspaceBaseChangeChartProj_mem_minimalPrimes; and the
  transport of Ring.minimalPrimeOrd along the surjection of local rings
  𝒪_{W,w} → 𝒪_{W ×_X X', w'} is Ring.minimalPrimeOrd_map_of_surjective. So the grouping of the
  branches over the components is now proved, as
  finsum_minimalPrimeOrd_stalkMap_eq_finsum_branch_on_component, and so is the recognition of its
  left-hand side as ord_Z(g ∘ f|_{X'}): ord_rationalFunctionMap_eq_finsum_branch_on_component,
  through the stalk-level chart reading
  chartPointRationalFunctionMap_rationalFunctionMap_componentChart, which composes the two halves,
  rationalFunctionsToTotalFractionRing_rationalFunctionMap_componentChart on global sections and
  Scheme.totalFractionRingToStalkFractionRing_map_appTop from global sections to the local ring.
  The sum over ALL the branches of 𝒪_{W,w} is ord_{Z'}(g) on Y, with the same element of
  Q(𝒪_{W,w}): PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_finsum_minimalPrimeOrd_etaleChartComp. So the whole grouping of
  the branches, the content of the source's third to sixth paragraphs, is proved. The coefficient
  of the pushforward along the inclusion of a component is proved too, in
  componentDivisorPushforward_apply_pushforward and _apply_of_forall_ne, through
  properCyclePushforward_ι_eq_integralClosedSubspacePushforward: the inclusion of an irreducible
  component is the inclusion of an integral closed subspace, so the pushforward of Stacks 0EP1
  along it is integralClosedSubspacePushforward, whose coefficients are the extension by zero of
  the coefficients on the component. WHAT NO DECLARATION PROVIDES is the CONVERSE presentation —
  that an integral closed subspace Z of X whose points lie in |X'| is the image of an integral
  closed subspace of X', of δ-dimension making it a prime divisor of X' — which is what cuts
  componentPushforwardCoeff Z, a sum over ALL the components, down to the components through the
  generic point of Z and matches each term with ord_{Z ∩ X'}(g ∘ f|_{X'}); nor is the partition of
  the minimal primes of 𝒪_{W,w} over those components
  (finsum_flatBranch_eq_finsum_component_finsum_flatBranch) joined to the two sums above

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycle_apply_eq_componentPushforwardCoeff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ2.** In Situation 0EDT let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an étale morphism of good algebraic
spaces over `B`, let `Y` be integral with `dim_δ(Y) = n` and let `g ∈ R(Y)^*`. Then, as cycles on
`X`,

`f^*(div_Y(g)) = ∑_{X'} (X' → X)_* div_{X'}(g ∘ f|_{X'})`,

the sum being over the irreducible components `X'` of `X` (Remark 0EE8). The identity is read
coefficientwise, at every integral closed subspace of `X`, because the family of irreducible
components is only locally finite and the right-hand side is therefore not a sum in `Z_{n-1}(X)`.

Both sides are formed at the canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK, on `Y` for `g` and on each
component `X'` for `g ∘ f|_{X'}`, so that the two orders of vanishing are read at the same data
and are tied to one another through `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionMap`.

Nothing beyond the source's own hypotheses goes in. The dominance of `f|_{X'}`, the source's
first step, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap_genericPoint_eq_genericPoint_irreducibleComponentSubspace`;
`dim_δ(X') = n`, the source's second paragraph, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.deltaDimensionClosed_univ_irreducibleComponentSubspace`; and the local
finiteness of Stacks 0ENN, on `Y` and on each component, which is what makes each principal
divisor a cycle at all, is discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.targetDivisorLocallyFinite_of_isGood` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.componentDivisorLocallyFinite_of_isGood`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycle_apply_eq_componentPushforwardCoeff
    (D : BaseSpaceDimensionSituation.{u})
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver D.site D.base D.base_mem)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space) (hY : D.IsGood sY)
    {f : X ⟶ Y} (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (hetale : IsEtale D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hintY : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
    (g : rationalFunctions D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1) (hg : IsUnit g) {n : ℤ}
    (hnY : deltaDimensionClosed D sY hY Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) :
    (etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycleOfGood D sX hX sY hY hbase hetale hintY g hg
        (targetDivisorLocallyFinite_of_isGood D sY hY hintY g hg) hnY).1 Z =
      (etaleComponentDivisorData D sX hX sY hY f hbase hetale hintY n hnY g hg
        (componentDivisorLocallyFinite_of_isGood D sX hX sY hY hetale hintY g
          hg)).toEtaleComponentDivisorData.componentPushforwardCoeff Z
declarations.comment:
the displayed equality of cycles on X, read coefficientwise at every integral
  closed subspace, the sum being over the irreducible components of X (Remark 0EE8); it is read
  coefficientwise because that family is only locally finite, so the right-hand side is not a
  sum in Z_{n-1}(X). Both sides are formed at the canonical Stacks 0ENK embeddings of
  genericFractionEmbedding, on Y and on each component, so the two orders of vanishing are taken
  at the same data and are tied through rationalFunctionMap. UNCONDITIONAL: nothing beyond the
  source's own hypotheses goes in. The left-hand side is the flat pullback of Stacks 0EP8 at
  relative dimension 0 (etalePullbackCycleMap), an etale morphism being flat by Stacks 0467 and
  of relative dimension 0; the right-hand side is the sum of the pushforwards of Stacks 0EP1 of
  the principal divisors of Stacks 0EQ1 on the components. The source's first step, dominance of
  f restricted to a component, is PROVED
  (pointsMap_genericPoint_eq_genericPoint_irreducibleComponentSubspace); its second paragraph,
  dim_delta(X') = n for every component, is PROVED
  (deltaDimensionClosed_univ_irreducibleComponentSubspace); the local finiteness of Stacks 0ENN
  on Y and on each component, which makes the principal divisors cycles at all, is PROVED
  (targetDivisorLocallyFinite_of_isGood, componentDivisorLocallyFinite_of_isGood, out of
  ordRationalFunction_mem_weilDivisor, the repository's Stacks 0ENN); and the source's third to
  sixth paragraphs are componentPushforwardCoeff_eq_ord_of_chart, which computes both sides on
  one affine etale chart of X through the generic point of Z -- also a chart of Y because f is
  etale -- as sums of Ring.minimalPrimeOrd over the branches at the chart point: the coefficient
  of the left side is ord_{Z'}(g) by Lemma 0EPY
  (etalePullbackPrincipalDivisorCycle_apply_eq_apply_closureImage) and is the sum over ALL the
  branches (PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_finsum_minimalPrimeOrd_etaleChartComp, Stacks 0ENM), each term
  of the right side is the subsum over the branches lying on its component
  (ord_rationalFunctionMap_eq_finsum_branch_on_component), and the branches are partitioned over
  the components through the generic point of Z
  (finsum_minimalPrimes_eq_finsum_componentSubspace), which is the source's last step that
  {1,...,t} is the disjoint union of the J(X'); that replaces the square of Remark 0EPL,
  Lemma 02M1 and Lemma 02QG

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_principalDivisorCycle_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ4, reduced to its coefficients at the prime divisors of `Y`.** In Situation
0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `p : X ⟶ Y` be quasi-compact over `B`, let `X` and `Y` be
integral with `dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y) = n`, and let `f ∈ R(X)^*` and `g ∈ R(Y)^*`. Then

`p_* div(f) = div(g)` in `Z_{n-1}(Y)`

holds exactly when it holds coefficientwise at every prime divisor of `Y`, that is when

`∑_Z ord_Z(f) · deg(Z/Z') = ord_{Z'}(g)`

for every prime divisor `Z' ⊆ Y`, the sum being over the integral closed subspaces `Z ⊆ X`.

Both sides are coefficient families on the integral closed subspaces of `Y`, and away from the
prime divisors of `Y` both vanish: the coefficient of `div(g)` at an integral closed subspace
whose point set does not have codimension one is zero by Stacks 0ENP, and the pushforward has no
contribution there by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforwardCoeff_principalDivisorCycleCoefficients_eq_zero`,
which is where the equality of the δ-dimensions is used. That is the whole content of the
reduction; the coefficient identity at a prime divisor of `Y` — which is the mathematical
content of Stacks 0EQ4 — is *not* proved here, and is not assumed either. Taking
`g = Nm_{R(X)/R(Y)}(f)`, that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionNorm D.site D.base D.base_mem … p hgen f`, gives the
source's statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_principalDivisorCycle_eq_iff
    (hfinX : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if principalDivisorCoefficients D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdecX embX f hf W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hfinY : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem Y =>
      if principalDivisorCoefficients D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1 hdecY embY g hg W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
    {p : X ⟶ Y} (hpB : p ≫ sY = sX) (hp : IsQuasiCompact D.site D.base D.base_mem p) :
    properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hp (n - 1)
          (principalDivisorCycle D sX hX hdecX embX f hf hfinX hintX dX hdX hnX) =
        principalDivisorCycle D sY hY hdecY embY g hg hfinY hintY dY hdY hnY ↔
      ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem Y,
        (∑ᶠ Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
            principalDivisorCycleCoefficients D sX hX hdecX embX f hf Z *
              properCycleMult D sX hX sY hY p Z
                (W.toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem)) =
          principalDivisorCoefficients D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1 hdecY embY g hg W
declarations.comment:
REDUCED, not proved: p_*div(f) = div(g) in Z_{n-1}(Y) IF AND ONLY IF it holds at
every prime divisor of Y; proved away from them, using dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y). Take g to be
rationalFunctionNorm, the norm Nm_{R(X)/R(Y)} constructed here, for the source's statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properCyclePushforward_rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ4.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `X` and `Y` be integral
with `n = dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y)`, let `p : X ⟶ Y` be a dominant proper morphism, let `f ∈ R(X)^*`
and set `g = Nm_{R(X)/R(Y)}(f)`. Then

`p_* div(f) = div(g)` in `Z_{n-1}(Y)`.

Here `div` is the principal divisor of Stacks 0EQ1
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle`, at the canonical embeddings of
Stacks 0ENK), `p_*` is proper pushforward of cycles (Stacks 0EP2) and `g` is the norm
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionNorm` along the extension of function fields `p`
induces, as a unit of `R(Y)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalFunctionNormUnit`); `R(X)/R(Y)`
is finite (Stacks 0AD5, from `dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y)`). Both sides are `(n-1)`-cycles on `Y`,
determined by their coefficients at the prime divisors of `Y`, where they agree by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finsum_rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle_mul_properCycleMult_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properCyclePushforward_rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle {p : X ⟶ Y}
    (hpB : p ≫ sY = sX) (hproper : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem p)
    (hdom : IsDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem p) {n : ℤ}
    (hnX : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (hnY : deltaDimensionClosed D sY hY Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (f : (rationalFunctions D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1)ˣ) :
    properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hproper.2.1.2 (n - 1)
        (rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle D sX hX hintX hnX f) =
      rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle D sY hY hintY hnY
        (rationalFunctionNormUnit D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hY.1 hintX hintY p
          (pointsMap_genericPoint_of_isDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hY.1 hintX hintY
            p hdom) f)
declarations.comment:
p_* div(f) = div(Nm_{R(X)/R(Y)}(f)) in Z_{n-1}(Y), for X/B, Y/B good and integral
with dim_δ X = dim_δ Y = n, p : X → Y dominant and proper, f ∈ R(X)^*; div is 0EQ1 at the
canonical embeddings, p_* is 0EP2, the norm is constructed; nothing carried

declarations.name: Stacks.Norm.norm_baseChange_eq_prod_quotient
declarations.doc:
**The field-theoretic step of Stacks 0EQ4, whose proof the source omits.** Let `K` be a
field, `L/K` a finite extension and `M/K` a finite *separable* extension. Then `M ⊗_K L` is a
finite product of fields `∏ᵢ Mᵢ` — concretely, the product of its quotients by its maximal
ideals — and for `t ∈ L` the image in `M` of `Nm_{L/K}(t)` is the product of the norms over `M`
of the images `tᵢ` of `1 ⊗ t`:

`Nm_{L/K}(t) = ∏ᵢ Nm_{Mᵢ/M}(tᵢ)` in `M`.

Separability of `M/K` is what makes `M ⊗_K L` reduced, and being also finite-dimensional over
`M` it is then the product of its residue fields. The identity itself is base change of the norm
followed by multiplicativity over the factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem norm_baseChange_eq_prod_quotient {K L M : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Field M]
    [Algebra K L] [Algebra K M] [FiniteDimensional K L] [FiniteDimensional K M]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable K M] [Fintype (MaximalSpectrum (M ⊗[K] L))] (t : L) :
    algebraMap K M (Algebra.norm K t) =
      ∏ p : MaximalSpectrum (M ⊗[K] L),
        Algebra.norm M (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal (1 ⊗ₜ[K] t))
declarations.comment:
the field-theoretic norm compatibility at the end of the proof, for which the
source says 'we omit the proof': for L/K finite and M/K finite separable, M ⊗_K L = ∏ M_i and
Nm_{L/K}(t) = ∏ Nm_{M_i/M}(t_i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleFamilySumCoeff_mem_cyclesOfDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ6, part (1).** The coefficientwise sum `∑ (i_j)_* c_j` of the pushforwards of a
family of `k`-cycles along the inclusions of a locally finite collection of integral closed
subspaces is a `k`-cycle on `X`.

Local finiteness of the collection gives local finiteness of the support: a neighbourhood of a
point meeting only finitely many of the `|W_j|` is shrunk, using the pushforwards from those
finitely many, to one meeting only finitely many point sets of subspaces with a nonzero
coefficient. The δ-dimension of each such subspace is `k` because that holds for the summand
it comes from.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleFamilySumCoeff_mem_cyclesOfDimension (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX)
    (W : J → IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hWfin : LocallyFinite fun j : J =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X (W j).subspace)
    (k : ℤ) (c : ∀ j, CycleGroup D ((W j).subspace.ι ≫ sX) k) :
    cycleFamilySumCoeff D sX hX W k c ∈ cyclesOfDimension D sX k
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleFamilySum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ6, part (1).** The element `∑ (i_j)_* c_j` of `Z_k(X)` determined by a locally
finite collection `{W_j ⊆ X}` of integral closed subspaces and a family of `k`-cycles `c_j` on
them; taking `c_j = div(f_j)` for `f_j ∈ R(W_j)^*` on subspaces of δ-dimension `k + 1` gives
the cycle of the source.
declarations.statement:
def cycleFamilySum (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX)
    (W : J → IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hWfin : LocallyFinite fun j : J =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X (W j).subspace)
    (k : ℤ) (c : ∀ j, CycleGroup D ((W j).subspace.ι ≫ sX) k) : CycleGroup D sX k
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRationallyEquivalentToZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ6, part (2).** A `k`-cycle on a good algebraic space `X/B` is *rationally
equivalent to zero* when it is the cycle `∑ (i_j)_* div(f_j)` of part (1): there is a locally
finite family `{W_j ⊆ X}` of integral closed subspaces with `dim_δ(W_j) = k + 1`, and on each a
principal divisor `div(f_j)`, `f_j ∈ R(W_j)^*`, whose pushforwards sum to the cycle.

The sum is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleFamilySum`, which is part (1) of the source.
declarations.statement:
def IsRationallyEquivalentToZero (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ)
    (α : CycleGroup D sX k) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2): rationally equivalent to zero. The sum is part (1), AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleFamilySum; the index type ranges over the universe v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalEquivalences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ6, part (2).** The subgroup of `k`-cycles rationally equivalent to zero. Its
carrier is exactly the set of cycles of the form `∑ (i_j)_* div(f_j)` of part (1); that this set
is a subgroup is the content of the three closure proofs.
declarations.statement:
def rationalEquivalences (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ) :
    AddSubgroup (CycleGroup D sX k)
declarations.comment: part (2): the cycles rationally equivalent to zero, as a subgroup of Z_k(X); the carrier is exactly the set of sums of part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RationallyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ6, part (3).** Two `k`-cycles are *rationally equivalent* when their difference
is rationally equivalent to zero.
declarations.statement:
def RationallyEquivalent (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ)
    (α β : CycleGroup D sX k) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3): α ∼_rat β, defined as α - β being rationally equivalent to zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationallyEquivalent_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ6, part (3).** Rational equivalence is an equivalence relation on `Z_k(X)`:
reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity are the three closure properties of the subgroup of
cycles rationally equivalent to zero, applied to `α - α = 0`, `β - α = -(α - β)` and
`α - γ = (α - β) + (β - γ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationallyEquivalent_equivalence (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ) :
    Equivalence (RationallyEquivalent.{v} D sX hX k)
declarations.comment: part (3): ∼_rat is an equivalence relation, from the subgroup property of the cycles rationally equivalent to zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ6, part (4).** The *Chow group of `k`-cycles on `X`*, that is the Chow group of
`k`-cycles modulo rational equivalence,

`CH_k(X) = Z_k(X)/∼_rat`,

the quotient of the group of `k`-cycles of a good algebraic space `X/B` by the subgroup of
cycles rationally equivalent to zero.
declarations.statement: abbrev chowGroup (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ)
declarations.comment: part (4): CH_k(X) = Z_k(X)/∼_rat, the quotient of Z_k(X) by the subgroup of cycles rationally equivalent to zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowClass
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0EQ6, part (4).** The class map `Z_k(X) → CH_k(X)`, the quotient homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
def chowClass (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ) :
    CycleGroup D sX k →+ chowGroup.{v} D sX hX k
declarations.comment: part (4): the class map Z_k(X) → CH_k(X) of the quotient by ∼_rat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowClass_cycleFamilySum_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ6, parts (2) and (4).** The class in `CH_k(X)` of the cycle
`∑ (i_j)_* div(f_j)` of part (1) is zero: a sum of principal divisors on a locally finite family
of integral closed subspaces of δ-dimension `k + 1` is rationally equivalent to zero, hence dies
in the quotient.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowClass_cycleFamilySum_eq_zero (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ)
    {J : Type v} (W : J → IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hWfin : LocallyFinite fun j : J =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X (W j).subspace)
    (c : ∀ j, CycleGroup D ((W j).subspace.ι ≫ sX) k)
    (hWdim : ∀ j, deltaDimension D sX (W j) = k + 1)
    (hWprin : ∀ j, IsPrincipalDivisorCycle D ((W j).subspace.ι ≫ sX) k (c j)) :
    chowClass.{v} D sX hX k (cycleFamilySum D sX hX W hWfin k c) = 0
declarations.comment: parts (2) and (4): the class map kills ∑ (i_j)_* div(f_j), the cycle of part (1); proved for the constructed CH_k(X), not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRationallyEquivalentToZeroCanonical
declarations.doc:
A `k`-cycle on a good algebraic space `X/B` is *rationally equivalent to zero* when it is
the cycle `∑ (i_j)_* div(f_j)` of part (1): there is a locally finite family `{W_j ⊆ X}` of
integral closed subspaces with `dim_δ(W_j) = k + 1`, and on each a rational function
`f_j ∈ R(W_j)^*` whose principal divisor `div(f_j)` is the `j`-th summand, the pushforwards
summing to the cycle.

Each `W_j` is good over `B` by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGood_integralClosedSubspace` and
integral by definition, so `div(f_j)` is read at the canonical embeddings
`R(W_j) → Q(𝒪^h_{W_j,ξ})` of Stacks 0ENK and depends on nothing but `f_j`: the summand condition
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsPrincipalDivisorCycleOfGood`. The sum is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleFamilySum`.
declarations.statement:
def IsRationallyEquivalentToZeroCanonical (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ)
    (α : CycleGroup D sX k) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2): rationally equivalent to zero, the summands being principal divisors at the canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK. The sum is part (1), AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleFamilySum; the index type ranges over the universe v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationalEquivalencesCanonical
declarations.doc:
The subgroup of `k`-cycles rationally equivalent to zero. Its carrier is exactly the set of
cycles of the form `∑ (i_j)_* div(f_j)`, the principal divisors being read at the canonical
embeddings of Stacks 0ENK.
declarations.statement:
def rationalEquivalencesCanonical (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ) :
    AddSubgroup (CycleGroup D sX k)
declarations.comment: part (2): the cycles rationally equivalent to zero, as a subgroup of Z_k(X); the carrier is exactly the set of sums of part (1) with div(f) at the canonical embeddings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RationallyEquivalentCanonical
declarations.doc:
Two `k`-cycles are *rationally equivalent* when their difference is rationally equivalent to
zero.
declarations.statement:
def RationallyEquivalentCanonical (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ)
    (α β : CycleGroup D sX k) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3): α ∼_rat β, defined as α - β being rationally equivalent to zero, for the reading of part (2) at the canonical embeddings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationallyEquivalentCanonical_equivalence
declarations.doc: Rational equivalence is an equivalence relation on `Z_k(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationallyEquivalentCanonical_equivalence (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ) :
    Equivalence (RationallyEquivalentCanonical.{v} D sX hX k)
declarations.comment: part (3): ∼_rat is an equivalence relation, from the subgroup property of the cycles rationally equivalent to zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroupCanonical
declarations.doc:
The *Chow group of `k`-cycles on `X`*, that is the group of `k`-cycles modulo rational
equivalence,

`CH_k(X) = Z_k(X)/∼_rat`,

the quotient of the group of `k`-cycles of a good algebraic space `X/B` by the subgroup of
cycles rationally equivalent to zero.
declarations.statement: abbrev chowGroupCanonical (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ)
declarations.comment: part (4): CH_k(X) = Z_k(X)/∼_rat, the quotient of Z_k(X) by the subgroup of cycles rationally equivalent to zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowClassCanonical
declarations.doc: The class map `Z_k(X) → CH_k(X)`, the quotient homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
def chowClassCanonical (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ) :
    CycleGroup D sX k →+ chowGroupCanonical.{v} D sX hX k
declarations.comment: part (4): the class map Z_k(X) → CH_k(X) of the quotient by ∼_rat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowClassCanonical_cycleFamilySum_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The class in `CH_k(X)` of the cycle `∑ (i_j)_* div(f_j)`, a sum of principal divisors on a
locally finite family of integral closed subspaces of δ-dimension `k + 1`, is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowClassCanonical_cycleFamilySum_eq_zero (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ)
    {J : Type v} (W : J → IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hWfin : LocallyFinite fun j : J =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X (W j).subspace)
    (c : ∀ j, CycleGroup D ((W j).subspace.ι ≫ sX) k)
    (hWdim : ∀ j, deltaDimension D sX (W j) = k + 1)
    (hWprin : ∀ j, IsPrincipalDivisorCycleOfGood D ((W j).subspace.ι ≫ sX)
      (isGood_integralClosedSubspace D sX hX (W j)) (W j).isIntegralSpace k (c j)) :
    chowClassCanonical.{v} D sX hX k (cycleFamilySum D sX hX W hWfin k c) = 0
declarations.comment: parts (2) and (4): the class map kills ∑ (i_j)_* div(f_j), the cycle of part (1); proved for the constructed CH_k(X), not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroup_localization
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, let `U ⊆ X` be an open subspace, let `Y ⊆ X` be a closed
subspace with `|Y| = |X| \ |U|` and let `i : Y → X`, `j : U → X` be the inclusions. Let `k ∈ ℤ`.

1. If `α, β ∈ Z_k(X)` satisfy `α|_U ∼_rat β|_U`, then `α ∼_rat β + i_*γ` for some `γ ∈ Z_k(Y)`.
2. In other words, `CH_k(Y) →[i_*] CH_k(X) →[j^*] CH_k(U) → 0` is an exact complex of abelian
   groups: the kernel of `j^*` is the image of `i_*`, and `j^*` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowGroup_localization
    (hcomplement : Set.range (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem Y.toFunctor Y.ι) =
      (Set.range (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem U.toFunctor U.ι))ᶜ) (k : ℤ) :
    (∀ α β : CycleGroup D sX k,
      RationallyEquivalent.{v} D (U.ι ≫ sX) (isGood_ι_of_isOpenSubspace D sX hX U hU) k
        (cycleGroupRestrict D sX hX (U.ι ≫ sX) (isGood_ι_of_isOpenSubspace D sX hX U hU) hU.2
          rfl k α)
        (cycleGroupRestrict D sX hX (U.ι ≫ sX) (isGood_ι_of_isOpenSubspace D sX hX U hU) hU.2
          rfl k β) →
      ∃ γ : CycleGroup D (Y.ι ≫ sX) k,
        RationallyEquivalent.{v} D sX hX k α
          (β + cycleGroupClosedPushforward D hX.1 hY.1 (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood sX hX) hY.2
            sX hX.2.2 (Y.ι ≫ sX) rfl k γ)) ∧
      Function.Exact (chowGroupClosedPushforward.{v} D sX hX Y hY k)
        (chowGroupRestrict.{v} D sX hX U hU k) ∧
      Function.Surjective (chowGroupRestrict.{v} D sX hX U hU k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationallyEquivalent_locallyFiniteCycleSum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQ8.** Let `{T_i}_{i ∈ I}` be a locally finite collection of subsets of `|X|` and
let `α_i, β_i ∈ Z_k(X)` be supported on `T_i`. If `α_i ∼_rat β_i` on `T_i` for every `i`, then
`∑ α_i ∼_rat ∑ β_i`: the combined family `{W_{i, j}}_{i ∈ I, j ∈ J_i}` of witnessing subspaces
is locally finite, so it is a single rational equivalence between the two sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationallyEquivalent_locallyFiniteCycleSum (sX : X ⟶ D.space) (hX : D.IsGood sX) (k : ℤ)
    (T : I → Set (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X)) (hT : LocallyFinite T)
    (α β : I → CycleGroup D sX k)
    (hαT : ∀ (i : I) (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X),
      (α i).1 Z ≠ 0 → subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X Z.subspace ⊆ T i)
    (hβT : ∀ (i : I) (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X),
      (β i).1 Z ≠ 0 → subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X Z.subspace ⊆ T i)
    (hαβ : ∀ i, RationallyEquivalentOn.{v} D sX hX k (T i) (α i) (β i)) :
    RationallyEquivalent.{v} D sX hX k (locallyFiniteCycleSum D sX k T hT α hαT)
      (locallyFiniteCycleSum D sX k T hT β hβT)
declarations.comment: the remark in full: for alpha_i, beta_i supported on a locally finite family T_i with alpha_i ~rat beta_i on T_i, the sums are k-cycles and are rationally equivalent, the combined witnessing family being locally finite

declarations.name: locallyFinite_sigma_of_subset
declarations.doc:
Let `T : I → Set Y` be a locally finite collection of subsets of a topological space and,
for each `i`, let `W i : J i → Set Y` be a locally finite collection with `W i j ⊆ T i` for all
`j`. Then the combined collection `fun ij : Σ i, J i ↦ W ij.1 ij.2` is locally finite.
declarations.comment: local finiteness of the combined family

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_multiplicity_mul_ord
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQA, coefficientwise.** *The order of vanishing of a rational function pulls back
with multiplicities.* Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat, let `Z' ⊆ Y` and `Z ⊆ X` be prime divisors with
`Z` lying over `Z'`, let `φ : 𝒪^h_{Y,ξ'} ⟶ 𝒪^h_{X,ξ}` be the induced flat local homomorphism and
let `m` be the multiplicity of `Z` over `Z'`. For a rational function `g` on `Y` whose ratio at
`ξ'` is `a / b` with `a` and `b` nonzerodivisors, and for the composite `g ∘ f|_X`, whose ratio
at `ξ` is therefore `φ(a) / φ(b)`,

  `ord_Z(g ∘ f|_X) = m · ord_{Z'}(g)`.

The multiplicity `m` is the one with which `Z` occurs in `f^{-1}(Z')`, so for `X` integral this
is the source's identity `f^* div_Y(g) = ∑ m_{X',X} (X' ⟶ X)_* div_{X'}(g ∘ f|_{X'})` read at
the coefficient of `Z`; for `X` with several components it is each of the two readings of that
identity, as the implementation notes explain.

Nothing about the conclusion is assumed. The multiplicity enters as the colength `hm` and the
whole content — that the order of vanishing multiplies by it — is `Ring.ord_map_of_flatHom`,
which is Stacks 02M1 applied to `𝒪^h_{Y,ξ'} / a` and to `𝒪^h_{Y,ξ'} / b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_multiplicity_mul_ord
    (hloc : IsLocalHom φ) (hflat : φ.Flat) {m : ℕ}
    (hm : primeDivisorFlatMultiplicity B S hS hX hdecX ZX hY hdecY ZY φ = (m : ℕ∞))
    (embY : rationalFunctions B S hS hY →+* ZY.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hY hdecY)
    (embX : rationalFunctions B S hS hX →+* ZX.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdecX)
    (g : rationalFunctions B S hS hY) (gf : rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
    (a b : nonZeroDivisors ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY))
    (hg : embY g = IsLocalization.mk' (ZY.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hY hdecY)
      (a : ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY)) b)
    (hgf : embX gf = IsLocalization.mk' (ZX.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdecX)
      (φ (a : ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY)))
      (⟨φ (b : ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY)),
        Ring.map_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_flatHom hflat b.2⟩ :
        nonZeroDivisors ↥(ZX.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdecX)))
    (hgu : IsUnit (embY g)) (hgfu : IsUnit (embX gf)) :
    ZX.ord B S hS hX hdecX (embX gf) hgfu =
      (m : ℤ) * ZY.ord B S hS hY hdecY (embY g) hgu
declarations.comment:
coefficientwise at a prime divisor Z of X with generic point ξ lying over a prime
divisor Z' of Y with generic point ξ': the order of vanishing of a rational function pulls back
with the multiplicity, ord_Z(g ∘ f) = m · ord_{Z'}(g), where m is the colength of the extended
maximal ideal — the multiplicity with which Z occurs in the closed subspace f^{-1}(Z'), hence
the coefficient the flat pullback of Stacks 0EP8 attaches to Z. PROVED, not assumed: that the
order of vanishing multiplies by the multiplicity, from Stacks 02M1
(length_baseChange_eq_length_mul_length_quotient) applied to the cyclic modules O^h/a and O^h/b,
which is how Stacks 02M1 computes with a multiplicity. For X integral this is the source's
identity f^* div_Y(g) = ∑ m_{X',X} (X' → X)_* div_{X'}(g ∘ f|_{X'}) read at the coefficient of
Z, the one component having multiplicity one; the statement is coefficientwise because neither
side exists in this repository — the flat pullback of cycles is Stacks 0EP8 and the principal
divisor div(g) is Stacks 0ENP — and for that same reason Stacks 0EPT and 0EPV are already
carried coefficientwise here. NOT COVERED: for X with several irreducible components, the step
from this identity to the cycle identity, namely the additivity over the components of the
multiplicities of Stacks 0EE2 and Stacks 0EE9; the statement applies to X and to each component
X' separately, with m read in each, but no additivity of those multiplicities is proved in this
repository. RESTRICTED: carried as explicit named hypotheses are (i) the flat local homomorphism
φ of the henselian local rings at the generic points, the map of henselian local rings induced
by a morphism of decent algebraic spaces not being available here, with its locality and
flatness as the hypotheses hloc and hflat; (ii) the embeddings R(Y) → Q(O^h_{Y,ξ'}) and
R(X) → Q(O^h_{X,ξ}) of Stacks 0ENK as embY and embX, exactly as Stacks 0EPT carries them;
(iii) the composite g ∘ f|_X as the parameter gf together with hgf, that its ratio at ξ is the
image under φ of the ratio of g at ξ' — this repository has no pullback of a rational function
along a morphism of algebraic spaces, only the chartwise fraction rule a/b ↦ f-sharp a /
f-sharp b of Stacks 0ENC, which is what hgf states; and (iv) finiteness of the multiplicity, as
hm naming the natural number m it equals. Locality, Noetherianness and the dimension bound on
the henselian local rings are instance arguments, as they are for PrimeDivisor.ord and
orderOfVanishingSection themselves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatPullbackMap_rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle_eq_finsum_components
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQA.** *Flat pullback of a principal divisor.* In Situation 0EDT let `X, Y/B` be
good, assume `Y` integral with `dim_δ(Y) = k`, and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism over `B`
of relative dimension `r`. Then for `g ∈ R(Y)^*`

  `f^* div_Y(g) = ∑_{X'} m_{X', X} (X' → X)_* div_{X'}(g ∘ f|_{X'})`

as `(k + r - 1)`-cycles on `X`: at every integral closed subspace `Z ⊆ X` the coefficient of the
flat pullback (Stacks 0EP8) of `div_Y(g)` (Stacks 0EQ1) is the sum over the irreducible
components `X'` of `X` of `m_{X', X}`, the multiplicity of `X'` in `X` (Stacks 0EE9), times the
coefficient at `Z` of the pushforward along `X' → X` (Stacks 0EP1) of the principal divisor of
`g ∘ f|_{X'} ∈ R(X')^*`. The sum is a locally finite one, which is why the identity of cycles is
stated at each coefficient.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullbackMap_rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle_eq_finsum_components {k : ℤ}
    (hk : deltaDimensionClosed D sY hY Set.univ isClosed_univ = (k : EInt))
    (g : (rationalFunctions D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1)ˣ)
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) :
    (flatPullbackMap D sX hX sY hY f hbase r hflat hr (k - 1) (k + r - 1) (by ring)
        (rationalFunctionPrincipalDivisorCycle D sY hY hintY hk g)).1 Z =
      ∑ᶠ W : IrreducibleComponentSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1,
        spaceMultiplicity D X hX.1 W.1 *
          (W.flatPullbackDivisorPushforward D sX hX sY hY f hbase r hr hflat hintY hk g).1 Z
declarations.comment:
the displayed identity of (k + r - 1)-cycles on X, at every integral closed
  subspace of X; the sum is over the irreducible components X' of X (a locally finite family),
  m_{X',X} is the length of O_X at the generic point of X' (0EE9 part (1) for the space X),
  g ∘ f|_{X'} is the image of g under the extension of function fields of the dominant
  f|_{X'} (0EML), and every cycle is the one of this chapter: f^* is 0EP8, div is 0EQ1 at the
  canonical embeddings of 0ENK, (X' → X)_* is 0EP1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationallyEquivalentCanonical_flatPullbackMap
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0EDT let `X, Y/B` be good and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism over `B` which is
flat of relative dimension `r`. If `α ∼_rat β` are rationally equivalent `m`-cycles on `Y`, then
`f^*α ∼_rat f^*β` as `n`-cycles on `X`, where `m + r = n`.

Rational equivalence is that of Stacks 0EQ6 with `div(g)` read at the canonical embeddings of
Stacks 0ENK (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RationallyEquivalentCanonical`), and `f^*` is the flat
pullback of cycles of Stacks 0EP8 (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatPullbackMap`). The family
presenting `α - β` is indexed in a universe `v`, the one presenting `f^*α - f^*β` in
`max v (u + 1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationallyEquivalentCanonical_flatPullbackMap (m n : ℤ) (hmn : m + (r : ℤ) = n)
    {α β : CycleGroup D sY m} (h : RationallyEquivalentCanonical.{v} D sY hY m α β) :
    RationallyEquivalentCanonical.{max v (u + 1)} D sX hX n
      (flatPullbackMap D sX hX sY hY f hbase r hflat hr m n hmn α)
      (flatPullbackMap D sX hX sY hY f hbase r hflat hr m n hmn β)
declarations.comment:
f^*α ∼_rat f^*β in Z_{m+r}(X) for α ∼_rat β in Z_m(Y), f flat of relative
  dimension r between good spaces over B; rational equivalence at the canonical embeddings of
  0ENK, the presenting family on X indexed in max v (u+1) when the one on Y is indexed in v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.rationallyEquivalentCanonical_properCyclePushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQC.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good and let `p : X ⟶ Y` be a
proper morphism over the base. If `α, β ∈ Z_k(X)` are rationally equivalent, then `p_*α` is
rationally equivalent to `p_*β`.

Rational equivalence is that of Stacks 0EQ6 with the summands `div(f_j)` read at the canonical
embeddings `R(W_j) → Q(𝒪^h_{W_j,ξ})` of Stacks 0ENK
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.RationallyEquivalentCanonical`), and `p_*` is the proper pushforward of
cycles of Stacks 0EP1.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationallyEquivalentCanonical_properCyclePushforward (sX : X ⟶ D.space)
    (hX : D.IsGood sX) (sY : Y ⟶ D.space) (hY : D.IsGood sY) {p : X ⟶ Y} (hpB : p ≫ sY = sX)
    (hp : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem p) (k : ℤ) {α β : CycleGroup D sX k}
    (h : RationallyEquivalentCanonical.{v} D sX hX k α β) :
    RationallyEquivalentCanonical.{v} D sY hY k
      (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hp.2.1.2 k α)
      (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hp.2.1.2 k β)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.divisorCycleOfSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQE, part (1).** The *Weil divisor associated to a nonzero meromorphic section `s`
of `ℒ`*, that is `div_ℒ(s) = ∑_Z ord_{Z,ℒ}(s) [Z]` of Stacks 0EPU, as an element of
`Z_{n-1}(X)`: it is an `(n-1)`-cycle because a prime divisor of an integral good algebraic
space of δ-dimension `n` has δ-dimension `n - 1` by Stacks 0EPZ.

Local finiteness of the prime divisors with `ord_{Z,ℒ}(s) ≠ 0` is Stacks 0EPS, here the
hypothesis `hfin`; `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.divisorCycleOfSectionOfGenerating` discharges it
from a nonempty open subspace over which `s` generates `ℒ`.
declarations.comment:
part (1): div_ℒ(s) = ∑ ord_{Z,ℒ}(s) [Z] as an element of Z_{n-1}(X); the
δ-dimension of a prime divisor is n-1 by Stacks 0EPZ, whose dimension-function hypotheses d and
hd are Stacks 0EDN, carried; local finiteness of the prime divisors with ord ≠ 0 is Stacks
0EPS, the hypothesis hfin; the ratio family at the generic points is the parameter ratio, as in
Stacks 0EPR and 0EPU

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.divisorCycleOfSectionOfGenerating
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQE, part (1).** The Weil divisor `div_ℒ(s) = ∑_Z ord_{Z,ℒ}(s) [Z]` of a nonzero
meromorphic section `s` of `ℒ` as an element of `Z_{n-1}(X)`, with the local finiteness of its
support supplied by Stacks 0EPS from a nonempty open subset of `|X|` containing the generic
point of no prime divisor along which `s` has nonzero order — the open subspace over which `s`
generates `ℒ`.
declarations.statement:
def divisorCycleOfSectionOfGenerating
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty D.site D.base D.base_mem X
      (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Y))
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L)
    (ratio : LocalRatioFamily.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L)
    (U : Set (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X)) (hUopen : IsOpen U) (hUne : U.Nonempty)
    (hgen : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratio W ≠ 0 →
        W.genericPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem X ∈ Uᶜ)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (d : DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (hd : ∀ x, d x = D.deltaValue sX x) {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt)) :
    CycleGroup D sX (n - 1)
declarations.comment:
part (1): div_ℒ(s) in Z_{n-1}(X), with local finiteness supplied by Stacks 0EPS
from the open subspace U over which s generates ℒ; the δ-dimension of a prime divisor is n-1 by
Stacks 0EPZ, whose dimension-function hypotheses d and hd are Stacks 0EDN, carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCapFundamental
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQE, part (2).** The *Weil divisor associated to `ℒ`*, that is
`c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] = [div_ℒ(s)] ∈ CH_{n-1}(X)`, the class of the Weil divisor of a nonzero
meromorphic section `s` of `ℒ`.

The class is independent of the chosen section:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq`. The Chow group `CH_{n-1}(X)` is the
parameter `chow`, only part (1) of Stacks 0EQ6 being available in this library.
declarations.statement:
def firstChernClassCapFundamental
    (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sX hX (n - 1) CH)
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L)
    (ratio : LocalRatioFamily.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L)
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratio W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (d : DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (hd : ∀ x, d x = D.deltaValue sX x)
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt)) : CH
declarations.comment:
part (2): c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] = class of div_ℒ(s) in CH_{n-1}(X); CH_{n-1}(X) together
with its class map and its principal divisors is carried as the ChowTarget parameter chow,
standing in for Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2)-(4); independence of the chosen section s is
firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQE, part (2), well-definedness.** The class `c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X]` does not depend on the
chosen nonzero meromorphic section of `ℒ`.

If the ratios of `s` and `s'` at the generic points of the prime divisors differ by the image of
a rational function `f`, then `div_ℒ(s) - div_ℒ(s') = div(f)` by Stacks 0EPT, and `div(f)` is
rationally equivalent to zero by Stacks 0EQ6: it is the one-member family `∑ (i_j)_* div(f_j)`
of part (1), taken on `X` itself. That `div(f)` is one of the principal divisors of the Chow
group parameter is the hypothesis `hprincipal`, the principal divisor of Stacks 0ENP not being
available in this library.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq
    (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sX hX (n - 1) CH)
    (s s' : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L)
    (ratio : LocalRatioFamily.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L)
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratio W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hfin' : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s' ratio W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (d : DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (hd : ∀ x, d x = D.deltaValue sX x)
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (emb : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      rationalFunctions D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 →+*
        W.genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec)
    (f : rationalFunctions D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1)
    (hf : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X, IsUnit (emb W f))
    (hratio : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      ((ratio W s : W.genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec)) =
        emb W f * (ratio W s' : W.genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec))
    (hprincipal : ∃ (Y : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
      (c : CycleGroup D (Y.subspace.ι ≫ sX) (n - 1)), c ∈ chow.principalDivisors Y ∧
        ∀ Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
          (integralClosedSubspacePushforward D sX hX Y (n - 1) c).1 Z =
            principalDivisorCycleCoefficients D sX hX hdec emb f hf Z) :
    firstChernClassCapFundamental D sX hX hdec L chow s ratio hfin hint d hd hn =
      firstChernClassCapFundamental D sX hX hdec L chow s' ratio hfin' hint d hd hn
declarations.comment:
part (2), well-definedness: c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] is independent of the chosen nonzero
meromorphic section, by Stacks 0EPT; the principal divisor div(f) of Stacks 0ENP is not carried
here, so that the cycle div(f) belongs to the principal divisors of the ChowTarget parameter —
the input of Stacks 0EQ6 part (1) — is the hypothesis hprincipal, and Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2) and
(4) are the parameter's field cls_cycleFamilySum_eq_zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionWeilDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQE, part (1).** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, let `X` be integral with
`n = dim_δ(X)` and let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. The *Weil divisor associated to a
nonzero meromorphic section `s` of `ℒ`*, the `(n-1)`-cycle

  `div_ℒ(s) = ∑ ord_{Z,ℒ}(s) [Z] ∈ Z_{n-1}(X)`,

the sum over the prime divisors `Z` of `X`, `ord_{Z,ℒ}(s)` being the order of vanishing of
Stacks 0EPR (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionWeilDivisor_apply_toIntegralClosedSubspace`).
declarations.statement:
def sectionWeilDivisor {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L)
    (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    CycleGroup D sX (n - 1)
declarations.comment: part (1): div_ℒ(s) = ∑ ord_{Z,ℒ}(s) [Z] as an element of Z_{n-1}(X), for X/B good and integral with n = dim_δ(X), ℒ invertible and s a nonzero meromorphic section; ord_{Z,ℒ}(s) at the generators of Stacks 0EPR, local finiteness by Stacks 0EPS for the section s, the δ-dimension n-1 of a prime divisor by Stacks 0EPZ with the dimension function of Stacks 0EDN, and the properties of the henselian local rings by Stacks 0ENK, all proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.weilDivisorOfInvertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQE, part (2).** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, let `X` be integral with
`n = dim_δ(X)` and let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. The *Weil divisor associated to `ℒ`*,

  `c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] = class of div_ℒ(s) ∈ CH_{n-1}(X)`,

for the nonzero meromorphic section `s` of `ℒ` of Stacks 0EPQ
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.regularMeromorphicSection`); the class does not depend on the choice
of `s` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowClass_sectionWeilDivisor`).
declarations.comment: part (2): c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] = the class of div_ℒ(s) in CH_{n-1}(X) = Z_{n-1}(X)/∼_rat (Stacks 0EQ6), for a nonzero meromorphic section s of ℒ, which exists by Stacks 0EPQ; it is the class of div_ℒ(s) for every nonzero s by chowClass_sectionWeilDivisor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowClass_sectionWeilDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQE, part (2), well-definedness.** `c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X]` is the class of `div_ℒ(s)` in
`CH_{n-1}(X)` for *every* nonzero meromorphic section `s` of `ℒ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowClass_sectionWeilDivisor {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L)
    (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    chowClass.{v} D sX hX (n - 1) (sectionWeilDivisor D sX hX hint L hL hn s hs) =
      weilDivisorOfInvertibleSheaf.{v} D sX hX hint L hL hn
declarations.comment: part (2), well-definedness: the class of div_ℒ(s) in CH_{n-1}(X) is c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] for every nonzero meromorphic section s, by Stacks 0EPT, the principal divisor div(f) of the ratio being rationally equivalent to zero in the sense of Stacks 0EQ6

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.zeroSchemeCycleCoeff_mem_cyclesOfDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQF.** The right side of both identities of the source is a `k`-cycle: the
coefficient family of `[Z(s)]_k` lies in `Z_k(X)`.

The δ-dimension clause holds by construction, the coefficient of Stacks 0EE9 at an integral
closed subspace of δ-dimension other than `k` being zero. Local finiteness is the argument
`hfin`, a property of the input datum `(ℒ, s, γ)`, as it is for `div_ℒ(s)` on the other side.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroSchemeCycleCoeff_mem_cyclesOfDimension
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if zeroSchemeCycleCoeff D sX hX L s k γ Z = 0 then ∅
      else subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X Z.subspace) :
    zeroSchemeCycleCoeff D sX hX L s k γ ∈ cyclesOfDimension D sX k
declarations.comment:
[Z(s)]_k is a k-cycle, so that at k = n - 1 the right side of both identities is
an element of Z_{n-1}(X); the multiplicity of Stacks 0EE9 is read at the chosen geometric
representative γ, which by Stacks 0EE1 (geometricLength_eq_of_image_eq) does not change its
value, and local finiteness of the coefficient family is the argument hfin, a property of the
input datum (ℒ, s, γ), as it is for div_ℒ(s) in Stacks 0EQE part (1) and for divisorOfSection in
Stacks 0EPU part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.divisorCycleOfSection_eq_zeroSchemeCycle_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQF, the identity in `Z_{n-1}(X)`, reduced to its coefficients at the prime
divisors.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, let `X` be integral with `n = dim_δ(X)`, let
`ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, let `s ∈ Γ(X, ℒ)` and let `σ` be a nonzero meromorphic
section of `ℒ`. Then

`div_ℒ(σ) = [Z(s)]_{n-1}` in `Z_{n-1}(X)`

holds exactly when it holds coefficientwise at every prime divisor of `X`, that is when
`ord_{Z,ℒ}(σ)` is the multiplicity of `Z` in `Z(s)` for every prime divisor `Z ⊆ X`.

Both sides are coefficient families on the integral closed subspaces of `X`, and away from the
prime divisors both vanish: the coefficient of `div_ℒ(σ)` at an integral closed subspace whose
point set does not have codimension one is zero by Stacks 0EQE, part (1), and such a subspace
has δ-dimension other than `n - 1` by Stacks 0EPZ, so its coefficient in `[Z(s)]_{n-1}` is zero
too. That is the whole content of the reduction. The right-hand side — the coefficient identity
at a prime divisor — is proved, for the canonical meromorphic section of `s`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.invertibleDivisorCoefficients_globalSection_toIntegralClosedSubspace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem divisorCycleOfSection_eq_zeroSchemeCycle_iff (_hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX L)
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if zeroSchemeCycleCoeff D sX hX L s (n - 1) γ Z = 0 then ∅
      else subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X Z.subspace) :
    divisorCycleOfSection D sX hX hdec L σ ratio hDv hint dimF hdimF hn =
        zeroSchemeCycle D sX hX L s (n - 1) γ hfin ↔
      ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
        divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L σ ratio W =
          zeroSchemeCycleCoeff D sX hX L s (n - 1) γ
            (W.toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem)
declarations.comment:
first conclusion REDUCED to its coefficients: div_ℒ(s) = [Z(s)]_{n-1} in
Z_{n-1}(X) holds IF AND ONLY IF it holds at every prime divisor, where div_ℒ(s) is Stacks 0EQE
part (1) and [Z(s)]_{n-1} is Stacks 0EE9 at the chosen geometric representative γ; what is proved
here is that the two coefficient families agree away from the prime divisors, by Stacks 0EQE part
(1) and Stacks 0EPZ. The coefficient identity ord_{Z,ℒ}(s) = m_{Z,Z(s)} AT a prime divisor — the
right-hand side of this equivalence — is proved separately, in GlobalSectionDivisorCycle.lean,
for the canonical meromorphic section of s and with no chart carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq_cls_zeroSchemeCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQF, the identity in `CH_{n-1}(X)`, from the identity in `Z_{n-1}(X)`.** In the
situation above, if

`div_ℒ(σ) = [Z(s)]_{n-1}` in `Z_{n-1}(X)`,

which is the first conclusion of the source and the hypothesis `heq`, then

`c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] = [Z(s)]_{n-1}` in `CH_{n-1}(X)`.

This is the source's own derivation of its second conclusion from its first: `c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X]` is by
Stacks 0EQE, part (2), the class of `div_ℒ(σ)` for a nonzero meromorphic section `σ` of `ℒ`, a
class independent of `σ` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq`, so the second identity is the image
of the first under the class map of the Chow group.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq_cls_zeroSchemeCycle
    (_hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX L) {CH : Type w} [AddCommGroup CH]
    (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sX hX (n - 1) CH)
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if zeroSchemeCycleCoeff D sX hX L s (n - 1) γ Z = 0 then ∅
      else subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X Z.subspace)
    (heq : divisorCycleOfSection D sX hX hdec L σ ratio hDv hint dimF hdimF hn =
      zeroSchemeCycle D sX hX L s (n - 1) γ hfin) :
    firstChernClassCapFundamental D sX hX hdec L chow σ ratio hDv hint dimF hdimF hn =
      chow.cls (zeroSchemeCycle D sX hX L s (n - 1) γ hfin)
declarations.comment:
second conclusion: c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] = [Z(s)]_{n-1} in CH_{n-1}(X), where c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] is
Stacks 0EQE part (2) — the class of div_ℒ(s) in the ChowTarget parameter standing in for Stacks
0EQ6; this is the source's own derivation of its second conclusion FROM its first, so the
argument heq is the FIRST conclusion of this tag (reduced to the prime divisors by
divisorCycleOfSection_eq_zeroSchemeCycle_iff) and not this theorem's own conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionWeilDivisor_eq_zeroSchemeCycle_and_weilDivisorOfInvertibleSheaf_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQF.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, let `X` be integral with
`n = dim_δ(X)`, let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and let `s ∈ Γ(X, ℒ)` be a nonzero global
section. Then

`div_ℒ(s) = [Z(s)]_{n-1}` in `Z_{n-1}(X)`  and  `c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] = [Z(s)]_{n-1}` in `CH_{n-1}(X)`.

`div_ℒ(s)` is the Weil divisor of Stacks 0EQE, part (1), of the meromorphic section of `ℒ` that
`s` is; `c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X]` is Stacks 0EQE, part (2), in the Chow group `CH_{n-1}(X)` of Stacks 0EQ6;
and `[Z(s)]_{n-1}` is the cycle of Stacks 0EE9 of the zero scheme of Stacks 0845, its
multiplicities read at the canonical geometric representative of each point — by Stacks 0EE1
any representatives lying over the points give the same cycle, and
`sectionWeilDivisor_eq_zeroSchemeCycle_and_weilDivisorOfInvertibleSheaf_eq_of_liesOver` states
the identities for all of them. That `[Z(s)]_{n-1}` is an `(n-1)`-cycle is part of the
conclusion: its coefficients are those of `div_ℒ(s)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionWeilDivisor_eq_zeroSchemeCycle_and_weilDivisorOfInvertibleSheaf_eq
    {s : L.sections} (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    sectionWeilDivisor D sX hX hint L hL hn
        (globalSectionMeromorphic D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 L s)
        (globalSectionMeromorphic_ne_zero_of_isInvertibleSheaf D sX hX L hL hs) =
      zeroSchemeCycle D sX hX L s (n - 1)
        (canonicalGeometricPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem
          (vanishingLocus D sX hX L s).1.toFunctor)
        (locallyFinite_zeroSchemeCycleCoeff_globalSection D sX hX hint L hL hn hs _
          (canonicalGeometricPoint_liesOver D _)) ∧
    weilDivisorOfInvertibleSheaf.{v} D sX hX hint L hL hn =
      chowClass.{v} D sX hX (n - 1) (zeroSchemeCycle D sX hX L s (n - 1)
        (canonicalGeometricPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem
          (vanishingLocus D sX hX L s).1.toFunctor)
        (locallyFinite_zeroSchemeCycleCoeff_globalSection D sX hX hint L hL hn hs _
          (canonicalGeometricPoint_liesOver D _)))
declarations.comment: both identities: div_ℒ(s) = [Z(s)]_{n-1} in Z_{n-1}(X) and c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] = [Z(s)]_{n-1} in CH_{n-1}(X), for X/B good and integral with n = dim_δ(X), ℒ invertible and s a nonzero global section; div_ℒ(s) and c₁(ℒ) ∩ [X] are Stacks 0EQE parts (1) and (2) with every ingredient constructed, CH_{n-1}(X) is Stacks 0EQ6, [Z(s)]_{n-1} is Stacks 0EE9 of the zero scheme of Stacks 0845 at the canonical geometric representatives; nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torsorOfInvertible_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQG, clause (3): formation of `(q : T ⟶ X, α)` commutes with base change.**  For a
morphism `g : Y ⟶ X` of good algebraic spaces, let `q_Y : T_Y ⟶ Y` and
`α_Y : q_Y^*(g^*ℒ) ≅ 𝒪_{T_Y}` be the multiplicative torsor of the invertible `𝒪_Y`-module
`g^*ℒ`.  There is a morphism `g' : T_Y ⟶ T` with `g' ≫ q = q_Y ≫ g` such that the square is
cartesian and `α` pulls back along `g'` to `α_Y`: the trivialization `g'^*α` of
`(g' ≫ q)^*ℒ = (q_Y ≫ g)^*ℒ` is `α_Y` composed with the canonical identification
`(q_Y ≫ g)^*ℒ ≅ q_Y^*(g^*ℒ)` of Stacks 03LU.
declarations.statement:
theorem torsorOfInvertible_baseChange :
    ∃ (g' : torsorOfInvertibleSpace D pY hpY ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem g).obj L)
        (isInvertible_modulePullback_obj D.site D.base D.base_mem g L hL) ⟶
        torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL)
      (w : g' ≫ torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL =
        torsorOfInvertibleProjection D pY hpY ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem g).obj L)
        (isInvertible_modulePullback_obj D.site D.base D.base_mem g L hL) ≫ g),
      IsPullback g' (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D pY hpY
        ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem g).obj L)
        (isInvertible_modulePullback_obj D.site D.base D.base_mem g L hL))
          (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL) g ∧
        𝔱[p, hp, L, hL, g', w] =
          (modulePullbackTriangle D.site D.base D.base_mem
            (rfl : torsorOfInvertibleProjection D pY hpY
              ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem g).obj L)
        (isInvertible_modulePullback_obj D.site D.base D.base_mem g L hL) ≫ g =
              torsorOfInvertibleProjection D pY hpY
                ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem g).obj L)
        (isInvertible_modulePullback_obj D.site D.base D.base_mem g L hL) ≫ g)).hom.app L ≫
            (torsorOfInvertibleTrivialization D pY hpY
              ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem g).obj L)
        (isInvertible_modulePullback_obj D.site D.base D.base_mem g L hL)).hom
declarations.comment:
clause (3): in Situation 0EDT with X/B good and L an invertible O_X-module, for
every morphism g : Y ⟶ X of good algebraic spaces the multiplicative torsor (q_Y : T_Y ⟶ Y,
alpha_Y) of g^*L, with T_Y = Spec_Y(⨁_n (g^*L)^{⊗n}), is the base change of (q : T ⟶ X, alpha):
there is g' : T_Y ⟶ T over g making the square cartesian and pulling alpha back to alpha_Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torsorOfInvertible_clause_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQG, clause (1).** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good and let `ℒ` be an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module.  The morphism `q : T = \underline{Spec}_X(⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} ℒ^{⊗ n}) ⟶ X` is surjective,
smooth, affine, and of relative dimension `1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem torsorOfInvertible_clause_one :
    IsSurjective D.site D.base D.base_mem (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ∧
      IsSmooth D.site D.base D.base_mem (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ∧
      IsAffineHom D.site D.base D.base_mem (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ∧
      HasRelativeDimension 1 D.site D.base D.base_mem
        (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom
declarations.comment: clause (1): q is surjective, smooth, affine, of relative dimension 1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torsorOfInvertible_clause_six
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQG, clause (6).** If `Z ⊆ X` is a closed subspace of `δ`-dimension `≤ k`, then
`q^{-1}(Z)` is a closed subspace of `T` of `δ`-dimension `≤ k + 1`, and
`q^*[Z]_k = [q^{-1}(Z)]_{k+1}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem torsorOfInvertible_clause_six (k : ℤ) (Z : Subfunctor X)
    (hZ : IsClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem Z)
    (hZk : deltaDimensionSubspace D p hp Z hZ ≤ (k : EInt)) :
    ∃ (hZ' : IsClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem
        (Z.preimage (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom))
      (hdim : deltaDimensionSubspace D _ (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)
        (Z.preimage (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom) hZ' ≤ ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt)),
      torsorOfInvertibleFlatPullback D p hp L hL k (closedSubspaceCycle D p hp Z hZ k hZk) =
        closedSubspaceCycle D _ (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)
          (Z.preimage (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom) hZ' (k + 1) hdim
declarations.comment:
clause (6): q^{-1}(Z) is a closed subspace of T of delta-dimension at most k + 1
and q^*[Z]_k = [q^{-1}(Z)]_{k+1}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torsorOfInvertible_clause_seven
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQG, clause (7).**  In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, let `ℒ` be an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module and `q : T = \underline{Spec}(⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} ℒ^{⊗ n}) ⟶ X`.  If `ξ' ∈ |T|` is the
generic point of the fibre of `|T| → |X|` over `ξ = q(ξ')` — every point of that fibre is a
specialization of `ξ'` — then the ring map `φ : 𝒪^h_{X, ξ} ⟶ 𝒪^h_{T, ξ'}` induced by `q` is flat,
`𝔪^h_{ξ'} = 𝔪^h_ξ 𝒪^h_{T, ξ'}`, and the residue field extension is purely transcendental of
transcendence degree `1`: it is generated by a single element transcendental over `κ(ξ)`.

The map `φ` is the one induced by `q`: it is the local homomorphism agreeing on the image of
`𝒪_{V, v}` with the stalk map of a commuting square of elementary étale neighborhoods
`U ⟶ V` over `q`, which determines it by the universal property of the henselization.
declarations.statement:
theorem torsorOfInvertible_clause_seven
    (ξ' : points D.site D.base D.base_mem (torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL).obj)
    (hξ' : ∀ t, pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem _
      (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom t =
      pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem _ (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ξ' →
        ξ' ⤳ t) :
    letI := henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem X hp.1
      (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem _ (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ξ')
      (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood p hp)
    letI := henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem
      (torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL).obj (torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL).property ξ'
      (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood _ (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL))
    ∃ (V : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood D.site D.base D.base_mem X hp.1
        (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem _ (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ξ'))
      (U : ElementaryEtaleNeighborhood D.site D.base D.base_mem
        (torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL).obj (torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL).property ξ')
      (j : U.scheme ⟶ V.scheme) (hj : j.left.1 U.point = V.point)
      (φ : (henselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem X hp.1
          (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem _ (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ξ')
          (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood p hp) : Type (u + 1)) →+*
        (henselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem (torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL).obj
          (torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL).property ξ'
          (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood _ (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)) : Type (u + 1))),
      yoneda.map j ≫ V.toSpace = U.toSpace ≫ (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ∧
        (∀ a, φ (stalkToHenselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem X hp.1 _
            (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood p hp) V a) =
          stalkToHenselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem _ _ ξ'
            (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood _ (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)) U
            (((V.scheme.left.1.presheaf.stalkCongr (.of_eq hj.symm)).hom ≫
              j.left.1.stalkMap U.point).hom a)) ∧
        ∃ _ : IsLocalHom φ,
          φ.Flat ∧
          Ideal.map φ (maximalIdeal _) = maximalIdeal _ ∧
          letI := (ResidueField.map φ).toAlgebra
          ∃ t : ResidueField (henselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem
              (torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL).obj
                (torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL).property
