              ξ' (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood _ (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)) :
                Type (u + 1)),
            Transcendental (ResidueField (henselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem X hp.1
              (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem _
                (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ξ')
              (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood p hp) : Type (u + 1))) t ∧
            IntermediateField.adjoin (ResidueField
              (henselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem X hp.1
              (pointsMap D.site D.base D.base_mem _
                (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ξ')
              (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood p hp) : Type (u + 1))) {t} = ⊤
declarations.comment:
clause (7): if ξ' ∈ |T| is the generic point of the fibre of |T| → |X| over ξ,
then the ring map O^h_{X,ξ} → O^h_{T,ξ'} induced by q (the local homomorphism compatible with the
stalk map of a commuting square of elementary etale neighbourhoods over q) is flat, the maximal
ideal of O^h_{T,ξ'} is m^h_ξ O^h_{T,ξ'}, and the residue field extension is purely transcendental
of transcendence degree 1 (generated by one element transcendental over the residue field of
O^h_{X,ξ})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torsorOfInvertible_clause_four
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0EQG, clause (4).** The flat pullback `q^* : Z_k(X) → Z_{k+1}(T)` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem torsorOfInvertible_clause_four (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Injective (torsorOfInvertibleFlatPullback D p hp L hL k)
declarations.comment: clause (4): q^* : Z_k(X) → Z_{k+1}(T) is injective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torsorOfInvertible_clause_five
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQG, clause (5).** If `Z ⊆ X` is an integral closed subspace, then
`q^{-1}(Z) ⊆ T` is an integral closed subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem torsorOfInvertible_clause_five (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) :
    IsClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem
        (Z.subspace.preimage (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom) ∧
      IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem
        (Z.subspace.preimage (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom).toFunctor
declarations.comment:
clause (5): q^{-1}(Z) is an integral closed subspace of T for Z an integral closed
subspace of X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherent_laurentAlgebraSheaf
declarations.doc:
The Laurent algebra sheaf `⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} ℒ^{⊗ n}` of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ` is
quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_laurentAlgebraSheaf :
    AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent (laurentAlgebraSheaf D p hp L hL)
declarations.comment:
the quasi-coherence of ⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} L^{⊗n} that clause (1) presupposes in forming
T = Spec_X(⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} L^{⊗n}): in Situation 0EDT with X/B good, the Laurent algebra of an
invertible O_X-module is a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra, with no hypothesis on L beyond
invertibility -- triviality of L on an etale covering is DISCHARGED here from local ringedness of
the small etale site, not assumed.  Nothing about the morphism q is covered by this
declaration

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_multiplicativeTorsorProjection
declarations.doc:
The projection `q : T = \underline{Spec}_X(⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} ℒ^{⊗ n}) ⟶ X` of the multiplicative
torsor of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module is an affine morphism of algebraic spaces.

**This statement is vacuous over any nondegenerate site**, since the parameter `E` it takes is
empty there; see the implementation notes above.  The assertion under the hypotheses of
Situation 0EDT alone is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_multiplicativeTorsorSpectrumProjection`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_multiplicativeTorsorProjection :
    IsAffineHom D.site D.base D.base_mem (multiplicativeTorsorProjection D p hp L hL E
      (isQuasicoherent_laurentAlgebraSheaf D p hp L hL)).hom
declarations.comment:
clause (1), the affineness part -- BUT VACUOUS AS STATED, and registered here only
because the base file carries this line.  The statement takes a parameter
E : AffineAlgebraAntiEquivalence, this development's rendering of Stacks 081V with the tag's
unrestricted target, and that type is EMPTY over any site one of whose algebraic spaces has an
affine etale chart with a nonzero ring of functions
(not_nonempty_affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_of_hasNonzeroAffineChart).  Over such a site this
theorem asserts nothing: quasi-coherence of the Laurent algebra, which IS discharged by
isQuasicoherent_laurentAlgebraSheaf, is discharged into a statement with no content.  THE
REGISTRATION THAT CARRIES THIS CLAUSE is
isAffineHom_multiplicativeTorsorSpectrumProjection (MultiplicativeTorsorSpectrum), which takes no
parameter at all; isAffineHom_boundedMultiplicativeTorsorProjection gives it inside the site of X
under the size condition of the corrected 081V, which E implies.  Read this line as covering
nothing

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_multiplicativeTorsorBaseChange
declarations.doc:
The base change of `q : T ⟶ X` along `g : Y ⟶ X` is cartesian, with corner
`\underline{Spec}_Y(g^*(⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} ℒ^{⊗ n}))`: forming the multiplicative torsor commutes with
arbitrary base change.

**This statement is vacuous over any nondegenerate site**, since the parameters `E` and `C` it
takes are empty there; see the implementation notes above.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_multiplicativeTorsorBaseChange :
    IsPullback (multiplicativeTorsorBaseChangeProjection D p hp L hL E C g)
      (multiplicativeTorsorBaseChange D p hp L hL E C g).obj.hom
      (multiplicativeTorsorProjection D p hp L hL E
        (isQuasicoherent_laurentAlgebraSheaf D p hp L hL)) g
declarations.comment:
clause (3) for q: the base change of q along an arbitrary g : Y ⟶ X is cartesian
and Y ×_X T is the relative spectrum over Y of g^*(⨁_n L^{⊗n}), the latter being the corner of
the cartesian square as stated.
VACUOUS AS STATED: it takes the parameters E : AffineAlgebraAntiEquivalence and C its
base-change clause, and E is EMPTY over any site one of whose algebraic spaces has an affine
etale chart with a nonzero ring of functions
(not_nonempty_affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_of_hasNonzeroAffineChart).  Over such a site this
theorem asserts nothing.  In particular, although Stacks 08AI at q -- the input the construction
of alpha : q^*L ≅ O_T consumes -- is genuinely discharged from X/B good and L invertible by
affineDirectImageEquivalence_multiplicativeTorsorProjection, that discharge is itself stated
under E and so is equally vacuous; it should not be read as evidence that this clause is in
better shape than it is.  Two further pieces of the source's clause (3) lie outside this
statement in any case: alpha itself, whose construction needs in addition the degree-shift
isomorphism of the Laurent algebra over itself, ⨁_n L^{⊗(n+1)} ≅ ⨁_n L^{⊗n}, which is clause
(2)'s own content and which this tree does not have (only the per-degree powSuccIso); and the
identification of g^*(⨁_n L^{⊗n}) with ⨁_n (g^*L)^{⊗n}.  No parameter-free counterpart of this
base-change square has been formed: MultiplicativeTorsorSpectrum supplies T, q and the
affineness of q without parameters, not the base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_multiplicativeTorsorSpectrumProjection
declarations.doc:
The projection `q : T ⟶ X` of the multiplicative torsor of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module is
an affine morphism of algebraic spaces, under the hypotheses of Situation 0EDT and no others:
`X/B` good and `ℒ` invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_multiplicativeTorsorSpectrumProjection :
    IsAffineHom
      (relativeSpectrumSite
        (laurentQuasicoherentAlgebra D p hp L hL (isQuasicoherent_laurentAlgebraSheaf D p hp L hL)))
      D.base
      (contains_relativeSpectrumSite
        (laurentQuasicoherentAlgebra D p hp L hL
          (isQuasicoherent_laurentAlgebraSheaf D p hp L hL)))
      (multiplicativeTorsorSpectrumProjection D p hp L hL).hom
declarations.comment:
clause (1), the affineness part only, in Situation 0EDT with X/B good: for an
invertible O_X-module L the projection q of T = Spec_X(⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} L^{⊗n}) is affine.  Carries NO
parameter and no size condition: quasi-coherence of the Laurent algebra is discharged by
isQuasicoherent_laurentAlgebraSheaf, itself resting on triviality of L on an etale covering,
discharged by isLocallyTrivial_of_isInvertibleSheaf from local ringedness of the small etale
site, and T is formed by relativeSpectrum, the unconditional form of Stacks 081W.  This replaces
isAffineHom_multiplicativeTorsorProjection, which asserts the same thing under a parameter
E : AffineAlgebraAntiEquivalence that is EMPTY over any site one of whose algebraic spaces has an
affine etale chart with a nonzero ring of functions
(not_nonempty_affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence_of_hasNonzeroAffineChart) and so asserts nothing
there.  q lives over relativeSpectrumSite, the Stacks 03FO enlargement of the site of X;
isAffineHom_boundedMultiplicativeTorsorProjection is the same assertion inside the site of X
itself, under the size condition of the corrected 081V, which E implies.
NOT COVERED by this or any other declaration: the rest of clause (1) -- q surjective, smooth and
of relative dimension 1 -- and clauses (2), (4), (5), (6), (7).  The source derives the three
remaining properties of clause (1) from T x_X U ≅ G_m x U for an etale chart U trivialising L,
and that identification does not exist in this tree: isPullback_affineChartSpec identifies the
relative spectrum over an affine chart with Spec of the algebra's sections there, nothing
identifies the Laurent algebra's sections at a trivialising chart V with O(V)[t,t^{-1}] (the
sheafification step is unaccounted for), and no scheme-level smoothness, surjectivity or
relative-dimension statement about multiplicativeGroupBaseChange exists

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.torsorOfInvertible_clause_two
declarations.doc: There is an isomorphism `α : q^*ℒ ≅ 𝒪_T`.

theorem torsorOfInvertible_clause_two :

      (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL)).obj L ≅ SheafOfModules.unit _)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_ord_of_extendedMaximalIdeal_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQH, coefficientwise.** *The divisor of a meromorphic section pulls back to the
divisor of the associated rational function on the multiplicative torsor.* Let `q : T ⟶ Y` be
the morphism of Stacks 0EQG for an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module `ℒ`, so that `q^*ℒ ≅ 𝒪_T` and a
nonzero meromorphic section `s` of `ℒ` becomes a nonzero meromorphic function `q^*(s)` on `T`.
Let `Z' ⊆ Y` be a prime divisor and `Z = q^{-1}(Z')`, and let `φ : 𝒪^h_{Y,ξ'} ⟶ 𝒪^h_{T,ξ}` be
the induced flat local homomorphism. Because `𝔪^h_{Y,ξ'} 𝒪^h_{T,ξ} = 𝔪^h_{T,ξ}`,

  `ord_Z(q^*(s)) = ord_{Z',ℒ}(s)`,

which is `q^* div_ℒ(s) = div_T(q^*(s))` coefficientwise.

The hypothesis `hmax` is the identity of ideals that Stacks 0EQG supplies, and it is what makes
the multiplicity one: the quotient is then the residue field of `𝒪^h_{T,ξ}`, whose length is
one, so `Ring.ord_map_of_flatHom` gives equality of the two orders rather than a multiple.
declarations.statement:
theorem PrimeDivisor.ord_eq_ord_of_extendedMaximalIdeal_eq
    (hloc : IsLocalHom φ) (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (hmax : Ideal.map φ
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY)) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ↥(ZX.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdecX))
    (L : Modules.{u, max u z} B S hS Y hY)
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} B S hS Y hY L)
    (ratioY : LocalRatio.{u, z} B S hS hY hdecY ZY L)
    (embT : rationalFunctions B S hS hX →+* ZX.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdecX)
    (qs : rationalFunctions B S hS hX)
    (a b : nonZeroDivisors ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY))
    (hs : (ratioY s : ZY.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hY hdecY) =
      IsLocalization.mk' (ZY.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hY hdecY)
        (a : ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY)) b)
    (hqs : embT qs = IsLocalization.mk' (ZX.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdecX)
      (φ (a : ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY)))
      (⟨φ (b : ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY)),
        Ring.map_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_flatHom hflat b.2⟩ :
        nonZeroDivisors ↥(ZX.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdecX)))
    (hqsu : IsUnit (embT qs)) :
    ZX.ord B S hS hX hdecX (embT qs) hqsu =
      orderOfVanishingSection.{u, z} B S hS hY hdecY ZY L s ratioY
declarations.comment:
coefficientwise at a prime divisor Z = q^{-1}(Z') of T: ord_Z(q^*(s)) =
ord_{Z',L}(s), which is the source's q^* div_L(s) = div_T(q^*(s)) read at the coefficient of Z.
No component bookkeeping arises: the source assumes the base integral, so the multiplicity of a
component is one, and the multiplicity of Z over Z' is one as well by hmax.
It is stated coefficientwise because the flat pullback of cycles is Stacks 0EP8, which this
repository does not have, and because the principal divisor div(q^*(s)) of Stacks 0ENP is not
available either; for the same reason Stacks 0EPT and 0EPV are already carried coefficientwise
here. The source's other case, a prime divisor of T dominating Y, where both coefficients
vanish, is bookkeeping internal to the flat pullback and does not arise in a statement indexed
by a prime divisor lying over a prime divisor. PROVED, not assumed: that the two orders of
vanishing are equal, from Stacks 02M1 (length_baseChange_eq_length_mul_length_quotient) through
Ring.ord_map_of_flatHom, the multiplicity being one because the extended maximal ideal is the
maximal ideal and the residue field has length one. RESTRICTED: carried as explicit named
hypotheses are (i) the flat local homomorphism φ : O^h_{Y,ξ'} → O^h_{T,ξ} with hloc and hflat,
and (ii) the identity hmax that the maximal ideal of O^h_{Y,ξ'} extends to the maximal ideal of
O^h_{T,ξ} — these are the two properties of q that Lemma 0EQG supplies and that the source uses
here, the morphism q itself being available in this repository only as
multiplicativeTorsorProjection, whose surjectivity, smoothness and relative dimension are not
proved there; (iii) the rational function qs standing for q^*(s), with the embedding embT of
Stacks 0ENK, and hqs, that its ratio at ξ is the image under φ of the ratio of s at ξ' — the
trivialization alpha : q^*L ≅ O_T is not constructed in this repository, as the clause of
Stacks 0EQG on multiplicativeTorsorBaseChange records, so the identification of q^*(s) as a
function is this hypothesis, which is the source's own step of writing s/s_{ξ'} = a/b and
pulling the fraction back; and (iv) the ratio of Stacks 0EPR at the generic point of Z' as the
parameter ratioY

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatPullbackMap_sectionWeilDivisor_torsorOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good and integral with `n = dim_δ(X)`, let
`ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, let `s` be a nonzero meromorphic section of `ℒ`, and let
`q : T ⟶ X` be the morphism of Stacks 0EQG. Then

  `q^* div_ℒ(s) = div_T(q^*(s))`

in `Z_n(T)`: the left-hand side is the flat pullback along `q` (flat of relative dimension one) of
the Weil divisor of `s`; on the right `q^*(s)` is the pullback of `s`, and the identity holds both
with `div_{q^*ℒ}(q^*s)` and, for every isomorphism `α : q^*ℒ ≅ 𝒪_T`, with the divisor
`div_{𝒪_T}(α(q^*s))` of the meromorphic function `α(q^*s)` on `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullbackMap_sectionWeilDivisor_torsorOfInvertible {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D p hp Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hp.1 L) (hs : s ≠ 0) :
    flatPullbackMap D ((torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ≫ p)
        (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL) p hp (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom
        rfl 1 (isFlat_torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL)
        (hasRelativeDimension_torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL) (n - 1) (n + (1 : ℕ) - 1)
        (by push_cast; ring) (sectionWeilDivisor D p hp hint L hL hn s hs) =
      sectionWeilDivisor D ((torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ≫ p)
        (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)
        (isIntegralSpace_torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL hint)
        ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL)).obj L)
        (isInvertibleSheaf_modulePullback D p hp _ (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)
          (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL) hL)
        (deltaDimensionClosed_torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp hint L hL hn)
        (pullbackMeromorphicSection D.site D.base D.base_mem
          (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL) L
          (pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_flat D.site D.base D.base_mem _
            (isFlat_torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL)) s)
        (pullbackMeromorphicSection_ne_zero_of_isFlat D p hp hint _
          (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)
          (isIntegralSpace_torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL hint) _
          (isFlat_torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL) hL s hs) ∧
    ∀ α : (modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem
          (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL)).obj L ≅
        SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite D.site
          D.base D.base_mem (torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL).obj
          (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL).1).O),
      flatPullbackMap D ((torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ≫ p)
          (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL) p hp
          (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom
          rfl 1 (isFlat_torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL)
          (hasRelativeDimension_torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL) (n - 1) (n + (1 : ℕ) - 1)
          (by push_cast; ring) (sectionWeilDivisor D p hp hint L hL hn s hs) =
        sectionWeilDivisor D ((torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL).hom ≫ p)
          (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)
          (isIntegralSpace_torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL hint) _
          (isInvertibleSheaf_unit D _ (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL))
          (deltaDimensionClosed_torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp hint L hL hn)
          (SheafOfModules.sectionsMap
            (meromorphicSectionSheafMap D.site D.base D.base_mem _
              (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL).1 α.hom)
            (pullbackMeromorphicSection D.site D.base D.base_mem
              (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL) L
              (pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_flat D.site D.base D.base_mem _
                (isFlat_torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL)) s))
          (sectionsMap_meromorphicSectionSheafMap_inv_ne_zero D _
            (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)
            (isIntegralSpace_torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL hint)
            (isInvertibleSheaf_unit D _ (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL))
            (isInvertibleSheaf_modulePullback D p hp _ (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)
              (torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL) hL) α.symm _
            (pullbackMeromorphicSection_ne_zero_of_isFlat D p hp hint _
              (isGood_torsorOfInvertible D p hp L hL)
              (isIntegralSpace_torsorOfInvertibleSpace D p hp L hL hint) _
              (isFlat_torsorOfInvertibleProjection D p hp L hL) hL s hs))
declarations.comment:
q^* div_L(s) = div_T(q^*(s)) as cycles on T, for X/B good and integral, L
invertible, s a nonzero meromorphic section and q : T -> X the morphism of 0EQG
(torsorOfInvertibleProjection: flat of relative dimension 1, T/B good, T integral, all proved).
Stated with div_{q^*L}(q^*s) and, for EVERY isomorphism alpha : q^*L ≅ O_T, with the divisor
div_{O_T}(alpha(q^*s)) of the nonzero meromorphic function alpha(q^*s); q^* on cycles is the flat
pullback of 0EP8, div is 0EQE, q^*s is the pullback of 0ENC. Proved from 0EQQ for q (T integral,
so the component sum collapses) and the invariance of div under an isomorphism of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap
declarations.doc:
*Intersection with the first Chern class of an invertible sheaf*: the cap product
`c₁(𝒩) ∩ - : Z_{k+1}(X) → CH_k(X)` attached to an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `𝒩` on a good
algebraic space `X/B`. It sends `α = ∑ n_W [W]` to the class of `∑_W n_W i_*(c₁(𝒩|_W) ∩ [W])`,
where `i : W → X` is the inclusion and the component cycle `c₁(𝒩|_W) ∩ [W]` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernRule`, the Weil divisor `div_{𝒩|_W}(t_W)` of
Stacks 0EQE, part (1), at the canonical ratios of Stacks 0EPR for the regular meromorphic section
of `𝒩|_W` given by Stacks 0EPQ. The target is the Chow group `CH_k(X) = Z_k(X)/∼_rat` of
Stacks 0EQ6, part (4); the pushforward `i_*` is applied to the cycle and the class is taken in
`CH_k(X)` afterwards.
declarations.statement: def canonicalFirstChernCap (k : ℤ) : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1) →+ chowGroup.{v} D sX hX k
declarations.comment:
the cap product c_1(N) ∩ - : Z_{k+1}(X) → CH_k(X) with the first Chern class of
an invertible O_X-module N on a good algebraic space X/B, cases (1) and (2): the component cycle
c_1(N|_W) ∩ [W] is the Weil divisor div_{N|_W}(t_W) of Stacks 0EQE at the canonical ratios of
Stacks 0EPR for a regular meromorphic section given by Stacks 0EPQ (canonicalFirstChernRule),
the target is the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6 part (4), and the pushforward i_* and the
fundamental cycle [W] are the genuine ones; nothing is a parameter. Case (1) is
canonicalFirstChernCap_integralCycle and case (2) is the coefficientwise additive extension
firstChernCapCycleMap. The source pushes the class of div_{N|_W}(t_W) forward, this pushes the
cycle forward and takes the class afterwards

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap_integralCycle
declarations.doc:
On the fundamental cycle `[W]` of an integral closed subspace `i : W → X` of δ-dimension
`k + 1` the cap product `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap` is the class of
`i_*(c₁(𝒩|_W) ∩ [W])`, the inner cycle being the Weil divisor `div_{𝒩|_W}(t_W)` of Stacks 0EQE at
the canonical choices.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalFirstChernCap_integralCycle (k : ℤ)
    {W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X}
    (hW : deltaDimension D sX W = k + 1) :
    canonicalFirstChernCap.{u, v} D sX hX N hN k (integralCycle D sX (k + 1) W hW) =
      chowClass.{v} D sX hX k (integralClosedSubspacePushforward D sX hX W k
        (canonicalFirstChernRule D sX hX N hN k W hW))
declarations.comment:
case (1): the value of the cap product on the fundamental cycle [W] of an
integral closed subspace W of δ-dimension k+1 is the class of i_*(c_1(N|_W) ∩ [W]), with the
component cycle c_1(N|_W) ∩ [W] the Weil divisor div_{N|_W}(t_W) of Stacks 0EQE at the
canonical ratios and the class taken in the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6; i_* is applied to the
cycle and the class taken afterwards, the source applying it to the class

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQJ.** *Intersection with the first Chern class of an invertible sheaf*: the cap
product `c₁(ℒ) ∩ - : Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ CH_k(X)` attached to an invertible sheaf `ℒ` on a good
algebraic space `X/B`.

On the cycle `[W]` of an integral closed subspace `W ⊆ X` of δ-dimension `k + 1` it is the
class of `i_*(c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩ [W])`, which is case (1) of the source; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCap_integralCycle`.  Case (2), the extension of that
rule by linearity over an arbitrary `(k+1)`-cycle, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernCapCycleMap`, which is proved to land in `Z_k(X)` and to be
additive.

The component cycle `c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩ [W]` on `W` and the Chow group `CH_k(X)` are explicit
parameters, standing in for Stacks 0EQE and Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2)–(4), neither of which is
available for algebraic spaces in this repository; see the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.FirstChernClassCap`.  The pushforward `i_*` and the
fundamental cycle `[W]` are not parameters.
declarations.statement:
def firstChernClassCap (_hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX L)
    (chern : FirstChernComponentCycleRule D sX k)
    {CH : Type w} [AddCommGroup CH] (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sX hX k CH) :
    CycleGroup D sX (k + 1) →+ CH
declarations.comment:
the cap product c_1(L) ∩ - : Z_{k+1}(X) → CH_k(X) with the first Chern class of
an invertible sheaf L on a good algebraic space X/B, cases (1) and (2); the component cycle
c_1(L|_W) ∩ [W] on an integral closed subspace W of δ-dimension k+1 and the Chow group CH_k(X)
are explicit parameters, standing in for Stacks 0EQE and Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2)-(4), neither of
which exists for algebraic spaces here; the pushforward i_* and the fundamental cycle [W] are
not parameters

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCap_integralCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQJ, case (1).** On the cycle `[W]` of an integral closed subspace `W ⊆ X` of
δ-dimension `k + 1` the cap product is the class of `i_*(c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩ [W])`, for the closed
immersion `i : W → X`.

The source applies the proper pushforward `i_* : CH_k(W) ⟶ CH_k(X)` to the *class* of
`c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩ [W]`; the form below applies the pushforward of cycles and takes the class
afterwards, which is the same statement once proper pushforward is known to respect rational
equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCap_integralCycle (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX L)
    (chern : FirstChernComponentCycleRule D sX k)
    {CH : Type w} [AddCommGroup CH] (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sX hX k CH)
    {W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X}
    (hW : deltaDimension D sX W = k + 1) :
    firstChernClassCap D sX hX L k hL chern chow (integralCycle D sX (k + 1) W hW) =
      chow.cls (integralClosedSubspacePushforward D sX hX W k (chern W hW))
declarations.comment:
case (1): the value of the cap product on the fundamental cycle [W] of an
integral closed subspace W of δ-dimension k+1 is the class of i_*(c_1(L|_W) ∩ [W]), with the
component cycle c_1(L|_W) ∩ [W] and the Chow group CH_k(X) as explicit parameters standing in
for Stacks 0EQE and Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2)-(4); the pushforward i_* is applied to the cycle and
the class taken afterwards, the source applying it to the class

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap_picardTensorModule
declarations.doc:
*Additivity of the first Chern class cap product.* For
invertible `𝒪_X`-modules `ℒ` and `𝒩` on a good algebraic space `X/B` and every `α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)`,

  `c₁(ℒ) ∩ α + c₁(𝒩) ∩ α = c₁(ℒ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒩) ∩ α`   in   `CH_k(X)`.

The cap product is the one of Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical choices,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap`, the tensor product is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.picardTensorModule`, and `CH_k(X)` is the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalFirstChernCap_picardTensorModule
    (L N : Modules.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1)
    (hL : IsInvertibleModule (⟨X, hX.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces D.site D.base D.base_mem) L)
    (hN : IsInvertibleModule (⟨X, hX.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces D.site D.base D.base_mem) N)
    (k : ℤ) (α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1)) :
    canonicalFirstChernCap.{u, u + 1} D sX hX L hL k α +
        canonicalFirstChernCap.{u, u + 1} D sX hX N hN k α =
      canonicalFirstChernCap.{u, u + 1} D sX hX
        (picardTensorModule D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 L N)
        (isInvertibleModule_picardTensorModule D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 L N hL hN) k α
declarations.comment: first assertion: c_1(L) ∩ α + c_1(N) ∩ α = c_1(L ⊗ N) ∩ α in CH_k(X), for the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical choices (canonicalFirstChernCap), the tensor product picardTensorModule and the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6. DISCHARGED: the component cycle c_1(L|_W) ∩ [W] is the constructed canonicalFirstChernRule, not a parameter, and the tensor product and the product of meromorphic sections are constructed too, so nothing is carried. Proved from Stacks 0EPV at the canonical choices, Stacks 03EL for the restriction of a tensor product to W, Stacks 0EPT, and Stacks 0EQ6 parts (1), (2) and (4). CORRECTED: the source writes α ∈ Z_{k-1}(X), which cannot give an identity in CH_k(X) for the operation Z_{k+1}(X) → CH_k(X) of Stacks 0EQJ; stated here for α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X), as the identical scheme-side lemma Stacks 02SP does

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap_tensorUnit_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
`c₁(𝒪_X) ∩ α = 0` in `CH_k(X)` for every `α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)`, the structure sheaf being the
tensor unit of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Modules`, which is `𝒪_X` as a module over itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalFirstChernCap_tensorUnit_eq_zero (k : ℤ) (α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1)) :
    canonicalFirstChernCap.{u, u + 1} D sX hX
      (𝟙_ (Modules.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1))
      (isInvertibleModule_tensorUnit hX) k α = 0
declarations.comment: second assertion: c_1(O_X) ∩ α = 0 in CH_k(X), for the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical choices (canonicalFirstChernCap) and the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6; O_X is the tensor unit of the modules on the small étale site, which is the structure sheaf viewed as a module over itself on the nose (modulesTensorUnit_eq). DISCHARGED: the component cycle is the constructed canonicalFirstChernRule, not a parameter, and no section of O_X|_W is chosen; proved from the first assertion at L = N = O_X, the invertibility of the tensor unit, the right unitor O_X ⊗ O_X ≅ O_X and the isomorphism invariance canonicalFirstChernCap_congr_iso. CORRECTED: stated for α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X), the source's Z_{k-1}(X) being a slip

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCap_tensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQK, first assertion.** *Additivity of the first Chern class cap product.* For
invertible sheaves `ℒ` and `𝒩` on a good algebraic space `X/B` and every `α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)`,

  `c₁(ℒ) ∩ α + c₁(𝒩) ∩ α = c₁(ℒ ⊗_{O_X} 𝒩) ∩ α`   in   `CH_k(X)`.

The cap product is the carried Stacks 0EQJ,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCap`, whose component cycle and Chow group are explicit
parameters; the three component rules here are its parameters for the three sheaves, and the
Chow group `CH` is shared.

Nothing about the conclusion is assumed.  Each of the three component rules is assumed only to
be presented by the Weil divisor of a meromorphic section of its own sheaf, which is the
definition Stacks 0EQE would supply, and the hypothesis `hst` is the source's own step that
`s_ξ ⊗ t_ξ` generates `(ℒ ⊗ 𝒩)_ξ`, so that `st/(s_ξ t_ξ) = (s/s_ξ)(t/t_ξ)`.  Additivity of the
component cycles is then Stacks 0EPV, and additivity of the cap product follows from it by the
extension of Stacks 0EQJ, case (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCap_tensor
    {L N M : Modules.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1}
    (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX L) (hN : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX N)
    (hM : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX M)
    {chernL chernN chernM : FirstChernComponentCycleRule D sX k}
    {CH : Type w} [AddCommGroup CH] (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sX hX k CH)
    (dL : ComponentDivisorData sX k setup chernL)
    (dN : ComponentDivisorData sX k setup chernN)
    (dM : ComponentDivisorData sX k setup chernM)
    (hst : ∀ (W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
      (P : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem W.subspace.toFunctor),
      (dM.ratio W P (dM.sect W) :
          P.genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem (setup.isSpace W)
            (setup.isDecent W)) =
        (dL.ratio W P (dL.sect W) :
            P.genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem (setup.isSpace W)
              (setup.isDecent W)) *
          (dN.ratio W P (dN.sect W) :
            P.genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem (setup.isSpace W)
              (setup.isDecent W)))
    (α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1)) :
    firstChernClassCap D sX hX L k hL chernL chow α +
        firstChernClassCap D sX hX N k hN chernN chow α =
      firstChernClassCap D sX hX M k hM chernM chow α
declarations.comment:
first assertion: c_1(L) ∩ α + c_1(N) ∩ α = c_1(L ⊗ N) ∩ α in CH_k(X), for the
cap product of Stacks 0EQJ as carried in this repository — so the component cycle
c_1(L|_W) ∩ [W] and the Chow group CH_k(X) remain explicit parameters, standing in for Stacks
0EQE and Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2)-(4), neither of which exists for algebraic spaces here.
QUALIFIED: carried as explicit named hypotheses are (i) that each of the three component rules
is the Weil divisor div_{L|_W}(s) of a meromorphic section, which is the definition of Stacks
0EQE, and (ii) that the ratio of the third section at the generic point of every prime divisor
is the product of the ratios of the first two, which stands in for `M = L ⊗ N` and `st = s·t`
because this repository has neither the tensor product of sheaves of modules on an algebraic
space nor the product of meromorphic sections — this is the hypothesis shape of the carried
Stacks 0EPV. Proved on top of those: the additivity of the component cycles, from Stacks 0EPV,
and the additivity of the cap product, from it. Neither side of the equality, and no conjunct
of it, is a hypothesis. CORRECTED: the source writes α ∈ Z_{k-1}(X), which cannot give an
identity in CH_k(X) for the operation Z_{k+1}(X) → CH_k(X) of Stacks 0EQJ; stated here for
α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X), as the identical scheme-side lemma Stacks 02SP does

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCap_structureSheaf_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQK, second assertion.** `c₁(O_X) ∩ α = 0` for every `α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)`.

The source's proof: the global section `1` of `O_X` restricts, on an integral closed subspace
`W ⊆ X`, to an everywhere nonzero section of `O_X|_W`, so `c₁(O_X|_W) ∩ [W] = 0`.  Here the
hypothesis `hunit` is that everywhere nonzero section: a nowhere vanishing section generates, so
its ratio against the chosen generator at the generic point of a prime divisor is a unit of the
henselian local ring there, and the order of vanishing of a unit is zero.  That the component
cycles all vanish is then proved, not assumed, and the vanishing of the cap product follows
from it.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCap_structureSheaf_eq_zero
    {L : Modules.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1} (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX L)
    {chern : FirstChernComponentCycleRule D sX k}
    {CH : Type w} [AddCommGroup CH] (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sX hX k CH)
    (d : ComponentDivisorData sX k setup chern)
    (hunit : ∀ (W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
      (P : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem W.subspace.toFunctor),
      ∃ vP : ↥(P.genericHenselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem (setup.isSpace W)
        (setup.isDecent W)), IsUnit vP ∧
        (d.ratio W P (d.sect W) :
            P.genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem (setup.isSpace W)
              (setup.isDecent W)) =
          algebraMap
            ↥(P.genericHenselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem (setup.isSpace W)
              (setup.isDecent W))
            (P.genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem (setup.isSpace W)
              (setup.isDecent W)) vP)
    (α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1)) :
    firstChernClassCap D sX hX L k hL chern chow α = 0
declarations.comment:
second assertion: c_1(O_X) ∩ α = 0 in CH_k(X), for the cap product of Stacks
0EQJ as carried in this repository — so the component cycle and the Chow group CH_k(X) remain
explicit parameters, standing in for Stacks 0EQE and Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2)-(4). QUALIFIED:
carried as explicit named hypotheses are (i) that the component rule is the Weil divisor
div_{O_X|_W}(s) of a meromorphic section, the definition of Stacks 0EQE, and (ii) that the
ratio of that section against the chosen generator is a unit of the henselian local ring at the
generic point of every prime divisor, which is the source's `1` restricting to an everywhere
nonzero section of O_X|_W — the structure sheaf itself is not named because this repository has
no tensor-unit sheaf of modules on an algebraic space. Proved on top of those: that every
component cycle vanishes, from the order of vanishing of a unit being zero, and that the cap
product vanishes, from that. The conclusion is not a hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.componentZeroCycleSumCoeff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQL, the right-hand side.** The coefficient family of the `k`-cycle
`∑ n_i [Z(s|_{X_i})]_k` on `X`: the sum, over the irreducible components `X_i ⊆ X` of
δ-dimension `k + 1`, of the pushforward along `X_i → X` of the cycle of the zero scheme of
`s|_{X_i}`, weighted by the multiplicity `n_i` of `X_i` in the fundamental cycle
`[X]_{k+1}`.

The sum is a finite sum at every integral closed subspace of `X`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasFiniteSupport_componentZeroCycleSumCoeff`.
declarations.statement:
def componentZeroCycleSumCoeff
    (γ : Space.points D.site D.base D.base_mem X →
      GeometricPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (γW : ComponentGeometricRepresentatives D sX hX L s k)
    (Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) : ℤ
declarations.comment:
RIGHT-HAND SIDE ONLY — the equality of 0EQM is NOT formalized here, see
cycleCoeffOfClosedSubspace_vanishingLocus_eq_componentZeroCycleSumCoeff: the sum
∑ n_i [Z(s_i)]_k as a coefficient family on the integral closed subspaces of X, over the
irreducible components X_i of X of δ-dimension k+1, of the pushforward along X_i → X of the
cycle [Z(s|_{X_i})]_k of Stacks 0EE9, weighted by the coefficient n_i of X_i in
[X]_{k+1} = [O_X]_{k+1}; the restriction s|_{X_i} is the inverse image of Stacks 03LU and
Z(s|_{X_i}) its zero scheme of Stacks 0845, both on X_i; the geometric representatives of the
generic points are the arguments γ and γW, as throughout this library, Lemma 0EE1 being absent
from it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleCoeffOfClosedSubspace_zeroScheme_eq_componentZeroCycleSumCoeff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQL.**  In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module,
let `s ∈ Γ(X, ℒ)` be a **regular** section and assume `dim_δ(X) ≤ k + 1`.  Write
`[X]_{k+1} = ∑ n_i [X_i]` with `X_i` the irreducible components of `X` of δ-dimension `k + 1`, and
`s_i = s|_{X_i}`.  Then

`[Z(s)]_k = ∑ n_i [Z(s_i)]_k`

as `k`-cycles on `X`.  This is equation 82.18.3.1, Stacks 0EQM.

The two sides are the coefficient families of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleCoeffOfClosedSubspace` at the zero scheme `Z(s)` of Stacks 0845 and
of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.componentZeroCycleSumCoeff`; the geometric representatives `γ`, `γW`,
`γZ` of the generic points are parameters throughout this library, Lemma 0EE1 being absent from
it, and the equality holds for every choice of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleCoeffOfClosedSubspace_zeroScheme_eq_componentZeroCycleSumCoeff
    (k : ℤ) (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX L)
    (hsreg : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection
      (structureCommRings D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hX.1⟩)
      (structureRingSheaf D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hX.1⟩).property s)
    (hdim : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ ≤ ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (γ : points D.site D.base D.base_mem X → GeometricPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hγ : ∀ x, (γ x).image = x)
    (γW : ComponentGeometricRepresentatives D sX hX L s k)
    (hγW : ∀ (W : ComponentsOfDeltaDimension D sX hX (k + 1)) y, (γW W y).image = y)
    (γZ : points D.site D.base D.base_mem (vanishingLocus D sX hX L s).1.toFunctor →
      GeometricPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem (vanishingLocus D sX hX L s).1.toFunctor)
    (hγZ : ∀ y, (γZ y).image = y) :
    cycleCoeffOfClosedSubspace D sX hX (vanishingLocus D sX hX L s).1
        (vanishingLocus D sX hX L s).2 k γZ =
      componentZeroCycleSumCoeff D sX hX L s k γ γW
declarations.comment:
equation 82.18.3.1, which is Stacks 0EQM, is the conclusion: the coefficient family
of [Z(s)]_k of Stacks 0EE9 equals componentZeroCycleSumCoeff, the sum over the irreducible
components X_i of X of δ-dimension k+1 of the pushforward along X_i → X of [Z(s|_{X_i})]_k
weighted by the coefficient n_i of X_i in [X]_{k+1}.  The geometric representatives of the generic
points are the parameters γ, γW, γZ, as throughout this library, Lemma 0EE1 being absent from it;
the equality holds for every choice of them.  The definition of the right-hand side is
componentZeroCycleSumCoeff (StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/Chow/FirstChernClassCap.lean)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowClassCanonical_firstChernCapCycleMap_closedSubspaceCycle_eq_vanishingLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQN.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good and let `ℒ` be an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module. Let `Y ⊆ X` be a closed subspace with `dim_δ(Y) ≤ k + 1` and let
`s ∈ Γ(Y, ℒ|_Y)` be a regular section. Then

`c₁(ℒ) ∩ [Y]_{k+1} = [Z(s)]_k`  in `CH_k(X)`.

Here `[Y]_{k+1}` is the cycle of Stacks 0EE9 of `Y` on `X`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedSubspaceCycle`; `c₁(ℒ) ∩ -` is the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ,
the cycle-level operation `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernCapCycleMap` at the canonical
component rule `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernRule`, its class taken afterwards;
`Z(s) ⊆ Y` is the zero scheme of Stacks 0845, whose `k`-cycle (defined because `dim_δ(Z(s)) ≤ k`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.deltaDimensionSubspace_vanishingLocus_closedSubspaceModuleRestrict_le`) is
read on `X` through the inclusion `Y → X`; and `CH_k(X)` is the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroupCanonical`, whose rational equivalences are sums of principal
divisors at the canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK.

The proof is the source's. Write `[Y]_{k+1} = ∑ n_i [Y_i]` over the irreducible components `Y_i`
of `Y` of δ-dimension `k + 1`. The restriction `s_i = s|_{Y_i}` is nonzero
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedSubspaceComponentImageSection_ne_zero`), so by Stacks 0EQF the
cycle `[Z(s_i)]_k` is the Weil divisor of `s_i`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleCoeffOfClosedSubspace_vanishingLocus_eq_canonicalDivisorCycleAt`),
which differs from the component cycle `c₁(ℒ|_{Y_i}) ∩ [Y_i]` of the cap product by a principal
divisor on `Y_i` at the canonical embeddings (Stacks 0EPT,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPrincipalDivisorCycleOfGood_zsmul_canonicalDivisorCycleAt_sub`). So
`c₁(ℒ) ∩ [Y]_{k+1} = ∑ n_i [Z(s_i)]_k` in `CH_k(X)`, and the right side is `[Z(s)]_k` by
Stacks 0EQL on `Y`
(`cycleCoeffOfClosedSubspace_vanishingLocus_eq_componentZeroCycleSumCoeff_of_isRegularSection`),
the zero schemes `Z(s_i)` being inverse images of `Z(s)` (Stacks 0846).
declarations.statement:
theorem chowClassCanonical_firstChernCapCycleMap_closedSubspaceCycle_eq_vanishingLocus
    (s : (closedSubspaceModuleRestrict D sX hX L Y).sections)
    (hs : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection
      (structureCommRings D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨Y.1.toFunctor, Y.2.1⟩)
      (structureRingSheaf D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨Y.1.toFunctor, Y.2.1⟩).property s) {k : ℤ}
    (hdim : deltaDimensionSubspace D sX hX Y.1 Y.2 ≤ ((k + 1 : ℤ) : EInt)) :
    chowClassCanonical.{max (u + 1) v} D sX hX k
        (firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k (canonicalFirstChernRule D sX hX L hL k)
          (closedSubspaceCycle D sX hX Y.1 Y.2 (k + 1) hdim)) =
      chowClassCanonical.{max (u + 1) v} D sX hX k (closedSubspaceCyclePushforward D sX hX Y k
        (closedSubspaceCycle D (Y.1.ι ≫ sX) (isGood_closedSubspace D sX hX Y)
          (vanishingLocus D (Y.1.ι ≫ sX) (isGood_closedSubspace D sX hX Y)
            (closedSubspaceModuleRestrict D sX hX L Y) s).1
          (vanishingLocus D (Y.1.ι ≫ sX) (isGood_closedSubspace D sX hX Y)
            (closedSubspaceModuleRestrict D sX hX L Y) s).2 k
          (deltaDimensionSubspace_vanishingLocus_closedSubspaceModuleRestrict_le D sX hX L Y hL s
            hs hdim)))
declarations.comment: c₁(ℒ) ∩ [Y]_{k+1} = [Z(s)]_k in CH_k(X), for X/B good, ℒ invertible, Y ⊆ X a closed subspace with dim_δ(Y) ≤ k + 1 and s ∈ Γ(Y, ℒ|_Y) a regular section; c₁(ℒ) ∩ - is Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical choices, [Y]_{k+1} and [Z(s)]_k are Stacks 0EE9 (the latter on Y, read on X through Y → X), Z(s) is Stacks 0845 and CH_k(X) is Stacks 0EQ6; nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.orderOfVanishingSection_eq_multiplicity_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQQ, coefficientwise.** *The order of vanishing of a meromorphic section pulls
back with multiplicities.* Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat, let `ℒ` be an `𝒪_Y`-module and `𝒩` an
`𝒪_X`-module standing for `f^*ℒ`, let `Z' ⊆ Y` and `Z ⊆ X` be prime divisors with `Z` over `Z'`,
and let `m` be the multiplicity of `Z` over `Z'` along the induced flat local homomorphism `φ`.
For a nonzero meromorphic section `s` of `ℒ` whose ratio `s / s_{ξ'}` at `ξ'` is `a / b`, and for
a meromorphic section `fs` of `𝒩` standing for `f^*s`, whose ratio at `ξ` against the
pulled-back generator is therefore `φ(a) / φ(b)`,

  `ord_{Z,𝒩}(fs) = m · ord_{Z',ℒ}(s)`.

The multiplicity `m` is the one with which `Z` occurs in `f^{-1}(Z')`, so for `X` integral this
is the source's identity `f^* div_ℒ(s) = ∑ n_i div_{f^*ℒ|_{X_i}}(s_i)` read at the coefficient
of `Z`; for `X` with several components it is each of the two readings of that identity, as the
implementation notes explain. The source proves it by passing to the multiplicative torsor
`q : T ⟶ Y`, where the section becomes a rational function, and then invoking Stacks 0EQA; here
the two are the same length computation, read on the ratio parameter of Stacks 0EPR rather than
on an embedding of the function field.
declarations.statement:
theorem orderOfVanishingSection_eq_multiplicity_mul
    (hloc : IsLocalHom φ) (hflat : φ.Flat) {m : ℕ}
    (hm : primeDivisorFlatMultiplicity B S hS hX hdecX ZX hY hdecY ZY φ = (m : ℕ∞))
    (L : Modules.{u, max u z} B S hS Y hY) (N : Modules.{u, max u z} B S hS X hX)
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} B S hS Y hY L)
    (fs : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} B S hS X hX N)
    (ratioY : LocalRatio.{u, z} B S hS hY hdecY ZY L)
    (ratioX : LocalRatio.{u, z} B S hS hX hdecX ZX N)
    (a b : nonZeroDivisors ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY))
    (hs : (ratioY s : ZY.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hY hdecY) =
      IsLocalization.mk' (ZY.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hY hdecY)
        (a : ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY)) b)
    (hfs : (ratioX fs : ZX.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdecX) =
      IsLocalization.mk' (ZX.genericTotalFractionRing B S hS hX hdecX)
        (φ (a : ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY)))
        (⟨φ (b : ↥(ZY.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hY hdecY)),
          Ring.map_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_flatHom hflat b.2⟩ :
          nonZeroDivisors ↥(ZX.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdecX))) :
    orderOfVanishingSection.{u, z} B S hS hX hdecX ZX N fs ratioX =
      (m : ℤ) * orderOfVanishingSection.{u, z} B S hS hY hdecY ZY L s ratioY
declarations.comment:
coefficientwise at a prime divisor Z of X with generic point ξ lying over a prime
divisor Z' of Y with generic point ξ': the order of vanishing of a meromorphic section pulls back
with the multiplicity, ord_{Z,f^*L}(f^*s) = m · ord_{Z',L}(s), where m is the colength of the
extended maximal ideal — the multiplicity with which Z occurs in f^{-1}(Z'), hence the
coefficient the flat pullback of Stacks 0EP8 attaches to Z. PROVED, not assumed: that the order
of vanishing multiplies by the multiplicity, from Stacks 02M1
(length_baseChange_eq_length_mul_length_quotient) applied to the cyclic modules O^h/a and O^h/b.
For X integral this is the source's identity f^* div_L(s) = ∑ n_i div_{f^*L|_{X_i}}(s_i) in
Z_{n+r-1}(X) read at the coefficient of Z, the one component having multiplicity one; the
statement is coefficientwise because the flat pullback of cycles is Stacks 0EP8, which this
repository does not have, and for the same reason Stacks 0EPV is already carried coefficientwise
here. NOT COVERED: for X with several irreducible components, the step from this identity to the
cycle identity, namely the additivity over the components of the multiplicities n_i = m_{X_i,X}
of Stacks 0EE2 and Stacks 0EE9; the statement applies to X and to each component X_i separately,
with m read in each, but no additivity of those multiplicities is proved in this repository.
RESTRICTED: carried as explicit named hypotheses are (i) the flat local homomorphism φ of the
henselian local rings at the generic points, with hloc and hflat; (ii) the module N and the
meromorphic section fs standing for f^*L and f^*s, this repository having no pullback of a
meromorphic section along a morphism of algebraic spaces, together with hfs, that the ratio of
fs at ξ against the pulled-back generator is the image under φ of the ratio of s at ξ' — which
is the source's own step of writing s/s_{ξ'} = a/b and pulling the fraction back, the chartwise
rule a/b ↦ f-sharp a / f-sharp b of Stacks 0ENC; (iii) the ratios of Stacks 0EPR at the two
generic points as the parameters ratioY and ratioX, exactly as Stacks 0EPR and 0EPV carry them;
and (iv) finiteness of the multiplicity, as hm naming the natural number m it equals. The
source's reduction through the multiplicative torsor of Stacks 0EQG is not used: the length
computation is the same one and is carried out directly on the ratio

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatPullbackMap_sectionWeilDivisor_eq_componentDivisorSum
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism over `B` which
is flat of relative dimension `r`, let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module, assume `Y` is integral
with `n = dim_δ(Y)`, and let `s` be a nonzero meromorphic section of `ℒ`. Then

  `f^* div_ℒ(s) = ∑ n_i div_{f^*ℒ|_{X_i}}(s_i)`

in `Z_{n + r - 1}(X)`: the left-hand side is the flat pullback (Stacks 0EP8) of the Weil divisor
`div_ℒ(s)` (Stacks 0EQE); on the right the sum runs over the irreducible components `X_i ⊂ X`
of δ-dimension `n + r`, `s_i = f|_{X_i}^*(s)` is the pullback of `s` (Stacks 0ENC), a nonzero
meromorphic section of the invertible module `f^*ℒ|_{X_i} = f|_{X_i}^*ℒ`,
`div_{f^*ℒ|_{X_i}}(s_i)` is its Weil divisor on `X_i` pushed forward to `X`, and
`n_i = m_{X_i, X}` is the multiplicity of `X_i` in `X` (Stacks 0EE9).
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullbackMap_sectionWeilDivisor_eq_componentDivisorSum :
    flatPullbackMap D sX hX sY hY f hbase r hflat hr (n - 1) (n + r - 1) (by ring)
        (sectionWeilDivisor D sY hY hintY L hL hn s hs) =
      componentDivisorSum D sX hX sY hY f r hflat hintY (n := n) L hL s hs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatCyclePullback_firstChernCapCycleMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQR, as an identity of cycles.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good,
let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat of relative dimension `r`, let `ℒ` be an invertible `O_Y`-module and let
`α` be a `(k+1)`-cycle on `Y`.  Then

  `f^*(c₁(ℒ) ∩ α) = c₁(f^*ℒ) ∩ f^*α`

in `Z_{k+r}(X)`.

The cap product is the carried Stacks 0EQJ at the level of cycles,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernCapCycleMap`, whose component rule is an explicit parameter;
the flat pullback is the carried Stacks 0EP8, whose defining formula is the field
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatCyclePullback.coeff`.  The identity of cycles is finer than the
source's identity of classes in `CH_{k+r-1}(X)`, which it implies; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatPullback_firstChernClassCap`.

Nothing about either side of the equality is assumed.  At a single integral closed subspace the
identity is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatCyclePullback_mult_firstChernComponentCycle`, whose
content is the pointwise Stacks 0EQQ; the passage to a general cycle exchanges two locally
finite double sums, which is the bookkeeping the source performs through Remark 0EQ8.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatCyclePullback_firstChernCapCycleMap
    (_hflat : IsFlat D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (_hr : HasRelativeDimension r D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (cmp : ∀ (W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
      (hW : deltaDimension D sY W = k + 1),
      FlatChernDivisorComparison D sX hX sY hY f r k pb setupY setupX chernY chernX W hW)
    (α : CycleGroup D sY (k + 1)) :
    pb.map k (k + (r : ℤ)) rfl (firstChernCapCycleMap D sY hY k chernY α) =
      firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX (k + (r : ℤ)) chernX
        (pb.map (k + 1) (k + (r : ℤ) + 1) (by ring) α)
declarations.comment:
as an identity of cycles in Z_{k+r}(X) rather than of classes in CH, which is the
finer statement and implies the source's once the class maps are known compatible — see
flatPullback_firstChernClassCap, which states the source's own grading. The cap product is the
cap product of Stacks 0EQJ as carried in this repository, firstChernCapCycleMap, so the
component cycle c_1(L|_W) ∩ [W] remains an explicit parameter standing in for Stacks 0EQE, which
does not exist for algebraic spaces here. PROVED, not assumed: the commutation itself. At a
single integral closed subspace W both coefficients collapse to one term and those terms are
equal by the pointwise Stacks 0EQQ
(orderOfVanishingSection_eq_multiplicity_mul); the passage to a general cycle is the
locally finite bookkeeping the source performs by appealing to Remark 0EQ8, and it is carried
out here by exchanging two double sums. No additive map is assumed to commute with the cap
product and no conjunct of the conclusion is a hypothesis. RESTRICTED: carried as explicit named
hypotheses are (i) the flat pullback of cycles of Stacks 0EP8, which this repository does not
construct, carried as FlatCyclePullback, that is TOGETHER WITH
ITS DEFINING FORMULA: a multiplicity mult W T for each pair of integral closed subspaces, the
maps Z_m(Y) → Z_n(X) for m + r = n, the statement that the coefficient of f^*α at T is
∑ α_W · mult W T, and that f^*[W] is carried by f^{-1}(W); (ii) the Weil divisor presentations of
Stacks 0EQE for the two component rules, exactly as Stacks 0EQK carries them, with
the sheaves L|_W and f^*L|_{f^{-1}(W)} and the sections s and f^*s as unconstrained parameters
identified by their ratios at the generic points, as in the carried Stacks 0EQQ, this repository
having no pullback of a sheaf of modules or of a meromorphic section along a morphism of
algebraic spaces; (iii) at each prime divisor of f^{-1}(W) the flat local homomorphism of
henselian local rings over the prime divisor of W beneath it, with its locality and flatness, as
in the carried Stacks 0EQA and 0EQQ; and (iv) the identification of the multiplicity Stacks 0EP8
attaches to that prime divisor with the colength primeDivisorFlatMultiplicity, which is Stacks
0EE9 read along a flat morphism and is not proved here. The inverse image of each integral
closed subspace occurring in α is assumed INTEGRAL, which is the case i = 1, n_1 = 1 of the
source's sum over the irreducible components of f^{-1}(W); the step to several components is the
additivity over them of the multiplicities of Stacks 0EE2 and Stacks 0EE9, which is NOT
COVERED by Stacks 0EQA and 0EQQ as stated here, and it is NOT COVERED here either

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatPullback_firstChernClassCap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQR.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat of
relative dimension `r`, let `ℒ` be an invertible `O_Y`-module and let `α` be a `(k+1)`-cycle on
`Y`.  Then

  `f^*(c₁(ℒ) ∩ α) = c₁(f^*ℒ) ∩ f^*α`

in `CH_{k+r}(X)`, for the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ as carried in this repository.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatCyclePullback_firstChernCapCycleMap` composed with the class
maps of the two Chow groups.  The flat pullback on Chow groups is the parameter `fstarCH`, and
all that is asked of it is that it be induced by the flat pullback of cycles, which is the
content of Stacks 0EQ9 — that flat pullback respects rational equivalence — and is the
hypothesis `hclass`.  That hypothesis says nothing about the cap product.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullback_firstChernClassCap
    (_hflat : IsFlat D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (_hr : HasRelativeDimension r D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (cmp : ∀ (W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
      (hW : deltaDimension D sY W = k + 1),
      FlatChernDivisorComparison D sX hX sY hY f r k pb setupY setupX chernY chernX W hW)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem Y hY.1)
    (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sY hY L)
    (N : Modules.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1)
    (hN : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX N)
    {CHY : Type w} [AddCommGroup CHY] (chowY : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sY hY k CHY)
    {CHX : Type w} [AddCommGroup CHX]
    (chowX : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sX hX (k + (r : ℤ)) CHX)
    (fstarCH : CHY →+ CHX)
    (hclass : ∀ β : CycleGroup D sY k,
      chowX.cls (pb.map k (k + (r : ℤ)) rfl β) = fstarCH (chowY.cls β))
    (α : CycleGroup D sY (k + 1)) :
    fstarCH (firstChernClassCap D sY hY L k hL chernY chowY α) =
      firstChernClassCap D sX hX N (k + (r : ℤ)) hN chernX chowX
        (pb.map (k + 1) (k + (r : ℤ) + 1) (by ring) α)
declarations.comment:
the source's own grading: f^*(c_1(L) ∩ α) = c_1(f^*L) ∩ f^*α in the Chow groups,
for the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ as carried here, so the component cycle c_1(L|_W) ∩ [W] and
the Chow groups CH of Stacks 0EQ6 remain explicit parameters, standing in for Stacks 0EQE and
Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2)-(4). PROVED, not assumed: the commutation, which is
flatCyclePullback_firstChernCapCycleMap — the identity of cycles whose content is the
pointwise Stacks 0EQQ — read through the two class maps. RESTRICTED: in addition to the
hypotheses of flatCyclePullback_firstChernCapCycleMap, which are listed on it (the flat pullback
of cycles of Stacks 0EP8 with its defining formula; the Weil divisor
presentations of Stacks 0EQE; the flat local homomorphisms of henselian local rings; the
identification of the multiplicity of Stacks 0EP8 with the colength; and the inverse image of
each integral closed subspace occurring in α assumed integral), the flat pullback on the Chow
groups is the parameter fstarCH together with hclass, that it is induced by the flat pullback of
cycles — which is Stacks 0EQ9, that flat pullback respects rational equivalence, and says
nothing about the cap product. The invertible sheaves L on Y and N on X, the latter standing for
f^*L, are unconstrained parameters as they are in the carried Stacks 0EQQ and as they are for
firstChernClassCap itself, which does not consume them

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatPullbackChowMapCanonical_canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQR.**  In Situation 0EDT let `X, Y/B` be good, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be flat of relative
dimension `r`, let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module and let `α` be a `(k+1)`-cycle on `Y`.  Then

  `f^*(c₁(ℒ) ∩ α) = c₁(f^*ℒ) ∩ f^*α`

in `CH_{k+r}(X)`.  Here `c₁(ℒ) ∩ - : Z_{k+1}(Y) → CH_k(Y)` is the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ
(`canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical`) into the Chow group `CH_k(Y)` of Stacks 0EQ6 at the canonical
embeddings of Stacks 0ENK, `f^* : CH_k(Y) → CH_{k+r}(X)` is the flat pullback on Chow groups of
Stacks 0EQB (`flatPullbackChowMapCanonical`), `f^*α` is the flat pullback of cycles of Stacks 0EP8
(`flatPullbackMap`) and `f^*ℒ` is the inverse image of Stacks 03LU (`modulePullback`).  The
source's `k`-cycle and `CH_{k+r-1}` are this statement's `(k+1)`-cycle and `CH_{k+r}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullbackChowMapCanonical_canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical
    (α : CycleGroup D sY (k + 1)) :
    flatPullbackChowMapCanonical.{u + 1} D sX hX sY hY f hbase r hflat hr k (k + (r : ℤ)) rfl
        (canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical.{u + 1} D sY hY L hL k α) =
      canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical.{u + 1} D sX hX
        ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem
          (ObjectProperty.homMk f : (⟨X, hX.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces D.site D.base D.base_mem) ⟶
            ⟨Y, hY.1⟩)).obj L)
        (modulePullbackInvertible
          (ObjectProperty.homMk f : (⟨X, hX.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces D.site D.base D.base_mem) ⟶
            ⟨Y, hY.1⟩) L hL) (k + (r : ℤ))
        (flatPullbackMap D sX hX sY hY f hbase r hflat hr (k + 1) (k + (r : ℤ) + 1) (by ring)
          α)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_divisorCycleOfSection_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQS, the identity in `Z_{n-1}(Y)`, reduced to its coefficients at the prime
divisors of `Y`.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be dominant
and quasi-compact over `B`, let `X` and `Y` be integral with `dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y) = n`, let `ℒ`
be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module and let `s` be a nonzero meromorphic section of `ℒ`. Then

`f_*(div_{f^*ℒ}(f^*s)) = [R(X) : R(Y)] div_ℒ(s)` in `Z_{n-1}(Y)`

holds exactly when it holds coefficientwise at every prime divisor of `Y`, that is when

`∑_Z ord_{Z, f^*ℒ}(f^*s) · deg(Z/Z') = [R(X) : R(Y)] · ord_{Z', ℒ}(s)`

for every prime divisor `Z' ⊆ Y`, the sum being over the integral closed subspaces `Z ⊆ X`.

Both sides are coefficient families on the integral closed subspaces of `Y`, and away from the
prime divisors of `Y` both vanish: the coefficient of `div_ℒ(s)` at an integral closed subspace
whose point set does not have codimension one is zero by Stacks 0EQE, part (1), and the
pushforward has no contribution there by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforwardCoeff_divisorCycleCoefficients_eq_zero`, which is
where the equality of the δ-dimensions is used. That is the whole content of the reduction; the
coefficient identity at a prime divisor of `Y` is *not* proved here.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_divisorCycleOfSection_eq_iff (_hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sY hY L)
    {f : X ⟶ Y} (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX) (hf : IsQuasiCompact D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (_hdom : IsDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hDvX : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdecX LX σX ratioX W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hDvY : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem Y =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1 hdecY L σ ratio W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem Y) :
    properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hf (n - 1)
          (divisorCycleOfSection D sX hX hdecX LX σX ratioX hDvX hintX dX hdX hnX) =
        (functionFieldDegreeAtGenericPoint D sX hX sY hY hintX f : ℤ) •
          divisorCycleOfSection D sY hY hdecY L σ ratio hDvY hintY dY hdY hnY ↔
      ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem Y,
        (∑ᶠ Z : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
            divisorCycleCoefficients D sX hX hdecX LX σX ratioX Z *
              properCycleMult D sX hX sY hY f Z
                (W.toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem)) =
          (functionFieldDegreeAtGenericPoint D sX hX sY hY hintX f : ℤ) *
            divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1 hdecY L σ ratio W
declarations.comment:
first conclusion REDUCED, not proved: f_*(div_{f^*L}(f^*s)) = [R(X):R(Y)] div_L(s)
in Z_{n-1}(Y) IF AND ONLY IF it holds at every prime divisor of Y; proved away from them, using
dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y); f^*L and f^*s are the unconstrained parameters LX and σX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_divisorCycleOfSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQS, first conclusion.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be dominant and quasi-compact over `B`, let `X` and `Y` be integral with
`dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y) = n`, let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module and let `s` be a nonzero
meromorphic section of `ℒ`. Then

`f_*(div_{f^*ℒ}(f^*s)) = [R(X) : R(Y)] div_ℒ(s)` in `Z_{n-1}(Y)`.

This is the plain equality the source asserts, resting on the single carried input
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ProperPushforwardNormRule`, which is Stacks 0EQ4 at the prime divisors
of `Y`. Everything else — that the two coefficient families agree away from the prime divisors
of `Y`, which is where `dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y)` is used — is proved, in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_divisorCycleOfSection_eq_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_divisorCycleOfSection (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sY hY L)
    {f : X ⟶ Y} (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX) (hf : IsQuasiCompact D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hdom : IsDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hDvX : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdecX LX σX ratioX W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hDvY : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem Y =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1 hdecY L σ ratio W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
    (hnorm : ProperPushforwardNormRule D sX hX sY hY hdecX hdecY LX σX ratioX L σ ratio
      hintX f) :
    properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hf (n - 1)
        (divisorCycleOfSection D sX hX hdecX LX σX ratioX hDvX hintX dX hdX hnX) =
      (functionFieldDegreeAtGenericPoint D sX hX sY hY hintX f : ℤ) •
        divisorCycleOfSection D sY hY hdecY L σ ratio hDvY hintY dY hdY hnY
declarations.comment:
first conclusion: f_*(div_{f^*L}(f^*s)) = [R(X):R(Y)] div_L(s) in Z_{n-1}(Y),
resting on the single carried input ProperPushforwardNormRule — Stacks 0EQ4 at the prime
divisors of Y, which this repository does not have; f^*L and f^*s are the parameters LX, σX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_firstChernClassCapFundamental_of_normRule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQS, second conclusion.** In the situation above,

`f_*(c₁(f^*ℒ) ∩ [X]) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ f_*[X]` in `CH_{n-1}(Y)`,

the right side being `[R(X) : R(Y)] · (c₁(ℒ) ∩ [Y])` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_integralCycle_integralClosedSubspaceUniv`, which is
`f_*[X] = [R(X) : R(Y)] [Y]`.

This rests on the same single carried input as the first conclusion; it is not conditional on
the first conclusion, which is proved from that input.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_firstChernClassCapFundamental_of_normRule
    (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sY hY L)
    {CH : Type w} [AddCommGroup CH] (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sY hY (n - 1) CH)
    {f : X ⟶ Y} (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX) (hf : IsQuasiCompact D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hdom : IsDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hDvX : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdecX LX σX ratioX W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hDvY : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem Y =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1 hdecY L σ ratio W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
    (hnorm : ProperPushforwardNormRule D sX hX sY hY hdecX hdecY LX σX ratioX L σ ratio
      hintX f) :
    chow.cls (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hf (n - 1)
        (divisorCycleOfSection D sX hX hdecX LX σX ratioX hDvX hintX dX hdX hnX)) =
      (functionFieldDegreeAtGenericPoint D sX hX sY hY hintX f : ℤ) •
        firstChernClassCapFundamental D sY hY hdecY L chow σ ratio hDvY hintY dY hdY hnY
declarations.comment:
second conclusion: f_*(c_1(f^*L) ∩ [X]) = c_1(L) ∩ f_*[X] in CH_{n-1}(Y), resting
on the same carried ProperPushforwardNormRule; the right side is [R(X):R(Y)] · (c_1(L) ∩ [Y]) by
the proved f_*[X] = [R(X):R(Y)][Y], the left the class on Y of the pushforward cycle

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_firstChernClassCapFundamental
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQS, the identity in `CH_{n-1}(Y)`, from the identity in `Z_{n-1}(Y)`.** In the
situation above, if

`f_*(div_{f^*ℒ}(f^*s)) = [R(X) : R(Y)] div_ℒ(s)` in `Z_{n-1}(Y)`,

which is the first conclusion of the source and the hypothesis `heq`, then

`f_*(c₁(f^*ℒ) ∩ [X]) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ f_*[X]` in `CH_{n-1}(Y)`,

the right side being `[R(X) : R(Y)] · (c₁(ℒ) ∩ [Y])` by `f_*[X] = [R(X) : R(Y)] [Y]`.

This is the source's own derivation of its second conclusion from its first. On the left,
`c₁(f^*ℒ) ∩ [X]` is by Stacks 0EQE, part (2), the class of `div_{f^*ℒ}(f^*s)`, and proper
pushforward on Chow groups is not available here, only on cycles, so the left side is the class
on `Y` of the pushforward cycle — the same reading the carried Stacks 0EQJ, case (1), uses for
`i_*`. On the right, `c₁(ℒ) ∩ [Y]` is again Stacks 0EQE, part (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCapFundamental`, a class independent of the chosen
nonzero meromorphic section by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCapFundamental_eq`, so the second identity is the image
of the first under the class map of the Chow group.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_firstChernClassCapFundamental (_hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sY hY L)
    {CH : Type w} [AddCommGroup CH] (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sY hY (n - 1) CH)
    {f : X ⟶ Y} (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX) (hf : IsQuasiCompact D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (_hdom : IsDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hDvX : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdecX LX σX ratioX W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hDvY : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem Y =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1 hdecY L σ ratio W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem Y)
    (heq : properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hf (n - 1)
        (divisorCycleOfSection D sX hX hdecX LX σX ratioX hDvX hintX dX hdX hnX) =
      (functionFieldDegreeAtGenericPoint D sX hX sY hY hintX f : ℤ) •
        divisorCycleOfSection D sY hY hdecY L σ ratio hDvY hintY dY hdY hnY) :
    chow.cls (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hf (n - 1)
        (divisorCycleOfSection D sX hX hdecX LX σX ratioX hDvX hintX dX hdX hnX)) =
      (functionFieldDegreeAtGenericPoint D sX hX sY hY hintX f : ℤ) •
        firstChernClassCapFundamental D sY hY hdecY L chow σ ratio hDvY hintY dY hdY hnY
declarations.comment:
second conclusion, DERIVED from the first (the hypothesis heq): f_*(c_1(f^*L) ∩
[X]) = c_1(L) ∩ f_*[X] in CH_{n-1}(Y), right side read as [R(X):R(Y)] · (c_1(L) ∩ [Y]) via
f_*[X] = [R(X):R(Y)][Y], left side as the class on Y of the pushforward CYCLE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properCyclePushforward_canonicalDivisorCycle_pullback
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism, let `ℒ`
be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module, assume `X` and `Y` integral, `f` dominant and
`dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y) = n`, and let `s` be a nonzero meromorphic section of `ℒ`. Then

`f_*(div_{f^*ℒ}(f^*s)) = [R(X) : R(Y)] div_ℒ(s)` in `Z_{n-1}(Y)`.

Here `f^*ℒ` is the inverse image `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback` (invertible by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackInvertible`), `f^*s` is the pullback of meromorphic
sections, defined because `f` carries the generic point of `X` to the generic point of `Y`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_genericPoint`, from dominance), and it
is nonzero because `f^*` preserves regular meromorphic sections; `div` is the Weil divisor of
Stacks 0EQE, part (1), at the canonical generators of Stacks 0EPR, `f_*` is proper pushforward
of cycles (Stacks 0EP2) and `[R(X) : R(Y)]` is the degree of the extension of function fields
(Stacks 0ENY).
declarations.statement:
theorem properCyclePushforward_canonicalDivisorCycle_pullback {f : X ⟶ Y} (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (hf : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem f) (hdom : IsDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    {n : ℤ} (hnX : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (hnY : deltaDimensionClosed D sY hY Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt)) (hσ : σ ≠ 0) :
    properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hf.2.1.2 (n - 1)
        (canonicalDivisorCycle D sX hX hintX
          ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem (goodSpacesHom D sX hX sY hY f)).obj L)
          (modulePullbackInvertible (goodSpacesHom D sX hX sY hY f) L hL)
          (pullbackMeromorphicSection D.site D.base D.base_mem (goodSpacesHom D sX hX sY hY f) L
            (pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_genericPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem (Z := ⟨X, hX.1⟩)
              (Y := ⟨Y, hY.1⟩) hintX hintY f
              (pointsMap_genericPoint_of_isDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hY.1 hintX hintY
                f hdom)) σ)
          (isRegularMeromorphicSection_pullbackMeromorphicSection D.site D.base D.base_mem
            (goodSpacesHom D sX hX sY hY f)
            (pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_genericPoint D.site D.base D.base_mem (Z := ⟨X, hX.1⟩)
              (Y := ⟨Y, hY.1⟩) hintX hintY f
              (pointsMap_genericPoint_of_isDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hY.1 hintX hintY
                f hdom)) L
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.toAlgebraicGeometry _ _ _ hL) σ
            ((isRegularMeromorphicSection_iff_ne_zero D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1 hintY
              (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian_of_isGood D sY hY) L hL σ).2 hσ)) hnX) =
      (functionFieldDegreeAtGenericPoint D sX hX sY hY hintX f : ℤ) •
        canonicalDivisorCycle D sY hY hintY L hL σ
          ((isRegularMeromorphicSection_iff_ne_zero D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1 hintY
            (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian_of_isGood D sY hY) L hL σ).2 hσ) hnY
declarations.comment:
first conclusion: f_*(div_{f^*L}(f^*s)) = [R(X):R(Y)] div_L(s) in Z_{n-1}(Y),
for f : X → Y proper and dominant of good integral spaces with dim_δ X = dim_δ Y = n, L invertible
on Y, s a nonzero meromorphic section; f^*L, f^*s, div (0EQE (1) at the canonical generators of
0EPR), f_* and [R(X):R(Y)] all constructed; nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properCyclePushforward_sectionWeilDivisor_pullback
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism, let `ℒ`
be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module, assume `X` and `Y` integral, `f` dominant and
`dim_δ(X) = dim_δ(Y) = n`, and let `s` be a nonzero meromorphic section of `ℒ`. Then

`f_*(div_{f^*ℒ}(f^*s)) = [R(X) : R(Y)] div_ℒ(s)` as cycles on `Y`, in `Z_{n-1}(Y)`,

and in particular

`f_*(c₁(f^*ℒ) ∩ [X]) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ f_*[X]` in `CH_{n-1}(Y)`.

`div` is the Weil divisor `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionWeilDivisor` of Stacks 0EQE, part
(1), `f^*ℒ` the inverse image `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback`, `f^*s` the pullback of
meromorphic sections (defined by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_isDominant_of_isIntegralSpace` and
nonzero by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackMeromorphicSection_ne_zero_of_isDominant`), `f_*`
proper pushforward of cycles (Stacks 0EP2) and `[R(X) : R(Y)]` the degree of the extension of
function fields (Stacks 0ENY).

In the second identity `c₁(f^*ℒ) ∩ [X]` is represented by the class of `div_{f^*ℒ}(f^*s)` in
`CH_{n-1}(X)` (Stacks 0EQE, part (2)), and `c₁(ℒ) ∩ f_*[X]` is written as
`[R(X) : R(Y)] (c₁(ℒ) ∩ [Y])`, since `f_*[X] = [R(X) : R(Y)] [Y]` (Stacks 0EP1), with
`c₁(ℒ) ∩ [Y]` the class `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.weilDivisorOfInvertibleSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properCyclePushforward_sectionWeilDivisor_pullback (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sY hY L)
    {f : X ⟶ Y} (hfB : f ≫ sY = sX) (hf : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem f)
    (hdom : IsDominant D.site D.base D.base_mem f) {n : ℤ}
    (hnX : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (hnY : deltaDimensionClosed D sY hY Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt)) (hσ : σ ≠ 0) :
    properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hf.2.1.2 (n - 1)
        (sectionWeilDivisor D sX hX hintX
          ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem (goodSpacesHom D sX hX sY hY f)).obj L)
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.toAlgebraicGeometry _ _ _
            (modulePullbackInvertible (goodSpacesHom D sX hX sY hY f) L
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.ofAlgebraicGeometry _ _ _ hL))) hnX
          (pullbackMeromorphicSection D.site D.base D.base_mem (goodSpacesHom D sX hX sY hY f) L
            (pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_isDominant_of_isIntegralSpace D sX hX sY hY hintX
              hintY hdom) σ)
          (pullbackMeromorphicSection_ne_zero_of_isDominant D sX hX sY hY hintX hintY L
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.ofAlgebraicGeometry _ _ _ hL) σ hdom hσ)) =
        (functionFieldDegreeAtGenericPoint D sX hX sY hY hintX f : ℤ) •
          sectionWeilDivisor D sY hY hintY L hL hnY σ hσ ∧
      chowClass.{v} D sY hY (n - 1) (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hfB hf.2.1.2 (n - 1)
        (sectionWeilDivisor D sX hX hintX
          ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem (goodSpacesHom D sX hX sY hY f)).obj L)
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.toAlgebraicGeometry _ _ _
            (modulePullbackInvertible (goodSpacesHom D sX hX sY hY f) L
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.ofAlgebraicGeometry _ _ _ hL))) hnX
          (pullbackMeromorphicSection D.site D.base D.base_mem (goodSpacesHom D sX hX sY hY f) L
            (pullbacksMeromorphicSections_of_isDominant_of_isIntegralSpace D sX hX sY hY hintX
              hintY hdom) σ)
          (pullbackMeromorphicSection_ne_zero_of_isDominant D sX hX sY hY hintX hintY L
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.ofAlgebraicGeometry _ _ _ hL) σ hdom hσ))) =
        (functionFieldDegreeAtGenericPoint D sX hX sY hY hintX f : ℤ) •
          weilDivisorOfInvertibleSheaf.{v} D sY hY hintY L hL hnY
declarations.comment:
both conclusions: f_*(div_{f^*L}(f^*s)) = [R(X):R(Y)] div_L(s) in Z_{n-1}(Y), and
f_*(c_1(f^*L) ∩ [X]) = c_1(L) ∩ f_*[X] = [R(X):R(Y)] (c_1(L) ∩ [Y]) in CH_{n-1}(Y), for f : X → Y
proper and dominant of good integral spaces with dim_δ X = dim_δ Y = n, L invertible on Y, s a
nonzero meromorphic section; div and c_1(-) ∩ [-] are Stacks 0EQE (1) and (2), f^*L, f^*s, f_*
and [R(X):R(Y)] constructed; the left side of the second identity is the class of the
pushforward of the cycle div_{f^*L}(f^*s) representing c_1(f^*L) ∩ [X]; nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_firstChernCapCycleMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQT, at the level of cycles.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let
`p : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism over `B`, let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module and let
`α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)`. Then

`p_*(c₁(p^*ℒ) ∩ α) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ p_*α` in `Z_k(Y)`,

an identity of `k`-cycles, hence also of classes in `CH_k(Y)`.

The cap products are the cycle-level cap product of Stacks 0EQJ, with the component rule of
`p^*ℒ` on `X` and of `ℒ` on `Y`, and the pushforwards are those of Stacks 0EP1, taken along the
quasi-compactness that properness of `p` supplies. The two carried inputs are the fields of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ProperPushforwardChernComparison`, both of them statements about the
pushforward along the component morphism `p|_W : W ⟶ W'` of Stacks 0EEG, which is proper
because `p` is: Stacks 0EP2 for the square of the source's reduction, and Stacks 0EQS along
`p|_W`, which is the source's final step. The passage from a single integral closed subspace to
an arbitrary cycle is proved.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_firstChernCapCycleMap
    (cmp : ProperPushforwardChernComparison D hX hY hpB hp k chernX chernY)
    (α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1)) :
    properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hp.2.1.2 k
        (firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k chernX α) =
      firstChernCapCycleMap D sY hY k chernY
