        (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hp.2.1.2 (k + 1) α)
declarations.comment:
at the level of cycles: p_*(c_1(p^*L) ∩ α) = c_1(L) ∩ p_*α in Z_k(Y) for α in
Z_{k+1}(X), with the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ and the pushforward of Stacks 0EP1; on the two
carried inputs of ProperPushforwardChernComparison — Stacks 0EP2 for the closed-immersion
square of the source's reduction, and Stacks 0EQS along the component morphism p|_W of Stacks
0EEG, which is proper
because p is; the component rule of p^*L is the parameter chernX, the repository having no
pullback of sheaves of modules; the reduction to a single subspace is PROVED

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_firstChernClassCap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQT.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `p : X ⟶ Y` be a proper
morphism over `B`, let `α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)` and let `ℒ` be an invertible sheaf on `Y`. Then

`p_*(c₁(p^*ℒ) ∩ α) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ p_*α` in `CH_k(Y)`.

The right side is the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ on `Y`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCap` at `ℒ`, applied to the pushforward of cycles
`p_*α`. Proper pushforward on Chow groups is not available in this repository, only on cycles,
so the left side is the class on `Y` of the pushforward of the cycle representing
`c₁(p^*ℒ) ∩ α`, which is the reading Stacks 0EQS and Stacks 0EQJ, case (1), already
use. The identity holds already at the level of cycles, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_firstChernCapCycleMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_firstChernClassCap
    (L : Modules.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem Y hY.1) (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sY hY L)
    {CH : Type w} [AddCommGroup CH] (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D sY hY k CH)
    (cmp : ProperPushforwardChernComparison D hX hY hpB hp k chernX chernY)
    (α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1)) :
    chow.cls (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hp.2.1.2 k
        (firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k chernX α)) =
      firstChernClassCap D sY hY L k hL chernY chow
        (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hp.2.1.2 (k + 1) α)
declarations.comment:
p_*(c_1(p^*L) ∩ α) = c_1(L) ∩ p_*α in CH_k(Y) for α in Z_{k+1}(X), the right side
being the cap product firstChernClassCap of Stacks 0EQJ at the invertible L, the left the class
on Y of the pushforward CYCLE, proper pushforward of Chow classes being unavailable here; on the
two carried inputs of ProperPushforwardChernComparison — Stacks 0EP2 for the closed-immersion
square of the source's reduction and Stacks 0EQS along the component morphism of Stacks 0EEG,
proper because p is; the component rule of p^*L is the parameter chernX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroupCanonicalProperPushforward_canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQT.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `p : X ⟶ Y` be a proper
morphism over `B`, let `α ∈ Z_{k+1}(X)` and let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module. Then

`p_*(c₁(p^*ℒ) ∩ α) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ p_*α`   in `CH_k(Y)`.

Every object is the constructed one, nothing is a parameter:

* `p^*ℒ` is the inverse image `(modulePullback p).obj ℒ` of Stacks 03LU, invertible by Stacks
  0B8P (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackInvertible`);
* `c₁(-) ∩ -` is the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ, `Z_{k+1} → CH_k`, at the canonical component
  rule (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical`), on `X` for `p^*ℒ` and on `Y`
  for `ℒ`;
* on the left `p_*` is proper pushforward on Chow groups, `CH_k(X) → CH_k(Y)`, of Stacks 0EQC
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroupCanonicalProperPushforward`); on the right it is proper
  pushforward of cycles `Z_{k+1}(X) → Z_{k+1}(Y)` of Stacks 0EP1;
* `CH_k` is the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6 (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroupCanonical`).

The proof is the source's: the formula is reduced to a single integral closed subspace `W` and
its image `W'`, where it is Stacks 0EQS for `W ⟶ W'` when the δ-dimension is preserved; the case
where it drops, which the source passes over, is
`properCyclePushforward_canonicalDivisorCycleAt_pullback_eq_zero_of_deltaValue_drop`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowGroupCanonicalProperPushforward_canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical
    (α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1)) :
    chowGroupCanonicalProperPushforward.{u + 1} D sX hX sY hY hqB hq k
        (canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical.{u + 1} D sX hX
          ((modulePullback D.site D.base D.base_mem q).obj L) (modulePullbackInvertible q L hL) k
          α) =
      canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical.{u + 1} D sY hY L hL k
        (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hqB hq.2.1.2 (k + 1) α)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_firstChernCapCycleMap_iff_component
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQT, reduced to the source's final step, in both directions.** In Situation 0EDT
let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `p : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism over `B`, let `ℒ` be an
invertible `𝒪_Y`-module and let `α` range over `Z_{k+1}(X)`. Then the projection formula

`p_*(c₁(p^*ℒ) ∩ α) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ p_*α` in `Z_k(Y)`

holds for every `α` **exactly when** it holds on the fundamental cycle `[W]` of every integral
closed subspace `W ⊆ X`, that is when

`p_*(c₁(p^*ℒ) ∩ [W]) = deg(W/W') · (c₁(ℒ) ∩ [W'])`

for `W'` the closure of the image of `|W|` and `deg(W/W')` the degree of Stacks 0EP1, part (1).

Both directions are proved and nothing is assumed: the forward direction is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_firstChernComponentCycle_of_firstChernCapCycleMap`,
the reverse the source's steps (2)–(4),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_firstChernCapCycleMap_of_component`.

The cap products are the cycle-level cap product of Stacks 0EQJ and the pushforwards those of
Stacks 0EP1, taken along the quasi-compactness that properness of `p` supplies. The component
rules of `p^*ℒ` and of `ℒ` are the parameters `chernX` and `chernY`; the instance at the
canonical rules, where `c₁(p^*ℒ)` is the first Chern class of the genuine inverse image `p^*ℒ`
of Stacks 03LU, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_canonicalFirstChernCapCycleMap_iff_component`.

The right-hand clause is Stacks 0EQS along the component morphism `p|_W : W ⟶ W'` of Stacks
0EEG, and it is open here; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_firstChernCapCycleMap_iff_component :
    (∀ α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1),
        properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hp.2.1.2 k
            (firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k chernX α) =
          firstChernCapCycleMap D sY hY k chernY
            (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hp.2.1.2 (k + 1) α)) ↔
      ∀ W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
        properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hpB hp.2.1.2 k
            (firstChernComponentCycle D sX hX k chernX W) =
          properCycleDegree D sX hX sY hY p W •
            firstChernComponentCycle D sY hY k chernY
              (IntegralClosedSubspace.closureImage D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1
                (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood sY hY) p W)
declarations.comment:
REDUCED, not proved: p_*(c_1(p^*L) ∩ α) = c_1(L) ∩ p_*α in Z_k(Y) for every α in
Z_{k+1}(X) IF AND ONLY IF it holds on the fundamental cycle [W] of every integral closed
subspace W of X. BOTH directions are proved and nothing is assumed, with the cap product of
Stacks 0EQJ and the pushforward of Stacks 0EP1. The remaining clause, at a single W, is Stacks
0EQS along the component morphism p|_W of Stacks 0EEG, which rests on Stacks 0EQ4 and is open in
this repository

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_canonicalFirstChernCapCycleMap_iff_component
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQT, reduced to the source's final step, with both component rules tied to `ℒ`.**
In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` and `Y/B` be good, let `p : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism over `B`,
let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module and let `α` range over `Z_{k+1}(X)`. Then

`p_*(c₁(p^*ℒ) ∩ α) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ p_*α` in `Z_k(Y)`

holds for every `α` **exactly when** it holds on the fundamental cycle `[W]` of every integral
closed subspace `W ⊆ X`. Both directions are proved and nothing is assumed; this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.properPushforward_firstChernCapCycleMap_iff_component` at the canonical
component rules of Stacks 0EQJ.

Here `c₁(p^*ℒ)` is the first Chern class of the *genuine* inverse image `p^*ℒ` of Stacks 03LU,
through `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalPullbackFirstChernRule`, and `c₁(ℒ)` that of `ℒ`,
through `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernRule`; neither is a parameter, and both are
the rule `W ↦ div(t_W)` of Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical ratios of Stacks 0EPR.

The remaining clause, at a single `W`, is Stacks 0EQS along the component morphism
`p|_W : W ⟶ W'` of Stacks 0EEG, and is open here: Stacks 0EQS rests on the coefficient identity
of Stacks 0EQ4, which this repository does not prove. See the implementation notes of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.ProperPushforwardOfDivisor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_canonicalFirstChernCapCycleMap_iff_component (hqB : q.hom ≫ sY = sX)
    (hq : IsProper D.site D.base D.base_mem q.hom) (k : ℤ) :
    (∀ α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1),
        properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hqB hq.2.1.2 k
            (firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k
              (canonicalPullbackFirstChernRule D hX hY q L hL k) α) =
          firstChernCapCycleMap D sY hY k (canonicalFirstChernRule D sY hY L hL k)
            (properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hqB hq.2.1.2 (k + 1) α)) ↔
      ∀ W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
        properCyclePushforward D sX hX sY hY hqB hq.2.1.2 k
            (firstChernComponentCycle D sX hX k
              (canonicalPullbackFirstChernRule D hX hY q L hL k) W) =
          properCycleDegree D sX hX sY hY q.hom W •
            firstChernComponentCycle D sY hY k (canonicalFirstChernRule D sY hY L hL k)
              (IntegralClosedSubspace.closureImage D.site D.base D.base_mem hY.1
                (D.isDecentSpace_of_isGood sY hY) q.hom W)
declarations.comment:
REDUCED, not proved, with BOTH component rules tied to L rather than parametric:
p_*(c_1(p^*L) ∩ α) = c_1(L) ∩ p_*α in Z_k(Y) for every α in Z_{k+1}(X) IF AND ONLY IF it holds
on the fundamental cycle [W] of every integral closed subspace W of X. BOTH directions are
proved and nothing is assumed. c_1(p^*L) is the canonical rule of Stacks 0EQJ at the genuine
inverse image p^*L of Stacks 03LU, invertible by Stacks 0B8P, and c_1(L) the canonical rule at
L. The remaining clause, at a single W, is Stacks 0EQS along the component morphism p|_W of
Stacks 0EEG, which rests on Stacks 0EQ4 and is open in this repository

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.genericResidueFieldEquivFunctionField
declarations.doc:
**The canonical isomorphism `θ_Z : κ(u) ≃+* R(Z)`** of Section 0EQU between the residue
field of the local ring of the chart at the generic point of a prime divisor and the function
field of the prime divisor.  Its inverse is evaluation at `ρ_Z`.
declarations.statement:
def PrimeDivisor.genericResidueFieldEquivFunctionField :
    Z.genericResidueField B S hS hX hdec ≃+* rationalFunctions B S hS Z.closed.1
declarations.comment: the identification κ(ξ) = R(Z) of the residue field at the generic point of a prime divisor with its function field, at the residue field of the chosen chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.henselianResidueFieldEquivFunctionField
declarations.doc:
**The composite `κ(𝒪^h_{X, ξ}) ≃+* R(Z)`**: the residue field of the henselian local ring at
the generic point of a prime divisor is the function field of the prime divisor, through the
residue field `κ(u)` of the chosen chart.  A unit `v` of `𝒪^h_{X, ξ}` thus has a residue
`θ(v̄) ∈ R(Z)`, which is how the key formula of Section 0EQU reads a change of generator on
`Z`.
declarations.statement:
def PrimeDivisor.henselianResidueFieldEquivFunctionField :
    letI := henselianLocalRing_isLocalRing B S hS X hX (Z.genericPoint B S hS X) hdec
    IsLocalRing.ResidueField ↥(Z.genericHenselianLocalRing B S hS hX hdec) ≃+*
      rationalFunctions B S hS Z.closed.1
declarations.comment: the residue field of the henselian local ring at the generic point of a prime divisor is its function field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.genericRestriction
declarations.doc:
**`σ_Z = s_ξ|_Z`, the restriction to a prime divisor of the generator at its generic point**:
the unique meromorphic section of `ℒ|_Z` whose pullback along `ρ_Z : Spec κ(u) → Z` is the image
of the generator `s_ξ` of `ℒ` at the generic point.
declarations.comment: the image s_ξ|_Z of a generator s_ξ of ℒ_ξ in the fibre at the generic point, as a meromorphic section of ℒ|_Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernCapCycleMap_divisorCycleAt_eq_componentDivisorSum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQU: either cycle identity of the section preceding the key formula, with the
component cycle `div_{𝒩|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i)` constructed and not assumed.**  In Situation 0EDT let
`X/B` be good and integral with `dim_δ(X) = n`, let `ℒ` and `𝒩` be `𝒪_X`-modules, let `s` be a
nonzero meromorphic section of `ℒ`, and let `{Z_i}`, `i ∈ I`, be an injective locally finite
family of prime divisors of `X` containing every prime divisor along which `s` has nonzero order
of vanishing.  Then

`c₁(𝒩) ∩ div_ℒ(s) = ∑_i ord_{Z_i,ℒ}(s) · (Z_i → X)_* div_{𝒩|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i)`

in `Z_{n-2}(X)`, the component cycle `c₁(𝒩|_{Z_i}) ∩ [Z_i]` being the Weil divisor
`div_{𝒩|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i)` of Stacks 0EQE part (1) on `Z_i`, that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.componentDivisorCycleRule`.  The two identities displayed in Section
0EQU before the key formula are the two instances of this statement, exchanging `(ℒ, s)` with
`(𝒩, t)` and `𝒩` with `ℒ`.

The orders `ord_{Z_i,ℒ}(s)` are those of Stacks 0EPR, which the source identifies with its
`ord_{B_i}(f_i)`; the δ-dimension hypothesis `hdim` is Stacks 0EPZ, proved as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.deltaDimension_toIntegralClosedSubspace`.

This statement takes, as inputs on each `W`, exactly what Stacks 0EQE takes on `X`: the
meromorphic section `t W` of `𝒩|_W`, which at `W = Z_i` is the source's reduction `t_i|Z_i`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.genericFibreReduction`, read through Stacks 0EN0); the
ratio family `ratioN` of Stacks 0EPR; the local finiteness `hfinN` of Stacks 0EPS; and the
dimension function `dimN` of Stacks 0EDN.  The same four, on `X`, are `ratio`, `hfin`, `d` and
`hd` here.  Two of those four are no longer needed once `𝒩` is invertible, which is Section
0EQU's own hypothesis on `𝒩`:
`firstChernCapCycleMap_divisorCycleAt_eq_componentDivisorSum_of_isInvertible`
is this identity with `t` produced by Stacks 0EPQ on `W` and with `dimN` derived from `d`.  This
version is kept because it needs no hypothesis on `𝒩` at all.

The key formula itself, Stacks 0EQV, **is** proved, unconditionally and axiom-clean:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.keyFormula_of_ne_zero` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.KeyFormulaProof.Headline`, at the canonical choices and
for the constructed tame-symbol sum, from which Stacks 0EQX follows there as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm`.  What is still open is only the
*predicate* `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.KeyFormula` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.KeyFormulaCycleIdentities`, which quantifies the
component rules of Stacks 0EQJ and the principal divisors of the tame symbols; at that generality
it is not a theorem of this library.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernCapCycleMap_divisorCycleAt_eq_componentDivisorSum
    {k : ℤ} {I : Type v}
    (t : ∀ W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem W.subspace.toFunctor
        (setup.isSpace W) (integralClosedSubspaceRestrict D sX hX N W))
    (ratioN : ∀ W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      LocalRatioFamily.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem (setup.isSpace W) (setup.isDecent W)
        (integralClosedSubspaceRestrict D sX hX N W))
    (dimN : ∀ W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem W.subspace.toFunctor))
    (hdimN : ∀ (W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
      (x : points D.site D.base D.base_mem W.subspace.toFunctor),
      dimN W x = D.deltaValue (W.subspace.ι ≫ sX) x)
    (hfinN : ∀ W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      LocallyFinite fun P : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem W.subspace.toFunctor =>
        if setup.sectionOrder W (integralClosedSubspaceRestrict D sX hX N W) (t W) (ratioN W) P = 0
          then ∅ else P.support D.site D.base D.base_mem W.subspace.toFunctor)
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L)
    (ratio : LocalRatioFamily.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L)
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratio W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (d : DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (hd : ∀ x, d x = D.deltaValue sX x) {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (hk : k + 1 = n - 1)
    (Z : I → PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hZinj : Function.Injective Z)
    (hZfin : LocallyFinite fun i : I =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X (Z i).subspace)
    (hdim : ∀ i, deltaDimension D sX
      ((Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) = k + 1)
    (hcover : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratio W ≠ 0 →
        ∃ i, Z i = W) :
    firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k
        (componentDivisorCycleRule sX hX setup N k t ratioN dimN hdimN hfinN)
        (divisorCycleAt.{u, z} D sX hX hdec L s ratio hfin hint d hd hn hk) =
      cycleFamilySum D sX hX
        (fun i => (Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) hZfin k
        (fun i => orderOfVanishingSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec (Z i) L s
          (ratio (Z i)) •
            componentDivisorCycleRule sX hX setup N k t ratioN dimN hdimN hfinN
              ((Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) (hdim i))
declarations.comment: either cycle identity of the section, c_1(N) ∩ div_L(s) = ∑ ord_{B_i}(f_i) (Z_i → X)_* div_{N|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i) in Z_{n-2}(X), with the component cycle no longer a parameter: it is the Weil divisor div_{N|W}(t_W) of Stacks 0EQE part (1) on W, for the restriction N|W of Stacks 03LU. N is arbitrary here, and what is then carried on W is what Stacks 0EQE carries on X: the meromorphic section t W, the Stacks 0EPR ratio family, the Stacks 0EPS local finiteness and the Stacks 0EDN dimension function. For N invertible, which is the section's own hypothesis, t W and the dimension function are produced and not carried, see firstChernCapCycleMap_divisorCycleAt_eq_componentDivisorSum_of_isInvertible. hdim is Stacks 0EPZ. The key formula 0EQV IS proved, unconditionally and axiom-clean, as keyFormula_of_ne_zero of StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.KeyFormulaProof.Headline, and 0EQX follows there as canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm; what is still open is only the quantified predicate KeyFormula of KeyFormulaCycleIdentities, which ranges over the component rules of 0EQJ and the tame-symbol divisors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernCapCycleMap_divisorCycleAt_eq_componentDivisorSum_of_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQU for an invertible `𝒩`, with the component cycle's meromorphic section and
dimension function produced and not assumed.**  Section 0EQU's cycle identity

`c₁(𝒩) ∩ div_ℒ(s) = ∑_i ord_{Z_i,ℒ}(s) · (Z_i → X)_* div_{𝒩|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i)`

in `Z_{n-2}(X)`, where the component cycle at an integral closed subspace `W ⊆ X` is the Weil
divisor `div_{𝒩|_W}(t_W)` of Stacks 0EQE part (1) on `W` **of a meromorphic section `t_W` this
statement constructs**: `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.componentMeromorphicSection`, a regular
meromorphic section of `𝒩|_W` produced by Stacks 0EPQ on `W`, whose hypotheses (a), (b), (c) of
Stacks 0ENA hold because `W` is integral and locally Noetherian.  The source's `t_i|Z_i` — the
reduction of a chosen generator of `𝒩_{ξ_i}`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrimeDivisor.genericFibreReduction` — is one such section, and the
identity holds for any of them: the component cycle is a parameter of Stacks 0EQJ occurring on
both of its sides.

The dimension function of Stacks 0EDN on each `W` is likewise no longer carried: it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.subspaceDeltaDimensionFunction`, the dimension function `d` on `|X|`
pulled back along the closed embedding `|W| → |X|`, which is a dimension function because an
intermediate point of a specialization starting in a closed set lies in that closed set.

Invertibility of `𝒩` is Section 0EQU's own hypothesis on `𝒩`.  What is still carried on each
`W` is the pair Stacks 0EQE carries on `X`: the ratio family `ratioN` of Stacks 0EPR and the
local finiteness `hfinN` of the prime divisors of `W` along which `t_W` has nonzero order,
Stacks 0EPS.  Neither can be discharged while
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.LocalRatio` is an unconstrained function type — a ratio family not
required to be `s ↦ s / s_ξ` for a generator `s_ξ` makes `ord` arbitrary, so the set of prime
divisors of nonzero order is not controlled; the *first* set of Stacks 0EPS, which does not
mention the ratio, is proved and applies to `t_W` because `t_W` is regular, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyFinite_primeDivisor_not_memGenericModuleStalk_of_isIntegral`.

The key formula itself, Stacks 0EQV, **is** proved, unconditionally and axiom-clean:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.keyFormula_of_ne_zero` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.KeyFormulaProof.Headline`, at the canonical choices and
for the constructed tame-symbol sum, from which Stacks 0EQX follows there as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm`.  What is still open is only the
*predicate* `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.KeyFormula` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.KeyFormulaCycleIdentities`, which quantifies the
component rules of Stacks 0EQJ and the principal divisors of the tame symbols; at that generality
it is not a theorem of this library.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernCapCycleMap_divisorCycleAt_eq_componentDivisorSum_of_isInvertible
    {k : ℤ} {I : Type v}
    (hN : IsInvertibleModule (⟨X, hX.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces D.site D.base D.base_mem) N)
    (ratioN : ∀ W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      LocalRatioFamily.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem (setup.isSpace W) (setup.isDecent W)
        (integralClosedSubspaceRestrict D sX hX N W))
    (d : DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (hd : ∀ x, d x = D.deltaValue sX x)
    (hfinN : ∀ W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      LocallyFinite fun P : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem W.subspace.toFunctor =>
        if setup.sectionOrder W (integralClosedSubspaceRestrict D sX hX N W)
            (componentMeromorphicSection sX hX setup N hN W) (ratioN W) P = 0
          then ∅ else P.support D.site D.base D.base_mem W.subspace.toFunctor)
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L)
    (ratio : LocalRatioFamily.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L)
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratio W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X) {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (hk : k + 1 = n - 1)
    (Z : I → PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hZinj : Function.Injective Z)
    (hZfin : LocallyFinite fun i : I =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X (Z i).subspace)
    (hdim : ∀ i, deltaDimension D sX
      ((Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) = k + 1)
    (hcover : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratio W ≠ 0 →
        ∃ i, Z i = W) :
    firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k
        (componentDivisorCycleRule sX hX setup N k
          (componentMeromorphicSection sX hX setup N hN) ratioN
          (fun W => subspaceDeltaDimensionFunction D sX hX d W)
          (fun W => subspaceDeltaDimensionFunction_eq_deltaValue D sX hX d hd W) hfinN)
        (divisorCycleAt.{u, z} D sX hX hdec L s ratio hfin hint d hd hn hk) =
      cycleFamilySum D sX hX
        (fun i => (Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) hZfin k
        (fun i => orderOfVanishingSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec (Z i) L s
          (ratio (Z i)) •
            componentDivisorCycleRule sX hX setup N k
              (componentMeromorphicSection sX hX setup N hN) ratioN
              (fun W => subspaceDeltaDimensionFunction D sX hX d W)
              (fun W => subspaceDeltaDimensionFunction_eq_deltaValue D sX hX d hd W) hfinN
              ((Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) (hdim i))
declarations.comment: either cycle identity of the section for an invertible N, with the component cycle div_{N|W}(t_W) of Stacks 0EQE part (1) on W and its meromorphic section t_W no longer a parameter: t_W is a regular meromorphic section of N|W produced by Stacks 0EPQ on W, and the Stacks 0EDN dimension function on W is the one on X pulled back along the closed embedding. What is carried on W is the Stacks 0EPR ratio family and the Stacks 0EPS local finiteness of the prime divisors of nonzero order, both blocked by LocalRatio being an unconstrained function type. hdim is Stacks 0EPZ. The key formula 0EQV IS proved, unconditionally and axiom-clean, as keyFormula_of_ne_zero of StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.KeyFormulaProof.Headline, and 0EQX follows there as canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm; what is still open is only the quantified predicate KeyFormula of KeyFormulaCycleIdentities, which ranges over the component rules of 0EQJ and the tame-symbol divisors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm
declarations.doc:
**Section 0EQU, the key formula: `c₁(𝒩) ∩ div_ℒ(s) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ div_𝒩(t)` in `CH_{n-2}(X)`.**
In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, `X` integral with `dim_δ(X) = n`, let `ℒ` and `𝒩` be
invertible `𝒪_X`-modules, and let `s`, `t` be nonzero meromorphic sections of `ℒ`, `𝒩`.  Then
`c₁(𝒩) ∩ div_ℒ(s) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ div_𝒩(t)` in the Chow group `CH_{n-2}(X)` of Stacks 0EQ6, the cap
products being those of Stacks 0EQJ and the divisors those of Stacks 0EQE, all at the canonical
choices.

The proof is the section's: the family `{Z_i}` of prime divisors where `s` or `t` fails to
generate is locally finite (Stacks 0EPS), the two cap products are the sums over it of
`ord_{B_i}(f_i) (Z_i → X)_* div(t_i|_{Z_i})` and `ord_{B_i}(g_i) (Z_i → X)_* div(s_i|_{Z_i})`, and
the key formula (Stacks 0EQV) makes their difference a locally finite sum of principal divisors of
tame symbols on the `Z_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L) (hs : s ≠ 0)
    (t : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 N) (ht : t ≠ 0)
    {n : ℤ} (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt)) :
    canonicalFirstChernCap.{u, u + 1} D sX hX N hN (n - 2)
        (canonicalDivisorCycleAt D sX hX hint L hL s
          (isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_ne_zero_of_isGood D sX hX hint L hL hs)
          (deltaDimensionClosed_eq_sub_two_add_one_add_one D sX hX hn)) =
      canonicalFirstChernCap.{u, u + 1} D sX hX L hL (n - 2)
        (canonicalDivisorCycleAt D sX hX hint N hN t
          (isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_ne_zero_of_isGood D sX hX hint N hN ht)
          (deltaDimensionClosed_eq_sub_two_add_one_add_one D sX hX hn))
declarations.comment: the key formula of the section, c_1(N) ∩ div_L(s) = c_1(L) ∩ div_N(t) in CH_{n-2}(X), at the section's hypotheses; Lemma 0EQV is keyFormula_of_ne_zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap_canonicalDivisorCycleAt
declarations.doc:
**Section 0EQU, claim (3).** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, `X` integral with
`dim_δ(X) = n = k + 2`, let `ℒ`, `𝒩` be invertible with `s` a regular meromorphic section of
`ℒ`, and let `{Z_i}` be a locally finite family of prime divisors such that `s` generates `ℒ_ξ`
at the generic point of every prime divisor outside it.  For generators `s_i = v_i s_{ξ_i}` of
`ℒ_{ξ_i}` write `s = f_i s_i`, `f_i ∈ Q(B_i)^*`.  Then for any regular meromorphic sections
`τ_i` of `𝒩|_{Z_i}` — in particular for the source's `t_i|_{Z_i}` —

`c₁(𝒩) ∩ div_ℒ(s) = ∑ ord_{B_i}(f_i) (Z_i → X)_* div_{𝒩|_{Z_i}}(τ_i)`  in `CH_{n-2}(X)`.

The cap product is the one of Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical choices,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap`, the divisors are those of Stacks 0EQE at the
canonical ratios, and `CH_{n-2}(X)` is the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6.  The second identity of
the section is this one with `(ℒ, s)` and `(𝒩, t)` exchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalFirstChernCap_canonicalDivisorCycleAt
    (N : Modules.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1)
    (hN : IsInvertibleModule (⟨X, hX.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces D.site D.base D.base_mem) N)
    {I : Type v} (Zf : I → PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hinj : Function.Injective Zf)
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun i : I =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X
        ((Zf i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem).subspace)
    (hcov : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X, (∀ i, Zf i ≠ W) →
      W.SectionGenerates D sX hX hint L hL s)
    {k : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = ((k + 1 + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))
    (v : ∀ i, ↥((Zf i).genericHenselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1
      (isDecentSpace_of_isGood D sX hX)))
    (hv : ∀ i, IsUnit (v i))
    (f : ∀ i, ((Zf i).genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1
      (isDecentSpace_of_isGood D sX hX))ˣ)
    (hf : ∀ i, (f i : (Zf i).genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1
        (isDecentSpace_of_isGood D sX hX)) * algebraMap _ _ (v i) =
      (Zf i).canonicalGenericRatio D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1
        (isDecentSpace_of_isGood D sX hX) L hL hint
        (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian_of_isGood D sX hX) s)
    (τ : ∀ i, MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem
      ((Zf i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem).subspace.toFunctor
      (isGood_integralClosedSubspace D sX hX _).1
      (integralClosedSubspaceRestrict D sX hX N
        ((Zf i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem)))
    (hτ : ∀ i, IsRegularMeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem _
      (isGood_integralClosedSubspace D sX hX _).1 _ (τ i)) :
    haveI := fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      W.nontrivial_genericHenselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1
        (isDecentSpace_of_isGood D sX hX) hint
        (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian_of_isGood D sX hX)
    haveI := fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      W.isNoetherianRing_genericHenselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1
        (isDecentSpace_of_isGood D sX hX) hint
        (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian_of_isGood D sX hX)
    haveI := fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      W.krullDimLE_genericHenselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1
        (isDecentSpace_of_isGood D sX hX) hint
        (hasEtaleLocalProperty_isLocallyNoetherian_of_isGood D sX hX)
    canonicalFirstChernCap.{u, v} D sX hX N hN k
        (canonicalDivisorCycleAt D sX hX hint L hL s hs hn) =
      chowClass.{v} D sX hX k (cycleFamilySum D sX hX
        (fun i => (Zf i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) hfin k
        (fun i => (Zf i).ord D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 (isDecentSpace_of_isGood D sX hX)
            (f i : (Zf i).genericTotalFractionRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1
              (isDecentSpace_of_isGood D sX hX)) (f i).isUnit •
          canonicalDivisorCycleAt D _ (isGood_integralClosedSubspace D sX hX _)
            ((Zf i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem).isIntegralSpace
            (integralClosedSubspaceRestrict D sX hX N
              ((Zf i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem))
            (isInvertibleModule_integralClosedSubspaceRestrict D sX hX N hN _) (τ i) (hτ i)
            (deltaDimensionClosed_univ_toIntegralClosedSubspace D sX hX hint hn (Zf i))))
declarations.comment: the cycle identities of the section, in CH_{n-2}(X) as the source states them: c_1(N) ∩ div_L(s) = ∑ ord_{B_i}(f_i) (Z_i → X)_* div_{N|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i), with everything at the canonical choices (the cap product, the divisors and the ratios s = f_i s_i are constructed, not carried) and for an arbitrary regular meromorphic section of N|Z_i in place of t_i|Z_i; the second identity is the same statement with (L, s) and (N, t) exchanged. Claims (1)-(2) of the section are canonicalDivisorCycle_apply_eq_zero_of_notMem, canonicalDivisorCycle_apply_primeDivisor and orderOfVanishingSection_canonical_eq_ord

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyFinite_primeDivisor_not_sectionGenerates
declarations.doc:
**Section 0EQU: the family exists** ("Such a set exists by Spaces over Fields, Lemma 0EPS").
The prime divisors at whose generic point `s` fails to generate `ℒ_ξ` or `t` fails to generate
`𝒩_ξ` form a locally finite family; it is the smallest family the section may be taken over.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFinite_primeDivisor_not_sectionGenerates :
    LocallyFinite fun W : {W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X //
        ¬ (W.SectionGenerates D sX hX hint L hL s ∧ W.SectionGenerates D sX hX hint N hN t)} =>
      W.1.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X
declarations.comment: existence of the family {Z_i}: the prime divisors at whose generic point s or t fails to generate form a locally finite family (by 0EPS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernCapCycleMap_divisorCycleAt_eq_cycleFamilySum
declarations.doc:
**Either cycle identity of the section preceding the key formula, for an arbitrary component
rule.**  In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good and integral with `dim_δ(X) = n`, let `ℒ` be an
`𝒪_X`-module with a nonzero meromorphic section `s`, and let `{Z_i}`, `i ∈ I`, be an injective
locally finite family of prime divisors of `X` containing every prime divisor along which `s` has
nonzero order of vanishing.  Then

`c₁(𝒩) ∩ div_ℒ(s) = ∑_i ord_{Z_i,ℒ}(s) · (Z_i → X)_*(c₁(𝒩|_{Z_i}) ∩ [Z_i])`

in `Z_{n-2}(X)`.  The two identities displayed in Section 0EQU before the key formula are the two
instances of this statement: the first is the one above, and the second is obtained by exchanging
`(ℒ, s)` with `(𝒩, t)` and `𝒩` with `ℒ`, that is by using the component rule of `ℒ` and the
divisor of `t`.

The orders `ord_{Z_i,ℒ}(s)` are those of Stacks 0EPR, which the source identifies with its
`ord_{B_i}(f_i)`, and they depend on the `ratio` parameter of Stacks 0EPR only through its value
at the generic points, not at all by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.orderOfVanishingSection_unit_smul`.  The δ-dimension hypothesis `hdim` is
Stacks 0EPZ, proved as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.deltaDimension_toIntegralClosedSubspace`.

The component cycle `c₁(𝒩|_{Z_i}) ∩ [Z_i]`, which the source writes `div_{𝒩|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i)`, is
here the arbitrary component rule `chern` of Stacks 0EQJ: nothing below uses any property of it.
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernCapCycleMap_divisorCycleAt_eq_componentDivisorSum` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.KeyFormulaComponentDivisor` is the instance of this
statement in which that cycle is the Weil divisor `div_{𝒩|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i)` of Stacks 0EQE part (1)
on `Z_i`; that is the form Section 0EQU displays, and it carries the tag.

The key formula itself, Stacks 0EQV, **is** proved, at the canonical choices and for the
constructed tame-symbol sum:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.keyFormula_of_ne_zero` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.KeyFormulaProof.Headline`, from which Section 0EQU's
`c₁(𝒩) ∩ div_ℒ(s) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ div_𝒩(t)` in `CH_{n-2}(X)` follows as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm`.  What is left open is only the
predicate `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.KeyFormula` below, which quantifies the component rules and
the tame-symbol divisors and so cannot be discharged at that generality.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernCapCycleMap_divisorCycleAt_eq_cycleFamilySum
    {k : ℤ} (chern : FirstChernComponentCycleRule D sX k) {I : Type v}
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L)
    (ratio : LocalRatioFamily.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L)
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratio W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (d : DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (hd : ∀ x, d x = D.deltaValue sX x) {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (hk : k + 1 = n - 1)
    (Z : I → PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hZinj : Function.Injective Z)
    (hZfin : LocallyFinite fun i : I =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X (Z i).subspace)
    (hdim : ∀ i, deltaDimension D sX
      ((Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) = k + 1)
    (hcover : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratio W ≠ 0 →
        ∃ i, Z i = W) :
    firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k chern
        (divisorCycleAt.{u, z} D sX hX hdec L s ratio hfin hint d hd hn hk) =
      cycleFamilySum D sX hX
        (fun i => (Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) hZfin k
        (fun i => orderOfVanishingSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec (Z i) L s
          (ratio (Z i)) •
            chern ((Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) (hdim i))
declarations.comment: the situation above, not the lemma: either cycle identity of Section 0EQU, c_1(N) ∩ div_L(s) = ∑ ord_{B_i}(f_i) (Z_i → X)_* div_{N|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i) in Z_{n-2}(X), for an arbitrary component rule chern of Stacks 0EQJ, of which it uses no property; hdim is Stacks 0EPZ. DISCHARGED ELSEWHERE: the instance at the registered cap product — the component cycle canonicalFirstChernRule at the canonical choices, in CH_{n-2}(X) — is canonicalFirstChernCap_canonicalDivisorCycleAt, and the key formula itself is proved unconditionally as keyFormula_of_ne_zero; neither carries a free component rule

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernCap_sub_firstChernCap_eq_cycleFamilySum
declarations.doc:
The first cycle of the key formula is the difference of the two cap products of Section
0EQU: with the family `{Z_i}` containing every prime divisor along which `s` or `t` has nonzero
order of vanishing,

`c₁(𝒩) ∩ div_ℒ(s) - c₁(ℒ) ∩ div_𝒩(t)
  = ∑_i (Z_i → X)_*(ord_{B_i}(f_i) div_{𝒩|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i) - ord_{B_i}(g_i) div_{ℒ|Z_i}(s_i|Z_i))`

in `Z_{n-2}(X)`.  It is the two cycle identities of Section 0EQU together with additivity of the
locally finite sum of Stacks 0EQ6 part (1).

The two restricted divisors `div_{𝒩|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i)` and `div_{ℒ|Z_i}(s_i|Z_i)` are the component
cycles carried as the parameters `chernN` and `chernL` of Stacks 0EQJ, standing in for Stacks 0EQE
on `Z_i`; the two orders are those of Stacks 0EPR, which the source identifies with
`ord_{B_i}(f_i)` and `ord_{B_i}(g_i)`; the δ-dimension hypothesis `hdim` is Stacks 0EPZ, proved as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.deltaDimension_toIntegralClosedSubspace`.

The key formula itself — the equality of this cycle with `∑_i (Z_i → X)_* div(∂_{B_i}(f_i, g_i))`
— **is** proved at the canonical choices, as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.keyFormula_of_ne_zero`; only the predicate
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.KeyFormula`, which quantifies the component rules and the tame-symbol
divisors, is left open.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernCap_sub_firstChernCap_eq_cycleFamilySum
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L)
    (t : MeromorphicSection.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 N)
    (ratioL : LocalRatioFamily.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L)
    (ratioN : LocalRatioFamily.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec N)
    (hfinL : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratioL W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hfinN : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec N t ratioN W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (dim : DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (hd : ∀ x, dim x = D.deltaValue sX x) {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (hk : k + 1 = n - 1)
    (hZinj : Function.Injective Z)
    (hZfin : LocallyFinite fun i : I =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X (Z i).subspace)
    (hdim : ∀ i, deltaDimension D sX
      ((Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) = k + 1)
    (hcoverL : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratioL W ≠ 0 →
        ∃ i, Z i = W)
    (hcoverN : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      divisorCoefficients.{u, z} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec N t ratioN W ≠ 0 →
        ∃ i, Z i = W) :
    firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k chernN
        (divisorCycleAt.{u, z} D sX hX hdec L s ratioL hfinL hint dim hd hn hk) -
      firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k chernL
        (divisorCycleAt.{u, z} D sX hX hdec N t ratioN hfinN hint dim hd hn hk) =
      cycleFamilySum D sX hX
        (fun i => (Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) hZfin k
        (keyFormulaDivisorTerm.{u, z} D sX hX hdec L N chernL chernN Z s t ratioL ratioN hdim)
declarations.comment: the situation above, not the lemma: the FIRST cycle of the key formula equals c_1(N) ∩ div_L(s) - c_1(L) ∩ div_N(t), from the two cycle identities of Section 0EQU, for arbitrary component rules chernN and chernL of Stacks 0EQJ, of which no property is used; hdim is Stacks 0EPZ. DISCHARGED ELSEWHERE: the key formula itself is proved unconditionally, at the canonical choices and for the constructed tame-symbol sum, as keyFormula_of_ne_zero, and its Section 0EQU consequence in CH_{n-2}(X) as canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.keyFormula_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQV, the key formula, for nonzero meromorphic sections.** In Situation 0EDT let
`X/B` be good, `X` integral with `dim_δ(X) = n`, let `ℒ`, `𝒩` be invertible with nonzero
meromorphic sections `s`, `t`, let `{Z_i}` be an injective locally finite family of prime divisors
outside of which `s` generates `ℒ_ξ` and `t` generates `𝒩_ξ`, and let `s_i = v_i s_{ξ_i}`,
`t_i = w_i t_{ξ_i}` be generators of `ℒ_{ξ_i}`, `𝒩_{ξ_i}` (`v_i`, `w_i` units of
`B_i = 𝒪^h_{X,ξ_i}`; every generator is of this form for a unique unit), so that `s = f_i s_i`,
`t = g_i t_i` with `f_i, g_i ∈ Q(B_i)^*`.  Then

`∑ (Z_i → X)_*(ord_{B_i}(f_i) div_{𝒩|_{Z_i}}(t_i|_{Z_i})
    - ord_{B_i}(g_i) div_{ℒ|_{Z_i}}(s_i|_{Z_i}))
  = ∑ (Z_i → X)_* div(∂_{B_i}(f_i, g_i))`

in `Z_{n-2}(X)`, with `t_i|_{Z_i}` the image of `t_i` in the fibre `𝒩_{ξ_i} ⊗ κ(ξ_i)` read as a
meromorphic section of `𝒩|_{Z_i}`, and `∂_{B_i}` the tame symbol of Stacks 0EAH read in
`κ(ξ_i)^* = R(Z_i)^*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem keyFormula_of_ne_zero
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L) (hs : s ≠ 0)
    (t : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 N) (ht : t ≠ 0)
    {n : ℤ} (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    {I : Type*} (Zf : I → PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hfin : LocallyFinite fun i : I =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X
        ((Zf i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem).subspace)
    (hinj : Function.Injective Zf)
    (hcov : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X, (∀ i, Zf i ≠ W) →
      W.SectionGenerates D sX hX hint L hL s ∧ W.SectionGenerates D sX hX hint N hN t)
    (v w : ∀ i, (↥((Zf i).genericHenselianLocalRing D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1
      (isDecentSpace_of_isGood D sX hX)))ˣ) :
    keyFormulaDivisorSum D sX hX hint L hL s
        (isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_ne_zero_of_isGood D sX hX hint L hL hs) N hN t
        (isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_ne_zero_of_isGood D sX hX hint N hN ht)
        (deltaDimensionClosed_eq_sub_two_add_one_add_one D sX hX hn) Zf hfin v w =
      keyFormulaTameSum D sX hX hint L hL s
        (isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_ne_zero_of_isGood D sX hX hint L hL hs) N hN t
        (isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_ne_zero_of_isGood D sX hX hint N hN ht)
        (deltaDimensionClosed_eq_sub_two_add_one_add_one D sX hX hn) Zf hfin v w

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernClassCap_comm_iff_isRationallyEquivalentToZero
declarations.doc:
**The conclusion of Stacks 0EQX, reduced to the key formula of Stacks 0EQV, for an arbitrary
component rule.**  In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good and integral with `dim_δ(X) = n`, let `ℒ`
and `𝒩` be invertible with nonzero meromorphic sections `s` and `t`, and set `α = div_ℒ(s)`,
`β = div_𝒩(t)`.  Then

`c₁(𝒩) ∩ α = c₁(ℒ) ∩ β` in `CH_{n-2}(X)`

holds if and only if the first cycle of the key formula of Section 0EQU is rationally equivalent
to zero, where that cycle is
`∑_i (Z_i → X)_*(ord_{B_i}(f_i) div_{𝒩|Z_i}(t_i|Z_i) - ord_{B_i}(g_i) div_{ℒ|Z_i}(s_i|Z_i))`.

This is an equivalence, so it does not by itself prove the equality; what proves it is the key
formula, which gives the right hand side.  **Stacks 0EQX itself is proved**, unconditionally and
at its own hypotheses, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.KeyFormulaProof.Headline`, which is where the tag's
mathematical content lives.  What this statement adds is the generality: the component cycle
`c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩ [W]` of Stacks 0EQE is the explicit parameter `chern` of Stacks 0EQJ and the
equivalence holds for every value of it, so it is the form that converts the open predicate
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.KeyFormula` — the key formula quantified over component rules and
tame-symbol divisors — into the equality at that generality.  `CH_{n-2}(X)` is the Chow group of
Stacks 0EQ6 constructed in `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroup`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstChernClassCap_comm_iff_isRationallyEquivalentToZero
    (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX L) (hN : IsInvertibleSheaf D sX hX N)
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L)
    (t : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 N)
    (ratioL : LocalRatioFamily.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L)
    (ratioN : LocalRatioFamily.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec N)
    (hfinL : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratioL W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hfinN : LocallyFinite fun W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X =>
      if divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec N t ratioN W = 0 then ∅
      else W.support D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (dim : DimensionFunction (points D.site D.base D.base_mem X))
    (hd : ∀ x, dim x = D.deltaValue sX x) {n : ℤ}
    (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt))
    (hk : k + 1 = n - 1)
    (hZinj : Function.Injective Z)
    (hZfin : LocallyFinite fun i : I =>
      subspacePointSet D.site D.base D.base_mem X (Z i).subspace)
    (hdim : ∀ i, deltaDimension D sX
      ((Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) = k + 1)
    (hcoverL : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec L s ratioL W ≠ 0 →
        ∃ i, Z i = W)
    (hcoverN : ∀ W : PrimeDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem X,
      divisorCoefficients.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem hX.1 hdec N t ratioN W ≠ 0 →
        ∃ i, Z i = W) :
    firstChernClassCap D sX hX N k hN chernN (chowTarget.{v} D sX hX k)
          (divisorCycleAt.{u, u} D sX hX hdec L s ratioL hfinL hint dim hd hn hk) =
        firstChernClassCap D sX hX L k hL chernL (chowTarget.{v} D sX hX k)
          (divisorCycleAt.{u, u} D sX hX hdec N t ratioN hfinN hint dim hd hn hk) ↔
      IsRationallyEquivalentToZero.{v} D sX hX k
        (cycleFamilySum D sX hX
          (fun i => (Z i).toIntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem) hZfin k
          (keyFormulaDivisorTerm.{u, u} D sX hX hdec L N chernL chernN Z s t ratioL ratioN
            hdim))
declarations.comment: not the lemma itself but its equivalence form: the equality c_1(N) ∩ div_L(s) = c_1(L) ∩ div_N(t) in CH_{n-2}(X) is shown to hold if and only if the first cycle of the key formula 0EQV is rationally equivalent to zero, for an arbitrary component rule chern of 0EQJ. The lemma's own statement is PROVED ELSEWHERE, unconditionally and at the hypotheses of 0EQX: canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm of StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.KeyFormulaProof.Headline, at the canonical component rule and the canonical divisors, registered under 0EQX as well. The equivalence is kept for its generality in chern, at which the key formula is the open predicate KeyFormula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm
declarations.doc:
**Section 0EQU, the key formula: `c₁(𝒩) ∩ div_ℒ(s) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ div_𝒩(t)` in `CH_{n-2}(X)`.**
In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, `X` integral with `dim_δ(X) = n`, let `ℒ` and `𝒩` be
invertible `𝒪_X`-modules, and let `s`, `t` be nonzero meromorphic sections of `ℒ`, `𝒩`.  Then
`c₁(𝒩) ∩ div_ℒ(s) = c₁(ℒ) ∩ div_𝒩(t)` in the Chow group `CH_{n-2}(X)` of Stacks 0EQ6, the cap
products being those of Stacks 0EQJ and the divisors those of Stacks 0EQE, all at the canonical
choices.

The proof is the section's: the family `{Z_i}` of prime divisors where `s` or `t` fails to
generate is locally finite (Stacks 0EPS), the two cap products are the sums over it of
`ord_{B_i}(f_i) (Z_i → X)_* div(t_i|_{Z_i})` and `ord_{B_i}(g_i) (Z_i → X)_* div(s_i|_{Z_i})`, and
the key formula (Stacks 0EQV) makes their difference a locally finite sum of principal divisors of
tame symbols on the `Z_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalFirstChernCap_divisor_comm
    (s : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 L) (hs : s ≠ 0)
    (t : MeromorphicSection.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X hX.1 N) (ht : t ≠ 0)
    {n : ℤ} (hn : deltaDimensionClosed D sX hX Set.univ isClosed_univ = (n : EInt)) :
    canonicalFirstChernCap.{u, u + 1} D sX hX N hN (n - 2)
        (canonicalDivisorCycleAt D sX hX hint L hL s
          (isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_ne_zero_of_isGood D sX hX hint L hL hs)
          (deltaDimensionClosed_eq_sub_two_add_one_add_one D sX hX hn)) =
      canonicalFirstChernCap.{u, u + 1} D sX hX L hL (n - 2)
        (canonicalDivisorCycleAt D sX hX hint N hN t
          (isRegularMeromorphicSection_of_ne_zero_of_isGood D sX hX hint N hN ht)
          (deltaDimensionClosed_eq_sub_two_add_one_add_one D sX hX hn))
declarations.comment: Lemma 82.21.1 itself: for X good and integral with δ-dimension n, L and N invertible and s, t nonzero meromorphic sections, c_1(N) ∩ div_L(s) = c_1(L) ∩ div_N(t) in CH_{n-2}(X). Unconditional at the source's hypotheses: integrality and goodness are the section variables, regularity of s and t is derived from s ≠ 0, t ≠ 0 rather than assumed, and the cap product of 0EQJ, the divisors of 0EQE and the Chow group of 0EQ6 are the constructed ones, not carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRationallyEquivalentToZeroCanonical_firstChernCapCycleMap_canonicalFirstChernRule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQY at the level of cycles.**  For `X/B` good and `𝒩` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module,
the cap product `c₁(𝒩) ∩ - : Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ Z_k(X)` of Stacks 0EQJ carries a `(k+1)`-cycle
rationally equivalent to zero to a `k`-cycle rationally equivalent to zero, both in the sense of
part (2) of Stacks 0EQ6 read at the canonical embeddings `R(W) → Q(𝒪^h_{W,ξ})` of Stacks 0ENK.

Nothing is assumed.  The reassembly over the presenting family of the rational equivalence is
`isRationallyEquivalentToZeroCanonical_firstChernCapCycleMap_of_pushforwardDivisor`, and the
summand statement it asks for is the previous theorem.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRationallyEquivalentToZeroCanonical_firstChernCapCycleMap_canonicalFirstChernRule
    {α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1)}
    (hα : IsRationallyEquivalentToZeroCanonical.{u + 1} D sX hX (k + 1) α) :
    IsRationallyEquivalentToZeroCanonical.{u + 1} D sX hX k
      (firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k (canonicalFirstChernRule D sX hX N hN k) α)
declarations.comment: the cap product with the first Chern class is compatible with rational equivalence, at the level of cycles: it carries a cycle rationally equivalent to zero to a cycle rationally equivalent to zero, both read at the canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCapCanonicalChowMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQY.**  The cap product of Stacks 0EQJ descends to

`c₁(𝒩) ∩ - : CH_{k+1}(X) ⟶ CH_k(X)`,

with `CH_*(X)` the Chow group `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroupCanonical` of Stacks 0EQ6 at the
canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK on both sides.

The descent is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroupCanonicalLift` and the hypothesis it needs is
the previous theorem.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalFirstChernCapCanonicalChowMap :
    chowGroupCanonical.{u + 1} D sX hX (k + 1) →+ chowGroupCanonical.{u + 1} D sX hX k
declarations.comment: the descended operation CH_{k+1}(X) -> CH_k(X), the Chow groups being those of Stacks 0EQ6 at the canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK on both sides

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernCapCanonicalChowMap_chowClassCanonical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQY.**  The descended operation agrees with the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ on the
class of a cycle, which is what it means for the cap product to factor through rational
equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalFirstChernCapCanonicalChowMap_chowClassCanonical
    (α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1)) :
    canonicalFirstChernCapCanonicalChowMap D sX hX k N hN
        (chowClassCanonical.{u + 1} D sX hX (k + 1) α) =
      canonicalFirstChernCapCanonical.{u + 1} D sX hX N hN k α
declarations.comment: the descended operation agrees with the cap product of Stacks 0EQJ on the class of a cycle, which is the factorization through rational equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowClassCanonical_firstChernCapCycleMap_firstChernCapCycleMap_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EQZ: the two iterated cap products with first Chern classes commute.** In
Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good and let `ℒ`, `𝒩` be invertible `𝒪_X`-modules. For every
`(k + 2)`-cycle `α` on `X`,

`c₁(ℒ) ∩ c₁(𝒩) ∩ α = c₁(𝒩) ∩ c₁(ℒ) ∩ α` in `CH_k(X)`.

The cap products are those of Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical choices
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalFirstChernRule`): the inner one is the cycle-level operation
`Z_{k+2}(X) → Z_{k+1}(X)` defining `c₁(-) ∩ -` on representatives, and so is the outer one
`Z_{k+1}(X) → Z_k(X)`, the class being taken afterwards in the Chow group `CH_k(X)` of
Stacks 0EQ6, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroupCanonical`, whose rational equivalences are sums of
principal divisors at the canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK. As every class of `CH_{k+2}(X)` is
the class of a cycle, this is the identity of the source on representatives.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowClassCanonical_firstChernCapCycleMap_firstChernCapCycleMap_comm (k : ℤ)
    (α : CycleGroup D sX (k + 1 + 1)) :
    chowClassCanonical.{max (u + 1) v} D sX hX k
        (firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k (canonicalFirstChernRule D sX hX L hL k)
          (firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX (k + 1) (canonicalFirstChernRule D sX hX N hN (k + 1))
            α)) =
      chowClassCanonical.{max (u + 1) v} D sX hX k
        (firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX k (canonicalFirstChernRule D sX hX N hN k)
          (firstChernCapCycleMap D sX hX (k + 1) (canonicalFirstChernRule D sX hX L hL (k + 1))
            α))
declarations.comment: c₁(ℒ) ∩ c₁(𝒩) ∩ α = c₁(𝒩) ∩ c₁(ℒ) ∩ α in CH_k(X), for every (k+2)-cycle α on X representing a class of CH_{k+2}(X); both cap products are the cycle-level operations of Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical choices, the classes taken in the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6 at the canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK (chowGroupCanonical); nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.refinedGysin
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ER1, parts (1) and (2).** The *refined Gysin homomorphism*
`i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ CH_k(E)` of the vanishing locus `E = Z(s)` of a global section `s` of an
invertible sheaf `ℒ` on a good algebraic space `X/B`, with `i : E → X` the closed immersion.

On the cycle of an integral closed subspace `W ⊆ X` of δ-dimension `k + 1` it is the class of
`[E ∩ W]_k` when `W ⊄ E`, which is part (1)(a), and the class of `i'_*(c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩ [W])` when
`W ⊆ E`, which is part (1)(b); see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.refinedGysin_integralCycle_of_not_le` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.refinedGysin_integralCycle_of_le`.  Part (2), the extension of that
rule over an arbitrary `(k+1)`-cycle, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.gysinCycleMap`, which is
proved to land in `Z_k(E)` and to be additive.

The Chow group `CH_k(E)` and the two component cycles `[E ∩ W]_k` and `c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩ [W]` are
explicit parameters, standing in for Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2)–(4), Stacks 0EE9 and Stacks 0EQJ,
none of which is available for algebraic spaces in this repository; see the implementation notes
of `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Chow.EffectiveCartierIntersection`.
declarations.statement:
def refinedGysin (_hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D p hp L)
    (rule : GysinComponentRule D p (vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k)
    {CH : Type w} [AddCommGroup CH]
    (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D ((vanishingLocus D p hp L s).1.ι ≫ p) hE k CH) :
    CycleGroup D p (k + 1) →+ CH
declarations.comment:
the refined Gysin homomorphism i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) → CH_k(D) of the vanishing locus
D = Z(s), parts (1)(a), (1)(b) and (2); the Chow group of D and the two component cycles
[D ∩ W]_k and c_1(L|_W) ∩ [W] are explicit parameters, instantiated by Stacks 0EQ6 parts
(2)-(4) (chowTarget), Stacks 0EE9 (closedSubspaceCycle) and Stacks 0EQJ
(canonicalFirstChernRule)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.effectiveCartierIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ER1, part (3).** Intersecting with an effective Cartier divisor: when `E = Z(s)`
is an effective Cartier divisor on `X` one writes `E · α = i_* i^* α` for the pushforward along
the closed immersion `i : E → X` of the refined Gysin class of `α`.

The pushforward is the honest pushforward of cycles along a closed immersion,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cycleGroupClosedPushforward`, applied to the cycle-level Gysin map; the
class map of a Chow group for `X` is applied afterwards.  The source applies `i_*` to a Chow
class, which needs proper pushforward to respect rational equivalence; the form below is that
statement at the level of cycles, and is the same once Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2)–(4) land.
declarations.statement:
def effectiveCartierIntersection (_hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D p hp L)
    (_hCartier : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩
      (vanishingLocus D p hp L s))
    (rule : GysinComponentRule D p (vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k)
    {CH : Type w} [AddCommGroup CH]
    (chow : ChowTarget.{u, w, v} D p hp k CH) :
    CycleGroup D p (k + 1) →+ CH
declarations.comment:
part (3): the operation D · α = i_* i^* α of an effective Cartier divisor
D = Z(s), with the Chow group of X and the component cycles [D ∩ W]_k and c_1(L|_W) ∩ [W] taken
as explicit parameters, instantiated by Stacks 0EQ6 parts (2)-(4) (chowTarget), Stacks 0EE9
(closedSubspaceCycle) and Stacks 0EQJ (canonicalFirstChernRule); the pushforward i_* is applied
to the cycle-level Gysin map, the source applying it to the class

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionRefinedGysin
declarations.doc:
The *refined Gysin homomorphism* `i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ CH_k(E)` of the vanishing locus
`E = Z(s)` of a global section `s` of an invertible sheaf `ℒ` on a good algebraic space `X/B`,
`i : E → X` the closed immersion, with values in the Chow group `CH_k(E) = Z_k(E)/∼_rat`.

On the cycle `[W]` of an integral closed subspace `W ⊆ X` of δ-dimension `k + 1` it is the class
of `[E ∩ W]_k` when `W ⊄ E` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionRefinedGysin_integralCycle_of_not_le`)
and the class of `i'_*(c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩ [W])` when `W ⊆ E`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionRefinedGysin_integralCycle_of_le`); on a general cycle
`α = ∑ n_W [W]` it is the class of `∑ n_W i^*[W]`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionRefinedGysin_apply`).
declarations.statement:
def sectionRefinedGysin (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D p hp L) :
    CycleGroup D p (k + 1) →+
      chowGroup.{v} D ((vanishingLocus D p hp L s).1.ι ≫ p)
        (isGood_vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k
declarations.comment: parts (1)(a), (1)(b) and (2): the refined Gysin homomorphism i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) → CH_k(D) of the vanishing locus D = Z(s) of a global section of an invertible sheaf, with values in CH_k(D) = Z_k(D)/∼_rat of Stacks 0EQ6, clause (1)(a) the cycle [D ∩ W]_k of Stacks 0EE9 of the scheme-theoretic intersection and clause (1)(b) the pushforward of div_{L|_W}(t_W) for the regular meromorphic section of Stacks 0EPQ, every ingredient constructed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionCartierIntersection
declarations.doc:
Intersecting with an effective Cartier divisor: when `E = Z(s)` is an effective Cartier
divisor on `X`, the operation `E · α = i_* i^* α` with values in the Chow group `CH_k(X)`, `i_*`
being the pushforward along the closed immersion
`i : E → X` of the cycle `∑ n_W i^*[W]` representing `i^* α`.
declarations.statement:
def sectionCartierIntersection (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D p hp L)
    (hCartier : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩
      (vanishingLocus D p hp L s)) :
    CycleGroup D p (k + 1) →+ chowGroup.{v} D p hp k
declarations.comment: part (3): the operation D · α = i_* i^* α of an effective Cartier divisor D = Z(s), with values in CH_k(X) = Z_k(X)/∼_rat of Stacks 0EQ6, i^* the refined Gysin homomorphism of parts (1) and (2) with every ingredient constructed, and i_* the pushforward along the closed immersion i : D → X of the cycle representing i^* α

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin
declarations.doc:
For a pair `(ℒ, s)` as in Stacks 0ER1, with `E = Z(s)` the vanishing locus
of `s` and `i : E → X` its closed immersion, the canonical map `i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) ⟶ Z_k(E)` on
cycles: the additive extension of the rule which sends the cycle of an integral closed subspace
`W ⊆ X` of δ-dimension `k + 1` to the cycle `[E ∩ W]_k` of the scheme-theoretic intersection
when `W ⊄ E`, as Stacks 0ER1(1)(a) prescribes, and to `0` when `W ⊆ E`, which is the requirement
of Stacks 0ER2.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin :
    CycleGroup D p (k + 1) →+ CycleGroup D ((vanishingLocus D p hp L s).1.ι ≫ p) k
declarations.comment:
the canonical map i^* : Z_{k+1}(X) → Z_k(D) on cycles of a pair (L, s) of
Definition 0ER1 with D = Z(s), constructed with clause (1)(a) of Stacks 0ER1 given by the cycle
[D ∩ W]_k of Stacks 0EE9 of the scheme-theoretic intersection D ∩ W = i^{-1}(W) and clause
(1)(b) by the zero cycle, which is the requirement i^*[W] = 0 for W ⊆ D of this remark; both
values are then proved of the map, in
canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin_integralCycle_of_not_le and
canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin_integralCycle_of_le, and determine it, in
gysinCycleMap_eq_canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin_integralCycle_of_le
declarations.doc:
The defining requirement for the pair of Stacks 0ER1: the canonical map on
cycles vanishes on the cycle of an integral closed subspace contained in `E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin_integralCycle_of_le
    {W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X}
    (hW : deltaDimension D p W = k + 1)
    (hWE : W.subspace ≤ (vanishingLocus D p hp L s).1) :
    canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin D p hp L s k (integralCycle D p (k + 1) W hW) = 0
declarations.comment:
the defining requirement i^*[W] = 0 for W ⊆ D, proved of the canonical map on
cycles of the pair of Definition 0ER1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin_integralCycle_of_not_le
declarations.doc:
On the cycle of an integral closed subspace not contained in `E` the canonical map is the
cycle `[E ∩ W]_k` of Stacks 0EE9 of the scheme-theoretic intersection, as Stacks 0ER1(1)(a)
prescribes.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin_integralCycle_of_not_le
    {W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X}
    (hW : deltaDimension D p W = k + 1)
    (hWE : ¬ W.subspace ≤ (vanishingLocus D p hp L s).1) :
    canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin D p hp L s k (integralCycle D p (k + 1) W hW) =
      gysinIntersectionCycle D p hp (vanishingLocus D p hp L s)
        (isGood_vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k W hW hWE
declarations.comment:
the remaining value i^*[W] = [D ∩ W]_k of Stacks 0ER1(1)(a), proved of the
canonical map on cycles, the right-hand side being the cycle of Stacks 0EE9 of the
scheme-theoretic intersection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.gysinCycleMap_eq_canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin
declarations.doc:
Canonicity for the pair of Stacks 0ER1: a component rule whose cycle map
takes the two prescribed values on the cycle of every integral closed subspace has the canonical
map of Stacks 0ER2 as its cycle map.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinCycleMap_eq_canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin
    (rule' : GysinComponentRule D p (vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k)
    (hle : ∀ (W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
      (hW : deltaDimension D p W = k + 1), W.subspace ≤ (vanishingLocus D p hp L s).1 →
      gysinCycleMap D p (vanishingLocus D p hp L s) (isGood_vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k rule'
        (integralCycle D p (k + 1) W hW) = 0)
    (hnotle : ∀ (W : IntegralClosedSubspace D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
      (hW : deltaDimension D p W = k + 1)
      (hWE : ¬ W.subspace ≤ (vanishingLocus D p hp L s).1),
      gysinCycleMap D p (vanishingLocus D p hp L s) (isGood_vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k rule'
          (integralCycle D p (k + 1) W hW) =
        gysinIntersectionCycle D p hp (vanishingLocus D p hp L s)
          (isGood_vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k W hW hWE) :
    gysinCycleMap D p (vanishingLocus D p hp L s) (isGood_vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k rule' =
      canonicalTrivialRestrictionGysin D p hp L s k
declarations.comment:
canonicity of the canonical map on cycles of the pair of Definition 0ER1: the
requirement i^*[W] = 0 for W ⊆ D, together with the value [D ∩ W]_k of Stacks 0ER1(1)(a) on the
remaining integral closed subspaces, determines the map on cycles

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackSheaf
declarations.doc: The inverse image `ℒ' = f^*ℒ` along `f` of a sheaf of modules `ℒ` on `X`.
declarations.statement: abbrev pullbackSheaf : Modules.{u, u} D.site D.base D.base_mem X' hp'.1
declarations.comment: the sheaf L' = f^*L of the construction, as the inverse image of Stacks 03LU

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackGlobalSection
declarations.doc: The inverse image `s' = f^*s` along `f` of a global section `s` of `ℒ`.
declarations.statement: abbrev pullbackGlobalSection : (pullbackSheaf D p hp p' hp' f L).sections
declarations.comment:
the section s' = f^*s of the construction, as the inverse image of a global
section along f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDivisor
declarations.doc:
The closed subspace `E' = X' ×_X E` of `X'`: the inverse image along `f` of the vanishing
locus `E = Z(s)`.
declarations.statement: def pullbackDivisor : ClosedSubspaces D.site D.base D.base_mem X'
declarations.comment:
the closed subspace D' = X' ×_X D of X', taken as the inverse image of D along f
in the sense of Stacks 083Q; its identification with Z(s') is
AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDivisor_eq_vanishingLocus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDivisor_comm
declarations.doc:
The diagram commutes: `g ≫ i = i' ≫ f`, for `i' : E' → X'` the inclusion of the closed
subspace `E'` and `i : E → X` the inclusion of the vanishing locus.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackDivisor_comm :
    pullbackDivisorProjection D p hp p' hp' f L s ≫ (vanishingLocus D p hp L s).1.ι =
      (pullbackDivisor D p hp p' hp' f L s).1.ι ≫ f.hom
declarations.comment: commutativity of the diagram, g ≫ i = i' ≫ f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDivisor_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The square with legs `g : E' → E` and `i' : E' → X'` is cartesian, which is the
identification `E' = X' ×_X E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackDivisor_isPullback :
    IsPullback (pullbackDivisorProjection D p hp p' hp' f L s)
      (pullbackDivisor D p hp p' hp' f L s).1.ι (vanishingLocus D p hp L s).1.ι f.hom
declarations.comment:
the identification D' = X' ×_X D, as the cartesian square with legs g : D' → D
and i' : D' → X'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackDivisor_eq_vanishingLocus
declarations.doc:
The identification `E' = Z(s')`: for an invertible `ℒ`, the inverse image along `f` of the
vanishing locus of `s` is the vanishing locus of the pulled-back section `s' = f^*s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackDivisor_eq_vanishingLocus (hL : IsInvertibleSheaf D p hp L) :
    pullbackDivisor D p hp p' hp' f L s =
      vanishingLocus D p' hp' (pullbackSheaf D p hp p' hp' f L)
        (pullbackGlobalSection D p hp p' hp' f L s)
declarations.comment: the identification D' = Z(s'), the vanishing locus of the pulled-back section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowClassCanonical_closedSubspaceCyclePushforward_gysinCycleMap_sectionGysinRule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ER4.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good, let `ℒ` be an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module with a global section `s`, and let `i : E → X` be the closed immersion of the
vanishing locus `E = Z(s)`. For every `(k+1)`-cycle `α` on `X`

`i_* i^* α = c₁(ℒ) ∩ α` in `CH_k(X)`.

Here `i^* α` is represented by the cycle `∑ n_W i^*[W]` of the refined Gysin map of Stacks 0ER1,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.gysinCycleMap` at the rule
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionGysinRule`; `i_*` is the pushforward of cycles along the closed
immersion; `c₁(ℒ) ∩ α` is represented by the cycle of Stacks 0EQJ,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernCapCycleMap` at the canonical component rule; and both classes
are taken in `CH_k(X)` of Stacks 0EQ6, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroupCanonical`, whose
rational equivalences are sums of principal divisors at the canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK.
As every class of `CH_{k+1}(X)` is the class of a cycle, this is the identity of the source on
representatives.

The difference of the two sides is, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedSubspaceCyclePushforward_gysinCycleMap_sub_firstChernCapCycleMap`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.firstChernCapCycleMap_eq_cycleFamilySum`, the locally finite sum of
the pushforwards of the cycles `n_W ([W ×_X Z(s)]_k - c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩ [W])` for `W ⊄ Z(s)` and
`n_W (c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩ [W] - c₁(ℒ|_W) ∩' [W])` for all `W`, the two cap products being formed with the
two regular meromorphic sections of `ℒ|_W` the two constructions choose. By Stacks 0EQF on `W`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedSubspaceCycle_preimage_vanishingLocus_eq_canonicalDivisorCycleAt`)
each of these is an integer multiple of the difference of the Weil divisors of two regular
meromorphic sections of `ℒ|_W`, hence a principal divisor at the canonical embeddings
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPrincipalDivisorCycleOfGood_zsmul_canonicalDivisorCycleAt_sub`).
declarations.statement:
theorem chowClassCanonical_closedSubspaceCyclePushforward_gysinCycleMap_sectionGysinRule (k : ℤ)
    (α : CycleGroup D p (k + 1)) :
    chowClassCanonical.{max (u + 1) v} D p hp k (closedSubspaceCyclePushforward D p hp
        (vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k (gysinCycleMap D p (vanishingLocus D p hp L s)
          (isGood_vanishingLocus D p hp L s) k (sectionGysinRule D p hp L s k hL) α)) =
      chowClassCanonical.{max (u + 1) v} D p hp k (firstChernCapCycleMap D p hp k
        (canonicalFirstChernRule D p hp L
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.ofAlgebraicGeometry _ _ _ hL) k) α)
declarations.comment: i_* i^* α = c₁(L) ∩ α in CH_k(X) for every (k+1)-cycle α, for X/B good, L invertible, s a global section and i : D = Z(s) → X: i^* α is the cycle of the refined Gysin map of Stacks 0ER1 (gysinCycleMap at sectionGysinRule), i_* the pushforward of cycles along the closed immersion, c₁(L) ∩ α the cycle of Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical choices, both classes taken in the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6 at the canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK (chowGroupCanonical); nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowClassCanonical_closedSubspaceCyclePushforward_gysinCycleMap_canonicalSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ER4, in particular.** In Situation 0EDT let `X/B` be good and let `D ⊆ X` be an
effective Cartier divisor, with invertible sheaf `𝒪_X(D)` and canonical section `1_D`
(Stacks 0841), whose vanishing locus `Z(1_D)` is `D` (Stacks 0847). For every `(k+1)`-cycle `α`
on `X`

`D · α = c₁(𝒪_X(D)) ∩ α` in `CH_k(X)`,

where `D · α = i_* i^* α` is the operation of Stacks 0ER1, part (3), for the pair
`(𝒪_X(D), 1_D)`: `i^* α` is represented by the cycle of the refined Gysin map,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.gysinCycleMap` at `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionGysinRule`, and `i_*`
is the pushforward of cycles along `i : Z(1_D) → X`. The cap product `c₁(𝒪_X(D)) ∩ α` is
represented by the cycle of Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical choices, and both classes are taken in
`CH_k(X)` of Stacks 0EQ6, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chowGroupCanonical`. This is
`chowClassCanonical_closedSubspaceCyclePushforward_gysinCycleMap_sectionGysinRule` for that
pair.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowClassCanonical_closedSubspaceCyclePushforward_gysinCycleMap_canonicalSection
    (Dv : ClosedSubspaces D.site D.base D.base_mem X)
    (hDv : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩ Dv) (k : ℤ)
    (α : CycleGroup D p (k + 1)) :
    chowClassCanonical.{max (u + 1) v} D p hp k (closedSubspaceCyclePushforward D p hp
        (vanishingLocus D p hp
          (associatedInvertibleSheaf D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩ Dv hDv)
          (canonicalSection D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩ Dv hDv)) k
        (gysinCycleMap D p (vanishingLocus D p hp
            (associatedInvertibleSheaf D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩ Dv hDv)
            (canonicalSection D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩ Dv hDv))
          (isGood_vanishingLocus D p hp _ _) k
          (sectionGysinRule D p hp
            (associatedInvertibleSheaf D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩ Dv hDv)
            (canonicalSection D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩ Dv hDv) k
            (associatedInvertibleSheaf_isInvertible D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩ Dv hDv))
          α)) =
      chowClassCanonical.{max (u + 1) v} D p hp k (firstChernCapCycleMap D p hp k
        (canonicalFirstChernRule D p hp
          (associatedInvertibleSheaf D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩ Dv hDv)
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible.ofAlgebraicGeometry _ _ _
            (associatedInvertibleSheaf_isInvertible D.site D.base D.base_mem ⟨X, hp.1⟩ Dv hDv))
          k) α)
declarations.comment: in particular: D · α = c₁(O_X(D)) ∩ α in CH_k(X) for an effective Cartier divisor D ⊆ X, with D · α = i_* i^* α of Stacks 0ER1 part (3) formed on cycles for the pair (O_X(D), 1_D) of Stacks 0847, whose vanishing locus is D, c₁(O_X(D)) ∩ α the cycle of Stacks 0EQJ at the canonical choices, and the classes taken in the Chow group of Stacks 0EQ6 at the canonical embeddings of Stacks 0ENK (chowGroupCanonical)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.gysinCycleMap_properPushforward_eq_of_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ER5.** In Situation 0EDT let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a proper morphism of good algebraic
spaces over `B`, let `(ℒ, s, i : E → X)` be as in Definition 0ER1, and form the diagram of
Remark 0ER3, with `E' = E ×_X X'`, `g : E' ⟶ E` and `i' : E' ⟶ X'`.  Then for every
`(k+1)`-cycle `α'` on `X'`

  `i^* f_* α' = g_* (i')^* α'`,

an identity of `k`-cycles on `E`, hence of classes in `CH_k(E)`.

`hsq` is the cartesian square of Remark 0ER3, which makes `E'` the scheme-theoretic base change
`E ×_X X'`.  Only quasi-compactness of `f` and of `g` is used, through Stacks 0ENZ; properness,
which the source assumes and from which it gets `g` proper by base change, is not needed for the
pushforwards themselves.

The single hypothesis beyond the setup is `cmp`, the comparison datum
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GysinProperPushforwardComparison`, whose docstring explains why it does
not follow from the other data.  Everything else — in particular the passage from the
prime cycles of the source's case analysis to an arbitrary cycle, which is not formal because a
cycle is an infinite formal sum — is proved.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinCycleMap_properPushforward_eq_of_comparison
    (cmp : GysinProperPushforwardComparison D p hp p' hp' f E hE E' hE' g k rule rule')
    (hsq : IsPullback g E'.1.ι E.1.ι f) (α' : CycleGroup D p' (k + 1)) :
    gysinCycleMap D p E hE k rule (properCyclePushforward D p' hp' p hp hfbase hfqc (k + 1) α') =
      properCyclePushforward D (E'.1.ι ≫ p') hE' (E.1.ι ≫ p) hE hgbase hgqc k
        (gysinCycleMap D p' E' hE' k rule' α')
declarations.comment:
i^*f_*α' = g_*(i')^*α' at the level of cycles, on the single carried input
GysinProperPushforwardComparison: the source's prime-cycle case analysis read coefficientwise at
the two component parameters of Definition 0ER1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sectionGysin_properPushforward_eq_chowGroupCanonicalProperPushforward
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0EDT let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a proper morphism of good algebraic spaces over `B`.
Let `(ℒ, s, i : D → X)` be as in Definition 0ER1: `ℒ` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, `s ∈ Γ(X, ℒ)`,
`D = Z(s)` its vanishing locus (here `E`, the letter `D` being the dimension situation) and `i`
the closed immersion. Form the diagram of Remark 0ER3

```
E' --i'--> X'
|          |
g          f
|          |
v          v
E  --i-->  X
```

with `ℒ' = f^*ℒ`, `s' = f^*s` and `E' = Z(s') = X' ×_X E`
