declarations.name: Stacks.ScaledPresentation.shortExact_ofBase_toFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ESU**, the second canonical short exact sequence of a local
presentation. For `A = f • B` with `f` a nonzerodivisor, writing `𝓕 = Rⁿ / A Rⁿ` and
`𝓕' = Rⁿ / B Rⁿ`, the sequence
```
0 → 𝓕' → 𝓕 → (R ⧸ (f))ⁿ → 0
```
is exact, and its submodule is the image of multiplication by `f` on `𝓕`, so that its quotient
is `Coker(f : 𝓕 → 𝓕)`; this is what makes the sequence canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_ofBase_toFree (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors R) :
    Function.Injective (ofBase B f) ∧
      LinearMap.range (ofBase B f) = LinearMap.ker (toFree B f) ∧
      Function.Surjective (toFree B f) ∧
      LinearMap.range (ofBase B f) = LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul R (Cokernel (f • B)) f)
declarations.comment: the canonical sequence 0 → ℱ' → ℱ → 𝒪_{D_n}^{⊕n} → 0 of a local presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.ScaledPresentation.exists_eq_smul_and_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ESU**, the local step of the induction. Let `𝓕 = R^{n} / A R^{n}` be
presented by a square matrix `A` with `n = m + 1` rows, with `A` injective, and suppose
`Fit_{n-1}(𝓕)` is generated by a nonzerodivisor `f`. Then `A = f A'` for a square matrix `A'`
which is again injective, so that `𝓕' = R^{n} / A' R^{n}` is presented by an exact sequence of
the same shape, and `𝓕` sits in the two canonical short exact sequences
```
0 → (R ⧸ (f))ⁿ → 𝓕 → 𝓕' → 0    and    0 → 𝓕' → 𝓕 → (R ⧸ (f))ⁿ → 0
```
whose free term is the structure sheaf of the divisor cut out by `f` — the divisor `D_n` of the
source — and whose submodule and quotient are `Ker(f : 𝓕 → 𝓕)` and `Coker(f : 𝓕 → 𝓕)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_eq_smul_and_shortExact {m : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors R)
    (hA : Function.Injective A.mulVecLin)
    (hfit : fittingIdeal (M := Cokernel A) (m : ℤ) = Ideal.span {f}) :
    ∃ A' : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R, A = f • A' ∧
      Function.Injective A'.mulVecLin ∧
      (Function.Injective (ofFree A' f) ∧
        LinearMap.range (ofFree A' f) = LinearMap.ker (toBase A' f) ∧
        Function.Surjective (toBase A' f) ∧
        LinearMap.range (ofFree A' f) =
          LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul R (Cokernel (f • A')) f)) ∧
      (Function.Injective (ofBase A' f) ∧
        LinearMap.range (ofBase A' f) = LinearMap.ker (toFree A' f) ∧
        Function.Surjective (toFree A' f) ∧
        LinearMap.range (ofBase A' f) =
          LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul R (Cokernel (f • A')) f))
declarations.comment: the local step: a principal Fit_{n-1} gives A = f A' and the two sequences

declarations.name: Stacks.ScaledPresentation.fittingIdeal_cokernel_eq_top_of_fittingIdeal_smul_eq_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ESU**: the entries of `A'` generate the unit ideal. If `𝓕` is presented
by `A = f A'` with `A'` square of size `n = m + 1` and `Fit_{n-1}(𝓕)` is generated by the
nonzerodivisor `f`, then `Fit_{n-1}(𝓕') = R` for `𝓕' = R^{n} / A' R^{n}`: the scaling identity
gives `(f) = (f) · Fit_{n-1}(𝓕')`, and `f` cancels. Since `Fit_{n-1}(𝓕')` is the ideal of
`1 × 1` minors of `A'`, this says the entries of `A'` generate the unit ideal, which is the
hypothesis under which the source invokes Algebra, Lemma 10.102.2 (tag 00MT) to drop the number
of generators by one.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdeal_cokernel_eq_top_of_fittingIdeal_smul_eq_span_singleton {m : ℕ}
    (A' : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors R)
    (hfit : fittingIdeal (M := Cokernel (f • A')) (m : ℤ) = Ideal.span {f}) :
    fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := Cokernel A') (m : ℤ) = ⊤
declarations.comment: the entries of A' generate the unit ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.ScaledPresentation.exists_cokernel_equiv_of_isUnit_entry
declarations.doc:
If some entry of a square matrix `A` of size `n = m + 1` is a unit, then the module `Rⁿ / A Rⁿ`
presented by `A` is the module presented by a square matrix of size `m`, which is again injective
if `A` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cokernel_equiv_of_isUnit_entry {m : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R) (a b : Fin (m + 1)) (hu : IsUnit (A a b)) :
    ∃ ψ : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) R,
      Nonempty (Cokernel A ≃ₗ[R] Cokernel ψ) ∧
        (Function.Injective A.mulVecLin → Function.Injective ψ.mulVecLin)
declarations.comment: dropping a generator: a unit relation entry gives a smaller presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.ScaledPresentation.exists_cover_cokernel_equiv_of_fittingIdeal_eq_top
declarations.doc:
Let `𝓕` be presented by a square matrix `A` of size `n = m + 1` with `Fit_{n-1}(𝓕) = R`. Then
the entries of `A` generate the unit ideal — so the basic opens `D(A i j)` cover `Spec R` — and
over each of those basic opens the module presented by `A` is the cokernel of a square matrix of
size `m`, and hence is generated by `m = n - 1` elements.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover_cokernel_equiv_of_fittingIdeal_eq_top {m : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R)
    (hfit : fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := Cokernel A) (m : ℤ) = ⊤) :
    Ideal.span (Set.range fun p : Fin (m + 1) × Fin (m + 1) => A p.1 p.2) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ p : Fin (m + 1) × Fin (m + 1),
        ∃ ψ : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) (Localization.Away (A p.1 p.2)),
          Nonempty (Cokernel (A.map (algebraMap R (Localization.Away (A p.1 p.2)))) ≃ₗ[
              Localization.Away (A p.1 p.2)] Cokernel ψ) ∧
            ∃ s : Fin m → Cokernel (A.map (algebraMap R (Localization.Away (A p.1 p.2)))),
              Submodule.span (Localization.Away (A p.1 p.2)) (Set.range s) = ⊤
declarations.comment: the Zariski cover on which ℱ' needs only n-1 generators

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_admissibleBlowup_isPerfectTorLEOne_ker_im_coker
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ESV.** Let `X` be a scheme and `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a homomorphism of perfect
`𝒪_X`-modules of Tor dimension at most one. Let `U ⊆ X` be a scheme-theoretically dense open with
`ℱ|_U = 0` and `𝒢|_U = 0`. Then there is a `U`-admissible blowup `b : X' ⟶ X` such that the
kernel, the image and the cokernel of `b^*φ` are perfect `𝒪_{X'}`-modules of Tor dimension at
most one.

The blowup is the blowup of `X` in the zeroth Fitting ideal of `Coker(φ)`. That cokernel is
finitely presented: it is the `H^0` of the cone `E` of `φ[0]` — the source's object `(ℱ ⟶ 𝒢)` of
`D(𝒪_X)`, which is perfect by tag 08CR and hence pseudo-coherent — and `E` has no cohomology in
positive degrees, so tag 08DN (2) applies. It vanishes over `U` because `ℱ` and `𝒢` do and
pullback is right exact, hence is finite locally free of rank `0` there. Tag 0ESN (1) therefore
makes the blowup `U`-admissible and tag 0ESN (4) makes `b^*Coker(φ)` perfect of Tor dimension at
most one; right exactness of pullback identifies that module with the cokernel of `b^*φ`. The
pullbacks `b^*ℱ` and `b^*𝒢` are perfect of Tor dimension at most one by tag 0ESS, after which the
image — the source's "kernel of the cokernel" — and then the kernel are
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfectTorLEOne_abelianImage_of_cokernel` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfectTorLEOne_kernel`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_admissibleBlowup_isPerfectTorLEOne_ker_im_coker {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (F G : OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsPerfectTorLEOne X F) (hG : IsPerfectTorLEOne X G)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense U)
    (_hFU : IsZero ((modulePullback U.ι.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj F))
    (hGU : IsZero ((modulePullback U.ι.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj G)) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (b : X' ⟶ X), Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U b ∧
      IsPerfectTorLEOne X' (kernel ((modulePullback b.toLRSHom.toShHom).map φ)) ∧
      IsPerfectTorLEOne X' (Abelian.image ((modulePullback b.toLRSHom.toShHom).map φ)) ∧
      IsPerfectTorLEOne X' (cokernel ((modulePullback b.toLRSHom.toShHom).map φ))
declarations.comment: the U-admissible blowup after which the kernel, image and cokernel of the pullback of φ are perfect of Tor dimension ≤ 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernClassArbitraryRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW.** The `n`-th Chern class `c_n(E) ∈ A^n(X)` of a finite locally free module of
not necessarily constant rank: the class which preserves the product decomposition of Chow
cohomology along the rank loci and whose component on `X_r` is `c_n(E|_{X_r})`.
declarations.statement: def chernClassArbitraryRank (n : ℕ) : chowCohomologyComponent C G sX (n : ℤ)
declarations.comment: chern_classes_arbitrary_rank; the constant-rank Chern classes the remark cites enter as a quantified family; the classes of Tag 0B7H themselves are Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClassBivariantClass

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rankLocusRestriction_chernClassArbitraryRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW.** The component of `c_n(E)` on the rank-`r` locus is `c_n(E|_{X_r})`, and is
zero when `r < n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rankLocusRestriction_chernClassArbitraryRank (n r : ℕ) :
    rankLocusRestriction C G sX E hgysO (n : ℤ)
        (chernClassArbitraryRank C G sX E hgysO hgysR hgysC cc n) r =
      rankLocusChernFamily C G sX E cc n r
declarations.comment: chern_classes_arbitrary_rank; the constant-rank Chern classes the remark cites enter as a quantified family; the classes of Tag 0B7H themselves are Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClassBivariantClass

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isChernClassBivariant_rankLocusRestriction_chernClassArbitraryRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW.** On the rank-`r` locus, `c_n(E)` acts by the already defined operation
`c_n(E|_{X_r}) ∩ -`: its component there satisfies the characterization of Stacks 0B7H for the
restricted module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isChernClassBivariant_rankLocusRestriction_chernClassArbitraryRank
    (hcc : ∀ (r : ℕ) (j : Fin (r + 1)),
      IsChernClassBivariant C ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (rankLocus E r).ι).obj E) r G (caps r) (hrank r) j (cc r j))
    (n r : ℕ) (h : n ≤ r) :
    IsChernClassBivariant C ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX)
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (rankLocus E r).ι).obj E) r G (caps r) (hrank r)
      ⟨n, Nat.lt_succ_of_le h⟩
      (rankLocusRestriction C G sX E hgysO (n : ℤ)
        (chernClassArbitraryRank C G sX E hgysO hgysR hgysC cc n) r)
declarations.comment: chern_classes_arbitrary_rank; the constant-rank Chern classes the remark cites enter as a quantified family; the classes of Tag 0B7H themselves are Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClassBivariantClass

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.eq_chernClassArbitraryRank_of_rankLocusRestriction_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW.** `c_n(E)` is the only class with these components, so the definition does
not depend on the way the family is assembled.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_chernClassArbitraryRank_of_rankLocusRestriction_eq (n : ℕ)
    {c : chowCohomologyComponent C G sX (n : ℤ)}
    (h : ∀ r : ℕ, rankLocusRestriction C G sX E hgysO (n : ℤ) c r =
      rankLocusChernFamily C G sX E cc n r) :
    c = chernClassArbitraryRank C G sX E hgysO hgysR hgysC cc n
declarations.comment: chern_classes_arbitrary_rank; the constant-rank Chern classes the remark cites enter as a quantified family; the classes of Tag 0B7H themselves are Stacks.Chow.GenuineChern.chernClassBivariantClass

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_infinite_chernClassOfLocallyFree_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**The Chern classes of a module of non-constant rank can be nonzero in infinitely many
degrees.** There are a base situation `(S, δ)` of chapter 42, a scheme `X`
locally of finite type over `S` and a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module `ℰ` such that
`c_p(ℰ) ≠ 0` for infinitely many `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_infinite_chernClassOfLocallyFree_ne_zero :
    ∃ (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (X : Scheme.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ C.S) (_ : LocallyOfFiniteType sX)
      (E : X.Modules) (_ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E),
      {p : ℕ | SectionZeroScheme.chernClassOfLocallyFree E C sX p ≠ 0}.Infinite
declarations.comment: it may happen that c_p(E) is nonzero for infinitely many p

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.SectionZeroScheme.rankLocusChowCohomologyEquivOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW, the decomposition of Chow cohomology.** `A^p(X) = ∏_{r ≥ 0} A^p(X_r)` for the
decomposition of `X` by the rank of `ℰ`: restriction to the rank loci is an isomorphism onto the
product (Stacks 0FDZ).
declarations.comment: A^p(X) = ∏_r A^p(X_r) for the rank decomposition X = ∐ X_r of a finite locally free module (via 0FDZ), at the Gysin system of the first Chern class rule, nothing assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.SectionZeroScheme.idRule_chernClassOfLocallyFree_of_rank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW, the operation of `c_p(ℰ)`.** On a test scheme `f : X' ⟶ X` along which `f^*ℰ`
has constant rank `r` — for instance the part `X'_r` of any test scheme lying over `X_r` — the
class `c_p(ℰ)` acts by the already defined operation `c_p(f^*ℰ) ∩ -` of Stacks 0B7H, which is zero
when `p > r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem idRule_chernClassOfLocallyFree_of_rank (r p : ℕ) {X' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj E) r] (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (f ≫ sX) k) :
    (chernClassOfLocallyFree E C sX p).idRule C sX (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) f k α =
      if h : p ≤ r then
        GenuineChern.chernCap C r (f ≫ sX) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj E) k
          ⟨p, Nat.lt_succ_of_le h⟩ α
      else 0
declarations.comment: c_p(E) acts on the factors X'_r by the already defined operations c_p(E|_{X'_r}) ∩ -: on every test scheme along which E has constant rank r the operation of c_p(E) is the cap product c_p(f^*E) ∩ - of 0B7H (zero for p > r)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.SectionZeroScheme.chowGroupRestrict_idRule_chernClassOfLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW, explicitly.** For a test scheme `g : X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type, with the
induced decomposition `X' = ∐ X'_r`, `X'_r = g⁻¹(X_r)`, the class `c_p(ℰ)` preserves the
decomposition `CH_*(X') = ∏_r CH_*(X'_r)` and acts on the factor `CH_*(X'_r)` by the already
defined operation `c_p(ℰ|_{X'_r}) ∩ -` of Stacks 0B7H (zero for `p > r`): restricting
`c_p(ℰ) ∩ α` to `X'_r` gives `c_p(ℰ|_{X'_r}) ∩ (α|_{X'_r})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowGroupRestrict_idRule_chernClassOfLocallyFree (r p : ℕ) {X' : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : X' ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ sX) k) :
    haveI := isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback_preimage_rankLocus E g r
    chowGroupRestrict C (g ≫ sX) (((g ⁻¹ᵁ rankLocus E r).ι ≫ g) ≫ sX) (g ⁻¹ᵁ rankLocus E r).ι
        (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm ((k : ℤ) - (p : ℤ))
        ((chernClassOfLocallyFree E C sX p).idRule C sX (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) g k α) =
      if h : p ≤ r then
        GenuineChern.chernCap C r (((g ⁻¹ᵁ rankLocus E r).ι ≫ g) ≫ sX)
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((g ⁻¹ᵁ rankLocus E r).ι ≫ g)).obj E) k
          ⟨p, Nat.lt_succ_of_le h⟩
          (chowGroupRestrict C (g ≫ sX) (((g ⁻¹ᵁ rankLocus E r).ι ≫ g) ≫ sX)
            (g ⁻¹ᵁ rankLocus E r).ι (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm k α)
      else 0
declarations.comment: explicit form: for every X' → X locally of finite type, c_p(E) preserves the decomposition CH_*(X') = ∏_r CH_*(X'_r) and acts on the factor X'_r by c_p(E|_{X'_r}) ∩ -

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.SectionZeroScheme.chernClassOfLocallyFree_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW, the Chern classes of a module of non-constant rank.** `c_p(ℰ) ∈ A^p(X)` is the
class whose restriction to every rank locus `X_r` is the Chern class `c_p(ℰ|_{X_r})` of
Stacks 0B7H (zero when `p > r`), and it is the only such class: under
`A^p(X) = ∏_r A^p(X_r)` it is the product of the classes `c_p(ℰ|_{X_r})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernClassOfLocallyFree_spec (p : ℕ) :
    (∀ r : ℕ, haveI := isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback_rankLocus E r
      chowCohomologyRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (rankLocus E r).ι (p : ℤ)
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
          (chernClassOfLocallyFree E C sX p) =
        if h : p ≤ r then
          GenuineChern.chernClass C ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX)
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (rankLocus E r).ι).obj E) r ⟨p, Nat.lt_succ_of_le h⟩
        else 0) ∧
    ∀ c : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (p : ℤ),
      (∀ r : ℕ, haveI := isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback_rankLocus E r
        chowCohomologyRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (rankLocus E r).ι (p : ℤ)
            (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) c =
          if h : p ≤ r then
            GenuineChern.chernClass C ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX)
              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (rankLocus E r).ι).obj E) r ⟨p, Nat.lt_succ_of_le h⟩
          else 0) →
      c = chernClassOfLocallyFree E C sX p
declarations.comment: c_p(E) ∈ A^p(X) as the product of the classes c_p(E|_{X_r}) ∈ A^p(X_r) of 0B7H under A^p(X) = ∏_r A^p(X_r): existence and uniqueness of the class with these restrictions

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.SectionZeroScheme.totalChernClassCompleted
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW, the total Chern class.** The total Chern class
`c(ℰ) = c_0(ℰ) + c_1(ℰ) + c_2(ℰ) + … ∈ A^*(X)^∧` of a finite locally free module of arbitrary
rank: the element of the completed bivariant group of Stacks 0FE0 whose degree `p` part is the
Chern class `c_p(ℰ)` for `p ≥ 0` (and zero for `p < 0`).
declarations.comment: the total Chern class c(E) = c_0(E) + c_1(E) + ... as an element of the completed bivariant cohomology ring A^*(X)^∧ of 0FE0

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.SectionZeroScheme.rankClassOfLocallyFree_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW, the rank as the unique class with the given restrictions.** `r(ℰ)` restricts
to `r · 1` on each rank locus `X_r`, and it is the only class of `A^0(X)` doing so.
declarations.statement:
theorem rankClassOfLocallyFree_spec :
    (∀ r : ℕ, chowCohomologyRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (rankLocus E r).ι 0
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) (rankClassOfLocallyFree C sX E) =
      (r : ℤ) • bivariantIdentityClassOfInvertible C ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX)) ∧
    ∀ c : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX 0,
      (∀ r : ℕ, chowCohomologyRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (rankLocus E r).ι 0
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) c =
        (r : ℤ) • bivariantIdentityClassOfInvertible C ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX)) →
      c = rankClassOfLocallyFree C sX E
declarations.comment: the rank r(E) ∈ A^0(X): the class whose restriction to each X_r is r times the unit of A^0(X_r), existence and uniqueness

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.SectionZeroScheme.idRule_rankClassOfLocallyFree_of_rank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW, the operation of the rank.** On a test scheme `f : X' ⟶ X` along which
`f^*ℰ` has constant rank `r` — for instance the part `X'_r` of any test scheme lying over `X_r` —
the class `r(ℰ)` acts as multiplication by `r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem idRule_rankClassOfLocallyFree_of_rank (r : ℕ) {X' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj E) r] (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (f ≫ sX) k) :
    (rankClassOfLocallyFree C sX E).idRule C sX (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) f k α =
      (r : ℤ) • identityCapRule C sX f k α
declarations.comment: the rank r(E) ∈ A^0(X) is the bivariant operation sending (α_r) to (r α_r): on every test scheme along which E has constant rank r it acts as multiplication by r

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.SectionZeroScheme.chowGroupRestrict_idRule_rankClassOfLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW, the rank explicitly.** For a test scheme `g : X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type,
with the induced decomposition `X' = ∐ X'_r`, the class `r(ℰ)` sends `(α_r) ∈ ∏_r CH_*(X'_r)` to
`(r α_r)`: restricting `r(ℰ) ∩ α` to `X'_r` gives `r · (α|_{X'_r})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chowGroupRestrict_idRule_rankClassOfLocallyFree (r : ℕ) {X' : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : X' ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ) (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ sX) k) :
    chowGroupRestrict C (g ≫ sX) (((g ⁻¹ᵁ rankLocus E r).ι ≫ g) ≫ sX) (g ⁻¹ᵁ rankLocus E r).ι
        (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm (k - 0)
        ((rankClassOfLocallyFree C sX E).idRule C sX (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) g k α) ≍
      (r : ℤ) • chowGroupRestrict C (g ≫ sX) (((g ⁻¹ᵁ rankLocus E r).ι ≫ g) ≫ sX)
        (g ⁻¹ᵁ rankLocus E r).ι (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm k α
declarations.comment: explicit form of the rank: r(E) is the bivariant operation sending (α_r) ∈ ∏_r CH_*(X'_r) to (r α_r), for every X' → X locally of finite type

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.SectionZeroScheme.chernClassOfLocallyFree_mem_center
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW, centrality of the Chern classes.** For a finite locally free module `ℰ` of
arbitrary rank, `c_p(ℰ) ∈ A^p(X)` lies in the center of the Chow cohomology ring `A^*(X)` of
Stacks 0B7E: on each rank locus it restricts to a Chern class of Stacks 0B7H, which is central by
Stacks 02UA, or to zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernClassOfLocallyFree_mem_center (p : ℕ) :
    DirectSum.of (fun q : ℤ ↦ chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX q) (p : ℤ)
        (chernClassOfLocallyFree E C sX p) ∈
      Subring.center (chowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX)
declarations.comment: c_p(E) is in the center of A^*(X), for E of non-constant rank

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.SectionZeroScheme.rankClassOfLocallyFree_mem_center
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW, centrality of the rank.** `r(ℰ) ∈ A^0(X)` lies in the center of `A^*(X)`: on
each rank locus `X_r` it restricts to `r · 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rankClassOfLocallyFree_mem_center :
    DirectSum.of (fun q : ℤ ↦ chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX q) 0
        (rankClassOfLocallyFree C sX E) ∈
      Subring.center (chowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX)
declarations.comment: r(E) is in the center of A^*(X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rankBivariantClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW.** The rank `r(E) ∈ A^0(X)` of a finite locally free module whose rank need not
be constant: the bivariant class which preserves the product decomposition of the Chow groups
along the rank loci and acts on the rank-`r` factor by multiplication by `r`.
declarations.statement: def rankBivariantClass : chowCohomologyComponent C G sX 0
declarations.comment: rank_bivariant_class; the flat transport axiom of Stacks 0B76 is proved here, and only the Gysin transport axiom is carried, as for the library's own first Chern class at Tag 0FDW

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rankLocusRestriction_rankBivariantClass
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0ESW.** The component of `r(E)` on the rank-`r` locus is `r` times the unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem rankLocusRestriction_rankBivariantClass (r : ℕ) :
    rankLocusRestriction C G sX E hgysO 0
        (rankBivariantClass C G sX E hgysO hgysR hgysC hgysin) r =
      (r : ℤ) • chowCohomologyOne C ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX) G
        (transportFlatNaturality_rankLocus C sX E r) (hgysin r)
declarations.comment: rank_bivariant_class; the flat transport axiom of Stacks 0B76 is proved here, and only the Gysin transport axiom is carried, as for the library's own first Chern class at Tag 0FDW

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rankBivariantClass_cap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESW.** `r(E)` sends `(α_r)` to `(r α_r)`: on a test scheme over the rank-`r` locus,
capping with `r(E)` is multiplication by `r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rankBivariantClass_cap (r : ℕ) {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : T ⟶ (rankLocus E r : Scheme.{u})) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX)) k) :
    chowPushforwardOfIso C
        (pullback.fst (𝟙 (rankLocus E r : Scheme.{u})) g ≫ ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX))
        (g ≫ ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX)) (identityBaseChangeIso g).hom
        (identityBaseChangeIso_hom_comp_base C ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX) g) (k - 0)
        ((rankLocusRestriction C G sX E hgysO 0
          (rankBivariantClass C G sX E hgysO hgysR hgysC hgysin) r).cap g k α) =
      (r : ℤ) • chowGroupDegreeEquiv C (g ≫ ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX))
        (by omega : k = k - 0) α
declarations.comment: rank_bivariant_class; the flat transport axiom of Stacks 0B76 is proved here, and only the Gysin transport axiom is carried, as for the library's own first Chern class at Tag 0FDW

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.eq_rankBivariantClass_of_rankLocusRestriction_eq
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0ESW.** `r(E)` is the only degree-zero class with those components.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_rankBivariantClass_of_rankLocusRestriction_eq
    {c : chowCohomologyComponent C G sX 0}
    (h : ∀ r : ℕ, rankLocusRestriction C G sX E hgysO 0 c r =
      (r : ℤ) • chowCohomologyOne C ((rankLocus E r).ι ≫ sX) G
        (transportFlatNaturality_rankLocus C sX E r) (hgysin r)) :
    c = rankBivariantClass C G sX E hgysO hgysR hgysC hgysin
declarations.comment: rank_bivariant_class; the flat transport axiom of Stacks 0B76 is proved here, and only the Gysin transport axiom is carried, as for the library's own first Chern class at Tag 0FDW

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.rankDecomposition
declarations.doc:
The rank of a finite locally free module `E` on a scheme `X` is locally constant, the loci
`X_r` where the rank is `r` are open and closed, pairwise disjoint and cover `X`, and `E` is free
of rank `r` on a neighbourhood of every point of `X_r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rankDecomposition :
    IsLocallyConstant ⇑(finiteLocallyFreeRank E) ∧
      (∀ r : ℕ, IsClopen (rankStratum E r : Set X)) ∧
      (∀ r s : ℕ, r ≠ s → Disjoint (rankStratum E r) (rankStratum E s)) ∧
      (⨆ r : ℕ, rankStratum E r) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (x : X), x ∈ rankStratum E r →
        ∃ (V : X.Opens) (_ : x ∈ V) (_ : V ≤ rankStratum E r) (I : Type u),
          Nonempty (I ≃ Fin r) ∧
            Nonempty (SheafOfModules.free.{u} I ≅ (toRingSheafModule E).over V)
declarations.comment: the decomposition X = ∐ X_r of a scheme by the rank of a finite locally free module: the rank is locally constant, the loci are open and closed, pairwise disjoint and covering, and the module is free of rank r near each point of X_r. The Chern classes c_p(E) ∈ A^p(X) of a module of non-constant rank, the total Chern class in the completed bivariant group, the rank class r(E) ∈ A^0(X) and the centrality of c_p(E) and r(E) in A^*(X) are not covered

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.fullChernCharacter
declarations.doc:
The full Chern character `ch(E) = (ch_0(E), ch_1(E), ch_2(E), …)` of a finite locally free
module whose rank need not be constant, as an element of the product `∏_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐)`.
declarations.statement: def fullChernCharacter : fullRationalChowCohomology C G sX
declarations.comment: the full Chern character of a finite locally free module of not necessarily constant rank as an element of the product ∏_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐), assembled over the rank loci from the constant-rank power sums P_p(c_1(E|X_r), …, c_p(E|X_r)) that the remark recalls from Tags 0ESW, 0FA7 and 0F9C; those are carried as a quantified family, the multiplication of A^*(X) — composition of bivariant classes, Tag 0FE0 — not being constructed in this library

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalCap_chernCharacterComponent_eq_zero_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
declarations.doc:
For `d < p` the class `ch_p(E)` caps every rational Chow class of a test scheme of dimension
at most `d` to zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalCap_chernCharacterComponent_eq_zero_of_topologicalKrullDim_le (d p : ℕ)
    (hp : d < p) {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (hT : topologicalKrullDim T ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ sX) k) :
    rationalCap C G sX (p : ℤ) g k α
      (chernCharacterComponent C G sX E hgysO hgysR hgysC P p) = 0
declarations.comment: the vanishing of the components ch_p(E) for p above the dimension d of X, by Tag 0FDX, read on the test schemes of dimension at most d as the library's form of that tag allows; the splitting principle of the source is not needed, that form being a delta-dimension count, and neither is quasi-compactness of X

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gradedChernCharacter_eq_fullChernCharacter
declarations.doc:
If the components of the Chern character vanish in the degrees above `d`, then the full
Chern character lies in `A^*(X) ⊗ 𝐐`: it is the image of the finite sum `⊕_{p ≤ d} ch_p(E)` under
the inclusion of the direct sum into the product `∏_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gradedChernCharacter_eq_fullChernCharacter (d : ℕ)
    (hvan : ∀ p : ℕ, d < p →
      chernCharacterComponent C G sX E hgysO hgysR hgysC P p = 0) :
    (fun p : ℕ ↦ gradedChernCharacter C G sX E hgysO hgysR hgysC P d p) =
      fullChernCharacter C G sX E hgysO hgysR hgysC P
declarations.comment: the membership ch(E) ∈ A^*(X) ⊗ 𝐐 for X of dimension at most d: the full Chern character is the image of the finite sum ⊕_{p ≤ d} ch_p(E). The vanishing of the components above d is a hypothesis: the library's Tag 0FDX reaches only the test schemes of dimension at most d, and by Tag 02UC the remaining ones are what the equality ch_p(E) = 0 in A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐 needs. Quasi-compactness of X is not assumed, being unused by the library's form of Tag 0FDX

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacter_apply_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESX, the Chern character of a module of arbitrary rank.** For a finite locally free
module `ℰ` whose rank need not be constant, the Chern character
`ch(ℰ) = (ch_0(ℰ), ch_1(ℰ), …) ∈ ∏_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐)` (`Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacter`) has
components `ch_p(ℰ) = P_p(ℰ)/p!`, where `P_p(ℰ) ∈ A^p(X)` is the power sum of Stacks 0F9B (with
`P_0 = r`) evaluated at the rank `r(ℰ)` and the Chern classes `c_i(ℰ)` of Stacks 0ESW, as in
Stacks 0FA7.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleChernCharacter_apply_eq (p : ℕ) :
    moduleChernCharacter C sX E p =
      ((Nat.factorial p : ℚ)⁻¹) ⊗ₜ[ℤ]
        chernPolynomialComponent C sX E p (powerSumChernPolynomial p)
declarations.comment: the components ch_p(E) = P_p(E)/p! ∈ A^p(X) ⊗ Q of the Chern character of a finite locally free module of not necessarily constant rank, with P_p of 0F9B evaluated at the rank and Chern classes of 0ESW (0FA7), so that ch(E) ∈ ∏_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(X) ⊗ Q)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_gradedRationalChowCohomology_eq_moduleChernCharacter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESX, the finite-dimensional case.** If `X` is quasi-compact and `dim X < ∞`, then
`ch(ℰ) ∈ A^*(X) ⊗ 𝐐`: the full Chern character is the image of an element of the direct sum
`⊕_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐)` under its inclusion into the product.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_gradedRationalChowCohomology_eq_moduleChernCharacter [CompactSpace X]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X < ⊤) :
    ∃ y : gradedRationalChowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX,
      ∀ p : ℕ, y p = moduleChernCharacter C sX E p
declarations.comment: for X quasi-compact with dim(X) < ∞, ch(E) ∈ A^*(X) ⊗ Q: the full Chern character is the image of an element of ⊕_p (A^p(X) ⊗ Q)

registrations.name: Stacks.Chow.moduleChernCharacter
registrations.comment: the full Chern character ch(E) ∈ ∏_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(X) ⊗ Q) of a finite locally free module of not necessarily constant rank, built from the genuine classes of 0B7H on the rank loci

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.totalChernClassComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ.** The total Chern class `c(ℰ^•) = ∏_n c(ℰ^n)^{(-1)^n}` of a complex of finite
locally free modules bounded in the degrees `a, …, a + k`, as an element of the group of series
with constant term `1` inside `∏_{p ≥ 0} A^p(X)`; the negative exponents are the formal inverses
of Stacks 0FEL. No rank is assumed constant.
declarations.statement:
def totalChernClassComplex (D : TotalChernClassSeries C Gy sX R)
    (P : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (a : ℤ) (k : ℕ) : UnitalSeries R
declarations.comment: the total Chern class c(E^bullet) of a complex of finite locally free modules bounded in a range of degrees, with no constant-rank hypothesis; the total Chern class of a module, Tag 0B7H, and the multiplication of A^*(X), Tag 0FE0, are carried as the parameters R and D, whose field ch_shortExact is the Whitney sum formula of Tag 02UI, exactly as in Stacks.Chow.chernClassKGroup; the locally bounded case is not delivered

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.totalChernClassComplex_eq_prod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ.** The total Chern class of a complex is the alternating product
`∏_n c(ℰ^n)^{(-1)^n}` of the total Chern classes of its terms, which is the formula of the
source.
declarations.statement:
theorem totalChernClassComplex_eq_prod (D : TotalChernClassSeries C Gy sX R)
    (P : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (a : ℤ) (k : ℕ) :
    totalChernClassComplex C Gy sX D P a k =
      ∏ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
        (⟨D.ch (P.X (a + (i : ℤ))), D.ch_apply_zero (P.X (a + (i : ℤ)))⟩ : UnitalSeries R) ^
          ((a + (i : ℤ)).negOnePow : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the defining formula c(E^bullet) = prod_n c(E^n)^{(-1)^n} of the section, the inverses being the formal inverses of Tag 0FEL

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.totalChernClassComplex_eq_of_cohomologyComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ.** The total Chern class of a complex of finite locally free modules depends
only on the cohomology modules of the complex. Two complexes representing the same object of
`D(𝒪_X)` have the same cohomology modules, and this is the form in which the independence of the
representative is delivered here; see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem totalChernClassComplex_eq_of_cohomologyComparison (D : TotalChernClassSeries C Gy sX R)
    {P Q : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ} {a : ℤ} {k : ℕ}
    (S : BoundedComplexSplitting X P a k) (T : BoundedComplexSplitting X Q a k)
    (cmp : ComplexCohomologyComparison S T) :
    totalChernClassComplex C Gy sX D P a k = totalChernClassComplex C Gy sX D Q a k
declarations.comment: the independence of the representative for the total Chern class. CARRIED: the degreewise data the source's proof extracts from an isomorphism in D(O_X) -- finite local freeness of the kernels and images (Tag 0F8J), the identification of the cohomology modules, and Schanuel's lemma (Tag 00O3) -- together with the reductions of Tags 02UC and 0ESR

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.powerSumClassComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ.** The class `P_p(ℰ^•) = ∑_n (-1)^n P_p(ℰ^n) ∈ A^p(X)` of a complex of finite
locally free modules bounded in the degrees `a, …, a + k`. No rank is assumed constant.
declarations.statement:
def powerSumClassComplex (W : PowerSumClassRule C Gy sX) (P : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (a : ℤ) (k : ℕ) (p : ℕ) : chowCohomologyComponent C Gy sX (p : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the class P_p(E^bullet) of a complex of finite locally free modules bounded in a range of degrees, with no constant-rank hypothesis; the constant-rank power sums P_p(E) of Tag 0F9B and their additivity, Tag 0F9C, are carried as the parameter W, as in Stacks.Chow.powerSumClassArbitraryRank; the locally bounded case is not delivered

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.powerSumClassComplex_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ.** The class `P_p` of a complex is the alternating sum of the classes `P_p` of
its terms, which is the formula of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem powerSumClassComplex_eq_sum (W : PowerSumClassRule C Gy sX)
    (P : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (a : ℤ) (k : ℕ) (p : ℕ) :
    powerSumClassComplex C Gy sX W P a k p =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
        ((a + (i : ℤ)).negOnePow : ℤ) • W.cls (P.X (a + (i : ℤ))) p
declarations.comment: the defining formula P_p(E^bullet) = sum_n (-1)^n P_p(E^n) of the section

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.powerSumClassComplex_eq_of_cohomologyComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ.** The class `P_p` of a complex of finite locally free modules depends only on
the cohomology modules of the complex. Two complexes representing the same object of `D(𝒪_X)`
have the same cohomology modules, and this is the form in which the independence of the
representative is delivered here; see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem powerSumClassComplex_eq_of_cohomologyComparison (W : PowerSumClassRule C Gy sX)
    {P Q : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ} {a : ℤ} {k : ℕ}
    (S : BoundedComplexSplitting X P a k) (T : BoundedComplexSplitting X Q a k)
    (cmp : ComplexCohomologyComparison S T) (p : ℕ) :
    powerSumClassComplex C Gy sX W P a k p = powerSumClassComplex C Gy sX W Q a k p
declarations.comment: the independence of the representative for P_p. CARRIED: the degreewise data the source's proof extracts from an isomorphism in D(O_X) -- finite local freeness of the kernels and images (Tag 0F8J), the identification of the cohomology modules, and Schanuel's lemma (Tag 00O3) -- together with the reductions of Tags 02UC and 0ESR

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterComplexComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ.** The degree-`p` component `ch_p(ℰ^•) = P_p(ℰ^•)/p! ∈ A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐` of the Chern
character of a complex of finite locally free modules bounded in the degrees `a, …, a + k`.
declarations.comment: the Chern character component ch_p(E^bullet) = P_p(E^bullet)/p! of a complex of finite locally free modules bounded in a range of degrees, with no constant-rank hypothesis; the constant-rank power sums and their additivity, Tag 0F9C, are carried as the parameter W; the locally bounded case is not delivered

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterComplexComponent_eq_of_cohomologyComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ.** The Chern character of a complex of finite locally free modules depends only
on the cohomology modules of the complex. Two complexes representing the same object of `D(𝒪_X)`
have the same cohomology modules, and this is the form in which the independence of the
representative is delivered here; see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernCharacterComplexComponent_eq_of_cohomologyComparison (W : PowerSumClassRule C Gy sX)
    {P Q : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ} {a : ℤ} {k : ℕ}
    (S : BoundedComplexSplitting X P a k) (T : BoundedComplexSplitting X Q a k)
    (cmp : ComplexCohomologyComparison S T) (p : ℕ) :
    chernCharacterComplexComponent C Gy sX W P a k p =
      chernCharacterComplexComponent C Gy sX W Q a k p
declarations.comment: the independence of the representative for the Chern character. CARRIED: the degreewise data the source's proof extracts from an isomorphism in D(O_X) -- finite local freeness of the kernels and images (Tag 0F8J), the identification of the cohomology modules, and Schanuel's lemma (Tag 00O3) -- together with the reductions of Tags 02UC and 0ESR

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.totalChernClassComplexLocallyBounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ.** The total Chern class `c(ℰ^•) = ∏_n c(ℰ^n)^{(-1)^n}` of a *locally bounded*
complex of finite locally free modules on a quasi-compact scheme, as an element of the group of
series with constant term `1` inside `∏_{p ≥ 0} A^p(X)`. Such a complex vanishes outside a single
global window of degrees, and the class is the bounded-window class of Stacks 0ESZ on one.
declarations.comment: the locally bounded case, on a quasi-compact scheme: the total Chern class of a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, which the bounded-window construction of this tag in Stacks.Chow.ChernClassComplex does not deliver; the total Chern class of a module (Tag 0B7H) and the multiplication of A^*(X) (Tag 0FE0) are carried as the parameters R and D exactly as there

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.powerSumClassComplexLocallyBounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ.** The class `P_p(ℰ^•) = ∑_n (-1)^n P_p(ℰ^n) ∈ A^p(X)` of a *locally bounded*
complex of finite locally free modules on a quasi-compact scheme. Such a complex vanishes outside
a single global window of degrees, and the class is the bounded-window class of Stacks 0ESZ on
one.
declarations.comment: the locally bounded case, on a quasi-compact scheme: the class P_p of a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, which the bounded-window construction of this tag in Stacks.Chow.ChernClassComplex does not deliver; the constant-rank power sums P_p(E) of Tag 0F9B and their additivity, Tag 0F9C, are carried as the parameter W exactly as there

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.complexChern
declarations.doc:
**The total Chern class of a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules.** On the
rank locus `Y_ρ` the complex is bounded with constant ranks `ρ`, and there the class is
`c(P|_{Y_ρ}) = ∏_n c(P^n|_{Y_ρ})^{(-1)^n}`; these classes are assembled into a total class on `Y`
by Stacks 0FDZ in every degree.
declarations.statement: def complexChern : TotalChowClass C sY
declarations.comment: the class c(E^bullet) in prod_{p >= 0} A^p(Y) of a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules -- the generalization the lemma refers to: no rank is assumed constant, the complex is only locally bounded, and Y is not assumed quasi-compact

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.complexPowerSumComponent
declarations.doc:
**The class `P_p(ℰ^•) ∈ A^p(Y)`**, the degree-`p` component of
`Stacks.Chow.complexPowerSum`.
declarations.statement:
def complexPowerSumComponent (p : ℕ) :
    chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sY (p : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the class P_p(E^bullet) in A^p(Y) of a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, as the universal power sum of Tag 0F9B applied to c(E^bullet) -- the degree-zero member being the alternating rank class

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.complexChernCharacter
declarations.doc:
**The Chern character `ch(ℰ^•) ∈ ∏_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(Y) ⊗ 𝐐)` of a locally bounded complex of
finite locally free modules**, the family of its components.
declarations.statement: def complexChernCharacter : fullRationalChowCohomology C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sY
declarations.comment: the class ch(E^bullet) in prod_{p >= 0} (A^p(Y) tensor Q) of a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, componentwise as ch_p = P_p/p! as the source reads it

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.complexPowerSumComponent_eq_of_iso
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0ESZ for `P_p ∈ A^p(Y)`.**
declarations.statement:
theorem complexPowerSumComponent_eq_of_iso
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P') (p : ℕ) :
    complexPowerSumComponent C sY hP p = complexPowerSumComponent C sY hP' p
declarations.comment: the independence of the choice of the complex for P_p(E^bullet) in A^p(Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.complexChernCharacter_eq_of_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ for the Chern character**, as the family
`ch(ℰ^•) ∈ ∏_{p ≥ 0} (A^p(Y) ⊗ 𝐐)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem complexChernCharacter_eq_of_iso
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P') :
    complexChernCharacter C sY hP = complexChernCharacter C sY hP'
declarations.comment: the independence of the choice of the complex for ch(E^bullet)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.complexChern_eq_of_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ESZ for the total Chern class.** Let `Y` be locally of finite type over the base of
chapter 42 and let `P`, `P'` be locally bounded complexes of finite locally free `𝒪_Y`-modules
representing the same object of `D(𝒪_Y)`. Then their total Chern classes
`c(P), c(P') ∈ ∏_{p ≥ 0} A^p(Y)` are equal.

The proof is the source's. By Stacks 02UC it suffices to compare the operations of the two
classes on the fundamental class of a proper birational modification of every integral scheme `T`
locally of finite type over `Y` (`Stacks.Chow.TotalChowClass.eq_of_op_fundamentalChowClass_eq`).
Over `T` the pulled-back complexes are bounded with constant ranks, after the admissible blowup of
Stacks 0ESR the cohomology of the pulled-back object is perfect of Tor dimension at most one, and
there the two classes agree by Stacks 0F8J, Schanuel's lemma and the Whitney sum formula
(`Stacks.Chow.exists_isBirational_op_complexChern_eq_of_iso`).
declarations.statement:
theorem complexChern_eq_of_iso (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P') :
    complexChern C sY hP = complexChern C sY hP'
declarations.comment: the independence of the choice of the complex for c(E^bullet), at the hypotheses of the source: two locally bounded complexes of finite locally free modules representing one object of D(O_Y), no rank assumed constant and Y not assumed quasi-compact

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.powerSumComplex_eq_of_iso
declarations.doc:
Let `P`, `P'` be locally bounded complexes of finite locally free `𝒪_Y`-modules representing
the same object of `D(𝒪_Y)`. Then `P_p(P) = P_p(P') ∈ A^p(Y)` for every `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem powerSumComplex_eq_of_iso (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P')
    (p : ℕ) : powerSumComplex C sY hP p = powerSumComplex C sY hP' p
declarations.comment: the classes P_p(E^bullet) of a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, ranks varying, depend only on its object of D(O_Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernCharacterComplex_eq_of_iso
declarations.doc:
`ch_p(P) = ch_p(P') ∈ A^p(Y) ⊗ 𝐐` for locally bounded complexes `P`, `P'` of finite locally
free modules representing the same object of `D(𝒪_Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernCharacterComplex_eq_of_iso (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P')
    (p : ℕ) : chernCharacterComplex C sY hP p = chernCharacterComplex C sY hP' p
declarations.comment: the Chern character ch(E^bullet) = sum_p P_p(E^bullet)/p! of a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, ranks varying, depends only on its object of D(O_Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Pushout.isPushout_spec_map_of_isPullback_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ET0.**  A fibre product of rings over a surjective map is sent by
`Spec` to a pushout of schemes: if `p : A' ⟶ A` is surjective and the square with sides `p'`,
`q'`, `q`, `p` is cartesian in `CommRingCat`, then its image under `Spec` is a pushout square
of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPushout_spec_map_of_isPullback_of_surjective
    {A A' B B' : CommRingCat.{u}} (p : A' ⟶ A) (q : B ⟶ A)
    (p' : B' ⟶ B) (q' : B' ⟶ A') (h : IsPullback p' q' q p)
    (hp : Function.Surjective p) :
    IsPushout (Spec.map p) (Spec.map q) (Spec.map q') (Spec.map p')

declarations.name: Deformation.exists_hull_isomorphismClasses_representation
declarations.doc:
The functor of isomorphism classes of deformations of a finite-dimensional representation of
a finitely generated group over a classical base has a hull: a versal formal object with
bijective differential.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hull_isomorphismClasses_representation (V : Type m) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    [Module.Finite k V] [Group.FG Γ] (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k) :
    let 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor (deformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀)
    let hpre := (tangentSpaceEquivSelfExt (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀).1
    let F := isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hpre.cofibered
    ∃ ξ : FormalObject (CategoryOfElements.π F),
      IsVersal (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered F) ξ ∧
        HasBijectiveDifferential (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered F) ξ
declarations.comment: representation_hull

declarations.name: Deformation.isProrepresentableULift_isomorphismClasses_representation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ET1**, prorepresentability: the functor of isomorphism classes of deformations of a
finite-dimensional representation of a finitely generated group over a classical base is
prorepresentable, as soon as the `Γ`-equivariant endomorphisms of the representation are exactly
the scalars, that is `H⁰(Γ, End_k(V)) = k`.

Prorepresentability is stated in the universe-raised form `Deformation.IsProrepresentableULift`,
because the values of the functor of isomorphism classes lie in the universe of the objects of
the deformation category rather than in the morphism universe of `𝒞_Λ`. The functor is the one
whose hull is `Deformation.exists_hull_isomorphismClasses_representation`, the other clause of
this tag.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProrepresentableULift_isomorphismClasses_representation
    (V : Type m) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V] [Group.FG Γ]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k)
    (h : ∀ f : IntertwiningMap ρ₀ ρ₀,
      ∃! a : k, (a • LinearMap.id : Module.End k V) = f.toLinearMap) :
    IsProrepresentableULift (isomorphismClasses
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (deformationCategoryProjection (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀))
      (isDeformationCategory_deformationCategoryProjection
        (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀).predeformation.cofibered)
declarations.comment: prorepresentability

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.exists_hull_continuousIsomorphismClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ET2**, the hull: the functor of isomorphism classes of deformations of a
finite-dimensional continuous representation of a topologically finitely generated group over a
classical base has a hull, that is a versal formal object with bijective differential.

Both hypotheses of Stacks 06IZ beyond the Rim–Schlessinger property are discharged: condition
(S1) and (S2) come from the deformation-category property of the continuous deformations of
`ρ₀`, and the finite-dimensionality of the tangent space is the tangent clause of Stacks
0DVW.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_hull_continuousIsomorphismClasses
    (V : Type m) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) (hρ₀ : IsContinuousRepresentation ρ₀)
    (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k)
    (hΓ : ∃ H : Subgroup Γ, Group.FG ↥H ∧ Dense (H : Set Γ)) :
    let 𝓕 := BasedCategory.ofFunctor (objectsOverFunctor
      (continuousProjection.{u, w, w, m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Γ := Γ))
      (continuousSpecialFiber (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀))
    let hpre := (isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory
      (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀).predeformation
    let F := isomorphismClasses 𝓕 hpre.cofibered
    ∃ ξ : FormalObject (CategoryOfElements.π F),
      IsVersal (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered F) ξ ∧
        HasBijectiveDifferential (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered F) ξ
declarations.comment: the functor has a hull

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.FiniteProjectiveRepresentation.isProrepresentableULift_continuousIsomorphismClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ET2**, prorepresentability: the functor of isomorphism classes of deformations of
a finite-dimensional continuous representation of a topologically finitely generated group over
a classical base is prorepresentable, as soon as the `Γ`-equivariant endomorphisms of the
representation are exactly the scalars, that is `H⁰(Γ, End_k(V)) = k`.

Prorepresentability is stated in the universe-raised form `Deformation.IsProrepresentableULift`,
because the values of the functor of isomorphism classes lie in the universe of the objects of
the deformation category rather than in the morphism universe of `𝒞_Λ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProrepresentableULift_continuousIsomorphismClasses
    (V : Type m) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
    (ρ₀ : Representation k Γ V) (hρ₀ : IsContinuousRepresentation ρ₀)
    (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k)
    (h : ∀ f : IntertwiningMap ρ₀ ρ₀,
      ∃! a : k, (a • LinearMap.id : Module.End k V) = f.toLinearMap)
    (hΓ : ∃ H : Subgroup Γ, Group.FG ↥H ∧ Dense (H : Set Γ)) :
    IsProrepresentableULift (isomorphismClasses
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (objectsOverFunctor
        (continuousProjection.{u, w, w, m} (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (Γ := Γ))
        (continuousSpecialFiber (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀)))
      (isDeformationCategory_continuousDeformationCategory
        (Λ := Λ) V ρ₀ hρ₀).predeformation.cofibered)
declarations.comment: prorepresentability

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.ProjectiveGradedAlgebra.exists_hull_isomorphismClasses_gradedAlgebra_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ET3.** In Example 0D3L, assume `P` is a finitely generated graded `k`-algebra
and `Λ → k` is the classical case (`Λ` a Noetherian complete local ring with residue field `k`).
Then the functor `A ↦ Ob(Def_P(A))/≅` of isomorphism classes has a hull: a versal formal object
with bijective differential.

The section variable `[∀ d, Module.Finite k (grading d)]` is Example 0D3L's standing condition
defining `Def_P`. The source requires `dim_k(P_d) < ∞` for all `d ≥ 0` before it forms
`x_0 = (k, P)` and sets `Def_P = F_{x_0}`, and `specialFiber` requires the same condition to
build `x_0`. It is not a hypothesis added to 0ET3. The only hypotheses that 0ET3 adds to
Example 0D3L are finite generation, which is `[Algebra.FiniteType k P]`, and the classical case,
which is `hΛ`.

The proof applies `exists_hull_isomorphismClasses_gradedAlgebra`. Its hypothesis on the tangent
space comes from `finiteDimensional_tangentSpace`, the tangent-space clause of Stacks 0DVZ,
through the comparison of the two tangent-space models.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_hull_isomorphismClasses_gradedAlgebra_of_finiteType
    [Algebra.FiniteType k P] (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k) :
    ∃ ξ : FormalObject (CategoryOfElements.π (Deformation.isomorphismClasses
        (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (deformationProjection (Λ := Λ) P grading))
        (isPredeformationCategory_deformationProjection (Λ := Λ) P grading).cofibered)),
      IsVersal (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered (Deformation.isomorphismClasses
          (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (deformationProjection (Λ := Λ) P grading))
          (isPredeformationCategory_deformationProjection (Λ := Λ) P grading).cofibered)) ξ ∧
        HasBijectiveDifferential
          (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered (Deformation.isomorphismClasses
            (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (deformationProjection (Λ := Λ) P grading))
            (isPredeformationCategory_deformationProjection (Λ := Λ) P grading).cofibered))
          ξ
declarations.comment: Def_P of 0D3L: finite-dimensional graded pieces define it, not an extra hypothesis

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.exists_hull_isomorphismClasses_ringDeformation_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
Let `Λ → k` be a classical base, let `P` be a `k`-algebra of finite type, and suppose
`Spec(P) → Spec(k)` is smooth except at a finite number of points. Then the functor of fibrewise
isomorphism classes of deformations of `P` has a hull: a versal formal object with bijective
differential.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_hull_isomorphismClasses_ringDeformation_of_finiteType
    [Algebra.FiniteType k P]
    (hsmooth : {q : PrimeSpectrum P | ¬ Algebra.IsSmoothAt k q.asIdeal}.Finite)
    (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k) :
    ∃ ξ : FormalObject (CategoryOfElements.π (Deformation.isomorphismClasses
        (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (ringDeformationProjection Λ k P))
        (isPredeformationCategory_ringDeformationProjection (Λ := Λ) (k := k) P).cofibered)),
      IsVersal (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered (Deformation.isomorphismClasses
          (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (ringDeformationProjection Λ k P))
          (isPredeformationCategory_ringDeformationProjection
            (Λ := Λ) (k := k) P).cofibered)) ξ ∧
        HasBijectiveDifferential
          (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered (Deformation.isomorphismClasses
            (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (ringDeformationProjection Λ k P))
            (isPredeformationCategory_ringDeformationProjection
              (Λ := Λ) (k := k) P).cofibered))
          ξ

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.exists_hull_isomorphismClasses_scheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ET5**, the hull. Let `X` be a proper scheme over the field `k` and
let `Λ` be a Noetherian complete local ring with residue field `k` (the classical case). Then the
functor `F : 𝒞_Λ → Sets, A ↦ Ob(Def_X(A))/≅` of isomorphism classes of deformations of `X` has
a hull: a versal formal object of `F` whose differential is bijective.

`Def_X` is a deformation category by Stacks 0DY8 and its tangent space is finite dimensional by
Stacks 0DYA (`Deformation.Examples.finiteDimensional_schemeTangentSpace`), so Stacks 06J7 and
06IZ give the hull.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hull_isomorphismClasses_scheme (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k)
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsProper X.hom] :
    let F := isomorphismClasses (schemeDeformationBased (Λ := Λ) X) (schemeDeformation_cofibered X)
    ∃ ξ : FormalObject (CategoryOfElements.π F),
      IsHull (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered F) ξ
declarations.comment: the hull: for X proper over k and Λ a complete local ring with residue field k, the functor A ↦ Ob(Def_X(A))/≅ of isomorphism classes of deformations of X has a hull

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isProrepresentableULift_isomorphismClasses_scheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ET5**, prorepresentability. Let `X` be a proper scheme over the field
`k` and let `Λ` be a Noetherian complete local ring with residue field `k`. If
`Der_k(𝒪_X, 𝒪_X) = 0`, then the functor `F : 𝒞_Λ → Sets, A ↦ Ob(Def_X(A))/≅` is
prorepresentable.

By the first display of Stacks 0DY9, `Inf(Def_X) = Der_k(𝒪_X, 𝒪_X)` vanishes
(`Deformation.Examples.infinitesimalAutomorphisms_schemeDeformation_eq_bot`), so `Def_X` and `F`
are equivalent (Stacks 06K0) and `F` is a deformation functor with finite-dimensional tangent
space (Stacks 0DYA); Schlessinger's theorem, Stacks 06JM, applies. Prorepresentability is stated
in the universe-raised form `Deformation.IsProrepresentableULift`, the values of `F` lying one
universe above the morphisms of `𝒞_Λ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProrepresentableULift_isomorphismClasses_scheme (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k)
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsProper X.hom]
    (hDer : ∀ D : schemeMorphismDerivations (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (𝟙 X.left) X.hom, D = 0) :
    IsProrepresentableULift
      (isomorphismClasses (schemeDeformationBased (Λ := Λ) X) (schemeDeformation_cofibered X))
declarations.comment: prorepresentability: for X proper over k and Λ a complete local ring with residue field k, if Der_k(O_X, O_X) = 0 then the functor A ↦ Ob(Def_X(A))/≅ is prorepresentable

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.exists_hull_schemeMorphismIsomorphismClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ET6, the hull.** Let `Λ` be a complete local ring with residue field `k` and let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of proper `k`-schemes. Then the functor
`A ↦ Ob(Def_{X → Y}(A))/≅` of isomorphism classes of deformations of `f` has a hull: a versal
formal object whose differential is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hull_schemeMorphismIsomorphismClasses (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k)
    [IsProper pX] [IsProper pY] :
    let G := isomorphismClasses
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (schemeMorphismDeformationCategoryProjection f pX pY hf))
      (isDeformationCategory_schemeMorphismDeformationCategoryProjection f pX pY
        hf).predeformation.cofibered
    ∃ ξ : FormalObject (CategoryOfElements.π G),
      IsHull (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered G) ξ
declarations.comment: the functor of isomorphism classes of Def_{X -> Y} has a hull

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isProrepresentableULift_schemeMorphismIsomorphismClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ET6, prorepresentability.** Let `Λ` be a complete local ring with residue field
`k` and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of proper `k`-schemes with
`Der_k(𝒪_X, 𝒪_X) = Der_k(𝒪_Y, 𝒪_Y) = 0`. Then the functor `A ↦ Ob(Def_{X → Y}(A))/≅` of
isomorphism classes of deformations of `f` is prorepresentable.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProrepresentableULift_schemeMorphismIsomorphismClasses (hΛ : IsClassical Λ k)
    [IsProper pX] [IsProper pY]
    (hX : ∀ D : schemeMorphismDerivations (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (𝟙 X) pX, D = 0)
    (hY : ∀ D : schemeMorphismDerivations (Λ := Λ) (k := k) (𝟙 Y) pY, D = 0) :
    IsProrepresentableULift (isomorphismClasses
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (schemeMorphismDeformationCategoryProjection f pX pY hf))
      (isDeformationCategory_schemeMorphismDeformationCategoryProjection f pX pY
        hf).predeformation.cofibered)
declarations.comment: if Der_k(O_X, O_X) = Der_k(O_Y, O_Y) = 0, the functor of isomorphism classes of Def_{X -> Y} is prorepresentable

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.exists_hull_spaceIsomorphismClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ET7, the hull.** Let `Λ` be a complete local ring with residue field `k` and let
`X` be a proper algebraic space over `k`. Then the functor `A ↦ Ob(Def_X(A))/≅` of isomorphism
classes of deformations of `X` has a hull: a versal formal object whose differential is
bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_hull_spaceIsomorphismClasses (hcl : IsClassical Λ k)
    (hproper : Space.IsProper B (Spec (.of Λ)) hΛ toK) :
    let G := isomorphismClasses
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (spaceDeformationProjection B hΛ hSpec X hX toK))
      (isDeformationCategory_spaceDeformationProjection B hΛ hSpec X hX
        toK).predeformation.cofibered
    ∃ ξ : FormalObject (CategoryOfElements.π G),
      IsHull (categoryOfElements_projection_isCofibered G) ξ
declarations.comment: for a proper algebraic space X over k and Λ complete local with residue field k, the functor of isomorphism classes of Def_X has a hull

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isProrepresentableULift_spaceIsomorphismClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ET7, prorepresentability.** Let `Λ` be a complete local ring with residue field
`k` and let `X` be a proper algebraic space over `k` with `Der_k(𝒪_X, 𝒪_X) = 0`. Then the functor
`A ↦ Ob(Def_X(A))/≅` of isomorphism classes of deformations of `X` is prorepresentable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProrepresentableULift_spaceIsomorphismClasses (hcl : IsClassical Λ k)
    (hproper : Space.IsProper B (Spec (.of Λ)) hΛ toK)
    (hDer : ∀ D : SpaceDerivations B hΛ (spaceStructureMap B hΛ hSpec X hX toK), D = 0) :
    IsProrepresentableULift (isomorphismClasses
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor (spaceDeformationProjection B hΛ hSpec X hX toK))
      (isDeformationCategory_spaceDeformationProjection B hΛ hSpec X hX
        toK).predeformation.cofibered)
declarations.comment: if Der_k(O_X, O_X) = 0, the functor of isomorphism classes of Def_X is prorepresentable

registrations.name: Profinite.hasLimits
registrations.comment:
every small diagram of profinite spaces has a limit in `Profinite`, i.e. its
  limit is again a profinite space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPHCovering_tfae
declarations.doc:
A family of locally finite type morphisms is a ph covering if and only if some ph
covering refines it, if and only if its disjoint-union morphism is a ph covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPHCovering_tfae {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I]
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hf : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (f i)) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsPHCovering X f,
      ∃ (K : Type v) (Y : K → Scheme.{u}) (g : ∀ k, Y k ⟶ T),
        IsPHCovering Y g ∧
          Nonempty
            (({ I₀ := K, X := Y, f := g } : PreZeroHypercover T).Hom
              ({ I₀ := I, X := X, f := f } : PreZeroHypercover T)),
      IsPHCovering
        (fun _ : Unit ↦ ∐ X) (fun _ ↦ Sigma.desc f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardVCovering
declarations.doc:
A finite family of morphisms from affine schemes to an affine scheme is a **standard V
covering** if every morphism from the spectrum of a valuation ring lifts to one member
after an extension of valuation rings.
declarations.statement:
public def IsStandardVCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] {I : Type v} [Finite I]
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) [∀ i, IsAffine (X i)] (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStandardVCovering_of_flat_affineCover
declarations.doc: A standard fpqc covering of an affine scheme is a standard V covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStandardVCovering_of_flat_affineCover
    {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] (𝒰 : T.AffineCover.{v} @Flat) [Finite 𝒰.I₀] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardVCovering (fun i ↦ Spec (𝒰.X i)) 𝒰.f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.StandardPHCovering.isStandardVCovering
declarations.doc: A standard ph covering is a standard V covering.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStandardVCovering_pullback
declarations.doc:
A standard V covering of an affine scheme remains a standard V covering after pullback
along a morphism from another affine scheme.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isStandardVCovering_pullback
    {T T' : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] [IsAffine T']
    {I : Type v} [Finite I] (X : I → Scheme.{u}) [∀ i, IsAffine (X i)]
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T) (g : T' ⟶ T)
    (hf : IsStandardVCovering X f) :
    IsStandardVCovering (fun i ↦ pullback (f i) g)
      (fun i ↦ pullback.snd (f i) g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardVCovering.comp
declarations.doc:
Composing a standard V covering with a standard V covering of each member gives a
standard V covering.
declarations.statement:
public lemma IsStandardVCovering.comp
    {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T]
    {J : Type v} [Finite J] (X : J → Scheme.{u}) [∀ j, IsAffine (X j)]
    (f : ∀ j, X j ⟶ T) (hf : IsStandardVCovering X f)
    {I : J → Type w} [∀ j, Finite (I j)]
    (Y : ∀ j, I j → Scheme.{u}) [∀ j i, IsAffine (Y j i)]
    (g : ∀ j i, Y j i ⟶ X j)
    (hg : ∀ j, IsStandardVCovering (Y j) (g j)) :
    IsStandardVCovering (fun ji : Σ j, I j ↦ Y ji.1 ji.2)
      (fun ji ↦ g ji.1 ji.2 ≫ f ji.1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStandardVCovering_tfae
declarations.doc:
A finite family of affine schemes over an affine scheme is a standard V covering if and only
if it admits a refining standard V covering, if and only if the morphism from the disjoint union
of the family is a standard V covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isStandardVCovering_tfae {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T]
    {I : Type v} [Finite I] (X : I → Scheme.{u}) [∀ i, IsAffine (X i)]
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsStandardVCovering X f,
      ∃ (K : Type v) (_ : Finite K) (Y : K → Scheme.{u}) (_ : ∀ k, IsAffine (Y k))
          (g : ∀ k, Y k ⟶ T),
        IsStandardVCovering Y g ∧
          Nonempty
            (({ I₀ := K, X := Y, f := g } : PreZeroHypercover T).Hom
              ({ I₀ := I, X := X, f := f } : PreZeroHypercover T)),
      IsStandardVCovering
        (fun _ : Unit ↦ ∐ X) (fun _ ↦ Sigma.desc f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsVCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETH.** A family of morphisms of schemes is a **V covering** if, over every
affine open of the target, a finite standard V covering by affine schemes refines the
pullback of the family.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def IsVCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_tfae
declarations.doc:
A family of morphisms of schemes is a V covering if and only if a V covering refines it,
if and only if its disjoint-union morphism is a V covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVCovering_tfae {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I]
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsVCovering X f,
      ∃ (K : Type v) (Y : K → Scheme.{u}) (g : ∀ k, Y k ⟶ T),
        IsVCovering Y g ∧
          Nonempty
            (({ I₀ := K, X := Y, f := g } : PreZeroHypercover T).Hom
              ({ I₀ := I, X := X, f := f } : PreZeroHypercover T)),
      IsVCovering
        (fun _ : Unit ↦ ∐ X) (fun _ ↦ Sigma.desc f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_of_isIso
declarations.doc: An isomorphism of schemes, regarded as a singleton family, is a V covering.
declarations.statement:
lemma isVCovering_of_isIso {T' T : Scheme.{u}} (f : T' ⟶ T) [IsIso f] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsVCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ T') (fun _ ↦ f)
declarations.comment: isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_pullback
declarations.doc: The pullback of a V covering along any morphism of schemes is a V covering.
declarations.comment: base_change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsVCovering.comp
declarations.doc:
Composing a V covering with V coverings of each of its members gives a V
covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsVCovering.comp {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsVCovering X f) {J : I → Type w}
    (Y : ∀ i, J i → Scheme.{u}) (g : ∀ i j, Y i j ⟶ X i)
    (hg : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.IsVCovering (Y i) (g i)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsVCovering
      (fun ij : Σ i, J i ↦ Y ij.1 ij.2)
      (fun ij ↦ g ij.1 ij.2 ≫ f ij.1)
declarations.comment: composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETK.** Every fpqc covering is a V covering.

Above an affine open of the target, Stacks 022E refines the base change of the family by a
standard fpqc covering, and Stacks 0ETC says that a standard fpqc covering is a standard V
covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVCovering_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T) :
    IsVCovering X f
declarations.comment: fpqc_v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_of_mem_fppfPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETK.** Every fppf covering is a V covering, being an fpqc covering by
Stacks 022C.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVCovering_of_mem_fppfPrecoverage {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T) :
    IsVCovering X f
declarations.comment: fppf_v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_of_mem_syntomicPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETK.** Every syntomic covering is a V covering, being an fpqc covering by
Stacks 022C.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVCovering_of_mem_syntomicPrecoverage {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈
      Scheme.precoverage (@Syntomic : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) T) :
    IsVCovering X f
declarations.comment: syntomic_v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_of_mem_smoothPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETK.** Every smooth covering is a V covering, being an fpqc covering by
Stacks 022C.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVCovering_of_mem_smoothPrecoverage {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈
      Scheme.precoverage (@Smooth : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) T) :
    IsVCovering X f
declarations.comment: smooth_v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_of_mem_etalePrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETK.** Every étale covering is a V covering, being an fpqc covering by
Stacks 022C.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVCovering_of_mem_etalePrecoverage {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.etalePrecoverage T) :
    IsVCovering X f
declarations.comment: etale_v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_of_mem_zariskiPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETK.** Every Zariski covering is a V covering, being an fpqc covering by
Stacks 022C.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVCovering_of_mem_zariskiPrecoverage {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage T) :
    IsVCovering X f
declarations.comment: zariski_v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_of_isPHCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETK.** Every ph covering is a V covering. It needs no finiteness hypothesis on the
members of the family.

This is also one half of Stacks 0ETR, which for a family locally of finite presentation asserts
that being a ph covering and being a V covering are *equivalent*; it carries no 0ETR
registration. The two conditions 0ETR compares are the numbered items of one assertion, that
equivalence, so a single implication is a fragment of that assertion and not a part of it; 0ETR
belongs where the equivalence is stated in full, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPHCovering_iff_isVCovering` in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Topologies/V/PhVFlatteningModification.lean`. The converse
implication is `AlgebraicGeometry.isPHCovering_of_isVCovering`, which carries
`AlgebraicGeometry.StandardVCoveringHasPHRefinement`; the inputs the Stacks argument needs for
that predicate are the generic flatness stratification of the base (Stacks 0H3Z),
`AlgebraicGeometry.finitePresentationHasFlatStratification`, and the Raynaud-Gruson flattening
theorem for an admissible blowup (Stacks 0815), and both are available.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVCovering_of_isPHCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hph : IsPHCovering X f) :
    IsVCovering X f
declarations.comment: ph_v

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsVSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETL.** A set-valued presheaf on schemes is a sheaf for the V topology if it
satisfies the sheaf condition for every V covering family.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsVSheaf (F : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVSheaf_iff_zariski_and_standard
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ETM.** The V sheaf condition is equivalent to the
Zariski sheaf condition together with the sheaf condition for all standard V
coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isVSheaf_iff_zariski_and_standard
    (F : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsVSheaf.{u, max u v, w} F ↔
      (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : T.OpenCover.{max u v}),
        (Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f).IsSheafFor F) ∧
      (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine T] (I : Type (max u v)) [Finite I]
        (X : I → Scheme.{u}) [∀ i, IsAffine (X i)] (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T),
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardVCovering X f →
          (Presieve.ofArrows X f).IsSheafFor F)
declarations.comment: Zariski and standard V criterion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStandardVSheaf_iff_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ETM, moreover.** Under the Zariski sheaf condition,
the sheaf condition for standard V coverings can be tested on one-arrow
standard V coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStandardVSheaf_iff_singleton
    (F : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
    (hZ : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : T.OpenCover.{max u v}),
      (Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f).IsSheafFor F) :
    (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine T] (I : Type (max u v)) [Finite I]
      (X : I → Scheme.{u}) [∀ i, IsAffine (X i)] (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T),
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardVCovering X f →
        (Presieve.ofArrows X f).IsSheafFor F) ↔
    (∀ (T X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine T] [IsAffine X] (f : X ⟶ T),
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardVCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ X) (fun _ ↦ f) →
        (Presieve.ofArrows (fun _ : Unit ↦ X) (fun _ ↦ f)).IsSheafFor F)
declarations.comment: single-arrow standard V criterion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_iff_valuation_lifting
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact morphism is a singleton V covering exactly when every map from
a valuation spectrum lifts after an extension of valuation rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isVCovering_iff_valuation_lifting {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [QuasiCompact f] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsVCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ X) (fun _ ↦ f) ↔
      (∀ (V : Type u) [CommRing V] [IsDomain V] [ValuationRing V]
        (g : Spec (.of V) ⟶ Y),
        ∃ (W : Type u) (_ : CommRing W) (_ : IsDomain W) (_ : ValuationRing W)
          (e : V →+* W),
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsExtensionOfValuationRings e ∧
            ∃ (h : Spec (.of W) ⟶ X),
              Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom e) ≫ g = h ≫ f)
declarations.comment: part (1) iff part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.valuation_lifting_iff_specialization_lifting
declarations.doc:
Valuation-ring lifting is equivalent to lifting every specialization after
arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuation_lifting_iff_specialization_lifting {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (∀ (V : Type u) [CommRing V] [IsDomain V] [ValuationRing V]
      (g : Spec (.of V) ⟶ Y),
      ∃ (W : Type u) (_ : CommRing W) (_ : IsDomain W) (_ : ValuationRing W)
        (e : V →+* W),
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsExtensionOfValuationRings e ∧
          ∃ (h : Spec (.of W) ⟶ X),
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom e) ≫ g = h ≫ f) ↔
      (∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (g : Z ⟶ Y) (z' z : Z),
        z' ⤳ z →
          ∃ (w' w : (pullback g f : Scheme.{u})),
            (w' ⤳ w) ∧
              (pullback.fst g f) w' = z' ∧
                (pullback.fst g f) w = z)
declarations.comment: part (2) iff part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_universallySubmersive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ETP.** The morphism from the disjoint union of a
V covering to its target is universally submersive.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVCovering_universallySubmersive {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v}
    [Small.{u} I] (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hf : IsVCovering X f) :
    universally (topologically @Topology.IsQuotientMap) (Sigma.desc f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPHCovering_iff_isVCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETR.** A family of morphisms of schemes which are locally of finite presentation
is a ph covering if and only if it is a V covering.

The implication from a ph covering to a V covering is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isVCovering_of_isPHCovering` and needs nothing; the converse is the six-step
argument of the source, whose last input — the refinement of a standard V covering of an affine
scheme by a standard ph covering, `AlgebraicGeometry.StandardVCoveringHasPHRefinement` — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.standardVCoveringHasPHRefinement` above.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPHCovering_iff_isVCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v} (X : I → Scheme.{u})
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T) (hfp : ∀ i, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f i)) :
    IsPHCovering X f ↔ IsVCovering X f
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (2) for a family locally of finite presentation, which is the whole of the lemma

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsHCovering
declarations.doc:
A family `{X i ⟶ T}` of morphisms of schemes is an *h covering* when
every member is locally of finite presentation and the family is a ph covering.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsHCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v} (X : I → Scheme.{u})
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isHCovering_of_universallySubmersive_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ETT, (1) implies (2).** A finite family of morphisms of finite type to a Noetherian
scheme whose disjoint-union morphism is universally submersive is an h covering.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.isHCovering_of_universallySubmersive` with its
hypothesis supplied by `AlgebraicGeometry.universallySubmersiveHasPHRefinement`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHCovering_of_universallySubmersive_of_isNoetherian {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    {I : Type v} [Finite I] [Small.{u} I] {Y : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ X)
    [∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (f i)] [∀ i, QuasiCompact (f i)]
    (hsub : UniversallySubmersive (Sigma.desc f)) : IsHCovering Y f
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)
