    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsFiniteType I)
    (b₁ : X₁ ⟶ X) (b₂ : X₂ ⟶ X)
    (h₁ : IsAlmostBlowUpSquare I b₁) (h₂ : IsAlmostBlowUpSquare I b₂) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (b : X' ⟶ X) (i₁ : X' ⟶ X₁) (i₂ : X' ⟶ X₂),
      IsAlmostBlowUpSquare I b ∧
        IsClosedImmersion i₁ ∧ IsClosedImmersion i₂ ∧
        i₁ ≫ b₁ = b ∧ i₂ ≫ b₂ = b ∧
        I.comap b = (I.comap b₁).comap i₁ ∧
        I.comap b = (I.comap b₂).comap i₂

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVC.** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let `X`
be a scheme of finite presentation over `Y`, and let `V ⊆ Y` be a quasi-compact open. Then there
is a diagram as in the tag: two almost blowup squares, over `Y` with a centre disjoint from `V`
and over `X` with the inverse-image centre, whose lower and top squares are cartesian
(`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerSquareIso`, `AlgebraicGeometry.topSquareIso`) and whose relative
morphism `X' ⟶ Y'` is flat and of finite presentation.

The flattening centre comes from
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_flat_strictTransform`, the library's form of Stacks tag
081R, and two things are carried beyond the tag's own hypotheses. The base is assumed locally
Noetherian: this is the case the Stacks proof calls immediate, the general case being reduced to
it by absolute Noetherian approximation, which is not done here. And the affine case of the
flatness half of Stacks tag 0815 is carried as
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartFlatteningCentre f X.unitModule V`, exactly as that form of
tag 081R carries it. The tag's remaining hypothesis that `X_V ⟶ V` be flat is not assumed
separately, because in the source it enters only through that affine case; so the statement below
is a generalization in that respect.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [CompactSpace Y]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : FinitePresentation f) (V : Y.Opens)
    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set Y)) (H : AffineChartFlatteningCentre f X.unitModule V) :
    HasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair f V
declarations.comment: locally Noetherian base; the affine case of the flatness half of [Stacks, Tag 0815] carried as the hypothesis `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartFlatteningCentre`, inherited from the library's form of [Stacks, Tag 081R]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EVC].** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let `X` be a
scheme of finite presentation over `Y`, and let `V ⊆ Y` be a quasi-compact open such that
`X_V ⟶ V` is flat. Then there is a diagram as in the tag: two almost blowup squares, over `Y`
with a centre disjoint from `V` and over `X` with the inverse-image centre, whose lower and top
squares are cartesian (`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerSquareIso`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.topSquareIso`) and whose relative morphism `X' ⟶ Y'` is flat and of finite
presentation.

The general case is reduced to the locally Noetherian case
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair` by absolute Noetherian approximation; see the
module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair_of_flat {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : FinitePresentation f)
    (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsCompact (V : Set Y)) (hflat : Flat (pullback.snd f V.ι)) :
    HasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair f V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair_of_affineCase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVC.** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be of finite presentation and let `V ⊆ Y` be a quasi-compact open such that
`X_V ⟶ V` is flat. Then there is a diagram as in the tag: two almost blowup squares, over `Y`
with a centre disjoint from `V` and over `X` with the inverse-image centre, whose lower and top
squares are cartesian (`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerSquareIso`, `AlgebraicGeometry.topSquareIso`) and
whose relative morphism `X' ⟶ Y'` is flat and of finite presentation.

Every hypothesis of the source is present, with no Noetherian hypothesis on `Y`: the Noetherian
case is `AlgebraicGeometry.hasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair_of_flat`, run at the Noetherian model
supplied by `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isNoetherian_model_of_finitePresentation_of_flat` and
pulled back along `Y ⟶ Y₀`. The affine case of the flatness assertion of
[Stacks, Tag 0815] it consumes is
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartFlatteningCentreUnderSourceHypotheses.of_compactSpace`, itself proved
from [Stacks, Tag 0811], which
`AlgebraicGeometry.NoetherianAffineChartFlatteningCentre.of_affineCase` turns into the form the
Noetherian case consumes.

The tag's hypothesis that `X_V ⟶ V` be flat is essential and is present here, where
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair` omits it: without it the affine case cannot be
applied at the model at all, its own hypothesis (5) being exactly that flatness.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair_of_affineCase {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace Y]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : FinitePresentation f) (V : Y.Opens)
    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set Y)) (hflat : Flat (f ∣_ V)) :
    HasFlatAlmostBlowUpSquarePair f V
declarations.comment: the conclusion in full, under exactly the source's hypotheses and with no Noetherian hypothesis on the base: the affine case of the flatness assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0815] that the proof consumes is `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartFlatteningCentreUnderSourceHypotheses.of_compactSpace`, itself proved from [Stacks, Tag 0811]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_of_almostBlowUpSquare_bigH
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVD.** A sheaf on the big h site over a scheme sends an almost blowup square to
a cartesian square of sets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPullback_of_almostBlowUpSquare_bigH
    (B : BigHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F)
    {X X' Z E : BigHOver B S hS}
    (b : X' ⟶ X) (z : Z ⟶ X) (p : E ⟶ X') (e : E ⟶ Z)
    (I : ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X).IdealSheafData)
    (hb : IsAlmostBlowUpSquare I ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map b))
    (hZ : Nonempty
      (Over.mk ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map z) ≅
        Over.mk I.subschemeι))
    (hSquare : IsPullback
      ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map e)
      ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map p)
      ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map z)
      ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map b)) :
    IsPullback (F.map z.op) (F.map b.op) (F.map e.op) (F.map p.op)
declarations.comment: big h site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_of_almostBlowUpSquare_bigAffineH
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVD.** A sheaf on the big affine h site over a scheme sends an almost blowup
square to a cartesian square of sets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPullback_of_almostBlowUpSquare_bigAffineH
    (B : BigHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigAffineH B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigAffineH.topology B S hS) F)
    {X X' Z E : BigAffineH B S hS}
    (b : X' ⟶ X) (z : Z ⟶ X) (p : E ⟶ X') (e : E ⟶ Z)
    (I : ((BigAffineH.toScheme B S hS).obj X).IdealSheafData)
    (hb : IsAlmostBlowUpSquare I ((BigAffineH.toScheme B S hS).map b))
    (hZ : Nonempty
      (Over.mk ((BigAffineH.toScheme B S hS).map z) ≅
        Over.mk I.subschemeι))
    (hSquare : IsPullback
      ((BigAffineH.toScheme B S hS).map e)
      ((BigAffineH.toScheme B S hS).map p)
      ((BigAffineH.toScheme B S hS).map z)
      ((BigAffineH.toScheme B S hS).map b)) :
    IsPullback (F.map z.op) (F.map b.op) (F.map e.op) (F.map p.op)
declarations.comment: big affine h site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_map_of_isThickening_bigH
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVE.** A sheaf on the big h site over a scheme restricts bijectively along a
morphism of the site which is a thickening and of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_map_of_isThickening_bigH
    (B : BigHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F)
    {X X' : BigHOver B S hS} (i : X ⟶ X')
    (hi : IsThickening ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map i))
    (hfp : FinitePresentation ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map i)) :
    Function.Bijective (F.map i.op)
declarations.comment: big h site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_map_of_isThickening_bigAffineH
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVE.** A sheaf on the big affine h site over a scheme restricts bijectively
along a morphism of the site which is a thickening and of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_map_of_isThickening_bigAffineH
    (B : BigHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigAffineH B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigAffineH.topology B S hS) F)
    {X X' : BigAffineH B S hS} (i : X ⟶ X')
    (hi : IsThickening ((BigAffineH.toScheme B S hS).map i))
    (hfp : FinitePresentation ((BigAffineH.toScheme B S hS).map i)) :
    Function.Bijective (F.map i.op)
declarations.comment: big affine h site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf_of_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVF, a sheaf satisfies condition (2).** A sheaf on the big h site over `S` satisfies
the sheaf condition for the one-element family attached to a morphism of the site with affine
target which is flat, proper, surjective and of finite presentation.

Flatness is not used: such a morphism is an h covering all by itself, and so is every proper
surjective morphism of finite presentation, which is the content of condition (2) of Stacks
0EU5.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf_of_isSheaf
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F) :
    BigHOver.IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf B S hS F
declarations.comment: only if, condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf.bijective_mapToEqualizer
declarations.doc:
**Condition (2) of Stacks 0EVF in the source's equalizer form.** Let `f : V ⟶ U` be a
morphism of the big h category over `S` whose target has affine underlying scheme and whose
underlying morphism of schemes is flat, proper, surjective and of finite presentation, and let
`p₁, p₂ : W ⟶ V` complete `f` to a cartesian square, so that `W = V ×_U V`.  Then condition (2)
says exactly that `F(U)` maps bijectively onto the equalizer of the two maps `F(V) ⟶ F(W)`.

This is the form in which the source states the condition; the two are identified by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSheafFor_singleton_iff_bijective_mapToEqualizer`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf.bijective_mapToEqualizer
    (hF : BigHOver.IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf B S hS F)
    {V U W : BigHOver B S hS} (f : V ⟶ U) (p₁ p₂ : W ⟶ V) (hW : IsPullback p₁ p₂ f f)
    (haffine : IsAffine ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U))
    (hflat : Flat ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map f))
    (hproper : IsProper ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map f))
    (hsurj : Surjective ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map f))
    (hfp : FinitePresentation ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map f)) :
    Function.Bijective (regularTopology.mapToEqualizer F f p₁ p₂ hW.w)
declarations.comment: condition (2) in equalizer form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isAffineAlmostBlowUpSheaf_of_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVF, a sheaf satisfies condition (3).** A sheaf on the big h site over `S` sends an
almost blowup square of the site with affine base to a cartesian square of sets.

Affineness of the base is not used: this is Stacks 0EVD for an arbitrary almost blowup square of
the site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffineAlmostBlowUpSheaf_of_isSheaf
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F) :
    BigHOver.IsAffineAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F
declarations.comment: only if, condition (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.zariski_and_affineFlatProperFP_and_affineAlmostBlowUp_of_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVF, the three conditions are necessary.** A sheaf on the big h site over `S`
satisfies condition (1), the sheaf condition for Zariski coverings, condition (2), the sheaf
condition for every morphism of the site with affine target which is flat, proper, surjective and
of finite presentation, and condition (3), the cartesianness of the image of every almost blowup
square of the site with affine base.

The converse is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isSheaf_of_zariski_and_affineFlatProperFP_and_affineAlmostBlowUp`, and
the two together are
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isSheaf_iff_zariski_and_affineFlatProperFP_and_affineAlmostBlowUp`,
both in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Topologies.HTopology.AlmostBlowUpSheafInduction`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem zariski_and_affineFlatProperFP_and_affineAlmostBlowUp_of_isSheaf
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F) :
    BigHOver.IsZariskiSheaf B S hS F ∧
      BigHOver.IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf B S hS F ∧
      BigHOver.IsAffineAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F
declarations.comment: only if, all three conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isSheaf_of_zariski_and_affineFlatProperFP_and_affineAlmostBlowUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVF, the three conditions are sufficient.** A presheaf of sets on the big h
category over `S` which satisfies condition (1), the sheaf condition for Zariski coverings,
condition (2), the sheaf condition for every morphism of the site with affine target which is
flat, proper, surjective and of finite presentation, and condition (3), the cartesianness of the
image of every almost blowup square of the site with affine base, is a sheaf for the h topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_of_zariski_and_affineFlatProperFP_and_affineAlmostBlowUp
    (hZ : BigHOver.IsZariskiSheaf B S hS F)
    (h2 : BigHOver.IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf B S hS F)
    (h3 : BigHOver.IsAffineAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isSheaf_iff_zariski_and_affineFlatProperFP_and_affineAlmostBlowUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVF.** A presheaf of sets on the big h category over `S` is a sheaf for the h
topology if and only if it satisfies condition (1), the sheaf condition for Zariski coverings,
condition (2), the sheaf condition for every morphism of the site with affine target which is
flat, proper, surjective and of finite presentation, and condition (3), the cartesianness of the
image of every almost blowup square of the site with affine base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_iff_zariski_and_affineFlatProperFP_and_affineAlmostBlowUp :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F ↔
      (BigHOver.IsZariskiSheaf B S hS F ∧
        BigHOver.IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf B S hS F ∧
        BigHOver.IsAffineAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAlmostBlowUpSquare_quotient_of_pow_mul_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVG.** For a finitely generated ideal `J` of `A` annihilated by a power
of `f`, the closed immersion `Spec (A ⧸ J) ⟶ Spec A` is the modification of an almost blowup
square whose centre is the closed subscheme cut out by `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAlmostBlowUpSquare_quotient_of_pow_mul_eq_zero (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (f : A) (J : Ideal A) (hJ : J.FG) (h : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ J, f ^ n * x = 0) :
    IsAlmostBlowUpSquare
      (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
        (Ideal.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom (Ideal.span {f})))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlmostBlowUp.isAlmostBlowUpSquare_twoGeneratorSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVH.** Let `A` be a ring and `f₁, f₂ ∈ A`. The square
```
E = Proj ((A/(f₁,f₂))[T₀,T₁]) ⟶ Proj (A[T₀,T₁]/(f₂T₀-f₁T₁)) = X'
            ↓                                ↓
     Z = Spec (A/(f₁,f₂))      ⟶       Spec A = X
```
is an almost blowup square: it is cartesian, so that `E = b⁻¹(Z)`; its lower arrow is, over
`Spec A`, the closed subscheme cut out by `(f₁,f₂)`; and the right-hand arrow `b` with that centre
satisfies the conditions of an almost blowup square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlmostBlowUpSquare_twoGeneratorSquare :
    letI := (twoGeneratorSquare A f₁ f₂).modificationGraded
    IsPullback (exceptionalToModification A f₁ f₂) (exceptionalToCenter A f₁ f₂)
        (modificationToBase A f₁ f₂) (centerToBase A f₁ f₂) ∧
      Nonempty (Over.mk (centerToBase A f₁ f₂) ≅
        Over.mk (centerIdealSheaf A f₁ f₂).subschemeι) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlmostBlowUpSquare (centerIdealSheaf A f₁ f₂)
        (modificationToBase A f₁ f₂)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isSheaf_iff_zariski_and_flatProper_and_generatorSquares
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVI.** A presheaf of sets on the big h category over `S` is a sheaf for the h
topology if and only if it satisfies condition (1), the sheaf condition for Zariski coverings,
condition (2), the sheaf condition for every morphism of the site with affine target which is
flat, proper, surjective and of finite presentation, condition (3), cartesianness of the image
of every almost blowup square of the site with affine base and the shape of Example 0EVG, and
condition (4), the same for the shape of Example 0EVH.

The sufficiency direction is the sufficiency direction of Stacks 0EVF,
`AlgebraicGeometry.affineAlmostBlowUpHSheafCriterion`, applied after the reduction of its
condition (3) to the two shapes, `AlgebraicGeometry.generatorAlmostBlowUpSquaresSuffice`.
Condition (2) in the source's equalizer form is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf.bijective_mapToEqualizer`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_iff_zariski_and_flatProper_and_generatorSquares
    (B : BigHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F ↔
      (BigHOver.IsZariskiSheaf B S hS F ∧
        BigHOver.IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf B S hS F ∧
        BigHOver.IsOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F ∧
        BigHOver.IsTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isSheaf_iff_generatorAlmostBlowUpConditions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVI.** A presheaf of sets on the big h category over `S` is a sheaf for the h
topology if and only if it is a Zariski sheaf, satisfies the sheaf condition for every flat proper
surjection of finite presentation of the site onto an affine object, and sends the almost blowup
squares of the site of the shapes of Examples 0EVG and 0EVH to cartesian squares of sets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_iff_generatorAlmostBlowUpConditions :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F ↔
      (IsZariskiSheaf B S hS F ∧ IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf B S hS F ∧
        IsOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F ∧ IsTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf_of_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVI, a sheaf satisfies condition (3).** A sheaf on the big h site over `S` sends an
almost blowup square of the site of the shape of Example 0EVG to a cartesian square of sets.

Neither the shape nor affineness of the base is used: this is Stacks 0EVD for an arbitrary
almost blowup square of the site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf_of_isSheaf
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F) :
    BigHOver.IsOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F
declarations.comment: only if, condition (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf_of_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVI, a sheaf satisfies condition (4).** A sheaf on the big h site over `S` sends an
almost blowup square of the site of the shape of Example 0EVH to a cartesian square of sets.

Neither the shape nor affineness of the base is used: this is Stacks 0EVD for an arbitrary
almost blowup square of the site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf_of_isSheaf
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F) :
    BigHOver.IsTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F
declarations.comment: only if, condition (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.zariski_and_affineFlatProperFP_and_generatorSquares_of_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVI, the necessity of all four conditions.** A sheaf on the big h site over `S` is a
sheaf for the Zariski topology, satisfies the equalizer condition for every morphism of the site
with affine target which is flat, proper, surjective and of finite presentation, and sends an
almost blowup square of the shape of Example 0EVG, respectively of Example 0EVH, to a cartesian
square of sets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem zariski_and_affineFlatProperFP_and_generatorSquares_of_isSheaf
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F) :
    BigHOver.IsZariskiSheaf B S hS F ∧
      BigHOver.IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationSheaf B S hS F ∧
      BigHOver.IsOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F ∧
      BigHOver.IsTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpSheaf B S hS F
declarations.comment: only if, all four conditions

declarations.name: Stacks.AlmostBlowUp.surjective_Γ_modificationToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVJ.** For the two-generator almost blowup square the ring map
`Γ(X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ Γ(X', 𝒪_{X'})` is surjective.

A global function on `X'` has a value on each of the two standard charts; the two agree on the
overlap, so `Stacks.AlmostBlowUp.exists_chartAwayMap_eq` produces an element of `A` with those
two values, and a global function is determined by its chart values.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_Γ_modificationToBase :
    letI := (twoGeneratorSquare A f₁ f₂).modificationGraded
    Function.Surjective (Scheme.Γ.map (modificationToBase A f₁ f₂).op).hom
declarations.comment: surjectivity

declarations.name: Stacks.AlmostBlowUp.isZero_hgroup_structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVJ.** `Hᵖ(X', 𝒪_{X'}) = 0` for `p > 0`.

The modification of the two-generator almost blowup square is covered by the two standard affine
opens `D₊(T₀)` and `D₊(T₁)`, whose intersection `D₊(T₀T₁)` is affine too. Mayer--Vietoris
therefore reduces positive-degree cohomology over the whole space to positive-degree cohomology
over those three affines, which vanishes by Serre, plus — in degree one — the surjectivity of
`Stacks.AlmostBlowUp.exists_restrict_add_restrict_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_hgroup_structureSheaf (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    letI := (twoGeneratorSquare A f₁ f₂).modificationGraded
    IsZero (Hgroup (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (modificationGrading A f₁ f₂)).ringCatSheaf ⊤ p
      (SheafOfModules.unit
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (modificationGrading A f₁ f₂)).ringCatSheaf))
declarations.comment: higher cohomology vanishing

declarations.name: Stacks.AlmostBlowUp.modificationToBase_ker_sq_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVJ.** The global functions on `Spec A` killed by the modification
of the two-generator almost blowup square form an ideal of square zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem modificationToBase_ker_sq_eq_bot (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f₁ f₂ : A) :
    letI := (twoGeneratorSquare A f₁ f₂).modificationGraded
    RingHom.ker (Scheme.Γ.map (modificationToBase A f₁ f₂).op).hom ^ 2 = ⊥
declarations.comment: kernel_square_zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.existsUnique_iso_frobeniusColimitSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVK.** Let `p` be a prime number, let `S` be a scheme over `𝔽_p` (that is, `p`
vanishes in `Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`), and let `(Sch/S)_h` be a big h site over `S` as in Stacks 0EU1.  There
is a unique sheaf `ℱ` on `(Sch/S)_h` such that `ℱ(X) = colim_F Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` for every quasi-compact
quasi-separated object `X`.

The identification is a morphism of presheaves `colim_F Γ(-, 𝒪) ⟶ ℱ` that is bijective on
quasi-compact quasi-separated objects, so naturality in `X` expresses compatibility with
restriction.  The first conjunct is existence and the second is uniqueness: two such sheaves are
isomorphic, by a unique isomorphism compatible with the identifications.

The sheaf constructed is `X ↦ Γ(Xᵃʷⁿ, 𝒪)`, global functions on the absolute weak normalization.
The proof does not use the criterion of Stacks 0EVI, whose sufficiency direction this
development lacks; it uses the absolute weak normalization instead.  The sheaf property comes
from the descent statements behind Stacks 0EVT and the h-sheaf criterion Stacks 0EU5.  The
comparison `colim_F Γ(X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ Γ(Xᵃʷⁿ, 𝒪)` is bijective on quasi-compact quasi-separated `X`.
On an affine open this is Stacks 0EVW, and the affine pieces glue over a finite affine covering
because the overlaps are quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_iso_frobeniusColimitSections (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hSp : Stacks.Frobenius.IsInCharacteristic S p) :
    (∃ (F : (BigHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (φ : frobeniusColimitSections B S hS p ⟶ F),
      Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F ∧
        ∀ X : BigHOver B S hS, CompactSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) →
          QuasiSeparatedSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) →
            Function.Bijective (φ.app (op X))) ∧
    ∀ {F G : (BigHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
      (φ : frobeniusColimitSections B S hS p ⟶ F) (ψ : frobeniusColimitSections B S hS p ⟶ G),
      Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) F →
      Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) G →
      (∀ X : BigHOver B S hS, CompactSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) →
        QuasiSeparatedSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) →
          Function.Bijective (φ.app (op X))) →
      (∀ X : BigHOver B S hS, CompactSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) →
        QuasiSeparatedSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) →
          Function.Bijective (ψ.app (op X))) →
      ∃! e : F ≅ G, φ ≫ e.hom = ψ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isSheaf_frobeniusLimitSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVL.** Let `p` be a prime number and let `S` be a scheme over `𝔽_p`, contained in a
big h site `B`.  Then `X ↦ lim_F Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, the limit of the `p`-power map on global functions,
is a sheaf on the big h site `(Sch/S)_h`.

The four conditions of the h sheaf criterion Stacks 0EVI hold for this presheaf; the sufficiency
direction of that criterion is `AlgebraicGeometry.affineAlmostBlowUpHSheafCriterion` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.generatorAlmostBlowUpSquaresSuffice`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_frobeniusLimitSections
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hChar : Stacks.Frobenius.IsInCharacteristic S p) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) (frobeniusLimitSections B S hS p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isStandardVCovering_limit_iff'
declarations.doc:
A morphism from a cofiltered limit of affine schemes over an affine base is a
standard V covering if and only if all stage morphisms are standard V coverings.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isStandardVCovering_limit_iff'
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I]
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine Y]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) [∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)]
    (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj Y)
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (f : c.pt ⟶ Y)
    (hf : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const I).map f) :
    (letI : IsAffine c.pt := Scheme.isAffine_of_isLimit c hc
     AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardVCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ c.pt) (fun _ ↦ f)) ↔
      ∀ i : I,
        (letI : IsAffine (((Functor.const I).obj Y).obj i) := by
           change IsAffine Y
           infer_instance
         AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardVCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ D.obj i)
           (fun _ ↦ t.app i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStandardVCovering_of_exists_isPHCovering_limit
declarations.doc:
A morphism of affine schemes which is a directed inverse limit over the base of affine ph
coverings is a standard V covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStandardVCovering_of_exists_isPHCovering_limit
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (h : ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
        (_ : IsDirectedOrder I) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
        (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
        (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D)
        (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p))
        (_ : IsColimit ((Scheme.Γ ⋙ forget CommRingCat).mapCocone (Cone.mk X p).op)),
      (p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f) ∧
        (∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsPHCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ D.obj i) (fun _ ↦ t.app i))) :
    IsStandardVCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ X) (fun _ ↦ f)
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPHCovering_limit_of_exists_isHCovering_limit
declarations.doc:
A presentation of a morphism of affine schemes as a directed inverse limit over the base of
affine h coverings is one by affine ph coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPHCovering_limit_of_exists_isHCovering_limit
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y] (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (h : ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
        (_ : IsDirectedOrder I) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
        (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
        (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D)
        (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p))
        (_ : IsColimit ((Scheme.Γ ⋙ forget CommRingCat).mapCocone (Cone.mk X p).op)),
      (p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f) ∧
        (∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsHCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ D.obj i) (fun _ ↦ t.app i))) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
      (_ : IsDirectedOrder I) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
      (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
      (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D)
      (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p))
      (_ : IsColimit ((Scheme.Γ ⋙ forget CommRingCat).mapCocone (Cone.mk X p).op)),
      (p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f) ∧
        (∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsPHCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ D.obj i) (fun _ ↦ t.app i))
declarations.comment: (3) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStandardVCovering_limit_tfae_unconditional
declarations.doc:
A morphism of affine schemes is a standard V covering exactly when it is a directed inverse
limit over the base of affine ph coverings, and exactly when it is such a limit of affine h
coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStandardVCovering_limit_tfae_unconditional
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsStandardVCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ X) (fun _ ↦ f),
      (∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
          (_ : IsDirectedOrder I) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
          (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
          (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D)
          (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p))
          (_ : IsColimit ((Scheme.Γ ⋙ forget CommRingCat).mapCocone (Cone.mk X p).op)),
        (p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f) ∧
          (∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)) ∧
          (∀ i, IsPHCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ D.obj i) (fun _ ↦ t.app i))),
      (∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
          (_ : IsDirectedOrder I) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
          (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
          (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D)
          (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p))
          (_ : IsColimit ((Scheme.Γ ⋙ forget CommRingCat).mapCocone (Cone.mk X p).op)),
        (p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f) ∧
          (∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)) ∧
          (∀ i, IsHCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ D.obj i) (fun _ ↦ t.app i)))]
declarations.comment: (1) implies (3); the other two implications are stated without the hard direction of Stacks 0ETR and tagged separately

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStandardVCovering_limit_equivalences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVP.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine schemes. Then `f` is a standard V
covering if and only if `X` is the limit of a directed inverse system of affine schemes `Xᵢ` over
`Y` with each `Xᵢ ⟶ Y` a ph covering, and that holds if and only if `X` is such a limit with each
`Xᵢ ⟶ Y` an h covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStandardVCovering_limit_equivalences {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (IsStandardVCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ X) (fun _ ↦ f) ↔
      ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
          (_ : IsDirectedOrder I) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
          (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
          (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D)
          (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p))
          (_ : IsColimit ((Scheme.Γ ⋙ forget CommRingCat).mapCocone (Cone.mk X p).op)),
        (p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f) ∧
          (∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)) ∧
          (∀ i, IsPHCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ D.obj i) (fun _ ↦ t.app i))) ∧
    ((∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
          (_ : IsDirectedOrder I) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
          (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
          (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D)
          (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p))
          (_ : IsColimit ((Scheme.Γ ⋙ forget CommRingCat).mapCocone (Cone.mk X p).op)),
        (p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f) ∧
          (∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)) ∧
          (∀ i, IsPHCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ D.obj i) (fun _ ↦ t.app i))) ↔
      ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
          (_ : IsDirectedOrder I) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
          (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
          (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D)
          (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p))
          (_ : IsColimit ((Scheme.Γ ⋙ forget CommRingCat).mapCocone (Cone.mk X p).op)),
        (p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f) ∧
          (∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i)) ∧
          (∀ i, IsHCovering (fun _ : Unit ↦ D.obj i) (fun _ ↦ t.app i)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVSheaf_of_isSheafFor_vCovering_of_isLimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVQ.** A presheaf of sets on schemes which satisfies the sheaf condition for
every h covering and which is limit preserving in the sense of Stacks 05LX over every base
satisfies the sheaf condition for every V covering.

An h covering is a family of morphisms locally of finite presentation satisfying one of the
two equivalent conditions of Stacks 0ETR, and the condition used here is the second: being a V
covering. The equivalence with the first condition, being a ph covering, is Stacks 0ETR, which
rests on `AlgebraicGeometry.StandardVCoveringHasPHRefinement` and so on the Raynaud-Gruson
flattening theorem; with the first condition in place of the second the statement below would
have to carry that hypothesis, since the predicate cannot be named this far up the import
graph.
declarations.statement:
theorem isVSheaf_of_isSheafFor_vCovering_of_isLimitPreserving (F : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
    (hH : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (I : Type (max u v)) (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (g : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T),
      (∀ i, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (g i)) → IsVCovering X g →
        (Presieve.ofArrows X g).IsSheafFor F)
    (hLP : ∀ Y : Scheme.{u}, Scheme.IsLimitPreserving Y ((Over.forget Y).op ⋙ F)) :
    IsVSheaf.{u, max u v, w} F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.isVSheafOver_of_isSheafFor_vCovering_of_isLimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
A functor on the schemes over `S` which satisfies the sheaf condition for every h covering
of `Sch/S` and which is limit preserving in the sense of Stacks 05LX satisfies the sheaf condition
for every V covering of `Sch/S`.

The h coverings are taken in the form of the second of the two equivalent conditions of
Stacks 0ETR: the hypothesis `hH` is the sheaf condition for the families of morphisms which are
locally of finite presentation and are V coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isVSheafOver_of_isSheafFor_vCovering_of_isLimitPreserving (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
    (hH : ∀ (T : Over S) (I : Type (max u v)) (X : I → Over S) (g : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T),
      (∀ i, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (g i).left) → IsVCoveringOver g →
        (Presieve.ofArrows X g).IsSheafFor F)
    (hLP : Scheme.IsLimitPreserving S F) :
    IsVSheafOver.{w, u, max u v} F
declarations.comment: the relative form, for a contravariant functor on the category of all schemes over `S`, which is how the source states it. The sheaf property for the h topology is read, as in the absolute case, through the second of the two equivalent conditions of Stacks 0ETR: the hypothesis is the sheaf condition for the families which are locally of finite presentation and are V coverings. Stacks 0ETR, `AlgebraicGeometry.isPHCovering_iff_isVCovering`, is what identifies that hypothesis with the ph reading fixed by `AlgebraicGeometry.IsHCovering`; it is proved in this library, further down the import graph than this file

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.exists_unique_isHSheaf_isVSheaf_extension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVR.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `P` be a full subcategory of `Sch/S` satisfying
conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 0EUW and let `F : Pᵒᵖ ⥤ Set` be an h sheaf whose values on a
directed inverse limit of affine objects form the filtered colimit of its values on the system.
Then `F` extends to a contravariant functor `F'` on all schemes over `S` which satisfies the
sheaf property for the h topology, is limit preserving in the sense of Stacks 05LX and satisfies
the sheaf property for the V topology, and any functor on `Sch/S` which is an h sheaf, is limit
preserving and restricts to `F` is isomorphic to `F'`.

This is the whole of the remark, the V clause included.  Properties (a) and (b) of the extension
are Stacks 0EV3, `isHSheaf_extension` and `isLimitPreserving_extension`; the
uniqueness is Stacks 0EUW, `exists_unique_extension`; and the V sheaf property is
Stacks 0EVQ read through Stacks 0ETR, by
`isVSheafOver_of_isHSheaf_of_preservesAffineLimits`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_isHSheaf_isVSheaf_extension
    (P : ObjectProperty (Over S))
    (hP1 : HasAffineOpens P) (hP2 : HasFinitePresentationAffines P)
    (F : P.FullSubcategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w (u + 1)))
    (hF : IsHCoveringSheafOnSubcategory.{max w (u + 1), u, u} P F)
    (hbF : PreservesAffineLimitsOnSubcategory P F) :
    ∃ (F' : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w (u + 1))) (_ : IsHSheaf.{max w (u + 1), u, v} F')
      (_ : PreservesAffineLimits F') (_ : IsVSheafOver.{max w (u + 1), u, v} F')
      (_ : P.ι.op ⋙ F' ≅ F),
      ∀ F'' : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w (u + 1)), IsHSheaf.{max w (u + 1), u, u} F'' →
        PreservesAffineLimits F'' → (P.ι.op ⋙ F'' ≅ F) → Nonempty (F' ≅ F'')
declarations.comment: the whole of the remark: the extension of an h sheaf on the big h category over `S` which carries a directed inverse limit of affine objects to a filtered colimit, together with its uniqueness and every property the remark asserts of it. The extension is an h sheaf on all schemes over `S`, is limit preserving in the sense of Stacks 05LX, satisfies the sheaf property for the V topology, restricts to the given functor, and is the only functor which is an h sheaf, is limit preserving and restricts to it, up to isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections
declarations.doc:
On a big ph site, global functions on absolute weak normalizations form a sheaf.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_hom_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections`, this shows
that the canonical map from the structure sheaf exhibits this sheaf as its ph sheafification.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections (B : BigPHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigPHOver.topology B S hS) (absoluteWeakNormalizationSections B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections
declarations.doc:
On a big ph site, global functions on absolute weak normalizations form a sheaf.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_hom_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections`, this shows
that the canonical map from the structure sheaf exhibits this sheaf as its ph sheafification.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections (B : BigPHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigPHOver.topology B S hS) (absoluteWeakNormalizationSections B S hS)
declarations.comment: ph topology, the sheaf property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_hom_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVU**, the ph case. On a big ph site over `S`, global functions on
absolute weak normalizations are the sheafification of the structure sheaf: every map from the
structure sheaf to a sheaf of rings factors uniquely through the canonical map. The other half
of the statement, that the target is a sheaf, is Stacks 0EVT.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_hom_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections
    (G : (BigPHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u})
    (hG : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigPHOver.topology B S hS) G)
    (α : (BigPHOver.toScheme B S hS).op ⋙ Scheme.Γ ⟶ G) :
    ∃! χ : absoluteWeakNormalizationSections B S hS ⟶ G,
      absoluteWeakNormalizationSectionsMap (BigPHOver.toScheme B S hS) ≫ χ = α
declarations.comment: ph topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isSheaf_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVU**, the sheaf property in the h case. On a big h site over `S`,
global functions on absolute weak normalizations form a sheaf for the h topology.

This is the h analogue of Stacks 0EVT, and is proved from the same two descent statements —
Zariski descent and descent along a proper surjection onto an affine — through the h sheaf
criterion of Stacks 0EU5, whose second condition carries the extra hypothesis that the proper
surjection is of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS)
      (absoluteWeakNormalizationSectionsOver (BigHOver.toScheme B S hS))
declarations.comment: h topology, the sheaf property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.existsUnique_hom_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVU**, the h case. On a big h site over `S`, global functions on
absolute weak normalizations are the sheafification of the structure sheaf: every map from the
structure sheaf to a sheaf of rings factors uniquely through the canonical map. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isSheaf_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections`, which is the other half
of the statement, this says that the rule `X ↦ Γ(Xᵃʷⁿ, 𝒪)` is the sheafification of the
structure sheaf on the big h site.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_hom_absoluteWeakNormalizationSections
    (G : (BigHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u})
    (hG : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) G)
    (α : (BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).op ⋙ Scheme.Γ ⟶ G) :
    ∃! χ : absoluteWeakNormalizationSectionsOver (BigHOver.toScheme B S hS) ⟶ G,
      absoluteWeakNormalizationSectionsMap (BigHOver.toScheme B S hS) ≫ χ = α
declarations.comment: h topology, the universal property of the sheafification

declarations.name: isAbsolutelyWeaklyNormalRing_iff_perfectRing
declarations.doc:
An algebra over `𝐅_p`, for `p` prime, is absolutely weakly normal if and only if its
Frobenius endomorphism is bijective.
declarations.statement:
lemma isAbsolutelyWeaklyNormalRing_iff_perfectRing
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Algebra (ZMod p) A] :
    IsAbsolutelyWeaklyNormalRing A ↔ PerfectRing A p

declarations.name: Algebra.existsUnique_frobeniusColimit_iso_absoluteWeakNormalization
declarations.doc:
For `p` prime and `A` an algebra over `ZMod p`, the colimit of the Frobenius sequence of `A`
is the absolute weak normalization of `A`, by a unique isomorphism compatible with the canonical
maps out of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_frobeniusColimit_iso_absoluteWeakNormalization
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra (ZMod p) A] :
    letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
    ∃! e : colimit (frobeniusDiagram p A) ≅
        CommRingCat.of (AbsoluteWeakNormalization A),
      colimit.ι (frobeniusDiagram p A) 0 ≫ e.hom =
        CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (AbsoluteWeakNormalization A))
declarations.comment: frobenius_colimit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.exists_bijective_hom_frobeniusColimitSections_of_isSheafification
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of Stacks Project, Tag 0EVW.** Let `p` be a prime number and let `S` be a scheme
over `𝔽_p`, that is, a scheme in which `p` vanishes on global functions.  Let `(Sch/S)_h` be a
big h site over `S` as in Stacks 0EU1.  Let `G` be the h sheafification of the structure sheaf
`𝒪`: a sheaf of rings together with a map `α : 𝒪 ⟶ G` initial among the maps from `𝒪` to sheaves
of rings.  Then the sections of `G` over a quasi-compact quasi-separated object `X` are
`colim_F Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.

The identification is given by a map of presheaves `colim_F Γ(-, 𝒪) ⟶ G` which agrees with `α`
on the stage `0` of the Frobenius tower and is bijective over every quasi-compact quasi-separated
object; naturality is compatibility with restriction.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_bijective_hom_frobeniusColimitSections_of_isSheafification (p : ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime) (hSp : Stacks.Frobenius.IsInCharacteristic S p)
    (G : (BigHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u})
    (hG : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) G)
    (α : (BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).op ⋙ Scheme.Γ.{u} ⟶ G)
    (hα : ∀ H : (BigHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u},
      Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) H →
      ∀ β : (BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).op ⋙ Scheme.Γ.{u} ⟶ H, ∃! χ : G ⟶ H, α ≫ χ = β) :
    ∃ φ : frobeniusColimitSections B S hS p ⟶ G ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{u},
      (∀ (X : BigHOver B S hS) (a : Γ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X, ⊤)),
        φ.app (op X) (colimitStage B S hS p 0 X a) = α.app (op X) a) ∧
      ∀ X : BigHOver B S hS, CompactSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) →
        QuasiSeparatedSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) →
          Function.Bijective (φ.app (op X))
declarations.comment: the h sheafification of the structure sheaf on qcqs objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusColimit_absoluteWeakNormalization_and_hSheafificationSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EVW.** Let `p` be a prime number.

(1) If `A` is an algebra over `𝔽_p`, then `colim_F A = A^{awn}`: the colimit of the Frobenius
tower of `A` is the absolute weak normalization of `A`, by a unique isomorphism compatible with
the canonical maps out of `A`.

(2) If `S` is a scheme over `𝔽_p` and `(Sch/S)_h` is a big h site over `S` as in Stacks 0EU1,
then the h sheafification of the structure sheaf `𝒪` — a sheaf of rings `G` with a map
`α : 𝒪 ⟶ G` initial among the maps from `𝒪` to sheaves of rings — sends a quasi-compact
quasi-separated object `X` to `colim_F Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, by an identification agreeing with `α` on the
stage `0` of the Frobenius tower.
declarations.statement:
public theorem frobeniusColimit_absoluteWeakNormalization_and_hSheafificationSections (p : ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime) :
    letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
    (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra (ZMod p) A],
      ∃! e : colimit (Algebra.frobeniusDiagram p A) ≅
          CommRingCat.of (Algebra.AbsoluteWeakNormalization A),
        colimit.ι (Algebra.frobeniusDiagram p A) 0 ≫ e.hom =
          CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (Algebra.AbsoluteWeakNormalization A))) ∧
    (∀ (B : BigHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S),
      Stacks.Frobenius.IsInCharacteristic S p →
      ∀ (G : (BigHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}),
        Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) G →
      ∀ α : (BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).op ⋙ Scheme.Γ.{u} ⟶ G,
        (∀ H : (BigHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u},
          Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) H →
          ∀ β : (BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).op ⋙ Scheme.Γ.{u} ⟶ H, ∃! χ : G ⟶ H, α ≫ χ = β) →
        ∃ φ : BigHOver.frobeniusColimitSections B S hS p ⟶
            G ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{u},
          (∀ (X : BigHOver B S hS) (a : Γ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X, ⊤)),
            φ.app (op X) (BigHOver.colimitStage B S hS p 0 X a) = α.app (op X) a) ∧
          ∀ X : BigHOver B S hS, CompactSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) →
            QuasiSeparatedSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) →
              Function.Bijective (φ.app (op X)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MayerVietoris.isIso_derivedCSquare_of_isPushout
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVY.** If the sheafified representables of the square form a pushout square and
`h_E^# ⟶ h_Y^#` is a monomorphism, then the canonical natural transformation of Stacks 0F16 is
an isomorphism, so that the Mayer-Vietoris triangle is distinguished and functorial for every
object of the derived category of module sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCSquare_of_isPushout (sq : Square S.C)
    (hpushout : (sq.map (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda S.J)).IsPushout)
    (hmono : Mono ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda S.J).map sq.f₁₂)) :
    IsIso (CanonicalMapOfComplexes.derivedCSquareData.{u, v}
      (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O)) sq).derivedCSquare

declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.PresheafSquare.isIso_derivedCSquare_of_isPushout
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVZ.** If the sheafifications of a square of presheaves of sets form a pushout
square and `D^# ⟶ F^#` is a monomorphism, then the canonical natural transformation of
Stacks 0F16 from derived sections over `G` to the mapping cocone is an isomorphism, so that the
Mayer–Vietoris triangle is defined at every object of the derived category of abelian
sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCSquare_of_isPushout
    (hpushout : (sq.map (presheafToSheaf J (Type u))).IsPushout)
    (hmono : Mono ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).map sq.f₁₂)) :
    IsIso (derivedCSquareData J sq).derivedCSquare
declarations.comment: the canonical comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.PresheafSquare.cSquareTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVZ.** The Mayer–Vietoris triangle of a square of presheaves of sets whose
sheafifications form a pushout square with monomorphic `D^# ⟶ F^#` is a distinguished triangle
of the derived category of abelian groups, at every object of the derived category of abelian
sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem cSquareTriangle_distinguished (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u})) :
    cSquareTriangle J sq hpushout hmono K ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
declarations.comment: the triangle is distinguished

declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.PresheafSquare.cSquareTriangle_functorial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EVZ, the functoriality in the derived object.** Every morphism of derived objects
induces a unique morphism of Mayer–Vietoris triangles whose three components are the maps
induced on derived sections and on the mapping cocone.
declarations.statement:
theorem cSquareTriangle_functorial
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u})} (f : K ⟶ K') :
    ∃! t : cSquareTriangle J sq hpushout hmono K ⟶ cSquareTriangle J sq hpushout hmono K',
      t.hom₁ = ((derivedCSquareData J sq).derivedSections sq.X₄).map f ∧
        t.hom₂ = ((derivedCSquareData J sq).sectionsData.biprodFunctor sq).map f ∧
        t.hom₃ = ((derivedCSquareData J sq).derivedSections sq.X₁).map f
declarations.comment: functoriality of the triangle in the derived object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigPHOver.isPullback_map_of_blowUpSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EW1.** Let `F` be a sheaf of sets on a big ph site over `S`. For every
blow up square in that site — a closed centre `Z ⊆ X` of finite presentation, the blowup
`b : X' ⟶ X` of `X` in `Z`, and the exceptional divisor `E = b⁻¹(Z)` — the square of restriction
maps `F(X) → F(Z) → F(E)` and `F(X) → F(X') → F(E)` is cartesian in the category of sets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPullback_map_of_blowUpSquare
    (B : BigPHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigPHOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigPHOver.topology B S hS) F)
    {X X' Z E : BigPHOver B S hS}
    (b : X' ⟶ X) (z : Z ⟶ X) (p : E ⟶ X') (e : E ⟶ Z)
    (I : ((BigPHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X).IdealSheafData)
    (hI : FinitePresentation I.subschemeι)
    (hb : Nonempty (Over.mk ((BigPHOver.toScheme B S hS).map b) ≅ Over.mk (blowUpToBase I)))
    (hZ : Nonempty (Over.mk ((BigPHOver.toScheme B S hS).map z) ≅ Over.mk I.subschemeι))
    (hSquare : IsPullback
      ((BigPHOver.toScheme B S hS).map e) ((BigPHOver.toScheme B S hS).map p)
      ((BigPHOver.toScheme B S hS).map z) ((BigPHOver.toScheme B S hS).map b)) :
    IsPullback (F.map z.op) (F.map b.op) (F.map e.op) (F.map p.op)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigPHOver.bijective_map_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EW2.** Restriction of a ph sheaf along a thickening is a bijection
of sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem BigPHOver.bijective_map_of_isThickening
    (B : BigPHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : Sheaf (BigPHOver.topology B S hS) (Type v))
    {X X' : BigPHOver B S hS} (i : X ⟶ X')
    (hi : Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening ((BigPHOver.toScheme B S hS).map i)) :
    Function.Bijective (F.obj.map i.op)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_longExactSequence_blowUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EW3.** Let `X` be a scheme, `K` an object of `D⁺(X_étale)` (a complex
of abelian sheaves on the small étale site, bounded below: `K.IsGE n`) with torsion cohomology
sheaves, and `Z ⊆ X` the closed subscheme cut out by a quasi-coherent ideal `I` of finite type
(finitely generated on every affine open). In the blowup square
```
E --j--> X'
|π       |b
v        v
Z --i--> X
```
(`X'` the blowup of `X` in `I`, `E = b⁻¹(Z)` the exceptional divisor) there is a long exact
sequence
`H^p(X, K) ⟶ H^p(X', K|_{X'}) × H^p(Z, K|_Z) ⟶ H^p(E, K|_E) ⟶ H^{p+1}(X, K) ⟶ ⋯`
whose first map is `x ↦ (x|_{X'}, x|_Z)`, whose second map is `(x', z) ↦ x'|_E - z|_E` (the two
restrictions read in `H^p(E, K|_E)`, `K|_E = (j ≫ b)⁻¹ K`, through
`j⁻¹ b⁻¹ K ≅ K|_E ≅ π⁻¹ i⁻¹ K`), and whose third map is a connecting map `δ`, exact at all three
places for every `p`. Here `H^p(Y, M) = Hom(ℤ_Y[-p], M)` in `D(Y_étale)`
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleDerivedCohomology`) and `K|_Y` is the derived inverse image.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_longExactSequence_blowUp {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : ∀ U : X.affineOpens, (I.ideal U).FG)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})) (n : ℤ)
    (hK : K.IsGE n)
    (hT : Stacks.Torsion.torsionCohomologyProperty.{u + 1} X.smallEtaleTopology K) :
    ∃ δ : ∀ p : ℤ, etaleDerivedCohomology.{u, 0} (exceptionalDivisor I) p
        ((etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0}
          ((exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι ≫ blowUpToBase I)).obj K) →+
      etaleDerivedCohomology.{u, 0} X (p + 1) K,
    ∀ p : ℤ,
      Function.Exact
        (fun x : etaleDerivedCohomology.{u, 0} X p K ↦
          (etaleDerivedCohomologyRestriction.{u, 0} (blowUpToBase I) p K x,
            etaleDerivedCohomologyRestriction.{u, 0} I.subschemeι p K x))
        (fun y : etaleDerivedCohomology.{u, 0} (blowUp I) p
              ((etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (blowUpToBase I)).obj K) ×
            etaleDerivedCohomology.{u, 0} I.subscheme p
              ((etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} I.subschemeι).obj K) ↦
          etaleDerivedCohomologyRestriction.{u, 0} (exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι p _ y.1 ≫
              (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImageCompIso'.{u, 0} (exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι
                (blowUpToBase I) _ rfl).inv.app K -
            etaleDerivedCohomologyRestriction.{u, 0} (exceptionalDivisorToCenter I) p _ y.2 ≫
              (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImageCompIso'.{u, 0} (exceptionalDivisorToCenter I)
                I.subschemeι _ (isPullback_exceptionalDivisor I).w).inv.app K) ∧
      Function.Exact
        (fun y : etaleDerivedCohomology.{u, 0} (blowUp I) p
              ((etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (blowUpToBase I)).obj K) ×
            etaleDerivedCohomology.{u, 0} I.subscheme p
              ((etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} I.subschemeι).obj K) ↦
          etaleDerivedCohomologyRestriction.{u, 0} (exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι p _ y.1 ≫
              (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImageCompIso'.{u, 0} (exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι
                (blowUpToBase I) _ rfl).inv.app K -
            etaleDerivedCohomologyRestriction.{u, 0} (exceptionalDivisorToCenter I) p _ y.2 ≫
              (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImageCompIso'.{u, 0} (exceptionalDivisorToCenter I)
                I.subschemeι _ (isPullback_exceptionalDivisor I).w).inv.app K)
        (δ p) ∧
      Function.Exact (δ p)
        (fun x : etaleDerivedCohomology.{u, 0} X (p + 1) K ↦
          (etaleDerivedCohomologyRestriction.{u, 0} (blowUpToBase I) (p + 1) K x,
            etaleDerivedCohomologyRestriction.{u, 0} I.subschemeι (p + 1) K x))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_distTriang_blowUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EW5.** Let `X` be a scheme and `Z ⊆ X` the closed subscheme cut out by
a quasi-coherent ideal `I` of finite type (finitely generated on every affine open), with blowup
square
```
E --j--> X'
|π       |b
v        v
Z --i--> X
```
(`X'` the blowup of `X` in `I`, `E = b⁻¹(Z)` the exceptional divisor) and `c = i ∘ π = b ∘ j`.
For every `K` in `D⁺(X_étale)` (a complex of abelian sheaves on the small étale site, bounded
below: `K.IsGE n`) with torsion cohomology sheaves there is a distinguished triangle
`K ⟶ Ri_*(K|_Z) ⊕ Rb_*(K|_{X'}) ⟶ Rc_*(K|_E) ⟶ K[1]`
in `D(X_étale)`, where `K|_Y` is the derived inverse image. Its first map is formed by the two
adjunction units and its second map is the difference of the two comparison maps
`Ri_*(K|_Z) ⟶ Rc_*(K|_E)` (along `c = i ∘ π`) and `Rb_*(K|_{X'}) ⟶ Rc_*(K|_E)` (along
`c = b ∘ j`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_distTriang_blowUp {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : ∀ U : X.affineOpens, (I.ideal U).FG)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})) (n : ℤ)
    (hK : K.IsGE n)
    (hT : Stacks.Torsion.torsionCohomologyProperty.{u + 1} X.smallEtaleTopology K) :
    ∃ δ : (etaleAbelianDerivedDirectImage.{u, 0}
          ((exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι ≫ blowUpToBase I)).obj
        ((etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0}
          ((exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι ≫ blowUpToBase I)).obj K) ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk (etaleAbelianDerivedSquareUnits.{u, 0} I.subschemeι (blowUpToBase I) K)
        (etaleAbelianDerivedSquareDifference.{u, 0} I.subschemeι (blowUpToBase I)
          (exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι (exceptionalDivisorToCenter I)
          ((exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι ≫ blowUpToBase I)
          (isPullback_exceptionalDivisor I).w rfl K) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_gluing_blowUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EW6.** Let `X` be a scheme and `Z ⊆ X` the closed subscheme cut out by
a quasi-coherent ideal `I` of finite type (finitely generated on every affine open), with blowup
square
```
E --j--> X'
|π       |b
v        v
Z --i--> X
```
(`X'` the blowup of `X` in `I`, `E = b⁻¹(Z)` the exceptional divisor, `c = i ∘ π = b ∘ j`).
Let `K'` be an object of `D⁺(X'_étale)` (bounded below: `K'.IsGE n₁`) with torsion cohomology
sheaves, `L` an object of `D⁺(Z_étale)` (`L.IsGE n₂`), and `γ : K'|_E ≅ L|_E` an isomorphism,
where `N|_Y` is the derived inverse image. Then there are an object `K` of `D⁺(X_étale)` and
isomorphisms `f : K|_{X'} ≅ K'`, `g : K|_Z ≅ L` such that `γ = g|_E ∘ f⁻¹|_E` (both sides read
through the canonical identifications `(K|_{X'})|_E ≅ K|_E ≅ (K|_Z)|_E`). Moreover, given an
object `M` of `D⁺(X_étale)` with torsion cohomology sheaves and morphisms `α : K' ⟶ M|_{X'}`,
`β : L ⟶ M|_Z` with `α|_E = β|_E ∘ γ` (read through `(M|_{X'})|_E ≅ M|_E ≅ (M|_Z)|_E`), there is a
morphism `K ⟶ M` in `D(X_étale)` whose restriction to `X'` is `α ∘ f` and whose restriction to
`Z` is `β ∘ g`.

The source writes the last morphism as `M ⟶ K` with restrictions `a ∘ f`, `b ∘ g`; these are
typos for `α ∘ f : K|_{X'} ⟶ M|_{X'}` and `β ∘ g : K|_Z ⟶ M|_Z`, which forces the direction
`K ⟶ M`, the direction of the morphism of triangles in the source's proof. The source's
hypothesis that `L` has torsion cohomology sheaves is not needed and is omitted.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_gluing_blowUp {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : ∀ U : X.affineOpens, (I.ideal U).FG)
    (K' : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (blowUp I).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})) (n₁ : ℤ)
    (hK' : K'.IsGE n₁)
    (hK'T : Stacks.Torsion.torsionCohomologyProperty.{u + 1} (blowUp I).smallEtaleTopology K')
    (L : DerivedCategory (Sheaf I.subscheme.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})) (n₂ : ℤ)
    (hL : L.IsGE n₂)
    (γ : (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι).obj K' ≅
      (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (exceptionalDivisorToCenter I)).obj L) :
    ∃ (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))
      (_ : K.IsGE (min n₁ n₂))
      (f : (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (blowUpToBase I)).obj K ≅ K')
      (g : (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} I.subschemeι).obj K ≅ L),
      γ.hom = (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι).map f.inv ≫
          (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImageCompIso'.{u, 0} (exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι
            (blowUpToBase I) _ rfl).inv.app K ≫
          (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImageCompIso'.{u, 0} (exceptionalDivisorToCenter I)
            I.subschemeι _ (isPullback_exceptionalDivisor I).w).hom.app K ≫
          (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (exceptionalDivisorToCenter I)).map g.hom ∧
      ∀ (M : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})) (m : ℤ),
        M.IsGE m →
        Stacks.Torsion.torsionCohomologyProperty.{u + 1} X.smallEtaleTopology M →
        ∀ (α : K' ⟶ (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (blowUpToBase I)).obj M)
          (β : L ⟶ (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} I.subschemeι).obj M),
          (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι).map α ≫
              (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImageCompIso'.{u, 0} (exceptionalIdeal I).subschemeι
                (blowUpToBase I) _ rfl).inv.app M ≫
              (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImageCompIso'.{u, 0} (exceptionalDivisorToCenter I)
                I.subschemeι _ (isPullback_exceptionalDivisor I).w).hom.app M =
            γ.hom ≫ (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (exceptionalDivisorToCenter I)).map β →
          ∃ φ : K ⟶ M, (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (blowUpToBase I)).map φ = f.hom ≫ α ∧
            (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} I.subschemeι).map φ = g.hom ≫ β

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleInverseImage_isZariskiSheaf_h
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EW8, the Zariski half of the h sheaf condition.** For a sheaf of sets `F` on the
small étale site of `S`, the presheaf underlying `π_S⁻¹F` — by the sections formula the rule
`X ↦ Γ(X_ét, f_X⁻¹F)` of the source — satisfies descent for every family of the big h category
over `S` whose underlying family of schemes is a Zariski covering.

A Zariski covering family is an fpqc covering family, and `π_S⁻¹F` is a sheaf for the fpqc
topology of the slice by Stacks 09XN,
`AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleToSmallEtale_inverseImage_isSheaf_fpqc`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleInverseImage_isZariskiSheaf_h :
    BigHOver.IsZariskiSheaf B S hS
      ((bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) S hS).inverseImage.obj
        F).obj
declarations.comment: the Zariski half of the h sheaf condition, condition (1) of Stacks 0EU5; descent along a proper surjective morphism of finite presentation is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleInverseImage_isSheaf_h_and_isIso_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EW8.** For a sheaf of sets `F` on the small étale site of `S`, the rule
`(f : X ⟶ S) ↦ Γ(X_ét, f⁻¹F)` — the presheaf underlying `π_S⁻¹F` on the big étale category over
`S`, by the sections formula `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleInverseImageSectionsIso` and Stacks 09XN —
is a sheaf for the h topology of the big h category over `S`, and the unit of `ε_S⁻¹ ⊣ ε_{S,*}`
at `π_S⁻¹F` is an isomorphism, so that this h sheaf is `ε_S⁻¹π_S⁻¹F`.

The h sheaf condition is Stacks 0EU5: the Zariski half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleInverseImage_isZariskiSheaf_h` and the proper half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleInverseImage_isProperFinitePresentationSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleInverseImage_isSheaf_h_and_isIso_unit :
    Presieve.IsSheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS)
        ((bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) S hS).inverseImage.obj
          F).obj ∧
      IsIso ((hToBigEtaleMorphism B (B.obj S hS)).adj.unit.app
        ((bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) S hS).inverseImage.obj F))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hToBigEtaleMorphism

The comparison `ε_X` from the big h topos to the big étale topos, induced by the identity
functor on the common slice category.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigHBigEtale_pushforwardCommIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EW9, first diagram.** The square formed by the big h and big étale base-change
morphisms over the change-of-topology comparisons `ε_X` and `ε_Y` commutes on direct
images.

public def bigHBigEtale_pushforwardCommIso (B : BigHSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Schemes} (f : X ⟶ Y) :

declarations.comment: the big h–big étale square
