declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_bigHSmallEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EWA.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of the big h site. Then the base change
map `a_Y⁻¹ ∘ f_{small,*} ⟶ f_{big,h,*} ∘ a_X⁻¹` of the square of topoi of Stacks 0EW9 is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_bigHSmallEtaleBaseChange [IsProper (B.inclusion.map f)] :
    IsIso (bigHSmallEtaleBaseChange B f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hTorsionComparison_smallEtaleInclusion
declarations.doc:
For an object `X` of the big h site and an abelian torsion sheaf `F` on `X_étale`,
`ε_{X,*}a_X⁻¹F = π_X⁻¹F` — the unit `π_X⁻¹F ⟶ ε_{X,*}ε_X⁻¹π_X⁻¹F` of the change of topology is an
isomorphism — and `R^i ε_{X,*}(a_X⁻¹F) = 0` for `i > 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hTorsionComparison_smallEtaleInclusion (X : (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).Scheme)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property) Ab.{u + 1})
    (hF : Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property) F) :
    IsIso ((abelianComparisonAdjunction B.precoverage
        (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).precoverage
        (BigHSite.etalePrecoverage_le_precoverage B) X).unit.app
        (((SmallEtale.inclusion (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property).sheafPullback
          Ab.{u + 1} (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
          ((hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).topology.over X)).obj F)) ∧
      ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → IsZero (((abelianComparisonPushforward B.precoverage
          (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).precoverage
          (BigHSite.etalePrecoverage_le_precoverage B) X).rightDerived i).obj
        ((abelianComparisonPullback B.precoverage
          (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).precoverage X).obj
          (((SmallEtale.inclusion (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property).sheafPullback
            Ab.{u + 1} (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
            ((hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).topology.over X)).obj F)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hTorsionHigherSmallEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
For a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of the big h site and an abelian torsion sheaf `F` on
`X_étale`, the base change map `a_Y⁻¹(R^i f_{small,*}F) ⟶ R^i f_{big,h,*}(a_X⁻¹F)` is an
isomorphism for every `i`. The map is `AlgebraicGeometry.higherSmallEtaleFineBaseChange`, the
degree `i` cohomology of the derived base change map
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedSmallEtaleFineBaseChange` at `F` placed in degree zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_hTorsionHigherSmallEtaleBaseChange
    {X Y : (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsProper ((hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).inclusion.map f))
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property) Ab.{u + 1})
    (hF : Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property) F)
    (i : ℕ) :
    IsIso (higherSmallEtaleFineBaseChange (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) B.precoverage
      (BigHSite.etalePrecoverage_le_precoverage B)
      (fun X F => (smallEtaleInverseImage_isSheaf_h_and_isIso_unit B X.1 X.2 F).1)
      (BigHSite.properDirectImageComparison B)
      (BigHSite.exists_properRefinement B) f F i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hTorsionDerivedComparisonUnit_app
declarations.doc:
For an object `X` of the big h site and `K` in `D⁺(X_étale)` with torsion cohomology sheaves,
the map `π_X⁻¹K ⟶ Rε_{X,*}(a_X⁻¹K)`, the derived unit of the change of topology at `π_X⁻¹K`, is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_hTorsionDerivedComparisonUnit_app (X : (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).Scheme)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus
      (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property) Ab.{u + 1}))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K)) :
    IsIso ((derivedComparisonUnit (hEtaleCohomologyComparison B) X).app
      (((SmallEtale.inclusion (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property).sheafPullback
        Ab.{u + 1} (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
        ((hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).topology.over X)).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hTorsionDerivedSmallEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
For a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of the big h site and `K` in `D⁺(X_étale)` with torsion
cohomology sheaves, the base change map `a_Y⁻¹(Rf_{small,*}K) ⟶ Rf_{big,h,*}(a_X⁻¹K)` of the
square of topoi `a_Y ∘ f_h = f_small ∘ a_X`, `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedSmallEtaleFineBaseChange`,
is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_hTorsionDerivedSmallEtaleBaseChange
    {X Y : (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsProper ((hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).inclusion.map f))
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus
      (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property) Ab.{u + 1}))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K)) :
    IsIso (derivedSmallEtaleFineBaseChange (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) B.precoverage
      (BigHSite.etalePrecoverage_le_precoverage B)
      (fun X F => (smallEtaleInverseImage_isSheaf_h_and_isIso_unit B X.1 X.2 F).1)
      (BigHSite.properDirectImageComparison B)
      (BigHSite.exists_properRefinement B) f K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hDerivedSmallEtaleUnit
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme, an object of a big h site `B`. For `K` in `D⁺(X_étale)` with torsion
cohomology sheaves, the map `K ⟶ Ra_{X,*}a_X⁻¹K` is an isomorphism, with
`a_X : Sh((Sch/X)_h) ⟶ Sh(X_étale)` the composite of the change of topology
`ε_X : Sh((Sch/X)_h) ⟶ Sh((Sch/X)_étale)` and the projection
`π_X : Sh((Sch/X)_étale) ⟶ Sh(X_étale)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_hDerivedSmallEtaleUnit (X : (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).Scheme)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus
      (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property) Ab.{u + 1}))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K)) :
    IsIso (hDerivedSmallEtaleUnit B X K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hCohomologyComparisonIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EWH (1).** Let `X` be a scheme, an object of a big h site `B`, and let `F` be a
torsion abelian sheaf on `X_étale`. For every `q`,

`H^q(X_étale, F) = H^q_h(X, a_X⁻¹F)`,

where `a_X⁻¹F = ε_X⁻¹π_X⁻¹F` is the h sheafification of the pullback of `F` to the big étale site
over `X`. The isomorphism is the canonical one: the degree `q` cohomology, at `F` placed in degree
zero, of `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedGlobalSectionsFineComparisonIso`, the pullback along `a_X` on
derived global sections.
declarations.statement:
public def hCohomologyComparisonIso
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hF : Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property) F)
    (q : ℕ) :
    (((sheafSections (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
        (op (SmallEtale.final (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property))).rightDerived q).obj
        F ≅
      ((Stacks.globalSectionsOver B.precoverage.toGrothendieck X).rightDerived q).obj
        ((abelianComparisonPullback B.precoverage (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).precoverage X).obj
          (((SmallEtale.inclusion (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property).sheafPullback
            AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
            ((hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).topology.over X)).obj F))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hCohomologyComparisonPlusIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EWH (2).** Let `X` be a scheme, an object of a big h site `B`, and let `K` be an
object of `D⁺(X_étale)` whose cohomology sheaves are torsion. For every `q`,

`H^q(X_étale, K) = H^q_h(X, a_X⁻¹K)`,

the cohomology of the derived global sections `RΓ(X_étale, K)` and `RΓ_h(X, a_X⁻¹K)`, where
`a_X⁻¹ = ε_X⁻¹ ∘ π_X⁻¹` on `D⁺`. The isomorphism is the canonical one: the degree `q` cohomology of
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedGlobalSectionsFineComparisonIso`, the pullback along `a_X` on derived
global sections.
declarations.statement:
public def hCohomologyComparisonPlusIso
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj
      X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K))
    (q : ℤ) :
    (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} q).obj
        (((sheafSections (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
          AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (op (SmallEtale.final (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj
            X.property))).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj K) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} q).obj
        ((Stacks.globalSectionsOver B.precoverage.toGrothendieck X).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj
          ((abelianComparisonPullback B.precoverage (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).precoverage
              X).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj
            (((SmallEtale.inclusion (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property).sheafPullback
              AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
              (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
              ((hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B).topology.over X)).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj K)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hCohomologyConstantComparisonIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EWH, the example.** Let `X` be a scheme, an object of a big h site `B`, and let `A`
be a torsion abelian group. For every `q`,

`H^q_étale(X, A) = H^q_h(X, A)`,

the cohomology of the constant sheaves with value `A` on the small étale site of `X` and on the
h site over `X`. The isomorphism is the canonical one: part (1) at the constant sheaf, followed by
the identification `a_X⁻¹A = A` of constant sheaves (both are left adjoint to global sections).
declarations.statement:
public def hCohomologyConstantComparisonIso (A : AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (hA : IsAddTorsion A)
    (q : ℕ) :
    (((sheafSections (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
        (op (SmallEtale.final (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property))).rightDerived q).obj
        ((constantSheaf (SmallEtale.topology (hAssociatedBigEtaleSite B) X.obj X.property)
          AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj A) ≅
      ((Stacks.globalSectionsOver B.precoverage.toGrothendieck X).rightDerived q).obj
        ((constantSheaf (B.precoverage.toGrothendieck.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj A)
declarations.comment: example

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlmostBlowUpSquare
declarations.doc:
An almost blowup square with centre `I.subscheme` and modification `b`. The exceptional
closed subscheme is `(I.comap b).subscheme`.
declarations.statement:
public structure IsAlmostBlowUpSquare {X X' : Scheme.{u}}
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (b : X' ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCSquareIso_of_essImage_almostBlowUpSquare_bigH
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EWN.** Let `J' ≤ J` be a topology coarser than the h topology on the big h
category over `S` — the fppf topology in the source — and let `𝒪` be a sheaf of rings for the h
topology, so that the identity functor is a comparison of ringed sites
`ε : (C_J, 𝒪_J) ⟶ (C_{J'}, 𝒪_{J'})`. Then for every almost blowup square in the big h category
over `S` and every object `K` of `D(𝒪_{J'})` in the essential image of the derived direct image
`Rε_*`, the canonical Mayer–Vietoris comparison `c^K_{X,Z,X',E}` of Stacks 0F16 for the coarser
topology is an isomorphism, i.e. a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of abelian groups.

The h sheafified representables of the square form a pushout square by Stacks 0EVD, and
`h_E^# ⟶ h_{X'}^#` is a monomorphism because `E ⟶ X'` is one, so Stacks 0F19 applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCSquareIso_of_essImage_almostBlowUpSquare_bigH
    (B : BigHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (O : Sheaf (BigHOver.topology B S hS) CommRingCat.{r})
    {J' : GrothendieckTopology (BigHOver B S hS)} (hJ : J' ≤ BigHOver.topology B S hS)
    [HasSheafify (BigHOver.topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
    [(BigHOver.topology B S hS).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
    [HasSheafify J' AddCommGrpCat.{v}] [J'.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
    [UnivLE.{u + 1, v}] [UnivLE.{u, v}] [UnivLE.{r, v}]
    (Rε : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (bigHRingedSite B S hS O).O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf ((bigHRingedSite B S hS O).ofLe hJ).O)))
    (η : (Stacks.Sites.CoarserTopology.modulePushforward.{u + 1, v, u, r} hJ
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (bigHRingedSite B S hS O).O)).mapHomotopyCategory
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rε)
    [Rε.IsRightDerivedFunctor η (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
      (SheafOfModules.{v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (bigHRingedSite B S hS O).O))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{v}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf ((bigHRingedSite B S hS O).ofLe hJ).O)))
    (hK : Rε.essImage K)
    (sq : Square (BigHOver B S hS))
    (I : ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj sq.X₄).IdealSheafData)
    (hb : IsAlmostBlowUpSquare I ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map sq.f₂₄))
    (hZ : Nonempty (Over.mk ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).map sq.f₃₄) ≅ Over.mk I.subschemeι))
    (hSquare : (sq.map (BigHOver.toScheme B S hS)).IsPullback) :
    (Stacks.MayerVietoris.CanonicalMapOfComplexes.derivedCSquareData.{u + 1, v}
      (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf ((bigHRingedSite B S hS O).ofLe hJ).O))
        sq).IsCSquareIso K

declarations.name: Stacks.MayerVietoris.CanonicalMapOfComplexes.isCSquareIso_obj₃_of_distTriang
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EWP.** The comparison for the third vertex is an isomorphism if it is
so for the first two vertices of a distinguished triangle.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCSquareIso_obj₃_of_distTriang
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O))))
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O))))
    (h₁ : (derivedCSquareData.{u, v} (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf S.O))

image of the derived direct image `Rε_*` and every almost blowup square of the site with affine

comparison of ringed sites `ε : (C_J, 𝒪_J) ⟶ (C_{J'}, 𝒪_{J'})`, and assume that affine almost

Mayer–Vietoris comparison `c^K_{X,X',Z,E}` of Stacks 0F16 is an isomorphism for every almost
blowup square of the site whose base is affine.

This is the derived functor, its unit and the object spelled out as binders, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.essImageIffAffineAlmostBlowUpBigH_of_isAffineAlmostBlowUpDetecting` with its
conclusion unfolded; the bundled form is the one a downstream file can state, because there the
binders no longer elaborate. The tag is registered here with the detection hypothesis named, and
again unconditionally on
`AlgebraicGeometry.essImage_iff_forall_isCSquareIso_affineAlmostBlowUp_fppf_bigH`, the assertion
at the fppf topology, where detection holds.

      (SheafOfModules.{v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (bigHRingedSite B S hS O).O))

        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf ((bigHRingedSite B S hS O).ofLe hJ).O)))

      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf ((bigHRingedSite B S hS O).ofLe hJ).O))).plus K) :

Example 0EVG.** Let `J' ≤ J` be a topology coarser than the h topology on the big h category
over `S` — the fppf topology in the source — and let `𝒪` be a sheaf of rings for the h topology,
so that the identity functor is a comparison of ringed sites
`ε : (C_J, 𝒪_J) ⟶ (C_{J'}, 𝒪_{J'})`. Let `K` be an object of `D(𝒪_{J'})` in the essential image
of the derived direct image `Rε_*`. Then for every almost blow up square of the shape of More on

The squares named by the source are almost blow up squares, by Stacks 0EVG transported along the

theorem isCSquareIso_of_essImage_principalCenterModelPair_bigH

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.essImage_singleFunctor_perfectionModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EWT.** Let `p` be a prime number and let `S` be a scheme over `𝔽_p`. Consider the
sheaf `𝒪^{perf} = colim_F 𝒪` on `(Sch/S)_{fppf}`. Then `𝒪^{perf}` is in the essential image of
`Rε_* : D((Sch/S)_h) ⟶ D((Sch/S)_{fppf})`.

Here `(Sch/S)_h` is a big h site over `S` and `(Sch/S)_{fppf}` its underlying category with the
fppf topology. `𝒪^{perf}` is the colimit of the Frobenius system of fppf sheaves of rings
(`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isColimitPerfectionCocone`); it is an h sheaf, so the identity is a
comparison of ringed sites `ε : ((Sch/S)_h, 𝒪^{perf}) ⟶ ((Sch/S)_{fppf}, 𝒪^{perf})`, and `Rε_*` is
any right derived functor of its direct image on sheaves of modules, with its unit `η`. The object
is `𝒪^{perf}` regarded as a module over itself and placed in degree zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_singleFunctor_perfectionModule
    (Rε : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (bigHRingedSite B S hS (awnRingSheaf B S hS)).O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        ((bigHRingedSite B S hS (awnRingSheaf B S hS)).ofLe
          (BigHOver.fppfTopology_le_topology B S hS)).O)))
    (η : (Stacks.Sites.CoarserTopology.modulePushforward.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u}
          (BigHOver.fppfTopology_le_topology B S hS)
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (bigHRingedSite B S hS (awnRingSheaf B S hS)).O)).mapHomotopyCategory
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rε)
    [Rε.IsRightDerivedFunctor η (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
      (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (bigHRingedSite B S hS (awnRingSheaf B S hS)).O))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    Rε.essImage ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (perfectionModule B S hS))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.hCohomologyIsoColimitFrobenius
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be a prime number and let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over
`𝔽_p`. Then

`H^i((Sch/S)_h, 𝒪^h) ≅ colim_F H^i(S, 𝒪)`

for every `i`, where `𝒪^h` is the h sheafification of the structure sheaf of the big h site of
`S`, and the colimit is over the system `H^i(S, 𝒪) →^F H^i(S, 𝒪) →^F ⋯` induced by the
Frobenius `F : 𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_S`, `f ↦ f^p`.

The left-hand side is cohomology over the final object of the big h category over `S`, and the
right-hand side is the colimit of the right derived functors of sections over `S` applied to the
Frobenius system `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.abelianFrobeniusSystem`.
declarations.statement:
def hCohomologyIsoColimitFrobenius [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (i : ℕ) :
    (((sheafSections (BigHOver.topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
        (op (BigHOver.final B S hS))).rightDerived i).obj (hStructureSheaf B S hS) ≅
      colimit (S.abelianFrobeniusSystem p hSp ⋙
        ((sheafSections (Opens.grothendieckTopology S) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
          (op ⊤)).rightDerived i)

declarations.name: IsBezout.instIsCoherentRing
declarations.doc:
A Bézout domain is a coherent ring: a finitely generated ideal is principal
(`IsBezout.isPrincipal_of_FG`), hence free since the ring is a domain, hence finitely presented.
The source states this for a valuation ring, which is a local Bézout domain
(`ValuationRing.iff_local_bezout_domain`); locality is not used.
declarations.statement:
public instance IsBezout.instIsCoherentRing (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsBezout A] :
    IsCoherentRing A
declarations.comment: Stated for a Bézout domain: the source's proof of the valuation ring case uses only that finitely generated ideals are principal and that the ring is a domain. The valuation ring case is instance search through `ValuationRing.instIsBezout`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.hasProjectiveDimensionLT_of_forall_ext_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Vanishing of `Ext^p_𝒜(X, -)` forces projective dimension `< p`.**
If `𝒜` is an abelian category and `Ext^p_𝒜(X, Y) = 0` for every object `Y` of `𝒜`, then `X` has
projective dimension `< p`, i.e. `Ext^i_𝒜(X, Y) = 0` for every `i ≥ p` and every `Y`. This
generalizes `CategoryTheory.hasProjectiveDimensionLT_of_enoughInjectives` by dropping the
assumption `[EnoughInjectives 𝒜]`. [Stacks, Tag 0EWW] states the reading for all pairs of
objects at once, which follows by applying this to every object of `𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasProjectiveDimensionLT_of_forall_ext_eq_zero (X : 𝒜) (p : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ (Y : 𝒜) (e : Abelian.Ext.{w} X Y p), e = 0) : HasProjectiveDimensionLT X p

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.nonempty_iso_biproduct_singleFunctor_obj_homology_of_forall_ext_two_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**A bounded complex over a category with no `Ext²` is the sum of its cohomologies.**
Let `𝒜` be an abelian category with `Ext²_𝒜(B, A) = 0` for every pair of objects `A`, `B`, and
let `K` be an object of `D(𝒜)` whose cohomology vanishes outside `[a, b]`. Then `K` is
isomorphic to the direct sum `⨁_{a ≤ i ≤ b} H^i(K)[-i]` of its cohomologies. The isomorphism
depends on choices of splittings, so only its existence is asserted. This is the special case
of `DerivedCategory.nonempty_iso_biproduct_singleFunctor_obj_homology_of_forall_ext_eq_zero`
([Stacks, Tag 0GM4]) in which the vanishing of `Ext^p`, `p ≥ 2`, comes from the category rather
than from `K`, via [Stacks, Tag 0EWW].
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_iso_biproduct_singleFunctor_obj_homology_of_forall_ext_two_eq_zero
    (K : DerivedCategory C) (a b : ℤ) [K.IsGE a] [K.IsLE b]
    (h : ∀ (A B : C) (e : Abelian.Ext.{w'} B A 2), e = 0) :
    Nonempty (K ≅ ⨁ fun i : Finset.Icc a b =>
      (singleFunctor C i.1).obj ((homologyFunctor C i.1).obj K))

declarations.name: subsingleton_dual_quotient_range_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EWY.** The dual of the cokernel of an injective endomorphism of a finite free
module is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_dual_quotient_range_of_injective
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (φ : M →ₗ[R] M) (hφ : Function.Injective φ) :
    Subsingleton (Module.Dual R (M ⧸ LinearMap.range φ))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.pseudoCoherentFrom_iff_finite_and_coherent_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EWZ.** Over a coherent ring, a bounded-above derived object is
`m`-pseudo-coherent exactly when its degree-`m` cohomology is finite and its higher cohomology
modules are coherent, equivalently finitely presented. It is pseudo-coherent exactly when all
its cohomology modules are coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherentFrom_iff_finite_and_coherent_homology
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsCoherentRing R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R))
    (hK : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) i).obj K))
    (m : ℤ) :
    let H := fun i : ℤ =>
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) i).obj K
    let finiteAndCoherent :=
      Module.Finite R (H m) ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, m < i → Module.IsCoherent R (H i)
    let finiteAndFinitePresentation :=
      Module.Finite R (H m) ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, m < i → Module.FinitePresentation R (H i)
    (IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m ↔ finiteAndCoherent) ∧
      (finiteAndCoherent ↔ finiteAndFinitePresentation) ∧
      (IsPseudoCoherent K ↔ ∀ i : ℤ, Module.IsCoherent R (H i))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.dedekindDomain_ideal_projective_and_bounded_complex_splitting
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EX0.** Ideals over a Dedekind domain are finite projective. Hence cyclic modules
have projective dimension at most one, every module has injective dimension at most one, all Ext
groups in degrees at least two vanish, and every bounded derived object is isomorphic to the
finite direct sum of its cohomologies placed in their degrees.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dedekindDomain_ideal_projective_and_bounded_complex_splitting
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R] [Small.{v} R] :
    (∀ I : Ideal R, Module.Finite R I ∧ Module.Projective R I) ∧
      (∀ I : Ideal R,
        HasProjectiveDimensionLE (ModuleCat.of R (Shrink.{v} (R ⧸ I))) 1) ∧
      (∀ M : ModuleCat.{v} R, HasInjectiveDimensionLE M 1) ∧
      (∀ (M N : ModuleCat.{v} R) (i : ℕ), 2 ≤ i →
        Subsingleton (Abelian.Ext M N i)) ∧
      ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (a b : ℤ), K.IsGE a → K.IsLE b →
        Nonempty (K ≅ ⨁ fun i : Finset.Icc a b =>
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i.1).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i.1).obj K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_isProper_comp_π_app_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EX1.** Let `X = lim Xᵢ` be the limit of a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact
and quasi-separated schemes over `S` with affine transition morphisms. A proper morphism
`f : Y ⟶ X` whose source is locally of finite type over `S` is proper over some stage of the
system and over every later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isProper_comp_π_app_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{v} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj S)
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (pX : c.pt ⟶ S)
    (hpX : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const I).map pX)
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (pY : Y ⟶ S) (f : Y ⟶ c.pt) (hf : f ≫ pX = pY)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [IsProper f] :
    ∃ i : I, ∀ (j : I) (_ : j ⟶ i), IsProper (f ≫ c.π.app j)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChange.affineTopDegreeTensorBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (c) of [Stacks, Tag 0EX3] for an affine base change over an affine base, at an
arbitrary quasi-coherent module**: `Hᵈ(X, F) ⊗_R B ≅ Hᵈ(X_B, q^* F)`.

Over an affine base the source obtains (c) from (b), and over an affine base (b) is the
Eilenberg-Watts identity `affineTopDegreeTensorCohomologyIso`: `M ↦ Hᵈ(X, F ⊗ p^* M~)` is
tensoring with `Hᵈ(X, F)`. Reading it at `M = B` and composing with
`affineTopDegreeFunctorObjBaseRingIso` gives the displayed identification, with no base-change
morphism constructed and no invertibility to prove.
declarations.statement:
def affineTopDegreeTensorBaseChangeIso
    (F : (_root_.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent W.left.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
    (hvan : ∀ G : W.left.Modules, G.IsQuasicoherent →
      IsZero (((moduleGlobalSections W.left).rightDerivedPlus ((d : ℤ) + 1)).obj G))
    {B : CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : CommRingCat.of R ⟶ B) {ZB : Scheme.{u}}
    (q : ZB ⟶ W.left) (pB : ZB ⟶ Spec B)
    (sq : IsPullback pB q (Spec.map φ) W.hom) :
    (MonoidalCategory.tensorLeft
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R Γ(W.left, ⊤))).obj
          ((qcohCohomology W.left d).obj F))).obj
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ.hom).obj (ModuleCat.of B B)) ≅
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R Γ(W.left, ⊤))).obj
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars q.appTop.hom).obj
          (((moduleGlobalSections ZB).rightDerived d).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback q).obj (show W.left.Modules from F.obj))))
declarations.comment: (c) for an affine base change over an affine base, at an arbitrary quasi-coherent module; the comparison is proved linear over the base ring and not over the base-changed ring, and no canonical base-change map is constructed

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChange.isIso_topDirectImageBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (c) of [Stacks, Tag 0EX3]: formation of `R^d f'_* 𝓕'` commutes with arbitrary
further base change.** For a top-degree base-change situation `S` (a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes whose higher direct images of quasi-coherent modules vanish
above `d`, and a base change `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` of it), every further cartesian square
`X'' --h'--> X'`, `X'' --f''--> Y''`, `Y'' --h--> Y'` and every quasi-coherent `𝒪_{X'}`-module
`𝓕'`, the canonical map `γ : h^* R^d f'_* 𝓕' ⟶ R^d f''_* (h')^* 𝓕'` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_topDirectImageBaseChangeMap
    (S : Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChangeSituation.{u})
    (F' : S.X'.Modules) [F'.IsQuasicoherent]
    (h' : X'' ⟶ S.X') (f'' : X'' ⟶ Y'') (h : Y'' ⟶ S.Y') (sq : IsPullback h' f'' S.f' h) :
    IsIso (topDirectImageBaseChangeMap S F' h' f'' h (toShHom_comm_of_isPullback h' f'' h sq))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChange.isZero_rightDerivedPlus_pushforward_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (a) of [Stacks, Tag 0EX3].** In a top-degree base-change situation the higher
direct images along the base-changed morphism `f'` of a quasi-coherent module vanish above the
degree `d`.

`isZero_rightDerivedPlus_pushforward_of_affineCase` reduces this to the case of a cartesian
square whose two bases are affine, which it carried as the hypothesis `haffine`; that case is
`isZero_rightDerivedPlus_pushforward_baseChange_of_isAffine`, so the conclusion is now
unconditional.

The degree `d` of a situation is a natural number, so `d < j` makes `j` nonnegative and the
integer-to-natural crossing the affine case asks for is available.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerivedPlus_pushforward_baseChange
    (S : Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChangeSituation.{u})
    (i : ℤ) (hi : (S.d : ℤ) < i) (F' : S.X'.Modules) [F'.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsZero (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward S.f').rightDerivedPlus i).obj F')

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChangeSituation.topDegreeTensorCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**The affine case of [Stacks, Tag 0EX3] (b) in the source's own form.** For a top-degree
base-change situation whose base `Y'` is affine and a quasi-coherent module `F` on `X'`, the
endofunctor `M ↦ H^d(X', F ⊗ (f')^* M~)` of `Γ(Y', ⊤)`-modules **is** tensoring with
`H^d(X', F)`.

This strengthens `topDegreeTensorIso`, which names the module only as `Φ(Γ(Y', ⊤))`; the two are
interchanged by `topDegreeFunctorObjSelfIso`.
declarations.statement:
def topDegreeTensorCohomologyIso :
    MonoidalCategory.tensorLeft (S.topDegreeCohomology F) ≅ S.topDegreeFunctor F
declarations.comment: (b) over an affine base, as an isomorphism of functors

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChangeSituation.topDegreeTensorCohomologyLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The affine case of [Stacks, Tag 0EX3] (b), module by module, in the source's own form**: a
`Γ(Y', ⊤)`-linear equivalence `H^d(X', F) ⊗_{R'} M ≃ₗ H^d(X', F ⊗ (f')^* M~)`, natural in `M` by
`topDegreeTensorCohomologyIso`. This is the displayed equation of the source.
declarations.comment: (b) over an affine base, the displayed tensor identity

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChange.isIso_higherDirectImageTensorMap
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (b) of [Stacks, Tag 0EX3].**  For a top-degree base-change situation, a
quasi-coherent module `F'` on `X'` and a quasi-coherent module `G` on the base `Y'`, the
canonical map

`R^d f'_* F' ⊗_{𝒪_{Y'}} G ⟶ R^d f'_*(F' ⊗_{𝒪_{X'}} (f')^* G)`

is an isomorphism.  The base carries no hypothesis: invertibility is local on it, the affine
opens cover it, and over an affine open the Eilenberg-Watts argument of
`TensorComparisonAffineRigidity.lean` applies to the restricted canonical map.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_higherDirectImageTensorMap (G : S.Y'.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsIso (higherDirectImageTensorMap S.f' F' G S.d)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChange.topDirectImageTensorComparison
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (b) of [Stacks, Tag 0EX3], as the isomorphism the tag asserts.**  For a
top-degree base-change situation and quasi-coherent modules `F'` on `X'` and `G` on the base,

`R^d f'_*(F' ⊗_{𝒪_{X'}} (f')^* G) ≅ R^d f'_* F' ⊗_{𝒪_{Y'}} G`,

whose inverse satisfies the canonicity condition
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChange.IsHigherDirectImageTensorMap` of the tag, so by
`eq_of_isHigherDirectImageTensorMap` it is the only candidate.
declarations.statement:
def topDirectImageTensorComparison (G : S.Y'.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] :
    { e : ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward S.f').rightDerivedPlus (S.d : ℤ)).obj
        ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
            ⟨S.X'.toRingedSpace.presheaf, S.X'.toRingedSpace.IsSheaf⟩).obj F').obj
              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback S.f').obj G))) ≅
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨S.Y'.toRingedSpace.presheaf, S.Y'.toRingedSpace.IsSheaf⟩).obj
            (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward S.f').rightDerivedPlus (S.d : ℤ)).obj F')).obj G) //
      IsHigherDirectImageTensorMap S.f' F' G S.d e.inv }

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChangeSituation.topDegreeTensorSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (b) of [Stacks, Tag 0EX3].** In a top-degree base-change situation, for `F'`
quasi-coherent on `X'` and `G'` quasi-coherent on `Y'`,

`Rᵈ f'_*(F' ⊗_{𝒪_{X'}} (f')^* G') ≅ Rᵈ f'_* F' ⊗_{𝒪_{Y'}} G'`.

No hypothesis is placed on `Y'`: the base-changed morphism `f'` is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated (`quasiCompact_f'`, `quasiSeparated_f'`) and its higher direct images vanish
above `d` by conclusion (a), `isZero_rightDerivedPlus_pushforward_baseChange`, so this is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChange.topDegreeTensorIso` for `f'`. Over an affine `Y'`
the same conclusion is read on global sections by `TopDegreeBaseChangeSituation.topDegreeTensorIso`
(`EilenbergWattsSituation.lean`).
declarations.statement:
def topDegreeTensorSheafIso
    (F' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X'.toRingedSpace)) [F'.IsQuasicoherent]
    (G' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.Y'.toRingedSpace)) [G'.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.Y'.toRingedSpace)) (S.d : ℤ)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward S.f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
          ((singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X'.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
            (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor S.X'.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj F').obj
              ((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback S.f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj G')))) ≅
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor S.Y'.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
        ((homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.Y'.toRingedSpace))
            (S.d : ℤ)).obj
          ((derivedPushforward S.f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
            ((singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X'.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
              F')))).obj
        G'

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.HigherDirectImageQcoh.isQuasicoherent_rightDerived_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EX4 (quasi-coherence).** Higher direct images of a quasi-coherent
module under a proper morphism are quasi-coherent: a proper morphism is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and properness is used for nothing else.
declarations.statement:
instance isQuasicoherent_rightDerived_of_isProper {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (i : ℕ) :
    (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived i).obj F).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag0EX4ProperQcoh.isQuasicoherent_rightDerived_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EX4 (quasi-coherence).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of
schemes and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then the higher direct image `R ⁱ f_* F` is
a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module, in every degree `i : ℕ`.

A proper morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so this is `isQuasicoherent_rightDerived`;
properness is not otherwise used, and neither is any bound on the degree or on the dimension of
the fibres.
declarations.statement:
instance isQuasicoherent_rightDerived_of_isProper [IsProper f] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived i).obj F).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeFiniteType.isFiniteType_rightDerived_of_isProper_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**The finite-type clause of [Stacks, Tag 0EX4] over a locally Noetherian base.** For
`f : X ⟶ Y` proper with `Y` locally Noetherian and `F` quasi-coherent of finite type, the
`𝒪_Y`-module `R ᵈ f_* F` is of finite type in every degree `d`, with no bound on the fibres
of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_rightDerived_of_isProper_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    [F.IsFiniteType] (d : ℕ) :
    (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived d).obj F).IsFiniteType
declarations.comment: finite-type clause only, and only over a locally Noetherian base; there in every degree and with no hypothesis on the fibres. An arbitrary base is not covered.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeFiniteType.isQuasicoherent_isFiniteType_rightDerived_of_isProper_of_forall_topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EX4].** For `f : X ⟶ Y` proper all of whose fibres have dimension at most
`d`, and `F` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type, the `𝒪_Y`-module `R ᵈ f_* F` is
quasi-coherent of finite type. The base is arbitrary.

The source prints the conclusion as an `𝒪_X`-module; `R ᵈ f_* F` is a sheaf on `Y`, and the
`𝒪_Y`-reading is the one the source's own proof uses.

Both clauses of the tag in one statement: quasi-coherence is
`…ProperQcoh.isQuasicoherent_rightDerived_of_isProper`, found by instance search because a proper
morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and finite type is
`isFiniteType_rightDerived_of_isProper_of_forall_topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_isFiniteType_rightDerived_of_isProper_of_forall_topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (d : ℕ)
    (hdim : ∀ y : Y, topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber y) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] :
    (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived d).obj F).IsQuasicoherent ∧
      (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived d).obj F).IsFiniteType
declarations.comment: both clauses at an ARBITRARY base, every d; the conclusion read as the 𝒪_Y-module R ᵈ f_* F, the source's 𝒪_X being a typo

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeFiniteType.isFinitePresentation_rightDerived_of_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EX5].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be proper and of finite presentation with every
fibre of dimension at most `d`, and let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation. Then the
`𝒪_Y`-module `R ᵈ f_* F` is of finite presentation.

No hypothesis is carried: `Y` is an arbitrary scheme, in particular not assumed locally
Noetherian, and nothing about Noetherian models or about base change is assumed.

The proof is the source's, which is the proof of [Stacks, Tag 0EX4] with the third paragraph
skipped, and it is now assembled from three pieces that are each unconditional:

* the conclusion is local on `Y`, so `Y` may be taken affine, and over an affine base the
  situation descends to an affine **Noetherian** stage together with the fibre bound and the
  module, over which the higher direct images vanish above `d` — this is
  `isFinitePresentation_rightDerived_of_topDegreeBaseChange` above;
* over that stage the top higher direct image of the base change is of finite presentation —
  `…AffineBaseChangeProjection.isFinitePresentation_rightDerived_pullback_of_noetherianModel`,
  the Eilenberg–Watts argument of [Stacks, Tag 0EX3] (b) applied at `Γ(Y, ⊤)`.

The conclusion is read as the statement about the `𝒪_Y`-module `R ᵈ f_* F`; the source prints
`𝒪_X`, which is a typo, the higher direct image being a sheaf on `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_rightDerived_of_finitePresentation
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (hfp : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation f)
    (d : ℕ) (hdim : ∀ y : Y, topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber y) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived d).obj F).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: conclusion read as the 𝒪_Y-module R ᵈ f_* F, the source's 𝒪_X being a typo

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentBaseCohomology.isCoherent_cohomology_of_isPerfect_derivedGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EX6].** Let `R` be a coherent ring, let `f : X ⟶ Spec R` be of finite
presentation ([Stacks, Tag 01TP] (3), spelled out as its three constituent properties) and let `G`
be an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation, flat over `R`, whose support is proper over `R`. Then
`Hⁱ(X, G)`, with its `R`-action restricted along `R ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, is a coherent `R`-module in
every degree.

The proof is the source's: `RΓ(X, G)` is a perfect object of `D(R)` ([Stacks, Tag 0A1H] for
`E = 𝒪_X` and the one-term complex `G`, carried here as the hypothesis `hperf`), a perfect object
is pseudo-coherent ([Stacks, Tag 0658]), and over a coherent ring the cohomology modules of a
bounded above pseudo-coherent object are coherent ([Stacks, Tag 0EWZ]); `cohomologyIso` identifies
the cohomology of `RΓ(X, G)` with `Hⁱ(X, G)`.

**Carried hypothesis.** `hperf : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (derivedGlobalSectionsOverBase f G)`
is Tag 0A1H over the affine base, the one input of the source's proof that this library does not
prove. It is a statement about the complex `RΓ(X, G)`, proved by Noetherian approximation, and not
the conclusion — which is coherence of the single module `Hⁱ(X, G)` — restated. The source's own
hypotheses are all present; when Tag 0A1H lands, `hperf` discharges by application.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_cohomology_of_isPerfect_derivedGlobalSections
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsCoherentRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (G : X.Modules) [G.IsFinitePresentation]
    (_hflat : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom G)
    (_hsupp : ∃ Z : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X,
      (Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp G ∧ IsProperOver f Z)
    (hperf : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (derivedGlobalSectionsOverBase f G))
    (i : ℕ) :
    Module.IsCoherent R
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (Stacks.Cech.globalRingHom f).hom).obj
        (((AlgebraicGeometry.moduleGlobalSections X).rightDerived i).obj G))
declarations.comment: carrying as an explicit hypothesis Tag 0A1H: RΓ(X, G) is perfect over the base

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentBaseCohomology.isCoherent_rightDerived_moduleGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EX6].** Let `R` be a coherent ring, let `f : X ⟶ Spec R` be of finite
presentation and let `G` be an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation, flat over `R`, whose support
is proper over `R`. Then for every `i` the cohomology module `Hⁱ(X, G)`, with its `R`-action
restricted along `R ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, is a coherent `R`-module.

The source's proof: `RΓ(X, G)` is a perfect object of `D(R)` by [Stacks, Tag 0A1H]
(`…ProperSupportGlobalSectionsPerfect.isPerfect_derivedGlobalSectionsOverBase_of_properSupport`),
and over a coherent ring the cohomology modules of a perfect complex are coherent by
[Stacks, Tag 0658] and [Stacks, Tag 0EWZ]
(`isCoherent_cohomology_of_isPerfect_derivedGlobalSections`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_rightDerived_moduleGlobalSections
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsCoherentRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (G : X.Modules) [G.IsFinitePresentation]
    (hflat : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom G)
    (hsupp : ∃ Z : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X,
      (Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp G ∧ IsProperOver f Z)
    (i : ℕ) :
    Module.IsCoherent R
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (Stacks.Cech.globalRingHom f).hom).obj
        (((AlgebraicGeometry.moduleGlobalSections X).rightDerived i).obj G))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteLocallyFree_iso_of_fiberwiseFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EX7, reduced to representability of the descent condition.** A finite locally
free module on `X` whose restriction to every fibre of `f` is free of finite rank is the pullback
of a finite locally free module on the reduced base `S`, provided the descent condition for it is
represented — that is, provided the conclusion of Stacks Tag 0BDP holds for `f` and `E`.

Tag 0BDP's hypotheses on `f` — flatness, properness, finite presentation, and invariance of the
structure sheaf under pushforward along every base change — enter only through that
representability, and so do not appear.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteLocallyFree_iso_of_fiberwiseFree {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (E : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))
    (h0BDP : HasDescentLocus f E) [IsReduced S]
    (hfiber : ∀ s : S, ∃ r : ℕ,
      Nonempty ((modulePullback
          (pullback.fst f (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E ≅
        _root_.SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))) :
    ∃ N : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace),
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} N ∧
        Nonempty ((modulePullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj N ≅ E)
declarations.comment: assuming the representability of the descent locus of Tag 0BDP

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteLocallyFree_iso_of_fiberwiseFree_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EX7.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a flat, proper morphism of finite presentation such
that `𝒪_S ⟶ f_*𝒪_X` is an isomorphism and remains so after arbitrary base change. Let `E` be a
finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module such that (1) `E|_{X_s} ≅ 𝒪_{X_s}^{⊕ r_s}` for every `s ∈ S`,
and (2) `S` is reduced. Then `E ≅ f^*N` for a finite locally free `𝒪_S`-module `N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteLocallyFree_iso_of_fiberwiseFree_of_isReduced {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [IsProper f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f)
    (hO : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S),
      IsIso (structureSheafHom (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom))
    (E : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E]
    (hfiber : ∀ s : S, ∃ r : ℕ,
      Nonempty ((modulePullback
          (pullback.fst f (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E ≅
        SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))
    [IsReduced S] :
    ∃ N : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toRingedSpace),
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} N ∧
        Nonempty ((modulePullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj N ≅ E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeTriviality.isTrivial_of_isTrivial_genericFiber
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EX8].** Let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be a proper flat
morphism of finite presentation over a valuation ring `A` with fraction field `K`, and let `L` be
an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. Assume that `L` is trivial on the generic fibre `X_K`, that the closed
fibre is integral, and that `K = H⁰(X_K, 𝒪_{X_K})`. Then `L` is trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTrivial_of_isTrivial_genericFiber
    [ValuationRing A] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    [IsProper f] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (L : X.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L]
    (hgen : SheafOfModules.IsTrivial
      (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))).presheaf
      (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))).ringCatSheaf.2
      ((modulePullback (pullback.fst f
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj L))
    [IsIntegral (f.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A))]
    (hΓ : Function.Bijective
      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)))).appTop.hom) :
    SheafOfModules.IsTrivial X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isStackInGroupoids_iff_generatorSquares
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EX9.** A category fibred over the big h category over `S` is a stack in groupoids
for the h topology if and only if it is a stack in groupoids for the Zariski topology, has
effective descent along every surjective flat proper morphism of finite presentation onto an
affine object of the site, and has `𝒮_X ⟶ 𝒮_Z ×_{𝒮_E} 𝒮_{X'}` an equivalence for every almost
blowup square of the site with affine base of the shape of Example 0EVG or of Example 0EVH.

Condition (2) is in its descent form: the source's literal condition (2), equivalence onto the
two-fibre product, is false for h stacks, as recorded in the module documentation.  Conditions (1)
and (3) are the source's.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isStackInGroupoids_iff_generatorSquares :
    p.IsStackInGroupoids.{u + 1} (BigHOver.topology B S hS) ↔
      IsZariskiStackInGroupoids B S hS p ∧ IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationDescent B S hS p ∧
        IsOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpStack B S hS p ∧ IsTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpStack B S hS p
declarations.comment: with condition (2) in its descent form: the source's literal condition (2) is false for h stacks, see `AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationDescent`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isZariskiStackInGroupoids_of_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EX9, necessity of condition (1).** A category fibred in groupoids over the big h
category over `S` which is a stack in groupoids for the h topology is a stack in groupoids for the
Zariski topology.

The Zariski topology on `(Sch/S)_h` is coarser than the h topology,
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.zariskiTopology_le_topology`, and the conditions of Stacks 02ZI are
indexed by the covering families of the topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZariskiStackInGroupoids_of_isStackInGroupoids
    (hp : p.IsStackInGroupoids.{u + 1} (BigHOver.topology B S hS)) :
    BigHOver.IsZariskiStackInGroupoids B S hS p
declarations.comment: only if, condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationDescent_of_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EX9, necessity of condition (2) in its descent form.** A category fibred in
groupoids over the big h category over `S` which is a stack in groupoids for the h topology has
effective descent, with descent of morphisms, along every surjective flat proper morphism of finite
presentation onto an affine object of the site.

Flatness and affineness of the target are not used:
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_isStackInGroupoids` holds for
every proper surjection of finite presentation, such a morphism being an h covering by itself.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationDescent_of_isStackInGroupoids [p.IsFibered]
    (hp : p.IsStackInGroupoids.{u + 1} (BigHOver.topology B S hS)) :
    IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationDescent B S hS p
declarations.comment: only if, condition (2) in its descent form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpStack_of_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EX9, necessity of condition (3) for the shape of Example 0EVG.**  A stack in
groupoids for the h topology satisfies condition (3) for the squares of Example 0EVG; this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isEquivalence_twoFibreProductComparison_of_isStackInGroupoids`, which
needs neither the affineness of the base nor the shape.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpStack_of_isStackInGroupoids [p.IsFibered]
    (hp : p.IsStackInGroupoids.{u + 1} (BigHOver.topology B S hS)) :
    IsOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpStack B S hS p
declarations.comment: only if, condition (3) for the shape of Example 0EVG

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpStack_of_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EX9, necessity of condition (3) for the shape of Example 0EVH.**  A stack in
groupoids for the h topology satisfies condition (3) for the squares of Example 0EVH; this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isEquivalence_twoFibreProductComparison_of_isStackInGroupoids`, which
needs neither the affineness of the base nor the shape.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpStack_of_isStackInGroupoids [p.IsFibered]
    (hp : p.IsStackInGroupoids.{u + 1} (BigHOver.topology B S hS)) :
    IsTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpStack B S hS p
declarations.comment: only if, condition (3) for the shape of Example 0EVH

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isStackInGroupoids_of_generatorSquares
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EX9, the sufficiency direction.**  A category fibred in groupoids over the big h
category over `S` which

1. is a stack in groupoids for the Zariski topology,
2. has effective descent, with descent of morphisms, along every surjective flat proper morphism
   of finite presentation `X ⟶ Y` of the site with `Y` affine: the functor from `𝒮_Y` to the
   descent data relative to `{X ⟶ Y}` is an equivalence, and
3. has `𝒮_X ⟶ 𝒮_Z ×_{𝒮_E} 𝒮_{X'}` an equivalence for every almost blow up square of the site of
   the shape of Example 0EVG or of Example 0EVH

is a stack in groupoids for the h topology.

Conditions (1) and (3) are those of the source.  Condition (2) is the source's condition (2) with
the two-fibre product `𝒮_X ×_{𝒮_{X ×_Y X}} 𝒮_X` replaced by the category of descent data, which
adds the cocycle condition over `X ×_Y X ×_Y X`: the literal condition fails for every h stack with
a nontrivial automorphism over an affine object, by the fold-map computation in the module
documentation of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Topologies.HTopology.GeneratorAlmostBlowUpStackCriterion`, and the
descent form is what the source's proof uses.  The three hypotheses are those of the sheaf-level
criterion of Stacks 0EVI that the proof of the source applies, read for a category fibred in
groupoids: the Zariski one is the topology condition (1) of 0EVI quantifies over, and the descent
along `{X ⟶ Y}` and the two equivalences range over the morphisms and squares conditions (2), (3)
and (4) of 0EVI range over.

The proof runs Stacks 0EVI on the two auxiliary presheaves of sets on the slice `(Sch/S)_h / U`
that the source builds out of `𝒮`: the presheaf of morphisms between two objects of the fibre over
`U`, whose sheaf property is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isMorSheaf_of_generatorSquares`, and the presheaf of solutions of a
descent problem, whose sheaf property is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.nonempty_descentSolution_id`.  Both are run through
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.of_localOnGenerators`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isStackInGroupoids_of_generatorSquares
    (h1 : IsZariskiStackInGroupoids B S hS p)
    (h2 : IsAffineFlatProperFinitePresentationDescent B S hS p)
    (h3 : IsOneGeneratorAlmostBlowUpStack B S hS p)
    (h4 : IsTwoGeneratorAlmostBlowUpStack B S hS p) :
    p.IsStackInGroupoids.{u + 1} (BigHOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: if, with condition (2) in its descent form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusColimitVectModelEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EXA: the explicit category is the colimit.** The category
`frobeniusColimitVectModel`, whose objects are the pairs `(ℰ, n)` and whose Hom-sets are the
colimits `colim_N Hom_S(F^{N - n, *}ℰ, F^{N - m, *}𝒢)`, is equivalent to the colimit
`colim_F Vect(S)` of `Vect(S) →F* Vect(S) →F* ⋯` in `Cat`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def frobeniusColimitVectModelEquivalence :
    frobeniusColimitVectModel X p hX ≌ frobeniusColimitVect X p hX
declarations.comment: colim_F Vect(S) is the category of pairs (E, n) described in the tag

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_frobeniusColimitVect_obj_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EXA: the objects of `colim_F Vect(S)` are the pairs `(ℰ, n)`.** Every object of
the colimit in `Cat` is the image of a finite locally free `𝒪_S`-module `ℰ` under the stage-`n`
coprojection, for some `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_frobeniusColimitVect_obj_eq (Y : frobeniusColimitVect X p hX) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (E : X.Vect),
      (EndoColim.catStage.{u + 1} (frobeniusPullback X p hX) n).obj E = Y
declarations.comment: an object of colim_F Vect(S) is a pair (E, n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusColimitVectModelHomIsColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EXA: the Hom-sets of `colim_F Vect(S)`.** In the explicit category,
`Hom((ℰ, n), (𝒢, m))` is the colimit `colim_N Hom_S(F^{N - n, *}ℰ, F^{N - m, *}𝒢)` over the
`N ≥ n, m` along `F^*`, the colimit maps taking a morphism of `Vect(S)` to the morphism it
presents.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def frobeniusColimitVectModelHomIsColimit (E G : X.Vect) (n m : ℕ) :
    IsColimit (EndoColim.homCocone (⟨E, n⟩ : frobeniusColimitVectModel X p hX) ⟨G, m⟩)
declarations.comment: Hom((E, n), (G, m)) = colim_N Hom_S(F^{N - n, *}E, F^{N - m, *}G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusColimitVectHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EXA: the Hom-sets of `colim_F Vect(S)`, in the colimit in `Cat`.** The
morphisms between the images of `ℰ` and `𝒢` under the stage-`n` and stage-`m` coprojections are
in bijection with `colim_N Hom_S(F^{N - n, *}ℰ, F^{N - m, *}𝒢)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def frobeniusColimitVectHomEquiv (E G : X.Vect) (n m : ℕ) :
    ((EndoColim.catStage.{u + 1} (frobeniusPullback X p hX) n).obj E ⟶
        (EndoColim.catStage.{u + 1} (frobeniusPullback X p hX) m).obj G) ≃
      colimit (EndoColim.homDiagram (⟨E, n⟩ : frobeniusColimitVectModel X p hX) ⟨G, m⟩)
declarations.comment: Hom((E, n), (G, m)) = colim_N Hom_S(F^{N - n, *}E, F^{N - m, *}G), for the colimit in Cat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusColimitVectModelShiftIso
declarations.doc: **Stacks Tag 0EXA: `(ℰ, n) ≅ (F^*ℰ, n + 1)`** in `colim_F Vect(S)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def frobeniusColimitVectModelShiftIso (E : X.Vect) (n : ℕ) :
    (⟨E, n⟩ : frobeniusColimitVectModel X p hX) ≅ ⟨(frobeniusPullback X p hX).obj E, n + 1⟩
declarations.comment: the object (E, n) is isomorphic to the object (F^* E, n + 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusColimitVect
declarations.doc:
**The category `colim_F Vect(X)` of Stacks Tag 0EXA.** It is the colimit of the sequential
diagram of categories of finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules whose transition functors are all
pullback along the absolute Frobenius.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def frobeniusColimitVect : Cat.{u + 1, u + 1}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusColimitVectEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EXB.** The category `colim_F Vect(X)` of Stacks Tag 0EXA is equivalent
to the category of finite locally free modules over the sheaf of rings `colim_F 𝒪_X`, the
equivalence being the comparison functor of the tag.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def frobeniusColimitVectEquivalence [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] :
    frobeniusColimitVectModel X p hX ≌ frobeniusColimitVectorBundles X p hX
declarations.comment: the category colim_F Vect(X) of Tag 0EXA is equivalent to the category of finite locally free modules over the sheaf of rings colim_F O_X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.colimVectComparison_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be a prime, let `A` be a ring with `p = 0`, let `f ∈ A` and let `J ⊆ A` be an ideal
annihilated by `f ^ n`, so that

```
A ⧸ (J + fA) <--- A ⧸ J
      ^             ^
      |             |
   A ⧸ fA   <---    A
```

is the almost blowup square of More on Flatness, Example 0EVG. Then the comparison functor

`colim_F Vect(Spec A) ⟶ colim_F Vect(Spec (A ⧸ fA)) ×_{colim_F Vect(Spec (A ⧸ (J + fA)))}
  colim_F Vect(Spec (A ⧸ J))`

of Frobenius-colimit categories of vector bundles **is an equivalence.**
declarations.statement:
theorem colimVectComparison_isEquivalence (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A) (J : Ideal A)
    (n : ℕ) (hann : ∀ x ∈ J, f ^ n * x = 0) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : (p : A) = 0) :
    (colimVectComparison A f J p hp).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_twoGeneratorColimVectComparison
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EXD], for the categories `colim_F Vect` of [Stacks, Tag 0EXA].**  Let `p` be
a prime, `A` a ring in which `p` vanishes and `f₁, f₂ ∈ A`.  For the almost blowup square
`X = Spec A`, `Z = Spec (A/(f₁,f₂))`, `X' = Proj (A[T₀,T₁]/(f₂T₀ - f₁T₁))`, `E = 𝐏¹_Z` of
[Stacks, Example 0EVH], the functor
`colim_F Vect(X) ⟶ colim_F Vect(Z) ×_{colim_F Vect(E)} colim_F Vect(X')`
built from the transition functors of the models `colim_F Vect(-)` is an equivalence.

It is `AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_twoGeneratorFrobeniusColimitComparison` carried back along
the comparison functors of [Stacks, Tag 0EXB]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_colimVectSquare_of_frobeniusColimitVectorBundlesComparison`):
the base is affine, the modification and the exceptional line are `Proj` of finitely generated
graded rings, so all four corners are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_twoGeneratorColimVectComparison :
    letI := (twoGeneratorSquare A f₁ f₂).modificationGraded
    ((CategoricalPullback.CatCommSqOver.toFunctorToCategoricalPullback _ _ _).obj
      (colimVectSquareCatCommSqOver p (modificationToBase A f₁ f₂) (centerToBase A f₁ f₂)
        (exceptionalToModification A f₁ f₂) (exceptionalToCenter A f₁ f₂)
        (isInCharacteristic_spec A p hpA)
        (isInCharacteristic_twoGeneratorModification A f₁ f₂ p hpA)
        (isInCharacteristic_twoGeneratorCenter A f₁ f₂ p hpA)
        (isInCharacteristic_twoGeneratorExceptional A f₁ f₂ p hpA)
        (twoGenerator_isPullback A f₁ f₂).w)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: for the categories colim_F Vect of Tag 0EXA

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_twoGeneratorFrobeniusColimitComparison
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EXD].** Let `p` be a prime and consider the almost blowup square `X, X', Z, E`
of [Stacks, Example 0EVH] in characteristic `p`, i.e. over a ring `A` in which `p` vanishes, with
arbitrary `f₁, f₂ ∈ A`.  Then the functor
`G : colim_F Vect(X) ⟶ colim_F Vect(Z) ×_{colim_F Vect(E)} colim_F Vect(X')`
is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_twoGeneratorFrobeniusColimitComparison :
    letI := (twoGeneratorSquare A f₁ f₂).modificationGraded
    (twoGeneratorFrobeniusColimitComparison A f₁ f₂ p hpA).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusVectorBundleGroupoidFiberEquivCoreColimitVect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0EXE, the "moreover" clause.** Let `S` be a scheme in characteristic `p` and let
`U` be an object of `(Sch/S)_h` whose underlying scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
Then the fibre `𝒮_U` over `U` of the category fibred in groupoids `𝒮 ⟶ (Sch/S)_h` of finite
locally free `colim_F 𝒪`-modules is `colim_F Vect(U)`, read as a groupoid: it is equivalent to the
maximal subgroupoid of the colimit `colim_F Vect(U)` in `Cat` of Stacks Tag 0EXA.

The fibre is the groupoid of finite locally free modules over `colim_F 𝒪_U`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusVectorBundleGroupoidFiberEquiv`), which is the core of the category
of such modules (`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.coreFullSubcategoryEquiv`); Stacks Tag 0EXB
(`AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusColimitVectEquivalence`) and Stacks Tag 0EXA
(`AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusColimitVectModelEquivalence`) identify that category with
`colim_F Vect(U)`, and the identification passes to cores.
declarations.statement:
def frobeniusVectorBundleGroupoidFiberEquivCoreColimitVect (U : BigHOver B S hS)
    [CompactSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)] :
    (frobeniusVectorBundleGroupoidFibration B S hS p hpS).Fiber U ≌
      Core (frobeniusColimitVect ((BigHOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) p
        (isInCharacteristic_bigHOver B S hS p hpS U))
declarations.comment: moreover: if U is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then the fibre S_U of the category fibred in groupoids S over (Sch/S)_h is colim_F Vect(U), as its maximal subgroupoid

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusVectorBundleGroupoidFibration_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EXE.** Let `p` be a prime number and let `S` be a scheme in
characteristic `p`. Then the category fibred in groupoids `p : 𝒮 ⟶ (Sch/S)_h` whose fibre category
over `U` is the category of finite locally free `colim_F 𝒪_U`-modules over `U` (with its
isomorphisms) is a stack in groupoids.

Here `(Sch/S)_h` is the big h site `AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver B S hS` of an arbitrary big h site
`B` containing `S`, and "stack in groupoids" is Stacks 02ZI for its h topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem frobeniusVectorBundleGroupoidFibration_isStackInGroupoids
    (B : BigHSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (hpS : IsInCharacteristic S p) :
    (frobeniusVectorBundleGroupoidFibration B S hS p hpS).IsStackInGroupoids.{u + 1}
      (BigHOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: stack in groupoids

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FreenessOverDVR.exists_thickening_exponent_free
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Tag 0EXF.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism where `S = Spec A` is the
spectrum of a discrete valuation ring. Denote `η ∈ S` the generic point and `Xₙ ⊆ X` the closed
subscheme cut out by the `n`-th power of a uniformizer. Then there exists an integer `n` such
that any finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module `𝓔` such that `𝓔|_{X_η}` and `𝓔|_{Xₙ}` are free, is
free.

The integer is `n = k + 1 + e`. Here `k` bounds the `π`-power torsion of the local rings of `X`
(`exists_forall_germ_pow_mul_eq_zero`), and `e` bounds the `π`-power torsion of
`H¹(X, πᵏ 𝒪_X^r)` for every rank `r` at once (`exists_pow_smul_cohomology_adicSub_free_eq_zero`).
Comparing the lengths of `H⁰(X, πᵏ (𝓔 / πᵏ⁺ᵐ 𝓔))` and `H⁰(X, πᵏ (𝒪_X^r / πᵏ⁺ᵐ 𝒪_X^r))` at
`m = e` and `m = e + 1`, which agree because `𝓔 / πⁿ 𝓔 ≅ 𝒪_X^r / πⁿ 𝒪_X^r`, transfers that
bound to `H¹(X, πᵏ 𝓔)` (`torsionBy_cohomology_eq_bot_of_adicQuotientIso`); the free ranks of the
two `H⁰` agree by the generic fibre. The basis sections of `𝒪_X^r / πⁿ 𝒪_X^r` then lift, modulo
`πᵏ⁺¹`, to global sections of `𝓔` (`exists_sections_lift`), and the resulting
`𝒪_X^r ⟶ 𝓔` is an isomorphism modulo `πᵏ⁺¹`, hence an isomorphism since `f` is proper over a
local base (`isIso_of_comp_adicProj`).

The source's hypothesis that the fibres of `f` be geometrically connected is not used: the
source needs it only to reduce to the case where `f` has a section, and the argument above does
not pass through a section.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_thickening_exponent_free (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f] :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∀ E : X.Modules, E.IsFiniteLocallyFree →
      IsFreeOfFiniteRank (genericFibreRestrict A f E) →
      IsFreeOfFiniteRank (thickeningRestrict A f n E) →
      IsFreeOfFiniteRank E
declarations.comment: without the hypothesis that the fibres are geometrically connected, which the proof does not use

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FreenessOverDVR.exists_thickening_exponent_free_of_free_generic_and_thickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Tag 0EXF.** Let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be proper with geometrically connected fibres over
a discrete valuation ring `A`, let `η` be the generic point of `Spec A` and let `X_n ⊆ X` be the
closed subscheme cut out by the `n`-th power of a uniformizer `π`. There is an integer `n`,
independent of the module, such that every finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module which is free on
`X_η` and on `X_n` is free.

The integer produced is `e + 1 + k`, which is the source's `k + e + 1`: `k` is the Artin-Rees
exponent carried by `TrivialityInput.comparison`, and `e` is an exponent annihilating the
`π`-power torsion of `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` and `H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`, both of which depend only on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_thickening_exponent_free_of_free_generic_and_thickening
    {π : A} (hπ : Irreducible π) (h : TrivialityInput A f π) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∀ E : X.Modules, E.IsFiniteLocallyFree →
      IsFreeOfFiniteRank (genericFibreRestrict A f E) →
      IsFreeOfFiniteRank (thickeningRestrict A f n E) →
      IsFreeOfFiniteRank E
declarations.comment: conditional on `TrivialityInput`, which carries the source's cited input [Stacks, Tag 02O6] (finiteness of the cohomology of a proper morphism, open in this library), the reduction to the case of a section — whose last step, invertibility of a determinant invertible at one point of each fibre, the source itself leaves to the reader — and the derived comparison `RΓ(X, 𝓔) ⊗^L A/π^m ≅ RΓ(X, 𝒪_X^r) ⊗^L A/π^m` read on cohomology. Of the inputs of that comparison the library does carry the subsheaf of sections supported on the special fibre ([Stacks, Tag 084L]), the quotients `𝓔/π^j 𝓔`, the Artin-Rees exponent ([Stacks, Tag 01YA]), the two-term complex `(𝓔 --π^m--> 𝓔)` in `D(𝒪_X)` with its distinguished triangle, and `RΓ(X, -) : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(A)`; what it lacks is the reduction formula `Hⁱ(K ⊗^L A/π^m) = Hⁱ(K)/π^m ⊕ Hⁱ⁺¹(K)[π^m]`, which is a step of the source's proof and not a tag. Proved here: the construction of both exponents and hence of `n`, the summand-counting transfer of the exponent bound from `𝒪_X` to `𝓔` (`torsionExponentTransfer`), and the two Nakayama steps that turn surjectivity modulo `π^{e+1}` into freeness. The hypotheses are satisfiable: `exists_thickening_exponent_free_specPowerSeries` discharges all of them over `k⟦X⟧`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VectorBundleCodimensionOne.exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_pullback_iso
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and proper with `𝒪_S = f_*𝒪_X`, let `S` be a normal Noetherian
scheme, and let `ℰ` be a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module whose pullback to `X ×_S Spec 𝒪_{S,s}`
is free for every point `s ∈ S` of codimension one, and also for every point `s` of codimension
zero that does not specialize to a point of codimension one. Then `ℰ` is isomorphic to the
pullback of a finite locally free `𝒪_S`-module.

The two conditions `hfree` and `hfree₀` together are equivalent to freeness over the local scheme
at every point of codimension at most one. The condition `hfree₀` is not in the source, and the
statement is false without it (`not_forall_exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_pullback_iso_of_codimOne`):
for a field `k`, take `S = Spec k`, `X = ℙ¹_k` and `ℰ = 𝒪(1)`; then `S` has no point of
codimension one, but `𝒪(1)` is not the pullback of a `k`-vector space. When every irreducible
component of `S` has a point of codimension one, `hfree₀` is vacuous.

Codimension of a point is the Krull dimension of its local ring, and freeness after base change
to the local scheme at `s` means an isomorphism with some free module `𝒪^{(I)}`, the index set
being arbitrary. The hypothesis `𝒪_S = f_*𝒪_X` is invertibility of the comparison map
`f.toLRSHom.toHom.c`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isFiniteLocallyFree_pullback_iso {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [IsProper f] [IsNoetherian S] [IsNormal S] (E : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E] (hO : IsIso f.toLRSHom.toHom.c)
    (hfree : ∀ s : S, ringKrullDim (S.presheaf.stalk s) = 1 →
      ∃ I : Type u, Nonempty
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f (S.fromSpecStalk s))).obj E ≅
          SheafOfModules.free I))
    (hfree₀ : ∀ s : S, ringKrullDim (S.presheaf.stalk s) = 0 →
      (∀ t : S, s ⤳ t → ringKrullDim (S.presheaf.stalk t) ≠ 1) →
      ∃ I : Type u, Nonempty
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f (S.fromSpecStalk s))).obj E ≅
          SheafOfModules.free I)) :
    ∃ M : S.Modules, SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} M ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj M ≅ E)
declarations.comment: corrected: freeness is also required at generic points of S with no codimension-1 specialization; as stated the lemma fails for X = ℙ¹_k over Spec k with ℰ = 𝒪(1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusColimitVectModelPullback_full_faithful_and_descends
declarations.doc:
**Descent of vector bundles in positive characteristic** (Stacks Tag 0EXH). Let `p` be a
prime, `Y` a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme over `𝐅_p` and `f : X ⟶ Y` a proper surjective
morphism of finite presentation with geometrically connected fibres. Then the pullback functor
`colim_F Vect(Y) ⥤ colim_F Vect(X)` is fully faithful, and if `ℰ` is a finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-module such that for all `y ∈ Y` there are `n_y, r_y ≥ 0` with
`F^{n_y,*}ℰ|_{X_{y,red}} ≅ 𝒪_{X_{y,red}}^{⊕ r_y}`, then for some `n ≥ 0` the Frobenius power
pullback `F^{n,*}ℰ` is the pullback of a finite locally free `𝒪_Y`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem frobeniusColimitVectModelPullback_full_faithful_and_descends (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (hY : IsInCharacteristic Y p) (f : X ⟶ Y) [CompactSpace Y]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] [IsProper f] [Surjective f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    [GeometricallyConnected f] :
    ((frobeniusColimitVectModelPullback f p (isInCharacteristic_of_hom f p hY) hY).Full ∧
      (frobeniusColimitVectModelPullback f p (isInCharacteristic_of_hom f p hY) hY).Faithful) ∧
    ∀ E : X.Vect,
      (∀ y : Y, ∃ n r : ℕ, Nonempty
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((f.fiber y).reductionι ≫ f.fiberι y)).obj
            ((frobeniusPullbackIter X p (isInCharacteristic_of_hom f p hY) n).obj E).obj ≅
          SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))) →
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : Y.Vect), Nonempty
        ((frobeniusPullbackIter X p (isInCharacteristic_of_hom f p hY) n).obj E ≅
          (Scheme.Vect.pullback f).obj G)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sites.InverseSystem.InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.cocycle_pullback_pushforward_of_colimit
declarations.doc:
**The cocycle condition of Stacks 09YN.** The canonical maps
`φ_a : f_a^{-1}f_{i, *}F → f_{j, *}F`, in the adjoint form `ψ`, satisfy
`φ_{b ∘ a} = φ_b ∘ f_b^{-1}φ_a`: each `ψ a` is the transport along `D.u a ⋙ u j = u i`, and the
transports compose.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cocycle_pullback_pushforward_of_colimit
    {C : Type w} [SmallCategory C] (D : InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.{u₁, u₂, w}) (u : ∀ i, D.C i ⥤ C)
    (hu : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : i ⟶ j), D.u a ⋙ u i = u j)
    (_hobj : ∀ X : C, ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i), (u i).obj Y = X)
    (_hhom :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (f : (u i).obj X ⟶ (u i).obj Y),
        ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (g : (D.u a).obj X ⟶ (D.u a).obj Y),
          (u j).map g =
            eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) X) ≫ f ≫ eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) Y).symm)
    (_hhom_inj :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (g₁ g₂ : X ⟶ Y),
        (u i).map g₁ = (u i).map g₂ → ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i), (D.u a).map g₁ = (D.u a).map g₂)
    (K : Precoverage C)
    (_hK :
      ∀ (X : C) (R : Presieve X),
        R ∈ K X ↔
          ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i) (h : (u i).obj Y = X) (S : Presieve Y),
            S ∈ (D.J i).toPrecoverage Y ∧ S ∈ Precoverage.finite (D.C i) Y ∧ R = h ▸ S.map (u i))
    -- the sheaf `F` on `C`, and the canonical maps `φ_a : f_a^{-1}f_{i,*}F → f_{j,*}F` in
    -- adjoint form: `ψ a` is the identity `f_{i,*}F → f_{a,*}f_{j,*}F`
    (F : Sheaf K.toGrothendieck (Type w))
    (ψ : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i), (u i).op ⋙ F.obj ⟶ (D.u a).op ⋙ ((u j).op ⋙ F.obj))
    (hψ :
      ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (V : D.C i) (x : F.obj.obj (op ((u i).obj V))),
        (ψ a).app (op V) x =
          F.obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) V).symm)) x)
    {i j k : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (b : k ⟶ j) (V : D.C i)
    (x : F.obj.obj (op ((u i).obj V))) :
    (ψ (b ≫ a)).app (op V) x =
      ((u k).op ⋙ F.obj).map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (D.comp b a) V).symm))
        ((ψ b).app (op ((D.u a).obj V)) ((ψ a).app (op V) x))
declarations.comment: weak-system variant (Stacks 00VH finite coverings): the cocycle condition `φ_{b ∘ a} = φ_b ∘ f_b^{-1}φ_a` of Stacks 09YN satisfied by the counits `φ_a : f_a^{-1}f_{i,*}F → f_{j,*}F`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sites.InverseSystem.InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.pullbackPushforwardDesc
declarations.doc:
**The factorization of a compatible family through the counits.** Writing
`F = colim_i f_i^{-1}f_{i, *}F` with the counits as structure maps, this is the map of sheaves
`F ⟶ H` whose restriction to the level `i` is `g i`. It is built level by level: a presentation
`u_i(V) = X` of an object `X` of `C` carries the section `g i` over `V`, and the compatibility
`hgcomp` makes the result independent of the presentation chosen.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardDesc
    {C : Type w} [SmallCategory C] (D : InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.{u₁, u₂, w}) (u : ∀ i, D.C i ⥤ C)
    (hu : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : i ⟶ j), D.u a ⋙ u i = u j)
    (hobj : ∀ X : C, ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i), (u i).obj Y = X)
    (hhom :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (f : (u i).obj X ⟶ (u i).obj Y),
        ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (g : (D.u a).obj X ⟶ (D.u a).obj Y),
          (u j).map g =
            eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) X) ≫ f ≫ eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) Y).symm)
    (_hhom_inj :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (g₁ g₂ : X ⟶ Y),
        (u i).map g₁ = (u i).map g₂ → ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i), (D.u a).map g₁ = (D.u a).map g₂)
    (K : Precoverage C)
    (_hK :
      ∀ (X : C) (R : Presieve X),
        R ∈ K X ↔
          ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i) (h : (u i).obj Y = X) (S : Presieve Y),
            S ∈ (D.J i).toPrecoverage Y ∧ S ∈ Precoverage.finite (D.C i) Y ∧ R = h ▸ S.map (u i))
    -- the sheaf `F` on `C`, and the canonical maps `φ_a : f_a^{-1}f_{i,*}F → f_{j,*}F` in
    -- adjoint form: `ψ a` is the identity `f_{i,*}F → f_{a,*}f_{j,*}F`
    (F : Sheaf K.toGrothendieck (Type w))
    (ψ : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i), (u i).op ⋙ F.obj ⟶ (D.u a).op ⋙ ((u j).op ⋙ F.obj))
    (hψ :
      ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (V : D.C i) (x : F.obj.obj (op ((u i).obj V))),
        (ψ a).app (op V) x =
          F.obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) V).symm)) x)
    -- a sheaf `H` on `C` and a family of maps `f_{i,*}F → f_{i,*}H` compatible with the `φ_a`
    (H : Sheaf K.toGrothendieck (Type w))
    (g : ∀ i, (u i).op ⋙ F.obj ⟶ (u i).op ⋙ H.obj)
    (hgcomp :
      ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (V : D.C i) (x : F.obj.obj (op ((u i).obj V))),
        (g i).app (op V) x =
          H.obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) V)))
            ((g j).app (op ((D.u a).obj V)) ((ψ a).app (op V) x)))
    : F ⟶ H
