public theorem isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_smooth_of_fibrewise_dense
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f] [IsNoetherian S] (U : X.Opens)
    (hfib : ∀ s : S, Module.depth (S.presheaf.stalk s) (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s))
      (S.presheaf.stalk s) ≤ 1 → f.base ⁻¹' {s} ⊆ (U : Set X))
    (hdense : ∀ s : S, f.base ⁻¹' {s} ⊆ closure ((U : Set X) ∩ f.base ⁻¹' {s})) :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange U.ι).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the full statement under the tag's four hypotheses and nothing else: (1) `Smooth f`, (2) `IsNoetherian S`, (3) `hfib`, the tag's `X_s = U_s` at every `s` with `depth 𝒪_{S, s} ≤ 1`, spelled as containment of the fibre `f⁻¹(s)` in `U`, and (4) `hdense`, the density of `U_s` in `X_s`, spelled as every point of `f⁻¹(s)` lying in the closure of `U ∩ f⁻¹(s)`; the conclusion is that the restriction `finiteEtaleBaseChange U.ι` is an equivalence `FÉt_X ⟶ FÉt_U`.

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_formallySmoothNAdic
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EYC]** (Ramanujam--Samuel for finite étale covers). Let `A → B` be a local
homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with `depth(A) ≥ 2`, with `A → B` formally smooth for
the `𝔪_B`-adic topology, and with `dim(B) > dim(A)`. Let `V ⊆ Y = Spec B` be an open which
contains every prime `𝔮` of `B` with `𝔮 ∩ A ≠ 𝔪_A` and contains the prime `𝔪_A B`. Then the
restriction functor `FÉt_Y ⟶ FÉt_V` is an equivalence.

The two conditions on `V` are `hV₁` and `hV₂`. `hV₂` is phrased as a condition on the points of
`Spec B` rather than on the ideal `𝔪_A B`, so that the primality of `𝔪_A B` need not be
produced.

The fully faithful half is proved: a point of `Spec B` outside `V` lies over `𝔪_A` by `hV₁`, so
its local ring has depth at least two by `two_le_depth_stalk_of_notMem_of_flat`, which is
flatness fed to [Stacks, Tag 0337]; `isConnectedPuncturedStrictHenselization_of_two_le_depth`
([Stacks, Tag 0BLR]) turns that into the local hypothesis of [Stacks, Tag 0BQF], whose
remaining hypothesis — the density of `V`, which the source does not verify — is
`dense_of_forall_comap_ne_maximalIdeal_mem`. That is the source's first paragraph.

Two hypotheses are carried.

* `hflat` is the flatness of `A → B`, asserted without justification in the source's first
  paragraph; it follows from `hsmooth` by [Stacks, Tag 07ED] and [Stacks, Tag 07PM].
* `hessSurj` is essential surjectivity, the source's argument after the first paragraph: the
  reduction to the completions of `A` and `B`, Popescu's theorem writing `B` as a filtered
  colimit of smooth `A`-algebras, the descent of `W ⟶ V` to a finite étale cover of an open of
  one `Spec B_i`, and the appeal to [Stacks, Tag 0EYB].
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_formallySmoothNAdic (A B : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hdepth : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth A (maximalIdeal A) A)
    (hsmooth : RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{u} (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal B))
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A < ringKrullDim B)
    (V : (Spec (.of B)).Opens)
    (hV₁ : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B, q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A B) ≠ maximalIdeal A → q ∈ V)
    (hV₂ : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
      q.asIdeal = Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A) → q ∈ V)
    (hflat : Module.Flat A B)
    (hessSurj : (finiteEtaleBaseChange V.ι).EssSurj) :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange V.ι).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the fully faithful half unconditionally: a point of `Spec B` outside `V` lies over `𝔪_A` by the tag's condition (1), hence its local ring has depth at least two by flatness of `B` over `A` fed to Tag 0337, which is the source's first paragraph; Tag 0BLR through `isConnectedPuncturedStrictHenselization_of_two_le_depth` turns that into the local hypothesis of Tag 0BQF, and the density of `V` that Tag 0BQF also needs — and that the source does not verify — is proved here: such an open contains every minimal prime of `B`, since a minimal prime lying over `𝔪_A` would give a zero-dimensional local ring of depth at least two, against Tag 00LK. Two hypotheses are carried. `hflat` is the flatness of `A → B`, which the source asserts in the first paragraph without justification and which follows from the formal smoothness hypothesis by Tag 07ED and Tag 07PM. `hessSurj` is the essential surjectivity half, that is the whole of the source's argument after the first paragraph: the reduction to the completions (Tags 07NV, 07NW, 07ED, 0BLL), Popescu's theorem (Tag 07GC), the descent along the resulting filtered colimit (Tags 01Z4, 01ZM, 01ZO, 07RP) and the appeal to Tag 0EYB. The formal smoothness hypothesis `hsmooth` and the tag's condition (2) on `V` are stated; they are consumed by the carried half and by the corollary at the punctured spectrum below rather than by the fully faithful half.

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_formallySmoothNAdic_of_depth
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EYC]** (Ramanujam--Samuel for finite étale covers). Let `A → B` be a local
homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume `A` has depth at least two, `A → B` is formally
smooth for the `𝔪_B`-adic topology, and `dim(B) > dim(A)`. For any open `V ⊆ Y = Spec B` which
contains every prime `𝔮 ⊆ B` with `𝔮 ∩ A ≠ 𝔪_A` (`hV₁`) and the prime `𝔪_A B` (`hV₂`, phrased as
a condition on the points of `Spec B`), the restriction functor `FÉt_Y ⟶ FÉt_V` is an
equivalence.

Full faithfulness is the source's first paragraph,
`isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_formallySmoothNAdic`; flatness of `A → B` is
[Stacks, Tag 07NP]; essential surjectivity is
`essSurj_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_formallySmoothNAdic`. The hypothesis `dim(B) > dim(A)` is the
source's own; it is what makes the punctured spectrum an open as in the tag (see
`hasPurity_of_formallySmoothNAdic`) and is not needed for the equivalence itself.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_formallySmoothNAdic_of_depth
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hdepth : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth A (maximalIdeal A) A)
    (hsmooth : RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{u} (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal B))
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A < ringKrullDim B)
    (V : (Spec (.of B)).Opens)
    (hV₁ : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B, q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A B) ≠ maximalIdeal A → q ∈ V)
    (hV₂ : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
      q.asIdeal = Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A) → q ∈ V) :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange V.ι).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence FÉt_Y → FÉt_V, under the tag's hypotheses; nothing is assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.hasPurity_of_formallySmoothNAdic
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EYC], "in particular purity holds for `B`".** Let `A → B` be a local
homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with `depth(A) ≥ 2`, formally smooth for the `𝔪_B`-adic
topology, with `dim(B) > dim(A)`. Then every finite étale cover of the punctured spectrum of `B`
extends to a finite étale cover of `Spec B`.

The punctured spectrum is an open as in the tag: condition (1) because the closed point contracts
to `𝔪_A`, condition (2) because `𝔪_A B ≠ 𝔪_B`, which is where `dim(A) < dim(B)` enters
(`mem_puncturedSpectrum_of_eq_map_maximalIdeal_of_ringKrullDim_lt`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasPurity_of_formallySmoothNAdic (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hdepth : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth A (maximalIdeal A) A)
    (hsmooth : RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{u} (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal B))
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A < ringKrullDim B) :
    HasPurity B
declarations.comment: purity holds for B, under the tag's hypotheses; nothing is assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.pulledBackCover_isFinite
declarations.doc: The canonical pullback of the cover is finite.
declarations.statement:
public instance pulledBackCover_isFinite
    (D : CodimensionOnePullbackSetup.{u}) :
    IsFinite D.pulledBackCover
declarations.comment: finite_etale_pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.pulledBackCover_etale
declarations.doc: The canonical pullback of the cover is étale.
declarations.statement:
public instance pulledBackCover_etale
    (D : CodimensionOnePullbackSetup.{u}) :
    Etale D.pulledBackCover
declarations.comment: finite_etale_pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.pulledBackCover_isUnramifiedInCodimensionOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EYD**, unramified half. If the cover `Y → U` is unramified over `X` in
codimension one, then the pulled-back cover is unramified over `X'` in codimension one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pulledBackCover_isUnramifiedInCodimensionOne
    (D : CodimensionOnePullbackSetup.{u})
    (h : IsUnramifiedInCodimensionOne D.U.ι D.f) :
    IsUnramifiedInCodimensionOne (pullback.fst D.g D.U.ι) D.pulledBackCover
declarations.comment: unramified_in_codimension_one

declarations.name: Stacks.FundamentalGroup.pulledBackCover_isTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EYD**, tamely ramified half. If the cover `Y → U` is tamely ramified over `X` in
codimension one, then the pulled-back cover is tamely ramified over `X'` in codimension one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pulledBackCover_isTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne
    (D : CodimensionOnePullbackSetup.{u})
    (h : IsTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne D.U.ι D.f) :
    IsTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne (pullback.fst D.g D.U.ι) D.pulledBackCover
declarations.comment: tamely_ramified_in_codimension_one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtale_extension_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYE.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme and let `D ⊆ X` be an
effective Cartier divisor such that `D` is a regular scheme. Let `f : Y ⟶ X ∖ D` be a finite
étale morphism. If `Y` is unramified over `X` in codimension one, then there exists a finite étale
morphism `p : Y' ⟶ X` whose restriction to `X ∖ D` is `Y`: an isomorphism
`Y' ×_X (X ∖ D) ≅ Y` over `X ∖ D`.

Here `D` is the closed subscheme `D.subscheme` cut out by the ideal sheaf `D`, and `X ∖ D` is the
open subscheme `D.support.compl`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteEtale_extension_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) (hDreg : IsRegular D.subscheme)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ D.support.compl) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    (hunr : Stacks.FundamentalGroup.IsUnramifiedInCodimensionOne
      (Scheme.Opens.ι D.support.compl) f) :
    ∃ (Y' : Scheme.{u}) (p : Y' ⟶ X), IsFinite p ∧ Etale p ∧
      ∃ e : pullback p (Scheme.Opens.ι D.support.compl) ≅ Y,
        e.hom ≫ f = pullback.snd p (Scheme.Opens.ι D.support.compl)
declarations.comment: a finite étale cover of `X ∖ D` unramified in codimension one extends across a regular effective Cartier divisor `D`; the special case `U = X ∖ D` of Tag 0H2W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra
declarations.doc: The standard tamely ramified algebra `A[X] / (X ^ e - f)`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A) (e : ℕ)
declarations.comment: standard_tamely_ramified_morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedMorphism
declarations.doc: The canonical morphism `Spec(A[X] / (X ^ e - f)) ⟶ Spec(A)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev standardTamelyRamifiedMorphism
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A) (e : ℕ) :
    Scheme.Spec.obj (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.of (standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra A f e))) ⟶
      Scheme.Spec.obj (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.of A))
declarations.comment: standard_tamely_ramified_morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedCover
declarations.doc:
The associated cover, obtained by restricting the standard morphism over
`Spec(A_f)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev standardTamelyRamifiedCover
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A) (e : ℕ) :
    Scheme.Spec.obj (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.of
        (Localization.Away (algebraMap A (standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra A f e) f)))) ⟶
      Scheme.Spec.obj (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.of (Localization.Away f)))
declarations.comment: standard_tamely_ramified_morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedCover_etale
declarations.doc:
Away from `f`, the standard cover defined by `X ^ e = f` is étale when
`e` is a unit in the base ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem standardTamelyRamifiedCover_etale
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A) (e : ℕ) [NeZero e]
    (he : IsUnit (e : A)) :
    Etale (standardTamelyRamifiedCover A f e)
declarations.comment: standard_cover_etale_away

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedMorphism_finiteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
The standard morphism `Spec(A[X] / (X ^ e - f)) ⟶ Spec(A)` is finite locally free: it is
finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. In fact `A[X] / (X ^ e - f)` is free of rank
`e` over `A` (`standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra_free`,
`standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra_finrank`), so the morphism is even finite free.
declarations.statement:
public theorem standardTamelyRamifiedMorphism_finiteLocallyFree
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A) (e : ℕ) [NeZero e] :
    IsFinite (standardTamelyRamifiedMorphism A f e) ∧
      Flat (standardTamelyRamifiedMorphism A f e) ∧
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation (standardTamelyRamifiedMorphism A f e)
declarations.comment: standard_morphism_finite_locally_free

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedCover_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EYF, finiteness of the standard cover.** The restriction
`Spec(C_f) ⟶ Spec(A_f)` of the standard morphism over `Spec(A_f)` is finite. The ring `C_f` is
the localization of `C = A[X] / (X ^ e - f)` at the image of `f`, so it is a finite module over
`A_f` because `C` is a finite `A`-module (`standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra_finite`); finiteness of
a ring map is preserved by localizing source and target at the same element. Together with
`standardTamelyRamifiedCover_etale` this is the assertion of the tag that
`Spec(C_f) ⟶ Spec(A_f)` is a *finite* étale morphism. As for étaleness, the Noetherian,
nonzerodivisor, reducedness and invertibility hypotheses of the tag are not needed away from
`f` and are omitted; only positivity of `e`, expressed by `NeZero e`, is used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem standardTamelyRamifiedCover_isFinite
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A) (e : ℕ) [NeZero e] :
    IsFinite (standardTamelyRamifiedCover A f e)
declarations.comment: the restriction of the standard morphism over Spec(A_f), that is the standard cover, is finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isDiscreteValuationRing_of_mem_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0EYF, the base of the standard tamely ramified morphism.** Let `A` be a Noetherian
ring, let `f : A` be a nonzerodivisor such that `A / fA` is reduced, and let `p` be a minimal
prime over `f`. Then the localization `A_p` is a discrete valuation ring and `f` is a
uniformizer of it. This is the implication asserted in the first sentences of the tag; it is
what licenses the discrete valuation ring hypotheses in the tameness statements below.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDiscreteValuationRing_of_mem_minimalPrimes [IsNoetherianRing A] {f : A}
    (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) (hred : _root_.IsReduced (A ⧸ Ideal.span ({f} : Set A)))
    {p : Ideal A} [p.IsPrime] (hp : p ∈ (Ideal.span ({f} : Set A)).minimalPrimes)
    (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra A S] [IsLocalization.AtPrime S p] :
    ∃ _ : IsDomain S, IsDiscreteValuationRing S ∧ Irreducible (algebraMap A S f)
declarations.comment: the hypotheses on the base imply that A_p is a DVR with uniformizer f, for every minimal prime p over f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedGenericFibreEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The generic fibre of the standard morphism is the Kummer extension.** Base changing
`C = A[X] / (X ^ e - f)` along `A → K` gives `K[X] / (X ^ e - f)`, i.e. the Kummer algebra
`K[f ^ (1 / e)]` of Tag 09EV.
declarations.statement:
public def standardTamelyRamifiedGenericFibreEquiv :
    K ⊗[A] standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra A f e ≃ₐ[K] K1 K f e
declarations.comment: standard_cover_generic_fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedGenericFibre_isTamelyRamified
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0EYF, tameness in codimension one.** Let `A` be a discrete valuation ring with
uniformizer `f`; this is the local ring of `Spec(A)` at the generic point of a prime divisor
contained in the complement of `Spec(A_f)`. Let `K` be its fraction field and let `e ≥ 2` be
invertible in `A`. The generic fibre of the standard morphism over that point is the field
`K[f ^ (1 / e)] = K[X] / (X ^ e - f)` (`standardTamelyRamifiedGenericFibreEquiv`), and that
field extension of `K` is tamely ramified with respect to `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem standardTamelyRamifiedGenericFibre_isTamelyRamified
    (hf : Irreducible f) (he : 2 ≤ e) (hinv : IsUnit (e : A)) :
    letI : Fact (Irreducible (kummerPoly K f e)) :=
      ⟨kummerPoly_irreducible K f e (by omega) hf⟩
    letI : Algebra.IsSeparable K (K1 K f e) :=
      isSeparable_K1 K f e he hf (ringChar_residue_coprime_of_isUnit (R := A) e hinv)
    IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsTamelyRamifiedWithRespectTo A K (K1 K f e)
declarations.comment: the generic fibre of the standard cover at a codimension-one point is tamely ramified with respect to the local ring, for an exponent e ≥ 2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTamelyRamified_self
declarations.doc:
**The trivial extension is tamely ramified.** `K / K` is tamely ramified with respect to
the discrete valuation ring `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTamelyRamified_self :
    IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsTamelyRamifiedWithRespectTo A K K
declarations.comment: trivial_extension_tame

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedGenericFibreEquivOne
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0EYF, the exponent `e = 1`.** The generic fibre of the standard morphism for `e = 1`
is `K` itself; combined with `isTamelyRamified_self` this is tameness in codimension one for
the degenerate exponent.
declarations.statement:
public def standardTamelyRamifiedGenericFibreEquivOne :
    K ⊗[A] standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra A f 1 ≃ₐ[K] K
declarations.comment: standard_cover_generic_fibre_one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedGenericFibreFactor_isTamelyRamified
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0EYF, tameness in codimension one for every field factor.** Let `A` be a discrete
valuation ring with uniformizer `f` — by `isDiscreteValuationRing_of_mem_minimalPrimes` this is
the local ring of `Spec(A)` at the generic point of a prime divisor outside `Spec(A_f)` — let
`K` be its fraction field, and let `e ≥ 1` be invertible in `A`. Then every field factor of the
generic fibre `K ⊗[A] C` of the standard cover, that is, every field `L` receiving a surjection
of `K`-algebras from it, is a finite separable extension of `K` which is tamely ramified with
respect to `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem standardTamelyRamifiedGenericFibreFactor_isTamelyRamified
    (hf : Irreducible f) (he : 1 ≤ e) (hinv : IsUnit (e : A))
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (φ : K ⊗[A] standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra A f e →ₐ[K] L)
    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) :
    ∃ (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L),
      IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsTamelyRamifiedWithRespectTo A K L
declarations.comment: every field factor of the generic fibre of the standard cover at a codimension-one point is tamely ramified with respect to the local ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.standardTamelyRamifiedCover_isTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EYF, tameness in codimension one.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, let `f : A` be a
nonzerodivisor such that `A / fA` is reduced, and let `e ≥ 1` be invertible in `A`.  The finite
étale cover `Spec(C_f) ⟶ Spec(A_f)` attached to `C = A[x] / (x ^ e - f)` is tamely ramified over
`Spec(A)` in codimension one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem standardTamelyRamifiedCover_isTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A) (e : ℕ) [NeZero e]
    (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (hred : _root_.IsReduced (A ⧸ Ideal.span ({f} : Set A)))
    (hinv : IsUnit (e : A)) :
    Stacks.FundamentalGroup.IsTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne
      (standardTamelyRamifiedOpen A f) (standardTamelyRamifiedCover A f e)
declarations.comment: standard_cover_tame_codimension_one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEtaleLocallyStandardTamelyRamified_of_isTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne
declarations.doc:
**Abhyankar's lemma for a regular divisor, [Stacks, Tag 0EYG].** Let `X` be a locally
Noetherian scheme and let `D ⊆ X` be an effective Cartier divisor such that `D` is a regular
scheme. Let `f : Y ⟶ X ∖ D` be a finite étale morphism. If `Y` is tamely ramified over `X` in
codimension one, then étale locally on `X` the morphism `Y ⟶ X` is a finite disjoint union of
standard tamely ramified morphisms as described in [Stacks, Example 0EYF]: every `x ∈ X` lies in
the image of an étale `Spec A ⟶ X` with `A` Noetherian, on which `X ∖ D` is `Spec A_φ` for a
nonzerodivisor `φ` with `A / φA` reduced, and over which `Y` is
`∐ᵢ Spec (A[x]/(x^{eᵢ} - φ))_φ` with each `eᵢ ≥ 1` invertible in `A`.

Here `D` is the closed subscheme `D.subscheme` cut out by the ideal sheaf `D`, and `X ∖ D` is the
open subscheme `D.support.compl`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleLocallyStandardTamelyRamified_of_isTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) (hDreg : IsRegular D.subscheme)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ (D.support.compl : X.Opens)) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    (htame : IsTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne (Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)) f) :
    IsEtaleLocallyStandardTamelyRamified (D.support.compl : X.Opens) f
declarations.comment: Abhyankar's lemma for a regular divisor: a finite étale cover of `X ∖ D` tamely ramified in codimension one is étale locally on `X` a finite disjoint union of the standard tamely ramified covers of Example 0EYF

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TameCovers.normalization_of_isTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYH.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, let `D ⊆ X` be an
effective Cartier divisor such that `D` is a regular scheme, and let `f : Y ⟶ X ∖ D` be finite
étale and tamely ramified over `X` in codimension one (the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0EYG]).
Then the normalization `π : Y' ⟶ X` of `X` in `Y` is a finite locally free morphism such that
1. the restriction of `Y'` to `X ∖ D` is isomorphic to `Y` (over `X ∖ D`),
2. `D' = π⁻¹(D)_red` is an effective Cartier divisor on `Y'`, and
3. `D'` is a regular scheme.
Moreover, étale locally on `X` the morphism `Y' ⟶ X` is a finite disjoint union of morphisms
`Spec(A[x]/(x^e - φ)) ⟶ Spec(A)` where `A` is a Noetherian ring, `φ ∈ A` is a nonzerodivisor
with `A/φA` regular, and `e ≥ 1` is invertible in `A`: every `x ∈ X` is in the image of an
étale `g : Spec A ⟶ X` over which `Y' ×_X Spec A ≅ ∐ᵢ Spec(A[x]/(x^{eᵢ} - φ))` over `Spec A`.

Here `π` is `(f ≫ ι).fromNormalization` for the inclusion `ι` of `X ∖ D = D.support.compl`,
and `D'` is the closed subscheme of the radical of the ideal sheaf `D.comap π`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalization_of_isTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne_of_isRegular {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) (hDreg : IsRegular D.subscheme)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ (D.support.compl : X.Opens)) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    (hf : Stacks.FundamentalGroup.IsTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne
      (Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)) f) :
    Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree
        (f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).fromNormalization ∧
      (∃ e : pullback (f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).fromNormalization
          (Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)) ≅ Y,
        e.hom ≫ f = pullback.snd _ _) ∧
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
        (D.comap (f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).fromNormalization).radical ∧
      IsRegular (D.comap (f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι
          (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).fromNormalization).radical.subscheme ∧
      ∀ x : X, ∃ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (g : Spec A ⟶ X) (_ : Etale g) (a : Spec A)
        (_ : g a = x) (φ : A) (_ : IsNoetherianRing A) (_ : φ ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
        (_ : IsRegularRing (A ⧸ Ideal.span {φ})) (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n → ℕ)
        (_ : ∀ i, 0 < e i ∧ IsUnit (e i : A)),
        ∃ ι : pullback (f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).fromNormalization g ≅
            ∐ fun i ↦ Spec (.of (standardTamelyRamifiedAlgebra A φ (e i))),
          ι.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i ↦ standardTamelyRamifiedMorphism A φ (e i)) =
            pullback.snd _ g
declarations.comment: the normalization of `X` in a tame cover `Y` of `X ∖ D` is finite locally free, restricts to `Y`, has `π⁻¹(D)_red` a regular effective Cartier divisor, and is étale locally a finite disjoint union of standard `Spec(A[x]/(x^e - f)) ⟶ Spec(A)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TameCovers.exists_lift_etaleAt_fromNormalization_of_isTamelyRamified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYI (1).** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `D ⊆ X` an
effective Cartier divisor such that `D` is a regular scheme, and `f : Y ⟶ X ∖ D` a finite étale
morphism tamely ramified over `X` in codimension one (the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0EYG]). Let
`π : Y' ⟶ X` be the normalization of `X` in `Y` ([Stacks, Tag 0EYH]). Let `R` be a discrete
valuation ring with fraction field `K` and `t : Spec R ⟶ X` a morphism such that the scheme
theoretic inverse image `t⁻¹D` is the reduced closed point of `Spec R`. If `t|_{Spec K}` lifts to
a point `y : Spec K ⟶ Y`, then there is a lift `t' : Spec R ⟶ Y'` of `t` (extending `y`) such
that `π` is étale along `t'(Spec R)`.

Here `D` is the closed subscheme `D.subscheme` cut out by the ideal sheaf `D`, `X ∖ D` is the
open subscheme `D.support.compl`, and `Y'` is the relative normalization of `Y ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_lift_etaleAt_fromNormalization_of_isTamelyRamified
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) (hDreg : IsRegular D.subscheme)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ (D.support.compl : X.Opens)) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    (hf : Stacks.FundamentalGroup.IsTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne
      (Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)) f)
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    (t : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X)
    (ht : D.comap t = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      ⟨({IsLocalRing.closedPoint R} : Set (Spec (.of R))),
        (PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_singleton_iff_isMaximal _).mpr
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal.isMaximal R)⟩)
    (y : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Y)
    (hy : y ≫ f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens) =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)) ≫ t) :
    ∃ t' : Spec (.of R) ⟶ (f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).normalization,
      t' ≫ (f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).fromNormalization = t ∧
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)) ≫ t' =
        y ≫ (f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).toNormalization ∧
      ∀ r, EtaleAt (f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).fromNormalization (t' r)
declarations.comment: (1): a lift of `t|_{Spec K}` to `Y` gives a lift `t'` of `t` to the normalization `Y'`, and `Y' ⟶ X` is étale along `t'(Spec R)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TameCovers.exists_opens_etale_fromNormalization_of_isTamelyRamified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYI (2).** In the situation of Tag 0EYI (1) (`X` locally Noetherian,
`D ⊆ X` an effective Cartier divisor which is a regular scheme, `f : Y ⟶ X ∖ D` finite étale and
tamely ramified over `X` in codimension one, `π : Y' ⟶ X` the normalization of `X` in `Y`, `R` a
discrete valuation ring with fraction field `K`, `t : Spec R ⟶ X` with `t⁻¹D` the reduced closed
point of `Spec R`): if `Spec K ×_X Y` is isomorphic, over `Spec K`, to a disjoint union of copies
of `Spec K`, then `π` is finite étale over an open neighbourhood `V` of `t(Spec R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_etale_fromNormalization_of_isTamelyRamified
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D) (hDreg : IsRegular D.subscheme)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ (D.support.compl : X.Opens)) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    (hf : Stacks.FundamentalGroup.IsTamelyRamifiedInCodimensionOne
      (Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)) f)
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    (t : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X)
    (ht : D.comap t = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      ⟨({IsLocalRing.closedPoint R} : Set (Spec (.of R))),
        (PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_singleton_iff_isMaximal _).mpr
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal.isMaximal R)⟩)
    (J : Type u)
    (eJ : pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)) ≫ t)
        (f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)) ≅ ∐ fun _ : J ↦ Spec (.of K))
    (heJ : eJ.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun _ ↦ 𝟙 _) = pullback.fst _ _) :
    ∃ V : X.Opens, (∀ r, t r ∈ V) ∧
      IsFinite ((f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).fromNormalization ∣_ V) ∧
      Etale ((f ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (D.support.compl : X.Opens)).fromNormalization ∣_ V)
declarations.comment: (2): if `Spec K ×_X Y` is a disjoint union of copies of `Spec K`, the normalization `Y' ⟶ X` is finite étale over an open neighbourhood of `t(Spec R)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteEtaleGaloisCover.exists_extension_of_genericFiber_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Extending a Galois cover of the generic fibre.** Let `S` be an integral normal Noetherian
scheme with generic point `η`, let `f : X ⟶ S` be a smooth morphism with geometrically connected
fibres and let `σ : S ⟶ X` be a section of `f`. Let `Z ⟶ X_η` be a finite étale Galois cover
with group `G` whose order is invertible on `S` (a unit in every residue field `κ(s)`), such that
`Z` has a `κ(η)`-rational point `z` mapping to `σ(η)`. Then there is a finite étale Galois cover
`Y ⟶ X` with group `G` whose restriction to `X_η` is `Z`: an isomorphism `Y ×_X X_η ≅ Z` over
`X_η` compatible with the actions of `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_extension_of_genericFiber_of_isNoetherian
    {S X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsNoetherian S] [IsIntegral S] [IsNormal S]
    [Smooth f] [GeometricallyConnected f]
    (σ : S ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 S)
    (G : Type v) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (hG : ∀ s : S, IsUnit (Nat.card G : S.residueField s))
    (Z : FiniteEtaleGaloisCover (f.fiber (genericPoint S)) G)
    (z : Spec (S.residueField (genericPoint S)) ⟶ Z.obj.left)
    (hz : z ≫ Z.obj.hom = genericFiberSection f σ hσ) :
    ∃ (Y : FiniteEtaleGaloisCover X G)
      (e : (finiteEtaleBaseChange (f.fiberι (genericPoint S))).obj Y.obj ≅ Z.obj),
      ∀ g : Gᵐᵒᵖ, (finiteEtaleBaseChange (f.fiberι (genericPoint S))).map (Y.action g).asIso.hom ≫
        e.hom = e.hom ≫ (Z.action g).asIso.hom
declarations.comment: the full statement under the tag's hypotheses and nothing else: `S` integral (`IsIntegral S`), normal (`IsNormal S`) and Noetherian (`IsNoetherian S`); `f` smooth with geometrically connected fibres (`Smooth f`, `GeometricallyConnected f`); a section `σ` of `f` (`hσ`); a finite étale Galois cover `Z` of the generic fibre `X_η` with group `G`, `G` finite of order invertible on `S` (`hG`: a unit in every residue field); a `κ(η)`-rational point `z` of `Z` over `σ(η)` (`hz`). The conclusion is a finite étale Galois cover `Y` of `X` with group `G` and a `G`-equivariant isomorphism `Y ×_X X_η ≅ Z` over `X_η`.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.toCover
declarations.doc:
**The first map of the Mayer--Vietoris sequence in degree `n`**,
`Rⁿf_*F ⟶ Rⁿa_*(F|_U) ⊕ Rⁿb_*(F|_V)`, as a natural transformation of functors in `F`: that
naturality is the functoriality asserted by the statement.
declarations.statement:
def toCover (n : ℕ) :
    higherDirectImage.{u, v} f n ⟶
      restrictedHigherDirectImage.{u, v} f U n ⊞
        restrictedHigherDirectImage.{u, v} f V n
declarations.comment: the map Rⁿf_*F → Rⁿa_*(F|_U) ⊕ Rⁿb_*(F|_V)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.toIntersection
declarations.doc:
**The second map of the Mayer--Vietoris sequence in degree `n`**,
`Rⁿa_*(F|_U) ⊕ Rⁿb_*(F|_V) ⟶ Rⁿc_*(F|_{U ∩ V})`, as a natural transformation of functors
in `F`.
declarations.statement:
def toIntersection (n : ℕ) :
    restrictedHigherDirectImage.{u, v} f U n ⊞
        restrictedHigherDirectImage.{u, v} f V n ⟶
      restrictedHigherDirectImage.{u, v} f (U ⊓ V) n
declarations.comment: the map Rⁿa_*(F|_U) ⊕ Rⁿb_*(F|_V) → Rⁿc_*(F|_{U ∩ V})

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.boundary
declarations.doc:
**The connecting map of the Mayer--Vietoris sequence**,
`Rⁿc_*(F|_{U ∩ V}) ⟶ Rⁿ⁺¹f_*F`, as a natural transformation of functors in `F`.
declarations.comment: the connecting map Rⁿc_*(F|_{U ∩ V}) → Rⁿ⁺¹f_*F

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.cohomologySequence_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYK (relative Mayer--Vietoris), exactness.** For a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes, two open subschemes `U` and `V` covering `X`, and every abelian sheaf
`F` on the small étale site of `X`, the six-term window

`Rⁿf_*F ⟶ Rⁿa_*(F|_U) ⊕ Rⁿb_*(F|_V) ⟶ Rⁿc_*(F|_{U ∩ V}) ⟶ Rⁿ⁺¹f_*F ⟶ ⋯`

of the Mayer--Vietoris sequence is exact, for every `n`. Since the three maps are natural
transformations of functors of `F`, the sequence is functorial in `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologySequence_exact (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤) (n : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    (ComposableArrows.mk₅ ((toCover.{u, v} f U V n).app F)
      ((toIntersection.{u, v} f U V n).app F) ((boundary.{u, v} f U V hUV n).app F)
      ((toCover.{u, v} f U V (n + 1)).app F)
      ((toIntersection.{u, v} f U V (n + 1)).app F)).Exact
declarations.comment: exactness of the long sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.mono_toCover_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYK (relative Mayer--Vietoris), the left end.** The Mayer--Vietoris
sequence starts with `0 ⟶ f_*F`: the degree-zero map `f_*F ⟶ a_*(F|_U) ⊕ b_*(F|_V)` is a
monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_toCover_zero (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    Mono ((toCover.{u, v} f U V 0).app F)
declarations.comment: the sequence begins with 0 ⟶ f_*F

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.higherDirectImageZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**The degree-zero term of the sequence is the direct image itself.** The direct image along
`f` is left exact, being a right adjoint, so `R⁰f_* ≅ f_*`; this is what makes the sequence of
the statement begin with `0 ⟶ f_*F`.
declarations.statement:
def higherDirectImageZeroIso :
    higherDirectImage.{u, v} f 0 ≅ etaleAbelianDirectImage.{u, v} f
declarations.comment: the degree-zero term is f_*F

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.restrictedHigherDirectImageZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**The degree-zero restricted term of the sequence is the pushed-forward restriction
itself**, `R⁰(F ↦ a_*(F|_U)) ≅ (F ↦ a_*(F|_U))`: restriction to `U` is exact and the direct
image along `a = f|_U` is left exact.
declarations.statement:
def restrictedHigherDirectImageZeroIso :
    restrictedHigherDirectImage.{u, v} f U 0 ≅ restrictedPushforward.{u, v} f U
declarations.comment: the degree-zero restricted term is a_*(F|_U)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSiteColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EYL.** Let `I` be a directed set, let `(X_i, f_{i'i})` be an inverse system of
schemes over `I` with affine transition morphisms and let `X = lim X_i`.  Then
`X_{affine, étale} = colim (X_i)_{affine, étale}` as sites in the sense of Stacks 09YL.
declarations.comment: canonical site system

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSiteColimit_level_cover
declarations.doc:
The level equivalences identify the Grothendieck topologies: a presieve is covering at a
stage exactly when its image generates a covering sieve of the corresponding affine étale site.
Finiteness is not imposed here, since an equivalence can identify distinct isomorphic source
objects and need not reflect finiteness of a particular presieve.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineEtaleSiteColimit_level_cover
    (i : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I)
    (Y : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.C i) (R : Presieve Y) :
    R ∈ ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.J i).toPrecoverage Y ↔
      R.map ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).levelEquiv i).functor ∈
        (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.topology B
          (D.obj ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj i))
          (hD ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj
            i))).toPrecoverage
          (((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).levelEquiv i).functor.obj Y)
declarations.comment: level coverings

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSiteColimit_levelEquiv_isDenseSubsite
declarations.doc:
**The level equivalences identify the Grothendieck topologies, in the form of a dense
subsite.** The topology of a level is the topology induced on the category of representatives by
the level equivalence, so that equivalence's functor is a dense subsite of the small affine étale
site of the corresponding `X_i`.

This is `affineEtaleSiteColimit_level_cover` in the form typeclass inference consumes.  The
covering correspondence is a statement about presieves; transporting sheaves across a level needs
continuity of the functor as an *instance*, and `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite` carries
both that and the cover-lifting direction.  Nothing is asserted beyond the covering
correspondence: the content is that it holds for sieves at every object, which is what makes the
induced topology the topology of the level.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineEtaleSiteColimit_levelEquiv_isDenseSubsite
    (i : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I) :
    ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).levelEquiv i).functor.IsDenseSubsite
      ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.J i)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.topology B
        (D.obj ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj i))
        (hD ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj i)))
declarations.comment: level coverings, as a dense subsite

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSiteColimit_levelToSmallEtale_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
**A level of the system, carried into the small étale site of its scheme, is a morphism of
sites.** The composite of the level equivalence with the inclusion of Stacks 04HR is continuous
from the topology of the level to the small étale topology of `X_i`.

This is the level-side counterpart of
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.AffineLimitCohomology.isContinuous_limitToSmallEtale`, and unlike that one
it is not a universe raising followed by 04HR: a level of this system is a category of
representatives, equivalent to the small affine étale site of `X_i` but not equal to it, so the
first factor is the level equivalence and its continuity is
`affineEtaleSiteColimit_levelEquiv_isDenseSubsite`.  Without this a sheaf on the small étale site
of `X_i` cannot be read on the level at all.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineEtaleSiteColimit_levelToSmallEtale_isContinuous
    (i : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I) :
    (((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).levelEquiv i).functor ⋙
        AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.inclusion B
          (D.obj ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj i))
          (hD ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj
            i))).IsContinuous
      ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.J i)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.topology B
        (D.obj ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj i))
        (hD ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj i)))
declarations.comment: levels as morphisms of sites to the small étale sites

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSiteColimit_levelToSmallEtale_sheafEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Restriction of sheaves of sets from the small étale site of `X_i` to a level is an
equivalence.** Both factors of the crossing are: the level equivalence by
`affineEtaleSiteColimit_levelEquiv_isDenseSubsite`, and the inclusion of the small affine étale
site by Stacks 04HR.

This says that reading a sheaf of a level as the restriction of a sheaf on the small étale site of
`X_i` is no restriction on the level sheaf: every one of them is isomorphic to such a restriction,
and every map of them to a map of those.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineEtaleSiteColimit_levelToSmallEtale_sheafEquiv
    (i : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I) :
    letI := affineEtaleSiteColimit_levelToSmallEtale_isContinuous D c B hD hX hc i
    ((((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).levelEquiv i).functor ⋙
      AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.inclusion B
        (D.obj ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj i))
        (hD ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj
          i))).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (max u v + 1))
      ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.J i)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.topology B
        (D.obj ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj i))
        (hD ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).indexEquiv.functor.obj
          i)))).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: sheaves of a level are sheaves of the small étale site of its scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSiteColimit_obj_descends
declarations.doc: Every affine étale object over the limit descends to a finite stage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineEtaleSiteColimit_obj_descends
    (Z : AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale B c.pt hX) :
    ∃ (i : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I)
      (Y : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.C i),
      ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit i).obj Y = Z
declarations.comment: objects

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSiteColimit_hom_descends
declarations.doc:
Every morphism between objects descended from one stage descends after increasing the
stage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineEtaleSiteColimit_hom_descends
    (i : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I)
    (X Y : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.C i)
    (f : ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit i).obj X ⟶
      ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit i).obj Y) :
    ∃ (j : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I) (a : j ⟶ i)
      (g : ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.u a).obj X ⟶
        ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.u a).obj Y),
      ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit j).map g =
        eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj
          ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit_transition a) X) ≫ f ≫
          eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj
            ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit_transition a) Y).symm
declarations.comment: morphisms

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSiteColimit_hom_eventually_eq
declarations.doc: Two morphisms that agree over the limit agree after increasing the stage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineEtaleSiteColimit_hom_eventually_eq
    (i : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I)
    (X Y : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.C i)
    (f g : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfg : ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit i).map f =
      ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit i).map g) :
    ∃ (j : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I) (a : j ⟶ i),
      ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.u a).map f =
        ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.u a).map g
declarations.comment: faithfulness

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSiteColimit_mem_precoverage_iff
declarations.doc:
Coverings of the small affine étale site of the limit are exactly the images of finite
coverings from a stage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineEtaleSiteColimit_mem_precoverage_iff
    (Z : AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale B c.pt hX) (R : Presieve Z) :
    R ∈ AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.precoverage B c.pt hX Z ↔
      ∃ (i : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I)
        (Y : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.C i)
        (h : ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit i).obj Y = Z)
        (S : Presieve Y),
        S ∈ ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.J i).toPrecoverage Y ∧
          S ∈ Precoverage.finite ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.C i) Y ∧
          R = h ▸ S.map ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit i)
declarations.comment: coverings

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSiteColimit_isColimitPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EYL**, the clause "as sites in the sense of Stacks 09YL". The standard étale
precoverage of the small affine étale site of the limit `X = lim X_i` *is* the colimit
precoverage that Stacks 09YL produces from the canonical system: its coverings are exactly the
images of the finite coverings of the stages, and it therefore satisfies the three axioms of a
site in the sense of Stacks 00VH — a one-element family given by an isomorphism is a covering,
coverings are stable under refinement by coverings, and the fibre products of a covering along
any morphism exist and again form a covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineEtaleSiteColimit_isColimitPrecoverage :
    (∀ (Z : AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale B c.pt hX) (R : Presieve Z),
        R ∈ AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.precoverage B c.pt hX Z ↔
          ∃ (i : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.I)
            (Y : (affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.C i)
            (h : ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit i).obj Y = Z)
            (S : Presieve Y),
            S ∈ ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.J i).toPrecoverage Y ∧
              S ∈ Precoverage.finite
                  ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).system.C i) Y ∧
                R = h ▸ S.map ((affineEtaleSiteColimit D c B hD hX hc).toLimit i)) ∧
      (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.precoverage B c.pt hX).HasIsos ∧
      (∀ (Z : AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale B c.pt hX) (R : Presieve Z)
          (T : ∀ ⦃Y : AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale B c.pt hX⦄ (f : Y ⟶ Z),
            R f → Presieve Y),
          R ∈ AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.precoverage B c.pt hX Z →
            (∀ ⦃Y : AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale B c.pt hX⦄ (f : Y ⟶ Z) (hf : R f),
                T f hf ∈ AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.precoverage B c.pt hX Y) →
              R.bind T ∈ AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.precoverage B c.pt hX Z) ∧
        ∃ _ : (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.precoverage B c.pt hX).HasPullbacks,
          ∀ (Z W : AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale B c.pt hX) (f : W ⟶ Z)
              (R : Presieve Z) [R.HasPullbacks f],
            R ∈ AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.precoverage B c.pt hX Z →
              R.pullbackArrows f ∈
                AlgebraicGeometry.SmallAffineEtale.precoverage B c.pt hX W
declarations.comment: colimit site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleStagesCoveringsRefine_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EYL for the small étale site.** Let `X = lim X_i` be the limit of a directed
inverse system of quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms inside
a big étale site. Every covering of the final object of the small étale site of `X` is refined
by the inverse image of a finite covering of the final object at some stage beyond a prescribed
one.

The hypotheses are the three geometric conditions the assertion needs and which
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtaleStagesCoveringsRefine`, a predicate on an arbitrary cone, does not
itself carry: the cone is limiting, the transition morphisms are affine, and the stages are
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Quasi-compactness is not cosmetic: the conclusion demands a
finite refining family, and over a vertex which is an infinite disjoint union the covering by
the components admits none.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleStagesCoveringsRefine_of_isLimit (hc : IsLimit c)
    (haff : ∀ {p q : Iᵒᵖ} (e : p ⟶ q), IsAffineHom (B.inclusion.map (Dg.map e)))
    (hqc : ∀ p : I, CompactSpace (Dg.obj (op p)).obj)
    (hqs : ∀ p : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (Dg.obj (op p)).obj) :
    SmallEtaleStagesCoveringsRefine B Dg c hX
declarations.comment: coverings of the final object, for the small étale site

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.transitionMap
declarations.doc:
**The transition maps of Stacks 0EYM**, `ψ_{i'i} : h_{i'i}^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} ℱ_i ⟶
R^p g_{i', *} ℱ_{i'}`: the base change map of the transition square
`g_{i'} ≫ h_{i'i} = f_{i'i} ≫ g_i` on higher direct images, followed by `R^p g_{i', *}` of the
transition map `φ_{i'i} : f_{i'i}^{-1}ℱ_i ⟶ ℱ_{i'}` of the system of sheaves.
declarations.statement:
def transitionMap (F : EtaleSheafSystem DX Ab.{u + 1}) {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j) :
    (smallEtalePullbackAb (DS.map a)).obj
        (((smallEtalePushforwardAb (γ.app j)).rightDerived p).obj (F.obj j)) ⟶
      ((smallEtalePushforwardAb (γ.app i)).rightDerived p).obj (F.obj i)
declarations.comment: the transition maps `ψ_{i'i} : h_{i'i}^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} ℱ_i ⟶ R^p g_{i', *} ℱ_{i'}` of the first paragraph of the proof, constructed from the base change map on higher direct images of Stacks 0F02 and the transition map of the system of sheaves. The cocycle condition `ψ_{i''i} = ψ_{i''i'} ∘ h_{i''i'}^{-1}ψ_{i'i}`, which the source gets from Stacks 0E47, is NOT proved: pasting of base change maps is carried for ringed topoi on sheaves of modules and for the unbounded derived étale base change map, but not for the bounded below `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb` that `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.higherBaseChangeMapAb` descends from. The colimit assertion `R^p g_* ℱ = colim_i h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} ℱ_i` is NOT proved either; it additionally needs the comparison of Stacks 04HR at the level of cohomology, the carried Stacks 09YQ being stated for the right-derived `sheafSections` of the small AFFINE étale sites.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.projectionMap
declarations.doc:
**The cocone maps of Stacks 0EYM**, `ψ_i : h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} ℱ_i ⟶ R^p g_* ℱ`: the base
change map of the projection square `g ≫ h_i = f_i ≫ g_i` on higher direct images, followed by
`R^p g_*` of the map `ι_i : f_i^{-1}ℱ_i ⟶ ℱ` presenting `ℱ` as `colim f_i^{-1}ℱ_i`.
declarations.statement:
def projectionMap (F : EtaleSheafSystem DX Ab.{u + 1})
    (ι : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, (smallEtalePullbackAb (cX.π.app i)).obj (F.obj i) ⟶ 𝓕) (i : Iᵒᵖ) :
    (smallEtalePullbackAb (cS.π.app i)).obj
        (((smallEtalePushforwardAb (γ.app i)).rightDerived p).obj (F.obj i)) ⟶
      ((smallEtalePushforwardAb (limitMorphism γ cX cS hcS)).rightDerived p).obj 𝓕
declarations.comment: the cocone maps `ψ_i : h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} ℱ_i ⟶ R^p g_* ℱ` of the first paragraph of the proof, constructed from the base change map on higher direct images of Stacks 0F02 and the map `ι_i : f_i^{-1}ℱ_i ⟶ ℱ` presenting the colimit. The compatibility `ψ_{i'} ∘ h_{i'}^{-1}ψ_{i'i} = ψ_i`, which the source gets from Stacks 0E47, is NOT proved, for the reason recorded on `transitionMap`; so these maps are not exhibited as a cocone. The colimit assertion `R^p g_* ℱ = colim_i h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} ℱ_i` is NOT proved.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.isHigherDirectImageColimit_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be a directed set, let `(X_i, f_{i'i})` and `(S_i, h_{i'i})` be inverse systems of
schemes over `I` with affine transition morphisms, let `g_i : X_i ⟶ S_i` be a morphism of inverse
systems with every `g_i` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let `X = lim X_i`, `S = lim S_i` and
`g : X ⟶ S` the limit morphism. Let `(F_i, φ_{i'i})` be a system of abelian
sheaves on `(X_i, f_{i'i})` and `ι_i : f_i^{-1}F_i ⟶ 𝓕` maps, compatible with the transition maps,
presenting `𝓕 = colim f_i^{-1}F_i`. Then for every `p ≥ 0`

`R^p g_* 𝓕 = colim_{i ∈ I} h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *}F_i`:

every family of maps out of the `h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *}F_i` compatible with the maps
`h_{i'}^{-1}ψ_{i'i}` induced by the transition maps
`ψ_{i'i} : h_{i'i}^{-1} R^p g_{i, *}F_i ⟶ R^p g_{i', *}F_{i'}` factors uniquely through the cocone
maps `ψ_i : h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *}F_i ⟶ R^p g_* 𝓕`, both families being built from the base change
maps on higher direct images as in the source
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.transitionMap`,
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.projectionMap`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isHigherDirectImageColimit_of_isLimit (p : ℕ)
    (𝓕 : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cX.pt) Ab.{max u v + 1})
    (F : EtaleSheafSystem DX Ab.{max u v + 1})
    (ι : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, (smallEtalePullbackAb (cX.π.app i)).obj (F.obj i) ⟶ 𝓕)
    (hι : ∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j),
      (conePullbackComp cX a).inv.app (F.obj j) ≫
        (smallEtalePullbackAb (cX.π.app i)).map (F.map a) ≫ ι i = ι j)
    (hpres : IsPullbackColimitPresentation cX 𝓕 F ι) :
    IsHigherDirectImageColimit γ p cX cS hcS 𝓕 F ι

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.higherDirectImageColimit
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be a directed set, `g_i : X_i ⟶ S_i` an inverse system of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated morphisms of schemes with affine transition morphisms `f_{i'i}`, `h_{i'i}`,
`g : X ⟶ S` its limit with projections `f_i`, `h_i`, `(ℱ_i, φ_{i'i})` a system of abelian sheaves
on `(X_i, f_{i'i})` and `ℱ = colim f_i⁻¹ℱ_i`. Then for every `p`

* the maps `ψ_{i'i} : h_{i'i}⁻¹R^p g_{i, *}ℱ_i ⟶ R^p g_{i', *}ℱ_{i'}` satisfy the cocycle condition
  `ψ_{i''i} = ψ_{i''i'} ∘ h_{i''i'}⁻¹ψ_{i'i}`;
* the maps `ψ_i : h_i⁻¹R^p g_{i, *}ℱ_i ⟶ R^p g_*ℱ` satisfy `ψ_{i'} ∘ h_{i'}⁻¹ψ_{i'i} = ψ_i`;
* they present `R^p g_*ℱ = colim_{i ∈ I} h_i⁻¹R^p g_{i, *}ℱ_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem higherDirectImageColimit (p : ℕ) (F : EtaleSheafSystem DX Ab.{u + 1})
    (𝓕 : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cX.pt) Ab.{u + 1})
    (ι : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, (smallEtalePullbackAb (cX.π.app i)).obj (F.obj i) ⟶ 𝓕)
    (hι : ∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j),
      (conePullbackComp cX a).inv.app (F.obj j) ≫
        (smallEtalePullbackAb (cX.π.app i)).map (F.map a) ≫ ι i = ι j)
    (hpres : IsPullbackColimitPresentation cX 𝓕 F ι) :
    (∀ {i j k : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j) (b : j ⟶ k),
        (systemPullbackComp DS Ab.{u + 1} a b).inv.app
              (((smallEtalePushforwardAb (γ.app k)).rightDerived p).obj (F.obj k)) ≫
            (systemPullback DS Ab.{u + 1} a).map (transitionMap γ p F b) ≫
              transitionMap γ p F a =
          transitionMap γ p F (a ≫ b)) ∧
      (∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j),
          (conePullbackComp cS a).inv.app
                (((smallEtalePushforwardAb (γ.app j)).rightDerived p).obj (F.obj j)) ≫
              (smallEtalePullbackAb (cS.π.app i)).map (transitionMap γ p F a) ≫
                projectionMap γ cX cS hcS p 𝓕 F ι i =
            projectionMap γ cX cS hcS p 𝓕 F ι j) ∧
        IsHigherDirectImageColimit γ p cX cS hcS 𝓕 F ι

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.directImageSystem
declarations.doc:
Let `(X_i, f_{i'i})` be an inverse system of schemes, let `f_i : X ⟶ X_i` be the projections
of a cone over it, and let `𝓕` be a sheaf on the small étale site of `X`. The direct images
`f_{i,*}𝓕`, with the canonical maps `φ_{i'i} : f_{i'i}^{-1} f_{i,*}𝓕 ⟶ f_{i',*}𝓕` adjoint to the
identification `f_{i,*}𝓕 ≅ f_{i'i,*} f_{i',*}𝓕` given by `f_i = f_{i'} ≫ f_{i'i}`, form a system
of sheaves on `(X_i, f_{i'i})` in the sense of Stacks 0EZL.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isPullbackColimitPresentation_directImageSystem
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EYN], the colimit.** Let `X = lim X_i` be a directed limit of schemes with
affine transition morphisms and projections `f_i : X ⟶ X_i`, and let `𝓕` be an abelian sheaf on
`X_étale`. Then the counits `f_i⁻¹f_{i,*}𝓕 ⟶ 𝓕` present `𝓕 = colim f_i⁻¹f_{i,*}𝓕` over the
system of sheaves `(f_{i,*}𝓕, φ_{i'i})` of `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.directImageSystem`.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isColimitPullbackDirectImageCocone
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EYN] (2), for sheaves of sets.** Let `X = lim X_i` be a directed limit of
schemes with affine transition morphisms `f_{i'i}` and projection morphisms `f_i : X ⟶ X_i`, and
let `𝓕` be a sheaf of sets on the small étale site of `X`. Then `𝓕 = colim_i f_i^{-1}f_{i,*}𝓕`:
the cocone of counits `f_i^{-1}f_{i,*}𝓕 ⟶ 𝓕` over the diagram
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.pullbackDirectImageDiagram`, whose transition maps are built from the maps
`φ_{i'i} : f_{i'i}^{-1}f_{i,*}𝓕 ⟶ f_{i',*}𝓕` of the system of sheaves of part (1),
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.directImageSystem`, is a colimit cocone. Equivalently, the canonical map
`colim_i f_i^{-1}f_{i,*}𝓕 ⟶ 𝓕` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
def isColimitPullbackDirectImageCocone
    (F : Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.smallEtaleTopology c.pt) (Type (max u v + 1))) :
    IsColimit (pullbackDirectImageCocone D (Type (max u v + 1)) c F)
declarations.comment: part (2): `𝓕 = colim_i f_i^{-1}f_{i,*}𝓕` for the system of part (1), on Mathlib's small étale site, for sheaves of sets

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.AffineLimitCohomology.restrictionIsColimit_limitToSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EYN, second half, on the small étale site of a limit of schemes.** Let `(X_i)` be
an inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms over a nonempty directed index, all
of them objects of a big étale site `B`, let `X = lim X_i`, and let `F` be a sheaf of sets on the
small étale site of `X`. Then

`F = colim_i p_i^{-1} p_{i,*} F`,

in the form the inverse-system machinery proves it: every family of maps out of the restrictions
of `F` to the levels of the system of sites of [Stacks, Tag 0EYL], compatible with the canonical
transition maps, is the restriction of a **unique** map of sheaves out of `F`. Those restrictions
are the `p_{i,*}F` read on the levels — they are `levelRestrict`, whose sections over a level
object are the sections of `F` over its image in the site of the limit (`levelRestrict_obj`, an
`rfl`), and that image is the base change of the level object along `p_i`.

This is the geometric instantiation of
`CategoryTheory.Sites.InverseSystem.InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.descent_along_restriction` at
`Λ = limitToSmallEtale`: the five site inputs of [Stacks, Tag 09YP] for the raised site are
`toLimitSmall_transition`, `toLimitSmall_obj_descends`, `toLimitSmall_hom_descends`,
`toLimitSmall_hom_eventually_eq` and `mem_limitSitePrecoverage_iff`, and the two instances making
restriction along the composite crossing fully faithful are `full_limitRestriction` and
`faithful_limitRestriction`.

**Why the conclusion is the named predicate.** Written out, the telescope mentions
`(sys D c B hD hX hc).I`, `.C i` and `.u a` some thirty times and exceeds the heartbeat budget in
the signature; the failure is a `(deterministic) timeout at isDefEq`
inside the compatibility hypothesis of the family `g`, before any proof runs. The docstring of
`CategoryTheory.Sites.InverseSystem.InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.RestrictionIsColimit` records the
rule and the three other places in this development where it was needed.

**Why `hK` is supplied by `rw` and not as a term.** `mem_limitSitePrecoverage_iff` states exactly
the required equivalence, but its last clause is a transport `R = h ▸ S.map (toLimitSmall …)`
whose motive was elaborated against the concrete functor, while the motive the machinery's
hypothesis carries is the one elaborated against its variable `u`. The two are definitionally
equal and deciding them is another heartbeat timeout; rewriting the goal with the equivalence
closes it outright instead.

Part (1) of the tag, that the `p_{i,*}F` carry canonical maps making them a system of sheaves in
the sense of [Stacks, Tag 0EZL], is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.directImageSystem`, which states it on
Mathlib's small étale site; that declaration and this one are the covering set of Tag 0EYN.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictionIsColimit_limitToSmallEtale
    (F : Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.topology B c.pt hX) (Type (max u v + 1))) :
    InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.RestrictionIsColimit
      (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.topology B c.pt hX) (sys D c B hD hX hc)
      (fun i => toLimitSmall D c B hD hX hc i ⋙ limitToSmallEtale D c B hX)
      (InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.compTransitionIso (limitToSmallEtale D c B hX)
        (sys D c B hD hX hc) (toLimitSmall D c B hD hX hc)
        (toLimitSmall_transition D c B hD hX hc)) F
declarations.comment: part (2): `F = colim_i p_i^{-1}p_{i,*}F`, on the site of Stacks 021B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_smallEtaleBaseChangeNatTrans_of_isIntegralHom_univ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYP.** Consider a cartesian square
```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```
of schemes of a big étale site with `f` integral, and a sheaf of sets `F` on the small étale site
of `X`, with values in `Type (max (u + 1) v)` for any universe `v`. Then the canonical
comparison `g⁻¹ f_* F ⟶ f'_* (g')⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism.

The comparison is checked on stalks at the geometric points `y'` of `Y'`. Both stalks embed into
the product of the stalks of `F` over the lifts of `y'`, because for an integral morphism the
stalk of a direct image is detected at the lifts
(`AlgebraicGeometry.finitePushforwardStalkComponent_injective_univ`); this gives injectivity. For
surjectivity, an affine open neighbourhood `V` of the image of `y'` in `Y` is chosen, the integral
morphism `X ×_Y V ⟶ V` is written as a limit of finite morphisms (Stacks 09YZ), the family of
germs attached to an element of the target is shown to be given by stage sections on cylinders
of lifts (`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_stage_forall_cylinderGerm_eq_univ`), finitely many cylinders
cover the lifts (`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finset_forall_exists_comp_eq_of_isLimit`), and the
finite case of the stalk computation, Stacks 03QP, at a common stage produces the required germ of
`f_* F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleBaseChangeNatTrans_of_isIntegralHom_univ
    (sq : IsPullback (B.inclusion.map g') (B.inclusion.map f') (B.inclusion.map f)
      (B.inclusion.map g))
    [IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map f)] (h : g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) (Type (max (u + 1) v))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleBaseChangeNatTransUniv B g' f' f g h).app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesLimitsOfShape_smallEtaleInverseImage_of_geometricallyReduced
declarations.doc:
For a morphism of schemes which is flat, locally of finite presentation and has
geometrically reduced fibres, the inverse image functor on sheaves of sets of the small étale
sites commutes with products.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesLimitsOfShape_smallEtaleInverseImage_of_geometricallyReduced
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [GeometricallyReduced f]
    (I : Type w) :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) (smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, max v w} f)
declarations.comment:
no residual hypothesis. Both inputs of the source's proof are supplied: the
covering of the small étale site by objects with a flat quasi-compact factorization with
geometrically connected fibres, which is Tag 0EY5 and is
`hasEnoughObjects_hasFlatConnectedFactorization`; and the bijectivity of the canonical
comparison `G(V) ⟶ (f⁻¹G)(U)` over such an object, which is Tag 0A3H in the localized form of
the source's own argument and is `smallEtaleSectionsComparisonIsIso`, proved from Tag 0EZK and
the small-étale instance of Tag 03EF. The globalization from sections to sheaves is Tag 0H6Y.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_flat_geometricallyReduced
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian square of schemes whose left vertical morphism `f : X ⟶ S` is flat, locally
of finite presentation and has geometrically reduced fibres, the canonical base change map
`f⁻¹ g_* F ⟶ h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism for every sheaf of sets `F` on the small étale site of
`T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_flat_geometricallyReduced (f : X ⟶ S) (h : Y ⟶ X)
    (e : Y ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ S) (sq : IsPullback h e f g)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [GeometricallyReduced f]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) (Type (max (u + 1) v))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, v} e h g f sq.w.symm).app F)
declarations.comment:
no residual hypothesis. The source merges Tag 0EZX with Tag 0EY5, and both are
supplied: the chain of identifications of the sections of `f⁻¹ g_* F` and of `h_* e⁻¹ F` over an
object carrying a flat quasi-compact factorization with geometrically connected fibres is
`local_baseChange_compatible`, exactly as for Tag 0EZX above, and the covering of the small
étale site of `X` by objects with such a factorization is Tag 0EY5 and is
`hasEnoughObjects_hasFlatConnectedFactorization`. The globalization from sections to sheaves is
Tag 0H6Y.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleBaseChangeAb_of_flat_geometricallyReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYS, for abelian sheaves.** In a cartesian square of schemes whose
left vertical morphism `f : X ⟶ S` is flat, locally of finite presentation and has
geometrically reduced fibres, the base change map `f⁻¹ g_* 𝓕 ⟶ h_* e⁻¹ 𝓕` is an isomorphism for
every abelian sheaf `𝓕` on the small étale site of `T`. The map is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleBaseChangeAb`, the underived base change map of
[Stacks, Tag 0F02]. It is invertible because the base change map of sheaves of sets is
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_flat_geometricallyReduced`), by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleBaseChangeAb_of_isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_smallEtaleBaseChangeAb_of_flat_geometricallyReduced (f : X ⟶ S)
    (h : Y ⟶ X) (e : Y ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ S) (sq : IsPullback h e f g)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [GeometricallyReduced f] :
    IsIso (smallEtaleBaseChangeAb f g h e sq.w)
declarations.comment: for abelian sheaves, at the comparison `smallEtaleBaseChangeAb` of [Stacks, Tag 0F02]; no residual hypothesis. The statement for sheaves of sets is `isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_flat_geometricallyReduced`, and the abelian map is invertible as soon as the set-valued one is, by `isIso_smallEtaleBaseChangeAb_of_isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange`.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_galoisCover_killing_class
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYT.** Let `K/k` be a field extension, `X` a smooth affine curve over
`k` with a rational point `x`, `F` an abelian sheaf on `Spec(K)_étale` annihilated by an integer
`n` invertible in `k`, `q > 0` and `ξ ∈ H^q(X_K, F)`. There are finite extensions `K'/K` and
`k'/k` with `k' ⊆ K'` and a finite étale Galois cover `Z ⟶ X_{k'}`, whose group has order
dividing a power of `n` and which is split over `x_{k'}`, such that `ξ` dies in
`H^q(Z_{K'}, F)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_galoisCover_killing_class [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine X]
    (x : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) (hx : x ≫ f = 𝟙 _)
    (F : Sheaf (Spec (.of K)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) (hF : n • 𝟙 F = 0) {q : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q)
    (ξ : Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1}
      ((etaleAbelianInverseImage.{u, u + 1} (pullback.fst (spectrumMap k K) f)).obj F) q) :
    ∃ (k' K' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Field K') (_ : Algebra k k') (_ : Algebra K K')
      (_ : Algebra k' K') (_ : Algebra k K') (_ : IsScalarTower k k' K')
      (_ : IsScalarTower k K K') (_ : FiniteDimensional k k') (_ : FiniteDimensional K K')
      (Z : Scheme.{u}) (p : Z ⟶ pullback (spectrumMap k k') f),
      IsGaloisCover p ∧ (∃ m : ℕ, Nat.card (Aut (Over.mk p)) ∣ n ^ m) ∧
        IsSplitOver p (basePoint f k' x hx) ∧ coverBaseChangeClass f K k' K' p F q ξ = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.SmoothBaseChange.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**The smooth base change theorem** ([Stacks, Theorem 0EYU]). In a cartesian square
```
X  ←-h-  Y
|f       |e
S  ←-g-  T
```
with `f` smooth and `g` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the base change map
`f⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism for every `q` and every abelian sheaf `F` on
`T_étale` all of whose stalks at geometric points are torsion of orders invertible on `S`: every
element of every such stalk is killed by a positive integer `n` which is a unit on `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_smooth
    {X Y S T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (h : Y ⟶ X) (e : Y ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ S)
    (sq : IsPullback h e f g) [Smooth f] [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1})
    (hF : ∀ (t : GeometricPoint T) (a : (smallEtaleStalkAb t.hom).obj F),
      ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ IsUnit ((n : ℤ) : Γ(S, ⊤)) ∧ n • a = 0) (q : ℕ) :
    IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f g h e sq.w q).app F)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.overMapPullbackSquare
declarations.doc:
The square of topoi attached to a commutative square

```
  U' --a--> U
  |b        |c
  V' --d--> V
```

of `C` by the relocalization morphisms commutes, in the form of the commutation isomorphism
`j_{V'/V}^{-1} ⋙ j_{U'/V'}^{-1} ≅ j_{U/V}^{-1} ⋙ j_{U'/U}^{-1}` between the two composite inverse
images.
declarations.comment:
The relocalization morphisms of a commutative square form a commutative
  square of topoi: the two composites `j_{V'/V}^{-1} ⋙ j_{U'/V'}^{-1}` and
  `j_{U/V}^{-1} ⋙ j_{U'/U}^{-1}` of inverse images are canonically isomorphic.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.isIso_overMapPushforwardBaseChange
declarations.doc:
If the square

```
  U' --a--> U
  |b        |c
  V' --d--> V
```

of `C` is cartesian, then the relocalization morphisms satisfy base change,
`j_{V'/V}^{-1} ∘ j_{U/V, *} = j_{U'/V', *} ∘ j_{U'/U}^{-1}`: the base change transformation
`overMapPushforwardBaseChange` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_overMapPushforwardBaseChange (hsq : IsPullback a b c d)
    [∀ (F : (Over U)ᵒᵖ ⥤ A), (Over.map c).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F]
    [∀ (F : (Over U')ᵒᵖ ⥤ A), (Over.map b).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F] :
    IsIso (J.overMapPushforwardBaseChange A hsq.toCommSq).natTrans
declarations.comment:
For a cartesian square, the base change transformation
  `j_{V'/V}^{-1} ∘ j_{U/V,*} ⟶ j_{U'/V',*} ∘ j_{U'/U}^{-1}` of the relocalization morphisms is an
  isomorphism.

declarations.name: CplxCplx.Hom.isTotalQuasiIso_of_isInternalQuasiIso
declarations.doc:
A morphism between complexes of cochain complexes
which is a quasi-isomorphism on every internal complex induces a quasi-isomorphism between
their product total complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTotalQuasiIso_of_isInternalQuasiIso {c c' : CplxCplx} (g : CplxCplx.Hom c c')
    (hg : g.IsInternalQuasiIso) : g.IsTotalQuasiIso

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Localization.jShriekUnitIsoFreeAbelianSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYY**, part (a), in the ambient category of sheaves of
`ULift ℤ`-modules. The extension by zero of the tensor unit along the localization morphism
`j : Sh(C)/F ⟶ Sh(C)` is the free abelian sheaf `Z_F^#` on `F`, read through the equivalence
between sheaves of `ULift ℤ`-modules and sheaves of abelian groups.

This transports the `AddCommGrpCat`-valued statement
`localizationShriek_constantInteger_iso_freeAbSheaf` across the bridge, using that the bridge
commutes with extension by zero and carries the tensor unit to the constant sheaf on
`ULift ℤ`.
declarations.comment: j_! ℤ = Z_F^#, in the ambient category carrying the tensor product

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Localization.jShriekPullbackIsoShriekUnitTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYY**, part (b), with no hypothesis beyond the data of the source.
For the localization morphism `j : Sh(C)/F ⟶ Sh(C)` and an abelian sheaf `H` on `C`,

`j_!(j⁻¹ H) ≅ j_! ℤ ⊗_ℤ H`.

This is `jShriekPullbackIsoTensor`, which is proved for a site of arbitrary size and therefore
states sheafification of `ModuleCat`-valued presheaves on `C` and on `C/F`, the monoidality of
the two sheafification localizers and the left Kan extensions along `C/F ⥤ C` as hypotheses.
On a site all five are available: the monoidality of the two localizers from
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.W.monoidal`, the left Kan extensions from Mathlib's
pointwise construction `CategoryTheory.Functor.pointwiseLeftKanExtension`, and the two
sheafifications through `preservesColimitsOfShape_cover_op_forget_moduleCat` above. So part (b)
carries no hypothesis the source does not make.
declarations.statement:
def jShriekPullbackIsoShriekUnitTensor
    (H : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} (ULift.{u} ℤ))) :
    let := Sheaf.monoidalCategory J (ModuleCat.{u} (ULift.{u} ℤ))
    let := Sheaf.monoidalCategory (localizationTopology J F)
      (ModuleCat.{u} (ULift.{u} ℤ))
    (abelianLocalizationShriek J F).obj
        ((abelianLocalizationInverseImage J F).obj H) ≅
      (abelianLocalizationShriek J F).obj (𝟙_ _) ⊗ H
declarations.comment: j_!(j⁻¹ H) = j_! ℤ ⊗ H, with no hypothesis beyond the data of the source

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Localization.jShriekPullbackIsoFreeAbelianSheafTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EYY**, the conclusion. For the localization morphism
`j : Sh(C)/F ⟶ Sh(C)` and an abelian sheaf `H` on `C`,

`j_!(j⁻¹ H) ≅ Z_F^# ⊗_ℤ H`,

the free abelian sheaf on `F` tensored with `H`. This combines part (b),
`jShriekPullbackIsoTensor`, with the identification of `j_! ℤ` with `Z_F^#` of part (a).
declarations.statement:
def jShriekPullbackIsoFreeAbelianSheafTensor
    (H : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} (ULift.{u} ℤ))) :
    let := Sheaf.monoidalCategory J (ModuleCat.{u} (ULift.{u} ℤ))
    (abelianLocalizationShriek J F).obj
        ((abelianLocalizationInverseImage J F).obj H) ≅
      (sheafIntegerModuleEquivalence J).inverse.obj
        ((Presheaf.freeAbelianSheaf J).obj ((sheafToPresheaf J (Type u)).obj F)) ⊗ H
declarations.comment: j_!(j⁻¹ H) = Z_F^# ⊗ H, the two parts joined

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.Localization.localizationShriek_constantInteger_iso_freeAbSheaf
declarations.doc:
For the localization morphism `j : Sh(C)/F ⟶ Sh(C)`, presented by the site of elements
`C/F`, the abelian sheaf `j_! ℤ` is the free abelian sheaf `Z_F^#` on `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizationShriek_constantInteger_iso_freeAbSheaf (F : Sheaf J (Type u)) :
    (Stacks.Sites.abelianShriek (localizationProjection J F)
          (localizationTopology J F) J).obj
        ((constantSheaf (localizationTopology J F) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
          (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) ≅
      (Presheaf.freeAbelianSheaf J).obj ((sheafToPresheaf J (Type u)).obj F)
declarations.comment: j_shriek_int

registrations.name: jShriekPullbackIsoTensor
registrations.comment: j_!(j⁻¹ H) = j_! ℤ ⊗ H, for a site of arbitrary size: sheafification, the monoidality of the two sheafification localizers and the left Kan extensions along C/F ⥤ C are instance hypotheses here, and every one of them holds at the hypotheses of the source -- see jShriekPullbackIsoShriekUnitTensor

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.derivedOverPushforwardBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZ0.** For a Cartesian square
```
  X' --a--> X
  |b         |c
  Y' --d--> Y
```
in a site, inverse image along `d` after derived direct image along `c` is naturally isomorphic
to derived direct image along `b` after inverse image along `a`.

All four derived functors are arbitrary choices with their canonical transformations from the
corresponding functors on homotopy categories.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedOverPushforwardBaseChangeIso
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {X' X Y' Y : C}
    (a : X' ⟶ X) (b : X' ⟶ Y') (c : X ⟶ Y) (d : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (h : IsPullback a b c d)
    [∀ U : C, HasSheafify (J.over U) Ab.{max u v}]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (AbelianSheaves J X)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (AbelianSheaves J Y)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wU} (AbelianSheaves J X')]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wV'} (AbelianSheaves J Y')]
    (Rc : DerivedCategory (AbelianSheaves J X) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (AbelianSheaves J Y))
    (Rb : DerivedCategory (AbelianSheaves J X') ⥤
      DerivedCategory (AbelianSheaves J Y'))
    (Ra : DerivedCategory (AbelianSheaves J X) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (AbelianSheaves J X'))
    (Rd : DerivedCategory (AbelianSheaves J Y) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (AbelianSheaves J Y'))
    (αc : homotopyToDerived (overPushforward J c) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rc)
    (αb : homotopyToDerived (overPushforward J b) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rb)
    (αa : homotopyToDerived (overPullback J a) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Ra)
    (αd : homotopyToDerived (overPullback J d) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rd)
    [Rc.IsRightDerivedFunctor αc
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (AbelianSheaves J X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Rb.IsRightDerivedFunctor αb
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (AbelianSheaves J X') (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Ra.IsRightDerivedFunctor αa
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (AbelianSheaves J X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [Rd.IsRightDerivedFunctor αd
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (AbelianSheaves J Y) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    Rc ⋙ Rd ≅ Ra ⋙ Rb

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.comparisonPullbackOverMapPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZ2.** For two comparable topologies, change of topology commutes with
restriction along a morphism, up to the canonical natural isomorphism of inverse-image
functors.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def comparisonPullbackOverMapPullbackIso
    {J K : GrothendieckTopology C} (h : K ≤ J) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    comparisonPullback (over_le_over h Y) ⋙ J.overMapPullback (Type (max u v)) f ≅
      K.overMapPullback (Type (max u v)) f ⋙ comparisonPullback (over_le_over h X)
declarations.comment: commutativity of the square of topoi
