declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.overMapPullback_comp_comparisonPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZ2.** On direct images for the comparison morphisms and inverse images for
restriction, the square commutes strictly:
`ε_{X,*} ∘ f_J^{-1} = f_K^{-1} ∘ ε_{Y,*}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem overMapPullback_comp_comparisonPushforward
    {J K : GrothendieckTopology C} (h : K ≤ J) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    J.overMapPullback (Type (max u v)) f ⋙ comparisonPushforward (over_le_over h X) =
      comparisonPushforward (over_le_over h Y) ⋙ K.overMapPullback (Type (max u v)) f
declarations.comment: the identity `ε_{X,*} f_J^{-1} = f_K^{-1} ε_{Y,*}`

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZ3.** The standing situation for comparing cohomology computed in a finer
coverage with cohomology computed in a coarser one.
declarations.statement: structure CohomologyComparison (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C]

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison.fineWeakSerre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZ9.** The class `𝒜_X` of abelian sheaves on the finer localized site: those of
the form `ε⁻¹ F` for `F` in the given weak Serre class `𝒜'_X` on the coarser localized site,
with `ε` the change-of-topology morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev fineWeakSerre (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C) :
    ObjectProperty (Sheaf (S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X) Ab.{max u v})
declarations.comment: the category `𝒜_X`

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison.fineWeakSerre_iff_weakSerre_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZ9.** A sheaf on the finer localized site belongs to `𝒜_X` if and only if its
change-of-topology direct image belongs to `𝒜'_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fineWeakSerre_iff_weakSerre_pushforward
    (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C)
    (F : Sheaf (S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X) Ab.{max u v}) :
    S.fineWeakSerre X F ↔
      S.weakSerre X
        ((abelianComparisonPushforward S.fineCoverage S.coarseCoverage
          S.coarse_le_fine X).obj F)
declarations.comment: the membership criterion for `𝒜_X`

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison.fineWeakSerre_overMapPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZ9.** Restriction along a morphism of the site preserves the class `𝒜` of
abelian sheaves on the finer localized sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem fineWeakSerre_overMapPullback (S : CohomologyComparison C)
    {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Sheaf (S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck.over Y) Ab.{max u v})
    (hF : S.fineWeakSerre Y F) :
    S.fineWeakSerre X
      ((S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck.overMapPullback Ab.{max u v} f).obj F)
declarations.comment: stability of `𝒜_X` under restriction

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.higherDirectImageComparison
declarations.doc:
**The comparison transformation.** The canonical degree-`i` map from the coarse
higher direct image of the change-of-topology direct image to the change-of-topology direct
image of the fine higher direct image,

`R^i f_{τ',*} ε_{X,*} ℱ ⟶ ε_{Y,*} R^i f_{τ,*} ℱ`,

natural in the abelian sheaf `ℱ` on the finer localized site over `X`.

It is the composite of the two edge morphisms of the Grothendieck spectral sequence of the
square of topoi `abelianComparisonPushforward_square`: the edge `E₂^{i,0} ⟶ H^i` for the pair
`(ε_{X,*}, f_{τ',*})`, followed by the edge `H^i ⟶ E₂^{0,i}` for the pair `(f_{τ,*}, ε_{Y,*})`.
declarations.statement:
def higherDirectImageComparison (S : CohomologyComparison C) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (i : ℕ) :
    abelianComparisonPushforward S.fineCoverage S.coarseCoverage S.coarse_le_fine X ⋙
        (overPushforward S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck f).rightDerived i ⟶
      (overPushforward S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck f).rightDerived i ⋙
        abelianComparisonPushforward S.fineCoverage S.coarseCoverage S.coarse_le_fine Y
declarations.comment: canonical comparison transformation

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.isIso_higherDirectImageComparison_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZA.** Assume the vanishing condition `(V_n)`. For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of the
distinguished class, an abelian sheaf `ℱ` of `𝒜_X` on the finer localized site over `X`, and a
degree `i ≤ n`, the comparison

`R^i f_{τ',*} ε_{X,*} ℱ ⟶ ε_{Y,*} R^i f_{τ,*} ℱ`

is an isomorphism.

Both factors of the comparison are invertible, for different reasons. The first edge morphism is
invertible in degree `i` as soon as `R^q ε_{X,*} ℱ` vanishes for `1 ≤ q ≤ i`, which is `(V_n)`;
this is `Stacks.Cohomology.RightDerivedEdgeIso.isIso_edge_app`, and no spectral sequence is
needed for it. The second edge morphism is invertible as soon as the object it starts from lies
in the essential image of the change-of-topology direct image, by
`Stacks.Cohomology.RightDerivedCoEdge.isIso_secondEdge_app_of_isIso_unit`; and that object is
`R^i f_{τ',*} ε_{X,*} ℱ` — by the first edge morphism, which has just been seen to be
invertible — which lies in the weak Serre class `𝒜'_Y` because `ε_{X,*} ℱ` lies in `𝒜'_X` and the
distinguished class is stable under higher direct images.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_higherDirectImageComparison_app (S : CohomologyComparison C) (n : ℕ)
    (hV : S.vanishingCondition n) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : S.morphismProperty f)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ n) (F : Sheaf (S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X) Ab.{max u v})
    (hF : S.fineWeakSerre X F) :
    IsIso ((higherDirectImageComparison S f i).app F)
declarations.comment: the comparison is an isomorphism through degree `n`

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.isIso_homology_derivedCohomologyComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZB.** In the comparison situation of Stacks 0EZ3, assume the vanishing condition
`(V_n)`. Let `X` be an object of `C` and let `L` be an object of `D(C_{τ'}/X)` whose cohomology
sheaves vanish in negative degrees and lie in the weak Serre class `𝒜'_X` in the degrees
`0 ≤ i ≤ n`. Then the canonical map

`H^n_{τ'}(X, L) ⟶ H^n_τ(X, ε_X^{-1}L)`

of `Stacks.ComparingTopologies.derivedCohomologyComparison` is an isomorphism.

The truncation `τ_{≤n}L` has all of its cohomology in `𝒜'_X` and none outside the degrees
`0, …, n`, so the comparison is invertible in degree `n` there; and the truncation morphism
`τ_{≤n}L ⟶ L` becomes invertible on `H^n` after applying either `RΓ_{τ'}(X, -)` or `ε_X^{-1}`
followed by `RΓ_τ(X, -)`. The naturality square of the comparison then carries the conclusion
from `τ_{≤n}L` to `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homology_derivedCohomologyComparison (S : CohomologyComparison C) (n : ℕ)
    (hV : S.vanishingCondition n) (X : C)
    (L : DerivedCategory (AbelianSheaves S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X))
    (hneg : ∀ i : ℤ, i < 0 → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (AbelianSheaves S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X) i).obj L))
    (hmem : ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ n → S.weakSerre X ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (AbelianSheaves S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X) (i : ℤ)).obj L)) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor Ab.{max u v} (n : ℤ)).map
      ((derivedCohomologyComparison S X).app
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.ofNonnegative L hneg)))

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.cohomologyComparison
declarations.doc:
The natural change-of-topology map `H^i_{τ'}(X, ε_{X,*} F) ⟶ H^i_τ(X, F)`, given by
pulling back cohomology classes along `ε_X`.
declarations.statement:
def cohomologyComparison (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C) (i : ℕ) :
    abelianComparisonPushforward S.fineCoverage S.coarseCoverage S.coarse_le_fine X ⋙
        (globalSectionsOver S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X).rightDerived i ⟶
      (globalSectionsOver S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck X).rightDerived i
declarations.comment: canonical cohomology map

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.cohomologyComparison_eq_injectiveResolution
declarations.doc:
An augmentation-preserving comparison from an injective resolution of the coarse direct
image to the direct image of an injective resolution computes the canonical cohomology map.
This characterizes its components in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologyComparison_eq_injectiveResolution (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C) (i : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X) Ab.{max u v})
    (I : InjectiveResolution F)
    (J : InjectiveResolution ((abelianComparisonPushforward S.fineCoverage
      S.coarseCoverage S.coarse_le_fine X).obj F))
    (φ : J.cocomplex ⟶
      ((abelianComparisonPushforward S.fineCoverage S.coarseCoverage
        S.coarse_le_fine X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex)
    (hφ : J.ι.f 0 ≫ φ.f 0 =
      (abelianComparisonPushforward S.fineCoverage S.coarseCoverage
        S.coarse_le_fine X).map (I.ι.f 0)) :
    (cohomologyComparison S X i).app F =
      (J.isoRightDerivedObj (globalSectionsOver S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X) i).hom ≫
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
          (((globalSectionsOver S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.up ℕ)).map φ) i ≫
          (I.isoRightDerivedObj (globalSectionsOver S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck X) i).inv
declarations.comment: canonical map via injective resolutions

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.mono_cohomologyComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZC.** Under `(Vₙ)`, the change-of-topology map on cohomology in degree `n + 1`
is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_cohomologyComparison (S : CohomologyComparison C) (n : ℕ)
    (hV : S.vanishingCondition n) (X : C)
    (F : Sheaf (S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X) Ab.{max u v})
    (hF : S.fineWeakSerre X F) :
    Mono ((cohomologyComparison S X (n + 1)).app F)
declarations.comment: injectivity

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.mem_range_cohomologyComparison_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZC.** Under `(Vₙ)`, a class in degree `n + 1` is in the image of the
change-of-topology map on cohomology precisely when it becomes zero on the members of a
covering for the coarser topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_range_cohomologyComparison_iff (S : CohomologyComparison C) (n : ℕ)
    (hV : S.vanishingCondition n) (X : C)
    (F : Sheaf (S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X) Ab.{max u v})
    (hF : S.fineWeakSerre X F)
    (ξ : sheafCohomology (S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X) F (Over.mk (𝟙 X)) (n + 1)) :
    (∃ η : sheafCohomology (S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X)
        ((abelianComparisonPushforward S.fineCoverage S.coarseCoverage
          S.coarse_le_fine X).obj F) (Over.mk (𝟙 X)) (n + 1),
        (cohomologyComparison S X (n + 1)).app F η = ξ) ↔
      (∃ R : Presieve X, R ∈ S.coarseCoverage X ∧
        ∀ ⦃V : C⦄ (f : V ⟶ X), R f →
          sheafCohomologyRestriction (S.fineCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X)
            (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk f) (V := Over.mk (𝟙 X)) f (by simp))
            (n + 1) F ξ = 0)
declarations.comment: image of the map

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.exists_coarseCovering_restrict_eq_zero_of_equalizer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZD.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of the distinguished class which by itself
is a covering for the finer topology, and let `F` be a sheaf of the weak Serre class `𝒜'_Y` on
the coarser site localized at `Y`. If a cohomology class of degree `n + 1` over `X` has equal
restrictions along the two projections from `X ×_Y X`, then there is a covering of `Y` for the
coarser topology such that the class restricts to zero over every base change `Yᵢ ×_Y X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coarseCovering_restrict_eq_zero_of_equalizer (S : CohomologyComparison C)
    {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : S.morphismProperty f)
    (hcover : Presieve.singleton f ∈ S.fineCoverage Y)
    (F : Sheaf (S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck.over Y) Ab.{max u v}) (hF : S.weakSerre Y F) (n : ℕ)
    (P : Over Y) (p₁ p₂ : P ⟶ Over.mk f) (hP : IsPullback p₁.left p₂.left f f)
    (θ : Stacks.sheafCohomology (S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck.over Y) F (Over.mk f) (n + 1))
    (hθ : Stacks.sheafCohomologyRestriction (S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck.over Y) p₁
        (n + 1) F θ =
      Stacks.sheafCohomologyRestriction (S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck.over Y) p₂
        (n + 1) F θ) :
    ∃ R : Presieve Y, R ∈ S.coarseCoverage Y ∧
      ∀ ⦃Z : C⦄ (g : Z ⟶ Y), R g →
        ∃ (Q : Over Y) (a : Q ⟶ Over.mk f) (b : Q ⟶ Over.mk g),
          IsPullback a.left b.left f g ∧
            Stacks.sheafCohomologyRestriction (S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck.over Y) a
              (n + 1) F θ = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison.vanishingCondition_succ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZE.** In the comparison situation of Stacks 0EZ3 the vanishing condition `(V_n)`
implies `(V_{n+1})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem CohomologyComparison.vanishingCondition_succ (S : CohomologyComparison C) (n : ℕ)
    (hV : S.vanishingCondition n) : S.vanishingCondition (n + 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.rightDerivedPushforward_mem_derivedCategoryBPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZF**, the first assertion of part (2). In a cohomology comparison situation,
total right derived direct image along a morphism of the distinguished class `P` carries
`D⁺_{𝒜'_X}` into `D⁺_{𝒜'_Y}`.

No hypothesis beyond those of the tag is used: in particular the vanishing conditions `(V_n)`,
which the tag asserts first, are not needed for this half. See the implementation notes for the
other clauses of the tag and where they live.
declarations.statement:
theorem rightDerivedPushforward_mem_derivedCategoryBPlus
    (S : CohomologyComparison C) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : S.morphismProperty f)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus
      (Sheaf (S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X) Ab.{max u v}))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus (S.weakSerre X) K.obj) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus (S.weakSerre Y)
      ((((Over.map f).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous Ab.{max u v}
          (S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X)
          (S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck.over Y)).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj K).obj)
declarations.comment: part (2), membership: `R f_{τ',*}` carries `D⁺_{𝒜'_X}` into `D⁺_{𝒜'_Y}`

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison.vanishingCondition_all
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZF, the leading assertion.** In the comparison situation of Stacks 0EZ3 the
vanishing condition `(V_n)` holds for every `n`: `(V_0)` is empty and Stacks 0EZE is the
induction step.
declarations.statement:
theorem CohomologyComparison.vanishingCondition_all (S : CohomologyComparison C) (n : ℕ) :
    S.vanishingCondition n
declarations.comment: (V_n) holds for all n

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.isIso_derivedComparisonUnit_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZF (1).** For `X` in `C` and `K'` in `D⁺_{𝒜'_X}(C_{τ'}/X)` the canonical map
`K' ⟶ Rε_{X,*}(ε_X^{-1}K')` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedComparisonUnit_app (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (AbelianSheaves S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, S.weakSerre X ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K)) :
    IsIso ((derivedComparisonUnit S X).app K)

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.isIso_derivedComparisonBaseChange_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZF (2), the base change.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of `C` and `K'` in
`D⁺_{𝒜'_X}(C_{τ'}/X)` the base change map `ε_Y^{-1}(Rf_{τ',*}K') ⟶ Rf_{τ,*}(ε_X^{-1}K')` is an
isomorphism. The source states this for `f` in the distinguished class; it holds for every `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedComparisonBaseChange_app (S : CohomologyComparison C) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (AbelianSheaves S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X))
    (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, S.weakSerre X
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor
        (AbelianSheaves S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X) n).obj K)) :
    IsIso ((derivedComparisonBaseChange S f).app K)
declarations.comment: (2), base change

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison.fineWeakSerre_isWeakSerreClass
declarations.doc:
**First assertion of Stacks 0EZG.** In the comparison situation of Stacks 0EZ3, for any
object `X` of `C` the class `𝒜_X ⊂ Ab(C_τ/X)` of Stacks 0EZ9 is a weak Serre subcategory.
declarations.statement:
theorem fineWeakSerre_isWeakSerreClass (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C) :
    (S.fineWeakSerre X).IsWeakSerreClass
declarations.comment: first assertion: `𝒜_X` is a weak Serre subcategory of `Ab(C_τ/X)`

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.boundedBelowComparisonEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Second assertion of Stacks 0EZG.** In the comparison situation of Stacks 0EZ3, for any
object `X` of `C` the derived change-of-topology direct image

`Rε_{X,*} : D⁺_{𝒜_X}(C_τ/X) ⟶ D⁺_{𝒜'_X}(C_{τ'}/X)`

is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse `ε_X^{-1}`.
declarations.comment: second assertion: `Rε_{X,*} : D⁺_{𝒜_X}(C_τ/X) ⟶ D⁺_{𝒜'_X}(C_{τ'}/X)` is an equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.boundedBelowComparisonEquivalence_functor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZG**, the identification of the functor of the equivalence with the restriction
of the derived change-of-topology direct image `Rε_{X,*}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem boundedBelowComparisonEquivalence_functor (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C) :
    (boundedBelowComparisonEquivalence S X).functor =
      derivedComparisonPushforwardLift S X
declarations.comment: the second assertion: the functor of the equivalence is `Rε_{X,*}`

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.boundedBelowComparisonEquivalence_inverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZG**, the identification of the quasi-inverse of the equivalence with the
restriction of the change-of-topology inverse image `ε_X^{-1}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem boundedBelowComparisonEquivalence_inverse (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C) :
    (boundedBelowComparisonEquivalence S X).inverse =
      derivedComparisonPullbackLift S X
declarations.comment: the second assertion: the quasi-inverse of the equivalence is `ε_X^{-1}`

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.isIso_cohomologyChangeOfTopology_app
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of Stacks 0EZH.** In the comparison situation of Stacks 0EZ3, let `X` be an
object of `C` and let `ℱ'` be a sheaf of the weak Serre class `𝒜'_X` on the coarser localized
site. Then for every `n` the canonical map

`H^n_{τ'}(X, ℱ') ⟶ H^n_τ(X, ε_X^{-1}ℱ')`

is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_cohomologyChangeOfTopology_app (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C)
    (F : Sheaf (S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck.over X) Ab.{max u v})
    (hF : S.weakSerre X F) (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso ((cohomologyChangeOfTopology S X n).app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.isIso_derivedCohomologyComparison_app_of_weakSerre
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of Stacks 0EZH, as an isomorphism in `D⁺(Ab)`.** In the comparison situation of
Stacks 0EZ3, let `X` be an object of `C` and let `K'` be a bounded below object of the derived
category of abelian sheaves on `C_{τ'}/X` all of whose cohomology sheaves lie in `𝒜'_X`, that
is, an object of `D⁺_{𝒜'_X}(C_{τ'}/X)`. Then the canonical map

`RΓ_{τ'}(X, K') ⟶ RΓ_τ(X, ε_X^{-1}K')`

is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCohomologyComparison_app_of_weakSerre (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (AbelianSheaves S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, S.weakSerre X ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K)) :
    IsIso ((derivedCohomologyComparison S X).app K)
declarations.comment: (2), as an isomorphism of derived global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.ComparingTopologies.isIso_homology_derivedCohomologyComparison_app_of_weakSerre
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of Stacks 0EZH.** With `X` and `K'` as above, the canonical map

`H^n_{τ'}(X, K') ⟶ H^n_τ(X, ε_X^{-1}K')`

is an isomorphism for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homology_derivedCohomologyComparison_app_of_weakSerre
    (S : CohomologyComparison C) (X : C)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (AbelianSheaves S.coarseCoverage.toGrothendieck X))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, S.weakSerre X ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K))
    (n : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor Ab.{max u v} n).map
      ((derivedCohomologyComparison S X).app K))

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.exists_isPullback_properMorphisms
declarations.doc:
A proper arrow of the site admits a base change along an arbitrary arrow, and that base change
is again proper.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPullback_properMorphisms
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound)
    ⦃X Y Y' : S.category⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : S.properMorphisms f) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) :
    ∃ (Z : S.category) (q : Z ⟶ X) (p : Z ⟶ Y'),
      IsPullback q p f g ∧ S.properMorphisms p
declarations.comment: condition (0EZ4) of Situation 0EZ3 for the proper maps of LC

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiPullbackClass_overMapPullback
declarations.doc:
Restriction along an arrow `f : X ⟶ Y` of the site carries the sheaves pulled back from `Y`
to the sheaves pulled back from `X`: a restriction of `π_Y^{-1}G` is `π_X^{-1}` of the inverse
image of `G` along the underlying map of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zariskiPullbackClass_overMapPullback
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound)
    ⦃X Y : S.category⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over Y) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    (hF : S.zariskiPullbackClass.{u, w, v} Y F) :
    S.zariskiPullbackClass.{u, w, v} X
      ((S.zariskiTopology.overMapPullback AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} f).obj F)
declarations.comment: condition (0EZ5) of Situation 0EZ3 for the sheaves pulled back from the space

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiPullbackClass_rightDerived_overMapPushforward
declarations.doc:
Every higher direct image along a proper arrow `f : X ⟶ Y` of a sheaf pulled back from the
space `X` is again pulled back from the space `Y`: if `F` lies in `zariskiPullbackClass X` then
`R^i f_{Zar,*}F` lies in `zariskiPullbackClass Y`, for every `i : ℕ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zariskiPullbackClass_rightDerived_overMapPushforward (hf : S.properMorphisms f)
    (F : Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    (hF : S.zariskiPullbackClass.{u, w, v} X F) (i : ℕ) :
    S.zariskiPullbackClass.{u, w, v} Y
      ((((Over.map f).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}
        (S.zariskiTopology.over X) (S.zariskiTopology.over Y)).rightDerived i).obj F)
declarations.comment: condition (4) of Situation 0EZ3 for this situation: all higher direct images along a proper arrow of a sheaf pulled back from the space are again pulled back from the space. This is the field `ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison.weakSerre_rightDerived_relocalizationPushforward`, proved outright for every i, with the witness `R^i g_* G` specified rather than obtained from the existential. The five conditions of Situation 0EZ3 are items (1)-(5) of that tag; the `(0EZ4)`/`(0EZ5)`/`(0EZ6)`/`(0EZ7)` names used elsewhere in this directory are this development's own, and this is `(0EZ7)`. ALL FIVE CONDITIONS ARE NOW PROVED: the other four are `morphismProperty_baseChange` and `weakSerre_relocalizationInverseImage` (ZariskiComparisonSituationData.lean), `weakSerre_isSheaf_fine` (`isSheaf_qc_zariskiPullbackClass`, ZariskiPullbackClassQcSheaf.lean) and `covering_refinement` (`exists_zariskiRefinement_properMorphisms`, ZariskiQcCoveringRefinement.lean). SITUATION 0EZ3 IS STILL NOT INSTANTIATED HERE, AND THIS CONDITION IS WHAT BLOCKS IT. The carrier is settled: `CohomologyComparison` is declared for `[SmallCategory C]` with coefficients `Ab` in the carrier's own universe, `S.category` is `Type (u+1)` with morphisms in `Type u`, and the carrier is `CategoryTheory.SmallModel S.category` in `Type u`, `EssentiallySmall.{u} S.category` being the instance `LocallyQuasiCompactQcSite.category_essentiallySmall`. That fixes the coefficients at `AddCommGrpCat.{u}`, where the sheaf condition is proved and where the restriction condition `zariskiPullbackClass_overMapPullback` now also holds, being stated for every `AddCommGrpCat.{max u t}`. THIS condition is stated only at `AddCommGrpCat.{max (u+1) v}`. ONE of the seven inputs of its proof now reaches `AddCommGrpCat.{u}`, being stated for every `AddCommGrpCat.{max u t}`: `abelianComparisonInverseImage_exact` (ZariskiSite.lean). That was the input believed OBSTRUCTED rather than merely unrestated, because it went through `Small.{max (u+1) v} ((S.zariskiTopology.over X).Cover Y)ᵒᵖ` and the slice's covering sieves do live in `Type (u+1)`; it turns out not to need them, and now takes the `essentiallySmall_over` route, its Kan-extension shapes being `u`-small by `small_costructuredArrow_opensToSlice`. The other six still carry `max (u+1) v` -- `topologicalPushforward` and `zariskiBaseChange` (ProperDerivedImage.lean), `isIso_zariskiBaseChange_of_properMap` (AbelianProperDirectImage.lean), `preservesFiniteLimits_zariskiSlicePushforward` (AcyclicityReduction.lean), and `isZero_rightDerived_sliceDirectImage_abelianComparisonInverseImage` with `rightDerivedZariskiBaseChangeIso` here. THE NEXT ONE NEEDS A LEMMA THAT DOES NOT EXIST: restating `preservesFiniteLimits_zariskiSlicePushforward` at `max u t` fails even with both sheafifications built from `essentiallySmall_over`, because `(Over.pullback f).sheafPushforwardContinuous` is a right adjoint only when the left Kan extension along `(Over.pullback f).op` exists, which needs `Small.{max u t} (CostructuredArrow (Over.pullback f).op Z)`. Those comma categories are indexed by `Over Y`, in `Type (u+1)`; at `max (u+1) v` their smallness is free from `Small.{max (u+1) v} α` for every `α : Type (max (u+1) v)` (Sheafification.lean), the one step that really uses `u+1 ≤ max (u+1) v`, and at `max u t` there is no such instance. What is owed is the analogue of `small_costructuredArrow_opensToSlice` for `Over.pullback f`. Past it the rest is RESTATEMENT, made large only because these facts are supplied as INSTANCES and an instance generalized to `max u t` is unusable -- `max u ?t =?= max (u+1) v` is not solvable by instance synthesis -- so each remaining input must take them as local `have`s, across the 32 files here that mention `max (u+1) v`. Transporting the conditions along `equivSmallModel` is also not done

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.exists_zariski_properMorphisms_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZI**, the refinement condition. Every quasi-compact covering of an object `U` of the
site is refined in three stages: by a Zariski covering `{V ⟶ U}`, then over each `V` by a single
proper arrow `f : W ⟶ V` which is itself a quasi-compact covering, and finally by a Zariski
covering of `W` whose composites factor through the given covering. This is condition (0EZ8) of
Situation 0EZ3 with the proper arrows as the class `P`, the quasi-compact topology as `τ` and the
Zariski topology as `τ'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_zariski_properMorphisms_refinement
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound)
    (U : S.category) (R : Presieve U) (hR : R ∈ S.qcSite.pretopology U) :
    ∃ T : Presieve U, T ∈ S.zariskiPrecoverage U ∧
      ∀ ⦃V : S.category⦄ (v : V ⟶ U), T v →
        ∃ (W : S.category) (f : W ⟶ V), S.properMorphisms f ∧
          Presieve.singleton f ∈ S.qcSite.pretopology V ∧
            ∃ P : Presieve W, P ∈ S.zariskiPrecoverage W ∧
              P.FactorsThruAlong R (f ≫ v)
declarations.comment:
condition (0EZ8) of Situation 0EZ3: a quasi-compact covering is refined by a
Zariski covering, then one proper arrow, then a Zariski covering

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.isSheaf_qc_zariskiPullbackClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZI.** An abelian sheaf on the localized Zariski site over `X` which is pulled back
from the space underlying `X` satisfies the sheaf condition for the quasi-compact topology over
`X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_qc_zariskiPullbackClass
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X : S.category)
    (G : Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (hG : S.zariskiPullbackClassOfSize.{u, w, u} X G) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (S.qcSite.grothendieckTopology.over X) G.obj
declarations.comment: condition (3) of Situation 0EZ3 for this situation: every abelian sheaf on the localized Zariski site that is pulled back from the space satisfies the sheaf condition for quasi-compact coverings. This is the field `ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison.weakSerre_isSheaf_fine`, proved outright, with the sheaf on the space and the isomorphism to it taken from the essential image rather than from a choice. The five conditions of Situation 0EZ3 are items (1)-(5) of that tag; the `(0EZ4)`/`(0EZ5)`/`(0EZ6)`/`(0EZ7)` names used elsewhere in this directory are this development's own, and this is `(0EZ6)`. ALL FIVE CONDITIONS ARE NOW PROVED for this situation, but SITUATION 0EZ3 IS STILL NOT INSTANTIATED HERE. `CohomologyComparison` is declared `(C : Type u') [SmallCategory C]` (ChangeOfTopology/ComparisonSituation.lean:117) and takes its coefficients in `Ab.{u'}`, so the carrier's universe fixes the coefficient universe. `S.category` is `Type (u+1)` with morphisms in `Type u`, so `SmallCategory S.category` does not synthesize and the carrier is `CategoryTheory.SmallModel S.category`, in `Type u`; `EssentiallySmall.{u} S.category` IS now an instance, `LocallyQuasiCompactQcSite.category_essentiallySmall`. The coefficients are therefore `AddCommGrpCat.{u}`, which is where this condition is proved and is why the carrier cannot be `AsSmall.{v} S.category`: that one would want `AddCommGrpCat.{max (u+1) v}`, where the germ model this condition is read off cannot even be stated. Condition `(0EZ5)` (`zariskiPullbackClassOfSize_overMapPullback`) is now stated for every `AddCommGrpCat.{max u t}` and so holds at `AddCommGrpCat.{u}`. WHAT BLOCKS THE BRIDGE is condition `(0EZ7)` (`zariskiPullbackClass_rightDerived_overMapPushforward`), still stated only at `AddCommGrpCat.{max (u+1) v}`. ONE of the seven inputs of its proof now reaches `AddCommGrpCat.{u}`: `abelianComparisonInverseImage_exact`, which was the one believed obstructed rather than merely unrestated and turns out not to need the slice's covering sieves at all. The next to move, `preservesFiniteLimits_zariskiSlicePushforward`, needs a lemma the library does not have -- `Small.{max u t} (CostructuredArrow (Over.pullback f).op Z)`, the analogue of `small_costructuredArrow_opensToSlice` for `Over.pullback f`, without which `(Over.pullback f).sheafPushforwardContinuous` is not known to be a right adjoint at `max u t`. Past that the remaining five are a RESTATEMENT rather than new proper-base-change mathematics, made large only because the smallness and sheafification facts are supplied as INSTANCES, which cannot be generalized to `max u t` because `max u ?t =?= max (u+1) v` is not solvable by instance synthesis. See `ZariskiHigherDirectImageClass.lean` for the list. Transport of both precoverages and of the class along `equivSmallModel` is also not done

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiPullbackClass_rightDerived_sliceDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZI, the condition on higher direct images.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper arrow of
the locally quasi-compact Zariski site and let `G` be an abelian sheaf on the localized Zariski
site over `X` of the form `π_X^{-1}G₀`. Then for every `i` the higher direct image `R^i f_{Zar,*}G`
is again of that form: it is `π_Y^{-1}` of the `i`-th higher direct image of `G₀` along the
continuous map underlying `f`.

This is condition (0EZ7) of Situation 0EZ3 for the data chosen by Stacks 0EZI — the proper arrows
as the class `P`, the sheaves pulled back from the space as `A'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zariskiPullbackClass_rightDerived_sliceDirectImage
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound)
    ⦃X Y : S.category⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : S.properMorphisms f)
    (G : Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    (hG : S.zariskiPullbackClass.{u, w, v} X G) (i : ℕ) :
    S.zariskiPullbackClass.{u, w, v} Y
      (((sliceDirectImage S f AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).rightDerived i).obj G)
declarations.comment:
condition (0EZ7) of Situation 0EZ3: higher direct images along a proper arrow stay
in the class

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiPullbackClass_isSheaf_qc
declarations.doc:
An abelian sheaf on the localized Zariski site over `X` which is pulled back from the space `X`
is already a sheaf for the quasi-compact topology: `F' = ε_{X,*}ε_X^{-1}F'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zariskiPullbackClass_isSheaf_qc
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X : S.category)
    (F : Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    (hF : S.zariskiPullbackClass.{u, w, v} X F) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (S.qcSite.grothendieckTopology.over X) F.obj
declarations.comment: condition (0EZ6) of Situation 0EZ3 for the sheaves pulled back from the space

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiPullbackClass_isWeakSerreClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZI, the weak Serre condition on the class `A'_X`.** Situation 0EZ3 requires the
class it is handed over each object of the site to be a weak Serre subcategory of the abelian
sheaves on the localized coarse site. For the choice Stacks 0EZI makes — the sheaves of the form
`π_X^{-1}F` on the localized Zariski site — this holds because `π_X^{-1}` is exact and fully
faithful and `π_{X,*}` is exact, all three being parts of Stacks 0DCU.
declarations.statement:
theorem zariskiPullbackClass_isWeakSerreClass
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X : S.category) :
    (S.zariskiPullbackClass.{u, w, v} X).IsWeakSerreClass
declarations.comment: the class A'_X of Situation 0EZ3 is a weak Serre class

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.exists_zariskiRefinement_properMorphisms
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZI**, the covering-refinement condition. Every quasi-compact covering `R` of an
object `U` of the site is refined in three stages: a Zariski covering `Q` of `U`, then over each
member `v : V ⟶ U` of `Q` a single proper arrow `f : W ⟶ V` which is itself a quasi-compact
covering of `V`, and then a Zariski covering of `W` all of whose members factor through `R` along
`f ≫ v`.

The quasi-compact coverings are stated as membership in the underlying precoverage of the site's
chosen pretopology, which is the same condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_zariskiRefinement_properMorphisms
    (U : S.category) (R : Presieve U) (hR : R ∈ S.qcSite.pretopology.toPrecoverage U) :
    ∃ Q : Presieve U, Q ∈ S.zariskiPrecoverage U ∧
      ∀ ⦃V : S.category⦄ (v : V ⟶ U), Q v →
        ∃ (W : S.category) (f : W ⟶ V), S.properMorphisms f ∧
          Presieve.singleton f ∈ S.qcSite.pretopology.toPrecoverage V ∧
          ∃ T : Presieve W, T ∈ S.zariskiPrecoverage W ∧ T.FactorsThruAlong R (f ≫ v)
declarations.comment: condition (5) of Situation 0EZ3 for this situation: the three-stage refinement of a quasi-compact covering, by a Zariski covering, then one proper arrow over each member, then a Zariski covering of its source. This is the field `ComparingTopologies.CohomologyComparison.covering_refinement`, proved outright and carrying no hypothesis beyond the covering itself. The five conditions of Situation 0EZ3 are items (1)-(5) of that tag `(0EZ7)` names used elsewhere in this directory are this development's own. ALL FIVE ARE NOW PROVED for this situation, and Situation 0EZ3 is nevertheless still NOT instantiated here: condition (1) is `morphismProperty_baseChange` (ZariskiComparisonSituationData.lean), condition (2) is `weakSerre_relocalizationInverseImage` (same file), condition (3) is `isSheaf_qc_zariskiPullbackClass` (ZariskiPullbackClassQcSheaf.lean) and condition (4) is `zariskiPullbackClass_rightDerived_overMapPushforward` (ZariskiHigherDirectImageClass.lean). What is missing is one coefficient universe. The carrier of a `CohomologyComparison` has to be `CategoryTheory.SmallModel S.category`, `S.category` having morphisms in `Type u` and only `EssentiallySmall.{u}` `LocallyQuasiCompactQcSite.category_essentiallySmall`, so the small model and `CategoryTheory.equivSmallModel` are available coefficients at `AddCommGrpCat.{u}`. Conditions (1) and (5) are universe-free, (3) is proved there, and (2) now holds at every `AddCommGrpCat.{max u t}`, but (4) is stated only at `AddCommGrpCat.{max (u+1) v}` and every input of its proof carries that universe in its own statement, so it cannot be instantiated at `u` without generalizing the proper-base-change chain. Transporting the five conditions along `equivSmallModel` is also not done

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteEtaleGaloisCover.exists_extending_genericFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EZJ.** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated integral normal
scheme with generic point `η`, let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated smooth
morphism with geometrically connected fibres and `σ` a section of `f`. Let `Z ⟶ X_η` be a finite
étale Galois cover (Section 03SF) with group `G` of order invertible on `S` such that `Z` has a
`κ(η)`-rational point `z` mapping to `σ(η)`. Then there is a finite étale Galois cover `Y ⟶ X`
with group `G` whose restriction to `X_η` is `Z`: the restriction is isomorphic to `Z` by an
isomorphism compatible with the two actions of `G`.

The order of `G` is invertible on `S` when it is a unit in every residue field of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_extending_genericFiber
    {S X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsIntegral S] [IsNormal S]
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [Smooth f] [GeometricallyConnected f]
    (σ : S ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 S)
    (G : Type v) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (hG : ∀ s : S, IsUnit (Nat.card G : S.residueField s))
    (Z : FiniteEtaleGaloisCover (f.fiber (genericPoint S)) G)
    (z : Spec (S.residueField (genericPoint S)) ⟶ Z.obj.left)
    (hz : z ≫ Z.obj.hom = genericFiberSection f σ hσ) :
    ∃ (Y : FiniteEtaleGaloisCover X G)
      (e : (finiteEtaleBaseChange (f.fiberι (genericPoint S))).obj Y.obj ≅ Z.obj),
      ∀ g : Gᵐᵒᵖ, (finiteEtaleBaseChange (f.fiberι (genericPoint S))).map (Y.action g).asIso.hom ≫
        e.hom = e.hom ≫ (Z.action g).asIso.hom
declarations.comment: the full statement under the tag's hypotheses: S qcqs integral normal; f qcqs smooth with geometrically connected fibres and a section σ; Z a finite étale Galois cover of X_η with group G of order invertible on S and a κ(η)-point over σ(η); the extension Y is G-equivariantly a Galois cover restricting to Z

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EZK.** For `f` universally submersive with geometrically connected
fibres, the *canonical* comparison `Γ(S, F) ⟶ Γ(X, f⁻¹F)` is an isomorphism, naturally in the
sheaf `F`. This is the form in which the source asserts the tag — it says "there is a canonical
map `Γ(S, F) → Γ(X, f⁻¹F)`" and then that it is injective and surjective — and it is strictly
stronger than the bare existence of an isomorphism of global-sections functors, which would not
say that the isomorphism is restriction of sections.

**Stacks erratum.** The hypothesis stated here is the corrected one;
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso` carries the characteristic-`2`
counterexample to the tag as the source writes it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hsub : (topologically @Topology.IsQuotientMap :
      MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).universally f)
    [GeometricallyConnected f] :
    IsIso (globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} f)
declarations.comment: corrected: Stacks erratum. The tag in the form the source asserts it, about the canonical comparison rather than a bare isomorphism of global-sections functors. The tag is false with only `f` submersive; see the counterexample in the docstring of globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EZK.** Pullback along a universally submersive morphism with
geometrically connected fibres preserves global sections of every sheaf of sets on the small
étale site, naturally in the sheaf. The isomorphism is the canonical comparison, which
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage` inverts.

**Stacks erratum.** The hypothesis stated here is the corrected
one. As the source writes the tag it asks only that `f` be submersive, and in that form the
statement is false: the proof reduces along an étale base change, and submersivity does not
survive one. The counterexample lives in characteristic `2`. Let `k` be a field of
characteristic `2`, let `A = {g ∈ k[t] ∣ g(0) = g(1)}` be the node — the affine line with the
two points `t = 0` and `t = 1` glued — let `B = k[t, 1/t]` be the affine line with `t = 0`
removed, and let `f : Spec B ⟶ Spec A` be the homeomorphism described in the Stacks proof: it
is bijective because the node has already glued the removed point `t = 0` to the surviving
point `t = 1`. Take `F = h_T`, the functor of points of `T = Spec A[z]/(z² + z + a)` with
`a = t² + t`, which is the connected étale double cover of `Spec A` — étale because the
derivative of `z² + z + a` in `z` is the unit `1` in characteristic `2`. Then `Γ(S, F)` is
EMPTY: a root of `z² + z + a` in `k[t]` is `t` or `t + 1`, and neither takes the same value at
`0` and at `1`, so neither lies in `A`. But `Γ(X, f⁻¹F)` has TWO elements, `t` and `t + 1`,
both of which lie in `B`. So the claimed bijection `Γ(S, F) = Γ(X, f⁻¹F)` cannot hold, and the
submersive hypothesis alone does not suffice. Universal submersivity — equivalently,
submersivity after every étale base change — is what the argument uses and what is assumed
here; it is part of the corrected statement, not a strengthening of it.
declarations.statement:
public def globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hsub : (topologically @Topology.IsQuotientMap :
      MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).universally f)
    [GeometricallyConnected f] :
    Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology S) (Type (max (u + 1) v)) ≅
      smallEtaleInverseImage f ⋙
        Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology X) (Type (max (u + 1) v))
declarations.comment: corrected: Stacks erratum. The tag is false with only `f` submersive, since the proof's reduction is an etale base change and submersivity does not survive one; universal submersivity is assumed instead. Counterexample in characteristic 2: the homeomorphism Spec k[t,1/t] -> Spec {g : g(0) = g(1)} and the double cover T = Spec A[z]/(z^2 + z + a) with a = t^2 + t, for which the sections downstairs are empty while there are two upstairs; see this declaration's docstring

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage_of_etaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EZK.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` have geometrically connected fibres and be
submersive after every étale base change: for every étale `g : V ⟶ S` the projection
`V ×_S X ⟶ V` is a quotient map. Then the canonical comparison `Γ(S, F) ⟶ Γ(X, f⁻¹F)` is an
isomorphism, naturally in the sheaf `F` on the small étale site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage_of_etaleBaseChange
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hsub : ∀ ⦃V : Scheme.{u}⦄ (g : V ⟶ S) [Etale g],
      Topology.IsQuotientMap (pullback.fst g f))
    [GeometricallyConnected f] :
    IsIso (globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} f)
declarations.comment: corrected: Stacks erratum: f submersive after every etale base change, the exact corrected hypothesis; the source's plain submersivity of f is not enough, see the counterexample in the docstring of globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso. The universally submersive special case is isIso_globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIsoOfEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EZK.** Pullback along a morphism with geometrically connected fibres
that is submersive after every étale base change preserves global sections of every sheaf of
sets on the small étale site, naturally in the sheaf; the isomorphism is the canonical
comparison `Γ(S, F) ⟶ Γ(X, f⁻¹F)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIsoOfEtaleBaseChange
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hsub : ∀ ⦃V : Scheme.{u}⦄ (g : V ⟶ S) [Etale g],
      Topology.IsQuotientMap (pullback.fst g f))
    [GeometricallyConnected f] :
    Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology S) (Type (max (u + 1) v)) ≅
      smallEtaleInverseImage f ⋙
        Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology X) (Type (max (u + 1) v))
declarations.comment: corrected: Stacks erratum: f submersive after every etale base change, the exact corrected hypothesis; the source's plain submersivity of f is not enough, see the counterexample in the docstring of globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso. The universally submersive special case is globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.inverseImageSystem
declarations.doc:
**The system of inverse images of a single sheaf, constructed.** Let `D` be an inverse system
of schemes, let `d` be a cocone on it with vertex `S` — so every `D_i` carries a morphism
`D_i ⟶ S` compatible with the transitions — and let `ℱ` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale
site of `S`. The inverse images `(D_i ⟶ S)^{-1} ℱ`, with the transition maps supplied by
`coconeInverseImageComp`, form a system of sheaves on `D` in the sense of Stacks 0EZL.

The cocycle condition is the associativity pentagon
`smallEtalePullbackAbCompIso'_assoc` of the inverse-image comparison, at the three morphisms
`D_i ⟶ D_j ⟶ D_k ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement: def inverseImageSystem : EtaleSheafSystem D Ab.{u + 1}
declarations.comment: the system of INVERSE IMAGES of a single sheaf: for a cocone on the inverse system with vertex `S` and an abelian sheaf on the small etale site of `S`, the system `𝒢_i = (D_i ⟶ S)^{-1} ℱ` together with its cocycle condition, constructed and not assumed. Coefficients are `Ab.{u + 1}` on Mathlib's `Scheme.smallEtaleTopology`, which is where the inverse image of abelian sheaves exists unconditionally

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.EtaleSheafSystem
declarations.doc:
A *system of sheaves* on an inverse system of schemes `D`: a sheaf on the small étale site of
each member, together with a map from the inverse image of the sheaf at an index to the sheaf at
any larger index, compatible with composition of the transition morphisms through the canonical
comparison `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.systemPullbackComp`.
declarations.statement: public structure EtaleSheafSystem

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.EtaleComplexSystem.isSystemColimit_etaleHypercohomologyPullback
declarations.doc:
**Étale cohomology commutes with colimits of bounded below systems of complexes over a limit
of schemes** ([Stacks, Tag 0EZM]). Let `X = lim X_i` be the limit of a directed inverse system of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, `(ℱ_i^•, φ_{i'i})` a
system of complexes of abelian sheaves on the small étale sites of the `X_i` with `ℱ_i^n = 0` for
`n < a`, `a` independent of `i`, and `ι_i : f_i⁻¹ℱ_i^• ⟶ ℱ^•` maps of complexes, compatible with
the transition maps, which present every term `ℱ^n` as the colimit `colim f_i⁻¹ℱ_i^n`. Then for
every `p ∈ ℤ` the pull back maps `H^p(X_i, ℱ_i^•) ⟶ H^p(X, ℱ^•)` exhibit `H^p(X, ℱ^•)` as the
colimit of the system of the `H^p(X_i, ℱ_i^•)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSystemColimit_etaleHypercohomologyPullback (a : ℤ) [∀ i, (F.obj i).IsStrictlyGE a]
    (𝓕 : CochainComplex (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology c.pt) Ab.{u + 1}) ℤ)
    (ι : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, ((smallEtalePullbackAb (c.π.app i)).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj (F.obj i) ⟶ 𝓕)
    (hι : F.IsPullbackCocone c ι)
    (hpres : ∀ n, LimitHigherDirectImage.IsPullbackColimitPresentation c (𝓕.X n) (F.term n)
      (fun i => (ι i).f n)) (p : ℤ) :
    IsSystemColimit
      (fun i => AddCommGrpCat.of
        (etaleHypercohomology (D.obj i) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (F.obj i)) p))
      (fun a => AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (etaleHypercohomologyPullback (D.map a) (F.map a) p))
      (AddCommGrpCat.of (etaleHypercohomology c.pt (DerivedCategory.Q.obj 𝓕) p))
      (fun i => AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (etaleHypercohomologyPullback (c.π.app i) (ι i) p))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isZero_rightDerived_smallEtalePushforward_constantSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EZP.** Higher direct images of a constant abelian
étale sheaf vanish when the source is integral, normal, and has separably
closed function field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_rightDerived_smallEtalePushforward_constantSheaf
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X] [IsSepClosed X.functionField]
    [HasSheafify X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [HasSheafify Y.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [HasInjectiveResolutions (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{w})]
    (M : AddCommGrpCat.{w}) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    IsZero ((((smallEtaleBaseChange f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      AddCommGrpCat.{w} Y.smallEtaleTopology X.smallEtaleTopology).rightDerived q).obj
        ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{w}).obj M))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleLocalBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZR.**  Let

```
X <--h-- Y
|f       |e
S <--g-- T
```

be a cartesian square of schemes, let `{Uᵢ → X}` be an étale covering of `X` such that each
composite `Uᵢ → X → S` factors as `Uᵢ → Vᵢ → S` with `Vᵢ → S` étale, and let

```
Uᵢ <--hᵢ-- Yᵢ
|fᵢ        |eᵢ
Vᵢ <--gᵢ-- Tᵢ
```

be the induced cartesian squares, with `Yᵢ = Uᵢ ×_X Y` and `Tᵢ = Vᵢ ×_S T`.  Let `F` be a sheaf
of sets on the small étale site of `T`, let `𝓖` be an abelian sheaf on it, let `K` be an object of
its unbounded derived category, and write `F|ᵢ`, `𝓖|ᵢ` and `K|ᵢ` for the inverse images along
`Tᵢ ⟶ T`.  Then:

1. if `fᵢ^{-1} g_{i,*} F|ᵢ ⟶ h_{i,*} eᵢ^{-1} F|ᵢ` is an isomorphism for every `i`, so is
   `f^{-1} g_* F ⟶ h_* e^{-1} F`;
2. if `fᵢ^{-1} Rg_{i,*} K|ᵢ ⟶ Rh_{i,*} eᵢ^{-1} K|ᵢ` is an isomorphism for every `i`, so is
   `f^{-1} Rg_* K ⟶ Rh_* e^{-1} K`;
3. for every degree `q`, if `fᵢ^{-1} R^q g_{i,*} 𝓖|ᵢ ⟶ R^q h_{i,*} eᵢ^{-1} 𝓖|ᵢ` is an
   isomorphism for every `i`, so is `f^{-1} R^q g_* 𝓖 ⟶ R^q h_* e^{-1} 𝓖`.

The hypotheses are exactly the source's: the square is cartesian, the family `{Uᵢ → X}` is an
étale covering, each `Uᵢ → S` factors through an étale `Vᵢ → S`, and the two families of induced
squares are cartesian.  Nothing is assumed of `f`, `g`, `h`, `e` beyond that, and the coefficients
are arbitrary sheaves of sets, arbitrary abelian sheaves and arbitrary objects of the unbounded
derived category.

The three parts are proved in
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetsBaseChange_app_of_isIso_local`,
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_etaleAbelianDerivedBaseChange_app_of_isIso_local` and
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_isIso_local`; each of them restricts
the base change map of the outer square to `Uᵢ`, compares it there with the base change map of
the `i`-th local square through the two decompositions of the rectangle `Uᵢ ⟶ X ⟶ S`, and
concludes by the locality of invertibility on the small étale site.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleLocalBaseChange
    (D : EtaleLocalBaseChangeData.{u, z, _, _} (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (𝓖 : Sheaf D.T.smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1})
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf D.T.smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1})) :
    ((∀ i : D.I, IsIso ((smallEtaleSetsBaseChange.{u, v} (D.e_i i) (D.h_i i) (D.g_i i)
          (D.f_i i) (D.local_cartesian i).w.symm).app
            ((smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} (D.toT_i i)).obj D.F))) →
        IsIso ((smallEtaleSetsBaseChange.{u, v} D.e D.h D.g D.f
          D.cartesian.w.symm).app D.F)) ∧
      ((∀ i : D.I, IsIso ((etaleAbelianDerivedBaseChange.{u, 0} (D.g_i i) (D.f_i i) (D.e_i i)
            (D.h_i i) (D.local_cartesian i).w.symm).app
              ((etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} (D.toT_i i)).obj K))) →
          IsIso ((etaleAbelianDerivedBaseChange.{u, 0} D.g D.f D.e D.h
            D.cartesian.w.symm).app K)) ∧
        ∀ q : ℕ, (∀ i : D.I, IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb (D.f_i i) (D.g_i i) (D.h_i i)
            (D.e_i i) (D.local_cartesian i).w q).app
              ((smallEtalePullbackAb (D.toT_i i)).obj 𝓖))) →
          IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb D.f D.g D.h D.e D.cartesian.w q).app 𝓖)
declarations.comment: parts (1), (2) and (3), as the conjunction of the three implications

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleSetsBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**The base change map `g^{-1} f_* ⟶ f'_* (g')^{-1}` for sheaves of sets** on the small étale
sites of a commutative square `g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g` of schemes: the mate, under the two
inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions, of the identification of the two composite direct images
around the square.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtaleSetsBaseChange {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (w : g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g) :
    smallEtaleDirectImage.{u, v} f ⋙ smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} g ⟶
      smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} g' ⋙ smallEtaleDirectImage.{u, v} f'
declarations.comment: the set-valued base change map and the locality calculus only: the map g^{-1} f_* to f'_* (g')^{-1} for sheaves of SETS, which the library previously had only for abelian coefficients, together with the hypothesis bundle and the option-free mate calculus the locality argument runs on. NONE of the tag's three clauses is proved here. Clause (1) is blocked at rightSquare_app by a kernel defeq the elaborator cannot reduce because getLimitCone is not exposed by the module system; clause (3) sits on top of it; clause (2) has no proof content anywhere in the repository.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetsBaseChange_of_isIso_local
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZR, part (1): the base change map of sheaves of sets may be checked étale-locally
on `X`.**  Let

```
X <--h-- Y
|f       |e
S <--g-- T
```

be a cartesian square of schemes, let `{Uᵢ → X}` be an étale covering such that each `Uᵢ → S`
factors as `Uᵢ → Vᵢ → S` with `Vᵢ → S` étale, and form the induced cartesian squares with
`Yᵢ = Uᵢ ×_X Y` and `Tᵢ = Vᵢ ×_S T`.  If for every `i` the base change map
`fᵢ^{-1} g_{i,*} Fᵢ ⟶ h_{i,*} e_i^{-1} Fᵢ` of the `i`-th local square is an isomorphism, where
`Fᵢ` is the inverse image of `F` on `Tᵢ`, then the base change map
`f^{-1} g_* F ⟶ h_* e^{-1} F` of the outer square is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetsBaseChange_of_isIso_local
    (D : EtaleLocalBaseChangeData.{u, z, max (u + 1) v, (max (u + 1) v) + 1}
      (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (hlocal : ∀ i : D.I,
      IsIso ((smallEtaleSetsBaseChange.{u, v} (D.e_i i) (D.h_i i) (D.g_i i) (D.f_i i)
        (D.local_cartesian i).w.symm).app
        ((smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} (D.toT_i i)).obj D.F))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSetsBaseChange.{u, v} D.e D.h D.g D.f D.cartesian.w.symm).app D.F)
declarations.comment: clause (1), for sheaves of SETS, which is the generality in which the source states it: the étale-local criterion for the ordinary base change map. Clause (2), the analogue for an object of the unbounded derived category, and clause (3), the analogue for the higher direct images, are not proved here.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_paste
declarations.doc:
**Base change maps of a rectangle of squares.** Consider a tower of two commutative squares
of schemes
```
X₂ --v₂--> X₁ --v₁--> X₀
|g₂         |g₁        |g₀
v           v          v
S₂ --u₂--> S₁ --u₁--> S₀
```
written in the notation of the Stacks Project by `u₁ = f`, `v₁ = e`, `g₀ = g`, `g₁ = h`,
`u₂ = i`, `v₂ = k`, `g₂ = j`, let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `X₀` and let
`q` be a degree.
If the degree-`q` base change maps `f⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` of the lower square and
`i⁻¹ R^q h_* (e⁻¹ F) ⟶ R^q j_* k⁻¹ (e⁻¹ F)` of the upper square are isomorphisms, then so is the
degree-`q` base change map `(i ≫ f)⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q j_* (k ≫ e)⁻¹ F` of the outer rectangle.
Nothing is assumed of the squares beyond commutativity: neither need be cartesian, and the
degree `q` is arbitrary — each degree is a separate statement, with the same degree in the
hypotheses and in the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_of_paste (g₀ : X₀ ⟶ S₀) (g₁ : X₁ ⟶ S₁)
    (g₂ : X₂ ⟶ S₂) (u₁ : S₁ ⟶ S₀) (u₂ : S₂ ⟶ S₁) (v₁ : X₁ ⟶ X₀) (v₂ : X₂ ⟶ X₁)
    (w₁ : g₁ ≫ u₁ = v₁ ≫ g₀) (w₂ : g₂ ≫ u₂ = v₂ ≫ g₁) (q : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X₀) Ab.{u + 1})
    (h₁ : IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb u₁ g₀ g₁ v₁ w₁ q).app F))
    (h₂ : IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb u₂ g₁ g₂ v₂ w₂ q).app
      ((smallEtalePullbackAb v₁).obj F))) :
    IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb (u₂ ≫ u₁) g₀ g₂ (v₂ ≫ v₁)
      (smallEtaleRectangle_comm g₀ g₁ g₂ u₁ u₂ v₁ v₂ w₁ w₂) q).app F)
declarations.comment: the abelian half: for an abelian sheaf F on T_étale and a degree q, if f⁻¹R^qg_*F → R^qh_*e⁻¹F and i⁻¹R^qh_*e⁻¹F → R^qj_*k⁻¹e⁻¹F are isomorphisms then (f∘i)⁻¹R^qg_*F → R^qj_*(e∘k)⁻¹F is an isomorphism; the derived statement of the same tag is `etaleAbelianDerivedBaseChange_isIso_of_comp`

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleAbelianDerivedBaseChange_isIso_of_comp
declarations.doc:
Consider a tower of two commutative squares of schemes
```
W <--j-- Z
|i       |k
X <--h-- Y
|f       |e
S <--g-- T
```
and `K` in `D(T_étale)`.  If the base change maps `f⁻¹ Rg_* K ⟶ Rh_* e⁻¹ K` and
`i⁻¹ Rh_* e⁻¹ K ⟶ Rj_* k⁻¹ e⁻¹ K` of the two squares are isomorphisms, then so is the base change
map `(i ≫ f)⁻¹ Rg_* K ⟶ Rj_* (k ≫ e)⁻¹ K` of the outer rectangle.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleAbelianDerivedBaseChange_isIso_of_comp (f : X ⟶ S) (g : T ⟶ S) (h : Y ⟶ X)
    (e : Y ⟶ T) (i : W ⟶ X) (j : Z ⟶ W) (k : Z ⟶ Y)
    (sq₁ : e ≫ g = h ≫ f) (sq₂ : k ≫ h = j ≫ i)
    (a : W ⟶ S) (ha : a = i ≫ f) (b : Z ⟶ T) (hb : b = k ≫ e) (hyp : b ≫ g = j ≫ a)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}))
    (h₁ : IsIso ((etaleAbelianDerivedBaseChange.{u, v} g f e h sq₁).app K))
    (h₂ : IsIso ((etaleAbelianDerivedBaseChange.{u, v} h i k j sq₂).app
      ((etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, v} e).obj K))) :
    IsIso ((etaleAbelianDerivedBaseChange.{u, v} g a b j hyp).app K)
declarations.comment: the derived half: for K in D(T_étale), if f⁻¹Rg_*K → Rh_*e⁻¹K and i⁻¹Rh_*e⁻¹K → Rj_*k⁻¹e⁻¹K are isomorphisms then (f∘i)⁻¹Rg_*K → Rj_*(e∘k)⁻¹K is an isomorphism; the R^q statement of the same tag is not covered here

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitBaseChange.isPullback_limitSquare
declarations.doc:
**The square on the limits is cartesian**, the assertion of the setup of Stacks 0EZT. A
morphism to `X` and a morphism to `T` agreeing over `S` induce, level by level, a morphism to
`Y_i` through the cartesian square at `i`; these are compatible with the transitions because the
two legs of the square at a larger index determine a morphism, so they define a morphism to
`Y = lim Y_i`, and the same two uniqueness statements make it the unique one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_limitSquare (hcX : IsLimit cX) (hcS : IsLimit cS) (hcT : IsLimit cT)
    (hcY : IsLimit cY)
    (hfL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, fL ≫ cS.π.app i = cX.π.app i ≫ f.app i)
    (hgL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, gL ≫ cS.π.app i = cT.π.app i ≫ g.app i)
    (hhL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, hL ≫ cX.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ h.app i)
    (heL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, eL ≫ cT.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ e.app i)
    (hsq : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsPullback (h.app i) (e.app i) (f.app i) (g.app i)) :
    IsPullback hL eL fL gL
declarations.comment: the square on the limits of an inverse system of cartesian squares is cartesian

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitBaseChange.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_limit
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (2) of Stacks 0EZT.** Let `(ℱ_i, φ_{i'i})` be a system of abelian sheaves on
`(T_i)` and let `ℱ` on `T` be a sheaf whose higher direct images along the limit are presented,
as in Stacks 0EYM, as the colimits of the `s_i^{-1}R^q g_{i,*}ℱ_i` and of the
`r_i^{-1}R^q h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}ℱ_i`, compatibly with the levelwise base change maps. If the base
change map of every level is an isomorphism, so is the base change map of the limit square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_limit
    (w : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, h.app i ≫ f.app i = e.app i ≫ g.app i) (wL : hL ≫ fL = eL ≫ gL)
    (hfL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, fL ≫ cS.π.app i = cX.π.app i ≫ f.app i)
    (𝓕 : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cT.pt) Ab.{u + 1})
    (Kg : I ⥤ Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cS.pt) Ab.{u + 1})
    (ρg : ∀ i : I, Kg.obj i ≅ sourceTerm g cS F q (Opposite.op i))
    (κg : Kg ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj
      (((smallEtalePushforwardAb gL).rightDerived q).obj 𝓕))
    (hκg : IsColimit (Cocone.mk _ κg))
    (Kh : I ⥤ Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cX.pt) Ab.{u + 1})
    (ρh : ∀ i : I, Kh.obj i ≅ targetTerm h e cX F q (Opposite.op i))
    (κh : Kh ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj
      (((smallEtalePushforwardAb hL).rightDerived q).obj ((smallEtalePullbackAb eL).obj 𝓕)))
    (hκh : IsColimit (Cocone.mk _ κh))
    (α : Kg ⋙ smallEtalePullbackAb fL ⟶ Kh)
    (hα : ∀ i : I, (smallEtalePullbackAb fL).map (ρg i).hom ≫
      stageComparison f g h e cX cS fL F q w hfL (Opposite.op i) = α.app i ≫ (ρh i).hom)
    (hκ : ∀ i : I, (smallEtalePullbackAb fL).map (κg.app i) ≫
      (higherBaseChangeMapAb fL gL hL eL wL q).app 𝓕 = α.app i ≫ κh.app i)
    (hstage : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ,
      IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb (f.app i) (g.app i) (h.app i) (e.app i) (w i) q).app
        (F.obj i))) :
    IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb fL gL hL eL wL q).app 𝓕)
declarations.comment: conclusion (2): base change for the higher direct images passes to the limit

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitBaseChange.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_limit_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (2) of Stacks 0EZT.** Let `I` be a directed set and let
`(X_i, Y_i, S_i, T_i, f_i, h_i, e_i, g_i)` be an inverse system of cartesian squares of schemes
with affine transition morphisms and with `g_i` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, with limit
square `(X, Y, S, T, f, h, e, g)`. Let `(ℱ_i, φ_{i'i})` be a system of abelian sheaves on
`(T_i)` and `ℱ = colim p_i⁻¹ℱ_i`. If the base change map
`f_i⁻¹R^q g_{i, *}ℱ_i ⟶ R^q h_{i, *}e_i⁻¹ℱ_i` is an isomorphism for every `i`, then so is
`f⁻¹R^q g_*ℱ ⟶ R^q h_*e⁻¹ℱ`.

The limit morphisms are any morphisms `f`, `g`, `h`, `e` satisfying the equations of the
projection squares, and `ℱ = colim p_i⁻¹ℱ_i` is given by maps `ι_i : p_i⁻¹ℱ_i ⟶ ℱ` compatible with
the transition maps and enjoying the universal property of the colimit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_limit_of_isLimit [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DX.map a)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DS.map a)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DT.map a)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DY.map a)]
    [∀ i, QuasiCompact (g.app i)] [∀ i, QuasiSeparated (g.app i)]
    (hsq : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsPullback (h.app i) (e.app i) (f.app i) (g.app i))
    (hcX : IsLimit cX) (hcS : IsLimit cS) (hcT : IsLimit cT) (hcY : IsLimit cY)
    (gL : cT.pt ⟶ cS.pt) (hL : cY.pt ⟶ cX.pt)
    (hgL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, gL ≫ cS.π.app i = cT.π.app i ≫ g.app i)
    (hhL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, hL ≫ cX.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ h.app i)
    (𝓕 : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cT.pt) Ab.{u + 1})
    (ι : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, (smallEtalePullbackAb (cT.π.app i)).obj (F.obj i) ⟶ 𝓕)
    (hι : IsPullbackCocone cT F ι) (hpres : IsPullbackColimitPresentation cT 𝓕 F ι)
    (hstage : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb (f.app i) (g.app i) (h.app i) (e.app i)
      (hsq i).w q).app (F.obj i))) :
    IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb fL gL hL eL
      (limitSquare_comm f g h e cX cS cT cY fL gL hL eL hcS hfL hgL hhL heL fun i => (hsq i).w)
        q).app 𝓕)
declarations.comment: conclusion (2): if base change for `R^q` holds at every level of the system of cartesian squares, it holds for the limit square

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitSetBaseChange.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EZT] (1): base change for the direct images of sheaves of sets passes to the
limit.** Let `I` be a directed set and let `(X_i ← Y_i, S_i ← T_i)` be an inverse system over `I`
of cartesian squares of schemes `h_i ≫ f_i = e_i ≫ g_i`, with affine transition morphisms and with
every `g_i` quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let `X, S, T, Y` be the limits, with the limit
morphisms `f, g, h, e` characterised by `f ≫ s_i = r_i ≫ f_i`, `g ≫ s_i = p_i ≫ g_i`,
`h ≫ r_i = q_i ≫ h_i` and `e ≫ p_i = q_i ≫ e_i`. Let `(ℱ_i, φ_{i'i})` be a system of sheaves of
sets on `(T_i)` (Stacks 0EZL) and let `ℱ = colim p_i^{-1}ℱ_i` on `T`, presented by legs
`ι_i : p_i^{-1}ℱ_i ⟶ ℱ`. If for every `i` the base change map
`f_i^{-1}g_{i,*}ℱ_i ⟶ h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}ℱ_i` of sheaves of sets is an isomorphism, then so is the base
change map `f^{-1}g_*ℱ ⟶ h_*e^{-1}ℱ` of the limit square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isLimit
    (hsq : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsPullback (h.app i) (e.app i) (f.app i) (g.app i))
    (hcX : IsLimit cX) (hcS : IsLimit cS) (hcT : IsLimit cT) (hcY : IsLimit cY)
    (hfL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, fL ≫ cS.π.app i = cX.π.app i ≫ f.app i)
    (hgL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, gL ≫ cS.π.app i = cT.π.app i ≫ g.app i)
    (hhL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, hL ≫ cX.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ h.app i)
    (heL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, eL ≫ cT.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ e.app i)
    (𝓕 : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cT.pt) (Type (u + 1)))
    (F : EtaleSheafSystem DT (Type (u + 1)))
    (ι : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, (etalePullback (cT.π.app i) (Type (u + 1))).obj (F.obj i) ⟶ 𝓕)
    (hι : ∀ ⦃i j : Iᵒᵖ⦄ (a : i ⟶ j),
      (Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso (systemAdjunction DT (Type (u + 1)) a)
          (etaleAdjunction (cT.π.app i) (Type (u + 1)))
          (etaleAdjunction (cT.π.app j) (Type (u + 1)))
          (coneProjectionComp (Type (u + 1)) cT a)).inv.app (F.obj j) ≫
        (etalePullback (cT.π.app i) (Type (u + 1))).map (F.map a) ≫ ι i = ι j)
    (hpres : IsSetPullbackColimitPresentation cT F 𝓕 ι)
    (hstage : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ,
      IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, 0} (e.app i) (h.app i) (g.app i) (f.app i)
        (hsq i).w.symm).app (F.obj i))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, 0} eL hL gL fL
      (LimitBaseChange.limitSquare_comm f g h e cX cS cT cY fL gL hL eL hcS hfL hgL hhL heL
        fun i => (hsq i).w).symm).app 𝓕)
declarations.comment: conclusion (1), at the source's hypotheses: for an inverse system over a directed set of cartesian squares of schemes with affine transition morphisms and quasi-compact quasi-separated `g_i`, with limit square `(f, g, h, e)`, and a system of sheaves of sets `ℱ_i` on the `T_i` (Tag 0EZL) with `ℱ = colim p_i^{-1}ℱ_i`, if every base change map `f_i^{-1}g_{i,*}ℱ_i ⟶ h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}ℱ_i` of sheaves of sets (`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleSetBaseChange`) is an isomorphism then so is `f^{-1}g_*ℱ ⟶ h_*e^{-1}ℱ`. Together with `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitBaseChange.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_of_isLimit`, conclusion (2), this covers the tag.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitBaseChange.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EZT] (2): base change for the higher direct images passes to the limit.**
Let `I` be a directed set and let `(X_i ← Y_i, S_i ← T_i)` be an inverse system over `I` of
cartesian squares of schemes `h_i ≫ f_i = e_i ≫ g_i`, with affine transition morphisms and with
every `g_i` quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let `X, S, T, Y` be the limits, with the limit
morphisms `f, g, h, e` characterised by `f ≫ s_i = r_i ≫ f_i`, `g ≫ s_i = p_i ≫ g_i`,
`h ≫ r_i = q_i ≫ h_i` and `e ≫ p_i = q_i ≫ e_i`. Let `(ℱ_i, φ_{i'i})` be a system of abelian
sheaves on `(T_i)` (Stacks 0EZL) and let `ℱ = colim p_i^{-1}ℱ_i` on `T`, presented by legs
`ι_i : p_i^{-1}ℱ_i ⟶ ℱ`. If for every `i` the base change map
`f_i^{-1}R^q g_{i,*}ℱ_i ⟶ R^q h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}ℱ_i` is an isomorphism, then so is the base change
map `f^{-1}R^q g_*ℱ ⟶ R^q h_*e^{-1}ℱ` of the limit square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_of_isLimit
    (hsq : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsPullback (h.app i) (e.app i) (f.app i) (g.app i))
    (hcX : IsLimit cX) (hcS : IsLimit cS) (hcT : IsLimit cT) (hcY : IsLimit cY)
    (hfL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, fL ≫ cS.π.app i = cX.π.app i ≫ f.app i)
    (hgL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, gL ≫ cS.π.app i = cT.π.app i ≫ g.app i)
    (hhL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, hL ≫ cX.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ h.app i)
    (heL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, eL ≫ cT.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ e.app i) (q : ℕ)
    (𝓕 : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cT.pt) Ab.{u + 1})
    (F : EtaleSheafSystem DT Ab.{u + 1})
    (ι : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, (smallEtalePullbackAb (cT.π.app i)).obj (F.obj i) ⟶ 𝓕)
    (hι : ∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j),
      (conePullbackComp cT a).inv.app (F.obj j) ≫
        (smallEtalePullbackAb (cT.π.app i)).map (F.map a) ≫ ι i = ι j)
    (hpres : IsPullbackColimitPresentation cT 𝓕 F ι)
    (hstage : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ,
      IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb (f.app i) (g.app i) (h.app i) (e.app i) (hsq i).w q).app
        (F.obj i))) :
    IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb fL gL hL eL
      (limitSquare_comm f g h e cX cS cT cY fL gL hL eL hcS hfL hgL hhL heL fun i => (hsq i).w)
      q).app 𝓕)
declarations.comment: conclusion (2), at the source's hypotheses: for an inverse system over a directed set of cartesian squares of schemes with affine transition morphisms and quasi-compact quasi-separated `g_i`, with limit square `(f, g, h, e)`, and a system of abelian sheaves `ℱ_i` on the `T_i` with `ℱ = colim p_i^{-1}ℱ_i`, if every base change map `f_i^{-1}R^q g_{i,*}ℱ_i ⟶ R^q h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}ℱ_i` is an isomorphism then so is `f^{-1}R^q g_*ℱ ⟶ R^q h_*e^{-1}ℱ`. Together with `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitSetBaseChange.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isLimit`, conclusion (1), this covers the tag.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitBaseChange.isIso_smallEtaleSheafBaseChange_limit
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (1) of Stacks 0EZT.** Let `I` be a directed set and let
`(X_i, Y_i, S_i, T_i, f_i, h_i, e_i, g_i)` be an inverse system of cartesian squares of schemes
with affine transition morphisms and with `g_i` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, with limit
square `(X, Y, S, T, f, h, e, g)`. Let `(ℱ_i, φ_{i'i})` be a system of sheaves of sets on `(T_i)`
and `ℱ = colim p_i⁻¹ℱ_i`. If the base change map `f_i⁻¹g_{i, *}ℱ_i ⟶ h_{i, *}e_i⁻¹ℱ_i` is an
isomorphism for every `i`, then so is `f⁻¹g_*ℱ ⟶ h_*e⁻¹ℱ`.

The limit morphisms are any morphisms `f`, `g`, `h`, `e` satisfying the equations of the
projection squares, and `ℱ = colim p_i⁻¹ℱ_i` is given by maps `ι_i : p_i⁻¹ℱ_i ⟶ ℱ` compatible with
the transition maps and enjoying the universal property of the colimit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSheafBaseChange_limit {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    [Nonempty I] {DX DS DT DY : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}}
    (f : DX ⟶ DS) (g : DT ⟶ DS) (h : DY ⟶ DX) (e : DY ⟶ DT)
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DX.map a)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DS.map a)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DT.map a)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DY.map a)]
    [∀ i, QuasiCompact (g.app i)] [∀ i, QuasiSeparated (g.app i)]
    (hsq : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsPullback (h.app i) (e.app i) (f.app i) (g.app i))
    {cX : Cone DX} {cS : Cone DS} {cT : Cone DT} {cY : Cone DY}
    (hcX : IsLimit cX) (hcS : IsLimit cS) (hcT : IsLimit cT) (hcY : IsLimit cY)
    (fL : cX.pt ⟶ cS.pt) (gL : cT.pt ⟶ cS.pt) (hL : cY.pt ⟶ cX.pt) (eL : cY.pt ⟶ cT.pt)
    (hfL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, fL ≫ cS.π.app i = cX.π.app i ≫ f.app i)
    (hgL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, gL ≫ cS.π.app i = cT.π.app i ≫ g.app i)
    (hhL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, hL ≫ cX.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ h.app i)
    (heL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, eL ≫ cT.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ e.app i)
    (F : EtaleSheafSystem DT (Type (u + 1))) (𝓕 : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cT.pt) (Type (u + 1)))
    (ι : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, (smallEtaleSheafPullback (Type (u + 1)) (X := cT.pt) (cT.π.app i)).obj
      (F.obj i) ⟶ 𝓕)
    (hι : F.IsSheafPullbackCocone cT ι) (hpres : F.IsSheafPullbackColimitPresentation cT 𝓕 ι)
    (hstage : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsIso ((smallEtaleSheafBaseChange (Type (u + 1)) (f.app i) (g.app i)
      (h.app i) (e.app i) (hsq i).w).app (F.obj i))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSheafBaseChange (Type (u + 1)) fL gL hL eL
      (limitSquare_comm f g h e cX cS cT cY fL gL hL eL hcS hfL hgL hhL heL
        fun i => (hsq i).w)).app 𝓕)
declarations.comment: conclusion (1): if base change for sheaves of sets holds at every level of the system of cartesian squares, it holds for the limit square

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitSetBaseChange.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_limit
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (1) of Stacks 0EZT.** Let `(ℱ_i)` be a family of sheaves of sets on the `T_i`
and let `ℱ` on `T` be a sheaf whose direct images along the limit are presented, as in Stacks
0EYM, as the colimits of the `s_i^{-1}g_{i,*}ℱ_i` and of the `r_i^{-1}h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}ℱ_i`,
compatibly with the levelwise base change maps. If the base change map of every level is an
isomorphism, so is the base change map of the limit square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_limit (w : ∀ i, h i ≫ f i = e i ≫ g i)
    (wL : hL ≫ fL = eL ≫ gL) (hfL : ∀ i, fL ≫ s i = r i ≫ f i)
    (𝓕 : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (Kg : I ⥤ Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology S) (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (ρg : ∀ i, Kg.obj i ≅ sourceTerm.{u, v} g s F i)
    (κg : Kg ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj
      ((smallEtalePushforward gL (Type (max (u + 1) v))).obj 𝓕))
    (hκg : IsColimit (Cocone.mk
      ((smallEtalePushforward gL (Type (max (u + 1) v))).obj 𝓕) κg))
    (Kh : I ⥤ Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (ρh : ∀ i, Kh.obj i ≅ targetTerm.{u, v} h e r F i)
    (κh : Kh ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj
      ((smallEtalePushforward hL (Type (max (u + 1) v))).obj
        ((smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} eL).obj 𝓕)))
    (hκh : IsColimit (Cocone.mk
      ((smallEtalePushforward hL (Type (max (u + 1) v))).obj
        ((smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} eL).obj 𝓕)) κh))
    (α : Kg ⋙ smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} fL ⟶ Kh)
    (hα : ∀ i, (smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} fL).map (ρg i).hom ≫
      stageComparison.{u, v} f g h e r s fL F w hfL i = α.app i ≫ (ρh i).hom)
    (hκ : ∀ i, (smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} fL).map (κg.app i) ≫
      setBaseChangeApp.{u, v} eL hL gL fL wL.symm 𝓕 = α.app i ≫ κh.app i)
    (hstage : ∀ i, IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, v} (e i) (h i) (g i) (f i)
      (w i).symm).app (F i))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, v} eL hL gL fL wL.symm).app 𝓕)
declarations.comment:
conclusion (1): base change for the direct images of sheaves of sets passes to
the limit. The two colimit presentations `g_*ℱ = colim_i s_i^{-1}g_{i,*}ℱ_i` and
`h_*e^{-1}ℱ = colim_i r_i^{-1}h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}ℱ_i` are the two instances of Stacks 0EYM that the
source's proof cites; this repository does not prove Stacks 0EYM --
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage` constructs only its comparison maps and says so
in its own clause strings -- and the compatibility of the two with the legs is the pasting of
base change maps of Stacks 0E47. All three are carried as declared hypotheses
(`Kg`/`ρg`/`κg`/`hκg`, `Kh`/`ρh`/`κh`/`hκh`, `α`/`hα`/`hκ`), exactly as for conclusion (2) in
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitBaseChange.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_limit`. What is proved is
the source's own argument from those inputs: inverse image is a left adjoint, so it carries the
first presentation to a colimit presentation of `f^{-1}g_*ℱ`, and a map of colimit cocones that
is invertible on every term is invertible. Since the two presentations are hypotheses, the
proof uses nothing of the inverse systems but the schemes and the morphisms, and the levels are
accordingly carried as bare families rather than as functors out of `Iᵒᵖ`: no functoriality, no
limit property of the cones and no cartesianness of the squares is assumed.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_forall_isIso_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZU.** Consider a cartesian diagram of schemes
```
X  ←-h-  Y
|f       |e
S  ←-g-  T
```
with `g : T ⟶ S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small
étale site of `T`, and let `q ≥ 0`. Then the base change map on higher direct images
`f⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism if and only if its map on the stalk at every
geometric point of `X` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_forall_isIso_stalk
    {X Y S T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (h : Y ⟶ X) (e : Y ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ S)
    (sq : IsPullback h e f g) [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1}) (q : ℕ) :
    (∀ x : GeometricPoint X,
        IsIso ((smallEtaleStalkAb x.hom).map ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f g h e sq.w q).app F))) ↔
      IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f g h e sq.w q).app F)
declarations.comment: base change on higher direct images is an isomorphism iff it is on every stalk

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_forall_isIso_stalkMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0EZU**, with the condition at a geometric point `x̄` of `X` phrased as invertibility
of the canonical map `(R^q g_* F)_{s̄} ⟶ (R^q h_* e⁻¹ F)_{x̄}` out of the stalk at the image
geometric point `s̄ = f(x̄)`. In the situation of
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_forall_isIso_stalk`, the base change
map `f⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism if and only if that map is an isomorphism
for every geometric point `x̄` of `X`.

This is the source's equivalence with each of its two cohomology groups replaced by the stalk
which it computes; the identification of the stalks with cohomology over the fibre products
`Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄}) ×_S T` and `Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{X,x̄}) ×_S T` is not available in the library.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_forall_isIso_stalkMap
    {X Y S T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (h : Y ⟶ X) (e : Y ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ S)
    (sq : IsPullback h e f g) [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1}) (q : ℕ) :
    (∀ x : GeometricPoint X,
        IsIso (higherBaseChangeMapAbStalk f g h e sq.w q F x)) ↔
      IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f g h e sq.w q).app F)
declarations.comment: the condition at a geometric point, as a map out of the stalk at its image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_forall_bijective
declarations.doc:
Consider a cartesian square of schemes
```
X  ←-h-  Y
|f       |e
S  ←-g-  T
```
