with `g : T ⟶ S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let `F` be an abelian sheaf on `T_étale` and
let `q ≥ 0`. The following are equivalent:

1. for every geometric point `x̄` of `X` with image `s̄ = f(x̄)`, the restriction map
   `H^q(T ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄}), F) ⟶ H^q(T ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{X,x̄}), F)` along the canonical
   morphism `AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationBaseChangeMap` is bijective;
2. the base change map `f⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism.

Here the cohomology groups are those of the inverse images of `F` along the projections to `T`, and
the restriction map is pull back along the canonical morphism together with the comparison of
the iterated inverse image with the inverse image along the composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_app_iff_forall_bijective
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1}) (q : ℕ) :
    (∀ x : GeometricPoint X, Function.Bijective
      (etaleCohomologyPullback (strictHenselizationBaseChangeMap B hX hS f g x)
        ((smallEtalePullbackAbComp' _ _ _
          (strictHenselizationBaseChangeMap_fst B hX hS f g x)).hom.app
          F) q)) ↔
      IsIso ((higherBaseChangeMapAb f g h e sq.w q).app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.bijective_strictHenselizationFiberRestriction_iff_of_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EZV.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, let `x̄` be a
geometric point of `X` with image `s̄` in `S`, let `Spec K ⟶ Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄})` be a morphism
with `K` a separably closed field, let `ℱ` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of
`Spec K` and let `q ≥ 0`. Then
`H^q(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{X,x̄}) ×_S Spec K, ℱ) = H^q(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄}) ×_S Spec K, ℱ)` holds if and
only if `H^q(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{X,x̄}) ×_{Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄})} Spec K, ℱ) = H^q(Spec K, ℱ)` does, each
equality read as bijectivity of the canonical restriction map.

The limit presentation of the two cohomology groups over `Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄}) ×_S Spec K` as
locally constant functions on a nonempty space is carried as the explicit datum
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.SepClosedFiberLocallyConstantPresentation`; what is proved here is the
equivalence, which comes down to post-composition with a map being bijective on locally constant
functions on a nonempty space exactly when the map is.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_strictHenselizationFiberRestriction_iff_of_presentation
    [IsSepClosed K] (A : Type u) [TopologicalSpace A]
    (F : Sheaf (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    (q : ℕ)
    (P : SepClosedFiberLocallyConstantPresentation.{u, v, w} B hX hS f x k A F q) :
    Function.Bijective (strictHenselizationFiberRestriction.{u, v, w} B hX hS f x k F q) ↔
      Function.Bijective (strictHenselizationPointRestriction.{u, v, w} B hX hS f x k F q)
declarations.comment:
the equivalence of the tag's two conditions. What is carried as the explicit datum
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.SepClosedFiberLocallyConstantPresentation`, rather than constructed, is
exactly the COHOMOLOGICAL identification of the source's proof: that the two cohomology groups
over `Spec(O^sh_{S,s̄}) ×_S Spec K` are locally constant functions on the limit index space with
values in the two groups over `Spec K`, compatibly with restriction. The geometric input it rests
on is proved here, not assumed -- the fibre product is affine
(`isAffine_strictHenselizationBaseFiber`), is `Spec` of a ring ind-étale over `K`
(`indEtale_strictHenselizationBaseFiberRing`, from `indEtale_etaleLocalRing` and Stacks 0BSH),
and each étale `K`-algebra of such a presentation has `Spec` a finite coproduct of copies of
`Spec K` (`specIsoSigmaOfIsSepClosed`). Three things block constructing the datum: Theorem 09YQ
is available only as the right-derived `sheafSections` of the small AFFINE étale site and its
transport to the `Sheaf.H` of the small étale site, which is what
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap` is stated for, needs a general-degree
comparison `Sheaf.H = rightDerived sheafSections` that exists nowhere at these universes; the
passage from `StacksDraft.IndEtale` to an explicit cofiltered limit of schemes is unavailable;
and the source's identification of the base change along the morphism of strict henselizations of
the different copies of `Spec K` in a stage -- distinct `K`-points of `Spec(O^sh_{S,s̄})`, Galois
twists of one another -- is suppressed in the source and not available either. The datum asserts
only the cohomological identification, not the equivalence, which is proved here

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.bijective_strictHenselizationFiberCohomologyPullback_iff
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0EZV], corrected.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, `x̄` a geometric
point of `X` with image `s̄`, `k : Spec K ⟶ Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄})` with `K` separably closed, `ℱ` an
abelian sheaf on `Spec K` and `q ≥ 0`. Then
`H^q(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{X,x̄}) ×_S Spec K, ℱ) = H^q(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄}) ×_S Spec K, ℱ)` if and only if
`H^q(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{X,x̄}) ×_{Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄}), k'} Spec K, ℱ) = H^q(Spec K, ℱ)` for every lift
`k'` of the composite `Spec K ⟶ S` to the strict henselization, each equality read as
bijectivity of the restriction map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_strictHenselizationFiberCohomologyPullback_iff
    (F : Sheaf (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1}) (q : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective (strictHenselizationFiberCohomologyPullback B hX hS f x k F q) ↔
      ∀ k' : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ strictHenselization B S hS (x.map f),
        k' ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS (x.map f) =
            k ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS (x.map f) →
          Function.Bijective (strictHenselizationPointCohomologyPullback B hX hS f x k' F q)
declarations.comment:
corrected: condition (1) is equivalent to condition (2) at every lift `k'` of
`Spec K ⟶ S` to the strict henselization, not only at the given point; that (2) at the given
point does not imply (1) is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_bijective_pointRestriction_and_not_bijective_fiberRestriction`

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_bijective_pointRestriction_and_not_bijective_fiberRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0EZV fails as stated: condition (2) at the given point does not imply condition (1).**
Let `S` be the nodal cubic over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, `s̄` its
geometric point at the node, and `X = Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄}/(e))` for the branch
`e = y - x √(1 + x)` of the node in the strict henselization, with `x̄` its geometric point over
`s̄`. For two `K`-points `κ`, `τ` of `Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s̄})` over the same point of `S`, with `κ` on
the branch and `τ` off it, take the point `κ` and `q = 0`, `ℱ = ℤ`. The fibre of `X` over `κ` is
`Spec K` itself, so condition (2) holds; the fibre over `τ` is empty, so the restriction map of
condition (1) kills the class of the constant function `1` on a clopen neighbourhood of `τ`, and
condition (1) fails.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_bijective_pointRestriction_and_not_bijective_fiberRestriction :
    ∃ (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X S : Scheme.{u}) (hX : B.Contains X) (hS : B.Contains S)
      (f : X ⟶ S) (x : GeometricPoint X) (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : IsAlgClosed K)
      (k : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ strictHenselization B S hS (x.map f)),
      Function.Bijective
          (strictHenselizationPointCohomologyPullback B hX hS f x k
            (constantZ (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) 0) ∧
        ¬ Function.Bijective
          (strictHenselizationFiberCohomologyPullback B hX hS f x k
            (constantZ (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) 0)
declarations.comment:
the statement as given fails: condition (2) at the given point does not imply
condition (1). Condition (1) is equivalent to condition (2) at every lift of `Spec K ⟶ S` to the
strict henselization.

registrations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.not_forall_bijective_strictHenselizationFiberRestriction_iff
registrations.comment:
erratum: the statement as printed is false; condition (2)
  at the given point does not imply condition (1). This is the negation of the printed equivalence,
  for the restriction maps of its statement, at the nodal cubic. The corrected statement, (1) iff
  (2) for every lift `k'` of `Spec K ⟶ S` to the strict henselization, is
  `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.bijective_strictHenselizationFiberCohomologyPullback_iff`.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_etaleLocalFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EZX.** In a cartesian square of schemes with `f : X ⟶ S` flat, if
every object of the small étale site of `X` has an étale covering whose members factor through
an étale `S`-scheme by a quasi-compact morphism with geometrically connected fibres, then the
canonical base change map `f⁻¹ g_* F ⟶ h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism for every sheaf of sets
`F` on the small étale site of `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_etaleLocalFactorization (f : X ⟶ S) (h : Y ⟶ X)
    (e : Y ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ S) (sq : IsPullback h e f g) [Flat f]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (hcover : ∀ U : X.Etale,
      ∃ (ι : Type (u + 1)) (U' : ι → X.Etale) (a : ∀ i, U' i ⟶ U)
        (V : ι → S.Etale) (k : ∀ i, (U' i).left ⟶ (V i).left),
        Sieve.ofArrows U' a ∈ smallEtaleTopology X U ∧
          ∀ i, k i ≫ (V i).hom = (U' i).hom ≫ f ∧
            QuasiCompact (k i) ∧ GeometricallyConnected (k i))
    (hlocal : ∀ ⦃U : X.Etale⦄, HasFlatConnectedFactorization f U →
      Function.Bijective
        (((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, v} e h g f sq.w.symm).app F).hom.app (op U))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, v} e h g f sq.w.symm).app F)
declarations.comment:
The chain of four identifications of the source's first paragraph -- that the
sections of `f⁻¹ g_* F` and of `h_* e⁻¹ F` over an object with such a factorization are both
the sections of `F` over `V ×_S T`, compatibly with the base change map -- rests on Tag 0A3H
(used twice, once for `f` and once for `e`) read through Tag 03EF, and is carried as the
declared hypothesis `hlocal`. What is supplied here is the source's second paragraph: the
covering condition gives enough objects with a flat such factorization, flatness coming from
`f` by `hasFlatConnectedFactorization_of_quasiCompact`, and a map of sheaves bijective on
sections over a family of objects covering every object is an isomorphism.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_etaleLocalFactorizationCover
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian square of schemes with `f : X ⟶ S` flat, if every object of the small étale
site of `X` has an étale covering whose members factor through an étale `S`-scheme by a
quasi-compact morphism with geometrically connected fibres, then the canonical base change map
`f⁻¹ g_* F ⟶ h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism for every sheaf of sets `F` on the small étale site of
`T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_etaleLocalFactorizationCover (f : X ⟶ S) (h : Y ⟶ X)
    (e : Y ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ S) (sq : IsPullback h e f g) [Flat f]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (hcover : ∀ U : X.Etale,
      ∃ (ι : Type (u + 1)) (U' : ι → X.Etale) (a : ∀ i, U' i ⟶ U)
        (V : ι → S.Etale) (k : ∀ i, (U' i).left ⟶ (V i).left),
        Sieve.ofArrows U' a ∈ smallEtaleTopology X U ∧
          ∀ i, k i ≫ (V i).hom = (U' i).hom ≫ f ∧
            QuasiCompact (k i) ∧ GeometricallyConnected (k i)) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, v} e h g f sq.w.symm).app F)
declarations.comment:
no residual hypothesis. Both paragraphs of the source's proof are supplied. The
first is the chain of four identifications -- that the sections of `f⁻¹ g_* F` and of
`h_* e⁻¹ F` over an object with such a factorization are both the sections of `F` over
`V ×_S T`, compatibly with the base change map -- and it is `local_baseChange_compatible`: Tag
0A3H in the localized form of the source's own argument, used twice, once at `f` and once at
`e`, is `smallEtaleInverseImageSectionsIso` and is unconditional, the factorization upstairs is
`etaleBaseChangeFactor`, and their compatibility with the base change map is the
Beck-Chevalley identity for the mate defining `smallEtaleSetBaseChange`. The second paragraph
is that the covering condition gives enough objects with a flat such factorization, flatness
coming from `f` by `hasFlatConnectedFactorization_of_quasiCompact`, and that a map of sheaves
bijective on sections over a family of objects covering every object is an isomorphism.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EZY**, in the case of `X` locally of finite type over the separably
closed field. Let `k` be a separably closed field and let `f : X ⟶ Spec k` be locally of finite
type. Then in a cartesian square over `f` the canonical base change map `f⁻¹ g_* F ⟶ h_* e⁻¹ F`
is an isomorphism for every sheaf of sets `F` on the small étale site of `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isSepClosed (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (h : Y ⟶ X) (e : Y ⟶ T)
    (g : T ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sq : IsPullback h e f g)
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (hlocal : ∀ ⦃U : X.Etale⦄, HasFlatConnectedFactorization f U →
      Function.Bijective
        (((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, v} e h g f sq.w.symm).app F).hom.app (op U))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, v} e h g f sq.w.symm).app F)
declarations.comment:
the case of `X` of finite type over the separably closed field, stated for `X`
locally of finite type. What is proved unconditionally is the covering condition of Tag 0EZX:
an affine open of an étale `X`-scheme is Noetherian, hence locally connected by Tag 04MF, so
the connected component of any of its points is an open quasi-compact subscheme, and over a
separably closed field a connected scheme is geometrically connected by Tag 0363; flatness of
`f` is automatic over a field. The source's reduction of the general case to this one -- write
an affine `X` as a cofiltered limit of affine finite-type `Spec k`-schemes and use the
compatibility of the base change map with such limits -- is Tag 0EZT part (1), which has no
carrier in the library, so the general case is not asserted. The chain of identifications of
sections on which Tag 0EZX feeds rests on Tag 0A3H read through Tag 03EF, a separate cited tag
unavailable in that form, and is carried -- exactly as in Tags 0EZX, 0EYS and 0EZZ -- as the
declared hypothesis `hlocal`.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isSepClosed_of_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a separably closed field and consider a cartesian square of schemes

```
X <--h-- Y
|f       |e
Spec k <--g-- T
```

with `g` quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then the canonical base change map
`f⁻¹ g_* F ⟶ h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism for every sheaf of sets `F` on the small étale site of
`T`. Nothing is assumed of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isSepClosed_of_quasiCompact
    (sq : IsPullback h e f g) [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) (Type (u + 1))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, 0} e h g f sq.w.symm).app F)
declarations.comment: the tag's statement for an arbitrary scheme `X` over the spectrum of a separably closed field, with nothing assumed of `X` and no result of the source assumed. The assumption that `g` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated is the standing convention of Section 0EZW, stated at its start for every cartesian diagram of the section, and the source's proof passes through Tag 0EZT, which assumes it; it cannot be dropped (see this file's module docstring for a counterexample with `g` not quasi-compact). The proof is the stalkwise one of Tag 0F00 specialized to `S = Spec k`: stalks at geometric points detect isomorphisms; the stalk at `x̄` is global sections over the strict henselization `Z = Spec(O^sh_{X,x̄})`; the pasting law for the base change maps of the square of `Z ⟶ X` stacked on the given square splits the base change map of the outer rectangle into `Γ(Z, ι⁻¹ β)` followed by the base change map of the square of `Z ⟶ X` over `h`; the latter is bijective on global sections by Tag 03Q9 for sheaves of sets (`isIso_Γ_map_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_strictHenselization`, `h` being quasi-compact and quasi-separated as a base change of `g`), and the former composite is bijective by the first paragraph of Tag 0EZX (`local_baseChange_compatible`) at the final object of `Z_étale`, `Z ⟶ Spec k` being flat, quasi-compact and geometrically connected (Z is local, hence connected, and connected implies geometrically connected over a separably closed field, Tag 0363). The source's reduction to `X` affine of finite type through Tags 0EZR and 0EZT is replaced by this: its limit argument is the one inside Tag 03Q9.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isSepClosed_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0EZY**, in the case of `X` locally of finite type over the separably
closed field. Let `k` be a separably closed field and let `f : X ⟶ Spec k` be locally of finite
type. Then in a cartesian square over `f` the canonical base change map `f⁻¹ g_* F ⟶ h_* e⁻¹ F`
is an isomorphism for every sheaf of sets `F` on the small étale site of `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isSepClosed_locallyOfFiniteType (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [IsSepClosed k] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (h : Y ⟶ X) (e : Y ⟶ T)
    (g : T ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sq : IsPullback h e f g)
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) (Type (max (u + 1) v))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, v} e h g f sq.w.symm).app F)
declarations.comment:
the case of `X` of finite type over the separably closed field, stated for `X`
locally of finite type. What is proved unconditionally is the covering condition of Tag 0EZX:
an affine open of an étale `X`-scheme is Noetherian, hence locally connected by Tag 04MF, so
the connected component of any of its points is an open quasi-compact subscheme, and over a
separably closed field a connected scheme is geometrically connected by Tag 0363; flatness of
`f` is automatic over a field. The chain of identifications of sections on which Tag 0EZX feeds
is supplied too, by `local_baseChange_compatible`, exactly as in Tags 0EZX, 0EYS and 0EZZ. What
is not asserted is the source's reduction of the general case to this one, which takes two steps.
Working locally on `X` to reduce to an affine `X` is Tag 0EZR clause (1), and that clause is now
proved, as `isIso_smallEtaleSetsBaseChange_of_isIso_local`; but it is proved about
`smallEtaleSetsBaseChange`, a second set-valued base change map built in
`BaseChangeHigher/OrdinaryLocality.lean` from the composition isomorphisms of direct images,
which no result identifies with the `smallEtaleSetBaseChange` of this square. The second step
writes an affine `X` as a cofiltered limit of affine finite-type `Spec k`-schemes and uses the
compatibility of the base change map with such limits, which is Tag 0EZT part (1); the two 0EZT
carriers give the cartesian square on the limits and part (2), for abelian coefficients and the
higher direct images, and part (1) -- sheaves of sets and the underived direct image, the form
this map takes -- has no carrier, nor has the set-valued colimit assertion of Tag 0EYM it would
be built from. The hypothesis that `f` be locally of finite type is therefore still needed, and
is more than the source's statement assumes.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isOpenMap_connectedFibreOpens
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and open, with separably closed residue fields on `S`, with every
affine étale `X`-scheme a finite disjoint union of open subschemes of `X`, and with every
nonempty open of a fibre of `f` connected. Then in a cartesian square over `f` the canonical base
change map `f⁻¹ g_* F ⟶ h_* e⁻¹ F` is an isomorphism for every sheaf of sets `F` on the small
étale site of `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleSetBaseChange_of_isOpenMap_connectedFibreOpens (f : X ⟶ S) (h : Y ⟶ X)
    (e : Y ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ S) (sq : IsPullback h e f g) [Flat f] (hopen : IsOpenMap f)
    (hsep : ∀ s : S, IsSepClosed (S.residueField s))
    (hsplit : ∀ U : X.Etale, IsAffine U.left →
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (V : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (j : ∀ a, V a ⟶ X)
        (_ : ∀ a, IsOpenImmersion (j a)) (i : U.left ≅ ∐ V),
        i.hom ≫ Sigma.desc j = U.hom)
    (hconn : ∀ s : S, ∀ W : (f.fiber s).Opens, W ≠ ⊥ → ConnectedSpace W.toScheme)
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) (Type (max (u + 1) v))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleSetBaseChange.{u, v} e h g f sq.w.symm).app F)
declarations.comment:
no residual hypothesis. The source's proof is omitted with the hint that the
hypotheses imply the covering condition of Tag 0EZX; that implication is what is proved here,
and the chain of identifications of sections which Tag 0EZX then feeds on is
`local_baseChange_compatible`, exactly as for Tag 0EZX above. Hypothesis (3) of the source is
read as the existence of an isomorphism of the étale `X`-scheme with a finite coproduct of open
subschemes of `X` over `X`; the parenthetical examples in (3) and (4), which the source derives
from Tag 09Z9, are not asserted.
